Nonparametric Instrumental Kernel Regression: The Well- and Misspecified Setting Under General Link Conditions
papers.abstract: We study nonparametric instrumental variable regression when the outcome takes values in a separable Hilbert space $\mathbb{Y}$, for instance a curve, a density or the kernel mean embedding of a distribution. The structural function solves an ill-posed operator equation whose conditional expectation operator need not be injective, and whose solutions need not belong to the hypothesis space. We analyse a two-stage kernel estimator that extends kernel instrumental variable regression to $\mathbb{Y}$-valued outcomes and allows spectral regularisation in both stages, including Landweber iteration and Showalter's method in the second stage. We show that the second stage is a regularisation method in the Hilbert scale generated by the inverse of the kernel integral operator. This viewpoint identifies the solution towards which the estimator converges: the minimum-norm solution in the reproducing kernel Hilbert space in the well-specified case and, in the misspecified case, the unique solution in the range of the continuous extension of the projection operator associated to the well-specified setting. Under source conditions and link conditions expressed through general index functions, we derive non-asymptotic bounds in a scale of interpolation norms that hold with high probability in terms of the first-stage error, with or without identification and in the well- and misspecified settings. For polynomial link conditions, we recover the rate of scalar kernel instrumental regression and extend it to targets outside the hypothesis space; for exponential link conditions, we obtain logarithmic rates in the severely ill-posed regime.

papers.title: Exactly Proper Forcing
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of exact properness, a strong form of properness for uncountable models, and prove iteration theorems and the consistency of forcing axioms for this class. We discuss examples of posets in the class and give some applications of the forcing axioms.

papers.title: Vanishing Relative Distance of Uniformly Random CSS LDPC Codes Built from Permutation Matrices
Carroll Double Copy
papers.abstract: We construct a double copy for Carroll gravity as the ``square'' of Carroll Yang-Mills theory at the linearised level. Starting from the convolutional double copy prescription in Lorentzian spacetime, we take the Carrollian limit $c \rightarrow 0$ to establish a double copy dictionary compatible both with symmetries and the corresponding equations of motion. Since this limit yields two distinct sectors, namely the electric and magnetic Carroll theories, we systematically investigate double copy constructions involving all possible combinations of these parent theories. To accommodate the time-independent on-shell configurations of the magnetic Carroll fields, we introduce a suitable regularisation procedure for the convolutional double copy. In addition, the covariance of the double copy under Carroll boosts requires an appropriate dressing of the fields, leading to the inclusion of a Goldstone-type object in the construction. We first develop the formalism using toy models involving scalar fields and then apply it to the double copy between linearised Carroll Yang-Mills theory and Carroll gravity.

papers.title: A Polynomial-Time Algorithm for Constant-Factor EFX Allocations of Chores
Continuous superradiant lasing on a narrow optical transition
papers.abstract: Lasers with ultrastable frequency are at the foundation of optical clocks, which enable precision tests of fundamental physics and relativistic geodesy at the centimetre scale. Such lasers inherit their frequency stability from the length stability of a sophisticated optical resonator, which is hard to maintain outside a well-controlled laboratory environment and limited by thermal and technical noise. Superradiant lasers promise to overcome these limitations by storing their coherence in the atoms making up the laser's gain medium. Superradiant lasing has been demonstrated on narrow optical atomic transitions with pulsed and quasi-continuous operation. However, atom loss has prevented truly continuous operation, which severely limits their suitability for clocks. Here we demonstrate a superradiant laser on a narrow optical transition in $^{88}$Sr that operates truly continuously. We sustain emission for more than eight hours and measure a linewidth of 320(40) Hz, more than 20 times below the natural linewidth. The emission frequency remains anchored to the atomic transition, making the laser itself an atomic frequency reference. Our results provide a route towards a laser that reaches short-term frequency stability comparable to that of the best resonator-stabilized lasers. Furthermore, truly continuous operation gives us access to physics beyond the transient regime, enabling the exploration of robust nonequilibrium steady states and sustained coherent collective dynamics.

papers.title: \(A_α\)-Wronskian Vertices of Paths and Controllability of Path-Rooted Products
papers.abstract: For a graph \(G\) with adjacency and degree matrices \(A(G)\) and \(D(G)\), set \(A_{\alpha}(G)=\alpha D(G)+(1-\alpha)A(G)\) for \(0\leq\alpha<1\). Using Chebyshev polynomials and a theorem of Conway and Jones, we classify the \(A_{\alpha}\)-Wronskian vertices of every path \(P_n\), \(n\geq2\) (equivalently, the standard basis vectors cyclic for \(A_{\alpha}(P_n)\)). The central vertex of an odd-order path is never Wronskian; for every other vertex, we determine an explicit finite set of algebraic exceptional parameters. These sets contain no rational parameters other than \(0\) and \(1/2\), for which the adjacency and signless Laplacian cases are characterized by gcd criteria. For even-order paths rooted at either central vertex, we explicitly evaluate the root resultant and the walk-determinant polynomial in the rooted-product factorization. The resulting controllability criterion combines \(A_{\alpha}\)-controllability of the base graph with at most three explicit spectral exclusions. For each parameter, one of two fixed complementary base graphs yields controllable products for every even-order path and both central roots. For \(1/2\leq\alpha<1\), algebraic conjugates further simplify the spectral test for general rooted products.

papers.title: Stability-Compensated Threshold Calibration for Selection-Conditioned Risk Control in Large Language Models
The Mask Is Not the Object: Volumetric Supervision for 3D Gaussian Segmentation
VisualArtifactSpec 1.0: Evaluating Visual Artifacts under Task Specifications
Multilevel AlScN Ferroelectric Diode Crossbar Arrays with Sub-200 nm Cells for Selector-Free Nonvolatile Memory
papers.abstract: Passive crossbar arrays are a leading route to high-density nonvolatile memory and in-memory computing, but without a selector the memory element itself must supply the nonlinearity that suppresses sneak-path currents. Here we scale aluminum scandium nitride (AlScN) ferroelectric diodes (FeDs) in both dimensions that matter - the ferroelectric is thinned to 10 nm and the junction diameter is reduced to 100 nm. We further integrate 200 nm cells into a 2-kilobyte (128 * 128) passive crossbar. At a junction area of 0.0314 um2 this is a ~625 reduction in cell area, at equal array capacity, relative to kilobyte-scale AlScN FeD crossbars built on 5 {\mu}m cells. The 10 nm Al0.64Sc0.36N layer reverses its polarization under pulses of 50 ns full width at half maximum at a pulse-energy density of ~16 pJ {\mu}m-2, corresponding to ~0.5 pJ per 200 nm cell. Pulsed programming at 17.5 V and 1 kHz yields an ON/OFF ratio of 4.2 * 103 in a 200 nm cell, while DC characterization of 283 randomly addressed cells of the 2-kB array gives ON/OFF and rectification ratios at 5 V of 43 33 and 61 74, from which we derive the sub-array size that selector-free reading currently supports. Eight conductance levels (three bits) written into a 200 nm array cell remain resolvable for 103 s, and the two extreme states are stable beyond 5 * 104 s. Mapping the measured, nonuniformly spaced levels onto a ResNet-20 network recovers 91.7 +- 0.1 % CIFAR-10 accuracy after quantization-aware training, against a 92.2 +- 0.1 % full-precision baseline. AlScN FeDs thus combine nanosecond switching, three-bit storage and sub-0.05 {\mu}m2 cells in a BEOL-compatible, selector-free crossbar.

papers.title: Heavy double-gluon quarkonium and $\overline{b}ggc$ mesons
papers.abstract: We investigate heavy double-gluon hybrid mesons, built from a heavy quark-antiquark pair and two valence gluons, using the two-point QCD sum rule method. The charmonium-like $\bar{c}GGc$ and bottomonium-like $\bar{b}GGb$ states are considered with $J^{PC}=0^{\pm\pm}$ and $1^{\pm\pm}$, whereas the open-flavor $\bar{b}GGc$ states are classified by $J^{P}=0^{\pm}$ and $1^{\pm}$. The currents with $J^{PC}=0^{+-}, 0^{--}, 1^{++}$, and $1^{-+}$ vanish identically, so sum rules are derived for the remaining four channels. The operator product expansion is carried out up to dimension twelve, and the Borel parameter and continuum threshold are fixed so that the pole contribution dominates and the OPE converges. The resulting masses lie in the ranges $M\simeq 6.2$--$6.7$~GeV for $\bar{c}GGc$, $M\simeq 12.0$--$12.2$~GeV for $\bar{b}GGb$, and $M\simeq 9.2$--$9.6$~GeV for $\bar{b}GGc$, and the current couplings are obtained for all channels. These predictions provide a basis for analyzing the strong decays of double-gluon hybrids and for interpreting future experimental data in the heavy-quark sector.

papers.title: What's the Difference? Voice Design and Confirmation Bias in AI-Assisted Self-Diagnosis: Anthropomorphic vs. Machine-Like Voice Output
Data-Driven Predictive Control for Autonomous Vehicle Racing under Varying Friction
Douglas--Rachford Algorithm with Relaxed Resolvents
papers.abstract: The Douglas--Rachford algorithm is a classical method for finding a zero of the sum of two maximally monotone operators. In its standard form, both operators are reflected in the same manner and are activated with the same step-size. In this article we break this symmetry by replacing the reflected resolvents by relaxed resolvents, letting the two operators be activated with different step-sizes. We show that this additional freedom is available precisely when the operators are cocoercive, the admissible range of the parameter being determined by their cocoercivity constants and reducing to the classical algorithm when these constants vanish. Within this range we quantify the averagedness of the resulting operator, which yields the weak convergence of the method together with relaxation steps beyond those allowed in the classical case, and, when one of the operators is in addition strongly monotone, a strict contraction. We compute in closed form the parameters minimizing the contraction factor and we exhibit instances attaining it, so that the resulting linear rates are tight. The optimal rates are strictly smaller than the best rates available for the classical Douglas--Rachford algorithm in the monotone inclusion and convex optimization settings, which are studied separately. All theoretical rates are corroborated by the numerical worst cases obtained via performance estimation.

papers.title: A Crowd-Audited Atlas of Implicit Bias in LLM-Powered Agents

An improved weighted broad $L^2$ estimate in $\mathbb{R}^2$
papers.abstract: For a compact smooth plane curve $S$ with nonzero curvature and a union $X\subseteq B_R$ of unit balls satisfying a one-dimensional Katz--Tao condition, we prove $\|\mathrm{Br}_A E_S f\|_{L^2(X)} \leq C_{\varepsilon,\varepsilon'} R^{\varepsilon}|X|^{13/62}\|f\|_2$. The proof relies on a refined local broad estimate that uses density decomposition and the short frequency intervals associated with coarse tubes.

Learning What Pairs Miss for Higher-Order Multimodal Alignment
Information Causality Defeats Every Finite NPA Level
papers.abstract: For every finite level of the Navascués-Pironio-Acín (NPA) hierarchy, we construct correlations that satisfy all its constraints but violate information causality. At each fixed level, one use of a binary-outcome correlation and one classical bit suffice for a violation that grows without bound as the number of measurement settings increases. Information causality bounds the information gained about independent database bits, summed over possible requests, by the length of the message. Quantum correlations obey the one-bit bound; the optimal information gain at any fixed NPA level grows logarithmically with the number of settings. The violation remains unbounded even when all outcome probabilities are positive and, for any fixed number of measurement settings on each side, every choice of those settings admits a local model. One communicated bit therefore exposes an unbounded gap between information causality and every finite NPA level.

papers.title: Federated TD Learning in Heterogeneous Environments with Average Rewards: A Two-timescale Approach with Polyak-Ruppert Averaging
EP241206a: A Sub-kilosecond X-Ray Flare Possibly from an Active Galactic Nucleus with a Flux Increase over 3 Orders of Magnitude
papers.abstract: EP241206a is a fast X-ray transient detected with the Wide-field X-ray Telescope (WXT) on board the Einstein Probe. The event exhibited a single-peaked soft X-ray flare with a duration of $\sim 500$ s and a peak flux of $1.0 \times 10^{-9}$ erg s$^{-1}$ cm$^{-2}$ in 0.5--4 keV, spatially coincident with a spectroscopically confirmed active galactic nucleus (AGN) at $z = 0.62$. Follow-up and archival observations revealed persistent X-ray emission at a level of $\sim 5 \times 10^{-13}$ erg s$^{-1}$ cm$^{-2}$, corresponding to $L_{2-10 \mathrm{keV}} \simeq 2.3 \times 10^{44}$ erg s$^{-1}$ if associated with the AGN; the WXT flare reached an estimated peak isotropic-equivalent rest-frame 2--10 keV luminosity of $\sim 1.4 \times 10^{48}$ erg s$^{-1}$, implying a peak-to-persistent luminosity contrast of over 3 orders of magnitude. Optical spectroscopy detected broad Mg II and H$\beta$ emission lines, suggesting a black hole mass of $\sim 3.8 \times 10^{7} M_{\odot}$ and Eddington ratios of 0.8 at the persistent state versus an apparent peak ratio of $\sim 4.6 \times 10^{3}$ during the flare. The extremely short duration and high apparent peak luminosity favor a jet origin, likely due to magnetic reconnection in the inner regions of a relativistic jet. Alternative scenarios include a jet-in-the-jet or a gamma-ray burst occurring within the AGN disk. However, the physical association between the transient and the AGN is not firmly established; for the radio-loud and X-ray-detected AGN counterpart class, the trial-corrected chance probability is $4.9 \times 10^{-3}$. EP241206a may represent an example of a broader population of unidentified fast X-ray transients detected with WXT.

papers.title: Astrophysical Constraints for Bosonic Dark Matter in and Around Quark Stars
papers.abstract: We investigate the structure, stability, and mass-radius relations of compact stars composed of quark matter within the non-ideal MIT Bag Model mixed with self-interacting bosonic dark matter with a $\phi^n$ self-interaction potential. By solving the coupled two-fluid Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equations for boson masses between 200 MeV and 1 GeV and self-interaction strengths with $n=4$ and $n=40$, we show that strong self-interactions and higher boson masses enhance the stability of compact star configurations at high central pressures, though they reduce maximum overall masses. Ultra-compact solutions with $C \ge 1/3$ capable of mimicking black holes are significantly restricted compared to hadronic models, emerging only for strong self-interactions and dark matter fractions exceeding 90\%. Depending on the parameters, the compact stars form either extended dark matter halos or compact cores: stronger self-interactions and higher boson masses suppress the radial extension to favor compact cores of dark matter. Matching our models against observational constraints highlights PSR J1614$-$2230 and XTE J1814$-$338 as potential window of opportunity for dark matter detection. Notably, XTE J1814$-$338 could confirm a dark sector, given its requirement for light boson masses ($m_b \approx 200\text{--}300\text{ MeV}$) and strongly DM-dominated configurations.

papers.title: Premise Recovery in Software Design: What Does This Decision Rest On?
ALIVE: Making Streaming Video Models Interactive
Exploring the link between predictive uncertainty and the sim-to-real gap in deep learning models utilizing synthetic data
A Game of Throngs: How Spotlight Tourism Reshapes Local Economies
papers.abstract: In July 2017, San Juan de Gaztelugatxe, a modest chapel in the Basque Country, appeared as "Dragonstone" in Game of Thrones, transforming a locally known site with limited tourism activity into a global tourist destination overnight. We exploit this exogenous spotlight shock to estimate its causal effects on the local economy using a novel administrative dataset and a Synthetic Control approach. We find an abrupt increase in tourism activity, far exceeding the effects documented in the literature. Despite this surge, employment gains in tourism-related sectors were largely offset by losses elsewhere, resulting in no net effect on total employment. We also document signs of housing-market overheating, with increases in both property transactions and prices. We find no evidence that the shock displaced the local population. Instead, it led to a roughly twofold increase in arrivals from abroad. Taken together, these findings suggest that a substantial increase in tourism activity does not necessarily translate into broad-based local economic gains. Instead, tourism-led growth may entail significant sectoral reallocation and housing-market pressures, underscoring the importance of looking beyond tourism activity alone when assessing its wider economic effects.

papers.title: Symmetry Detection with Patch Embedding Models by Means of a Scalar Product Transform
What You Post Is What You Symptom: Estimating Psychometric Networks from Social Media Discourse

papers.title: Inclusive Heavy Quarkonium Production in Lepton-Hadron Scattering in a Joint QCD+QED Factorization Approach
papers.abstract: The Electron-Ion Collider (EIC) will provide an opportunity for precision studies of heavy quarkonium production in electron-proton ($ep$) and electron-nucleus ($eA$) collisions. Comparing production in $ep$ and $eA$ collisions provides a clean, well-controlled experimental environment to study interactions between a heavy quark pair and nuclear matter and the formation of quarkonia in a nuclear medium. In this talk, we present the first calculation of heavy quarkonium production in both $ep$ and $eA$ collisions at EIC energies using a joint QCD+QED factorization framework that treats collision-induced QCD and QED radiation on equal footing, and discuss the role of the nuclear medium in exploring how a physical quarkonium is emerged from a produced heavy quark pair. We also systematically extend our calculation to include next-to-leading power contributions in the inverse power expansion of quarkonium transverse momentum, and discuss the matching of our calculations to fixed-order calculations in the nonrelativistic Quantum Chromodynamics (NRQCD) approach.

papers.title: Sequential strategy for depolarizing strength estimation
papers.abstract: We study the advantages of applying a sequential strategy for enhancing the precision in estimating the strength $p$ of a depolarizing channel, using qudit and two-qubit probes. The sequential strategy requires that the same depolarizing channel is repeatedly applied $M$ times to the quantum probe. From the analysis of the probe's output state, both the quantum Fisher information (QFI) and its regularization RQFI, given from multiplication by $p$, are analyzed. We determine that in the limit of $p \to 0$, the QFI is {\it linearly amplified} with the number of channel repetitions. Instead, in the weak-noise regime, the QFI is maximized at a finite value of $M$. Then, the RQFI decreases more quickly with $p$ as $M$ increases. In particular, for two-qubit probes, the RQFI decreases with the depolarization strength proportionally to the amount of correlation between the qubits. The greater the number of channel repetitions, the wider the range of $p$ for which the initial state of the probe that allows for the maximization of the QFI is a separable state. We also show that a single qubit probe undergoing a sequential encoding protocol outperforms the optimal two-qubit single-round QFI for $M>3$ in the weak-noise regime.

papers.title: K-out-of-N Oblivious Transfer over Erasure Channels: Capacity and Reductions
From very fine Vertical Resolution to Range Super-Resolution on BIOMASS P-BAND SAR Data
papers.abstract: This paper demonstrates range super-resolution over arid regions using SAR tomography data with very fine vertical resolution from the European Space Agency's BIOMASS mission. As the first civilian spaceborne P-band SAR mission, BIOMASS is operating with a bandwidth limited to 6~MHz by International Telecommunication Union regulations, yielding a native slant-range resolution of approximately 25 m. The large spatial baseline data acquired during the commissioning phase in July and August 2025 provide a valuable opportunity to enhance range resolution based on the InSAR wavenumber shift principle. According to this principle, a wider effective bandwidth can be synthesized by combining complementary sub-bands of the ground reflectivity spectrum sampled across acquisitions at different look angles. Unlike existing literature, this paper offers a novel interpretation of this problem from the perspective of SAR tomography. Furthermore, the proposed method also accounts for residual topography errors. The range resolution enhancement performance is validated using all 20 available acquisitions from the July-August 2025 commissioning phase over Lop Nur, China, and Wadi al-Hayat, Libya, achieving spatial detail comparable to optical satellite imagery in a grid finer than 2 m. Furthermore, the reconstructed range spectrum of the central Libyan oasis exhibits an effective bandwidth exceeding 70 MHz. The point spread function (PSF) of a point like target in the scene demonstrates a slant-range resolution finer than 2.1 m, representing more than a twelvefold improvement over the native resolution.

papers.title: Accessing Electrode Edges: Upright Mounting for Site-Specific Cryogenic Atom Probe Tomography of Lithium-Ion Batteries
papers.abstract: Cryogenic atom probe tomography (cryo-APT) is increasingly being used to map the three-dimensional distribution of highly reactive species in heterogeneous materials, including those found in battery systems. However, site-specific preparation of localised features and liquid-solid interfaces remains challenging, particularly when regions of interest (ROIs) are concentrated along electrode edges that are difficult to access using conventional mounting geometries. Here, we present a cryo-APT workflow incorporating an upright-mounting procedure that enables targeted specimen preparation of localised regions using plasma focused ion beam (PFIB) microscopy and milling under cryogenic conditions. We first demonstrate the approach using an electrolyte-wetted graphite electrode, successfully preparing and analysing a specimen containing both an edge-localised electrolyte deposit and the underlying graphite and Cu current collector. We then apply the workflow to a cycled graphite electrode, targeting Li dendrites concentrated around the electrode perimeter and successfully preparing and analysing the targeted Li-rich region. Beyond battery systems, this approach offers potential for site-specific cryo-APT of edge-localised features across a broader range of material systems, where conventional specimen preparation geometries may limit access to ROIs.

papers.title: The Stability of the Higgs vacuum inside a Schwarzschild Black Hole
papers.abstract: I investigate the behaviour of the Higgs field inside a Schwarzschild black hole, including a Planck-suppressed coupling between the Higgs field and the Kretschmann scalar, the leading curvature invariant in a Ricci-flat geometry. Because the radial coordinate is timelike in the interior, the Higgs condensate evolves in time rather than tracking the minimum of its potential. Near the singularity the interior field equation reduces to Bessel's equation, with solution $H=vJ_0(x)$, where $x\propto\sqrt\xi\,t_p/\tau$ and $\tau$ is the proper time to the singularity. Contrary to static analyses, the field remains frozen in its broken phase while the potential changes shape, departing from its vacuum value only when the curvature becomes Planckian, independently of the black-hole mass. Including the one-loop correction from Higgs vacuum fluctuations yields the same Bessel equation with a source term, which I solve exactly; the condensate is reduced by at most about ten per cent. The electroweak symmetry therefore remains broken throughout the interior within the regime of validity of effective field theory.

papers.title: Critical curves and throat degeneracy in black bounces
papers.abstract: Identical critical curves need not imply identical null-orbit dynamics. For a class of static spherical areal-radius deformations, we show that a surviving original photon sphere retains its critical impact parameter and orbital frequency, while its coordinate-time Lyapunov exponent is multiplied by the radial Jacobian. The logarithmic strong-deflection coefficient acquires the inverse factor. At a reflection-symmetric throat, stability factorizes into a derivative of the original optical potential and the throat curvature. More generally, an order-$m$ extremum of the original potential composed with an order-$q$ areal-radius minimum produces an optical degeneracy of order $p=mq$, with critical approach $|x|\propto|t|^{-2/(p-2)}$ and reflected strong deflection $\Delta\phi\propto(b/b_{\rm c}-1)^{-(p-2)/(2p)}$ for $p>2$. For the Simpson--Visser family with mass $M$ and bounce parameter $a$, the critical impact parameter remains Schwarzschild-like for $a<3M$, although the instability varies with $a$. The merger at $a=3M$ is quartic, separating stable and unstable throat branches. These results isolate the null-orbit information preserved by a radial deformation from that encoded in its local geometry.

papers.title: Vortex states in submicron titanomagnetite particles
papers.abstract: Numerical simulation is used to study the magnetic properties of spheroidal titanomagnetite particles Fe(3-x)TixO4 (0.4 < x < 0.6) with semi-axes ratio ranging from 0.5 to 1.5 and transverse diameters D = 100 - 480 nm. It is shown that various vortex micromagnetic states can emerge in the titanomagnetite particles depending on the titanium concentration, aspect ratio and particle diameter. The single-domain particle diameters are determined using the energy diagrams for stationary uniform and vortex states. The remanent magnetization of dilute assemblies of titanomagnetite particles with varying titanium content are calculated as a function of the transverse particle diameter D. It is demonstrated that for submicron-sized titanomagnetite particles, D ~ 500 nm, the normalized remanent magnetization of the assembly reaches very low values, M/Ms < 0.01, where Ms is the saturation magnetization of the particles.

papers.title: An Adaptive Reduced Speed of Light Approximation
authors: Benjamin D. Wibking (2) ((1) Australian National University
(2) The Observatories of the Carnegie Institution for Science
papers.abstract: The reduced speed of light approximation (RSLA) is a common approach in radiation-hydrodynamic (RHD) simulations of non-relativistic systems where the gas speed $v_{\rm gas} \ll c$. In the RSLA one eases the severe time step constraint imposed by the speed of light $c$ by replacing it with a reduced value $\hat{c}$ chosen so that $v_{\rm gas} \ll \hat{c} \ll c$. This approach works well in flows with low or moderate optical depth, but fails in optically thick media, where it makes thermal relaxation too slow and gives incorrect RHD wave modes. Here we propose an Adaptive Reduced Speed of Light Approximation (ARSA) that removes these problems by replacing the global speed reduction factor $\phi_0 \equiv \hat{c}/c$ with a local, cell-by-cell reduction factor $\phi$ derived from a von Neumann stability analysis of the implicit-explicit update used by modern two-moment RHD codes. The resulting limiter has no tunable parameters, can be computed using only local operations, and improves on the classic RSLA by allowing $\phi \to 1$ in cells where a reduced speed of light is not required because the exchange with the gas damps unstable modes, allowing recovery of the correct thermal relaxation and wave-damping rates in highly-opaque regions. We compare ARSA to the classic RSLA in a range of standard RHD test problems, and show that in opaque regions where gas holds most of the heat capacity the ARSA is much more accurate than the RSLA at the same time step, or that it can achieve the same accuracy as the RSLA with up to 100 times fewer time steps. However, gains are limited in regions where radiation holds a large share of the heat capacity, as it does in some astrophysical systems.

papers.title: Specificity-Guided Knowledge Diversion for Decomposable Generative Models
A Free Energy Approach to Modelling Disordered Hyperuniform Patterns
papers.abstract: We present a free-energy-based approach for modelling disordered hyperuniform patterns. Specifically, we devise a phase-field crystal model with a correlation kernel that simultaneously selects for a continuous range of degenerate wave modes. At small wave vectors, we construct the correlation function by inverting the Ornstein-Zernike relation to approximate the structure factor of a hyperuniform pattern. Our model demonstrates a crossover between liquid, crystalline, quasicrystalline, and long-lived disordered states depending on the specified free energy parameter and driving force. We show that, for a fixed driving force, the specific structures and wave vectors selected by the density field can be controlled by modulating the width of the correlation kernel. Furthermore, we show that the scaling of the low-wave-vector region of the correlation function can accurately reproduce a specified hyperuniform exponent, independently of the structural properties at larger wave numbers. Our results establish a free-energy-based framework for describing disordered hyperuniform states, demonstrating and enabling independent control over structural selection and long-wavelength density correlations.

papers.title: Unexpected Plateau: The Constant $ \rm \log ε(Th/Eu)$ Ratio of Actinide-Boost Stars
papers.abstract: The astrophysical site of the rapid neutron-capture process ($r$-process) is still one of the major open questions in astronomy. A key mystery is the origin of the peculiar actinide-to-lanthanide ratio found in the so called actinide-boost stars, with $ \rm \log \epsilon (Th/Eu)>-0.35$. Here we present the largest sample of Th measurements in stars formed in an external galaxy, Gaia Sausage Enceladus. From this sample, we present the three most metal-rich actinide-boost stars discovered to date, $\rm -1.6<[Fe/H]<-1.1$. In addition, we measured Th in a comparison sample of Milky Way stars formed in situ, and compiled Th measurements from the literature which do not account for non-local thermodynamic equilibrium (NLTE) effects. After applying NLTE corrections to the combined sample, a bimodality in the $\rm\log\epsilon (Th/Eu)$ ratio is revealed. Unexpectedly, actinide-boost stars lie on a very narrow $(\sigma=0.02)$ plateau of $\rm \log\epsilon(Th/Eu)=-0.2$, clearly separated from actinide-normal stars. Most (if not all) of the actinide-boost stars in our sample originate from outside the Milky Way. Chemical evolution models show that such a plateau can arise, even at [Fe/H] = $-$1, when a single actinide-rich event dominates the r-process content of a small or gas-depleted system. Combined with other evidence, our results suggest that mergers with neutron stars are the most promising astrophysical site for actinide-boost stars.

papers.title: Catalytic compression of classical communication in exact entanglement transformations
papers.abstract: Entanglement catalysis is usually associated with making otherwise impossible transformations possible. Here we show that it can also change how much classical communication a transformation requires. A catalyst, returned exactly and uncorrelated with the output, can reduce the message alphabet size required for exact transformations of bipartite pure states by a factor that grows without bound as the Schmidt rank increases. In the asymptotic many-copy regime, however, this advantage disappears at the level of the leading communication rate: the optimal catalytic and noncatalytic rates coincide. We characterize the optimal catalytic cost in terms of Rényi entropies, revealing how the entanglement structure of the source and target governs the finite-copy advantage. Our results establish reusable entanglement as a resource for compressing classical communication in quantum state manipulation.

papers.title: Representational Change Under Self-Consuming Training: A Sparse Autoencoder Analysis
On the blow-up of the one-particle Lieb-Thirring constant in dimension two
papers.abstract: We establish three-term asymptotics for the one-particle Lieb-Thirring constant in dimension two as $\gamma\to 0$ and identify, up to rescaling and symmetries, the profile of the asymptotically worst potential. The proof uses the well-known relation between the one-particle constant and an integral moment of optimizers of the Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality. Through the optimizers' characterization as positive, vanishing solutions of the nonlinear elliptic equation $-\Delta Q + Q = Q^{s}$ in $\mathbb{R}^2$, the essence of the proof lies in the asymptotic analysis of solutions $Q$ as $s\to\infty$.

papers.title: Harmonic-Constrained Hosting Capacity of Active Distribution Networks Using ESS Compensation and Certified Adaptive Decision-Tree Envelopes
Arithmetic Universality and Integer Decomposition in Disjunctions of Three Staircase Simplices
papers.abstract: The staircase simplices $\{x\in[0,1]^d:x_{\sigma(1)}\le\cdots\le x_{\sigma(d)}\}$, $\sigma\in S_d\,$, are the $d!$ unimodular cells of the staircase triangulation of the unit cube. The disjunctive hull (Cayley polytope) of a selection $P_0, \ldots, P_n$ of them has the integer decomposition property (IDP) if, for all integers $\lambda_i\ge0$, every lattice point of $\sum_i\lambda_i P_i$ is a sum of vertices, $\lambda_i$ of them from $P_i$. For two simplices, IDP always holds. For three, every nontrivial finite abelian group $G$ arises, in the optimal dimension $\Theta(\log|G|)$, as the residue group of a simplex facet whose $|G|-1$ nonzero box points are Hilbert basis elements of the whole cone; $k$ times such a point is a sum of vertices exactly when its order in $G$ divides $k$. Isolating this arithmetic is costly: if a simplex face has a single Hilbert basis element $h$ that is not a vertex, then $kh$ is a sum of vertices exactly when some $q$ divides $k$, and $d\ge3q-2$, attained for every $q\ge3$; we also find the least dimension for each $G$ with the fewest such elements. Without isolation, every nonzero submonoid of $\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$ omitting $1$ is $\{k\ge0:kh$ is a sum of vertices$\}$ for a Hilbert basis element $h$ of degree three. For every $0/1$ polytope with $N$ vertices in $\mathbb{R}^r$, three staircase simplices in dimension $O(N(r+1))$ have a face that has IDP exactly when the polytope does. Deciding whether a lattice point $h$ is a sum of vertices is strongly NP-complete, even given vertex expressions of $2h$ and $3h$, and recognizing IDP of a designated facet is coNP-complete; for the whole hull, IDP can first fail in degree linear in $d$, and it holds whenever $d\le5$. For a family of triples defined by words over three letters, we determine the entire Hilbert basis and characterize IDP by two forbidden subsequences.

papers.title: TEMPO: Regime-Aware Operator Learning with Locally Adapted POD Bases
Toeplitz coefficients and the Lu-Tian correspondence on Sasakian manifolds
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a compact embeddable strictly pseudoconvex CR manifold with Reeb field $T$ and Szeg\H o projection $\Pi$. Herrmann, Hsiao, Marinescu and the second author showed, for any volume form, that the semi-classical cut-offs $\chi(k^{-1}\Pi P\Pi)$ of first-order elliptic self-adjoint Toeplitz operators have full asymptotic expansions. For $P=-\sqrt{-1}T$ and $T$-invariant volume forms, Chang, Herrmann and Hsiao showed that the diagonal coefficients are $a_{j}\int\chi(t)t^{n-j}dt$ with local invariants $a_{j}$, computed $a_{0}$ and $a_{1}$, and used normal forms in the Sasakian case. We add one step: on a compact Sasakian manifold, regular or not, $a_{j}=a_{j}(g^{T})/(2\pi^{n+1})$, where $a_{j}(\cdot)$ is the universal Bergman kernel polynomial and $g^{T}$ the transverse Kähler metric; no line bundle on $X$ is needed. This gives an exact correspondence: the logarithmic term of the Szeg\H o kernel vanishes to infinite order over an open set if and only if $a_{j}(g^{T})=0$ there for all $j\ge n+1$, which for circle bundles is a local form of the theorem of Lu and Tian with its converse. For $(n,0)$-forms on complete Sasakian manifolds, a cut-off by the self-adjoint generator of the Reeb flow, which avoids the self-adjointness question for the Toeplitz operator, gives the same results with twisted coefficients.

papers.title: No Supersoft X-rays Before SN 2026ahvu: Constraints on a Potentially Prompt Type Ia Progenitor
papers.abstract: The nearby Type Ia supernova SN 2026ahvu offers a rare opportunity to probe its progenitor that may have evolved unusually rapidly. If the progenitor formed in either of the two young stellar clusters near the explosion site in NGC 1433, the delay from star formation to explosion could have been $\sim$100 Myr or less. The distance to NGC 1433 remains uncertain, with published estimates of 9.1 Mpc and 18.9 Mpc. Our preliminary fit to the rising ATLAS light curve yields a distance of $17.7^{+1.5}_{-1.4}$ Mpc. In the classical single-degenerate scenario, a white dwarf steadily burning hydrogen accreted from a non-degenerate companion can emit detectable supersoft X-rays before explosion. We search for this emission using two archival Chandra observations obtained before the explosion. The observations provide a combined exposure of 95.3 ks, with no 0.3-7 keV photons detected within 2" of the supernova position. For a 100 eV blackbody with Galactic foreground absorption, the 95\% bolometric luminosity limits are $6.3\times10^{37}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ and $2.7\times10^{38}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ at 9.1 Mpc and 18.9 Mpc, respectively. At both distances, the observations exclude a hot, compact white dwarf undergoing steady hydrogen burning if the absorption is limited to the Galactic foreground. However, cooler, expanded, or more heavily absorbed photospheres remain viable. Together with the pre-explosion non-detections for SN 2011fe and SN 2014J, our results reinforce the absence of luminous supersoft progenitors in nearby SNe Ia. This pattern is naturally consistent with double-degenerate explosions, although X-ray-faint single-degenerate configurations remain viable. Post-explosion X-ray observations can test for circumstellar interaction and help determine whether material around the progenitor could have obscured a luminous nuclear burning white dwarf.

papers.title: Quantum adiabatic and diabatic optimization: A Hilbert space engineering strategy with Rydberg arrays
papers.abstract: Neutral-atom arrays provide a versatile platform for encoding combinatorial optimization problems with arbitrary graph connectivity [Nguyen et al., PRX Quantum 4, 010316 (2023)]. Although the dynamics of individual encoding gadgets has been studied [Bombieri et al., PRX Quantum 6, 020306 (2025)], understanding annealing bottlenecks in larger networks remains challenging. We investigate how engineering the Hilbert-space geometry controls quantum annealing in a family of blockaded-chain models motivated by these encodings. While boundary terms encode the target maximum independent set problem, the bulk geometry induces an auxiliary optimization problem associated with independent sets of cliques. Spectrally, the energetics of the quantum system can be approximated by physically derived clique weights. When the target problem and the auxiliary problems are consistent, the low-energy modes lie predominantly within the target subspace. This spectral structure motivates a diabatic annealing strategy that exploits target-compatible excited states, as tested on the diamond-chain graph family. These results provide a framework for predicting annealing bottlenecks, and demonstrate Hilbert-space engineering as a strategy for improving neutral-atom quantum optimization protocols.

papers.title: Fourier--Stieltjes palettes on compact abelian groups
papers.abstract: Let G be an infinite compact abelian group and let K={0,a_1,a_2,...}, where a_1>a_2>...>0 and a_n\to 0. We construct a nonzero real, even, purely singular Rajchman measure whose Fourier--Stieltjes range is contained in K. We then classify the compact abelian groups on which every positive null palette is exactly realizable in each of four classes: purely singular measures, atomless purely singular measures, strongly continuous purely singular measures, and Rajchman purely singular measures. Exact realization by a purely singular measure is always possible; atomless exact realization fails precisely for groups topologically isomorphic to \mathbb{T}\times F with F finite; and universal exact Rajchman realization is equivalent to \operatorname{Tor}(\widehat G) being infinite, or equivalently to G/G_0 being infinite. On \mathbb{T} we also give palette-dependent sufficient conditions for exact Rajchman realization. Finally, if U\subset\mathbb{C} is open and 0\in\overline U, we construct a continuous Rajchman measure with nonzero singular part whose Fourier--Stieltjes range is contained in U, assuming metrizability of G when 0\notin U. This gives a negative answer to an open-range absolute-continuity question of Ohrysko and Wojciechowski.

papers.title: MovieRoll: A Systematic Framework for Rolling Out Long-Form Videos
Generating a simple silicon detector simulation with an open-weight large language model
papers.abstract: Recent LLM developments have seen AI-generated code become commonplace in the software development industry. Without tool access, LLMs cannot execute simulations, and their knowledge of toolkits such as Geant4 is limited. We demonstrate here, a detector simulation workflow with a Qwen3.6-27B model with Q4_K_M GGUF quantisation together with custom resources and tools served via MCP servers to generate a particle detector simulation. In 50 independent runs, 42(29--56)% at 95% CI produced energy-deposit distributions statistically consistent with a reference simulation, measured against a reference simulation. These results provide a proof of concept that MC simulations can be generated using text-based prompts with an LLM, given the necessary resources and tools. More extensive resources, such as example code and additional documentation, are likely to be required for more complex simulation tasks.

papers.title: On the origin of Milky Way binary black holes with LISA
papers.abstract: Primordial black holes (PBHs) may constitute a fraction of dark matter, but distinguishing them from black holes of stellar origin remains a major challenge. We propose a new method based on the three-dimensional localization of Galactic Binary Black Holes (BBHs) by the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA). While stellar-origin BBHs are expected to be associated with the stellar distribution of the Milky Way, PBHs may trace its more extended dark matter halo. We introduce a spatial overlap ratio that compares the gravitational-wave localization of each binary with the normalized stellar and dark matter density profiles. Using a Fisher-matrix forecast and 1000 Monte Carlo realizations of a 10-year LISA mission, we find that detecting three BBHs with an overlap ratio ln B < 0 occurs in approximately 99% of simulations where BBHs trace dark matter, but in fewer than 0.1% of simulations where they follow the stellar distribution, even when including a stellar halo containing 3% of the Galactic stellar mass. These results suggest that the localization of only a few Galactic BBHs could provide strong evidence for a primordial population, offering an independent test of their possible contribution to dark matter.

papers.title: Why Cassini's Oval Could Not Replace Kepler's Ellipse?
papers.abstract: In the later seventeenth century, Kepler's ellipse was not yet accepted. Ward claimed that Boulliau's conic hypothesis amounted to a Ptolemaic equant at the ellipse's empty focus, and built his own model on it. Around 1675--1680, Giovanni Domenico Cassini proposed another curve, the ``oval'', a genus-1 quartic with no closed-form Kepler equation; yet its eccentric anomaly shares exactly the leading coefficient of Kepler's, and its empty focus is, for the Sun, 38 times closer to a true equant than the ellipse's. Dynamically, Binet's formula shows that the force producing the oval under the area law departs from the inverse square by an index $\mathcal{D}(e)\sim3/(4e^2)$, depending on the oval's parameter $e$: no single exponent serves the whole family. This absence of universality, not of an area law, distinguishes it from the ellipse, and arguably explains why Cassini, the Académie and Leibniz kept the question open after the \emph{Principia} (1687).

papers.title: Anchoring Motion, Refining Trajectories: Generalizable Continuous Neural Decoding
Real-world Polarimetric Environment Map Dataset
Non-factorisable Yangian Lax matrices through oscillators
papers.abstract: We construct oscillator realisations of Yangian Lax operators in type $A$, with particular interest in non-factorisable operators associated with prime snake modules. Our construction applies to finite-dimensional skew representations of $Y(\mathfrak{gl}_n)$. We prove that these representations are generated by the tensor vacuum in suitably ordered tensor products of oscillator representations. Their Lax operators are obtained by restricting the corresponding products of linear oscillator Lax operators to these submodules. We determine the vacuum eigenvalues and Drinfeld polynomials, and give a determinant formula for the dimensions directly in terms of the highest loop weights. A $21$-dimensional example illustrates the construction, including an explicit basis and a transfer-matrix identity.

papers.title: Experimentally relevant witness for non-Markovianity in discrete time crystals
papers.abstract: Discrete time crystals (DTCs) are almost always analyzed under the Born-Markov approximation, in which the environment is memoryless. We show that a reservoir with a finite correlation time $\tau_m$ leaves an exact and strikingly simple imprint on the stroboscopic dynamics of DTCs, which can be used as an experimentally relevant witness for non-Markovianity. By analyzing a post-Markovian master equation we prove that the Floquet spectrum splits into the ordinary Markovian spectrum plus a replica of the purely unitary Floquet spectrum, uniformly contracted by $e^{-T/\tau_m}$, where $T$ is the drive period. Consequently, the DTC signal decay rate becomes independent of any system parameter once $\tau_m$ exceeds the Markovian lifetime of the DTC. The measured decay, and in particular its insensitivity to tunable system parameters, thus becomes a direct read-out of the reservoir correlation time. Below this threshold the dynamics is already non-Markovian, but the memory remains hidden in the decay. We confirm this in two structurally unrelated DTCs, a collective long-range model with incoherent pumping and a disorder-free Ising chain with dephasing, where a single estimator recovers $\tau_m$. The time crystal thereby witnesses the non-Markovianity of its own environment.

papers.title: TRIAGE-CPG: A Cross-Model Study of Budgeted Static Malware Triage with Large Language Models
An Alternative to Crawlers: Scalable P2P Network Monitoring Using the Network Scale-Up Method
Convex polynomial approximation on the unit ball
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbb{B}^d$ be the closed unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^d$, $d\ge1$. We prove that, for every convex $f\in C(\mathbb{B}^d)$ and every integer $n\ge1$, there exists a polynomial $P_n$ of total degree at most $n$, convex on all of $\mathbb{R}^d$, such that $\|f-P_n\|_{C(\mathbb{B}^d)}\le c\,\omega_2(f,n^{-1};\mathbb{B}^d)$. Here $\omega_2$ is the ordinary second modulus of smoothness and $c=c_d$ depends only on $d$. In particular, we obtain the rate $O(n^{-2})$ for convex functions with uniformly bounded second derivatives.

papers.title: A description of the space with no separable quotient presented by OpenAI
papers.abstract: OpenAI recently presented a remarkable solution to the longstanding separable quotient problem in Banach space theory. The result establishes its independence from ZFC, relative to the consistency of ZFC with a measurable cardinal. Under the continuum hypothesis, the paper constructs a nonseparable Banach space $X$ with no separable infinite-dimensional quotient. The present paper offers an alternative exposition of the mechanism leading to $X$ and its properties. Our aim is to make the methods and results more accessible and to offer a clearer understanding of this exotic space.

papers.title: tsspiral: An R Package to Create Circular Versions of Time Series Plots
papers.abstract: `tsspiral` is an open-source R package that introduces a circular approach to time series visualisation using polar coordinates. We refer to this circular representation of time series data as a spiral. `tsspiral` provides a collection of `ggplot2` geometries for creating a spiral representation of time series data. In our approach, we arrange observations around a circle. Each year is represented by a circle, with the angular position corresponding to the day of the year, and successive years appear as concentric rings. This arrangement facilitates the exploration of periodicity, seasonality, and recurring temporal patterns, particularly in long time series. The package also supports temporal hierarchical visualisations to compare patterns across time scales. By bringing polar-coordinate-based visualisation into routine time series analysis, `tsspiral` offers a practical tool for exploring temporal patterns and communicating complex time-dependent structures. Rather than treating spiral plots as standalone graphics, our approach brings them into the grammar of graphics framework, enabling users to explore temporal patterns through a broader range of visual encodings.

papers.title: Neural Marked Point Processes for Health Insurance Claims
papers.abstract: Health insurance claims exhibit temporal dependence, as previous claims may provide information about the timing, type and amount of subsequent claims. Such dependencies are difficult to capture with traditional actuarial models based on aggregated claim counts. We investigate a neural marked point process in which a causal Transformer represents individual claim histories and determines type-specific conditional intensities, allowing for self-excitation and interactions between claim types. The framework also incorporates conditional severity distributions, reporting delays and stochastic medical-cost inflation. We develop a likelihood-based calibration procedure that accounts for incomplete claim reporting and evaluate the model using both simulated and empirical data. A simulation study with 10,000 insurance contracts examines the recovery of known claim dynamics, while an application to MEPS-derived medical-event data assesses predictive performance. The fitted model reproduces the main patterns in claim frequencies and severities, although some discrepancies remain in the tails of the distributions. On the MEPS data, the neural model achieves better predictive performance than two generalized linear model benchmarks in terms of claim-count deviance and expenditure discrimination.

papers.title: A scaling approach to double phase equations in $\mathbb{R}^N$
papers.abstract: We study radial solutions of the double phase equation $-\Delta_p u - \operatorname{div}(|x|^{-b}\,|\nabla u|^{q-2}\nabla u) = f(|x|,u)$ in $\mathbb{R}^N$, whose operator admits a scaling that acts on both phases simultaneously. Our first main result is a sharp description of the continuous and compact embeddings of the radial energy space into weighted Lebesgue spaces $L^s(\mathbb{R}^N;|x|^{-c})$ with an explicit characterization of their admissible regions in the $(s,c)$-plane. The two critical edges reflect the two phases: on the edge attached to the $p$-phase compactness is lost by spreading to infinity, while on the edge attached to the weighted $q$-phase it is lost by concentration at the origin. Our second main result concerns equations with one critical term on each edge. We show that bounded Palais-Smale sequences either converge or lose at least the energy $\beta^\ast = \min\{\beta_1,\beta_2\}$, where $\beta_1$ and $\beta_2$ are the explicit single-phase thresholds, and that this level is optimal when the critical terms are unweighted. Thus, the two mechanisms cannot combine to lower the compactness threshold. Combining these results with a Pohožaev identity, variational methods for scaled functionals and the Fadell-Rabinowitz cohomological index, we prove nonexistence results, obtain an unbounded sequence of eigenvalues on the scaling line and infinitely many solutions for pure power equations, and show that large superscaled and small subscaled perturbations of the doubly critical equation yield multiple solutions.

papers.title: The pinched Veronese has no Koszul filtration
papers.abstract: In this paper we prove that the pinched Veronese subalgebra $k [x^3,x^2y,xy^2,x^2z,xz^2,y^3,y^2z,yz^2,z^3] \subset k[x,y,z]$ has no Koszul filtration regardless of the field $k$, despite it being a Koszul algebra. We do this by showing that no ideal $(f,g)$ minimally generated by two linear forms can belong to a Koszul filtration. By the definition of a Koszul filtration this, in turn, implies that no Koszul filtration can exist.

papers.title: Detectability of Eccentric Intermediate Mass-Ratio Inspiral in the Decihertz Band
papers.abstract: The proposed decihertz gravitational-wave (GW) band $(\sim 10^{-2}-1\,\Hz)$ will observe the late inspiral of intermediate mass-ratio inspirals (IMRIs), binaries with mass ratios $10^2 \lesssim q \lesssim 10^4$ that assemble dynamically in dense stellar environments and are expected to retain measurable eccentricity. Search and parameter-estimation pipelines are predominantly built around circular templates, and we test this assumption. Using black-hole perturbation theory waveforms from \textsc{FastEMRIWaveforms} for a representative IMRI ($M=10^4\,\modot$, $q=100$, observed for its final $10\,\hr$), we compute fitting factors between eccentric signals and circular templates, maximizing over the template's total mass and mass ratio with a differential-evolution search, for the B-DECIGO, LGWA-Si, and IndIGO-D noise curves and a flat PSD. The mismatch grows with initial eccentricity $e_0$ and crosses the standard $3\%$ threshold at $e_0\simeq3\times10^{-2}$, well within the range allowed by the waveform model and expected from dynamical formation. The best-fitting circular templates also bias the total mass and mass ratio by several percent at $e_0=0.1$. Combining the mismatch with the signal-to-noise-dependent distinguishability criterion, we find that for a source at $1\,\mathrm{Gpc}$, eccentricities as small as $e_0\simeq5\times10^{-4}$ (B-DECIGO and IndIGO-D) and $5\times10^{-3}$ (LGWA-Si) are resolvable, one to two orders of magnitude below where detection efficiency degrades. The loss of match arises from the excitation of radial Teukolsky harmonics, which spread power into sidebands that circular templates cannot represent, and from the slower orbital decay of eccentric binaries at fixed initial semi-latus rectum. Robust detection and parameter estimation of IMRIs with DECIGO, LGWA, and IndIGO-D will require eccentric waveform models and template banks.

papers.title: RevealLO: Global-Scale FWI Including Long-Period Major-Arc Surface Wave and Multi-Orbit Body Wave Data
papers.abstract: Global full-waveform inversion (FWI) has matured significantly in recent years, but resolution in the southern hemisphere often remains limited due to sparse receiver coverage. To address this problem, we constructed RevealLO, a global-scale FWI model that updates its predecessor REVEAL by expanding the inversion time window from 1 hour to 3.5 hours. The extended time window incorporates both minor-arc ($R_1, G_1$) and major-arc ($R_2, G_2$) surface wave arrivals, as well as late-arriving multi-orbit body waves, thereby increasing azimuthal coverage beneath ocean basins and the southern hemisphere. We simulate 3-D viscoelastic wavefields using the spectral-element solver Salvus on global fourth-order cubed-sphere meshes, and update velocity structure by successively broadening the period band from 100 - 200 s to 60 - 200 s. Measurements and adjoint sources are based on time-frequency phase misfits, which are suitable for both large-amplitude surface and low-amplitude multiply-reflected body waves. For iterative optimization, we employ a mini-batch stochastic trust-region L-BFGS algorithm, followed by mesh reprojection onto the $33~s$ REVEAL baseline mesh and lowermost-mantle regularization. RevealLO preserves short-period whole-Earth body wave fits while improving azimuthal sampling and mitigating trade-offs between unmodeled azimuthal anisotropy and isotropic structure in the upper and mid mantle.

papers.title: TCBP-JOBS: GPU-Accelerated Quantum Error Correction Decoding and Noise Learning with Near-Optimal Accuracy
papers.abstract: Achieving near-optimal quantum error correction (QEC) decoding accuracy often requires computationally expensive searches that limit both large-scale simulation and real-time operation. We introduce trajectory-calibrated belief propagation (TCBP), which learns calibrated fault probabilities from BP trajectories, and jittered OSD beam search (JOBS), which uses these probabilities to guide parallel GPU searches. Across surface, color and bivariate-bicycle code memory and surgery circuits, TCBP-JOBS achieves logical error rates comparable to those of the Tesseract most-likely-error decoder at physical error rates of 0.1% to 0.4%, and up to 4.5$\times$ lower on the largest codes. Serial speedups over Tesseract's sparsified presets range from 10$\times$ to 7,400$\times$, and against unsparsified long-beam Tesseract they reach 13,000$\times$ on the bivariate-bicycle codes, at logical error rate ratios of 0.97 to 1.57. At lower physical error rates ($10^{-4}$ to $5\times10^{-4}$), rare-event splitting on the gross code shows that Tesseract is more accurate. Batched execution accelerates offline simulation for rapid, efficient exploration of large-scale QEC design spaces. For QPUs with longer logical clock cycles, our serial memory and logical-surgery experiments demonstrate accuracy comparable to Tesseract while meeting the millisecond-scale latency requirements of online feed-forward operation. Beyond memory and logic decoding, we demonstrate using TCBP-JOBS for confidence scores for postselection in memory and magic-state cultivation, enabling end-to-end color code cultivation. Together, these methods provide a GPU framework for accelerating QEC research via accurate decoding, noise estimation, and confidence assessment.

papers.title: Pharmaco-mechanical computational simulation of atherosclerotic arteries: effects of calcium channel blockers on local stress distributions
Wavelet-Energy-Driven Dynamic Patching for Time Series Forecasting
Narrowband active noise control for continuous wave operation of TESLA cavities
papers.abstract: TESLA 9-cell elliptical cavities are used in the accelerators of the European XFEL and LCLS-II. The high duty cycle upgrade study for EuXFEL and the LCLS-II-HE program target loaded quality factors of 6.10^7 and beyond, leading to RF cavity half bandwidths below 11 Hz. Stable operation in these conditions heavily relies on active RF resonance control, since the RF drive power required to maintain amplitude and phase lock would surpass amplifier max ratings if detuning is not compensated. To counteract mechanical vibrations, e.g. introduced by rotational machines in the proximity of the accelerating modules, a dedicated narrowband active noise control algorithm was introduced in previous work. This proceeding presents CPU based implementations and latest test results obtained at the Cryomodule Test Bench (CMTB) at DESY and LCLS-II at SLAC, where the stable operation gradient of a cavity could be increased from 9 to 15 MV/m without violating RF control limits.

papers.title: Non-thermal emission from molecular clouds illuminated by continuous cosmic-ray accelerators: application to the stellar cluster W43
papers.abstract: Context: Cosmic rays escaping from their accelerators produce gamma-ray emission through interactions with ambient gas. While the scenario of an impulsive injection of cosmic rays has been extensively studied, that of a continuous injection in time has received comparatively less attention. The latter scenario is particularly relevant for stellar clusters, which may contribute to a non-negligible fraction of Galactic cosmic rays. Aims: We intend to characterize the excesses of cosmic rays around their accelerators and to assess the detectability of the gamma-ray emission resulting from the interactions of cosmic rays in nearby molecular clouds. We focus in particular on star clusters and seek to apply these considerations to the case of W43. Methods: We derive analytical estimates for the cosmic ray excess around sources as a function of source properties and transport parameters. We also evaluate under which conditions the predicted gamma-ray emission from illuminated molecular clouds can be detected by current and future instruments. We then apply these results to explain the gamma-ray emission from the the W43 region. Results: We find that producing detectable gamma-ray emission from molecular clouds illuminated by cosmic rays escaping from star clusters generally requires either suppressed diffusion relative to the Galactic value or anisotropic diffusion, with the latter scenario requiring a smaller global energetic. We applied this approach to the case of W43 and by fitting its gamma-ray emission we were able to constrain the underlying CR transport parameters.

papers.title: Continuous Kakeya type problems with special points that sweep much more area than the rest
papers.abstract: For any $\varepsilon>0$ we construct a continuous motion of a line segment in the plane, such that the center point of the line segment traverses a given bounded set except for a subset of area less than $\varepsilon$, while the rest of the line segment sweeps only an area less than $\varepsilon$. We further show that a circle with a pair of antipodal points removed has the Strong Kakeya Property in the plane: that is, given any two copies of such a punctured circle, we can continuously move one to the other, while staying in a set of arbitrarily small Lebesgue measure. We give a full characterization of those subsets of a great circle that have this property on the sphere. We also show how the first mentioned result can be applied to obtain discontinuity results about the area swept by continuously moving objects.

Stability manifolds and resolutions of singularities
papers.abstract: In this article, we study descent and lifting of Bridgeland stability conditions along Verdier quotients. We give a torsion-pair criterion for lifting every stability condition on the quotient to a weak stability condition with a prescribed heart on the null category. When this criterion holds for every heart on the null category, the space of weak stability conditions with this massless subcategory is homeomorphic to the product of the stability space of the quotient and the discrete set of hearts of bounded $t$-structures on the null category. We apply these results to contractions of relative dimension one, resolutions of nodal varieties, and blowups of smooth projective varieties along smooth centers. For projective surfaces with ADE singularities, we identify the discrete factor through a simply transitive braid group action. When the minimal resolution is a K3 surface, every weak stability condition obtained by lifting a numerical stability condition from the singular surface is the limit of a continuous, quasi-convergent family of numerical Bridgeland stability conditions on the resolution with the same heart.

papers.title: Lifting asymptotic symmetries from metric to tetrad formulation
papers.abstract: Metric solution spaces defined by gauge and boundary conditions are associated with a residual symmetry algebra, consisting of the diffeomorphism generators whose action preserves these conditions. Describing a metric solution space in terms of tetrad variables adds a local Lorentz freedom. When part of this freedom is fixed by additional tetrad gauge and boundary conditions, metric residual symmetries must be supplemented by compensating Lorentz transformations. If a residual Lorentz freedom remains, there is an ambiguity in these compensating transformations. The most direct choices generally fail to realize the metric residual symmetry algebra as a subalgebra of the tetrad one, because of a field-dependent cocycle. We show that a reference tetrad, that is a section of the tetrad solution space seen as a principal bundle over the metric one, always provides a lift free of this cocycle, so that the tetrad residual symmetry algebra is the semi-direct sum of the metric one and the ideal of field-dependent residual Lorentz transformations. The construction is independent of the gauge conditions, of the residual group, of the first-order Lagrangian, and reduces to the Kosmann lift on metric isometry generators. We illustrate it on a Weyl BMS-type solution space with time-dependent boundary metric, described in tetrad variables with a residual U(1) Lorentz freedom, for which the cocycle of a naive lift is computed and then explicitly removed.

Radiofrequency disorientation in migratory birds: radical pairs or a separate sensory system?
papers.abstract: Alongside other directional cues, migratory songbirds use the Earth's magnetic field to help them navigate the hundreds or thousands of kilometres between their breeding and over-wintering sites. If it seems surprising that an animal can extract information from a magnetic field a hundred times weaker than a small refrigerator magnet, it should be astounding that this ability can be disrupted by radiofrequency magnetic fields thousands of times weaker still. Magnetic fields with strengths between 1 and 100 nT and frequencies between 0.1 and 100 MHz have been found to prevent captive night-migratory songbirds from orienting in the geomagnetic field (25-65 microtesla, depending on geographic location). Remarkably, the frequency dependence of this disruption agrees closely with predictions for radical pairs in cryptochrome (the leading hypothesis for the mechanism of the avian magnetic compass), whereas the extraordinarily weak fields that cause disorientation are difficult to reconcile with conventional radical-pair theory. This perspective examines the evidence for radiofrequency-induced disorientation and its relationship to the cryptochrome hypothesis. It concludes by considering a suggestion that birds may possess a distinct radiofrequency-sensitive system based on electromagnetic induction.

Generalized transverse-momentum-dependent parton distributions of a photon and orbital angular momentum
papers.abstract: The coefficients of generalized transverse-momentum-dependent distributions (GTMDs) that encode the canonical fermion orbital angular momentum and spin--orbit correlation do not contribute to the direct transverse-momentum-dependent (TMD) and generalized-parton-distribution (GPD) projections. We present, to our knowledge, the first explicit calculation of the leading-twist, time-even, chiral-even fermion GTMDs of an on-shell real photon at zero skewness and order $\alpha$. The coefficients $\mathcal{F}_A$ and $\mathcal{G}_A$, which multiply the $k_\perp\times\Delta_\perp$ structure, yield the fermion orbital angular momentum $\ell_z^f$ and spin--orbit correlation $\mathcal{C}_z^f$. For photon helicity $+1$, both are obtained in closed form in the leading fermion--antifermion sector and obey $\mathcal{C}_z^f=-\ell_z^f/2$ for a common transverse regulator independent of $x$, because the channel with the active fermion's spin anti-aligned with its orbital motion carries three times the integrated weight of the aligned channel. The projections reproduce the known photon TMDs and leading-logarithmic photon-to-fermion kernels, and energy-momentum-tensor overlaps reproduce the known one-loop photon gravitational form factors $F_1$, $F_2$, and $F_3$. Our result provides an analytic benchmark for fermionic orbital and spin--orbit structure in the real photon.

Third-body-corrected Two-Pion Femtoscopic Correlations in Au+Au Collisions at High Baryon Density
papers.abstract: Identical charged pion femtoscopy provides a sensitive probe of the space-time structure of particle-emitting sources in heavy-ion collisions. At high baryon density, the differences between $\pi^+\pi^+$ and $\pi^-\pi^-$ Hanbury Brown--Twiss (HBT) radii may originate from both the third-body Coulomb effect and the initial-state isospin asymmetry. Since the latter is related to the equation of state (EoS) of asymmetric nuclear matter, separating these two effects is essential. In these proceedings, we present the measurements of identical charged pion correlations in Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=3.0$, 3.2, 3.5, 3.9, 4.5, and 7.7 GeV collected by the STAR experiment. A correction procedure is developed to remove the residual third-body Coulomb effect. After correction, the extracted HBT radii of $\pi^+\pi^+$ and $\pi^-\pi^-$ become consistent within uncertainties. The results indicate that the observed charge dependence is dominated by the third-body Coulomb effect, while any remaining contribution from the initial-state isospin asymmetry to the relative HBT radius difference, $(R_{\pi^-}-R_{\pi^+})/R_{\pi^+}$, is constrained to be less than 5\% at the 95\% confidence level.

papers.title: PLECTA: Overlap-aware instance segmentation of dense strand networks from binary masks
papers.abstract: Many materials and tissues, including carbon-nanotube sheets, collagen and paper, comprise overlapping strands whose arrangement influences their effective properties. Measuring this geometry from micrographs requires individual strands to be traced through crossings and signal gaps, which merge distinct strands or split one strand into disconnected fragments. We present PLECTA (from Latin plecta, a braid), a deterministic method that segments individual strands using only a binary image whose foreground pixels mark strand centrelines. At each junction, PLECTA selects which strand segments continue into one another while allowing segments to terminate. It formulates this decision as an exact maximum-weight partial-matching problem, with an explicit penalty for unpaired segments and no restriction on the number of segments entering a junction. The output permits crossing pixels to belong to multiple strands. On synthetic scenes, PLECTA resolved strand identities more accurately than three released alternatives at every density tested. The same ranking held on an independently published generator run at its own settings. A separate stage uses the corresponding greyscale micrograph to estimate which strand lies on top at each crossing. The complete workflow is demonstrated on scanning electron micrographs of carbon nanotube sheets, from raw images to individual strand instances with estimated crossing order, without manual annotations for training or as pipeline inputs.

papers.title: How to calculate temperature and energy in Molecular Dynamics
papers.abstract: Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulation of the dynamics of classical objects has become incredibly popular in natural sciences since the method was developed in the sixties. A conservative estimate is that it involves many hundreds of thousands of scientific articles and all subdisciplines of natural sciences. The earliest MD simulations also introduced a simple time-symmetric expression for the momentum and velocity, which has since been used uncritically in almost all MD simulations. The expression is incorrect and can lead to significant errors. But it is straightforward to replace the expression with the correct one, and the motive of the article is to draw attention to how to calculate velocity, kinetic energy, temperature, and energy in an MD simulation correctly. Newton's algorithm of the discrete dynamics has the same quality as his analytical dynamics, and Newton's discrete dynamics conserves the energy exactly. That is the second motive for the article, namely to show that conservation of energy in a conservative system is only obtained by the correct expressions for the velocity and kinetic energy.

papers.title: A database of optical and thermal-radiative behaviour of materials under solar radiation
papers.abstract: Solar-matter interactions are important in many scientific and engineering applications. Modeling them needs consistent optical and thermal-radiative properties over the full solar spectrum. Here we present SpaderOptics, a database for 21 materials: metals, oxides, semiconductors, polymers, ceramics, and carbon. It compiles wavelength-dependent refractive indices and extinction coefficients from the literature. Each literature source is kept separate, together with its original conditions. One physics-based calculation chain turns these data into reflectivity, transmissivity, absorptivity, and emissivity for different incidence angles, slab thicknesses, and temperatures. Combined with the Air Mass Zero (AM0) solar spectrum, the properties give absorbed, reflected, and transmitted solar flux for concentrated sunlight. Equilibrium temperatures are given for both a theoretical lumped body and for a slab body, in which thermal conduction is considered. All data are limited to the solid state, up to a material-specific upper temperature limit. Currently, the database applies to extraterrestrial (AM0) sunlight only. A graphical App is also provided for exploring and visualizing the database.

papers.title: Numerical range of finite perturbations of a 2-periodic weighted shift
papers.abstract: In this note, we consider a weighted shift operator of weight sequence which is a finite perturbation of a 2-periodic weighted shift. We characterise the equality of the closure of its numerical range and its essential numerical range. We end up with some applications and comments.

papers.title: Pulsar Timing Correlations Induced by Stochastic Spin-2 Ultralight Dark Matter
papers.abstract: Ultralight dark matter (ULDM) can generate time-dependent gravitational perturbations, providing a potential signal for pulsar timing arrays (PTAs). In Galactic halos, the velocity dispersion of ULDM gives rise to finite spatial coherence, which influences the correlations between pulsar timing signals. In this work, we derive the timing-residual cross-correlations induced by rapid metric oscillations of spin-2 ULDM, allowing for general polarization statistics. Under equipartition among the five polarization modes, the intrinsic angular kernel contains monopole and quadrupole components and exhibits an angular profile closely resembling that of spin-1 ULDM, suggesting a potential degeneracy between the two ULDM candidates in PTA observations.

papers.title: Mono-Z Signatures of Vector Dark Matter Detection at Future Electron-Positron Colliders: FCC-ee and ILC
papers.abstract: We investigate the mono-$Z$ signature of a vector dark matter (VDM) model at future electron-positron colliders. In this model, a stable vector boson, arising from an extended $U(1)$ gauge symmetry, serves as a viable DM candidate that interacts with the Standard Model (SM) through a Higgs portal. We perform a detailed cut-based analysis for the mono-$Z$ channel at the FCC-ee (with $\sqrt{s}=240$ and $365$ GeV) and the ILC (with $\sqrt{s}=1$ TeV), considering both leptonic and hadronic decays of the $Z$ boson. Signal significances are evaluated for benchmark points using fast event simulation with MadGraph5, PYTHIA8, and Delphes3. Our results demonstrate that future $e^+e^-$ colliders provide excellent sensitivity to Higgs-portal VDM, with the ILC's beam polarization offering an additional handle to suppress SM backgrounds. This study highlights the potential of lepton colliders in probing DM interactions.
