Certified Nash Equilibrium Learning for Nonzero-Sum Jump-Diffusion Games: Policy Iteration and Off-Policy Q-Learning
papers.abstract: This paper establishes two model-free reinforcement learning methods for infinite-horizon N-player linear-quadratic nonzero-sum stochastic differential games whose drift, Brownian diffusion, and Poisson jump amplitudes depend on all players' controls. Control dependence in the diffusion and jump terms couples the players' simultaneous feedback updates. A verifiable certificate ensures that the partially model-free policy iteration map is contractive on an invariant closed ball centered at an admissible initial feedback profile. All feedback iterates are mean-square stabilizing, and the algorithm achieves local geometric convergence of feedback gains and value matrices to those associated with a closed-loop Nash equilibrium. The term certified refers to a verifiable convergence certificate that guarantees mean-square stability of all policy iterates and local geometric convergence to a closed-loop Nash equilibrium. To implement the policy updates from data, the off-policy Q-learning algorithm reuses the same behavior-policy data across iterations without requiring the system coefficients or jump intensity. Under quantitative persistence of excitation and a common initialization, exact population regression reproduces the policy-iteration sequence. The same local convergence guarantee therefore applies to off-policy Q-learning at the population level. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the two proposed algorithms.

papers.title: Soft momentum expansion about the Stokes topological limit of Bogoliubov coefficients
papers.abstract: It is known that particle production in time-dependent cosmological backgrounds can be computed using the Stokes phenomena occurring in Bogoliubov transformations with an analytically continued time coordinate. We analytically compute the soft momentum expansion of the particle production amplitude about the Stokes topological limit that was recently discovered in this context. The computational technique relies on an exponentially improved asymptotic expansion that involves automorphisms in the space of functions defined partly by the angular step function intrinsic to the Stokes topological sectors. We combine this with special discrete symmetries tied to the time dependence of the dispersion relation $\omega_k^2(z) = C(k) + A z^n$ for even $n$ to explicitly compute the leading momentum dependence of the amplitude which is nonperturbative in $A$. We also use this result to give a semi-analytic estimate of the number density of particles in this class of scenarios.

papers.title: SCOPE: A Physical Execution Latency-Guided Quantum Circuit Compilation Framework
Singular Global Compactness for Logarithmically Coupled \(p\)-Laplacian Systems
papers.abstract: We establish global compactness for logarithmically coupled p-Laplacian systems on RN, where p=N>4 and bounded positive potentials converge to positive constants at infinity. The finite-energy domain need not be closed under subtraction, obstructing direct profile subtraction. We develop a scalar localisation method using slowly expanding cutoffs and residual commutator estimates uniform in the regularisation parameter. As the regularisation vanishes, residual Palais-Smale sequences split into a solution of the original system and finitely many separating autonomous profiles, with a strongly vanishing remainder and splitting of the logarithmic densities. A converse construction characterises all levels of compactness failure. Applications include convergence of ground-state levels, a compactness-escape alternative for minimising sequences, and a directional response formula for the ground-state energy.

Variance-adaptive confidence regions for fixed-benchmark binomial mixtures, with application to LLM evaluation
papers.abstract: We construct confidence intervals for linear functionals $\theta(F_m)=\int h\,dF_m$ of the empirical law $F_m$ of success probabilities $p_1,\dots,p_m$, from independent counts $c_i\sim\mathrm{Bin}(n,p_i)$, as for a language model run $n$ times per problem. Coverage is at least $1-\alpha$ for every $n$, $m$ and fixed $(p_i)$, simultaneously for all bounded $h$. The variance-adaptive (VA) region tests each candidate mixing law with the conditional variance of the tail counts it implies. This variance is linear in the law, so the region is a linear program, and cell envelopes keep it valid off-grid. Regions calibrated for iid sampling target a super-population law and are conservative for $\theta(F_m)$. With all $n$ tail counts, fixed $n$, continuous $h$ and a grid refined as $m\to\infty$, the identification part of VA's width is first-order worst-case optimal, as for any localization with the same index set. Under a rule fixed before the main comparator runs, VA was narrower than a two-stage plug-in band at every $n$ (median width ratio 0.60 at $n=128$), but not than the asymptotic, pointwise AMARI interval at $n=128$; on real rollout pools it was wider than both pointwise and Bonferroni-adjusted AMARI at $n\le128$. For $P(p>0)$ and pass@$k$ with $k\gg n$ the data support only lower bounds.

Belavin--Drinfeld bivectors and Poisson deformations
papers.abstract: We study Belavin--Drinfeld Poisson bivectors $\pi_{(\bar{\mathbf{\Gamma}}^r,\bar{\mathbf{\Gamma}}^c)}$ on $\operatorname{Mat}_{n\times m}(\mathbb{C})$ from the perspective of Poisson deformation theory. We prove that the log-canonical part $\pi_0$ of $\pi_{(\bar{\mathbf{\Gamma}}^r,\bar{\mathbf{\Gamma}}^c)}$ is $\mathbb{T}_{(\mathbf{\Gamma}^r,\mathbf{\Gamma}^c)}$-log-symplectic if and only if the pair $(\mathbf{\Gamma}^r,\mathbf{\Gamma}^c)$ of Belavin--Drinfeld triples is aperiodic. In this case, we show that $\pi_{(\bar{\mathbf{\Gamma}}^r,\bar{\mathbf{\Gamma}}^c)}$ is a maximal $\mathbb{T}_{(\mathbf{\Gamma}^r,\mathbf{\Gamma}^c)}$-invariant Poisson deformation of $\pi_0$, and we construct a $\mathbb{T}_{(\mathbf{\Gamma}^r,\mathbf{\Gamma}^c)}$-equivariant Poisson birational map between $(\operatorname{Mat}_{n\times m},\pi_0)$ and $(\operatorname{Mat}_{n\times m},\pi_{(\bar{\mathbf{\Gamma}}^r,\bar{\mathbf{\Gamma}}^c)})$.

Analytic Tools and Weighted Composition Operators on Paley--Wiener Spaces
papers.abstract: We develop a scale-explicit analytic framework for operator-theoretic problems on the Paley--Wiener spaces $B_\sigma^p$, $\sigma>0$, throughout the full range $0<p\leq\infty$. Using localized Paley--Wiener packets, we obtain sharp-order point-evaluation estimates, quantitative separation of distinct point-evaluation functionals, sampling estimates, and Carleson measure characterizations. As a principal application, we develop a comprehensive theory of weighted composition operators $W_{\psi,\varphi}:B_\sigma^p\to B_\tau^q$, $0<p,q\leq\infty$, $\sigma,\tau>0$. Boundedness forces every nonconstant symbol to be affine with real slope. A sharp dichotomy appears: when $p\leq q$, the weight is governed by the residual bandwidth $\tau-\sigma|a|$; when $q<p$, the weight must also supply the missing integrability, with exponent $pq/(p-q)$, and boundedness coincides with compactness. We also obtain compactness criteria and essential-norm estimates, characterize differences of weighted composition operators via a no-cancellation principle for distinct symbols, and determine the connected and path-connected components of the corresponding operator spaces.

Quasi-locality and weak containment for Roe algebras
papers.abstract: We establish two characterisations of Property A for discrete metric spaces of bounded geometry. Such a space has Property A if and only if its Roe algebra coincides with its quasi-local algebra, and if and only if the canonical map from its maximal Roe algebra to its reduced Roe algebra is injective. Both characterisations hold in the uniform and ordinary Roe settings. We also prove, without assuming Property A, that strong quasi-locality is equivalent to norm approximability by finite-propagation operators. In particular, the strongly quasi-local algebra always coincides with the Roe algebra. As applications, we show that a discrete group is exact whenever its full group $C^*$-algebra has the local lifting property, and that the maximal injective crossed-product functor agrees with the reduced crossed-product functor precisely for exact discrete groups.

papers.title: Dimension-free spectral laws and the risk of spectral filters
papers.abstract: Spectral properties of the sample covariance are key to modern machine learning with high-dimensional data. Random matrix theory (RMT) supplies powerful tools; however, most classical results assume proportional asymptotics, where $d/n$ tends to a finite limit. In functional data analysis and kernel methods, a fixed infinite-dimensional Hilbert space is often the more natural setting for the observations, beyond the scope of proportional asymptotics. This calls for a dimension-free spectral theory for i.i.d. observations $\boldsymbol{x}_1, \dots, \boldsymbol{x}_n$ in a Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$ with trace-class population covariance $\Sigma$. Building on the dimension-free ridge regression analysis of Cheng and Montanari (2024), we establish two deterministic equivalents with explicit nonasymptotic error bounds. The first approximates the empirical spectral law $\widehat{\mu}_n$ of the sample Gram matrix by a deterministic law $\mu_n$. The second characterizes the conditional prediction risk of analytic spectral filters in linear regression. Previous sharp approximations to prediction risk in this setting have focused on ridge regression and closely-related problems. Our analysis covers a broader class of filters at the bulk scale, with an explicit user-friendly spectral stability condition to check. We apply our theory to power and critical spectral laws, and we recover the proportional regime. For prediction, we study (negative) ridge estimators, iterated ridge, and gradient flow. Mathematically, building on the idea of stochastic interpolation, we construct a deterministic backward path to interpolate the spectral parameter. The resulting bounds on resolvent and mixed-resolvent traces give mesoscopic approximations to the spectral law within the bulk and, by Cauchy's formula, deterministic equivalents for the prediction variance and squared bias of analytic spectral filters.

papers.title: QuantileGS: Quantile-Based Conformal Bounds on RGB Rendering Errors for Novel View Synthesis with 3D Gaussian Splatting
Phenomenology of neutrino mass ordering synergies in reactor, accelerator, and atmospheric neutrino experiments, and the role of the detector response
papers.abstract: The neutrino mass ordering is one of the main open questions of neutrino physics, addressed by reactor, accelerator, and atmospheric experiments and by their combination. When the data are fitted under the wrong ordering, each experiment returns its own value of $\Delta m^2_{31}$, its wrong-ordering solution. We show that this solution is a weighted average of the values preferred by the individual bins of the measured event spectra, in reconstructed energy and, for atmospheric neutrinos, also zenith angle, with weights set by their statistical precision. Both the values and the weights depend on the detector response. In the plane of $\Delta m^2_{31}$ fitted under the two orderings, the solutions lie on lines of slope close to $-1$, so that each experiment is described by one intercept. The weighted bin average extends the mass ordering sum rule to any oscillation experiment, including atmospheric neutrinos in Earth matter. It recovers the known closed forms for short-baseline reactors and for accelerators in vacuum, and for JUNO it equals a closed form evaluated at one effective energy, which depends on the energy resolution. Above the MSW resonance the frequency of atmospheric $\nu_\mu$ disappearance becomes nearly independent of $\delta_{CP}$, and the $\nu_\mu$ disappearance solution moves mainly with $\theta_{23}$. The atmospheric intercept depends on the energy and direction resolutions, the energy window, and the event classes, and differs between detectors. The synergy of two experiments is determined by the separation of their intercepts relative to their precisions on $|\Delta m^2_{31}|$. With JUNO, this separation depends strongly on $\delta_{CP}$ for an accelerator and is nearly independent of $\delta_{CP}$ and $\theta_{23}$ for IceCube DeepCore using all channels.

Noise and quasi-periodic oscillations in black hole accretion flows
papers.abstract: Temporal fluctuations of the viscosity parameter at different radii in an accretion flow are known to give rise to variability in the accretion rate onto the black hole. The power spectrum of accretion-rate fluctuations is expected to exhibit a broad-band power-law dependence on frequency (e.g., flicker noise). We show that viscosity fluctuations can also generate quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) in the power spectrum. In our model, QPOs are caused by reflection of accretion-rate fluctuations at the outer radius of the accretion flow and arise near the low-frequency break of the power spectrum, which corresponds to the inverse viscous timescale at the outer radius. These QPOs occur in geometrically thick advection-dominated accretion flows but are absent in geometrically thin cooling-dominated flows.

papers.title: All-sky spectroscopic survey of bright δ Scuti stars from TESS Projected rotational velocities and pulsation characteristics
papers.abstract:
Context. The second most numerous class of pulsating stars -- $\delta$ Scuti ($\delta$ Sct) -- lack a homogeneous, large-scale spectroscopic sample in the Kepler and TESS era, limiting our understanding of how rotation shapes stellar pulsations. Aims. We analyse projected rotational velocities ($v \sin i$) from high-resolution spectroscopy alongside 2-minute TESS photometry to establish empirical links between stellar rotation and pulsation parameters. Methods. Combining observations from three high-resolution échelle spectrographs with two spectral libraries, we assemble an all-sky sample of 262 $\delta$ Sct stars ($R = 25\,000$ to $115\,000$). We derive $v \sin i$ via three independent methods and extract pulsation frequencies and amplitudes from TESS light curves. Results. The $v \sin i$ distribution is unimodal, with a mean of $120.3	ext{ km s}^{-1}$ and peak probability at $113.8	ext{ km s}^{-1}$. Minimum ($
u_{m min}$), dominant ($
u_{m dom}$), amplitude-weighted ($
u_{m AW}$), and power-weighted ($
u_{m PW}$) frequencies decrease with $v \sin i / v_{m crit}$, whereas maximum frequency ($
u_{m max}$) does not. Fast rotators show a narrower range of photometric and pulsation amplitudes than slow rotators, and their lower mean stellar density ($ ar{ho}$) cannot fully explain the frequency decrease. Calibrating Gaia's $v_{m broad}$ against our measurements removes its systematic offset, enabling use across larger $\delta$ Sct samples. Multi-spectrum comparisons reveal method discrepancies mainly for fast rotators ($v \sin i > 200	ext{ km s}^{-1}$) and inter-spectrograph offsets up to $20	ext{ km s}^{-1}$. Conclusions. We present the largest homogeneous high-resolution $v \sin i$ sample for bright $\delta$ Sct stars in the TESS era, showing that $v \sin i$ measurements in pulsating stars require careful treatment across instruments and velocity regimes.

papers.title: A Density Functional Tight Binding Model for Rapid Screening of Spin-Orbit-Coupling-Driven Topological Properties in Bismuth
papers.abstract: We present a transferable Density Functional Tight Binding (DFTB) model for bismuth with explicit spin-orbit coupling that enables exploration of the structural degrees of freedom governing topological properties with minimal computational resources. We have used our DFTB model to run high-throughput calculations at a scale that would be significantly more expensive with standard Kohn-Sham Density Functional Theory (DFT) to determine a strain-buckling map of electronic and topological properties for bismuthene, where we identify regions of band gap closure and band inversion as a function of structural parameters. We show that our approach yields an accurate band structure for the rhombohedral phase, where small band gaps exist at or near time-reversal-invariant momentum (TRIM) points. We then demonstrate the transferability of our model to bismuth properties not included in our training data through determination of the rhombohedral phase phonon density of states and energetic ordering of additional bismuth solid phases. Finally, we have validated our topological predictions through comparison to DFT results for the optimized bilayer geometries, a band inversion order parameter, and the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ invariant as a function of monolayer unit cell length. Our efforts establish DFTB as a rigorous approach for topological characterization while yielding approximately three orders of magnitude increase in computational efficiency relative to DFT. Our model can thus serve as a computational tool for topological materials discovery by enabling large-scale computational screening to address the potentially complex relationship between physical-chemical properties and the resulting topological classification.

papers.title: Slower but Faster: When Self-Organized Traffic Flows Beat Traffic Signal Control
A boson representation of the electronic structure calculation based on the quantum Krylov subspace algorithm
papers.abstract: Quantum calculations are expected to broaden the range of strongly correlated phenomena in solids accessible to first-principles calculations. The quantum Krylov diagonalization method, or in a broader sense, the quantum subspace expansion method (QSE) offers an advantage over other variational methods in terms of numerical stability. In this work, we propose a boson representation of electronic systems with the aim of reducing QSE quantum circuit depth, where electron-hole pair bosons serve as the fundamental degrees of freedom. We benchmark the boson representation in comparison with a corresponding fermionic QSE and CCSD for an equidistant and a dimerized configuration of a periodic hydrogen chain \ce{(H2)_n}. Despite the drastic approximation we reveal the boson QSE scheme provides practically useful accuracy in the ground state energy. Our results support its applicability to realistic quasi-two- and three-dimensional electronic systems.

papers.title: Anytime-Valid PAC-Bayes Certificates for Adaptive Test-Time Scaling
How Developer Personality Shapes the Use of AI Coding Assistants
What kind of quantum advantage is this?
papers.abstract: Quantum advantage encompasses fundamentally different claims, from resource reductions to exponential separations in sample complexity. Evaluating these claims requires distinguishing how an algorithm achieves an advantage from what is necessary for the separation and how strongly it is supported against classical alternatives. We propose a multi-label taxonomy that makes these distinctions explicit, classifying structural, interference, and coherent mechanisms while separately recording their necessity and the evidence for the classical comparison. Coherent mechanisms are further divided into memory and output, reflecting distinct restrictions on quantum information processing. A two-part entanglement-breaking test distinguishes loss of information from loss of algorithmic efficiency. The hidden subgroup problem illustrates the distinction: among the cases examined, cross-copy coherence is information-theoretically necessary only for the symmetric group. We present this as a diagnostic methodology rather than a theory of quantum advantage: for a new claim, it identifies the relevant adversary, separates the mechanisms a protocol uses from those shown to be necessary, and records the strength of the evidence and the quality of the advantage separately.

papers.title: Recursive Spectral Graph Partitioning Coding for Index Assignment in Semantic Communications
Finite presentations for Thompson monoids
papers.abstract: Thompson's group $V$ was introduced in 1965 as one of the first examples of an infinite finitely presented simple group. The Higman-Thompson groups $V_{k, r}$ naturally generalize $V$; they exhibit many of the same interesting properties and have been extensively studied in the literature. Monoid theoretic analogues $TV_{k, r}$, $PTV_{k, r}$, and $IV_{k, r}$ of the Higman-Thompson groups were first considered by Thompson, and published many years later in work of Birget. The monoid theoretic analogue of the symmetric group is the full transformation monoid, in that every monoid is isomorphic to a submonoid of some full transformation monoid. The analogous role for inverse monoids is played by the symmetric inverse monoid. Birget's three monoids $TV_{k, r}$, $PTV_{k, r}$, and $IV_{k, r}$ are to $V_{n, r}$ what the full, and partial transformation monoids, and the symmetric inverse monoid are to the symmetric group. The second author and De Witt recently showed that $TV_{k, r}$ is finitely presented. In this paper we show that the remaining two monoids $PTV_{k, r}$ and $IV_{k, r}$ are also finitely presented.

papers.title: Specifying & Verifying Quantum Error-Correcting Codes
Language-model agents' beliefs can be manipulated via truthful evidence in open channel
Infinite projections and failure of pure infiniteness in simple nuclear $C^*$-algebras
papers.abstract: We construct a separable, unital, simple, nuclear $C^*$-algebra in the UCT class such that every nonzero projection in its stabilization is infinite, while it contains a nonzero projectionless hereditary subalgebra. The construction gives a negative answer to the question whether infiniteness of all nonzero projections in a unital simple nuclear $C^*$-algebra implies pure infiniteness.

papers.title: A Study on Performance Enhancement of a Webcam-Based Real-Time Eye-Tracking System
A Generative AI-Driven Architecture for Whole-Home Intelligent Services: Edge Models, Memory Management, and Household Applications
Weak error of approximation of a Lévy-type process using dynamic cutting
papers.abstract: In this note we consider, on one hand, the implementation of the parametrix method for estimation of the distance between functionals $\Ee^x f(X_t)$ and $\Ee^x f(\widetilde X_t)$ of two Lévy-type processes $X$ and $\tilde X$. On the other hand, we estimate the weak error appearing by substituting small jumps by a (time-inhomogeneous) diffusion. Both methods rely on the time-dependent cutting procedure, designed to remove small jumps in a time-dependent way.

papers.title: Shrink Responsibly: Empirical Bayes in Economics
papers.abstract: Empirical researchers are often interested in the relative causal impact of individuals or institutions such as teachers, schools, hospitals, or neighborhoods. Regression-based estimates of such unit-specific parameters are often noisy; empirical Bayes (eB) methods can help isolate the signal from the estimation noise. This article provides an overview of eB methodology, showing how eB shrinkage can improve compound decisions---such as selecting individuals with the highest causal impacts---even when the working model motivating the shrinkage is misspecified. Not all analyses benefit from eB shrinkage, however, and we discuss which types of causal summaries are best estimated directly and how to do so robustly. We illustrate practical takeaways with a running analysis of public elementary and middle school value-added.

papers.title: Investigating the Benefit of Transfer Learning from the Locus Coeruleus for Substantia Nigra Pars Compacta Segmentation
Immersive virtual reality in learning physics: a systematic review of opportunities and challenges
papers.abstract: Immersive virtual reality (IVR) can heighten presence and enable active, embodied interaction in realistic 3D environments, which has been associated with potential benefits in physics education. This article presents a comprehensive review of IVR implementation in physics education at both school and university levels. The analysis included 34 studies indexed in Scopus and ERIC, published between 1 January 2018 and 1 June 2025. Methodologically, this review followed a preferred reporting items for systematic reviews and meta-analyses approach. IVR implementations for physics learning were assessed, topic-aligned activity types were summarized, and associated opportunities and challenges were documented. Findings indicate that IVR can support physics learning by providing complementary visualizations, optimizing cognitive load, enabling haptic learning, saving time, and fostering collaborative inquiry. Conversely, the most frequent potential IVR challenges include discomfort, unreliable interaction, orchestration issues, relatively high costs, and significant extraneous cognitive load.

papers.title: Low-energy states of a Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain connected perpendicularly to a metallic lead
papers.abstract: Recently, Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chains (SSHCs) coupled to metallic leads have attracted attention. In particular Mart\'ınez {\it et al.} [Phys. Rev. Res. {\bf 8}, 043118 (2026)] studied a topological SSHC connected at one of its ends perpendicularly to a metallic lead modeled by a tight-binding chain. Here, we extend their results by incorporating the finite-size splitting of the end modes of the isolated SSHC, which are determined analytically with high accuracy. We also derive simple analytical expressions, valid in the low-energy regime, for the zero-temperature conductance through the lead and the relevant spectral densities. We find that, when the chemical potential coincides with that of the half-filled SSHC, the conductance reaches its maximum value, equal to that of the lead in the absence of the SSHC. By contrast, the conductance vanishes when the chemical potential is shifted by an amount equal to half the end-mode splitting.

papers.title: Weak lensing data beyond flexion
papers.abstract: In weak lensing, shear and convergence are well studied and have provided a wealth of information about the distribution of matter in the universe. More recently, flexion -- the next term in the multipole expansion of the lensing potential, responsible for the characteristic banana-shaped distortion of lensed images -- has been shown to provide additional constraints on the mass distribution of lensing systems, particularly for galaxy clusters. Here we investigate whether weak-lensing information beyond flexion is similarly useful for lens-mass reconstruction. Using the roulette-amplitude formalism, we construct synthetic datasets for a single SIE lens and for SIE and SIS cluster lenses, with and without simulated Gaussian noise, and perform a least-squares reconstruction of the lens parameters using amplitudes truncated at third (flexion), fourth, and fifth order. As a proof of concept, we find that higher-order amplitudes do provide additional, useful information: the benefit is modest for a single lens, where flexion already constrains most parameters, but becomes substantial for cluster lenses, where the rotation and ellipticity are otherwise poorly recovered. The improvement is most pronounced in the presence of noise, where third-order reconstruction can become unreliable while higher-order amplitudes restore much of the lost accuracy. These results suggest that, as weak-lensing surveys grow in depth and precision, data beyond flexion could meaningfully improve mass reconstruction for the most complex and noisiest lensing systems, motivating further work using observational rather than synthetic data.

papers.title: Simultaneous reconstruction of an obstacle and its wavenumber for the Helmholtz equation: a robust optimization approach
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose a method to recover simultaneously the shape and wavenumber of an object from noisy radar or sonar measurements. The physical problem is modeled in a bounded domain with the Helmholtz equation and appropriate transmission conditions. The approach relies on a Kohn-Vogelius formulation of the inverse problem and uses Nesterov's accelerated gradient descent combined with shape optimization techniques. To address the robustness of the method with respect to measurement noise, we are looking to minimize a convex combination of the expected value and variance, which we achieve by using a Karhunen-Lo{è}ve expansion. The effectiveness of the approach is demonstrated through twodimensional numerical experiments.

papers.title: Moiré Excitons in a Chern Ferromagnet
papers.abstract: Recent experiments have established excitonic optical resonances as powerful probes and control knobs of moiré Chern ferromagnets. However, the microscopic nature of excitons formed on such interaction-driven, time-reversal-symmetry-broken ground states remains largely unexplored. In this paper, using a Gutzwiller plus Bethe-Salpeter equation framework, we investigate twisted bilayer MoTe2 at hole filling {\nu}_h=1 and identify two near-infrared Chern-ferromagnet excitons (CFEs) selectively coupled to opposite circular polarizations. Strong electron-hole interactions markedly enhance their energy separation and drive a pronounced momentum-space reconstruction of the emergent X- state, beyond the quasiparticle-transition picture. We further find that this reconstruction enhances the interlayer electron-hole character of X-, giving rise to a giant quadratic Stark response. These findings reveal the nontrivial interplay between electron-electron correlations and electron-hole interactions underlying CFE formation, providing optical fingerprints of moiré Chern-ferromagnetic order and a microscopic basis for its optical control.

papers.title: Oriented Semi-DETR for Semi-Supervised Aerial Object Detection
Verifiable Random Sampling of Private Data Without a Trusted Single Party
Fluid exchange and renewal in the left atrial appendage
papers.abstract: Fluid exchange through the opening of a cavity does not uniquely determine how the cavity is washed out. We investigate this phenomenon in the left atrial appendage (LAA), a deforming side cavity of the heart, using simulations of 17 patient-specific atria with wall motion reconstructed from time-resolved computed tomography. Fluid exchange through the LAA ostium is decomposed into a component driven by LAA volume change and a component due to simultaneous bidirectional flow, with no net volume transport. Washout of a scalar initially confined to the LAA is compared with predictions from two well-mixed washout models and assessed alongside residence-time distributions. Volume-driven transport accounts for approximately 24-78% of total exchange across the simulated atria. Relative washout efficiencies are approximately 26-53% with respect to the inflow-driven washout model that assumes scalar-free inflow. A scalar-balance decomposition identifies two contributions to this discrepancy: re-ingestion of previously expelled scalar and preferential export of scalar-poor fluid. Both effects reduce the effective washout rate in every configuration. Residence-time distributions reveal coexisting distinct younger and older fluid regions, and a regional analysis of one appendage localizes the older population predominantly in its distal region. These findings show that substantial exchange across the LAA ostium coexists with prolonged distal retention. Effective renewal depends on how much fluid crosses the ostium and which fluid is exchanged.

papers.title: Capacities from the Chiu-Tamarkin complex II: Product formula and toric domains
papers.abstract: In this article, we continue our study of equivariant symplectic capacities of open sets in a cotangent bundle defined via the Chiu-Tamarkin complex constructed from the microlocal theory of sheaves. The paper consists of two parts: 1) We develop the theory of $S^1$-equivariant Chiu-Tamarkin complex over complex-oriented ring spectra. 2) Applications of the theory to symplectic capacities: We show that a product formula for the capacities, whose Ekeland-Hofer capacities version is folklore since 1988, is not true via an (uncountable family of) counterexample(s). The counterexample (family) is the product of a concave toric domain of dimension $6$ ($2n\geq 6$) and a $2$-dimensional disk. We also prove a Weyl law of the capacities for all toric domains in dimension $2n$. The algebraic verification is based on a chain model for the Chiu-Tamarkin complex of all toric domains in $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$, which recovers Irie's conjectural chain model of $S^1$-equivariant symplectic homology for star-shaped toric domains (defined only) in $\mathbb{R}^4$.

papers.title: Heavy-quark gluon radiation in transversely flowing QCD matter: First-subeikonal corrections
papers.abstract: We investigate medium-induced gluon radiation from energetic heavy quarks propagating through a finite-size QCD medium with transverse collective flow. Within the DGLV framework, we calculate the radiation spectrum at first order in opacity and to first-subeikonal accuracy, retaining finite heavy-quark and effective gluon masses. Subleading corrections to the longitudinal propagator poles generate mass-dependent modifications of both the residue denominators and formation phases. For rotationally symmetric transverse-momentum integration domains, all contributions linear in the transverse flow velocity vanish after full azimuthal integration, while a nonzero static first-subeikonal correction remains. For representative medium parameters, this correction increases the integrated fractional radiative energy loss by approximately $10$--$20\%$, depending on the quark mass, initial energy, and path length. At the differential level, transverse flow produces a dipolar angular anisotropy, enhancing radiation along the flow direction and suppressing it in the opposite direction.

papers.title: InclusionMed: Benchmarking AI for Inclusive Healthcare
Torsional Hall Viscosity of Massive Chern Insulators: Finite Temperature and Chemical Potential
papers.abstract: We study the torsional Hall viscosity $\zeta_{\rm H}$ of Chern insulators at finite temperature and chemical potential. Our analysis considers the massive Dirac fermion and two deformations: a constant out-of-plane magnetic field and a momentum-dependent mass described by the single-block Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang (BHZ) Hamiltonian. For the massive Dirac theory, we show that temperature and chemical potential lead to UV-finite corrections and that a chemical potential outside the bulk gap modifies $\zeta_{\rm H}$ even at zero temperature. In a constant magnetic field, the response of massive Dirac fermions is dictated by the relativistic Landau-level spectrum, leading to a plateau structure at zero temperature that is smoothed at finite temperature. The jumps are proportional to the Dirac mass and inversely proportional to the squared magnetic length and the newly occupied Landau-level energy. Finally, we present a detailed study of the correction to $\zeta_{\rm H}$ in the single-block BHZ continuum model due to temperature and chemical potential. For parameters relevant to (Hg,Mn)Te quantum wells, the magnitude of the jump across a mass domain wall retains its vacuum enhancement due to the BHZ deformation as long as the chemical potential lies sufficiently deep inside the gap compared with the thermal energy. Our results extend the theory of torsional Hall viscosity to experimentally relevant conditions and may facilitate its future detection.

papers.title: MiSTiQ: MicroScaling Trellis Quantization for Extreme KV Cache Compression
Open-fMIND: A Large-Scale Open-Access fMRI Corpus for Pretraining Brain Foundation Models
Taking Time Out of TOCTOU: From Race Reproduction to Security Discovery
A necessary regularity condition for finite-time stopping of the string with dry friction
papers.abstract: We consider the one-dimensional wave equation with dry (Coulomb) friction, u\_{tt} -u\_{xx} + Sgn(u\_t )= 0, with Dirichlet boundary conditions. Whether every finite-energy solution stops in finite time has been open since 1978. We show that stopping in finite time is impossible whenever the initial slope or the initial velocity is unbounded: the space W 1,$\infty$ x L $\infty$ for (u, u t ) is invariant under the flow in both time directions, while stopped states are Lipschitz. In particular the answer is negative for general finite-energy data, and the open question is reduced to Lipschitz data.

papers.title: Explicit cohomological transfer for Morita equivalent Lie groupoids
papers.abstract: It is well known that Morita equivalent Lie groupoids have isomorphic differentiable cohomology. At the cochain level, however, explicitly transporting a cocycle from one groupoid to a Morita equivalent one is less straightforward. We provide explicit formulas for such cohomological transfers in arbitrary degree. More precisely, for the pullback of a Lie groupoid along a surjective submersion, we construct an explicit cochain-level homotopy inverse to the natural pullback map. We first treat Čech groupoids, where the construction only involves a partition of unity, and then extend it to arbitrary surjective submersions, for which the extra choice of local sections is needed. We also show that the resulting operators preserve the complexes associated with $\mathcal{VB}$-groupoids, including homogeneous and $\mathcal{VB}$-cochains. As an application, we obtain explicit transfer maps for deformation cocycles of Morita equivalent Lie groupoids and recover the Morita invariance of deformation cohomology.

papers.title: Teaching Language Models to Adapt Answer Granularity to Their Confidence
Full-Cover and Non-Overlapping Uni-domination in Graphs: Bounds and Complexity
BoBDeLaN: Bounded-Bandwidth Context Adaptation for Deep Lagrangian Robot Control
Validating LLM-Based Essay Scorers: A Comparative Analysis in Critical Online Reasoning in Medical Education
Who Is the Regression About? Auditing AI-Labeled Treatments When Effects Differ
papers.abstract: Researchers increasingly regress outcomes on treatments labeled by large language models. When effects differ, OLS averages the effect on the treated (ATT) and on the untreated (ATU), weighting the smaller group more. A label's bias then has two parts: classical attenuation from misclassification, and a selective term when its errors are correlated with the outcome. In LinkedIn postings, the model misses better-paid remote jobs: a precision check passes, yet the remote pay gap is understated by nearly 40 percent, a bias that more data cannot remove. A stratified, blind audit of both labeled groups corrects it and recovers both effects.

papers.title: PQC Migration: End-to-End Performance Profiling of Post Quantum Cryptographic Algorithms in mTLS
Cyclic homology of Sheaf Categories
papers.abstract: In this note, we explain the circle action on the Hochschild homology of categories of sheaves and their admissible subcategories in terms of the six-functor formalism using factorization homology, including (quasi-)coherent sheaves on derived stacks, sheaves on manifolds with prescribed microsupports, and Tamarkin categories with prescribed microsupports. We also explain the Gysin sequence for $C_\ell$ and $S^1$-(co)invariants and the Künneth sequence for $S^1$-(co)invariants of the Hochschild homology relative to any complex-oriented symmetric monoidal category.

papers.title: Digital Twin Enabled Talkative Power Conversion
Decision-Relevant Forecast Calibration for Predictive Control
Zeta Functions of Polygonal Numbers: Analytic Continuation, Poles and Zero Scattering
papers.abstract: We study the Zeta functions associated with polygonal numbers, focusing on their meromorphic continuation, poles, residues, and trivial zeros. We then investigate the distribution of their nontrivial zeros. Under explicit hypotheses, we derive an asymptotic formula for the mean real part of zeros in long height windows. The formula predicts convergence of this mean to 1/4 as the height tends to infinity. We also formulate a stronger concentration conjecture and examine numerical evidence for it.

papers.title: Möbius-Pseudorandomness for Algebraic Circuits
Hands-On Beyond Classrooms: Elevating Control Engineering Education with Take-Home Labs
Generalized Limits of Finitely Additive Measures on Locally Compact Groups
papers.abstract: Let $\mathscr{E}=\{E_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I}$ be an increasing family of Borel subsets of a locally compact topological group $G$, indexed by a linearly ordered set $I$ with no greatest element. We call a nonnegative finitely additive $\sigma$-finite measure on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $G$ admissible if it takes finite values on the sets in $\mathscr{E}$ and these values are not bounded above. Every admissible measure $\mu$ can be normalized to have total mass one by applying a generalized limit pointwise to the net of measures $\left\{B\mapsto\frac{\mu(B\cap E_\alpha)}{\mu(E_\alpha)}\right\}_{\alpha\in I}$, defined for all sufficiently large $\alpha$. We study invariant finitely additive measures obtained by normalizing admissible measures. We show that every invariant measure constructed in this way can be obtained by normalizing a measure of a special form. An example is given showing that not every measure of the type under consideration can be obtained by normalizing a countably additive measure. We obtain a generalization of the Yosida-Hewitt decomposition to finitely additive $\sigma$-finite measures.

papers.title: Cooperative Mobile Manipulation using Learned Dynamical Systems
Counterexamples to Green's Conjecture via E_6-covers
papers.abstract: We show that curves of genus 10 which are W(E_6)-covers of the projective line provide counterexamples to Green's Conjecture on syzygies of canonical curves. This leads to a 9-dimensional family of explicit counterexamples to Green's Conjecture. We also show that the same curves provide counterexamples to the Green-Lazarsfeld Secant Conjecture. Both Green's Conjecture and the Secant Conjecture are know to be true in the generic case, as well as in many other situations.

papers.title: Determining Concentration from Raman Spectroscopy with Manifold Learning and Y-shaped Conformal Autoencoders
On Mean Field Games with Focusing Logarithmic Local Couplings
papers.abstract: In this note we study the existence theory of classical solutions to a second order stationary discounted Mean Field Games (MFG) system with focusing logarithmic local coupling in one space dimension. We then show the convergence of classical solutions to the discounted stationary MFG system in the large discount/cheap control limit in the spirit of the work of Bardi--Cardaliaguet.

papers.title: Interaction Landscapes of Structurally Distorted Toroidal Classical Spin Textures
papers.abstract: We develop a classical discrete magnetostatic model of localized magnetic moments arranged in a toroidal texture, where the moments are represented by static current loops and study the behavior of the magnetic dipole-dipole interaction under several types of structural deformations. The purpose is to disentangle effects due to geometric and magnetic deformations, including elliptical, lopsided, alternating, and tilted configurations. In particular, we investigate how distortions modify the toroidal moment and the interaction energy between pairs of toroidal structures. The resulting interaction landscapes exhibit characteristic symmetry patterns and anisotropies that are highly sensitive to the underlying deformation. As a separate proof-of-concept comparison, first-principles calculations on a molecular spin-toroidal system reveal qualitatively similar orientation-dependent behavior. The calculated interaction is microscopically the conventional pairwise magnetic dipole-dipole interaction between localized moments arranged in a spin-toroidal texture; the toroidal moment characterizes the collective texture and should not be interpreted as introducing an additional elementary interaction term. Our results provide a platform for exploring orientation-dependent interactions of spin-toroidal textures in molecular magnets and related nanoscale magnetic systems that are essential to understand the role of toroidal order.

papers.title: Sharp Bounds for the Nodal Measure of Clamped Plate Eigenfunctions in Smooth Domains
papers.abstract: We investigate measure estimates for the nodal sets of nonzero real eigenfunctions $u$ of the biharmonic operator, satisfying $\Delta^2u=\lambda u$ in $\Omega$ with clamped boundary conditions $u=\partial_\nu u=0$ on $\partial\Omega$. We establish the optimal upper bound of order $\lambda^{1/4}$ for the $(n-1)$-dimensional Hausdorff measure of their nodal sets on general bounded connected $C^\infty$ domains. Our approach combines an enhanced annular Carleman estimate with propagation of mass along a finite chain of balls, these yield a doubling index bounded uniformly up to the this http URL analyticity then gives the nodal measure away from the boundary. To estimate the measure near the boundary, we develop a subdivision argument using the boundary values of $\Delta u$ and $\partial_\nu\Delta u$. Estimates from these data reduce large doubling indices and control the nodal measure in the region associated with a selected child cube whenever both the doubling index of the parent cube and $r\lambda^{1/4}$ are bounded, where $r$ is the side length of the parent cube.

papers.title: Borel--Serre Callias Classes and Cuspidal Localization
papers.abstract: We construct equivariant Callias classes on the Borel--Serre space of a Hilbert modular group and prove a Kasparov product formula. For torsion-free normal congruence subgroups and twists by powers $m_j\geq2$ of the holomorphic cotangent line bundles, we identify the image of the maximal higher index in the representation ring of the finite quotient with the equivariant index of the cuspidal Dolbeault operator on total forms. The comparison uses a Fredholm homotopy that separates an invertible noncuspidal block. As an application, we compute the $A_5$-equivariant index on the principal level-two Hilbert modular surface over $\mathbb Q(\sqrt5)$ for all parallel powers $m\geq2$. The resulting class in $R(A_5)$ is $15$-periodic in $m$ and has virtual dimension four. We express this class as an alternating sum of Hilbert cusp-form representations and deduce dimension identities for the full Hilbert modular group.

papers.title: Symmetric Chemical Reaction Networks: Realizations and Steady States
papers.abstract: We investigate symmetric chemical reaction networks and their steady states. From classical equivariant dynamical systems and network theory it is known that the mass- action ODE of any symmetric chemical reaction network is equivariant. For symmetries that permute the species, we prove that any equivariant mass-action ODE is realized by a symmetric chemical reaction network and construct a sparsest such realization. We apply the half-degree principle to show that a symmetric CRN that has a steady state also has one with few distinct coordinates.

papers.title: Linear Network Coding for Sum All-Reduce over Ring Networks
Separations Between Randomized and Exact Quantum Query Complexity for Boolean Functions
No complete set of mutually unbiased bases in dimension ten contains the Fourier pair or three product bases
papers.abstract: With computer-assisted proofs that $\mathbb{C}^6$ admits at most three mutually unbiased bases (MUBs) now available, $\mathbb{C}^{10}$ is the smallest dimension in which it is unknown whether a complete set of $d+1=11$ MUBs exists; only three MUBs are known. We prove that every triple of mutually unbiased product bases of $\mathbb{C}^2\otimes\mathbb{C}^5$ is strongly unextendible: no vector is unbiased to all three bases. Consequently no set of four MUBs in dimension ten, and in particular no complete set, contains three product bases. This settles the case $d=2\times5$ anticipated by McNulty, Pammer and Weigert; it was known only for the Heisenberg-Weyl triple. The proof covers all ten equivalence classes with explicit Nullstellensatz certificates modulo one prime on $91$ charts of $\mathbb{P}^9\times\mathbb{P}^9$ for each class ($910$ in all), transferred to characteristic zero by a projective reduction lemma, together with an independent rank certificate for eight of the ten classes. We also prove that the pair formed by the standard and the Fourier basis of $\mathbb{C}^{10}$ is contained in no set of four MUBs. Exactly $3040$ rays are unbiased to both bases (this confirms the count found numerically by Führ and Rzeszotnik), each of them is unbiased to at most eight of the others, and every triple formed by the pair and a third MUB is strongly unextendible. For this we certify $34,940$ cyclic $10$-roots in Krawczyk uniqueness boxes, decide unimodularity exactly through an involution, and prove completeness by a four-dimensional interval branch-and-bound obtained from the Chinese-remainder splitting $\mathbb{Z}_{10}=\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_5$.

papers.title: A Polynomial Time Algorithm for Finding a Minimum 5-Partition of a Submodular Function
Coalescing and annihilating random walks on the ring
papers.abstract: We study correlation functions in the model of coalescing and annihilating random walks on the one-dimensional periodic lattice $\mathbb{Z}_N$. We prove that, for a special class of initial conditions, the $n$-point correlation function can be represented as a linear combination of two Pfaffians of $2n\times 2n$ matrices constructed from $2\times2$ matrix kernels, which in turn can be expressed in terms of two scalar kernels. This is an analogue of the single-Pfaffian form exhibited by correlation functions of the same model on $\mathbb{Z}$, where it serves as a signature of a Pfaffian point process. We derive equations for the kernels and construct their solutions. We also show that a particular example of an initial condition leading to bi-Pfaffian correlation functions is the inhomogeneous Bernoulli point process, which includes a fixed initial configuration as a particular limiting case.

papers.title: Surrogate-Based Optimization of Tandem Twin-Rotor Wind Turbines Accounting for Wake Interactions
papers.abstract: Wake interaction in a tandem twin-rotor turbine couples power capture with thrust on the shared support. This study develops a time-resolved surrogate for upstream IEA Wind 22 MW and downstream NREL 5 MW rotors. It covers spacing ratios $0.01\leq L/D\leq0.20$ and tip-speed ratios $4\leq\lambda\leq11$. Vortex-method simulations of 160 configurations under turbulent inflow train per-time-node XGBoost models to predict 600 s power, thrust, and torque histories. A CNN-Attention-LSTM network extends these histories, and a genetic algorithm balances the system power and thrust coefficients. Ten-fold cross-validation gives median power-history $R^2$ values of 0.995 upstream and 0.958 downstream for unseen configurations, but the first stage cannot extrapolate in tip-speed ratio. With fixed pitch and prescribed rotor speed, the coefficients apply where both rotors reach the simulated tip-speed ratio below rated wind speed. Increasing spacing raises upstream power by up to 6% and lowers downstream power by up to 62%. System power changes by less than 4% at fixed $\lambda$. The high-power end of the Pareto front lies near $\lambda=10$. At $L/D=0.20$, the system power coefficient is highest. This configuration has the lowest peak thrust among the high-power candidates.

papers.title: An Optimal Online Algorithm for Single-machine Scheduling with Two Agents
Seeing Isn't Resolving: Visual and Linguistic Disambiguation with Conversational Grounding
A note on meromorphicity in infinite dimensions
papers.abstract: In this note we develop the notion of a meromorphic mapping between infinite-dimensional complex manifolds. We restrict ourselves with second countable Hilbert manifolds modelled on a separable Hilbert space.

papers.title: Average character degree below 14/3
papers.abstract: We prove that a finite group with average irreducible character degree less than $14/3$ is solvable if it has no chief factor isomorphic to $A_5$. This answers a question of Aziziheris and Eivazzadeh.

papers.title: Existence and uniqueness of entropy solutions for nonautonomous pressureless gas dynamics
papers.abstract: We study the Cauchy problem for one-dimensional pressureless gas dynamics with a continuous positive transport coefficient $\alpha(t)$ and a continuous nonnegative linear damping coefficient $\sigma(t)$, for every nonnegative locally finite Radon measure $\rho_0$ as initial density and every $u_0\in L^\infty(d\rho_0)$ as initial velocity. A central contribution of this paper is a new and direct proof of uniqueness under the original assumptions of Huang and Wang. It is carried out on the generalized potentials, and the energy condition enters only through the vanishing of the velocity dispersion at the initial time. The proof applies on every finite time strip and requires neither finite mass nor finite moments. We then show that time-dependent transport and damping act on entropy solutions only through an effective time, so that the nonautonomous system is the homogeneous one observed on a time interval $[0,A_\infty)$. Together with uniqueness on strips, this yields a global entropy solution, unique in density and momentum at every time, for all such coefficients. We also show that the energy condition cannot be dropped, and that its defect equals the mass of an atom times the variance of the velocities into which it splits. As consequences, we obtain an explicit representation of the solution by a generalized potential, the Riemann solutions with delta shocks, and the vanishing-damping limit.

papers.title: Learning to Clear Peer-to-Peer Energy Markets
TRACK: Tool-Augmented Reasoning over Time Series for Fault Diagnosis in Power Management System
RAGE: Residual-Adaptive Gating for Flow-Based Image Editing
Scientific Coding with Large Language Models: Evidence from Finite Element Analysis
A COMPASS to the Galaxy: Joint nucleosynthetic yield set comparison and parameter inference in Galactic chemical evolution
papers.abstract: Galactic Chemical Evolution (GCE) models connect stellar nucleosynthesis to observed abundance patterns, but their interpretation requires simultaneous parameter inference and comparison between competing stellar yield prescriptions. This remains challenging due to intractable likelihoods and growing dataset complexity. Using compass, a novel simulation-based inference framework, we perform, for the first time, amortized joint Bayesian model comparison and parameter inference for GCE models with intractable likelihoods within a unified architecture. Compass employs a conditional score-based diffusion model with a transformer architecture to learn both the posterior and likelihood directly from forward simulations, enabling efficient inference and likelihood-based ranking of competing nucleosynthetic yield sets. In controlled tests, compass identifies the generating yield set and recovers ground-truth parameters with accuracy comparable to existing simulation-based inference (SBI) methods, while reducing computational cost by orders of magnitude. Applied to Milky Way data, the framework favors a hybrid NuGrid + IllustrisTNG yield prescription, confirmed by an independent classifier, and infers an initial mass function slope of $\alpha_{\rm IMF} = -2.65 \pm 0.02$ and a SN$_{\rm Ia}$ normalization of $\log(N_{\rm Ia}) = -2.81 \pm 0.02$, with a systematic spread of $\approx 0.3$ in $\alpha_{\rm IMF}$ between the best-ranked yield sets, consistent with independent constraints. The attention mechanism confirms that the inferred parameters are driven by physically meaningful abundance signatures. By unifying amortized parameter inference, Bayesian model comparison, and interpretability in a single probabilistic framework, compass provides a scalable approach for precision chemical evolution studies with current and forthcoming spectroscopic surveys.

papers.title: On the regularity of branching loci for $\mathbb{Z}_2$-harmonic spinors
papers.abstract: We show that the branching locus of a $\mathbb Z_2$-harmonic spinor is smooth (resp. real-analytic) near every point of frequency $\frac{1}{2}$ for smooth (resp. real-analytic) ambient defining data. This partially strengthens the previous regularity results obtained by Clifford Taubes and Boyu Zhang.

papers.title: Elliptic Gromov-Witten Invariants of Instanton Moduli
papers.abstract: We calculate the genus $1$ Gromov-Witten invariants with one tautological divisor insertion of the moduli space $\mathcal{M}(r,n)$ of rank-$r$, $c_2=n$ torsion-free sheaves on $\mathbb{P}^2$ framed along the infinity divisor. As rational functions of the framing parameters, we determine the polar parts of these invariants by exploring the equivariant geometry of the Gieseker-Uhlenbeck map $\mathcal{M}(r,n)\to\mathcal{M}_0(r,n)$. We determine the polynomial part of these invariants by relating their large framing limits to the results \cite{ILPT} for the rank $1$ case, namely $\mathrm{Hilb}^n(\mathbb{C}^2)$. The degree-$0$ invariants with one divisor insertion are evaluated by studying the combinatorics of multi-partitions. We also prove reconstruction results for invariants with multiple insertions. Under the assumption that the eigenvalues of the divisor operator are linearly independent as functions of the Novikov variable, these results determine the full genus $1$ theory from the one-divisor series and the genus $0$ divisor operator.

papers.title: Precise Analytic Boundaries and Positive Symplectic Paths in the Stability Diagrams of Elliptic Relative Equilibria
papers.abstract: We investigate the dependence of the linear stability of elliptic relative equilibria on the mass parameter and eccentricity. Using a periodic matrix Riccati decomposition, we derive explicit analytic curves separating hyperbolic--hyperbolic and complex--saddle spectra. The construction applies to the Lagrangian, Euler--Robe, and $(2+2)$-body families. A Hermitian Riccati factorization also yields an eccentricity-independent sufficient condition for positivity of the associated operators under every unit-circle boundary condition, and hence for hyperbolicity of the monodromy matrix. Finally, we construct an explicit lower bound for the second antiperiodic degeneracy curve by a finite trigonometric test function. This bound agrees with the value and tangent of the degeneracy curve at the circular limit. Together, these results provide analytic descriptions and estimates for distinct spectral boundaries in the stability diagrams.

papers.title: Observation of Crossover from Repulsive to Attractive Interactions between Two $nS$-Rydberg Atoms in Dual-Species Atom Arrays
papers.abstract: Dual-species Rydberg atom arrays provide a flexible platform for engineering long-range interactions beyond the conventional isotropic blockade regime. We spectroscopically study interactions between different $s$-state Rydberg levels in a $^{87}\mathrm{Rb}$--$^{85}\mathrm{Rb}$ optical-tweezer array. By varying the principal-quantum-number difference $\Delta n$ around $61S_{1/2}$, we observe a crossover from repulsive to attractive interactions. We identify a distinct regime at $\Delta n=2$ in which Förster-enhanced electronic spin exchange dominates over orbital exchange and produces a strongly bond-orientation-dependent pair spectrum. Time-domain collective-excitation measurements reveal this geometry-dependent spin exchange through a pronounced anisotropy of the double-excitation probability. For $\Delta n=1$, by contrast, orbital exchange dominates and the interaction is nearly isotropic. These results establish the principal-quantum-number difference and bond orientation as complementary control parameters for tailoring Rydberg interaction spectra and collective excitation dynamics, opening new opportunities for engineering spin-dependent Hamiltonians in programmable atom arrays.

papers.title: An Alternative Explicitly Correlated Approach for Describing Strongly Correlated Systems within a Single-Determinant Framework
papers.abstract: We introduce an alternative explicitly correlated single-reference approach for strongly correlated systems within a single-determinant framework, providing a balanced description of strong and weak electron correlations by integrating singlet-paired coupled-cluster singles and doubles with explicitly correlated theory. While the singlet interactions are captured via standard explicitly correlated terms, the triplet correlation omitted during regularization is recovered through a newly formulated explicitly correlated pseudo-excitation operator that satisfies Kato's cusp condition and integrates a full virtual space to retrieve the missing triplet-paired correlations based on the interelectronic distance. We show that CCSD0 [J. Chem. Theory Comput. 11, 3171 (2015)] is structurally related to the complex molecular orbital framework, an orbital theory that addresses the stability dilemma by yielding an energy lower than that of restricted Hartree-Fock in the presence of imaginary spin-singlet instabilities, while the symmetry dilemma is resolved via projection [J. Chem. Phys. 69, 4535 (1978)]. Prompted by this structural correspondence, we introduce the explicitly correlated "CCSD0-F12Pi" and perturbative triples methodologies. The performance of these new single-reference frameworks has been evaluated for the bond-breaking processes of N2 and CO2, and benchmarked against Mukherjee's multireference coupled-cluster method for the strongly correlated regimes of linear singlet methylene and cyclobutadiene. Our results show that the new framework systematically avoids unphysical artifacts along the potential energy surfaces while accelerating convergence toward the complete basis set limit, offering a single-reference alternative to multireference methodologies for closed-shell molecules.

papers.title: Long-time asymptotics of advection-diffusion of finite element differential forms
Beyond Token Stacking: Multi-scale Visual Modulation and Adaptive Fused-feature Calibration for MLLMs
Iterated Steiner symmetrization of convex bodies always converges in shape
papers.abstract: We prove that every sequence of iterated Steiner symmetrals of a convex body converges in shape. That is, every such sequence can be corrected by a sequence of rotations to achieve convergence in Hausdorff distance. Moreover, for a fixed corresponding family of subspaces, the same rotations can be used for every initial convex body, and their successive increments can be chosen to be square-summable.

papers.title: On the Matlis duals of $\mathcal D$-modules in characteristic zero
papers.abstract: Let $R=k[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]$ be a formal power series ring over a field $k$ of characteristic zero, and let $\mathcal D=\mathcal D(R,k)$ be the ring of $k$-linear differential operators. We prove that if $\mathcal M$ is a nonzero left $\mathcal D$-module with $(0)\notin\operatorname{Ass}_R(\mathcal M)$, then $(0)\in\operatorname{Ass}_R D(\mathcal M)$, where $D(-)$ denotes Matlis duality, without assuming holonomicity or finite generation over $\mathcal D$. As a significant consequence of this result, we establish the Lyubeznik--Yıldırım conjecture in equicharacteristic zero. We also obtain a criterion for the Matlis dual of a $\mathcal D$-module to be non-holonomic.

papers.title: A Matter of Stages: Energy-Latency Trade-offs in Multimodal LLM Serving
Microstate Response Model: A Unified IRT Framework from Latent Nominal States to a Theory of Tests
papers.abstract: Several features outside of the conventional assumptions in traditional item response theory (IRT) models have been revealed to be related, yet no unifying framework explains the features simultaneously. They can be unified by treating each cause as a distinct reason, and then regarding every reason as a choice in a latent multiple-choice item. Here, we propose the Microstate Response Model (MiRM), which decomposes each response category (macrostate) into multiple latent reasons (microstates) using Boltzmann weights. The consequences of this simple framework are substantial; for example, it reads the lower and upper asymptotes of item characteristic curves (ICCs) as additional states, and ICC asymmetry and item complexity as multiple states. The model unifies many classical models from the dichotomous logistic family to mixture models. Moreover, the algebra of the model provides the intuition that items and tests are the same object. Two consequences naturally come out: partial credits and test scores are unified, and a new test-level monotonicity condition is proposed. We examine item characteristics including nonmonotonicity on PISA 2015, and show that MiRM provides a deeper understanding of items while achieving the strongest overall performance across fit, parsimony, and prediction.

papers.title: Polygraph: Large-Scale Multi-Session Trajectory Optimization using Pose Graphs
DRaGAN: Dynamic Graph Attention Network for Multi-Radar Point Cloud Encoding in Automotive Radar Perception
Suppression, flow, and chemical components of heavy flavor hadrons in relativistic heavy-ion collisions within an improved Langevin framework
papers.abstract: We improve the Langevin model to incorporate both perturbative and non-perturbative interactions between heavy quarks and the quark-gluon plasma (QGP) in relativistic heavy-ion collisions. The transport coefficient of heavy quarks is evaluated by a potential scattering model in which both the short-range Yukawa interaction and the long-range string interaction are included. The updated model provides the correct thermal equilibrium limit of the heavy quark system with the medium background, and improves the accuracy in describing the nuclear modification factor and elliptic flow coefficient of $D$ mesons observed at RHIC and the LHC. Nuclear modification of different chemical components of charm hadrons, including $D^0$, $D_s^+$, $\Lambda_c^+$, $\Xi_c^0$, and $\Omega_c^0$, is investigated. Their spectrum ratios are found sensitive to not only the hadronization mechanism of charm quarks but also the medium-modified charm quark spectrum in heavy-ion collisions, offering additional constraints on the heavy quark dynamics inside a color-deconfined nuclear medium.

papers.title: PlainPairs: A Corpus Pairing the Prescriber and Patient Texts of U.S. Prescription Medicine Labels
When Feature Representation Changes Local Explanations: A Controlled Comparison of SHAP and LIME under Numerical Discretization
authors: Parv Patel (Indian Institute of Technology Palakkad)

papers.title: Summary Sufficiency in Simulation-Based Inference via Mutual Information
papers.abstract: Simulation-based inference (SBI) enables posterior estimation when the likelihood is intractable but data can be simulated from the model. For high-dimensional or variable-length data, SBI methods typically rely on low-dimensional summary statistics as conditioning inputs for posterior estimation, making their sufficiency crucial for accurate inference. Mutual information (MI) provides a natural information-theoretic characterization of sufficiency, quantifying how much parameter information a summary retains. However, these MI quantities are generally intractable in likelihood-free settings. Sui et al. (2026) estimate MI from a trained neural posterior using the Barber--Agakov (BA) lower bound, while discussing, but not computing, a Fisher-information upper bound. This makes the estimate ambiguous: a small lower bound may indicate either an insufficient summary or an inaccurate density estimator. We address this limitation with a tractable diagnostic that estimates the BA gap and reveals what the difference between bounds has actually measured. We extend the resulting sufficiency metric to observation-centered restricted data spaces, allowing simulations to focus on a neighborhood of the data while preserving the target posterior and enabling valid sufficiency comparisons between summaries. We illustrate the use of this diagnostic tool on a temporal epidemic-type aftershock sequence model by comparing learned and hand-crafted summary statistics for variable-length earthquake catalogs.

papers.title: Going Deep Inside Public Announcement Logic
Deterministic nonlinear domain engineering algorithm with variable sub-coherence-length domains
papers.abstract: We present a new and improved deterministic algorithm that calculates the poling domains for the implementation of arbitrary phase-matching functions (PMF) in quasi-phase-matched nonlinear crystals for parametric down-conversion photon sources. In contrast to previous work, the algorithm presented here makes full use of the limits of the fabrication process, such as the minimum feature size and resolution of the lithographic process underpinning the poling procedure. This minimizes the tracking error to the target electric field and improves the accuracy in reaching the desired PMF. We give a tutorial on how to calculate the target function for arbitrary PMFs and run the algorithm. We also demonstrate the procedure on a relevant application in quantum sensing, where we use a quadratic phase on the PMF to implement a broadband photon spectrum while maintaining high nonlinearity across the crystal. The designed crystal is experimentally tested, and the result matches expectations.

papers.title: Edit Recommendation: Can LLMs Anticipate Edit Requests from Users, and When?
KuroshioVis: Hypothesis-Driven Discovery of Mesoscale Air-Sea Interaction through Coarse-to-Fine Exploration
Orbifold Morse Handles I. Morse Indices and Isomorphism Classes of Ordered Handles
papers.abstract: We classify the Morse indices and ordered handles arising from nondegenerate critical points of smooth functions on effective orientable four-dimensional orbifolds. Let $\rho\colon G\to\mathrm{SO}(4)$ be a faithful representation of a finite group. Let $V\subset\mathbb R^4$ be the negative eigenspace of a nondegenerate Hessian that is invariant under $\rho(G)$. The splitting $\mathbb R^4=V\oplus V^\perp$ determines an ordered quotient handle. Two such ordered handles admit an orientation-preserving isomorphism if and only if their negative eigenspaces lie in the same orbit under $N_{\mathrm{SO}(4)}(\rho(G))$. We determine the possible Morse indices and the normalizer orbits for every family in the completed Du Val list.

papers.title: From Repositories to Training Environments: Scaling Long-Horizon Coding Agents with Environment Evolution Loop
Fast computation of microscopic optical potentials: beyond existing capabilities
papers.abstract: A microscopic approach to optical potential calculations, based on the leading term in the spectator expansion of the optical potential operator and carried out in momentum space, has been successful in describing nucleon elastic scattering above 100 MeV. However, high computational cost precludes the inclusion of all physics relevant to scattering, such as the tensor part of the nucleon-nucleon (NN) amplitude, three-nucleon forces, multiple scattering and medium effects. Also, this approach does not provide any nucleon-nucleus scattering wave functions needed for reaction calculations. In this Letter, we develop a harmonic oscillator expansion version of this approach, which provides the same representation of optical potential both in momentum and coordinate spaces, accelerates calculations by two orders of magnitude, includes the missing tensor component of the NN scattering amplitude and is applicable to nuclei with any spin. Test calculations have been performed for several light nuclei whose densities were obtained in the No-Core Shell Model using a chiral Hamiltonian. We demonstrate convergence of this expansion and clarify the role of the tensor force, which manifests itself mainly in coupling between channels with different spin. Comparison to experimental data is presented for selected cases. The methodology could be extended for scattering of other projectiles (hadronic and pionic), small complex nuclei and hypernuclei. It also suggests a pathway for including more complicated physics into the scheme and extending it to lower energies. It could be also helpful in assessing the accuracy of upcoming scattering emulators.

papers.title: Resolution of ladder representations
papers.abstract: Let $\pi$ be a ladder representation of $\mathbf{GL}_m(F)$, $F$ a non-Archimedean local field. We construct an exact sequence of costandard modules, indexed by a lower Bruhat interval of a symmetric group and graded by the length, whose Euler characteristic is the determinantal formula of Tadić and Lapid--Mínguez. This is an analogue of the dual Bernstein--Gelfand--Gelfand resolution. The proof is combinatorial, through Jacquet modules and the Bruhat order; we also interpret the coresolution as a Cousin complex on Zelevinsky's space, which extends it to the balanced representations of Lapid--Mínguez.

papers.title: Cap-Aware Boosting for Green Day-Ahead Electricity Price Forecasting
SAFE: Formal Specification and Implementation of a Scalable Analysis Framework for ECMAScript
Large-scale Monte Carlo/Molecular Dynamics simulations with Atomic Cluster Expansion potentials in LAMMPS
papers.abstract: Monte Carlo/molecular dynamics (MCMD) simulations are widely used to study the properties of materials at the mesoscale. Simulations with hundreds of thousands of atoms usually rely on empirical potentials because MCMD with machine-learning interatomic potentials is impractical at this scale in existing implementations. Here, we introduce a hybrid MPI/OpenMP scheme for MCMD with Atomic Cluster Expansion (ACE) potentials in LAMMPS. Monte Carlo moves are evaluated from local energy changes and carried out in parallel over MPI ranks, while molecular dynamics is parallelized over OpenMP threads. At a fixed number of CPUs, the wall time of the Monte Carlo moves decreases by a factor equal to the number of MPI ranks. Larger simulation cells also reduce the statistical errors of free energy calculations because thermal fluctuations decrease with system size. We demonstrate the scheme by calculating free energies of the HCP and BCC phases in the strongly anharmonic Hf--Ti system and by simulating zirconium segregation in a nanocrystalline copper sample of 670,000 atoms. For Cu--Zr, an ACE potential and an empirical potential predict similar grain boundary compositions but different amounts of zirconium dissolved in the grains. The scheme makes MCMD simulations with machine-learning interatomic potentials practical at the length scales of microstructure.

papers.title: Model-based neural network for global floodplains analysis
Exposure and remediation in the French maritime sector: a passive measurement of 129 organisations
A Hybrid Systems Approach to Parameterizing the PERC1 Model for Data Centers Using Synchrophasor Measurements
WinDEX: Metric 3D Hand Motion Reconstruction in the Wild for Dexterous Teleoperation and Policy Learning
Cassini ovals, translated polynomials, and the arithmetic of their discriminants and resultants
papers.abstract: For a polynomial $f$, $a>0$ and $b,\omega\in\mathbb{C}$, consider the translate $J^{(a,b,\omega)}f(z)=f(z/a)-\omega f(b/a)$. We show that for $f(x)=(x^{2}-1)^{n}$ and $\omega=\pm1$ every zero of $J^{(a,b,\omega)}f$ lies on the Cassini oval $|z^{2}-a^{2}|=|b^{2}-a^{2}|$. We call these translates \emph{Cassini polynomials} and give their zeros explicitly, prove that the zeros for $\omega=1$ and $\omega=-1$ strictly interlace on each component of the oval, and evaluate their discriminants and resultants in closed form. We then prove the reduced monic polynomials $Q_{n}=a^{2n}J^{(a,b,\omega)}f/(z^{2}-b^{2})$ factor into homogenized cyclotomic polynomials, satisfying $\operatorname{Res}(Q_{m},Q_{n})=(b^{2}-a^{2})^{2(m-1)(n-1)}$ for coprime $m,n$, and have discriminants governed by a Lucas sequence. We then prove a comparison principle: if $f$ is even or odd with all zeros in $[-1,1]$, $b\in\mathbb{R}$ and $|\omega|\le1$, then every zero of $J^{(a,ib,\omega)}f$ satisfies $|z^{2}-a^{2}|\le a^{2}+b^{2}$, and the symmetry hypothesis cannot be removed. As an application, every solution of $\det(A(P_{n})-\lambda I)=F_{n+1}$, where $A(P_{n})$ is the adjacency matrix of the path on $n$ vertices and $F_{n+1}$ is a Fibonacci number, satisfies $|\lambda^{2}-4|\le5$. This disproves, for every $n$, a conjecture of Gullerud, Johnson and Mbirika that the real parts of these solutions are unbounded.

papers.title: On Schroedinger operators with subordinated complex potentials
papers.abstract: We disprove a decade-old conjecture about a spectral stability of Schroedinger operators with potentials which are small in a subordination sense. Our counterexample is based on a complex perturbation of a critical attractive square well.

papers.title: Towards Microphone-Invariant Speech Representations for Transformer-Based Voice Disorder Detection
Entropy of Noncommutative Spaces
papers.abstract: We give an overview of the second quantisation of spectral triples and compute the entropy of the noncommutative space described by it in terms of a spectral action. This reviews earlier work by Chamseddine, Connes and the second author, but presented here concisely, including the procedure of second quantisation using infinite-dimensional Clifford algebras. We exemplify the theory by considering noncommutative metric spaces consisting of $N$ points. The entropy of these discrete spaces is explicitly computed, and we study the resulting entropic force as well as the evolution of the spaces in time.

papers.title: Orbital-dependent electronic correlations and single-band character in layered palladates
papers.abstract: Layered palladates provide a $4d$ platform for examining electronic correlations in materials with cuprate-like structural and orbital characteristics. Using fully charge-self-consistent density functional theory plus dynamical mean-field theory, we investigate the orbital- and layer-resolved electronic structures of LaPdO$_2$, RbSr$_2$PdO$_3$, BaLaPdO$_2$Cl$_2$, La$_4$Pd$_3$O$_8$, and La$_5$Pd$_4$O$_{10}$. Under the conditions studied, all compounds remain metallic, with low-energy states dominated by the Pd-$d_{x^2-y^2}$ orbital. This orbital exhibits stronger mass renormalization than the Pd-$d_{z^2}$ orbital. LaPdO$_2$ and BaLaPdO$_2$Cl$_2$ show moderate correlations, whereas RbSr$_2$PdO$_3$ is more weakly correlated. Both the trilayer La$_4$Pd$_3$O$_8$ and quadlayer La$_5$Pd$_4$O$_{10}$ remain weakly correlated, with similar Pd-$d_{x^2-y^2}$ mass enhancements and little difference between inner- and outer-layer Pd sites. Among the structures studied, BaLaPdO$_2$Cl$_2$ is closest to a cuprate-like single-band description, whereas RbSr$_2$PdO$_3$ retains an additional electron pocket with Pd-$d_{z^2}$ character. These results establish a comparative picture of weak to moderate, orbital-dependent electronic correlations in layered palladates.

papers.title: Scribble Once, Segment the Sequence: Bidirectional Temporal Consistency for Weakly Supervised Segmentation in Echocardiography Sequences
Sums of Integers with Small Prime Factors
papers.abstract: Let $P^+(n)$ denote the largest prime factor of $n$, with $P^+(1)=1$.
