We prove that, for every $\beta>103/(256\sqrt e)$, there is a constant $C=C(\beta)>0$ such that every sufficiently large integer $N$ can be written as $N=a+b$, where $a,b\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$ and $$ P^+(a)\leq N^\beta,\qquad P^+(b)\leq(\log N)^C. $$ This strengthens Balog's result, which gives two $N^\beta$-smooth summands for $\beta>4/(9\sqrt e)$. The proof combines Balog's argument with convolution estimates that are uniform in the residue class.

papers.title: Preserver Problems for Products of Operator Differences
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate surjective maps $\Phi:\mathscr B(H)\to\mathscr B(H)$ preserving various operator quantities associated with products of differences, namely, $$\alpha\big((\Phi(A)-\Phi(B))\Phi(C)\big) =\alpha\big((A-B)C\big) \quad \text{for all}~ A,B,C\in\mathscr B(H),$$ where $\alpha$ denotes one of the following: the numerical radius, maximal numerical range, minimum modulus, surjectivity modulus, reduced minimum modulus, or spectral radius. Under suitable assumptions, we establish structural characterizations of these maps and determine their possible forms.

papers.title: Robust Data-Driven Output-Feedback Reference Governor with Quantified Model Uncertainty
Polynomial growth and dynamic asymptotic dimension
papers.abstract: We show that principal ample groupoids with local polynomial growth of degree at most $s$ have dynamic asymptotic dimension at most $\lfloor s\rfloor$. As a consequence, $\sigma$-compact principal ample groupoids with local polynomial growth have slow dynamic asymptotic dimension growth.

papers.title: Region-VAD: Video Anomaly Localization and Detection via Region Selection
How to Explain your Unexplainable Video Anomaly Detector
Vanishing Dissipation Limit to Planar Euler Shock for the Full Compressible Navier-Stokes Equations in $\mathbb{R}^3$
papers.abstract: We prove the vanishing dissipation limit to a weak planar Euler shock for the full compressible Navier--Stokes equations in $\mathbb{R}^3$. The viscosity and heat conductivity are proportional to $\varepsilon$, with their ratio fixed. The conservative initial perturbation may depend on all three spatial variables and is assumed small only in the scaled $H^2 \cap \dot H^{-1}$ norm. No $L^1$ bound or zero-mass condition is required. For these data, we obtain a unique global strong solution and an energy estimate uniform in time and in $\varepsilon$. On every cylinder with a measurable transverse section of finite positive area, the $L^2$ error has an explicit leading term, yielding the sharp rate $O(\sqrt{\varepsilon})$. The remainder has order $\varepsilon^{3/2}$ times the scaled initial norm; both estimates are uniform for $t \geq 0$. If this norm tends to zero, convergence away from the shock front is uniform in time, including at $t=0$. The entropy production measures converge locally weakly to the measure carried by the Euler shock. Low frequencies are controlled by an entropy-weighted elliptic estimate. At second order, integration by parts in the pressure and viscous heating terms leaves at most two derivatives on the density, while third derivatives of velocity and temperature enter only through the time-integrated dissipation.

papers.title: Linglong Agent Service: A Runtime for Centralized Agent Reasoning and Distributed Execution
Mapping the obscured Galactic disk: ERIS J-band low-resolution spectroscopy of 27 Classical Cepheids
papers.abstract: Classical Cepheids (CCs) are standard candles and key tracers of young stellar populations. However, their use in the most obscured regions is hampered by the high interstellar extinction at optical wavelengths. Near-infrared spectroscopy offers major advantages by greatly reducing absorption corrections and enabling access to regions of the Milky Way that are still poorly sampled. In this work, we determine the atmospheric parameters and abundances of Fe, Mg and Si for a sample of 27 CCs based on observations with ERIS@VLT in J-band low-resolution mode ($R \sim 4000$). Combining PySME with 1D MARCS atmosphere models and non local thermal equilibrium grids, we simultaneous optimise the atmospheric parameters through spectral fitting. This method is validated with a direct comparison with high-resolution optical investigations and re-analysis of archive optical spectra for the targets in common. The results show good consistency in both metallicity and chemical abundances. We obtain mean abundance ratios of $\mathrm{\langle[Mg/Fe]\rangle=0.01\pm0.12~dex}$ and $\mathrm{\langle[Si/Fe]\rangle=0.10\pm0.09~dex}$, in agreement with reference samples. Moreover, we provide for the first time the Mg and Si abundances of 12 CCs. Finally, we have found distinct kinematic properties for two of the most distant Galactic CCs, located at Galactocentric distances of $\mathrm{\approx 28-29~kpc}$ and with extreme values of vertical height, $\mathrm{\approx +4.8~kpc}$ and $\mathrm{\approx -5.3~kpc}$; more data are required to constrain their nature. Our results confirm that J-band spectroscopy at low-resolution can be used as a good diagnostic for the chemical investigation in highly obscured Galactic regions, otherwise inaccessible at optical wavelengths.

papers.title: Thermal deep inelastic scattering, universality and complex geodesics
papers.abstract: In deep inelastic scattering (DIS), a lepton scatters off a target hadron whose structure is probed by an exchanged photon with large spacelike virtuality. We consider two-point functions of currents in strongly interacting quantum field theories at finite temperature in this kinematic regime and use a holographic description to compute them. At large virtuality, the crossover from vacuum-dominated to thermally dominated physics corresponds to a transition from exponentially suppressed absorption to power-law behavior of the response functions. This regime is related to a particular near-lightcone limit of thermal CFT correlators. We show that the response functions exhibit a large degree of universality: the dependence on the three-point couplings of currents to the stress tensor enters through a channel-dependent coefficient multiplying the kinematic parameter that controls the relative size of vacuum and thermal effects. The same coefficient controls conformal collider bounds; when either bound is saturated, the corresponding response function takes its vacuum form in the near-lightcone limit. Furthermore, the absorption exponent in the low-temperature regime is related to a complex geodesic propagating in the near-lightcone geometry.

papers.title: IGRecon4D: Dynamic-Object-Aware Feed-Forward Reconstruction of Driving Scenes
Human-AI Co-Ideation Across Socio-Technical Configurations: An Interactional Analysis of Planar and Immersive Workspaces
Group classification and equivalence of two classes of evolution equations of arbitrary order
papers.abstract: We revisit the group classification of the $(1{+}1)$-dimensional evolution equations $u_t=F(u_n)$ and $u_t+uu_x=F(u_n)$ of arbitrary order $n\geq2$, where $u_n=\partial_x^n u$, and describe the usual point equivalence groups of the two classes. We recover the known contact equivalences between the three second-order equations with seven-dimensional maximal Lie invariance algebras and extend the hodograph construction to points where $u_x=0$. For $n>2$, the dimensions of the contact symmetry algebras distinguish the two classes. We give reciprocal transformations linking the two classes at order three and formulate a nonlocal classification problem. We also classify the extensions of the Lie invariance algebra of the Burgers equation in a wider class of Galilei-invariant equations.

papers.title: Stabilizer-Restricted Antidistinguishability in Quantum Computation with Magic States
papers.abstract: An antidistinguishing measurement for a family of preparations excludes at least one preparation for every possible outcome, constraining 'classical' representations of these processes, known as ontological models. We develop this connection within quantum computing with magic states (QCM), a universal model of quantum computation. Our constructions use adaptive Pauli measurements on tensor products of single-qubit non stabilizer states, including families associated with the Clifford hierarchy. These constructions yield stabilizer-restricted versions of the Pusey-Barrett-Rudolph theorem: any ontological model reproducing these measurement statistics and satisfying preparation independence must assign disjoint ontic supports to the preparations considered. We demonstrate this obstruction to preparation independence in a concrete ontological model based on convex polytopes used for the classical simulation of QCM.

papers.title: Policy Iteration Convergence for Exploratory Two-State Mean-Field Control Problems
papers.abstract: This paper studies the theoretical policy iteration convergence for two-state mean-field control (MFC) problems with Wright--Fisher common noise under entropy regularization. The population dynamics lead to a degenerate Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman equation of Kimura type. After an arcsine transformation, the degeneracy becomes a singular Bessel drift whose coefficients and weights depend on the feedback stochastic policy. This policy dependence prevents a direct application of estimates for a fixed operator. We establish weighted Sobolev estimates and Hölder embeddings uniformly over the admissible policy class. Combining these estimates with logarithmic entropy bounds and boundary estimates that remain valid when the policy changes, we prove the well-posedness, monotone improvement and convergence of policy iteration to the optimal solution. We also establish the convergence to the original MFC problem when the entropy parameter $\lambda$ tends to zero. Both the regularization error and the performance loss of the regularized optimal policy are bounded by $O(\lambda(1+|\ln\lambda|))$ in a weighted Hölder norm. An epidemic containment example of MFC is presented to illustrate the policy iteration convergence and the vanishing entropy convergence.

papers.title: Néron Functions on Jacobians of Odd-Degree Hyperelliptic Curves
papers.abstract: We express Néron functions on Jacobians of odd-degree hyperelliptic curves of arbitrary genus in terms of admissible pairings, using the pullback of the theta divisor via a generalized Abel--Jacobi morphism. Over non-archimedean local fields, we relate Néron functions to local Néron pairings on the curve and, moreover, deduce a comparison between unramified $p$-adic Néron functions and unramified local Coleman--Gross height functions. Furthermore, we decompose the Néron function into an intersection term $I$ and a Green function term $T$, and compute $T$ for specific semistable reduction types. We compare our decomposition with other decompositions in the literature.

papers.title: Path-constrained Packing on Trees
The Limits of Closed-Form Couplings for Few-Step Generation
Intersection theory and Chern classes on normal varieties II
papers.abstract: We prove a uniform bound linear in the rank for the local correction terms in the Riemann--Roch formula for reflexive sheaves on normal surfaces over algebraically closed fields of arbitrary characteristic. We also establish the usual tensor and symmetric-power formulas for second Chern characters and prove Wahl's asymptotic Riemann--Roch conjecture and its higher-rank generalization. These results yield second Chern classes of reflexive sheaves on arbitrary normal projective varieties, compatible with pullback by finite surjective morphisms. We characterize their discriminants as infima of normalized discriminants of compatible vector bundles on smooth alterations. As applications we prove Bogomolov's inequality, effective restriction and boundedness theorems on normal projective varieties, a Miyaoka-type inequality, and a Segre-class criterion for bigness of reflexive sheaves on normal surfaces.

papers.title: Explicit Tartakowsky theorem and universality criterion sets over totally real number fields
papers.abstract: We prove an explicit version of Tartakowsky's theorem over all totally real number fields. Namely, a positive definite integral lattice of rank at least five represents every totally positive integer that it represents locally, provided that the norm of the integer exceeds an explicit bound, exponential in powers of the volume of the lattice and of the discriminant of the field. As an application, we give explicit criterion sets for universal quadratic forms over all but finitely many real quadratic fields. Finally, we determine the minimal criterion sets for an infinite family of real quadratic fields.

papers.title: Out-of-training properties in frozen interatomic potential embeddings are decodable and ordered by physical scale
papers.abstract: Machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) are trained on energies, forces and stresses, yet their frozen representations can predict other materials properties. We probe ORB-v3 and UMA-S across layers, read-outs and equivariant channels for nine properties of 154,875 Materials Project crystals. Both models outperform composition-only descriptors on all targets, including five outside their training objectives; errors in physical units help assess potential screening applications. Optimal depth varies by property, consistent with a physical-scale ordering. Random-weight controls reveal strongly property-dependent benefits of pretraining. UMA-S's rotation-invariant angular channels improve crystal-system classification, while higher scores from its full tensor disappear under rotation; matched-model controls do not isolate equivariance as the explanation. Accuracy varies across different probes, but nearest-neighbour prediction often approaches XGBoost performance, even though materials do not form distinct clusters according to their properties. We also test whether a linear predictor trained on one model's embeddings can predict properties using the other model's embeddings after a learned linear transformation. Predictive accuracy is largely preserved, despite differences in which atoms the two models place close together. These results guide the reuse of frozen MLIP representations for materials prediction.

papers.title: ReuseMem: One Memory, Multiple Goals in Robot Manipulation
VAE Rhythm: Temporal Decoding Traces for AI-Generated Video Detection
Intransigence or compromise: concatenated opinion dynamics with voting feedback
Global analysis of the $ρ$ resonance in lattice QCD
papers.abstract: We present a lattice-QCD study of the $\rho$ resonance in which we address the quark-mass and lattice-spacing dependence in a novel way using a global analysis of four $N_f=2+1$ ensembles. We parametrize discretization effects in the lattice energy levels and not in the scattering amplitude, which is defined in the continuum. We describe the amplitude using a $K$-matrix parameterization, which contains the light- and strange-quark mass dependence. By varying the parameterizations of quark-mass and lattice-spacing dependence, we examine the sensitivity of the physical-limit $\rho$ pole position to these choices and obtain the result $\sqrt{s}_\rho = 744(11)(7) - i\,69(7)(3)~\text{MeV}$ from a model average.

papers.title: Searching for Autoregressive Neural Architectures from Fundamental Operations
Reversal of dynamical backaction and cooling below the quantum backaction limit in Floquet-driven multimode optomechanical resonators
papers.abstract: Dynamical backaction describes how a driven cavity field responds with delay to mechanical motion, and can be used to cool that motion toward its quantum ground state or amplify it into self-oscillation. Control over this interaction underpins laser cooling, high-fidelity state preparation, quantum transduction, and phonon lasing. In conventional cavity optomechanics, both the sign and the magnitude of the optical damping are dictated by the laser detuning, and cooling is bounded by quantum backaction (QBA), the optomechanical analogue of the Doppler limit in cold atoms. We show, in theory and experiment, that dynamical backaction can be strongly enhanced in multimode optomechanical resonators driven by time-varying (Floquet) optical fields. A modulated drive couples a sideband-unresolved MHz mode to a sideband-resolved GHz mode through the shared cavity, replacing the QBA limit of the target mode by the occupancy of the auxiliary mode. Experimentally, we cool the MHz mode to $47 \pm 13$ phonons, about half its single-mode QBA limit and an order of magnitude below what single-tone backaction reaches at the same intracavity photon number. The character of the interaction can moreover be completely inverted at fixed laser detuning, turning cooling into amplification and vice versa, controlled solely by the modulation frequency. Floquet driving thus extends open-loop quantum control, which requires no measurement or feedback, to mechanical resonators outside the resolved-sideband regime.

papers.title: Impact of the Initial Lorentz Factor on Kinetic Instabilities, Magnetic-Field Evolution, and Particle Acceleration in Relativistic Jets
papers.abstract: We investigate how the initial Lorentz factor shapes the evolution of relativistic jets---a key open question in high-energy astrophysics. Using global three-dimensional particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations with cylindrical jet geometry on a Cartesian grid, we analyze the self-consistent evolution of relativistic electron--positron and electron--ion jets from active galactic nuclei (AGN) and their interaction with the ambient medium. We implement an injection scheme that assigns space- and time-dependent velocities to injected particles and simulate jets with initial Lorentz factors of $\gamma_{0} = 10$ and 15. Jets with the higher Lorentz factor ($\gamma_{0} = 15$) exhibit stronger electron collimation, whereas those with $\gamma_{0} = 10$ show larger growth rates of kinetic instabilities during the linear stage. In both cases, a non-oscillatory electric field accelerates and decelerates charged particles throughout the linear and nonlinear stages. Upon entering the nonlinear regime, the initial toroidal magnetic field undergoes significant amplification driven by the Weibel instability (WI), the kinetic Kelvin--Helmholtz instability (kKHI), and the mushroom instability (MI), and subsequently reorganizes into complex topologies. In the late nonlinear stage, magnetic islands with randomly swirling fields indicate a highly turbulent magnetic structure. These findings demonstrate that global 3D~PIC modeling is essential for capturing the interplay among kinetic instabilities, magnetic turbulence, and particle acceleration in relativistic outflows, bridging microscopic plasma physics with macroscopic observations of AGN jets and gamma-ray bursts.

papers.title: Equivariant geometry of quadrics blown-up along a twisted quartic
papers.abstract: We prove that $G$-Fano threefolds which are given by the blow-up of a smooth quadric along a twisted quartic curve are $G$-birationally superrigid if and only if $G$ is isomorphic to $\mathfrak{A}_5\times\mathbb{Z}_2$. We also prove that the action of $G$ is linearisable if and only if $G$ does not contain a subgroup isomorphic to $\mathbb{Z}_2^3$.

papers.title: Source-Free Domain Adaptation for Multi-Label Image Classification: A Framework, Baselines, and Benchmark
Compact Dielectric Barrier Discharge Source for a Pulsed Supersonic Beam of Metastable Triplet H$_2$
papers.abstract: We present a compact dielectric barrier discharge (DBD) source for producing pulsed supersonic beams of metastable molecules, designed to mount directly onto existing gas valves without modification. Unlike plate or corona discharge sources, the DBD produces no static electric field in the expansion zone and relies on capacitively coupled microdischarges that are inherently self-limiting. Charge accumulation on the dielectric terminates each event within nanoseconds and locally suppresses re-ignition, so that successive microdischarges are distributed across the nozzle. Arc formation and the associated hot spots are thereby prevented, and the gas is excited uniformly over the duration of the pulse. The source requires only a single custom ceramic nozzle and a compact printed circuit board (PCB) carrying the drive electronics, mounted directly in front of the valve. The high-voltage pulses are generated in-vacuum on the PCB from a DC supply voltage. Complete design files, circuit schematics, fabrication details, and validated simulation files are provided to allow straightforward reproduction. The DBD is applied to produce H$_2$ in the metastable c$^3\Pi_u^-$ state. This state can be used as an intermediate step for state-selective preparation of H$_2^+$ molecular ions by pulsed field ionization of optically prepared molecular Rydberg states, without requiring vacuum-ultraviolet radiation. We characterize the source by time-of-flight and Resonance-Enhanced Multiphoton Ionization (REMPI) spectroscopy, obtaining an excitation fraction on the order of $10^{-8}$ into the metastable state. The dependence of the yield on stagnation pressure and discharge voltage is consistent with collisional quenching as the dominant pressure-dependent loss.

papers.title: CivilBench: Benchmarking Vision-Language Models for Multimodal Information Integration in Civil Engineering
GRAZE: Text-Free Grasp Synthesis for Unseen Objects from Human Gaze
ASDL: A Fast Vector Approximation Algorithm for Multiplierless Designs of Convolutional Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Matrix multiplications are one of the main computational bottlenecks in neural networks. The calculation reduces to numerous sums of partial products, which scale with the total number of Signed Power of Two (SPT) values in the multiplier matrix. Minimizing the SPT count can significantly reduce the computational this http URL this context, we present a Sum Of (signed) Powers Of Two (SOPOT) vector approximation algorithm that limits SPT counts, namely the Accelerated Signed Digit Loading (ASDL) algorithm. This approximation algorithm converts ResNet50 $10$ times faster than its predecessor MPGBP, while being more precise. We apply this method to the pre-trained coefficients of different convolutional neural networks, achieving $80.41\%$ ImageNet accuracy down from $81.3\%$, at an average of only $1.5$ active bits per coefficient. This is done without any retraining or calibration, which are typically required for the most aggressive quantization methods. Our approach offers a promising direction for neural network inference with higher energy efficiency and fewer hardware requirements: we anticipate up to $10$ times improvement over float16 inference.

papers.title: Beyond Family Labels: A Taxonomic Ornstein-Uhlenbeck Prior for Avian 3D Shape Recovery
Evaluation of Performance of the p-stop fabrication process variations in ATLAS18 strip sensors, Pre- and Post-Irradiation
papers.abstract: The High-Luminosity upgrade of the Large Hadron Collider (HL-LHC) requires the replacement of the ATLAS Inner Detector with a new all-silicon Inner Tracker (ITk). Radiation-hard n-in-p micro-strip sensors were developed for use in the ITk. During quality control (QC) and quality assurance (QA) procedures performed on ATLAS18 production sensors and test chips, ATLAS ITk strip sensor institutes identified instances of low p-stop density in certain production batches. To investigate the origin of these issues and to try some technological improvements, two dedicated sample batches with four variations of the p-stop fabrication process were produced. These process types (1-4) were systematically evaluated to determine their effectiveness and uniformity. In total, 56 full-size sensors, along with numerous miniature sensors and test chips, were tested. A number of samples were used in the irradiation campaign reaching the maximum expected levels for the HL-LHC operation after 10 years - with neutrons up to 1.6E15 neq/cm2, and with gamma rays from a 60Co source up to 66 Mrad. The goal of this evaluation program is to assess the impact of of p-stop fabrication process variations on interstrip isolation performance and to provide feedback for future sensor development. This paper describes the applied test procedures and presents the corresponding results, which demonstrate good sensor performance for all investigated p-stop types. The findings confirm the reliability of the evaluated designs and identify specific advantages that can inform further optimization of strip sensor fabrication.

papers.title: Design of nSPIRAL: a Neutron Spectrometric Position-Weighted Radial Array Long-Counter
papers.abstract: We present here the design of a neutron long counter intended to measure neutrons originating from radioactive decays or nuclear reactions. Like other similar detectors, it relies on a moderator (polyethylene) and $^{3}$He tubes. A novel feature of our design is the use of the weighting technique to achieve an efficiency that is virtually independent of the energy spectrum of the neutrons being measured; a property known as \textit{flat efficiency}. This approach offers two primary advantages: it yields a flatter efficiency response than conventional analysis methods, and it provides greater flexibility regarding the geometry of the long counter. The latter has enabled us to design the detector with almost every $^{3}$He tube positioned at a different distance from the neutron source, which allows us to perform not only neutron counting but also neutron spectroscopy.

papers.title: ForceHarness: Turning Force into Action and Physics for Frozen Frontier Models
MedicalDPO: Multi-Objective Direct Preference Optimization for CT to PET Translation
Design of an optimal positive state observer for a diffusion system with point observation
papers.abstract: An optimal state observer design problem for a diffusion system with point observation is studied. As the considered system is positive, the analysis takes into account this additional condition. The solution of the optimization problem is derived by means of a discretization approach, which consists in considering the analogous problem adapted for a spatially discretized version of the pure diffusion system.

papers.title: Inference Equivalence and Quotient Coding
SWE-WhatIf: Simulating Real Users of Coding Agents from Recorded Session
Conflict-Aware Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation in Aligned Action Spaces for Cross-Game Generalization
On Chen's Extended Action for $κ(R,T)$ Gravity: Gravity in a Polarizable Medium, Material Folds and a No-Bounce Theorem
papers.abstract: Chen's local adjoint action reproduces the field equations of $\kappa(R,T)$ from a local variational principle, and we show that it does physical work. In flat FLRW, Dirac reduction gives a Hamiltonian independent of $\kappa(T)$ on regular branches, where the coupling enters through a second-class matter constraint. The physical stress tensor is not generally conserved, but a dressed particle number is. An exact decomposition of the effective source motivates a polarizable-medium interpretation: $\kappa=0$ corresponds to total screening, the repulsive phase to overscreening, and a fold of the matter map to saturation. For linear coupling and dust, the expanding low-density branch has a past endpoint at the fold, where the volume is minimal and the density reaches $\rho_c/2$ at finite curvature. Dirac consistency rules out smooth Hamiltonian continuation through the fold. More generally, a flat-FLRW bounce is excluded for $\kappa>0$, positive density and $w>-1$. The linear dust model reproduces the effective Friedmann equation of loop quantum cosmology (LQC), but the two models obey different conservation laws. An effective pressure $-\rho^2/\rho_c$ restores the homogeneous LQC dynamics, and the fold density coincides with the signature-change threshold in the deformed-algebra approach to LQC. The reduced dust constraint admits an exactly solvable Koopman--von Neumann transport quantization and the adjoint field acts as a response variable, motivating an open-system interpretation.

papers.title: Stochastic control representations for extremal solutions of HJB Dirichlet problems with measurable coefficients
papers.abstract: We study stochastic control problems for uniformly elliptic controlled diffusions on bounded domains whose coefficients are merely measurable in the state variable and whose drift is dominated by an $L_d$-function. The associated Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) Dirichlet problems may have more than one $L_p$-viscosity solution, so that the equation alone does not determine the value function. We show that the control problem selects the minimal solution: for all $p$ in a range $(d_0,d)$ determined by the spatial dimension, the ellipticity constant and the drift bound, the value function is the minimal $L_p$-viscosity supersolution of the HJB Dirichlet problem. In particular, every continuous $L_p$-viscosity supersolution bounds the optimal cost from above, which yields a one-sided verification theorem without regularity assumptions. We further prove the existence of optimal relaxed control rules for running costs dominated by an $L_p$-function, and the lower semicontinuity of the value function under perturbations of the coefficients. An example shows that upper semicontinuity may fail even when the coefficients are Lipschitz continuous in the control variable and the approximating coefficients are smooth, so that regularization may overestimate the optimal cost. The proof approximates arbitrary supersolutions from below by Sobolev supersolutions of HJB equations whose coefficients are modified only on sets of vanishing measure, and passes to the limit by means of Krylov estimates and martingale problem techniques.

papers.title: Higher-point amplitudes and recursion relations from the worldsheet in complex Liouville string
papers.abstract: We consider multipoint perturbative string amplitudes in genus zero in complex Liouville string theory (CLS) in the worldsheet approach. Based on explicit worldsheet calculations and analytic bootstrap, we first compute correlators involving ground ring operators, which additionally depend on a choice of integration cycle on the moduli space. Using this result and higher equations of motion in Liouville theory, we calculate higher-point tachyon correlators with one degenerate field and explain what contributions were missed in previous attempts to apply this method in the literature. This allows us to derive a recursion formula, which agrees with the general recursion for amplitudes known from "matrix model" approach to CLS. We also propose an expression for correlators with ground ring insertions in terms of tautological classes on the moduli space of curves and comment on generalization of these results to the case of rational minimal strings.

papers.title: A hyperhamiltonian approach to symmetry of the Dirac equation
papers.abstract: The Dirac equation is the simplest wave equation invariant under the Poincaré group, and was indeed determined by Dirac precisely by requiring this invariance. Moreover it is invariant under dilations of the wave function, as follows by its linear character. It is known that the Dirac equation possesses, besides these, other symmetries, which in this sense are the special part of the Dirac equation's full symmetry. In previous work we have shown that the Dirac equation can be cast in hyperhamiltonian terms. Here we show that the symmetries can also be described in hyperhamiltonian terms.

papers.title: A High-Resolution TOA Estimation Algorithm Based on Compressed Sensing for Coherent Multi-Band Signals
papers.abstract: High-resolution time-of-arrival (ToA) estimation is crucial for accurate ranging and localization in future wireless networks. While multi-band operation can synthesize a large virtual bandwidth by probing several separated subbands, the resulting non-contiguous frequency layout induces pronounced sidelobes and dense local maxima in the delay response, making reliable ToA estimation challenging. This paper studies coherent multi-band ToA estimation from a single multi-band channel state information (CSI) snapshot. We derive a multiband least-squares formulation and analyze its point-spread function (PSF) and Cramer-Rao bound (CRB) to characterize the effects of the subband layout on delay accuracy and sidelobe ambiguity. Building on this analysis, we propose a low complexity two-stage particle swarm optimization estimator and incorporate it into orthogonal matching pursuit with a RELAX-type cyclic refinement procedure for multipath delay estimation, mitigating basis mismatch and improving robustness to the dense local maxima induced by non-contiguous multi-band layouts. Numerical results are consistent with the PSF and CRB analyses and show that the proposed framework approaches the CRB in the single-path setting and achieves accurate multipath delay estimation with low computational complexity. Real channel measurements further validate the predicted impact of different subband layouts on delay-estimation performance.

papers.title: AudioTrace: File-Level Membership Detection for Audio Large Language Models
Experimental Evidence of Elastic Instability in Viscoelastic Kolmogorov Flow
papers.abstract: Inertialess elastic instabilities can profoundly affect transport in complex-fluid flows, from mixing in microfluidic devices and displacement through porous media to polymer processing. While such instabilities are well understood in flows with curved streamlines, their origin in rectilinear flows like the prototypical Kolmogorov flow remains unresolved. Here, we report the first experimental evidence of the center-mode elastic instability, at vanishing inertia, in a confined quasi-two-dimensional viscoelastic Kolmogorov flow, driven by electromagnetic forcing. The instability is characterized by the emergence of "arrow-shaped" structures in the velocity field, which fluctuates chaotically as the forcing strength increases. We reproduce these observations in simulations of the Oldroyd-B model and trace the dynamics in the confined flow to the travelling arrowhead structures that emerge from the center-mode instability of unbounded Kolmogorov flow. Our work establishes a generic route to purely elastic instability in rectilinear flows, broadening the conditions under which elastic turbulence and enhanced mixing can arise.

papers.title: Closing the loop on memory: accurate, shallow and transferable decoding of quantum LDPC codes
papers.abstract: Quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes have attracted interest for fault-tolerant quantum computing because their high-rate constructions offer a route to reduced qubit overhead. Realizing this potential requires reliable decoding. Belief propagation (BP) forms the basis of many qLDPC decoders, but can fail to converge under circuit-level noise. Memory-based variants can improve convergence, yet selecting memory strengths that work reliably across different syndromes remains challenging. Here we introduce TEMPO-BP, which adapts each variable's memory strength to the evolving decoding state through local feedback. On the gross code at a physical error rate of 0.4%, single-run TEMPO-BP achieves a per-shot logical failure rate of 0.73%, compared with 2.51% for BP+OSD+CS-10. Ensembles of 10-15 concurrent instances match or lower failure counts relative to Relay-BP-5 at all ten tested operating points, with per-instance iteration caps at least tenfold lower than its serial limit. Without retuning, the gross-code parameters yield fewer observed failures than Relay-BP-5 in its published gross-code configuration across four additional code families. Ablations support state-dependent memory control, while a loop-gain analysis characterizes specific amplification modes in the decoding dynamics.

papers.title: State-Message Interaction Adapter for Cross-Domain Few-Shot Segmentation
CompCert4Lean: Porting a Verified C Compiler to Lean in Six Weeks with Parallel Coding Agents
Think2Listen: Evidence-Centric Learning For Agentic Audio Understanding With LALMS
Subwavelength confinement of optical and acoustic waves for enhancing Brillouin gain in a planar waveguide structure
papers.abstract: We propose a planar waveguide structure consisting of two layers separated by a gap that provides subwavelength confinement of optical and acoustic modes and a large overlap integral between them. This, in turn, leads to an increase in Brillouin gain. Using the structure of two Si$_3$N$_4$ layers with a subwavelength gap from SiO$_2$ as an example, we demonstrate that a hybridized transverse-magnetic (TM) optical mode exhibits strong field confinement in the SiO$_2$ gap. Simultaneously, a high-frequency acoustic mode can be confined in the same gap, providing a high spatial overlap between the optical and acoustic fields. This provides a high opto-acoustic interaction with a Brillouin gain up to $5$ W$^{-1}$m$^{-1}$. The proposed structure is compatible with planar photonic integration and offers a promising platform for compact, low-threshold Brillouin lasers and coherent phonon generation.

papers.title: The random analyst
papers.abstract: Modern data-analysis pipelines increasingly involve searching among candidate analyses before reporting an estimate. We investigate the replicability of the resulting conclusions by studying independent repetitions of the entire search-and-report procedure on new samples. Can the reported estimates become increasingly similar across studies while remaining systematically displaced from the scientific target? We first show that this can happen in a simple Gaussian model. Although every prespecified candidate estimator is unbiased and consistent, searching over exponentially many candidates within each study yields a selected estimator converging to a limit different from the target, a selection-induced pseudotruth. Across independent repetitions, the reported estimates thus become replicable but systematically inaccurate, while the selected candidates differ with probability tending to one. We then study dependent Gaussian candidates, including marginal regression coefficients, and show that Gaussian width governs the displacement, which persists when squared width is of the same order as sample size. Metric entropy and generic chaining reveal that the effective complexity of the search is determined by the geometry of statistically distinguishable analyses rather than by their nominal number. Large-deviation arguments further extend the phenomenon beyond Gaussian models. Numerical agreement between independent studies therefore need not indicate either a stable analytical path or proximity to the scientific target.

papers.title: Success Probability of Block-Encoding Methods
papers.abstract: Block-encoding methods apply nonunitary functions $f(\widetilde H)$ of a normalized Hermitian operator on a quantum computer, but only upon a successful postselection, which introduces a shot overhead rarely included in resource estimates. We analyze the success probability $p^{(f)}_{\mathrm{success}}=\sum_n w_n|f(\tilde E_n)|^2$ of three constructions, namely linear combination of unitaries (LCU), qubitization and quantum singular value transformation (QSVT), where $w_n$ are the weights of the input state on the eigenstates of $\widetilde H$. Using the one-dimensional Hubbard model with up to 14 sites (35 qubits), we show that for LCU, the success probability is bounded by the squared ratio between the spectral norm and the $1$-norm of the Pauli decomposition, and that for a Hartree--Fock input it plateaus with system size while the ground-state overlap keeps decreasing. For qubitization, it oscillates with the Chebyshev degree, and favorable degrees can be identified from a few dominant spectral components or predicted from shallow-degree data. For QSVT, the polynomial normalization constant directly sets the success probability, and a tight certified bound balances it against phase-finding robustness. An application to quantum Krylov methods shows a nonuniform shot overhead across Krylov moments. The success probability should therefore be part of the resource estimation of block-encoding-based algorithms.

papers.title: SemiNovo: Learning Beyond Search-Identified Spectra for De Novo Peptide Sequencing
Subexponential algorithms for structural parameterizations of Vertex Cover in geometric graphs
MORE: Merge Once, Route Early for Training-Free Multi-Subject Composition from Large LoRA Pools
Counting What Matters: Reducing Redundant Object Detections in Overlapping UAV Mapping Imagery for Disaster Response
Finite-Step Algorithms for Input-Constrained Control Barrier Function-Based Safety Filters
Gorenstein toric Fano $d$-varieties have Picard ranks at most $2d$
papers.abstract: We show that the Picard rank of $d$-dimensional Gorenstein toric Fano varieties is at most $2d$. This generalizes Batyrev's conjecture of Picard ranks for smooth toric Fano varieties, which was proved by Casagrande for all $\mathbb{Q}$-factorial Gorenstein toric Fano varieties. The convex-geometric proof is a generalization of Casagrande's proof and Eikelberg's theory of non-$\mathbb{Q}$-factorial toric Picard groups, with key ideas from work of Debarre, Øbro, Fujita and the first author. The proof was found using ChatGPT 6.1.

papers.title: Semantic Validity vs. Graphical Arrangement in Visualization Grammars
Sage S2.1 Flash Technical Report
Centralizers in Catalan Monoids
papers.abstract: Fix a chain $X_n=\{1<\cdots<n\}$, where $n$ is a positive integer. The Catalan monoid $\mathcal{C}_n$ consists of all decreasing and order-preserving transformations of $X_n$, with function composition as the operation. For $\beta\in\mathcal{C}_n$, its centralizer is $C(\beta)=\{\alpha\in\mathcal{C}_n:\alpha\beta=\beta\alpha\}$. We characterize the elements of $C(\varepsilon)$, $C(\mu)$, and $C(\beta)$, where $\varepsilon\in\mathcal{C}_n$ is an idempotent, $\mu\in\mathcal{C}_n$ is a nilpotent, and $\beta\in\mathcal{C}_n$ is a general element. For an idempotent $\varepsilon\in\mathcal{C}_n$, we derive formulas for the cardinality of $C(\varepsilon)$, as well as formulas for the numbers of idempotents and nilpotents of $C(\varepsilon)$. We relate indexing sets arising in these formulas to Dyck paths and Narayana numbers. For a nilpotent $\mu\in\mathcal{C}_n$, we present algorithms that construct $C(\mu)$, its subset of idempotents, and its subsemigroup of nilpotents, thereby determining their cardinalities. We also describe the nilpotents whose centralizers consist only of idempotents, of nilpotents together with the identity, or of nilpotents and idempotents. We extend these descriptions to arbitrary elements of $\mathcal{C}_n$. To obtain our results, we represent $\beta\in\mathcal{C}_n$ as a sequence $\langle T_1,\ldots,T_m\rangle$ of rooted trees. The sets of vertices of the trees form a partition of $X_n$. Each tree is level-ordered, which means that it can be drawn in such a way that moving from the root down, level by level, from left to right at each level, we pass through an increasing sequence of consecutive elements of $X_n$.

papers.title: Trade Tensions Meet the Gig Economy: Evidence from the 2025 Halving of Chinese Travel to Japan
papers.abstract: How do geopolitical shocks to services exports reach local labor markets? Using China's November 2025 Japan travel advisory and postings on Japan's largest spot-work platform, we provide the first such evidence for the gig economy. Posted hourly wages fall immediately and persistently in prefectures more dependent on Chinese visitors, relative to others, whereas postings, hours, and employment show no robust change. Wages fall more for early morning and daytime shifts, when hotels and shops hire, than for evening and night shifts. Where each shift is priced anew, a services-trade shock lowers the price of labor in the hours it hits.

papers.title: CoopDistill: Equilibrium-Guided Multi-Agent Policy Distillation for Cooperative Driving
Reconstruction and Forecast of Extreme Waves from a Single Observation
papers.abstract: The state space of a dynamical system can, under suitable conditions, be reconstructed from a single observational time-series through delay-coordinate embedding. However, reconstructing the spatiotemporal evolution of nonlinear water waves from highly sparse measurements remains a considerable challenge. Here, by combining deep learning, compressed sensing, and the self-similarity properties of unidirectional nonlinear water wave evolution equation, we show that the evolving surface elevation of a highly nonlinear wave field can be reconstructed from observations collected at a {\it single} measurement location. We subsequently use these reconstructions to forecast rogue waves associated with self-focusing soliton dynamics from point observations obtained in controlled water wave tank experiments, demonstrating excellent agreement with measurements of the fully evolved wave field. Our results show that extreme wave events can be forecast from remarkably sparse observations and provide a framework that may be extended to other nonlinear dispersive systems governed by the interplay of dispersion and nonlinearity.

papers.title: The $N$-channel white-noise Schrödinger operator in all three Dyson classes. I. Explicit stationary admittance distribution, density of states and outgoing Kontsevich matrix Airy integrals
papers.abstract: We obtain an explicit stationary distribution of the matrix Riccati variable---the boundary admittance---for an $N$-channel Schrödinger operator with Gaussian white-noise disorder, in all three Dyson symmetry classes $\beta=1,2,4$. Uniform absorption regularizes the Riccati dynamics, and the distribution's normalization factorizes into outgoing Kontsevich matrix Airy integrals. This gives a common route to the density of states and the sum of Lyapunov exponents, extending Halperin's scalar solution to coupled channels. Exact finite-$N$ formulas connect two spectral regimes: the Lifshitz tail, including its symmetry-dependent prefactor, and the collective large-$N$ edge. We reduce the $\beta=4$ and even-$N$ $\beta=1$ problems to unitary orthogonal polynomials and an auxiliary recursion. Their critical double-scaling limit yields edge profiles on the $N^{-4/5}$ energy scale, governed by a complex Painlevé-I tritronquée solution and a linear auxiliary equation. We conjecture that these profiles describe a universal edge regime of random band matrices.

papers.title: Large pseudo-orbital magnetic moment of magnons in CrI$_3$ nanotubes
authors: J. Fernández-Rossier (1 and 2) ((1) Universidad de Alicante
papers.abstract: Recently discovered CrI$_3$ nanotubes are expected to host unusual radial magnetic order states, on account of the strong out-of-plane magnetic anisotropy of the two-dimensional parent material. The detection of these peculiar magnetic states is challenging, and motivates the quest for unique features that can be probed experimentally. Using linear spin-wave theory, we show that an axial magnetic field tilts the radial phase into a conical one that threads the tube with an Aharonov-Bohm flux for magnons. This flux endows magnons with a pseudo-orbital magnetic moment, reaching approximately six Bohr magnetons, three times conventional magnon spin moment, and therefore detectable through magnon spectroscopy, providing a smoking gun for the radial and conical magnetic order in CrI$_3$ nanotubes.

papers.title: What Makes a Good Move? Learning to Act from Experience in Visual Worlds
Boundedness properties of bilinear Fourier integral operators with complex phases
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate mapping properties on Lebesgue spaces of bilinear Fourier integral operators (FIOs) with complex phases. Indeed, we provide for bilinear Fourier integral operators with complex phases boundedness theorems for the corresponding Seeger-Sogge-Stein orders, including the endpoint estimates. Our results extend the same boundedness property in the case of real-valued phases proved by Rodriguez-López, Rule, and Staubach, and provide the bilinear version for the linear one proved earlier by Ruzhansky for phases of positive type. Also, our Seeger-Sogge-Stein theorem for bilinear operators with complex phases cannot be directly deduced from its real counterpart. A new approach used in this article consists of providing directly the boundedness theorems on Lebesgue spaces without the use of the multilinear Fefferman-Stein interpolation theorem. For this, a maximal function theorem due to Bourgain is applied. As a byproduct, we also consider transference boundedness theorems of FIOs with complex phases from $\mathbb{R}^n$ to the torus $\mathbb{T}^n\equiv \mathbb{R}^n/\mathbb{Z}^n$ and then, we provide new criteria for the boundedness of Fourier integral operators on the torus with complex phases (Fourier series operators in the sense of Ruzhansky and Turunen).

papers.title: A Hierarchically Compressed Immittance Operator Formulation for Fast Statics-to-Full-Wave Electromagnetic Simulation with the Boundary Element Method
Observing Earth's ionospheric irregularities from the Moon
papers.abstract: Radio signals that propagate through the Earth's ionosphere carry information about possible irregular plasma structures. Such irregularities manifest themselves as amplitude signatures that depend on the propagation and observation geometry [1, 2]. Conventional ground and low-Earth-orbit (LEO) measurements sample these effects close to Earth. Here we present a systematic characterization of terrestrial ionospheric irregularities using Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) amplitude observations from the lunar surface, at distances of approximately 356,000-398,000 km from Earth's surface [3]. Using nearly 93 h of 1-Hz lunar-surface observations of GPS L1/L5 and Galileo E1/E5a collected by the Lunar GNSS Receiver Experiment (LuGRE), we reconstruct the propagation and scanning geometry to characterize the spatiotemporal signatures of amplitude and phase fluctuations. At lunar distance, the Fresnel scale approaches its finite-source limit, extending the observations to a propagation regime beyond conventional near-Earth configurations. Detrended receiver-reported carrier-to-noise density ratios (${\delta}C/N_0$) reveal pronounced polar amplitude fluctuations at both frequency bands, also visible in the original measurements. Within the regions and local times sampled, large fluctuations occur in about 30% of valid one-minute polar windows, compared with less than 5% in either the equatorial or mid-latitude band. These findings support using the lunar surface as a vantage point for studying Earth's polar ionospheric irregularities and testing how propagation and scanning relative to the magnetic field shape their amplitude signatures. Future lunar observations could extend this approach to long-term monitoring of Earth's ionospheric irregularities

papers.title: Segregated normalized solutions for a nonlinear Schrödinger system with two mass constraints
papers.abstract: We study a two-component nonlinear Schrödinger system with two prescribed positive $L^2$ masses and a fixed competitive coupling $\beta<0$, for $N=1,2,3$ and $4\le p<2^*$. We first consider families whose peak heights diverge and whose components converge uniformly to zero away from disjoint finite peak sets. For such families, we prove that both Lagrange multipliers tend to $-\infty$ and that the mass of each component concentrates at its own peaks. We also construct positive multi-peak solutions near prescribed nondegenerate critical points of the respective potentials and compute the leading displacement of each peak. The target frequencies may grow at different rates, provided that $\Lambda_*\to\infty$ and $\log(2+\Lambda^*)=o(\sqrt{\Lambda_*})$, where $\Lambda_*$ and $\Lambda^*$ denote their minimum and maximum. In the $L^2$-noncritical case, the first frequency correction is minus the average potential at the prescribed points. In the $L^2$-critical case, the leading mass term is independent of the frequencies. For each component, we compute the mass correction of order \(\lambda_i^{-2}\) in terms of the sum of the Laplacians of its potential at the prescribed points. When both sums are nonzero, these corrections determine the leading-order asymptotics of the two frequencies and the side from which each self-interaction coefficient approaches its critical value.

Hunting dark matter: the present and future of direct particle detection
papers.abstract: The nature of dark matter remains one of the major open questions in particle physics and cosmology. Direct detection experiments aim to identify dark matter particles through their interactions with ordinary matter, but despite substantial improvements in experimental sensitivity, no conclusive detection has been achieved. In this review, we provide a comprehensive overview of the present status and future prospects of direct particle detection, focusing on searches for dark matter particles from the Galactic halo. We introduce the theoretical framework for interpreting experimental results, including nuclear and electron scattering, collective excitations, particle absorption, and time- and direction-dependent signatures. We review the detection technologies employed in these searches, highlighting their operating principles, advantages, and limitations, as well as the calibration techniques and background mitigation strategies required to achieve high sensitivity. Particular emphasis is placed on experimental results reported since 2020, covering nuclear and electron recoil searches, annual modulation measurements, and directional detection. We also discuss experiments under construction and proposed future detectors, ranging from large-scale noble-liquid experiments to low-threshold technologies targeting sub-GeV dark matter. Finally, we examine the challenges that will shape the next generation of experiments, including the need for increasingly low energy thresholds, improved background understanding and discrimination, and the growing importance of neutrino-induced backgrounds. The diversity and complementarity of detector technologies will remain essential for exploring the dark matter parameter space and establishing the nature of any potential signal.

papers.title: Singular Kähler-Ricci solitons and complete gradient shrinking Kähler-Ricci solitons on non-compact manifolds
papers.abstract: We construct a class of complete gradient shrinking Kähler-Ricci solitons on non-compact toric manifolds by exhausting a family of singular Kähler-Ricci solitons associated to multiple divisors. The construction method will be also extended on non-compact $\mathbf G$-manifolds.

papers.title: Rigidity of Stationary Domains for Robin Torsion in the Plane
papers.abstract: For every positive Robin parameter, we prove that a bounded simply connected planar domain with $C^{2,\alpha}$ boundary is stationary for Robin torsional rigidity under an area constraint if and only if it is a disk. No convexity, curvature bound, or additional condition on the overdetermined constant is assumed. The difficulty is that the stationarity condition couples the boundary trace of the Robin torsion function, its tangential derivative, and the boundary curvature. We encode this condition through a normalized Airy stress function and construct a superharmonic auxiliary function by a quartic minimization calibrated on disks. The boundary structure of this auxiliary function allows us to identify a point where it attains its minimum on the boundary and has a nonnegative outward normal derivative. The strong maximum principle and Hopf's boundary point lemma then force the auxiliary function to be constant. Consequently, for any stationary domain in the class under consideration, the Robin torsion function has a constant boundary trace, and the stationarity condition forces the boundary curvature to be constant.

papers.title: Fast HOSVD via Randomized Preconditioning and Mixed Precision
Relaxing the i.i.d. state preparation assumption with the block QKD protocol
papers.abstract: In this work, we propose a novel approach to handling the independent and identically distributed assumption for the state preparation in prepare-and measure QKD protocols. Contrary to previous approaches, we do not prove the security using sub-protocols, and instead opt to guarantee security in the presence of correlations by dividing the communication into finite blocks of consecutive pulses, and adding an additional assumption of no dependence between each block. In turn we obtain a protocol which uses only a relaxed i.i.d. assumption and is easier to implement than subprotocol-style approaches since it does not require separate statistics for each sub-protocol, whose number grows with the correlation length of the underlying dependency.

papers.title: The imprint of neutron escape on non-thermal protons in AGN coronae
papers.abstract: The coronae of active galactic nuclei (AGN) are promising sites of proton acceleration to hundreds of TeV, potentially accounting for the neutrino excess from NGC 1068 reported by IceCube. We show that photohadronic proton-to-neutron conversion provides an important proton escape channel, as neutrons can leave the corona well before decaying. In magnetized turbulent coronae, neutron escape can reduce the characteristic neutrino energy by up to a factor of four and the integrated neutrino luminosity by approximately 30% at a fixed non-thermal proton energy density. More strikingly, proton-to-neutron conversion offers an escape route roughly two orders of magnitude faster than proton diffusion, requiring a correspondingly larger proton injection rate to sustain the non-thermal population. The effect is considerably weaker when proton escape is already ballistic, as expected in magnetic-reconnection scenarios. Therefore, neutron escape is essential for quantitatively connecting neutrino emission from AGN coronae to the efficiency of proton injection into the acceleration process.

papers.title: On the invariants of L-functions of degree 2, II: twisted conductor
papers.abstract: We continue our study of the invariants of the $L$-functions of deree 2 twisted by Dirichlet characters. In a previous paper, we proved that twisting does not change degree and internal shift. Our aim now is to show a corresponding theorem for the conductor. This paper is intended as the second part of a series aiming to prove a general version of the Weil converse theorem with minimal assumptions on the shape of the functional equation of twists.

papers.title: Nonlinear Joint State and Noise Estimation under Packet Dropouts and Additive Measurement Corruption
papers.abstract: This paper investigates joint state and noise covariance estimation for nonlinear systems subject to dual reliability impairments: random packet dropouts and additive measurement corruption. This scenario poses challenging nonconjugate inference, as clean and corrupted measurements share an unknown baseline covariance $\boldsymbol{R}_k$ with fixed known corruption covariance $\boldsymbol{E}_k$. Packet reception is observable, whereas the authenticity of received measurements remains latent and must be inferred. To resolve this intractable estimation problem, we cast joint posterior inference as a variational optimization problem and develop a conjugate variational inference adaptive Kalman filter with dual reliability (CVIAKF-DR). The proposed method retains analytical updates for the prediction covariance and two reliability probabilities, while adopting CVI to estimate the state and baseline measurement covariance. The covariance update combines the analytical contribution from clean measurements with Monte Carlo gradient estimates for corrupted measurements. Numerical results on a re-entry tracking benchmark demonstrate the superior accuracy of the proposed method in both state and noise covariance estimation. Remarkably, even built upon the linear Kalman filtering (KF) framework that is originally designed for linear systems, our method achieves more accurate estimation performance than dedicated nonlinear filtering algorithms based on the cubature Kalman filter (CKF).

papers.title: Body of Evidence: Triangulating 3D Human Pose with Geometry-Conditioned Depth
Maximum entropy reconstruction of the black hole greybody factors from its Korteweg-de Vries integrals
authors: (4) Institute of Space Studies of Catalonia (IEEC))
papers.abstract: The dynamics of perturbed non-rotating black holes (BHs) can be described by master wave equations with a potential barrier. Recent work has shown that these equations possess an infinite number of symmetries generated by the Korteweg-de Vries (KdV) hierarchy, leading to conserved quantities (KdV integrals) that fully determine the BH greybody factors via a moment problem. In this paper, we introduce and validate a new method to solve this moment problem using the maximum entropy principle. The method reconstructs, at each order of truncation, the least-biased transmission probability compatible with a finite set of KdV integrals, guaranteeing positivity by construction. We first validate the technique against the exactly solvable Pöschl-Teller potential. We then apply it to the Regge-Wheeler potential governing axial perturbations of a Schwarzschild BH, where no exact solution is available; the resulting reconstruction agrees closely with the fourth-order Wentzel-Kramers-Brillouin (WKB) approximation across several multipoles. This is the first application of the maximum entropy method to the reconstruction of BH greybody factors, demonstrating that a modest number of KdV integrals is sufficient to recover them accurately.

papers.title: The Velocity Curves and Three-Dimensional Kinematics of the Milky Way from Gaia DR3
papers.abstract: We investigate the fundamental kinematic parameters of stellar motions in the Milky Way using a statistical sample of 27,485,720 stars with measured three-dimensional velocities from the Gaia DR3 catalogue. From these data, we determine the local solar velocity $(U_{\odot},V_{\odot},W_{\odot}) = \left(10.5\pm0.7,14.5\pm0.9,7.33\pm0.1\right) ~\mathrm{km/s}$, the average rotation velocity\linebreak $\mathrm{V}_{0} = \left( 228\pm4\right) $ km/s, and the circular velocity $\mathrm{V}_{c} = \left( 234\pm4\right) $ {km/s,} both at the radius $R_{\odot}$. Next, within the range of $3-14$ kpc, we derive the Galactic circular velocity curve $\mathrm{V}_{c}(R)$ and determine the average spherical components of the stellar velocities as functions of both Galactocentric radius $R$ and distance from the Galactic plane $\left\vert Z\right\vert $. Two-dimensional $R-Z$ maps of these components reveal a complex three-dimensional kinematic structure. In particular, the pattern observed at $R\lesssim5$ kpc can be associated with the influence of the Galactic bar. To facilitate the description of the observations, we employ a simplified axisymmetric Monte Carlo model with several free parameters that reproduces the main kinematic trends.

papers.title: Linear Electrostatic Instabilities Driven by Relativistic Non-Maxwellian Pair Beams
papers.abstract: We investigate how non-Maxwellian momentum distributions affect the linear growth of electrostatic instabilities driven by relativistic pair beams, motivated by the lack of a universally accepted analytical description of blazar-induced pair beams. Different beam distributions are used to describe relativistic pair beams in analytical studies and particle-in-cell simulations. A systematic comparison is therefore needed to determine how the beam distribution influences the instability growth rates. We formulate the relativistic electrostatic response in the weak-beam limit for an anisotropic $\kappa$-type distribution and compare the resulting growth rates with those obtained for Gaussian and Maxwell--Jüttner distributions. We require $\kappa>3/2$ for a finite root-mean-square momentum spread. For the parameters considered, the $\kappa$-type distributions yield higher maximum growth rates than the Gaussian distribution, even when their mean momenta and momentum spreads are the same. The fastest-growing modes correspond to parallel propagation for the $\kappa$ and Gaussian distributions, whereas the Maxwell--Jüttner distribution exhibits its maximum for oblique propagation for a mildly relativistic beam. An additional calculation for a highly relativistic pair beam with $\kappa=2$ finds an oblique maximum of the electrostatic growth rate. The beam momentum distribution influences the linear growth of electrostatic instabilities under the conditions investigated.

papers.title: Towards wearable-scale, transition-aware sleep staging for clinical populations
Multivariable $(φ, N)$-modules and $(φ, N_\nabla)$-modules
papers.abstract: The goal of this article is to introduce the category of effective filtered multivariable $(\varphi, N)$-modules and the category of multivariable $(\varphi, N_\nabla)$-modules of finite $E_{\Delta}$-height over the rigid-analytic open polydisk $\mathcal{O}_{\Delta}$, and to establish an exact tensor equivalence between them. This generalizes Kisin's analytic classification of filtered $(\varphi, N)$-modules and provides the rigid-analytic foundation for multivariable $p$-adic Hodge theory.

papers.title: ScoutCache: Efficient Few-Step Autoregressive Video Diffusion via Conditional Readout and Selective Caching
