Gravitational collapse in Lorentz-violating gravity and the spin-0 mode
papers.abstract: Einstein-Aether theory is a theory of gravity with a preferred frame, in which Lorentz symmetry is broken by a dynamical unit timelike vector field. The theory is closely related to Horava gravity, and in spherically symmetric collapse the two produce the same dynamics. Both propagate a scalar (spin-0) mode besides the tensor mode and, in Einstein-Aether theory, the vector mode. The physical nature of the spin-0 mode has recently been called into question following the post-Newtonian analysis of Taherasghari and Will, whose post-Newtonian calculation of radiation reaction in compact binaries finds no trace of its speed in the energy loss, suggesting that the mode may not be a dynamical, energy-carrying wave. We test this with fully nonlinear evolutions of scalar-field collapse in spherical symmetry, where the spin-0 mode is the only radiative degree of freedom. The collapse emits an outgoing spin-0 wave that falls off as the inverse of the radius, travels at the speed predicted by the linear theory, and carries positive energy to infinity. The static aether configuration left around the black hole has negative energy instead, so that the horizon mass exceeds the ADM mass. For large couplings, collapse does not produce a black hole: we recover the transient white holes found by Akhoury, Garfinkle and Gupta, but at higher resolution the collapsing shell keeps steepening, not hidden behind any trapped surface, which may signal a naked singularity.

papers.title: POKE: Probe Offline, Keep Efficiently for Vision-Language-Action Models
EE-Motion: An EEG-based Web Architecture for Live Affective Music Recommendation
Probing the QCD critical point through linearized sound wave dispersion and attenuation at finite baryon density
papers.abstract: We investigate the linearized sound-channel response of a finite baryon density Israel-Stewart hydrodynamic system coupled to a parameterized equation of state containing a critical end point. The attenuation of sound is characterized by a threshold wavelength below which sound perturbations are strongly damped. We systematically study the dependence of this threshold scale on the non-universal parameters of the Beam Energy Scan Theory (BEST) equation of state framework. In our present study, the threshold wavelength remains finite but develops a pronounced peak in the vicinity of the critical end point, indicating strong absorption of sound modes on fireball-scale wavelengths. We further estimate the impact of this enhanced attenuation on the linearized anisotropic flow response and find a reduction of the elliptic and triangular flow harmonics near the critical region. Our results establish a phenomenological connection between critical sound attenuation, Mach cone like correlations, and the linearized flow response in baryon rich QCD matter. These results suggest a non-monotonic beam-energy dependence of the sound attenuation scale. Together with a corresponding suppression of Mach cone like correlations and the linearized anisotropic flow response, they may provide a consistent signature that the system trajectory passes close to the critical point of the chosen equation of state.

papers.title: Learning Morse Lyapunov functions through invertible neural networks
Sparse Attention for Visual Generation: Toward Algorithm-System Co-Design
Reconfigurable Dysprosium Isotope Mixtures with Selectable Quantum Statistics
papers.abstract: Dipolar quantum mixtures offer new opportunities to explore many-body phenomena shaped by long-range anisotropic interactions, intercomponent coupling, and quantum statistics. Here we develop a reconfigurable platform for bosonic and fermionic dysprosium isotope mixtures using a single-isotope-like optical layout. We time-multiplex the 421-nm light to generate isotope-selective slow-atom fluxes, while spectrally engineered 626-nm light provides simultaneous common-path narrow-line cooling and trapping. By reconfiguring optical frequencies, we prepare seven isotope pairs spanning Bose--Bose, Bose--Fermi, and Fermi--Fermi combinations, with continuous population-balance control through the 421-nm dwell-time allocation. Systematic comparisons with sequence-matched single-isotope references, from magneto-optical-trap loading and compression to optical-dipole-trap transfer, reveal nearly single-isotope-like performance for most combinations. The larger deviations occur only for certain isotope pairs and preparation stages, with controlled measurements revealing optical sensitivities during loading and additional losses under high-density conditions. Our results make isotope composition and quantum statistics selectable within a strongly dipolar system while largely preserving single-isotope preparation simplicity and performance, opening new possibilities for exploring multicomponent dipolar quantum matter.

papers.title: Risk-Aware Handover Management Approach for Non-Terrestrial Networks with the NTN-Connect Simulator
papers.abstract: The continuous movement of low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites in non-terrestrial networks (NTNs) leads to frequent handovers, requiring joint optimization of visibility duration, transmit power, and user quality-of-service (QoS). This work address this issue by proposing a risk-aware handover management framework that minimizes transmit power and maximizes admitted users under per-satellite power budgets and user-rate chance constraints, while a preference score term penalizes short duration associations. We decompose the resulting mixed-integer nonlinear program (MINLP) into an inner power allocation subproblem and an outer generalized assignment association subproblem. The inner subproblem reformulates the chance constraint into its deterministic counterpart using the value-at-risk (VaR) closed-form. The obtained transmit power allocation is then used in the association subproblem, which is solved optimally using an off-the-shelf solver. Finally, we employ the polynomial-complexity Hungarian algorithm to solve the relaxed assignment problem and enforce the per-satellite power budget using a knapsack algorithm. Simulations, using the proposed NTN-Connect simulator, on the OneWeb and Starlink constellations show that the proposed low-complexity solution achieves near-optimal performance and better performance compared to the risk-aware maximum stay (RA-MST) and risk-aware maximum received signal received power (RA-MRSRP) baselines. On the Starlink constellation, it increases the inter-handover interval (IHI) from $0.37$ to $1.47$~min, reducing the handover rate by $75\%$. At a maximum-IHI operating point, it reduces the total transmit power by 1.1 dBW (22\%) while increasing the admission rate from 97.4\% to 99.3\%.

papers.title: Bias Conditioning and Long-Range Electrostatics for Consistent Machine-Learning Potentials of Electrified Interfaces
papers.abstract: Machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) of electrified interfaces need the bias as input, but it is unclear whether a scalar electrode charge suffices and whether short-range models capture the non-local response. We add charge and field conditioning to short- and long-range MLIPs. State-of-the-art field-conditioned short-range models overpolarize thick water films nearly twofold and miss work-function shifts at stepped Pt. Our long-range model captures both, needs only the electrode charge at metals as input, and reproduces ab initio simulations of the Pt(111)--water interface.

papers.title: Bourgain's vector-valued Stein inequality implies superreflexivity
papers.abstract: We prove that if \(X\) is a Banach space for which Bourgain's vector-valued Stein inequality holds, then \(X\) is superreflexive. We also present an example of a superreflexive Banach space for which the vector-valued Stein property fails.

papers.title: Laser Processing for Energy Applications
papers.abstract: Laser processing has emerged as a transformative technology in the energy sector, enabling precise, efficient, and scalable solutions for energy generation, storage, and sustainability. This chapter explores the diverse applications of laser technology in energy applications. It begins with an overview of laser-driven inertial confinement fusion for energy production, highlighting key experimental facilities and crucial laser parameters. The role of lasers in solar energy harvesting is examined, including photovoltaic cell optimization, concentrated solar power, and laser-assisted recycling of solar modules. The chapter further reviews recent developments into laser-based techniques for enhancing electrochemical performance through surface texturing at various scales. Advancements in lithium-ion battery technology are also discussed, focusing on next-generation materials, battery manufacturing processes, and the impact of laser techniques on performance, safety, and scalability. The chapter concludes with insights into future prospects for laser applications in sustainable energy solutions.

papers.title: Intrinsic Berry Curvature on the Higher-order Poincare Sphere
papers.abstract: Higer-order geometric phase enable versatile spin-orbit manipulation of structured light . Con ventional theories describe this phase via a total-angular-momentum dependent Berry curvature . We develop an intrinsic theory restricted to the effective two-dimensional subspace, where the Berry curvature is independent of the topological charge of the light field . In our framework, the total-angular-momentum difference does not alter the effective monopole strength, whereas it controls the solid angle enclosed by the trajectory of the state evolution, insteadly. Our theory provides a different topological interpretation of geometric phase of the structured light, which unifies the underlying structures of generalized Poincare Spheres. Furthermore, it does not impose any specific form on the physical operation of the optical element, naturally encomoassing the case of previously reported experiment, and can be applied in arbitrary state evolutions in both classical structured light and quantum spin-orbit systems .

papers.title: How many events does entanglement-based positronium imaging need? Information limits of Compton polarimetry with CZT detectors
papers.abstract: The degree of polarisation correlation of the two annihilation photons, measured by Compton polarimetry, has been proposed as a PET biomarker of tissue microstructure, but the statistics it requires have not been quantified. We parameterise the measurement by the linear-polarisation correlation coefficient $\kappa$ ($\kappa=1$ maximally entangled, $1/2$ separable), derive the classical Fisher information of double-Compton events and compare it with the quantum Fisher information, relate $\kappa$ to the annihilation channels of positronium in tissue, and simulate pixelated CdZnTe (CZT) rings. The model is checked against three published measurements and an independent GATE/Geant4 simulation. A double-Compton event carries at most 0.12-0.14 units of Fisher information about $\kappa$ and 0.015 on average, 0.1-0.6% of the quantum limit. Event-wise maximum likelihood reaches the Cramer-Rao bound, whereas the conventional ratio R needs 1.2-2.3 times more events. The observed coefficient is $\kappa_{obs}=1-\alpha(1-\kappa_{pick})$, with a pick-off share $\alpha$ of 0.13-0.29 in tissue; it is sensitive to lipid fraction but not to oxygen, and carries no tissue information if pick-off photons are maximally entangled. Published porous-polymer data imply $\kappa_{pick}$ = 0.34-0.58. In a 15-mm CZT module, ordering ambiguity, position errors and electron transport roughly halve the information per event, and sequence reconstruction of multi-site events recovers this loss. With $^{18}$F and an eight-module ring, $\kappa$ can be measured to $\pm0.01$ in a 10-mm tumour, but separating tissues by $\kappa$ alone requires 6-74 times more decays than are available.

papers.title: Hund physics in the quarter-filled two-band Hubbard-Kanamori model: Crystal-field splitting and non-local Correlations
papers.abstract: We address the effect of crystal-field splitting and non-local correlations in the quarter-filled two-orbital Hubbard-Kanamori model. The role of the Hund's coupling in this configuration is not obvious since the atomic ground state has only one electron per site. Yet, previous works identified fingerprints of the Hund's coupling defining a weak Hund's metal at least at finite temperature. Using single-site dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) and two-site cellular DMFT based on a selected configuration-interaction solver we investigate the zero-temperature properties of the weak Hund's metal. Within DMFT we draw the boundary for the weak Hund's metal, which is consistent with previous finite-temperature results. Interestingly, we find that the fingerprints of the Hund's coupling are quite robust to the lifting of the orbital degeneracy and they survive up to splittings of a quarter of the bandwidth, well beyond those at which a two-stage Kondo screening disappears. Including non-local correlations in cluster DMFT demonstrates the robustness of the single-site DMFT picture, even if Mott localization occurs at smaller interactions. In the metal the intersite correlations are weak and insensitive to $J$, while in the localized state we find nearest-neighbor ferromagnetic, antiferro-orbital correlations that are manifest also in the mutual information between sites.

papers.title: SWE-OPD: On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Coding
MemDoctor: Stage-wise Error Attribution and Repair for MLLM Agent Memory
Classes of non-invertible simple derivations of $k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$
papers.abstract: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic zero, and let $n\geq 3$ be an integer. For $2\leq j\leq n-1$, let $a_j\in k$, and $g_j(x_j)\in k[x_j]\setminus k.$ We give two classes of simple and non-invertible $k$-derivations of $k[x_1,\ldots,x_n].$ The first class consists of the $k$-derivations $(1 +x_1^{m_2}x_2)\partial_{x_1}+x_1^{m_1}\partial_{x_2}+(a_2 x_3 +g_2(x_2))\partial_{x_3}+\cdots+(a_{n-1}x_n + g_{n-1}(x_{n-1}))\partial_{x_n},$ where $m_1$ and $m_2$ are two positive integers such that $m_2$ does not divide $m_1$. The second class consists of $k$-derivations $(1-x_2^{\alpha} x_1^{\beta})\partial_{x_1} +x_1^m\partial_{x_2}+(a_2 x_3 +g_2(x_2))\partial_{x_3}+\cdots+(a_{n-1}x_n + g_{n-1}(x_{n-1}))\partial_{x_n},$ where $\alpha\geq 1,\beta\geq 1$ and $m\geq \beta+1$ are integers, under the assumption that $a_j=0,$ for all $2\leq j\leq n-1$ or deg$_{x_2}g_2(x_2)=1$.

papers.title: Locally homogeneous PID gain-scheduling for motion control systems
Angular-Pole Flag Curvature and Conformal Control of Radial Jacobi Fields in Diagonal Conic Finsler Optics
papers.abstract: We study diagonal conic Finsler optical structures with radial coefficients and an arbitrary angular Finsler norm. We obtain the spray curvature block and identify the angular-pole radial-transverse flag curvature at a critical radius with the negative optical-arclength radial Jacobi coefficient. We prove that a compactly supported radial conformal two-jet determines the critical radius and any signed radial coefficient. A navigation Randers sphere yields unequal oriented periods with a common radial coefficient.

papers.title: A physics-constrained emulator for time-discretised landslide runout modelling
AstroSat Observations of Stellar Mass Black Hole X-ray Binaries: Towards a Unified Accretion Disc Configuration
papers.abstract: We present spectro-temporal review of $34$ black hole X-ray binaries (BH-XRBs), classified as persistent-cum-variable, persistent and transient, observed with \textit{AstroSat} during its first decade of operations. Using over $12$ Ms of data, wide-band multi-wavelength coverage in UV/Optical and X-rays, and $\sim10\,\mu\text{s}$ temporal resolution, we probe accretion-ejection dynamics in strong gravity. LFQPOs ($0.1-8.0\text{ Hz}$) are detected across several sources, exceeding $40\text{ keV}$ in MAXI J1535$-$571 and H 1743$-$322, while Swift J1727.8$-$1613 exhibits the first detection of LFQPOs up to $100$ keV, indicating the dominant Comptonized emission. In GRS 1915$+$105, we identify a new variability class ($\tau$), expanding known classes to fifteen, and detect $\sim70\text{ Hz}$ HFQPOs in the $\gamma$, $\kappa$, $\delta$, $\omega$, and $\tau$ classes, implying a `compact' oscillating corona within $\lesssim 10\,r_g$. Among persistent sources, we report the first detections of a type-A LFQPO ($\sim2.7\text{ Hz}$) in 4U 1957$+$11 and type-B LFQPOs ($4-8\text{ Hz}$) in 4U 1630$-$472. Broadband thermal disc along with Comptonization modelling reveals tight correlations among QPO frequency, time-lag, rms variability, photon index ($\Gamma_{\rm th}$), disc-to-Comptonized flux ratio ($F_{\rm ratio}$), and bolometric luminosity ($L_{\rm bol}$), tracing disc-corona-jet coupling and identifying `canonical' spectral states (LHS, HIMS, SIMS, HSS). Type-C QPOs exhibit soft-lags with occasional reversals at high coronal fractions ($>0.8$), whereas type-B QPOs show hard-lags at lower fractions ($<0.5$), linking to disc-jet coupling. Supported by simulations and radiation driven spectral modelling, these results favor a unified accretion framework while outlining limitations, challenges and future prospects.

papers.title: The least Carmichael numbers with $k$ prime factors
papers.abstract: Let $S_k$ denote the least Carmichael number with exactly $k$ prime factors. Like the later searches of Pinch, our algorithm builds the prime factors of a candidate in increasing order and stops as soon as the preproduct $P$ satisfies $P\lambda(P) > B$. At that point there is at most one possible cofactor, and we recover all of its prime factors at once in polynomial time. We prove an unconditional bound on the number of candidates the search examines, in terms of how far $B$ exceeds the product of the first $k$ primes. When the search is run in doubling passes, this gives a running time of $e^{O(k)} = S_k^{O(1/\log k)}$ under a natural conjecture on the size of $S_k$. We also show that the constant in the exponent is sharp for the set of square-free numbers that the bound counts. Finally, we compute $S_k$ for every $k \leq 64$; Pinch had computed it for $k \leq 35$.

papers.title: Two-Dimensional Kowalevski Top Problem as the Genus Two Full Jacobi Inversion Problem -Formulation Using Kolossoff Variables-
papers.abstract: For the Kowalevski top, we introduce another variable in addition to time variable, and formulate as the two-dimensional model. In this paper, since the results for the genus two full Jacobi inversion problem for the two variables Kowalevski top are already known, we utilize these results in reverse, introducing Kolossoff variables, to derive a more transparent formulation of the genus two full Jacobi inversion problem. Since there are two implicit equations of motion using Kowalevski variables, we derived two explicit equations of motion using Kolossoff variables, which is different from the Kolossoff method to derive only one explicit equation and to use Hamiltonian-Jacobi theory.

papers.title: Particle Identification Studies using a Highly Granular Crystal Electromagnetic Calorimeter
papers.abstract: A proposal for the Circular Electron Positron Collider electromagnetic calorimeter is a highly granular scintillating crystal design that uses silicon photomultipliers to measure physics signals from photons. The potential to develop particle identification methods using deep and traditional machine learning is explored. A contrastive machine learning technique was found to enable the separation of showering and 'punch-through' pions without explicit labels. A supervised particle identification method was then trained using the results, using both a graph neural network and a boosted decision tree to distinguish electron, showering hadron, and minimum-ionizing-particle-like events. The classifier achieved an area-under-the-receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.996 for both cases. A Shapley additive explanations analysis showed the boosted decision tree classifier matched expectations for each event type. The particle identification capability is then demonstrated on experimental data taken from the CERN Proton Synchrotron T9 beamline.

papers.title: The Singular LeBrun Transform: Complex Conformal and Contact Geometry
papers.abstract: A holomorphic conformal structure is rigid in the presence of rational curves: a complex conformal manifold that is not conformally flat contains no immersed rational null geodesic. So a natural compactification of such a manifold, on which its null geodesics close up, must degenerate along the boundary. We study this phenomenon for the complex conformal manifold that LeBrun attached to a complex contact manifold $Z$ in inverting Salamon's twistor construction: the space $M_{\mathbb{C}}$ of balanced conics of $Z$ transverse to the contact distribution, with its holomorphic Riemannian metric of holonomy contained in $\mathrm{Sp}(n,\mathbb{C})\mathrm{Sp}(1,\mathbb{C})$. Its compactification by the degenerate conics of $Z$ forces the metric to become singular at the boundary. We develop a framework, the singular LeBrun transform, in which these singularities are a source of information rather than an obstacle: the singularities of the metric and of its curvature are read off from the degenerate rational curves of $Z$, locally through the contact neighbourhood of a curve and globally through the incidence variety. As an application, we give an alternative proof of the LeBrun--Salamon conjecture that all positive quaternionic-Kähler manifolds are symmetric, which was recently claimed by OpenAI and by Hu, Liu and Wan. The emphasis of the paper, however, is less on this result than on the framework developed here, which should apply to other problems of the same kind; we conclude with two such directions, negative quaternionic-Kähler manifolds and a singular Merkulov transform for Legendre moduli spaces.

papers.title: Learning and Verifying Stabilizing Controllers with Structured Neural Control Lyapunov Functions
The Odd Shift is not sofic in dimensions $d \ge 3$
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove that the Odd Shift $S_{odd}$ is not sofic for dimensions $d \ge 3$. Our proof uses lower bounds from communication complexity, specifically the result of Raz and Spieker on the nondeterministic communication complexity for the connectivity problem. We also prove that $S_{odd}$ is not sofic for dimension $d=2$ under the assumption we call Mute Ocean.

papers.title: Radial symmetry for the positive Kähler--Einstein Dirichlet problem on the ball
papers.abstract: We prove radial symmetry for every strictly plurisubharmonic function $u$ on the unit ball in $\C^n$, $n\ge2$, that is smooth up to the boundary, vanishes there, and has complex Hessian determinant $\mu e^{-u}$ for a constant $\mu>0$. The known Fubini--Study family therefore exhausts all such solutions. For the corresponding complex Monge--Ampère mean field equation, this establishes the Berman--Berndtsson symmetry conjecture in the smooth class and gives uniqueness throughout the known existence range. The classification also yields the sharp Moser--Trudinger inequality on the ball in Cegrell's finite-energy class.

papers.title: The Exact Optimal Delivery Scheme for the Cyclically $L$-Separated Placement in Multi-Access Coded Caching
The relationship between junctional zone, smooth muscle tone and intra-uterine pressure
papers.abstract: The junctional zone is a thin low contrast region of the inner myometrium, visible on T2weighted MRI images. Investigators have long sought histologic particularities of this region. Here, we summarize evidence that this region's specific appearance is not due to a particular tissue composition, but is a reflection of underlying smooth muscle activity. Smooth muscle tone in the spirally fibered myometrium wrings out blood and interstitial fluids to create a static low-contrast T2 region around the myometrium, while phasic smooth muscle contractions create transient, propagative low-contrast waves. We show that the competition between centripetal inhibitory adrenergic innervation from the serosa and centrifugal excitatory hormonal gradients from the endometrium divides the uterus in a tonic inner-and a quiescent outer-region. Bridging MRI and manometry studies, we discuss the relation between smooth muscle activity and intra-uterine pressure. Dysregulation of nerve and/or hormonal activity can result in a thicker tonic smooth muscle layer, entailing a thicker junctional zone and high intrauterine pressures characteristic of dyscontractility in severe dysmenorrhea, endometriosis and adenomyosis.

papers.title: Optimal Quadrature and the Curse of Dimensionality for a Veronese Class
K2-Horizon: A Frontier Fleet of Open Source Language Models
Null flag curvature of anisotropically conformal pseudo-Finsler metrics
papers.abstract: We consider the Zermelo navigation problem for a time-dependent Finsler metric, which can be recast as the study of lightlike geodesics of a Lorentz--Finsler metric on a non-relativistic spacetime. To control how such geodesics separate, we introduce a null flag curvature, defined for any pseudo-Finsler metric with a lightlike cone, and show that it governs the Taylor expansion of the norm of a Jacobi field. We then prove a formula relating the null flag curvatures of two anisotropically conformal pseudo-Finsler metrics. Applying it to the spacetime associated with a time-independent Randers metric, which is anisotropically conformal to a stationary spacetime, we obtain compact expressions for the flag curvature of Randers metrics, both in terms of their $(\alpha,\beta)$ data and of their Zermelo data $(h,W)$. These expressions allow us to compute explicitly the flag curvature when $W$ is conformal, affine or projective, and when $\alpha$ is a Kähler metric. We also introduce a Weyl-type curvature, invariant under anisotropic conformal changes, whose vanishing characterizes Finsler manifolds of scalar flag curvature, and we obtain the flag curvature of $F + \mathrm{d}f$, showing in particular that $F$ has scalar flag curvature if and only if $F + \mathrm{d}f$ does.

papers.title: Does the Voice Matter? Evaluating Frustration Detection on Deployed Clinical Voice-Agent Calls
Rotating Polytropic Twins and the Fragmentation Problem
papers.abstract: Polytropic n=1 stellar configurations with strong differential rotation have been considered. The so-called twin configurations: stars having almost identical integral characteristics, but clearly structurally different have been found. Hydrodynamic 3D modeling has been performed for two such structures and has shown that these configurations also differ in the dynamic aspect: one of them remains practically stationary, while the other turns out to be unstable with respect to the development of the bar mode and fragmentation. The gravitational wave signal accompanying the fragmentation process has been calculated.

papers.title: How Can Size, Ceiling, and Time Bounds Affect the Complexity of Nonuniform Automata Families?
A tunable multi-gated platform for superlattice engineering in bilayer graphene
papers.abstract: Periodic potentials with length scales much larger than crystal lattice constants can generate low-energy electronic minibands. While small-angle twisted van der Waals heterostructures have been widely used to realize such physics, correlated phases are often limited by twist-angle inhomogeneity, strain, and disorder. Here, we investigate high-quality Bernal bilayer graphene placed on a patterned graphite gate, featuring a triangular array of holes, forming a new class of "gate-engineered" superlattices tunable through three independent electrostatic gates. Near the charge neutrality point, we observe insulating states characteristic of miniband formation. Temperature-dependent transport reveals activated gaps consistent with theory, and Hall measurements indicate charge-carrier inversion. Notably, the superlattice can be reconfigured electrostatically using various gate combinations, enabling flexible band-structure design without mechanical twisting. The results highlight a new route to band engineering, potentially extendable to complex periodic structures that are untenable in natural materials.

Curvature condition on the Wasserstein space over a closed Riemannian manifold
papers.abstract: We establish regularity results for the solution flow of Stochastic Differential Equations (SDE) on the Wasserstein space $\mathscr{P}(M)$ over a closed Riemannian manifold, under suitable assumptions on the driving vector fields. We derive the SDE governing the associated tangent process and prove its well-posedness by means of the framework developped in \cite{Martin2025} for Covariant SDEs on Inverse Limit Hilbert vector bundles over the diffeomorphism group. We introduce the $\mathrm{IWC}(K)$ condition, a geometric curvature-type condition which generalizes, in the setting of SDEs on $¶(M)$, both the $\mathrm{H.C.K.}$ condition introduced in \cite{cattiaux:hal-00805299} and the ergodicity condition of \cite[Section 4]{wang2020}. Finally, combining this condition with the theory of entropic interpolations (see \cite{Leonard2014}), we establish several consequences of $\mathrm{IWC}(K)$, including control of the distance between two trajectories, gradient estimates for the associated Markov semigroup and a local Poincar{é} inequality. In the case $K >0$, we further obtain the existence and uniqueness of an ergodic invariant measure for the associated semigroup.

The monoid of orientation preserving mappings on a chain
papers.abstract: We introduce new kinds of regular monoids of transformations consisting of mappings which preserve or reverse the orientation of a finite cycle.

GRACE: Parallel Best-of-N Multi-Agent Analysis of Closed-Form Questions over Dataframes with Guardrail Selection and Adaptive Retry
Schur multipliers, vanishing minors and Gaussian conditional independence
papers.abstract: Conditional independence in a Gaussian vector is the vanishing of almost-principal minors of its covariance matrix $\Sigma$. A sensitivity analysis replaces $\Sigma$ by the Schur product $\Delta\circ\Sigma$, where the symmetric multiplier $\Delta$ differs from one exactly at the changed positions. Such a change generally destroys some conditional independences, and we determine which minors stay zero. A vanishing minor is preserved for every matrix exactly when the corresponding block of $\Delta$ has rank one. When variances or covariances change, each almost-principal minor of $\Delta\circ\Sigma$ is a polynomial in the amounts added, with minors of $\Sigma$ as coefficients, and a conditional independence survives every such change exactly when they vanish. In an undirected graphical model, changing variances joins the neighbours of the perturbed vertices, while changing covariances leaves a structure read from the graph by a separation rule, possibly not graphical. Both extend to ancestral graphs, directed acyclic graphs included, and identify the entries that can vary freely. For the other entries, blocks of rank one along a junction tree characterize the multipliers that preserve a decomposable model. A sensitivity analysis can therefore rest on the conditional independence structure after the change, as illustrated on examination marks of 88 students.

Adaptive-Elbow Graph Traversal for Schema Retrieval in Text-to-SQL
Inverse Kinematics in Endoscopic Scenarios using MoveIt
Relaxation of one-dimensional variational problems without growth constraints
papers.abstract: We study the integral representation of the relaxation of integral functionals of the form u-> \int f(x,u(x),u'(x)) dx, for Sobolev functions u\,: (a, b) $\rightarrow$ RN with fixed Dirichlet boundary conditions. Unlike classical works on the subject, we require a very mild growth condition on the Lagrangian f to make our statement as natural and general as possible. We state four different situations in which we manage to obtain an explicit expression for the relaxation on BV , which is usually the natural framework for such weak growth conditions. Our goal is also to express a few unifying assumptions on the Lagrangian to obtain the expected relaxation formula.

papers.title: Living Context Graphs: Continual Semantic Learning for Enterprise Data Reasoning
STORMGUIDE-FL: Stochastic Remote Guidance for Efficient Mining of Federated Streaming Data
Projective planes with abelian collineation groups of type (F) are Desarguesian
papers.abstract: We use prime ideal factorization and residue class fields of cyclotomic integer rings to prove that every abelian direct product difference set is classical. This implies that every projective plane of order $n$ with an abelian collineation group of order $n(n-1)$ is Desarguesian, proving a conjecture of Jungnickel and de Resmini. As a consequence, we obtain the classification of circular Costas maps and of Costas polynomials conjectured by Muratovic-Ribic, Pott, Thomson and Wang and by Torres and Rubio.

papers.title: The kinematic response of RGB centroids and O--B stars to the Milky Way spiral structure: testing the solid-body rotation of the spiral pattern
papers.abstract: Using the centroid velocities of RGB stars and the individual velocities of O-B stars from the Gaia DR3, we test whether the spiral structure in the investigated region of the Galaxy can be described by a single wave with a constant pattern speed within the framework of Lin-Shu density-wave theory. The amplitudes of the radial and azimuthal velocity perturbations are determined for three centroid samples: centroids within strips 350 pc wide around five spiral arms; centroids within the same strips, with an additional condition on the radial gradient of the radial velocity, $M_{11}^+$; and all centroids within $5 \leq R \leq 15$ kpc and $130^\circ \leq \theta \leq 270^\circ$. The periodic and smooth non-periodic velocity components are fitted simultaneously. For each sample, the amplitudes derived from the RGB centroid velocities and the individual O-B stellar velocities are used to calculate the relative frequency as a function of Galactocentric radius, $R$, and subsequently the pattern speed at different radii. The analysis is performed for both stellar populations and for two assumed numbers of spiral arms, $m=4$ and $m=5$, using either the amplitude ratio or the radial amplitude alone. None of the cases considered supports a constant pattern speed within the adopted Lin-Shu model. We regard the pattern speed inferred from the radial solution for a specified perturbing potential as our main result. The estimate based on the amplitude ratio provides a complementary result that is consistent with the main conclusion of a non-constant pattern speed, but is less reliable because of the azimuthal response.

papers.title: Hilbert States for Decision-Making under Partial Observability
AutoDiDact: Input Reduction over Inferred Structure
Simulating high-speed solar wind streams from coronal holes using an L5-L1 configuration of Lagrangian points
papers.abstract: Coronal holes (CHs) are known to be sources of high-speed solar wind streams (HSSs), yet the physical mechanisms linking CH position and characteristics to solar wind (SW) behaviour remain unclear. Our results reveal that the latitude of CHs, especially smaller ones, combined with the heliographic latitude of the solar disk's central point (B0 angle), plays a critical role in driving discrepancies in SW velocity across the heliosphere. To investigate this, we use archival data from STEREO-B, STEREO-A, and Earth to simulate an L5-L1 configuration, where L5 is a vantage point approximately behind Earth in its orbit (as proposed for the Vigil mission), and L1 is between Earth and the Sun where SW measurements are typically taken. We use these insights to develop a predictive algorithm for HSSs, beginning with an analysis of the separation angle and distances between L5 and L1. We then introduce a predictive indicator and empirical criteria based on CH properties and the B0 angle to adjust for changes in SW velocity at L1. Our results show that the L5 viewpoint demonstrates the capability to significantly improve the accuracy and lead times of HSS predictions, enhancing our understanding of the CH-HSS relationship and potentially improving space weather forecasting.

papers.title: The Interplay of Stellar Feedback and Gravity in the Wat01-S208 Star-forming Complex
papers.abstract: To investigate the processes governing clustered star formation, we present a multi-wavelength study of the star-forming complex hosting clusters Waterloo 01 and [BDS2003]64 in Sh 2-208. Both clusters exhibit elongated morphologies, with radii of $\sim1.5$ and $\sim0.9$ pc, respectively, and are located at a common distance of $\sim3.5$ kpc. Wat01 displays hierarchical structure ($Q=0.6$) and signature of mass segregation ($\Gamma_{\rm MSR}=1.5\pm0.6$). Its relaxation time, comparable to or longer than its age, suggests that the observed segregation may have a primordial contribution. The mass function follows a single power law, $\Gamma=-1.62\pm0.15$, over $\sim0.7$-$19.6$ M$_\odot$. Molecular-line observations reveal distinct velocity components associated with S208 and Wat01, indicating different molecular environments within the complex. Wat01 is strongly shaped by massive-star feedback, with an evacuated cavity, surrounding shell, and compressed globules consistent with an expanding H\,{\sc ii} region; feedback may have promoted localized star formation, although a direct causal connection cannot be established. In contrast, \textit{Herschel} data uncover a hub-filament system (HFS) in S208, with the central hub associated with BDS64 and the H\,{\sc ii} region powered by 'S1'. The filaments remain relatively well-preserved, indicating that gravity continues to play an important role in assembling dense gas toward the hub and in clustered star formation, even as feedback begins to affect the immediate surroundings. Overall, this complex illustrates the coexistence of feedback-processed and comparatively less-disrupted star-forming environments, highlighting the evolving interplay between stellar feedback and gravity in clustered star formation.

papers.title: Finite-order exponential mixing does not imply the central limit theorem for unique equilibrium states
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a compact smooth manifold of dimension at least three, $\varphi:M\to\mathbb R$ be continuous, and $R\ge2$ be an integer. We construct a $\mathcal C^\infty$ diffeomorphism $T:M\to M$ and an observable $f\in\mathcal C^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$ such that $(T,\varphi)$ has a unique equilibrium state $\mu$ and $\mu(f)=0$. The system $(T,\mu)$ is exponentially mixing of order $R$ but not of order $R+1$ for Hölder observables, and $n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}f\circ T^i$ does not satisfy the central limit theorem. The main results have been formalised in Lean 4.

papers.title: A General Theory of Nonparametric Response-Adaptive Randomization
papers.abstract: Response-Adaptive Randomization (RAR) assigns incoming patients to treatments with probabilities that depend on previously observed responses. While most existing RAR procedures rely on finite-dimensional summaries of treatment performance (such as rates, means, or model parameters), we develop a nonparametric (NP) distribution-based framework in which the treatment outcome distributions are learned sequentially and adaptation is driven by their functionals. The framework naturally accommodates multiple treatments and is particularly suited to endpoints for which average effects may conceal relevant differences across the outcome distribution. We introduce an ethical NP-RAR rule driven by a pre-specified distributional score and a nonparametric extension of the multi-arm efficient randomized adaptive design (NP-ERADE) able to approach generic distribution-dependent targets selected according to ethical or inferential optimality criteria. We establish strong consistency and joint functional central limit theorems for the empirical treatment distributions, together with asymptotic normality of functional scores, estimated targets and allocation proportions. We further show that the NP-ERADE allocation proportions attain the semiparametric efficiency bound for the target. We develop post-trial inference for score contrasts and distributional features, including crossing locations, and investigate finite-sample properties, robustness and inferential performance via simulations.

papers.title: A Soft Sponge-Pillar Electrode Platform for Motion-Tolerant Ambulatory EEG and Sleep Monitoring
papers.abstract: Long-term wearable electrophysiological recording systems are essential for both clinical and real-world environments. While a wide range of wearable devices have been reported for electrocardiogram (ECG) and electromyogram (EMG) recording applications, most electroencephalography (EEG) measurements still require subjects to remain stationary while wearing rigid and uncomfortable equipment. Here, a soft and wearable sponge pillar EEG electrode is presented for long-term and motion-tolerant EEG recording. The electrode is composed of two layers of a carbon black (CB)-polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) composite, where a firmer solid base assists in bypassing hair, enabling stable access to the scalp, while a porous sponge tip ensures comfort, reliable contact, and low skin-electrode impedance. Fabricated via a sugar templating process without microfabrication steps, the microporous sponge structure offers low modulus and significantly enhances the contact area with the skin when loaded with conductive gel. This allows the electrode to achieve a lower contact impedance of $1.62 \times 10^{4}\,\Omega$ at 10 Hz, outperforming conventional gelled electrodes while maintaining gel stability for over 18 hours. With the electrodes integrated into wearable form factors such as headbands, headphones, and baseball caps, EEG signal recording during motion have been demonstrated, achieving a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of 16.46 dB. These features establish the sponge pillar electrode as a promising platform for next generation wearable EEG systems, enabling comfortable, stable, and prolonged brain signal acquisition on ambulatory subjects and in naturalistic environments.

papers.title: Global bound-state spectrum and spin- and angular-momentum-dependent confinement in an inverse-$3/2$ magnetic quantum dot
papers.abstract: We investigate the bound-state spectrum and confinement thresholds of a two-dimensional electron governed by the Schrödinger--Pauli equation in an inverse-$3/2$ radial magnetic-field profile. The radial problem reduces to the biconfluent Heun equation, but instead of restricting the solution to the quasi-exact polynomial sector, we impose the bound-state condition globally through a spectral Wronskian between the endpoint-selected Frobenius solution and the subdominant asymptotic solution. The resulting spectrum contains continuous nonpolynomial bound-state branches on which the known quasi-exact solutions appear as isolated exact points. In this global description, the polynomial index $N$ remains a termination index within the quasi-exact sector but does not uniquely label the spectral branches. An independent exact analysis of the continuum edge yields spin- and angular-momentum-dependent critical couplings that can lie below the quasi-exact restriction $U_0a>4$, where $U_0$ is the Coulomb-strength parameter and $a$ is the magnetic-profile length scale. These results establish quasi-exact solvability as a set of special analytic points embedded in a broader biconfluent-Heun spectrum with spin- and angular-momentum-dependent confinement thresholds.

papers.title: Discriminants and resultants of orthogonal polynomials
papers.abstract: The concept of a linked pair of two sequences of polynomials, one of which is orthogonal, is introduced. Such a pair always has a resultant that factors. Two methods for producing such linked pairs are given: one for general orthogonal polynomials and the other for any polynomial in the Askey scheme. Generalized discriminants are introduced and evaluated, including a general product formula for each operator in the Askey scheme. A new notion of companion orthogonal polynomials is also introduced and used to evaluate the discriminants of orthogonal polynomials. These methods recover all known formulas for the generalized discriminants of classical polynomials and provide new ones.

papers.title: Using an instrumented hammer to predict the lateral hinge fracture in high tibial osteotomy: A cadaveric study
papers.abstract: Open-wedge High-Tibial Osteotomy is the most commonly employed technique addressing varus knee osteoarthritis. During this procedure, the osteotome passes through cortical and trabecular bone. A common complication is lateral hinge fractures, which depends upon when the surgeon stops impacting the osteotome. The aim of the present study is to determine whether an instrumented hammer can be employed to detect (i) the bone type (cortical or trabecular) surrounding the osteotome tip and (ii) when bone is fractured by the osteotome. Seventeen lower-limb specimens were obtained from nine fresh human anatomical subjects. The osteotome was impacted using the instrumented hammer until rupture. Each impact signal was recorded and analyzed. An algorithm was developed to detect the transitions between cortical and trabecular bone and vice versa. Detection was based on the relative variation of $\tau$ derived from the force signal as a function of time as the time difference between the second___and___first impact peaks. The values of $\tau$ were significantly lower in cortical bone compared to trabecular bone. Considering the arrival of the osteotome tip in trabecular bone during a medial, a difference of less than 2 impacts between the surgeon and the algorithm was obtained for 71% of the cases. For the lateral osteotomy it was obtained in 81% of the cases. This cadaveric study demonstrated that the instrumented hammer could prevent impacts leading to hinge rupture, which suggests that future clinical trials are warranted.

papers.title: Triples in matroid circuits
papers.abstract: We prove that, if $X$ is a four-element independent set in a vertically $5$-connected representable matroid $M$, then either there is a circuit of $M$ that contains at least three elements of $X$, or there is a representation $A$ of $M$ such that each column of $A$ has at most two non-zero elements and each of the columns indexed by $X$ has exactly one non-zero element. We also prove a version of this result without the connectivity assumptions.

papers.title: Detecting the pterygomaxillary disjunction using an instrumented hammer: A cadaveric study
papers.abstract: Background: In many maxillofacial surgeries, the surgeon must perform a pterygomaxillary disjunction in order to separate the jaw from the skull. The disjunction is performed using an osteotome which is impacted with a hammer until its tip crosses through the pterygoid plates. To determine whether the disjunction has occurred and avoid complications, surgeons still rely on their proprioception. Methods: The aim of this study is to validate a vibroacoustic set-up constituted by an instrumented hammer equipped with a force sensor, aiming at detecting if the disjunction has occurred. To do so, fourteen osteotomies were performed in anatomical subject jaws. For each impact, the force signal was recorded and analyzed. A classification algorithm (Support Vector Machine method coupled with a cost matrix) was developed based on indicators extracted from the signal to determine whether the disjunction had occurred. Impacts were classified into two classes, one before and the other after the osteotome had crossed the pterygoid plates. To avoid undetected disjunctions a cost matrix was added to the algorithm. The coefficients from the matrix were chosen using by minimizing the Negative Likelihood Ratio. Findings: The algorithm was able to distinguish impacts before and after the disjunction with an accuracy of 96 %. Moreover, the instrumented hammer was able to detect the disjunction with a maximum delay of two impacts. Interpretation: These results pave the way for the development of a per-operative decision support system for the pterygomaxillary disjunction.

papers.title: Static Bounds on Thermal Fast Scrambling
papers.abstract: Scrambling, the process by which initially localized quantum information spreads across an interacting many-body system, is a hallmark of quantum chaos and plays a central role in understanding black hole dynamics. In thermal systems, the chaos bound of Maldacena, Shenker and Stanford limits the exponential growth rate of out-of-time-order correlations to $2\pi/\beta$, assuming that time-ordered correlation functions factorize after a dissipation time. Establishing the corresponding rigorous logarithmic lower bounds on scrambling times at arbitrary fixed temperature has remained an open problem, most notably in disordered systems, where the Gibbs state depends on the same random couplings that drive the dynamics. Here we prove such bounds at every fixed temperature for the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model and for random $k$-local spin systems, without assuming real-time factorization. Our approach uses the operator-size distribution of the square root of the Gibbs state to quantify how local probes modify its structure. This static information bounds the thermal correlator uniformly in time along the edges of its analytic strip in complex time, and analyticity then limits how rapidly scrambling can develop. For both families of models, we prove that with probability tending to one the scrambling time is at least $(1-\epsilon)[\beta/(2\pi)]\log N$ for any $0<\epsilon<1$, with the coefficient $\beta/(2\pi)$ suggested by the chaos bound. The bound holds for each fixed pair of distinct Majorana modes in the SYK model and for the target average of any fixed single-site source in the spin model. These results place the thermal fast-scrambling timescale on a rigorous footing and show how static properties of the Gibbs state can constrain real-time information spreading.

papers.title: Branch-and-Cut for Maximum $k$-Independent Sets with Spectral Bounds
papers.abstract: We develop a branch-and-cut method for finding maximum distance-independent sets in graphs. Our approach solves a sequence of fixed-size clique problems, combining graph reductions with combinatorial and spectral bounds. We give a compact formulation, derive strengthened inequalities, establish conditions for using spectral information, and evaluate them in a comprehensive computational study.

papers.title: From Vision to Interaction: Evaluating Dynamic Social Intelligence of VLM Agents in ALIVE-World
Jev-as-a-Reward: Validating Probabilistic Safety Judges for Reinforcement Learning
Layer-wise Linear Probing of an Encoder-free Audio-capable Language Model
papers.abstract: Encoder-free audio-capable multimodal language models pro- vide a unique setting for studying how speech representations emerge inside a language-model decoder. In Gemma-4-12B, short waveform frames are projected directly into the shared embedding space, and all subsequent contextual processing is performed by the decoder layers. We use this architecture to examine where acoustic, phonetic, segmental, and paralinguis- tic information becomes linearly accessible across depth. Us- ing the TIMIT corpus, we extract all 49 representations from the frozen model, including the embedding output and the out- puts of its 48 decoder layers. We train linear probes for log- F0, log-energy, voicing, phone identity, word-onset structure, speaker identity, recorded speaker gender, and dialect-region labels. The results show a broad progression in linear acces- sibility. Acoustic properties are most strongly decodable in the early layers, paralinguistic attributes are most accessible in the early-to-middle layers, and phone identity and boundary- sensitive information reach their highest performance around layer 11. Several properties remain strongly decodable across broad near-peak regions rather than at a single uniquely optimal layer. In deeper layers, phone identity and closed-set speaker identity decline sharply, while voicing, log-F0, and gender re- main more accessible. These findings provide an initial map of how speech information develops when the decoder is the first contextual stage to process audio.

papers.title: Same Fix, Different Weights: Replicating Weight-Space Programming with Claude
Altermagnetism in moiré quasicrystals
papers.abstract: Altermagnetism is a collinear compensated magnetic phase with zero net magnetization and momentum-dependent spin polarization. Quasicrystalline altermagnetism extends altermagnetism beyond periodic crystals, with noncrystallographic symmetries allowing high-order spin polarization patterns. Here, we propose a symmetry-based approach to realizing quasicrystalline altermagnetism by twisting collinear magnetic layers. Specifically, we demonstrate that the $30^{\circ}$-twisted honeycomb lattice bilayers form the dodecagonal quasicrystals supporting an $i$-wave altermagnetic phase. We further find that $45^{\circ}$-twisted bilayers preserving fourfold rotational symmetry support a mirror-driven $l$-wave phase with eight nodal lines. We characterize these altermagnetic patterns through plane-wave-projected spin-resolved spectral functions and spin-resolved conductances. Our work provides a systematic route to high-angular-order quasicrystalline altermagnetism through twist engineering.

papers.title: A Convergence Analysis of the Random Feature Method for Linear PDEs
ROSE: A Shared Cross-Embodiment Facial-Motion Latent Space for Humanoid Robot Expression
Multimodal assessment of the skin biomechanical properties during wound healing and hyaluronic acid response
papers.abstract: Various methods such as elastography or mechanical testing have been developed to quantify the mechanical properties of soft tissues, which are related to the tissue local pathophysiological conditions. This study is the first one to investigate the in vivo performances of the Impact-Based Analysis Method (IBAM) to characterize the biomechanical behavior of skin during physiological mechanisms. A murine model (12 Sprague-Dawley rats) was considered and various measurements of skin mechanical properties were conducted on different regions of interest over a 3-week period. The effects of wound healing after full-thickness excisional wound and an intradermal hyaluronic acid (HA) injection were monitored using IBAM, as well as two commercially available devices: Cutometer__ and MyotonPro__. The indicators $\Delta$t (from IBAM), R0 and R5 (from Cutometer__) vary significantly as a function of wound healing time, which corresponds to a stiffening of healing tissue compared to healthy tissue. The indicator $\Delta$t and S (from MyotonPro__) are significantly different when HA was injected compared to healthy tissue, which also corresponds to less stiff tissue. Additionally, both IBAM and Cutometer__ detect significant biomechanical variations in superficial soft tissue related to tissue growth in all measurement regions. This first in vivo use of IBAM shows that IBAM could assess significant variations related to wound healing or regeneration mechanisms following HA injection. This study paves the way for the development of a simple, low-cost and objective device. Future clinical studies or other animal models should be carried out to confirm these results.

papers.title: One Code per Material: Neural Representation and Generation of Measured BTFs
List colouring of circular-arc graphs
papers.abstract: A circular-arc graph takes a set of nonempty closed arcs on a circle as its vertex set, and two vertices are adjacent when their corresponding arcs intersect on the circle. We show the chromatic number of any circular-arc graph equals its list chromatic number. Our methodology is an application of Schauz's coefficient formula within the Alon-Tarsi and Combinatorial Nullstellensatz framework.

papers.title: Dynamical theory of the East model. I. A review on the Zwanzig-Mori projection-operator formalism
papers.abstract: The East model is a paradigmatic kinetically constrained spin model in one dimension that exhibits glassy dynamics. This review surveys the progress on the theoretical description of the dynamics of the East model, focusing on the spin time correlation function and the relaxation time. We summarize rigorous results on the super-Arrhenius scaling of the relaxation time in the low-temperature limit. We then present a unified derivation of the Zwanzig-Mori projection-operator formalism for both the fluctuation and domain bases. Within this formalism, an infinite hierarchy of coupled equations for the time correlation function and memory kernels emerges---a structure reminiscent of generalized mode-coupling theory developed for supercooled liquids. We review the analytical approximations obtained by truncating or closing the hierarchy at first or second orders and compare them against Monte Carlo simulations. Although these approaches perform reasonably at moderate temperatures, they universally fail in the low-temperature regime: mode-coupling closure schemes in the fluctuation basis introduce spurious ergodicity-breaking transitions, while truncations in the domain basis discard slower modes and fail to capture the asymptotic divergence of the relaxation time. The loss of analytical tractability beyond second order remains the central obstacle, underscoring the fundamental difficulty of describing hierarchical relaxation even in this ``simplest'' model of glassy dynamics.

papers.title: Metrological Channels Induced by Encrypted Quantum Cloning: Optimal-Probe Fisher-Information Broadcasting and Single-Use Operational Recovery
papers.abstract: Encrypted quantum cloning creates multiple individually inaccessible signal systems from which an unknown input state can be recovered by combining any selected signal with a shared quantum key. Here we study parameter estimation when a local sensing transformation is applied after encrypted cloning and before decryption. For the two-clone qubit protocol, a local Pauli rotation on one encrypted signal is shown to induce, after standard decryption, a parameter-dependent Pauli dephasing channel rather than a unitary rotation. We derive its Pauli-transfer representation and the corresponding quantum Fisher information (QFI) for arbitrary mixed qubit probes. We then distinguish raw QFI, which for an optimal decoded probe may remain simultaneously present in a decoded output and its complement, from decoder-accessible QFI, which is operationally single-use because a first decryption destroys the shared syndrome information needed for a second standard recovery. For $n\geq2$ encrypted clones, the effective channel family is independent of clone number up to a clone-parity-dependent permutation of the Pauli axes (the single-clone case is exceptional for $Y$-sensing, where the decoded map stays unitary). This produces a metrological parity switch: for fixed probe and generator, even and odd clone numbers can yield respectively vanishing and maximal QFI. Closed expressions are obtained for the degradation of this parity contrast under probe depolarization and Pauli-diagonal Bloch-vector contraction.

papers.title: Polymorphism and crystal suppression in symmetric mixtures with entropic interactions
papers.abstract: We investigate the phases of a binary mixture of hard spheres with equal diameter and negative non-additivity, favoring hetero-coordination in dense samples. By performing extensive swap Monte Carlo simulations, we show that in an interval of small non-additivities, close to the eutectic point, the mixture fails to crystallize and the compressed fluid gets stuck in an amorphous state. The onset of glass at intermediate compositions is associated with the competition between FCC and B2 (CsCl-type) crystal structures. As the propensity of particles to hetero-coordinate grows further, however, the B2 crystal gives way to a B1 (NaCl-type) crystal at equimolarity, and again the mixture orders for all compositions. We argue that this happens because of the underlying FCC symmetry of the B1 crystal. These results, pertaining to a model with excluded-volume interactions only, point to the key role of entropy in generating amorphous structures in multi-component metallic, inorganic, and soft-matter glass formers.

papers.title: From Strong Normalization to WhatsApp: the Journey of an Axiom
vividRGB: Various visual cue detection in RGB photographs with forced focused attention
Vanishing geodesic distance phenomenon and boundedness of curvatures
papers.abstract: This article concerns a conjecture proposed by Michor and Mumford in their 2005 paper, in which the vanishing of the geodesic distance is associated to the local unboundedness of the sectional curvature. In this article, we consider a Riemannian Banach manifold with all of its curvature tensors locally bounded. We derive several properties regarding the local boundedness of curvature tensors, and give a sufficient condition for a non-degenerate geodesic distance, which partially verifies the conjecture in its converse form.

papers.title: Gravitational Potential of CALIFA Galaxies from the Blue Cloud to the Red Sequence
papers.abstract: We explore the gravitational potential of 238 (E1$-$Sdm) CALIFA galaxies from the Blue cloud to the Red Sequence using the star formation rate$-$stellar mass diagram ($\mathrm{SFR}-M_\star$) diagnosis. On average, galaxies in the Blue cloud possess slow-rising circular velocity curves (CVCs), those in the Green valley have flat CVCs, while galaxies in the Red sequence are characterised with peaked CVCs. Both the maximum circular velocity ($V_{c,\mathrm{max}}$) and asymptotic circular velocity ($V_{c,\mathrm{flat}}$) of the galaxies increase from the Blue cloud to the Red sequence, and show approximately linear relations with the logarithmic offsets from the star-forming main sequence ($\Delta\mathrm{SFR}$s). The $\Delta\mathrm{SFR}-\log_{10}(V_{c,\mathrm{max}})$ relation has a steeper slope ($-0.154 \pm 0.012$) than the $\Delta\mathrm{SFR}-\log_{10}(V_{c,\mathrm{flat}})$ relation ($-0.124 \pm 0.011$). These results suggest that $V_{c,\mathrm{max}}$, tracing the inner gravitational potential, indicates a stronger variation along the quenching parameter $\Delta\mathrm{SFR}$ than $V_{c,\mathrm{flat}}$, which is more strongly influenced by the outer mass distribution and dark matter halo.

papers.title: TacBridge: Learning Unified Tactile Representations through Cross-Sensor Correspondence
A consistent (3D) EFT expansion of the bubble nucleation rate. Part I: scalar theories
papers.abstract: Precise predictions of bubble nucleation are essential for connecting cosmological phase transitions to their potential observational signatures. In this first paper of a two-part series, we develop a general, fully perturbative framework for incorporating higher-dimensional operators (HDOs) into nucleation calculations in scalar high-temperature effective field theories. Our approach consistently includes their effects on the bounce and the fluctuations around it, including interactions with higher derivatives. We prove that the resulting statistical rate is invariant under field redefinitions, and establish sufficient conditions for the existence of the perturbative bounce solution in the presence of HDOs. We illustrate the framework by applying it to a model containing a scalar and a fermion, where we find modest HDO corrections in its regime of moderately strong transitions. We thus extend the systematic study of HDO effects beyond critical thermodynamics and provide a controlled method for determining their impact on bubble nucleation.

papers.title: Learning What the True Labels Would Teach: Posterior Analytic Class-Incremental Learning with Unlabeled Data
ReAccess: Look Once, Stay Focused with Efficient Test Time Memory

XRISM/Xtend detection of solar wind charge exchange induced by multiple coronal mass ejections in 2024 August
papers.abstract: Solar wind charge exchange (SWCX) emission is often a major component of the soft X-ray background, but it also provides a remote diagnostic of the composition and ionization state of solar wind plasma. We present an analysis of a SWCX event observed with XRISM/Xtend during 2024 August 9-13. The event occurred during intense solar activity with multiple flares, including an X1.3-class solar flare, and associated coronal mass ejections (CMEs). We found a clear enhancement in the 0.3-3.0 keV count rate that occurred nearly simultaneously with an increase in the solar wind proton flux measured by ACE. We fitted the spectrum during the enhancement period with a set of Gaussian emission lines. In addition to the commonly detected C, N, and O lines, we detected Ne, Mg, Si, and Fe lines at $>15\sigma$ significance. We extracted two characteristic periods within the enhanced interval based on the CME arrival timeline. The O$_{\rm VIII}$/Si$_{\rm XIII}$ line ratio changed significantly between the two periods, suggesting contributions from multiple CME components. We then applied the AtomDB charge exchange model with a multi-temperature setup. The estimated ionization temperatures for Ne, Mg, Si, and Fe increased with the peak soft X-ray flux of the associated solar flares. This trend suggests that coronal heating becomes more efficient for more intense flares. Meanwhile, the ionization temperatures were lower than typical flare electron temperatures, implying that CME plasma may have been released into interplanetary space under non-equilibrium ionization conditions. We also found an indication of an inverse-FIP pattern, with reduced relative abundances of Si and S. These results demonstrate that XRISM/Xtend can diagnose the coronal plasma through SWCX emission, including heavy ions such as Ne, Mg, and Si, which are difficult to measure with current in-situ instruments (e.g., ACE satellite).

papers.title: Convergence rates of moment--SOS hierarchies with correlative sparsity via gluing and projection
papers.abstract: This paper studies convergence rates of moment--SOS hierarchies with correlative sparsity. Following the method proposed in~\cite{tran}, we bound the Hausdorff distance between the set of sparse truncated moment sequences and sparse truncated pseudo-moment sequences. The central step is a quantitative gluing lemma on a clique tree: local moment errors and separator discrepancies in total variation control the error of a joint approximating measure. Over hypercube, polynomial kernels give the convergence rates $O((\log_2r)^3/r^2)$ for the correlative sparse quadratic module and $O(r^{-2})$ for the correlative sparse preordering, where the certificate degree is $2r$. On compact basic semialgebraic sets, slack variable lifting and global atom projection yield $O((\log_2r)^{3\Lo/2}/r^{\Lo})$ and $O(r^{-\Lo})$ with a Łojasiewicz exponent $0<\Lo \le1$. These bounds hold for fixed-degree Hausdorff distances and polynomial objective gaps. We also extend to result to the correlative sparse quadratic-module rate for scalar objectives with clique-local polynomial matrix constraints.

papers.title: Variational Corrections to Strong-Disorder Renormalization in the Two-Dimensional Random Transverse Field Ising Model on Quantum Hardware
papers.abstract: Strong-disorder renormalization-group (SDRG) methods provide an effective description of disordered quantum many-body systems by identifying the dominant couplings for the low energy physics. However, the resulting renormalization-group flow is approximate and neglects correlations beyond the RG description. Here, we investigate whether variational quantum optimization can be used to correct these approximations. Building on the emergent-coupling-based ansatz (ECBA) developed for the one-dimensional random Heisenberg model, we introduce a formulation adapted to the two-dimensional random transverse field Ising model. The SDRG flow determines the structure of the circuit, while variational optimization allows the state to deviate from the RG approximation. We study the resulting ansatz numerically and experimentally on an IQM superconducting quantum processor. For a 16-qubit system, we perform full variational optimization on the quantum processor, while a 49-qubit system is investigated using pre-optimized parameters, achieving a relative energy accuracy of 89% and 97%, respectively. Our results demonstrate that RG information can be translated into shallow, hardware-compatible quantum circuits while variational optimization enables corrections beyond the underlying RG approximation also for two-dimensional systems.

papers.title: Delay-induced anomalous density-polarization relation in chiral active matter
papers.abstract: Aligning active matter can spontaneously exhibit diverse forms of ordered collective motion, and higher local density is generally expected to enhance local polarization. Meanwhile, delays in agents' responses are widespread in real active systems, raising the question of how delayed alignment affects collective motion and, in particular, whether higher local density still strengthens polar order. Here, using a chiral active particle (CAP) model with delayed alignment, we uncover a counterintuitive anomalous density-polarization relation (DPR) within droplets: the local polarization first increases and then decreases with increasing local density. Analysis of the deviation-angle dynamics reveals a delay-induced supercritical discrete Hopf bifurcation. Noise-sustained oscillations before the bifurcation and self-sustained oscillations afterward broaden the deviation-angle distribution and reduce polarization. Increasing the delay shifts the bifurcation to lower densities, enhancing the anomalous DPR in agreement with simulations. Using the nonequilibrium landscape-flux theory, we further identify the nonequilibrium flux as the dynamical origin of the anomalous DPR. Our findings not only establish time delay as a control knob for collective behavior in chiral active matter, but also offer a useful analytical perspective on anomalous density-order relations in other nonequilibrium systems exhibiting collective order.

papers.title: Affine pairs of minimizing units in totally real non-Galois cubic fields
papers.abstract: Let $\Gamma$ be a rank-two subgroup of the integral norm-one units in a totally real non-Galois cubic field. We prove that two distinct affinely equivalent minima of Godwin's spread on $\Gamma\setminus\{1\}$ generate $\Gamma$ and determine its complete minimum set: a pair with sum $\pm2$ or a triple of integral translates of product one. Every minimum generates the order $\mathbb{Z}[\Gamma]$. For an order whose norm-one units have such a pair, the order generated by its units is the smallest suborder with the same minimum value. We also give explicit families and a maximal order with minima in two distinct affine classes.

papers.title: Transferable Neural CBFs via Generalized Closure
Recovery of accidental bound states in the continuum in vertically asymmetric photonic lattices through radiation-source parity restoration
papers.abstract: Vertical asymmetry generally precludes accidental bound states in the continuum (BICs) in planar photonic lattices, yet the underlying physical mechanism remains unclear. In this study, we show that accidental-BIC formation is governed by the definite parity of the transverse radiation-source profile rather than by geometric vertical mirror symmetry. A semianalytical coupled-mode analysis shows that an accidental BIC occurs when the radiation overlap integral of a leaky Bloch mode vanishes. We decompose the overlap into contributions from the even- and odd-parity components of the transverse radiation-source profile. Complete radiation suppression requires both contributions to vanish simultaneously. In vertically symmetric lattices, the source profile has definite even or odd parity, causing one contribution to vanish identically. Thickness tuning can null the remaining contribution and produce an accidental BIC. In vertically asymmetric lattices, by contrast, both parity components are generally present. The waveguide dispersion forbids their simultaneous vanishing, thereby precluding an accidental BIC. Introducing a parity-restoring layer into a vertically asymmetric lattice restores definite parity to the transverse radiation-source profile, thereby enabling the formation of an accidental BIC. Finite-element simulations confirm the analytically predicted recovery of accidental BICs for both TE$_0$ and TE$_1$ Bloch modes.

papers.title: LEDGER: Auditable Agent Memory Under Change
Advancing Cognitive Pairwise Comparisons for Human-Centric Artificial Intelligence and Data Science: A Human-in-the-Loop Framework
Improving Radio SLAM via Information Sharing: Collaborative Performance Bounds
papers.abstract: This paper studies the fundamental performance limits of radio-based collaborative simultaneous localization and mapping (C-SLAM) in dense vehicular environments towards the 6G integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) era. We consider a collaborative estimation task consisting of multiple user equipments (UEs) with unknown local state variables together with joint estimation of unknown states of the environment landmarks or targets, using cellular radio measurements. Specifically, a posterior Cramér-Rao bound (PCRB) is derived for such centralized multi-UE cellular radio SLAM with information sharing, capturing the effects of the number of involved UEs, their geometric configuration, and their mutually different abilities to measure or observe different landmarks. The analysis reveals how information sharing scales with UE density, identifies regimes of diminishing returns, and provides estimator-independent limits for collaborative radio-based environment mapping and localization. The provided numerical results validate the proposed framework in a vehicular system context, while also demonstrating substantial gains against more ordinary single-UE radio SLAM approach.

papers.title: Navital Gym: Rule-Graded Agent Environments for Indian Workflows
Linear Algebra over Bands
papers.abstract: We introduce Eckmann-Hilton operators on bands, which allow for a suite of matroidal constructions, in particular, matroid unions and matroid stable intersections. This enables the construction of general linear monoids over bands. Geometrically, we show that matroid stable intersection extends the transverse intersection of linear spaces over fields and the stable intersection of tropical linear spaces, lending new insight into intersection theory on bands.
