papers.title: Cartan geometry and the Hamiltonian analysis of gravitational actions in terms of forms
papers.abstract: The purpose of the paper is to review the Hamiltonian formulation for several actions related to general relativity that can be written in terms of differential forms. As we will show the powerful ideas of Cartan geometry can be used to simplify the Hamiltonian analysis and arrive at a coherent and comprehensive geometrical understanding of it.

papers.title: Constructing high-dimensional representations of twin groups via several techniques
papers.abstract: In this article, we consider the twin group $T_n$ for a positive integer $n$ and present two techniques for constructing high-dimensional and complicated representations of $T_n$. The first technique consists of composing a known representation of $T_n$ with the well-established Cohen map, while the second technique relies on the tensor product of two known representations of $T_n$. To implement these techniques, we consider the two representations $\eta_1$ and $\eta_2$ of $T_n$ introduced recently by Nasser. The first technique is applied to the representation $\eta_1: T_n \longrightarrow \mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{F}_n)$, which maps $T_n$ into the automorphism group of the free group $\mathbb{F}_n$ with $n$ generators. The second technique is applied to the representation $\eta_2: T_n \longrightarrow \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{Z}[t^{\pm 1}])$, which maps $T_n$ into the general linear group over the ring of Laurent polynomials in an indeterminate $t$. Using these techniques, we construct new high-degree representations of $T_n$ and examine, for some of them, structural properties such as faithfulness and reducibility. This work provides new avenues for developing representations of $T_n$ and related groups using these techniques.

papers.title: MolReps: Taking SELFIES, Making SMILES, Teaching LLMs
The Göttsche conjecture and the Göttsche--Yau--Zaslow formula
papers.abstract: The aim of these notes is to give an account, intended for the non-specialist, of the two proofs of the Göttsche conjecture given, respectively, first by Tzeng, and shortly after by Kool, Shende and Thomas. Given a smooth, complex, projective surface $S$ and a positive integer $\delta$, the Göttsche conjecture predicts that if $L$ is a sufficiently positive line bundle on $S$, then the number of $\delta$-nodal curves in a general $\delta$-dimensional linear subsystem $\Lambda\subset |L|$ is given by a universal polynomial of degree $\delta$ in the four numbers $L^2$, $L K_S$, $K_S^2$, and $c_2(S)$. Besides, the Göttsche--Yau--Zaslow formula expresses the generating function of the aforementioned numbers of $\delta$-nodal curves in terms of three explicit quasimodular forms and two unknown universal power series, whose coefficients can be determined by recursion.

papers.title: EDITORS Know Your Style! Editing LoRA Subspaces for Stylistic Attribution and Imitation
Tight Width Minimisation of Self-Join-Free Quantified Conjunctive Queries
DetourBench: Trajectory-Level Evaluation of Interactive Agents with Exact Minimum-Action Bounds
Characterization of Cubic Graphs with Exactly Two Lonely Edges
papers.abstract: Perfect matchings are fundamental to understanding structural connectivity in cubic graphs, with "lonely edges" (edges in exactly one perfect matching) forming a critical underexplored class. Goedgebeur et al. (J. Graph Theory, 112 (2026) 276-289) established an upper bound of 6 on the number of lonely edges in 3-connected non-double covered cubic graphs and completely characterized the classes $\mathcal{U}_k$ for $3 \le k \le 6$. Narayana et al. subsequently gave a recursive characterization of the subclass in which the two lonely edges lie in the same perfect matching. This paper completes the classification by presenting a full structural characterization of $\mathcal{U}_2$, the family of 3-connected cubic graphs with exactly two lonely edges. We identify the minimally non-contractible "primitive kernels" of $\mathcal{U}_2$ and develop constructive operations to generate any graph in $\mathcal{U}_2$ from these kernels.

papers.title: Singular limits of the subelliptic Allen-Cahn equation and geometric flows
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the singular limits of a bistable reaction-diffusion equation in a subelliptic setting, where the standard Euclidean diffusion is replaced by a subelliptic operator defined by a family of vector fields. We introduce a Riemannian approximation of these vector fields to regularize the problem, yielding a uniformly parabolic equation whose ellipticity degenerates as the singular parameter vanishes. We prove that the family of solutions converges globally in time to the stable equilibria away from a propagating interface. Our approach uses the definition of generalized geometric flow developed by Barles--Souganidis, uniquely defined through the level-set equation and viscosity solutions. The behavior of the interface depends on the traveling wave speed c: when c is not 0, the front propagates with constant normal velocity governed by a first-order subelliptic eikonal equation. When c = 0, the front evolves according to the horizontal mean curvature flow equation defined by the original vector fields. At present, this case comes with limitations: it requires a more restrictive condition on test functions at characteristic points to define generalized flows, where the horizontal gradient vanishes and standard arguments break down. This framework relies on our earlier work, where the equivalence between the generalized flow and the level-set approach was established when the vector fields generate a step-two Carnot group. We also assume that the comparison principle holds for the level-set equation in order for the level-set approach to be well-posed.

papers.title: Vision-Language Model-Based Phase-OTDR Event Classification
Interpretable deep concepts of organoid morphology
Stochastic Modelling of High-frequency (HF) Crypto Limit Order Book (LOB) with General Compound Marked Hawkes Process
papers.abstract: The paper is devoted to the stochastic modelling of high-frequency crypto Limit Order Book (LOB) with general compound marked Hawkes process (GCMHP). We consider marked Hawkes process in a general form. LLN and FCLTs with stochastic and constant centralization are stated. Numerical example for high-frequency LOB dataset for BTC (bitcoin) based on sources from HF crypto LOB data is presented as well. The novelty of the paper lies in the new LLN and FCLTs for the GCMHP, and in the new application associated with high-frequency (HF) crypto LOB.

papers.title: Optimal Dynamic Fees for L2s: A Vault Approach
Evidence Diet: When Graph Evidence Helps LLMs Rank Competing Candidates
Universal Quantizer Design for Identification of Systems with Memory
Hierarchical Regime-Conditioned Dynamics for Spatiotemporal Graphs
From antidepressants to psychedelics: revisiting the pharmacology of so-called serotoninergic treatments
papers.abstract: Recent years have seen a resurgence of interest in serotoninergic psychedelics as potential treatment for diverse psychiatric disorders. Here, we will delve into the molecular mechanisms of drugs used to treat depression and obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), with implications on the mechanism of action of so-called ''serotoninergic'' psychedelics as well as selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs). In particular, we argue that the pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic properties of SSRIs suggest that the inhibition of the serotonin transporter (SERT) alone does not provide a comprehensive account of their clinical effects. On the contrary, the SSRI posology required to treat depression and OCD is consistent with their major molecular target(s) displaying an SSRI affinity much lower than SERT. Such is the case for the tyrosine receptor kinase B (TrkB), recently described as a putative target for drugs with antidepressant effects. TrkB might thus provide a unifying framework for understanding the therapeutic effects of antidepressant drugs. We finally discuss the pharmacological implications of this hypothesis on the therapeutical potential of psychedelics.

papers.title: Maximum principle preserving approximation of scalar conservation equations with a fractional Laplacian
Creation Sequences for Numerical Semigroups and Exact Counts of Semigroup Partitions
papers.abstract: A numerical semigroup is a subset of the non-negative integers that contains $0$, is closed under addition and has finite complement. A threshold graph is built by adding vertices one at a time, each new vertex being isolated or dominating, and the record of these choices is its \emph{creation sequence}. Reading the creation sequence as a lattice path gives an integer partition and, through the Keith--Nath correspondence, a numerical set in which the dominating vertices are the elements and the isolated vertices are the gaps. We show that threshold graphs with an isolated vertex correspond bijectively to numerical sets, and we study numerical semigroups through their creation sequences. We prove that in the creation sequence of a numerical semigroup of multiplicity $m$ every block of ones and every non-initial block of zeros has length less than $m$, we give criteria for partitions with a unique smallest part and with two distinct part sizes, and we classify all partitions with at most four parts. We show that every partition $\lambda$ with $g$ parts corresponding to a numerical semigroup satisfies $\ell(\lambda)\ge\lambda_1$ and, more strongly, fits inside the staircase $(g,g-1,\dots,1)$; equivalently, its creation sequence begins with a Dyck path. Its size equals the genus plus the Weierstrass weight of the semigroup, and asymptotically at most half of all partitions correspond to numerical semigroups. Finally, we obtain exact formulas for the numbers of partitions of $n$ corresponding to numerical semigroups of genus $g$, multiplicity $m$ and Frobenius number $f$, valid in the sharp ranges $g\ge n/2$, $m>n/3$ and $f\ge n-\frac{n-1}{4}$. These formulas solve the open problems posed by Burson, Nam and Sisneros-Thiry \cite{BNS}, recover all of their counting theorems, and correct several of their statements.

papers.title: Optimal Importance Sampling Densities for Estimating Several Expectations at Once
papers.abstract: Simulation studies often estimate several quantities from a single sample, and the best importance sampling density depends on how the errors on these quantities are combined. We characterise the optimal auxiliary density for a general error criterion. We show that it is the nominal density reweighted by a weighted length of the vector of estimated functions, where the weights are set by the error criterion, or by the curvature of the loss when the criterion comes from a loss on the errors. We also provide a lower bound on the best achievable error. The optimal density is explicit for smooth losses, including the usual losses on covariance matrices. We also derive allocation laws for the cells of a histogram and characterise the minimax density for the probabilities of several events. When there is no closed form, we show how to compute the optimal density numerically.

papers.title: Investigating the Impact of CI-Source Sensitivity in Carbon-Aware Resource Management Systems
On the volume of amoebas of complete intersections
papers.abstract: We study the $2k$-dimensional volume of the amoeba of a smooth complete intersection $V$ of dimension $k$ in $(\C^*)^n$, $n\ge2k$, with Newton polytopes $\Delta_1,\dots,\Delta_{n-k}$. For $n=2k$ we prove $\Vol(\A(V))\ge\mathcal M(V)/\MV(\Delta_1,\dots,\Delta_k,-\Delta_1,\dots,-\Delta_k)$, where $\mathcal M(V)$ is the coamoeba volume counted with multiplicity, and we show $\mathcal M(V)\ge\pi^{2k}$ for plane curves ($k=1$, $n=2$) whose Newton polygon is not centrally symmetric, for nondegenerate varieties with odd $\MV(\Delta_1,\dots,\Delta_k,\Delta_1,\dots,\Delta_k)$, and for smooth towers of curve fibrations. We determine the equality case for curves and towers, and prove that $k$-planes in general position never attain the bound. For $n>2k$ we prove two-sided bounds for $\Hm^{2k}(\A(V))$ through coordinate projections, and show that for generic coefficients almost every fibre of the amoeba map is an orbit of a finite group. For lines we prove that in several random models the area of the amoeba of a line in $(\C^*)^n$ is asymptotic to $\frac\pi2n\log n$, and we compute its limit under degenerations of the configuration. Finally we characterise the varieties attaining the extremal volumes. For $n=2k$ every regular fibre of the amoeba map has an even number of points, divisible by $4$ for real varieties with $k\ge2$; the volume-maximal varieties are those with two-to-one amoeba maps and maximal rolled coamoebas, and they are never real when $k\ge2$; a volume-minimal plane curve is characterised by a group of symmetries of maximal order, and its amoeba has no holes. For $n>2k$ the extremal varieties lie in translates of $2k$-dimensional subtori.

papers.title: LAMOST III Low-resolution Spectroscopic Survey: Overview and Target Selection
papers.abstract: We present an overview of the LAMOST III Low-resolution Spectroscopic Survey (LRS), including its scientific goals, target selection strategy, and current observing status. Targets in the main survey are selected via weighted random sampling, using the inverse local density in the Hertzsprung-Russell (HR) diagram and in the G-magnitude distribution, with additional enhancement in selected regions of the HR diagram. The main survey is complemented by 35 dedicated add-on catalogs (including very metal-poor star candidates, halo stars, hot/young stars, wide binaries, extragalactic sources and so on) and a time-domain program providing multi-epoch spectroscopy of binaries and other peculiar systems. LAMOST III LRS is designed to map the structure and evolution of the Galactic disk, reconstruct the assembly and early chemical-enrichment history of the Galactic halo, improve stellar-parameter calibration, and characterize rare and variable objects. By June 2025, the LAMOST III LRS had obtained 1.53 million low-resolution spectra from 658 plates, corresponding to 1,264,052 unique sources. Relative to LAMOST I+II, the current sample is enriched in O/B stars, subgiants, main-sequence turn-off stars, metal-poor stars, and other previously underrepresented populations. In particular, the fractions of metal-poor and very metal-poor stars increase from 3.8% and 0.4% in LAMOST I+II to 9.0% and 1.1% in LAMOST III LRS, respectively, demonstrating the improved efficiency of the revised target-selection strategy for Galactic archaeology and stellar astrophysics.

papers.title: ProcReverser: Multi-Agent Black-Box Microarchitectural Reverse Engineering for Processor Vulnerability Analysis
Conversing with a Conversational Agent: A Real Conversation, Not a Simulated One
A conic optimization framework for shape-constrained functional regression analysis
papers.abstract: Standard regression methods do not always guarantee that the estimated model reflects prior knowledge about how predictors relate to the response, which motivates constrained regression. When the effects to be estimated are smooth nonlinear functions, a natural family of constraints is that of shape constraints, such as sign, monotonicity, or curvature, which encode qualitative properties that these functions are often expected to satisfy. While shape-constrained estimation of smooth functions is well established in classical regression with scalar covariates and response, its extension to functional regression, where the coefficients are themselves functions, remains largely unexplored. In this paper, we propose the functional shape-constrained conic P-spline estimator (FunSCOPE), a unified framework for shape-constrained functional linear regression that covers scalar-on-function, function-on-scalar, and function-on-function models, and in which any combination of the shapes above can be imposed on the functional regression coefficient. Building on a P-spline approach, the desired shapes are expressed as conditions on the scalar regression coefficients, which leads to an estimation problem formulated as a conic optimization problem. For univariate coefficients, as in scalar-on-function, function-on-scalar, and a particular case of the function-on-function regression, the concurrent case, these conditions are both necessary and sufficient, in contrast to existing approaches, which provide only sufficient conditions; for bivariate coefficients, as in general function-on-function models, they are neither necessary nor sufficient. Numerical experiments show that FunSCOPE outperforms competing methods in terms of estimation error and computational time.

papers.title: Network-Native DNN Architecture Synthesis for Distributed Inference
Medical question answering collapses in Hausa: a pre-registered pilot on three small open models
No-Shot Text-to-Speech: Limitations of Zero-Shot TTS and its Evaluation Methods in Representing Queer and Transgender Voices
CuRSE-Bench: A Benchmark for Probing Cultural Blind Spots in Text-to-Image Safety Evaluation
Collapsibility of Vietoris--Rips complexes of hypercube graphs in codimension two
papers.abstract: Shukla conjectured that the collapsibility number of the Vietoris-Rips complex $\mathrm{VR}(I_n;r)$ of the $n$-dimensional hypercube graph at scale $r$ equals $2^r$ for all $n\ge r+1$. We prove the conjecture for $n=r+2$ and every $r$, which gives the first known cases with $r\ge 4$ beyond the cross-polytope case $n=r+1$. Writing $\mathrm{VR}(I_n;r)$ as the independence complex of the graph $H_{n,r}$ that joins two points when their Hamming distance exceeds $r$, we construct a cover of $H_{r+2,r}$ by $2^r$ co-chordal subgraphs. The key general tool is the inequality that, for every graph $G$, the $\theta$-number of Bıyıkoğlu and Civan of the independence complex of $G$, and hence the collapsibility number of that complex, is at most the co-chordal cover number of $G$; this strengthens Woodroofe's regularity bound. We also show, using a theorem of Alon, Jin, and Sudakov, that the induced matching number of $H_{n,r}$ equals $2^r$ for every $n>r$, and that $\mathrm{VR}(I_n;r)$ is vertex decomposable if and only if $r=1$ or $n=r+1$. As consequences, we determine the top degree of nonvanishing homology and the coconnectivity of $\mathrm{VR}(I_{r+2};r)$, and we prove split injectivity in top-degree integral homology. Finally, assuming a recent skew Hamming set-pair theorem of Gao and Zhao, we prove that the collapsibility number of $\mathrm{VR}(I_n;r)$ is at most $2^{r+1}-4$ for all $n>r\ge 2$.

papers.title: Surprise-Gated Memory for Live Speaker Diarization
Tight PAC-Bayes Generalisation Guarantees for Large Language Model Judges
Quantum chaos from time-dependent CFT states at large central charge
papers.abstract: We provide a first study of the behavior of four probes on heavy, time-dependent background states of conformal field theories at large central charge. Employing the monodromy method and including subleading corrections to the identity block, we compute the correlation function of two light and two middle-heavy operators on such a heavy background, by switching on a small interaction between the light and middle-heavy sectors. Summing the discontinuity contributions and analytically continuing from Euclidean to Lorentzian signature, we show that the out-of-time-ordered correlator (OTOC) exhibits maximal chaos, that is, the Lyapunov exponent saturates the MSS bound.

papers.title: Criterion for Glasner property and IC-Rigidity for actions on homogeneous space
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a semi-group acting continuously on a compact metric space $X$. The action $G\curvearrowright X$ is called Glasner if for every infinite set $A\subseteq X$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, there exists $g\in G$ such that $gA$ is $\varepsilon$-dense in $X$. Let $\mathcal{K}(X)$ denote the space of nonempty compact subsets of $X$. A $G$-invariant Borel probability measure on $\mathcal{K}(X)$ is called an invariant random compact (IRC), and the action is IC-rigid if $\delta_X$ is the only IRC supported on infinite compact subsets of $X$. In this paper we give a pair-correlation criterion implying both IC-rigidity and the Glasner property. As an application, we prove both these properties for finitely generated $\operatorname{Ad}$-Zariski-dense semi-groups acting on compact homogeneous spaces $G/\Lambda$, where $G$ is connected and noncompact with simple Lie algebra and $\Lambda<G$ is a cocompact lattice; in particular, this applies to finitely generated Zariski-dense semi-groups of $\mathrm{SL}_d(\mathbb{R})$ and $\mathrm{PSL}_d(\mathbb{R})$. We also derive a Fourier-analytic criterion for semi-group actions on $\mathbb{T}^d$ and use it to prove IC-rigidity for actions arising from suitable matrix-valued polynomials.

papers.title: ForeSay: Tell the Future in Words, Branch the Details in Noise for Precipitation Nowcasting
Non-stationary motion of an inextensible closed string
papers.abstract: We consider a non-stationary motion of an inextensible closed string. The motion of the string is governed by nonlinear and nonlocal hyperbolic equations. The nonlocality of the equations is caused by the unknown tension of the string and reflects the inextensibility of the string. We show that the initial value problem to the equations of motion is well-posed locally in time. In the proof, it is crucial to show a strict positivity of the tension when the string is in motion. To this end, we derive a sharp lower bound of the Green's function for a periodic boundary value problem. We also derive a blow-up criterion of smooth solutions, which states that any singularities on the velocity or on the tension of the string do not take place before a curvature singularity appears.

papers.title: Condensation-related expansion work of water vapor as a major pathway for kinetic energy generation in the lower atmosphere
papers.abstract: Earth's atmosphere operates a steam cycle: water evaporates from the surface, expands as vapor, condenses in colder air, and returns as precipitation. Yet its power and relationship to atmospheric mechanical power remain poorly quantified. Applying the Clausius--Clapeyron relation between saturated vapor expansion work and latent heat converted at Carnot efficiency to vertically distributed condensation, we derive the steam-engine power as a sum of the gravitational and condensation-related contributions, $W_v=W_g+W_c$; it is not the net power of a complete moist-air cycle. Using twelve years of GPM/DPR spectral latent-heating profiles and MERRA-2 fields, we estimate $W_v\simeq4.1$ W m$^{-2}$, with $W_c\simeq2.8$ W m$^{-2}$. Separately, we diagnose total atmospheric mechanical power $W=W_P+W_K\simeq4.3$ W m$^{-2}$, comprising gravitational power of precipitation $W_P\simeq1.1$ W m$^{-2}$ and kinetic energy generation $W_K\simeq3.2$ W m$^{-2}$, including $2.4$ W m$^{-2}$ below 500 hPa. Both correspondences $W_v\simeq W$ and $W_c\simeq W_K$ lie within 20--30\% uncertainty estimates. To explain these correspondences, we propose that $W_c$ generates the potential energy associated with surface pressure gradients. Cross-isobaric flow in the frictional lower atmosphere converts this energy into kinetic energy. In a horizontally isothermal atmosphere, this positive pressure work would be nearly cancelled by compression aloft. An idealized circulation illustrates how differential heating can offset compression, allowing nearly isobaric upper return flow. In the proposed mechanism, condensation-driven circulation unlocks this thermal compensation thus providing a major pathway for lower-atmospheric kinetic energy generation. We discuss how changes in the coupling between condensation and differential heating could test this proposed causal relationship.

papers.title: The Cybersecurity Dataset Observatory: Which Data for AI in Cybersecurity?
Auditing World-Model Explanations in Retail Forecasting: Faithfulness, Accuracy and Price Response
Prediction-Driven Contract Matching with Controlled Overbooking for Cloud-Edge DDoS Scrubbing Markets
Experimental observation of higher-harmonic generation of whistler waves in magnetized plasma of Large Volume Plasma Device
papers.abstract: We report the higher-harmonic generation of whistler waves using a loop antenna in the Large Volume Plasma Device (LVPD). The antenna is energized using a pulse-forming network (PFN), and the excited magnetic fluctuations are measured using a three-axis B-dot probe. Experiments are performed in a moderate-density ($n_e \sim 1-2 \times 10^{17}\ \text{m}^{-3}$), low-temperature ($T_e \sim 2-5\ \text{eV}$) argon plasma in a uniform axial magnetic field ($B_z \sim 6.2\ \text{G}$). A Helmholtz coil is employed to investigate the dependence of the wave response and propagation on the local magnetic-field configuration. A clear distinction between wave characteristics is observed in the absence and presence of plasma: in plasma, the excited wave shows a significant $\delta B_y$ component along with $\delta B_x$, indicating polarization. In addition to the fundamental frequency, distinct spectral peaks are observed at $300\ \text{kHz}$, $450\ \text{kHz}$, and $600\ \text{kHz}$. These harmonics indicate nonlinear wave-plasma interactions, and bicoherence analysis further provides evidence of nonlinear coupling between the observed frequency components. The spatial propagation of the wave was systematically diagnosed using a linear array of five identical B-dot probes. Spatial cross-correlation analysis reveals strong structural coherence during wave propagation, allowing the explicit experimental determination of the wave phase velocity ($V_{ph}$) and parallel wave number ($k_{\parallel}$) for the generated higher harmonics. The measured propagation is oblique at an angle of approximately $48^\circ$ with respect to the background magnetic field, and the experimental dispersion relation agrees with the cold-plasma oblique whistler dispersion relation within experimental uncertainty.

papers.title: Communication-Efficient Hamiltonian Evaluation for Massively Parallel Tensor-Product Bitstring Selected Configuration Interaction
papers.abstract: Extreme-scale selected configuration interaction (SCI) requires coordinated Hamiltonian evaluation, distributed CI-vector storage, and interprocess communication on massively parallel computers. Our previous work [J. Chem. Phys. 164, 194103 (2026)] introduced the tensor-product bitstring selected configuration interaction (TBSCI) framework, combining on-the-fly Hamiltonian evaluation with fully distributed CI-vector storage and enabling parallel diagonalization of trillion-determinant spaces on up to 54,000 Fugaku nodes. Here, we introduce FLIP, a new Hamiltonian evaluation algorithm within TBSCI that reorganizes the CI-vector layout and excitation-link data to replace remote CI-coefficient transfers for $\alpha$-electron double excitations with local coefficient access and link retrieval from nearby MPI ranks. In communication-intensive full configuration interaction (FCI) benchmarks on Fugaku, no exposed communication waiting time was recorded on the slowest process across all 32 measured Hamiltonian-vector multiplications. For N$_2$/cc-pVTZ with $2.62\times10^{12}$ determinants, the multiplication achieved 91.3% strong-scaling efficiency from 18,000 to 81,000 nodes (more than 3.8 million compute cores). We also obtained an FCI reference potential-energy curve for N$_2$/cc-pVTZ. At all six bond lengths, spin bitstrings selected by their collective weights in reference SCI wavefunctions yielded variational TBSCI energies within 0.1 m$E_h$ of FCI using fewer than 1% of the FCI determinants, demonstrating the compactness of the tensor-product bitstring representation. Finally, we discuss local construction of double-excitation links to substantially reduce communication volume and eliminate persistent storage of precomputed double-link tables for future second-order perturbation theory calculations with large external determinant spaces.

papers.title: QuarkDB: A Hybrid Database System for Quantum Data Management
Do Hierarchical Networks Actually Learn? Insights from Word-of-Mouth Estimation
papers.abstract: We study recursive estimation of a constant state vector by a hierarchical network of asymmetrically informed linear estimators, modeled as a directed tree. Only the leaves observe the regression signal, whereas every other estimator learns by word of mouth from noisy signal estimates relayed by its children. Authority within the hierarchy is expressed through common prior information: after each round, every estimator adopts the estimate and error covariance broadcast by the root. The more accurate this common information, the larger the effective noise variance on local observations, which makes estimation intrinsically self-defeating. The resulting performance is the subject of this paper. We show that recursive least-squares (RLS) estimators do learn the state in mean square, albeit slowly. Under strong persistency of excitation, the broadcast error covariance decays polynomially in time, at a rate that we characterize by upper and lower bounds of matching order. The exponent is determined by the smallest number of relays between a leaf and the root, and it decreases exponentially with this number.

papers.title: An Efficient Training Paradigm for Image Restoration via Improved Fréchet Loss
A Recursive Construction of Perfect Arrays of Every Shape $2^{a_1}\times\cdots\times2^{a_d}$ over the Unit Quaternions
What Do Digital Traces Predict? Task Effects, Student Differences, and Critical Online Reasoning
Parametrised-Quadratic Interface Reconstruction and Geometric Velocity Extension in the Volume-of-Fluid Framework
papers.abstract: A conservative Volume-of-Fluid (VOF) framework using local parametric-curve interface reconstruction (PI-VOF) is developed for geometric interface propagation on fixed Cartesian grids. While VOF methods achieve conservative and second-order accurate interface advection under prescribed velocity fields, normal-velocity-driven interface propagation requires the interfacial velocity to be extended to neighbouring staggered-grid locations. Existing studies on interface evolution employ auxiliary distance functions, kernel smoothers, or high-resolution VOF in multiple grids to compute propagation velocities and address first-order-accuracy limitations. In contrast, PI-VOF directly employs higher-order parametric interface geometry for local normal-velocity extension, aiming to achieve second-order accurate interface evolution on fixed Cartesian grids. The resulting velocity field is employed in conservative geometric advection using a directionally split Eulerian-implicit and Lagrangian-explicit (EI-LE) scheme, while the reconstructed interface provides the geometric information required for curvature evaluation and the ghost-fluid finite-difference discretisation of sharp interfacial Dirichlet conditions. Static reconstruction and reversible-vortex advection tests demonstrate higher-order interface geometry and approximately second-order transport convergence, with mass conservation to the chosen tolerance on refined grids. Prescribed normal-velocity and curvature-dependent propagation tests establish near second-order convergence. Coupled Stefan benchmarks involving capillarity and attachment kinetics demonstrate approximately second-order thermal convergence and decreasing interface errors under mesh refinement. The results establish a geometric formulation connecting conservative VOF transport, local normal-velocity extension, and sharp Stefan conditions for evolving interfaces.

papers.title: Solubility and Diffusion of Hydrogen Isotopes and Helium in Molten FLiBe
papers.abstract: Tritium produced in molten 2LiF-BeF$_2$ (FLiBe) may dissolve as T$_2$ or as TF, which differ greatly in solubility. Permeation experiments give a solubility close to that of HF and a flux proportional to the square root of the T$_2$ pressure, which has usually been taken as evidence of dissociation. We have developed a fixed-charge classical potential for FLiBe containing atomic tritium, T$_2$, TF, the hydride ion T$^-$ and helium, fitted only to periodic DFT calculations for hydrogen. The nuclei are classical, so the solubilities apply to all hydrogen isotopes. The host reproduces the measured density and neutron structure factor but is too fluid close to the liquidus. The calculated solubilities of T$_2$ and TF agree with experiment, and neither molecule dissociates in the melt. Because TF is much more soluble, it holds most of the dissolved tritium unless the salt is strongly reducing, and at constant redox potential its concentration varies with the square root of the T$_2$ pressure, which accounts for the permeation results without dissociation. Helium does not change the solubility of T$_2$: a helium bubble in the melt takes up T$_2$ as its Henry constant predicts, while TF is enriched at the bubble surface. T$_2$ diffuses somewhat faster than measured, and TF and T$^-$ two to three times more slowly than T$_2$.

papers.title: High-order Crank-Nicolson method via diagonal Padé factorization
Some notes on Erdős' last equation
papers.abstract: We study the Diophantine equation $$n^h(x_1 + \ldots + x_n) = x_1 x_2 \cdots x_n,$$ where $h \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$, and $x_1 \le \ldots \le x_n \in \mathbb{Z}^+$. We define the solution set $ELE(h, n)$ consisting of all such integer tuples. We derive bounds on $x_n$ and $x_{n-1}$ in $ELE(h,n)$. We prove that $x_1 \cdot\ldots\cdot x_n \le n^h(n^h + 1)(n^h + n - 1)$. We also show that for $h = 1$, $x_{n-1} \le n + \max_{d \mid 2n^2 - 2n,\, d \le \sqrt{2n^2 - 2n}} d$, and for $h \ge 2$, the inequality $x_{n-1} \le 2n^h$ holds in $ELE(h, n)$. Moreover, we study the minimal value $g(h, n)$ of the largest coordinate $x_n$, and define $g(h) = \min_{n \ge 2} g(h,n)$. We prove that $$ \liminf_{n \to \infty} \frac{g(h,n)}{\frac{\log \log n \cdot \log \log \log \log n}{\log \log \log n}} \ge 1. $$ We also estimate the growth of the number of solutions. We show that for any $\varepsilon > 0,$ we have $\sum_{m \le n} |ELE(h,m)| < n^{h+1+\varepsilon} $ for sufficiently large $n$, and that $|ELE(h,n)| > n^{1 - \varepsilon}$ for infinitely many $n$.

papers.title: Sign Primal-Dual Gradient Dynamics for Supply-Demand Coordination under Binary Human Feedback
Correspondence-Free Camera Pose Estimation by Matching Moments
A scaling-based approach to mixed fractional $p$-Laplacian equations in $\mathbb{R}^N$
papers.abstract: We study equations driven by a sum of two fractional $p$-Laplacians with different orders and exponents. A central contribution of this paper is a Pohožaev identity for finite-energy weak solutions, established without additional regularity assumptions by means of a new approach based on scaling and convexity defects. This identity, which is of independent interest, yields nonexistence results for critical problems. Furthermore, we establish weighted Sobolev embeddings, construct an unbounded sequence of positive eigenvalues without relying on the Pohožaev identity, and prove multiplicity results for subcritical and doubly critical problems using scaling-based variational methods.

papers.title: Speed-Robust Scheduling for Total Completion Time
Regularizing Treatment Leakage for LLM-based Uplift Estimation
Multiple moiré polarization textures in twisted trilayers
papers.abstract: Twisted van der Waals layers exhibit nontrivial polarization textures from moiré-modulated stacking and the inherited sliding ferroelectricity. However, in any twisted bilayer, the topology of polarization texture is essentially fixed due to the inherent twist-stacking landscape for a given material. Here, this constraint is overcome in some twisted trilayers, where the relative moiré phase emerges as an additional structural degree of freedom. Using CrI$_3$ and BN as representative sliding ferroelectrics with distinct symmetries, it is clarified how the relative moiré phases reshape the trilayer stacking landscapes and tune the net polarization texture by layer sliding. The multiple moiré polarization textures can be attributed to the interference of original moiré patterns of the two bilayer subsystems.

papers.title: TRR: A Thermal Interaction Engine for Robot Simulation and RGBT Data Generation
QTOP: Scaling Humanoid Motion Tracking with Quantile Critics
Relationship between generic Hecke algebra modules and $0$-Hecke algebra modules
papers.abstract: Let $H_{R,a}(\mathfrak{S}_n)$ be the Hecke algebra over a principal ideal domain $R$ with parameter $a\in R$. The representation theories of $H_{\mathbb{C}(v^{1/2});v}(\mathfrak{S}_n)$ and $H_{\mathbb{C};0}(\mathfrak{S}_n)$ differ substantially and have largely been studied independently. In this paper, we relate the categories of finitely generated modules of these two algebras through specialization functors from the category of finitely generated $H_{\mathbb{C}[v^{1/2}];v}(\mathfrak{S}_n)$-modules. We first investigate the fundamental properties of these functors concerning dimensions, essential surjectivity, and characters. We then construct $H_{\mathbb{C}[v^{1/2}];v}(\mathfrak{S}_n)$-modules which, through these functors, provide connections between skew Specht modules of $H_{\mathbb{C}(v^{1/2});v}(\mathfrak{S}_n)$ and $0$-Hecke skew Specht modules of $H_{\mathbb{C};0}(\mathfrak{S}_n)$, and between Kazhdan--Lusztig cell modules of $H_{\mathbb{C}(v^{1/2});v}(\mathfrak{S}_n)$ and dual plactic class modules of $H_{\mathbb{C};0}(\mathfrak{S}_n)$. Both families of $H_{\mathbb{C};0}(\mathfrak{S}_n)$-modules are closely related to regular Schur labeled skew shape posets. We further explore how specialization functors relate the Frobenius characteristic to the quasisymmetric characteristic and connects the branching rules for skew Specht modules with those for $0$-Hecke skew Specht modules. Finally, we use the established connection with Kazhdan--Lusztig cell modules to obtain a result on the classification of dual plactic class modules up to isomorphism.

papers.title: Detecting False Self-Consistency in Density-Functional Calculations
papers.abstract: Density-functional calculations feed materials databases and machine-learning models, and are declared converged when energy changes and residuals fall below thresholds. We show that these criteria, and even the agreement of independent optimizers, can accept a state from which the energy still descends or whose Hamiltonian is inconsistent with the energy. A variational formulation of self-consistency in the space of Kohn-Sham Hamiltonians yields a descent probe that exposes lower states accessible from a returned solution, and a frozen-orbital Janak test detects such an inconsistency. Both apply to any code without modification. In VASP, a UO$_2$ PBE+$U$ calculation converges 1.46 eV above a lower state, and CoO and FeO converge as metals 0.8-0.9 eV above insulating states. In a census of 339 converged calculations on tungsten-free Materials Project structures, recomputed with a modified static protocol, 57 (16.8%) show energy decreases above the threshold, 49 without an initial energy rise exceeding the tolerance.

papers.title: VA-Assembly: View-Aligned Score Guidance for Training-Free 3D Part Assembly
PhaseCLIP: Phase-Aware Frequency-Domain Adaptation of Vision-Language Models for Few-Shot Remote-Sensing Classification
ThermoSight: From Appearance to Internal Thermofluid Fields via Physics-Guided Neural Reconstruction
Validation of Ariel candidates orbiting K-M stars
papers.abstract: One of the key goals of planetary population studies is to achieve broad coverage of the parameter space, which is not yet fully represented by confirmed planets. This limitation can be mitigated by including planets that have been statistically validated through a vetting procedure, even if they are not fully confirmed. In preparation for the Ariel mission, a Mission Candidate Sample has been assembled, comprising both confirmed planets and several unvalidated candidates. In this context, we apply a vetting analysis to a selected subsample of these candidates. Our methodology is based on the TRICERATOPS tool, aimed at confirming the presence of transiting planets or ruling out false-positive scenarios. We applied TRICERATOPS to a sample of 318 targets drawn from the last three Ariel TESS Planet Candidates catalogues. The analysis includes evaluation of statistical probabilities, as well as checks on stellar binarity indicators such as the Renormalized Unit Weight Error (RUWE) and the IPD_frac_multi_peak values from Gaia Data Release 3. Our analysis validated 56 candidates as planets, identified 29 false positives, and classified 35 as likely planets. These results are intended to support the Ariel mission by providing a probabilistic priority ranking to guide follow-up observations and optimise targets for atmospheric characterisation studies.

papers.title: On homogeneous hypertournaments
On Erdős' last equation
papers.abstract: For a positive integer $n\ge 2$, we look at the number of solutions of the Diophantine equation $$ n(x_1+\cdots+x_n)=x_1\cdots x_n. $$ Denoting by $f(n)$ this number we show that $\liminf_{n\to\infty} \log f(n)/\log n=0$.

papers.title: Baryonic Keys and the Inheritance of Crypto-Assets: Revisiting the Tales From the Crypt Protocol
Verification-Guided Safety-Repair of Learned Controllers
Top-Level Operational Equilibrium: When is the response of a distributed system predictable from its own telemetry?
EEGProbe: Do Vision-Language Models Really Understand EEG? A Benchmark for Signal-Grounded EEG Signals Evaluation
Longitudinal Parton Correlations in MRW-Type Unintegrated Double Parton Distributions
papers.abstract: Double parton scattering offers a way to investigate correlations between partons inside the proton that are absent from the usual product approximation for double parton distributions. In this contribution, we discuss how these correlations enter unintegrated double parton distributions when transverse momentum is generated using MRW-type prescriptions. Starting from non-factorized GS09 distributions evolved to unequal scales, we examine the double LO-MRW, virtuality-ordered MRW, and modified KMRW constructions, focusing on their transverse-momentum dependence and flavor structure.

papers.title: Treewidth and Separation Number: An Optimal Linear Bound
papers.abstract: The \emph{separation number} $\sn(G)$ of a graph $G$ is the smallest integer $a$ such that every subgraph $H$ of $G$ admits a separation $(A,B)$ of {\em order} $|A\cap B|\le a$ whose two sides $A\setminus B$ and $B\setminus A$ each contain at most $2|V(H)|/3$ vertices. Dvořák and Norin proved that $\tw(G)\le 15\sn(G)$ for every nonempty graph $G$. We improve the constant to its optimal value: every nonempty graph satisfies $\tw(G)\le 4\sn(G)-2$. This is best possible: for every $k\ge 2$, there is a graph $G_k$ with $\tw(G_k)=4k+2$ and $\sn(G_k)=k+1$.

papers.title: Extensions of $q$-supercongruences arising from a quadratic summation of Gasper and Rahman
papers.abstract: In this paper, inspired by recent work of Guo and Zhao, and of Guo and Zudilin, we establish two parametric extensions of their $q$-supercongruences using Gasper and Rahman's quadratic summation, the Chinese remainder theorem, and the creative microscoping method. These extensions yield two one-parameter generalizations of the $q$-supercongruences considered by Guo and Zhao and by Guo and Zudilin.

papers.title: Co-simulation-Based Safety-Assessment of Black-Box Maritime Cyber-Physical Systems
Flat and very flat pro-quasi-coherent pro-sheaves on ind-schemes
papers.abstract: This is a paper about homological algebra of flat pro-quasi-coherent pro-sheaves. We recall and collect various techniques such as accessibility and deconstructibility, and adopt them to ind-schemes under various assumptions. We also discuss the foundations of the notion of an ind-scheme.

Deep Learning for Satellite-Based Mountain Hazard Screening: A Retrospective Failure Analysis on the 2021 Chamoli Rock-Ice Avalanche
Hemispheric asymmetry and up/down anisotropy of Jupiter's auroral electron precipitation: Juno/JEDI statistics
papers.abstract: Energetic electron precipitation shapes Jupiter's auroral emissions, thermal structure, and atmospheric chemistry. Whether its intensity differs between hemispheres, and whether that difference is consistent across auroral sub-regions, remains statistically unexplored over a large perijove sample. We statistically characterize the precipitating electron energy flux in Jupiter's auroral sub-regions, polar emission (PE) and main emission (ME), separating downward and upward fluxes and comparing hemispheres, using Juno/JEDI data from PJ3 to PJ66. Juno footprints from JRM33 and a current sheet model assign each spectrum to an auroral sub-region, where the downward and upward energy flux are integrated over the corresponding loss cone. The median energy flux differs between hemispheres by a factor of about two in the PE and the ME, for both flux directions, but the dominant hemisphere is reversed, the north dominating in the PE (N/S of 2.5 downward, 2.0 upward) and the south in the ME (0.65 and 0.5). The mean electron energy is nearly identical in both hemispheres in every sub-region, so the asymmetry lies in the number flux rather than the local acceleration efficiency. The PE also shows a systematic upward excess over downward flux in both hemispheres, maximal at the magnetic pole. The PE/ME reversal shows that the two hemispheres partition precipitated energy differently between the polar cap and the main oval. The PE anisotropy, qualitatively identical in both hemispheres, indicates that this partition is not driven by a hemispheric contrast in field-aligned acceleration efficiency.

Tunneling effect in some singular wells
papers.abstract: The Schrödinger operator in one dimension is considered. When the electric potential has a linear/V-shaped well, an approximation of the ground-state is established at fixed distance from the well. In this situation, the classical WKB analysis and the localization techniques à la Agmon near a non-degenerate minimum do not work. We propose an alternative to the WKB analysis better suited to the shape of the well and we prove that our Ansatz is an exponentially good approximation by means of revisited (and simplified) Agmon estimates.

papers.title: Rigidity and classification of complete translating solitons and self-expanders with constant curvature in $\mathbb{R}^{4}$
papers.abstract: For complete immersed surfaces in Euclidean four-space whose mean curvature vector has constant length, translators are affine planes parallel to their fixed nonzero velocity, and self-expanders are planes through their centre. This rigidity requires no Lagrangian assumption, properness, volume growth control, or bound on the second fundamental form. Complete Lagrangian translators and self-expanders in $\mathbb{C}^{2}$ with constant Gaussian curvature are flat and, up to unitary equivalence, are properly embedded products of two complete planar curves. Translating factors are lines or grim reapers. Expanding factors are lines through the origin or nonstraight self-expanders. The proofs use moving frames, a transnormal function, a cubic tensor identity, and analytic continuation.

papers.title: Muon and Tau Anomalies and $Δα_{had}^{(5)} (M_Z^2)$ in the Standard Model
authors: CNRS-IN2P3 and Univ.Montpellier - FR and iHEPMAD
papers.abstract: I review the present status of the Standard Model (SM) determination of the muon anomaly by emphasizing the estimate of the lowest hadronic vacuum polarization contributions using recent $e^+e^-$ data on $2\pi$ and $3\pi$ and the inclusive ratio $R^{ee}$ of total cross-sections compiled by PDG to which we add the QCD continuum including HO PT QCD up to $\alpha_s^5$, quark mass $m_q^2$ up to $\alpha_s^3$, $m_s^4$ up to $\alpha_s^2$ and QCD condensates. Adding the $e^+e^-\to \pi^0\gamma + \eta\gamma$ contributions to the CMD3 data, one obtains\,: $a_\mu\vert^{hvp}_{lo}=(7094\pm 37)\times 10^{-11}$. Combining this LO result with the HO estimate of the hadronic, QED and EW contributions, one obtains\,: $\Delta a_\mu^{sm} \equiv (a_\mu^{exp}-a_\mu^{sm})= (86\pm 38_{th}\pm 14.5_{exp})\times 10^{-11} $. The average of the recent estimates quoted in Table\,3 [$\oplus$ attempt to fit all $\,e^+e^-$ data] gives\,: $\Delta a_\mu^{sm} = (84.9[90.0]\pm 21.3_{th}\pm 14.5_{exp})\times 10^{-11}$\,. These results agree with the precise BMW20 lattice one and still suggest a window for new physics beyond the SM of $(2.1\sim 3.5)\,\sigma$. Besides some future projects for improving the $e^+e^-$ data, the MUonE for extracting directly $a_\mu^{tot}\vert^{hvp}_{lo}$ and J-PARC (E34) for an independent measurement of $a_\mu$, it is important to improve the Lattice results shown in Fig.\,9 which (at first sight) disagree each others despite the large errors and may question the reliability of the {\it averages of different averages} used in the White Paper (WP25) Our analysis is completed by updating the estimate of the hadronic contribution to the tau anomaly\,: $a_\tau\vert^{hvp}_{lo}=(3516\pm 25)\times 10^{-9}$ and to $\alpha(M_Z)\,: \,\Delta \alpha_{had}^{(5)} (M_Z^2)= (2770.7\pm 4.5)\times 10^{-5}. $

papers.title: Large deviations and the asymptotic geometry of Lorentz balls
papers.abstract: We study the uniform distribution on finite-dimensional Lorentz balls $B_{q,p}^n$ in the range $1<p<q<\infty$. We prove a Sanov-type large deviation principle for the empirical measures of the absolute coordinates of a random vector uniformly distributed on $n^{1/q}B_{q,p}^n$. The rate function is given by an entropy deficit under a weighted quantile constraint. We show that the entropy maximizer is unique and characterize its distribution function as the unique increasing solution of a nonlinear boundary-value problem. The limiting distribution has compact support, for which we obtain an explicit bound. These results establish the conjectured empirical limit of Kabluchko, Prochno and Sonnleitner [Journal of Functional Analysis, 288(1):110682, 2025] in the range $1<p<q<\infty$. As consequences, we determine the exponential volume asymptotics of Lorentz balls and obtain asymptotic independence of any fixed number of coordinates. We also prove a law of large numbers for Lorentz norms with finite parameters and use it, together with the volume asymptotics, to obtain a Schechtman--Schmuckenschläger type theorem for intersections of volume-normalized Lorentz balls. We further derive a variational formula for the logarithmic intersection asymptotics. The proof combines an exponential change of measure with quantile interpolation and a variational argument that does not assume regularity of the maximizing quantile in advance.

papers.title: Deformation Quantization of Coisotropic A-branes
papers.abstract: Motivated by the Gukov--Witten proposal that the endomorphism algebra of a coisotropic A-brane should be described by a deformation quantization of its transverse holomorphic symplectic geometry at the perturbative level, we study deformation quantization on transverse holomorphic symplectic manifolds $(M,\Omega)$. Extending the approach of Nest--Tsygan to this setting, we show that, under an admissibility condition, equivalence classes of deformation quantizations are in bijection with \[ \hbar H^2\bigl(\operatorname{F}_1\Omega^\bullet(M,\mathbb C),d\bigr) [[\hbar]], \] where $\operatorname{F}_1\Omega^\bullet(M,\mathbb C)$ is the differential ideal generated by transverse $(1,0)$-forms. We further illustrate this framework through examples arising from mapping tori, $T$-duality, and coisotropic lifts in cotangent bundles. These examples clarify the roles of admissibility and the transverse Atiyah class, as well as the distinction between deformation quantizations and global star products. Finally, for a coisotropic A-brane $M$ induced from a transverse complex manifold $Q$, we use transverse jets and the Fock representation to construct a perturbative level action $End(M)\curvearrowright Hom(M,Q)$ under suitable compatibility assumptions, providing a geometric realization of the brane quantization philosophy.

Genuine multipartite entanglement in ring-shaped Hubbard models
papers.abstract: Spin states can be extracted from many-electron systems by detecting electrons at a set of lattice sites, which act as particle labels. Here we quantify the genuine multipartite entanglement (GME) of such spin states, which are generally mixed, in standard and extended Hubbard rings, together with the corresponding detection probability. We show that the on-site repulsion, by suppressing charge fluctuations, enhances the GME, and that in the strongly interacting regime at half filling the detection probability decreases only weakly with the number of spins. The GME is robust at temperatures below the singlet--triplet gap, and can even be enhanced by doping, in spite of the induced charge fluctuations. The transition from spin- to charge-density waves in the extended Hubbard model is signaled by an abrupt suppression of both the GME and the detection probability.

papers.title: GPRM: Global Perspective Process Reward Model
Directionality of low-energy electron recoils in the CYGNO experiment
papers.abstract: Electron-recoil directionality can help distinguish solar-neutrino interactions from backgrounds and, together with recoil-energy measurements and three-dimensional tracking, enable neutrino-energy spectroscopy. We study the reconstruction of the initial direction of low-energy electron recoils in the CYGNO optical time-projection chamber, focusing on the 50 L LIME prototype and its high-granularity scientific CMOS (sCMOS) readout. A dedicated algorithm identifies the interaction point from the asymmetry of the track light distribution and estimates the recoil direction from the early portion of the ionization trail, before multiple scattering erases most of the directional information. The method is characterized with a detailed Monte Carlo simulation of electron recoils and detector response. Samples spanning 15 keV to 70 keV are used to optimize the algorithm parameters by minimizing the width of the reconstructed-minus-true projected-angle distribution. The projected angular response is modeled by two Gaussian components that account for its dependence on track inclination. The narrower component, associated with favorable projections approximately parallel to the Gas Electron Multiplier (GEM) plane, has a width that improves from about $20^\circ$ near 20 keV to about $12^\circ$ at 60 keV. We also quantify the fraction of events in the correctly reconstructed angular core and discuss the dominant limitations of a camera-only two-dimensional measurement.

papers.title: UIAnchor: Anchoring UI Perception and Action Execution for Reliable Service-Composed Mobile Task Automation with GUI Agents
Who Benefits from Telemonitoring? Uplift Modelling of a Nationwide Home Blood Pressure Monitoring Programme
Cavity Control of Emission Dynamics from Spin Defects in Hexagonal Boron Nitride
papers.abstract: Optically addressable negatively charged boron vacancy ($\mathrm{V_B^-}$) defects in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) are promising for quantum sensing at room temperature. The two-dimensional structure of hBN allows direct access to the local environment, enabling proximal sensing of target materials. However, its broadband emission and low quantum yield hinder efficient light-matter interaction, and the coupling of $\mathrm{V_B^-}$ optical dipoles to confined cavity fields remains poorly understood. In this study, we integrate $\mathrm{V_B^-}$ defects with a tunable plano-concave microcavity, achieving three-dimensional optical confinement. This approach yields photoluminescence (PL) enhancement and cavity-modified optical decay dynamics, providing insights into the orientation of the $\mathrm{V_B^-}$ defect dipole. Time-resolved PL measurements identify a distinct fast decay component, suggesting a complex dipole geometry for the defects. Therefore, a tilted optical dipole model is considered to attribute the fast and slow decay components to in-plane and out-of-plane dipole contributions, respectively. Additionally, optically detected magnetic resonance and excitation-polarisation-dependent PL measurements provide further insights into local symmetry breaking and potential optical dipole configurations. These results highlight the role of optical dipole orientation in $\mathrm{V_B^-}$ defect-cavity coupling.

papers.title: Scintillator-Based Event-Mode Neutron Imaging with Timepix4 Readout
papers.abstract: Scintillator-based event-mode neutron imaging is emerging as a powerful approach to neutron radiography. Unlike conventional integrating-mode neutron imaging, which accumulates scintillation light during an exposure, event reconstruction estimates neutron-event positions and arrival times from time-stamped optical responses. We investigated this approach using a self-developed Timepix4-based optical readout system, image-formation analysis, and beam experiments at the China Spallation Neutron Source under different scintillator and optical configurations. The analysis explains how event localization can reduce image blur associated with the spatial extent of individual scintillation responses. Under the same 0.35$\times$ optical configuration, event reconstruction improved the spatial resolution from 164.2 to 91.9 $\mu$m at 10% modulation transfer function (MTF), while a 2.1$\times$ configuration with a $\mathrm{Gd_2O_2S:Tb}$ scintillator achieved 26.1 $\mu$m at the same MTF threshold. Following event reconstruction and rejection of single-photon reconstructed events, the mean peak-normalized spectral response in the 6-8 angstrom out-of-band interval decreased by 85.4% relative to the raw-pixel wavelength-count spectrum, indicating reduced afterglow-related spectral background. Under the tested pulsed-beam conditions, the maximum instantaneous pixel-hit rate per pixel was approximately four times its time-averaged value, providing an experimental basis for assessing readout requirements at higher neutron flux. Conventional radiography resolved structural details, while energy-selective imaging enhanced the contrast between materials with similar broadband transmission and Bragg-edge imaging revealed crystallographic features in steel. These results demonstrate the imaging-quality benefits and capabilities of scintillator-based event-mode neutron imaging.

papers.title: Kinetic and Thermodynamic Limits of Sodium Pore Filling in Hard Carbon
authors: Oleksandr I. Malyi (1) ((1) Qingyuan Innovation Laboratory
(2) Centre of Excellence ENSEMBLE3 Sp. z o. o.
papers.abstract: The low-voltage plateau-like capacity of hard carbon anodes is widely regarded as a key signature of sodium storage in closed pores, often defining the performance of Na-ion batteries. Here, we combine first-principles calculations with a grand canonical Monte Carlo pore-filling model to show that Na storage in closed pores is not governed by a single equilibrium-plateau mechanism but by a distribution of pore-specific thermodynamic and kinetic activation processes. Thermodynamically, the voltage at which Na pore filling becomes favorable decreases with increasing pore size. Kinetically, pore filling involves Na nucleation, coalescence, growth, and bulk diffusion. While small pores fill rapidly, large pores exhibit both a smaller thermodynamic stimulus and significant kinetic limitations. Nucleation can be accelerated by introducing defects at the pore walls, although an excessively high defect concentration slows bulk diffusion. This work shows that not all closed pores contribute equally to Na storage: some may be thermodynamically favorable but kinetically inactive under realistic charge/discharge rates. Because of this, the inverse design of hard carbon electrodes should target a kinetically accessible pore-size and defect-density window that balances high plateau-like capacity with fast-charging performance.

papers.title: NL2RCtrl: Risk-Controlled Controller Synthesis from Natural Language Requirements
Dimension-seven spectator effects in charm-hadron lifetimes at NLO
papers.abstract: We compute the next-to-leading-order (NLO) QCD corrections to the connected current-current part of the dimension-seven spectator coefficients in the heavy-quark expansion of charm-hadron widths. The finite terms are fixed in NDR-$\overline{\rm MS}$, with the evanescent operators defined by the standard Greek projection and averaged over Hermitian-conjugate pairs, and with a finite subtraction that sets the finite mixing of the dimension-seven operators into the dimension-six ones to zero. In several channels the one-loop term is comparable to the LO coefficient, and two operator families absent at LO are generated. Since the NLO matrix elements of the dimension-seven operators are not known, we estimate the effect of the coefficients on the widths with tree-level matrix elements from vacuum insertion for $D$ mesons and from the bag model for charmed baryons. The $1/m_c$ corrections to the matrix elements of the dimension-six QCD operators are treated by a naive expansion. Without their $O(\alpha_s)$ part the semileptonic width of the $D_s^+$ would be negative. The NLO dimension-seven correction raises the $D^+$ width by 0.78 ps$^{-1}$, so that its central value, slightly negative as published, becomes positive. At central inputs, it is about 1% of the $D^0$ width, 10% of the $D_s^+$ width and at most 2% of the widths of the singly charmed baryons. Added to the published pole-scheme width, the $D^+$ correction gives $\tau(D^+)=1.41^{+\infty}_{-0.76}$ ps. The NLO term reduces the scale dependence of the nonleptonic dimension-seven contribution severalfold for the singly charmed baryons, whose matrix elements are evolved, but not uniformly for the $D$ mesons.

papers.title: European derivatives pricing via constrained Gaussian process regressions
papers.abstract: This article develops a Gaussian process method for pricing European derivatives when the underlyings, and the risk factors driving them, follow a multivariate jump-diffusion. A Gaussian process prior on the pricing function is conditioned on the Feynman-Kac partial integro-differential equation at a set of collocation points. The price is returned as a closed-form and differentiable function, allowing the Greeks to be obtained without simulation or finite differences. The jump terms are handled iteratively: the price is computed as the limit of a sequence of boundary value problems. Our main theoretical contribution is a convergence result for this iteration: using Weissinger's fixed-point theorem in the supremum norm, we show that it converges from any starting point, and provide a worst-case number of iterations for a given precision. The method is illustrated with derivatives of two underlyings under the Heston model with Kou double-exponential jumps, a five-dimensional problem, and benchmarked against Monte Carlo simulation.

papers.title: A Seismic Foundation Model for Dense Feature Extraction
Linear Dynamics of Composition Operators on Zygmund Spaces of Rooted Trees
papers.abstract: We conjugate composition operators on the Zygmund and little Zygmund spaces of an infinite, locally finite rooted tree $T$ by the second-difference isometries. A path Green kernel gives row-finite matrices that characterize boundedness and yield exact operator norms. A rigidity result holds on the chain $\mathbb{N}_0$. Boundedness on $\mathcal{Z}_0(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is equivalent to $\varphi(n)=qn+b$ for all sufficiently large $n$, with $q\in\mathbb{N}_0$ and $b\in\mathbb{Z}$. For these symbols, $\varphi(n)>n$ eventually characterizes Li-Yorke chaos of $C_\varphi$ on either Zygmund space, allowing noninjectivity and periodic vertices. If $C_\varphi$ is bounded on $\mathcal{Z}_0(T)$ and $\varphi^k(T)$ eventually avoids every finite set, then for each $\lambda\ne0$, $\lambda C_\varphi$ is Li-Yorke chaotic on either space exactly when the norms of its powers are unbounded. For $\varphi_q(n)=q(n+1)-1$ with integer $q\ge2$, the corresponding conditions are $|\lambda|q^2>1$ on both Zygmund spaces and $|\lambda|q>1$ on the little Lipschitz space. For bounded $C_\varphi$ on $\mathcal{Z}_0(\mathbb{N}_0)$, topological mixing and Devaney chaos each hold exactly for injective symbols with no periodic vertices and eventual slope $q\ge2$. For such bounded operators with strictly increasing $\varphi$ and $\varphi(0)>0$, $q\ge2$ also characterizes hypercyclicity and frequent hypercyclicity.

papers.title: An adaptive Gaussian splitting scheme for linear Fokker--Planck equations
Reduced Density Matrices from Renormalization-Group Flows
papers.abstract: We reconstruct complete one- and two-body reduced density matrices (RDMs) by a single collective backward evolution along the in-medium similarity renormalization-group flow. Benchmarks show improved accuracy and physical consistency over conventional elementwise evolution. In neutron matter, two-body RDMs reveal spin-triplet dominance in interaction-dependent Fermi-sea depletion trends. Meanwhile, the forward-backward energy difference provides an internal diagnostic of many-body truncation errors, whose quantification remains challenging in nuclear $ab\ initio$ calculations.

papers.title: Robotic Reward Models in the Foundation-Model Era
High-quality intrinsic circular dichroism in silicon-based bound states in the continuum metasurfaces via strong coupling
papers.abstract: Bound states in the continuum (BICs) can significantly enhance spin-selective light-matter interactions. However, current BIC metasurfaces generally rely on single or multiple chiral BIC modes to enhance circular dichroism (CD), limiting their application in functional integrated devices. This paper proposes a method that utilizes the strong coupling effect in BIC metasurfaces to achieve intrinsic CD with both a high quality factor (Q-factor) and high efficiency. The metasurface is designed as a silicon-based cross-shaped nanohole array, which can simultaneously support a TM-like BIC mode and a TE-like guided-mode resonance (GMR) mode. By introducing under-etching to break the out-of-plane symmetry and tuning the in-plane asymmetry parameter, strong coupling between the quasi-BIC (QBIC) mode and the GMR mode can be induced, thereby achieving near-perfect intrinsic CD with a high Q-factor. In the strong-coupling region, the resonant wavelengths of the QBIC and GMR modes exhibit anti-crossing behavior, while the imaginary parts of the eigenfrequency cross; the corresponding Rabi splitting energy reaches a minimum of 3.16 meV, and the induced intrinsic CD achieves a maximum of 0.995 at a wavelength of 1653.9 nm, with a high Q-factor of 1083. The evolution of far-field polarization singularities shows that, under strong coupling, the {\Gamma} point corresponds to a left-handed circular polarization singularity (C-point). Furthermore, the strong-coupling-induced CD exhibits good robustness. Even under considerable variations in structural parameters, the high-Q and high-efficiency CD response is maintained. This method offers a novel design strategy for integrated chiral photonic devices and holds promise for applications in areas such as chiral sensing, chiral lasers, and nonlinear chiral optics.

papers.title: On Sobolev spaces and Koksma-Hlawka-type inequalities of fractional order
Simultaneous tests of post-Newtonian inspiral using GW250114 and GW250207
papers.abstract: We perform the one of the most general tests of post-Newtonian (PN) inspiral in binary black holes to date by allowing all eight phase coefficients up to 3.5PN order to vary simultaneously from their general-relativistic values. Using two of the loudest binary black hole events observed to date, GW250114 and GW250207, we carry out Bayesian inference with the IMRPhenomXPHM_SpinTaylor waveform model augmented by parametrized deviations in the post-Newtonian phasing. We then identify the combinations of phase coefficients most strongly constrained by the data through a principal component analysis of the eight-dimensional deformation space. We find that the data constrain the three leading principal components beyond their priors, and that all three are consistent with the predictions of general relativity. These results demonstrate that exceptionally loud gravitational-wave events enable robust, high-dimensional tests of inspiral dynamics and provide direct access to the measurable subspace of post-Newtonian deformations.

papers.title: CLIFT: Contrastive LiDAR Instance Features for 3D Pedestrian Tracking
GainCtrl: Predicting Remaining Gains for Efficient LLM Agent Execution
Material Tailored Multispectral Magnetization via the Inverse Faraday Effect in Tunable Coaxial Nanoantenna
papers.abstract: All-optical control of magnetization via the Inverse Faraday Effect presents a transformative pathway for ultrafast high-density data storage and nanoscale spintronics. However, unlocking its full potential requires moving beyond traditional gold-centric, narrowband constraints. In this study, we present a comprehensive theoretical framework evaluating IFE-driven static magnetic field generation across a diverse library of plasmonic materials, including gold, silver, copper, aluminum, and titanium nitride. Using a dimensionally tunable coaxial nanoantenna, we map the optomagnetic response across the deep-ultraviolet to near-infrared spectrum. Our findings reveal highly distinct, material-dependent behaviors: aluminum uniquely sustains robust magnetization in the deep-UV, whereas silver, copper, and gold exhibit superior efficiency at longer wavelengths. Crucially, we demonstrate that shifting the excitation to the near-infrared regime amplifies the generated magnetic field by several orders of magnitude, establishing these frequencies as critical for helicity-dependent all-optical switching. Furthermore, by resolving the local optical spin density, we elucidate how extreme subwavelength confinement drives synchronized drift currents, enabling efficient multispectral magnetization through localized surface plasmon resonances and higher-order Fabry-Perot modes. Strikingly, comparing these distinct modes reveals that structural geometry tunes the resonant wavelength, while the maximum achievable optomagnetic amplitude is fundamentally governed by the metal's intrinsic properties.

papers.title: Can LLMs Give Good Product Advice? A Framework for Diagnosing Failures
MemEmo: Evaluating Emotion in Memory Systems
Routing Beyond Task Categories: A Cost-Aware LAB-Bench Study
A note on Padmanabhan's path-integral duality
papers.abstract: We develop a field-theoretic implementation of Padmanabhan's principle of invariance under the duality $\mathcal S \rightarrow {L_0^2}/{\mathcal S}$, where ${\mathcal S}$ is the proper length (the action integral along a particle's trajectory) and $L_0$ is a quantum of length. Starting from the particle propagator and its Schwinger proper-time representation, we derive the wave operator associated with the duality transformation in terms of a scalar field, rather than a point particle. The resulting theory is governed by a nonlocal operator involving modified Bessel functions. We analyse the infrared and ultraviolet regimes, demonstrate the recovery of standard Klein-Gordon theory at low energies, and show the appearance of exponential ultraviolet suppression. Our analysis provides a natural extension, to quantum field theory, of Padmanabhan's duality for point particles.

papers.title: Selective Sensor Acquisition for Multimodal Place Recognition
Beyond Finite Dimensions: Duflo-Serganova Cohomology, the Formal Superdimension, and a Kac-Wakimoto Theorem for Unitarizable Supermodules
papers.abstract: The main results of this manuscript are fourfold. First, we introduce relative holomorphic discrete series supermodules over basic classical Lie superalgebras $\mathfrak{g}$ and $\mathfrak{sl}(n\vert n)$. These are unitarizable highest weight supermodules whose $\mathfrak{g}_{\bar{0}}$-constituents are Harish-Chandra modules of relative holomorphic discrete series representations. We show that these are exactly the unitarizable highest weight supermodules whose globalizations have supermatrix coefficients square-integrable modulo the center. Second, we define the formal superdimension of a relative holomorphic discrete series supermodule as the parity-weighted sum of the formal dimensions of its $\mathfrak{g}_{\bar{0}}$-constituents. We show that it equals, up to sign, the value at zero of an $L$-packet supercharacter obtained by averaging over the Weyl group. Third, we prove a Kac-Wakimoto theorem for formal superdimension: it is nonzero if and only if the highest weight is maximally atypical. For integral highest weights, it equals the superdimension of a finite-dimensional simple supermodule with the same degree of atypicality. We realize these supermodules through derived Zuckerman functors. For nonintegral highest weights, it is computed by generalized Duflo-Serganova cohomology. Finally, to establish the Kac-Wakimoto conjecture, we develop the theory of generalized Duflo-Serganova cohomology for unitarizable supermodules. We prove that the cohomology of a unitarizable simple supermodule is unitarizable and either zero or simple.

papers.title: ANCHOR: Cluster-Grounded 5W1H Extraction via Large-Small Model Collaboration
Multi-bubble solutions for an exponential biharmonic Neumann problem in dimension four
papers.abstract:
We are concerned with the biharmonic Neumann problem \[ \Delta^2u+u=0\quad	ext{in }\Omega,\qquad \partial_
u u=0,\quad \partial_
u\Delta u=-\varepsilon h e^{24\pi^2u} \quad	ext{on }\partial\Omega, \] where $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^4$ is a smooth bounded domain, $
u$ is the outward unit normal, $h\in C^5(\partial\Omega)$ is positive, and $\varepsilon>0$ is sufficiently small. For each fixed integer $m\ge1$, we construct $m$-bubble solutions $u_\varepsilon$ by Lyapunov--Schmidt reduction. As $\varepsilon	o0$, the solutions concentrate at $m$ distinct boundary points, each carrying unit mass for the measure $\varepsilon h e^{24\pi^2u_\varepsilon}\,d\sigma$. For solutions corresponding to nondegenerate critical points $\xi^*$ of the interaction function $\mathcal F_m$, we establish local uniqueness and nondegeneracy, and prove $\ind(u_\varepsilon)=m+\ind(-D^2\mathcal F_m(\xi^*))$. In particular, for a generic positive weight $h$, all critical points of $\mathcal F_m$ are nondegenerate, and the $m$-bubble solutions associated with global minima of $\mathcal F_m$ have Morse index $4m$.
