papers.title: Frac-BKT Under Mechanism Scrutiny: Response Assimilation and a Failed Fractional-Memory Test
On Covariance Steering with Nonlinear Measurements
papers.abstract: This paper examines two ways nonlinear measurements complicate the statistical predictions during covariance steering. The covariance steering problem optimizes a control policy across a distribution of possible trajectories rather than a single specific trajectory. This approach has attracted growing interest as a way to account for uncertainty in aerospace applications such as trajectory optimization, stationkeeping, and landing. In many of these applications, covariance steering can account for measurement uncertainty through output feedback. Because standard formulations assume linear dynamics and measurements, applications with nonlinear measurements typically use an extended Kalman filter to estimate the state. This paper shows that techniques used to improve filter convergence, such as measurement underweighting, can reduce the accuracy of conventional covariance steering predictions by violating a key assumption. This is addressed with a new convex formulation that relaxes the assumption. This paper also demonstrates that adjusting the control policy during execution can improve agreement between predicted and actual state statistics. A numerical example of angles-only spacecraft rendezvous illustrates the benefits of the proposed method, and discussions are made regarding the implications of this generalized covariance steering formulation.

papers.title: Spectral Landmarks: Alignment of Landmark Kernel Translates with the Leading Eigenfunctions of a Kernel Operator
When Should Decision Models Compare Candidates?
Residual-Tail-Informed Flow Matching for Time Series Anomaly Detection
Beyond Service Discovery: Coverage Awareness in LLM-Driven Service Composition
The monogenicity of $\boldsymbol{x^n+c\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}a^{n-j-1}x^j}$
papers.abstract: We say that a monic polynomial $f(x)\in {\mathbb Z}[x]$ is {\em monogenic} if $f(x)$ is irreducible over ${\mathbb Q}$ and $\{1,\theta,\theta^2,\ldots,\theta^{{\rm deg}(f)-1}\}$ is a basis for the ring of integers of ${\mathbb Q}(\theta)$, where $f(\theta)=0$. Let $n,a,c\in {\mathbb Z}$ with $n\ge 3$, and suppose that \[{\mathcal F}_{n,a,c}(x):=x^n+cx^{n-1}+acx^{n-2}+a^2cx^{n-3}+\cdots +a^{n-2}cx+a^{n-1}c\] is irreducible over ${\mathbb Q}$. Recently, Jakhar, Kalwaniya and Yadav have given necessary and sufficient conditions for the monogenicity of ${\mathcal F}_{n,a,c}(x)$, under the assumption that all prime divisors of the discriminant of ${\mathcal F}_{n,a,c}(x)$ not dividing $ac$ also do not divide $n+1$. In this note, we provide necessary and sufficient conditions for the monogenicity of ${\mathcal F}_{n,a,c}(x)$ without this restriction.

papers.title: LENS: Replacing LayerNorm and Softmax in Transformers with Learnable Normalization States
Sidewalk Stewards: A Visual Analytics Approach for Interactive Topology Repair of Sidewalk Networks
Ternary-Valued FDTD Method for Nonlinear Optics: Third-Harmonic Generation on a Multiplier-Free Solver
Phase Structure and Thermodynamic Geometry of STU Black Holes
papers.abstract: We study the thermodynamics of four-dimensional STU black holes, a family of charged solutions of gauged N = 8, SO(8) supergravity, from the perspective of geometric thermodynamics. We focus on non-rotating solutions carrying pairwise-equal charges, obtaining closed-form expressions for the thermodynamic quantities directly in terms of the physical charges, and use them to determine the equation of state and associated phase structure. We also construct the Ruppeiner geometry for the STU black hole, taking the temperature and thermodynamic volume as fluctuation variables, and study its renormalized curvature as a probe of the black hole microstructure. We find a rich phase structure with two critical points present whenever the charge ratio is sufficiently large, and identify regions in parameter space associated with attractive and repulsive microscopic interactions.

papers.title: Exceptional structure and Lifshitz criticality in a non-Hermitian Kitaev chain
papers.abstract: We study an exactly solvable non-Hermitian $N$-site Kitaev chain with unequal pair-creation and pair-annihilation amplitudes and vanishing intersite hopping. We show that the chain supports an exceptional point (EP) at which all the many-body energies collapse to zero and the largest Jordan block grows quadratically with $N$. By constructing an explicit positive metric for the associated $N$-dimensional one-body problem which admits an extension to the full many-body Hamiltonian, we demonstrate that this EP collapse can be approached through a continuous quasi-Hermitian path in the parameter space. Further, in a different regime with onsite energies alternating between two unequal positive values, we show that pairing amplitudes of opposite signs can lead to crossings between ground states of opposite fermion parity within a quasi-Hermitian regime. Their accumulation in the thermodynamic limit produces a Lifshitz transition, characterized by particle-/hole-pocket formation, quadratic critical dispersion, and a nonanalytic ground-state energy density. We show that this transition remains separated from the EP boundary and ceases to exist for balanced real pairing.

papers.title: Simulating access to alcohol screening, brief intervention, referral to and receipt of specialty treatment for alcohol use disorder in California and Texas: A study protocol for an agent-based modeling study (AUDTxSim)
Measuring Coherence in Predictive Models
High-Speed Forward and Reverse Tractor-Trailer Driving with Learned Vehicle Dynamics
Strain-Engineering Giant Pseudo-Electric Fields in Multilayer Graphene
papers.abstract: Electromagnetic scalar and vector potentials can be engineered in solids through lattice distortions, providing a versatile means of tuning electronic band structures. The pseudovector component, which generates pseudo-magnetic fields, has received much attention for its ability to realize a zero-field quantum Hall effect. However, the pseudoscalar component, giving rise to pseudo-electric fields to which many electronic systems are intrinsically susceptible, has not yet been experimentally explored. Here, we demonstrate the emergence and profound consequences of the pseudoscalar potential in a multilayer graphene system. Atomic relaxation reconstructs the system into large Bernalstacked domains separated by one-dimensional rhombohedral channels. Within this inter-dimensional system, we achieve the first direct atomic-scale imaging of distinct lattice deformations in graphene under strain. In rhombohedral channels, we observe that the tensile lattice deformation induces giant pseudo-electric fields, producing ultra-flat dispersion with divergent density of states and a large energy gap. This results in enhanced electronic correlations, leading to flat-band instabilities and striped modulation in the density of states that would otherwise require strong external displacement fields. Moreover, the gap opened by the pseudoscalar potential protects topological boundary states that persist in the absence of applied fields. Our results provide a comprehensive atomic-scale characterization of graphene elasticity and direct spectroscopic evidence for the nontrivial pseudo-electric field arising from lattice distortion. More broadly, it provides an intrinsic and tunable pathway to new quantum states

papers.title: Maximum Scores and Treatment Feedback in Regression Discontinuity Designs
papers.abstract: Hospitals use repeated risk scores to decide when to send an alert. Some evaluations summarize these scores by their maximum and use the maximum as the running variable in a regression discontinuity (RD) design. The maximum shows correctly whether a patient was ever alerted. However, it can include scores recorded after an earlier alert has already changed care. In this paper, we study what the maximum-score RD estimates when an earlier intervention changes a later score. We use a two-assessment model and derive a formula that splits the RD contrast into the causal effect and a composition term. When feedback moves scores in one direction, the composition term equals the relative jump in the density of the maximum at the cutoff times a prognostic contrast. Therefore, an exactly continuous density means no bias, and the population density jump bounds the bias. Valid inference on the jump turns this into a confidence bound under a stated sensitivity assumption. Within this model, bias behind a continuous density requires feedback in both directions. For this case, we bound bias by total boundary movement and construct conservative confidence sets for binary outcomes under explicit sensitivity and smoothness assumptions. We give closed forms for independent uniform scores and for correlated Gaussian scores. In one example, a true risk reduction of four percentage points appears as a one-point increase. Simulations confirm the formulas. Narrower bandwidths, robust bias correction, and machine-learning covariate adjustment do not remove the bias. A fuzzy RD on the first score recovers the causal effect when early and late treatment have the same effect. Our results concern how the running variable is built. We do not assess any published clinical study.

papers.title: Unreasonable Confidence from Simulator Misspecification: Directional Robustness on the SPEED+ Sim-to-Real Benchmark
Course-Referenced Lateral Control of Trail-Following Convoys: String Stability and Adaptive Feedforward under Load Uncertainty
How did data sharing evolve in the decade since the FAIR Principles?
Near-Optimal Methods for Generalized Lipschitz Convex Optimization
Electronic bridge for the $J=0$ state and effects of electrons on frequency and lifetime of the nuclear clock transition in $^{229}$Th$^{2+}$ ion
papers.abstract: We investigate the electronic bridge (EB) process for excitation of the $^{229}$Th nuclear isomer in Th III ions initially prepared in the metastable electronic state with $J=0$. This state is of particular interest for developing a nuclear clock with suppressed electronic hyperfine interactions. Using a combination of configuration interaction and coupled-cluster methods, we calculate EB transition rates for several excitation schemes involving one or two laser fields. We express the rates in terms of the enhancement factor $R$, defined as the ratio of the EB transition rate to the direct nuclear M1 transition rate. Schemes that return the ion to its initial $J=0$ state have relatively small enhancement factors, $R \sim 1$. However, allowing the final electronic state to differ from the initial state produces a strong resonant enhancement: $R$ reaches $5\times10^3$. In addition, we calculate the shift in the nuclear transition frequency caused by changing the electronic state from the ground state to two excited metastable states. We also examine how the electronic state affects the nuclear transition lifetime and calculate the probabilities of electron transitions induced by nuclear decay. The EB mechanism shortens the nuclear decay lifetime by a factor of 2.6 when the electrons are initially in the ground state and by a factor of 6.85 when they are in the metastable $J=0$ state.

papers.title: Solving the Discretised Shallow Water Equations on Distorted Structured Grids with Neural Physics
Vibe Interventions: Can Users Personalize and Iterate Their Way to Behavior Change?
NF-VLA: A Normalizing-Flow Baseline for Vision-Language-Action Learning
Generalized Rotating-Wave Approximations Hierarchy for the Interacting Two-Qubit Rabi Model
papers.abstract: We investigate the two-qubit quantum Rabi model for identical qubits symmetrically coupled to a single bosonic mode and interacting with each other through transverse and longitudinal couplings. We extend the adiabatic, generalized rotating-wave (GRWA), and squeezed generalized rotating-wave (SGRWA) approximations to include the qubit-qubit interactions, including self-consistent and variational choices of the bosonic parameters. The resulting analytical hierarchy allows us to distinguish the interplay between both kinds of qubit-qubit interactions and the effects of displacement, neighboring-manifold mixing, and squeezing on the low-energy properties. We find that the transverse interaction mainly changes the collective-spin structure of the states, while the longitudinal interaction also modifies the displacement-dependent oscillator overlaps and introduces an additional two-boson coupling. We compare the analytical results with numerically exact diagonalization for the low-energy spectrum, ground-state energy, mean photon number, two-qubit concurrence, and spin correlations. The results provide a compact analytical description of how direct qubit-qubit interactions modify both the spectrum and the eigenstate structure beyond the rotating-wave approximation for few-qubit light-matter systems.

papers.title: Soft-constrained Schrödinger bridge for generative AI: numerical algorithms and approximation guarantees
papers.abstract: We study a soft-constrained formulation of the Schrödinger bridge problem, in which the terminal distribution constraint is relaxed into a penalty on the discrepancy between the terminal law of the controlled process and a target distribution. This leads to an unconstrained McKean--Vlasov stochastic control problem, where the interaction enters only through the terminal cost. We characterize the optimizer via a McKean--Vlasov forward-backward stochastic differential equation and establish well-posedness under very mild assumptions. We also analyze two approximation regimes relevant to data-driven computation: approximation of the target law by empirical samples, and finite-particle approximation of the McKean--Vlasov control problem. For both, we derive convergence results and error estimates. Finally, building on the well-posedness and approximation results, we investigate two neural numerical methods: one based on the forward-backward system and the other on direct control optimization. Both methods are tested on state-of-the-art generative tasks. Our results provide both an algorithmic foundation and its theoretical guarentee for soft-constrained Schrödinger bridge problems in sample-based generative modeling.

papers.title: Reveal: A Provenance-Aware System for Multimodal Urban Data Exploration
Strengthening Compact Vehicle Routing Formulations through Arc-Flow Aggregation and Refinement
Graph spectra and late-time concurrence in a lossy reservoir network
papers.abstract: We investigate how coupling the local environments of noninteracting qubits into a network changes their late-time entanglement dynamics. Each qubit interacts with a lossy bosonic memory mode, with coherent hopping between memory modes determined by an underlying graph. The initial state contains at most two excitations. We show that the graph spectrum selects the collective modes that survive longest, thereby controlling both the decay and spatial distribution of pair concurrence. At resonance, nonbipartite graphs generically approach a fixed pattern of relative concurrence determined by the Perron eigenvector, whereas bipartite graphs support interference between two equally damped modes. This interference can produce arbitrarily late entanglement revivals when it overcomes the exponential decay of the surviving modes. We derive explicit thresholds separating revival and eventual monotonic decay, and show that loss from two-excitation states can drive the system across these thresholds without changing the graph or the initial one-excitation state. Underlying these results is a general bound on the sector decay rates, $\gamma_2\ge2\gamma_1$, valid at arbitrary uniform detuning. We also identify an exceptional equal-rate regime in which coherence between the vacuum and two-excitation sectors contributes to the leading concurrence. Together, these results establish how the topology of a structured dissipative environment and the redistribution of excitations through loss determine the long-time behavior of entanglement.

papers.title: Stability conditions on Lazarsfeld-Mukai bundles over abelian surfaces
papers.abstract: We study the stability of Lazarsfeld-Mukai bundles associated with smooth curves over abelian surfaces. When the general curve in $|L|$ have Clifford dimension one and maximal gonality, for $\rho \gg 0$ we show that every component of the relative Brill-Noether loci \(W^1_d(|L|)\) dominating the linear system parametrizes generically \(\mu_L\)-stable rank-two Lazarsfeld-Mukai bundles. We also apply Bayer-Li wall-crossing to higher-rank bundles: if \(\operatorname{NS}(S)=\mathbb Z\cdot L\), \(A\) is a globally generated complete linear series of degree \(d\) on a smooth curve \(C\in|L|\), \(h^0(C,A)=r+1\) with \(r>2\), and \(d\ne g-1\), then the associated bundle \(E_{C,A}\) is \(\mu_L\)-stable and \(L\)-Gieseker-stable. The corresponding object \(E_{C,A}^{\vee}[1]\) for \(d<g-1\), or \(E_{C,A}\) for \(d>g-1\), is stable in the adjacent chamber, as its reduction. These results connect dimension estimates for Brill-Noether loci with stability and wall-crossing on abelian surfaces.

papers.title: PoCoAttn: Position-Content Collaborative Sparse Attention for Fast and High-Fidelity Video Generation
Ontology-Compiled Control Barrier Functions for Heterogeneous Robot Teams
Hochschild Cocycle and Universality of Merge
A notion of pseudo-morphisms with applications to the study of polynomial maps and of link-homotopy groups of 2-string link
papers.abstract: We introduce a notion of pseudo-morphism for groups, which extends the notion of group morphism from a group to a ring. We show that pseudo-morphisms from a group $G$ to an integral domain $R$ form a filtred Hopf algebra which can be seen as an efficient notion of dual for $G$. We also show that pseudo-morphisms are closely related to the notion of polynomial maps in the sense of Eilenberg-MacLane/Passi, the two notions even coinciding when $G$ is finitely generated and $R$ is a field. It follows that, in that case, polynomial maps are endowed with an Hopf structure. In a second part, we study non repeated Milnor invariants (in the $4$-dimensional context of $2$-string links) from this pseudo-morphism point of view. We show that they form a sub-bialgebra of the Hopf algebra of pseudo-morphisms on the group of $2$-string links up to link-homotopy, and prove that it is isomorphic to an explicit quotient $\textrm{Mil}$ of a polynomial ring. This leads to a fully algebraic description of the group of 2-string links up to link-homotopy as the dual group associated to $\textrm{Mil}$. As a by-product, we obtain that non repeated Milnor invariants are polynomial maps, and we show that this can be used to give a new proof of their finite type property.

papers.title: On dynamical and parameter spaces for the Maximally Generalized McMullen family of rational maps
papers.abstract: We explore the maximally generalized McMullen family of rational maps $F_{n,d,c,a}(z) = z^n + a/z^d + c$, for $n,d\in \mathbb{Z},$ with $n,d\geq 3$, $a\in \mathbb{C}^*$ and $c\in \mathbb{C}$. In the dynamical plane, we establish annular regions containing the Julia sets, and show that the geometric limits of both the Julia and filled Julia sets as $n,d\to \infty$ are contained in the unit circle. In parameter space, for any fixed $a\in \mathbb{C}^*$, we examine the boundedness locus in the $c$-plane. When $n=d$ we find that as $n\to \infty$, the boundedness locus tends to the union of two unit circles centered at $\pm 2\sqrt{a}$. For arbitrary $n,d$, we identify a spine consisting of unit circles determined by the critical values, and prove that the boundedness locus tends to the spine as $n,d\to \infty$.

papers.title: Population structure of the velocity distribution in normal shock waves: Gaussian representations, Mach-number similarity, and prediction
papers.abstract: Normal shock waves are commonly described as mixtures of upstream and downstream Maxwellians. Discrete-velocity solutions of three relaxation models up to Mach 12 and direct simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) of hard-sphere and variable-hard-sphere gases up to Mach 25 are used to examine the population structure, Mach-number similarity and upstream precursor of their velocity distributions. Three anisotropic Gaussian populations reproduce the streamwise reduced distributions of the Bhatnagar--Gross--Krook (BGK) model and of DSMC to within 4\% up to Mach 12, and of DSMC to within 6\% at Mach 25, whereas two Maxwellians incur errors up to 50\% (BGK) and 37\% (DSMC). Collision histories identify the hard-sphere beam with unscattered stream molecules, which carry half of the peak viscous stress; the other populations are effective descriptions, not collision classes. Above Mach 5, Rankine--Hugoniot-scaled distributions are nearly Mach-independent, with corrections linear in $1/M^2$, consistent with the scaled kinetic equation. At equal normalised density, Mach 8 and 12 give the heat flux and stress at Mach 25 within 1\%, comparable to the accuracy of the reference; with one moment equation for position, physical-space profiles follow within 5\%. Comparing three prediction methods shows that the accuracy comes from the scaling; the Gaussian form adds compactness. Ahead of the shock, the mass of upstream-moving molecules decays as a stretched exponential with effective exponent 0.68--0.87. Collisions regenerate upstream-moving molecules, which explains a decay slower than free-flight survival; a linear cascade model with a downstream-Maxwellian source and no input from the shock interior reproduces the decay rates within 1.2\%.

papers.title: Multi-output neural network surrogate for double-pulse femtosecond optothermal control of thin silicon films on fused silica
papers.abstract: We introduce a multi-output feedforward neural network surrogate trained on a coupled multiple-reflection and two-temperature model to map double-pulse femtosecond laser excitation (1030 nm) of crystalline silicon films on fused silica across film thicknesses (50-500 nm) and inter-pulse delays (0-10ps). Trained via Levenberg-Marquardt optimization on 2000 physical simulations, the dual-hidden-layer network ([40,30] neurons) simultaneously predicts six strongly coupled optothermal observables, peak electron temperature, peak lattice temperature, peak carrier density, minimum and maximum absorptivity and minimum refractive index achieving coefficients of determination R2 larger than 0.9998 across all targets. Evaluating a dense 200 by 200 design grid in milliseconds resolves pronounced thin-film interference fringes and carrier-induced index modulation, identifying an optimal optothermal coupling regime at d=156 nm and Dt=4.572 ps. This unified machine-learning workflow eliminates computationally expensive multi-physics runtime bottlenecks for real-time laser processing control and inverse photonic thin-film design.

papers.title: Faster $χ^2$ periodogram: Accelerating linear algebra with fast Toeplitz solvers
papers.abstract: In recent years, the traditional Lomb--Scargle periodogram, relying on least-squares fitting of a sinusoid to data with a known mean, has been mostly superseded by its floating-mean extension---the generalized Lomb--Scargle periodogram---due to the superior robustness and accuracy of the latter. While further generalization to higher-degree trigonometric polynomials (known as the multiharmonic analysis of variance and the fast $\chi^2$ periodogram) has been known for decades, its usage remains relatively uncommon, mostly due to its significantly higher computational cost. Here we present a technique reducing the computational complexity of such an extension by combining a Toeplitz formulation of the system of normal equations with non-uniform fast Fourier transforms, coupled with condition-number monitoring to protect against numerical instability. When modified for practical efficiency rather than asymptotic computational complexity, our approach reaches speed-ups exceeding an order of magnitude over current state-of-the-art implementations across a wide range of hyperparameters when evaluated on multithreaded systems, while matching or exceeding their accuracy. Additionally, we provide a reference implementation used for benchmarking, along with the code used to generate the results presented in this work.

papers.title: On cover exacting cardinals
papers.abstract: We answer a question of Goldberg about cover exacting cardinals. Concretely, we show that if $\kappa$ is $\omega_1$-strongly compact, then no cardinal $\lambda>\kappa$ is $\gamma$-cover exacting for some cardinal $\gamma$.

papers.title: Type-Confusion Security
Reliable Mining of Heterogeneous AI Coding-Agent Data: Context-Aware Prediction and Resource-Aware Ranking
Descending Everest, Part III: Oracle Complexity of Monotone Variational Inequalities with $(L_0,L_1)$-Lipschitz Operators
papers.abstract: We consider monotone variational inequalities in which the Jacobian norm of the operator $F:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^d$ is bounded by an affine function of the norm of the operator itself: $\|DF(z)\|\le L_0+L_1\|F(z)\|$. The main case is the problem on the whole space, that is, finding a zero of $F$. We assume that a solution exists and that an upper bound $R$ on the distance from the starting point to the solution is known. Neither strong monotonicity nor cocoercivity is assumed. Global Lipschitz continuity is not assumed either: for $L_1>0$, the Jacobian norm may grow together with the norm of the operator. We obtain upper and lower bounds on the number of oracle calls sufficient to find a point $\hat z$ with $\|F(\hat z)\|\le\varepsilon$. For $L_0R/\varepsilon\ge1$, both bounds are, up to logarithmic factors in $L_1R$, of order $1+L_0R/\varepsilon+(L_1R)^{6/5}$. The upper bound is attained by a deterministic extragradient-type method, and the lower bound holds for arbitrary randomized methods. The same bounds are obtained for the Minty gap on the ball of radius $R$, where $L_0R/\varepsilon$ is replaced by $L_0R^2/\eta$. In addition, we show that for a variational inequality on a bounded set the numbers $L_0,L_1$ and the diameter of the set are not sufficient: a uniform complexity bound requires additional information, for example, an upper bound on the norm of the operator at the solution.

papers.title: Off-shell one-loop counterterms of Palatini gravity with an independent background connection
papers.abstract: We compute the one-loop divergences of pure gravity in the first-order (Palatini) formulation, using the background field method in Goldberg variables, with a background connection independent of the background metric. Background Ward-Takahashi identities are verified at one loop. The divergences of the two-point functions, obtained in arbitrary dimension and gauge, require, besides the curvature-squared terms, invariants built from the nonmetricity of the background connection; in particular, the Gauss-Bonnet combination, which is not topological for a nonmetric connection, does not suffice. Three- and four-point functions in the Feynman-de Donder gauge complete the counterterm Lagrangian up to fourth order in the nonmetricity and provide parameter-free tests of it. All the counterterms vanish on shell, as in the metric formulation, and off shell they can be removed by field redefinitions.

papers.title: "God says we are right!": The Interplay between Religion and Propaganda on Arabic Social Media
Model-Free Stealthy Attack on Vehicle Systems and Its Implications for ISO/SAE 21434 Risk Assessment
Causal Discovery for Resiliency-Prioritized Transmission Expansion Planning in Power Systems with Grid-Forming Inverter-Based Resources
Where the Savings Go: The Limits of Hiding Cross-Tenant Cache Hits in LLM Serving
Geometric tracking of a halo CME using full-circle wide-field views from PUNCH
papers.abstract: We tracked the large, geoeffective halo coronal mass ejection (CME) of 2025-May-31 across the very wide field of view of the Polarimeter to Unify the Corona and Heliosphere (PUNCH) mission, as a proof of concept for data-informed forecasting of CME arrival times at Earth. using simple point-and-click measurement of the front location as far as 47 degrees away from the Sun itself, we constrained an analytic "ludicrous ice-cream cone" geometric model with just three parameters: position angle, off-Earth-Sun angle, and propagation speed. We show that the model is sufficient to capture the bulk envelope of the CME, and also insufficient to capture the complexity of the CME's evolution. We generated simulated arrival-time forecasts for the CME by extrapolating the constant-velocity propagation to determine the time of impact with Earth. These "retro-forecasts" converged to within 30 +/- 15 minutes of the actual arrival time, 8 hours prior to arrival. The convergence was marked by a clear inflection point in the curve of predicted-arrival-time vs time-of-forecast. We conclude that continuous wide-field tracking is sufficiently powerful to enable even crude models to substantially improve arrival-time forecasting precision, and discuss future work required both to validate this single-event result and to extend it to more sophisticated analyses.

papers.title: Benchmarking LLM Inference on Desktop-Scale NVIDIA Grace Blackwell Clusters
Protecting Safety during Reasoning Training with Low-Rank Fisher Regularisation
Structural properties of semi-cutting sets
Maximum likelihood degrees of 3D polytopes built from polygons of ML degree one
papers.abstract: We construct 3D polytopes that admit a scaling with maximum likelihood (ML) degree one by using codimension zero toric fiber products of lower-dimensional polytopes and classify all the 3D polytopes that can be constructed in this way. We also study a family of 3D polytopes whose faces admit ML degree one scalings. We give a tight lower bound for the ML degree of these polytopes with a square base and we show that every value between this bound and the normalized volume of the polytope can be attained. These values depend on counting common and repeated roots associated to certain univariate polynomials. This is similar in spirit to the description of the possible ML degrees of rational normal scrolls.

papers.title: Characterizing nonlocal Sobolev spaces as generalized Bessel potential spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study nonlocal Sobolev spaces $H^{\rho,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ with $p \in (1,\infty)$, defined via a general class of nonlocal gradients $D^\rho$ associated with a kernel function $\rho$. As our main contribution, we establish three new equivalent characterizations of these spaces. First, we describe $H^{\rho,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ in terms of Fourier multipliers involving the symbol of the nonlocal potential associated with $D^\rho$. Second, we give a thorough functional analytic treatment of the nonlocal $\rho$-Laplacian $\Delta^\rho$, which allows us to represent general nonlocal Sobolev spaces through its square root $(-\Delta^\rho)^{1/2}$. Third, we show that $H^{\rho,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ coincides with the image $g_\rho * L^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$ for a suitable convolution kernel $g_\rho \in L^1(\mathbb{R}^n)$, which confirms that these spaces are genuine potential spaces. These results generalize the well-known fact that, in the special case of the Riesz kernel, the resulting fractional Sobolev spaces coincide with the classical Bessel potential spaces. In this spirit, the present work can also be viewed as introducing a natural notion of generalized Bessel potential spaces.

papers.title: Multi-seed information diffusion with varying reproduction
CiGS: Conduction in Gaussian Splats for Interior Temperature Field from Thermal Images
Canonical metrics on punctured spheres, II: compactified moduli spaces of black holes
papers.abstract: Let $g_{\mathfrak{p}_{\ell}}$ denote the canonical scalar-flat metric on $S^n\setminus \mathfrak{p}_{\ell}$ introduced in Part~I, which for $n=3$ corresponds to the Brill--Lindquist initial data for $\ell$ black holes, and let $\eta\in H_{\ell}$ be its associated mass matrix. In this paper, we investigate the asymptotic behavior of the metrics and the mass matrix $\eta$ as subsets of punctures collide. Such collisions cause every mass to diverge; if a cluster $A$ of black holes collapses at a relative scale $t$, the mass matrix satisfies $\eta=E(A)\ln(1/t)+O(1)$, diverging along an explicit ray $E(A)\in H_{\ell}$. For nested families of clusters, this degeneracy structure naturally organizes into a space of rooted trees. Subtracting the divergence gives a renormalized mass matrix which extends smoothly to every stratum of the Axelrod--Singer compactified moduli space $\overline{M}{}^{\,\mathrm{AS}}_\ell= \overline C_{\ell-1}(\mathbb{R}^n)/\mathrm O(n)$ and splits naturally into one mass matrix per vertex of the bubble tree. Geometrically, at each vertex carrying punctures the suitably rescaled metrics converge to a complete scalar-flat metric with the nodes filled in, adjacent such pieces being joined by Schwarzschild necks, and the renormalized matrix acting as its mass data. For $n=3$, the necks contain minimal spheres, which are common apparent horizons of the merging holes. At vertices bearing two holes, we determine on which side of the limiting horizon each node lies, and we formulate as a conjecture the resulting criterion for a neck to be a component of the outermost horizon. We also compare the mass lower bound of Part~I with the Riemannian Penrose inequality. Because the mass matrix is invariant under rotations of the bubbles, it lives on a Deligne--Mumford-type quotient of the compactification.

papers.title: Resolvent-based modeling of turbulent flow over multilayer compliant surfaces
papers.abstract: Compliant coatings offer a passive approach to modifying near-wall turbulence and potentially reducing skin-friction drag, but high-fidelity exploration of the coupled parameter space is costly. We develop a two-way coupled resolvent-Galerkin framework for turbulent channel flow over finite-thickness, layered viscoelastic coatings. The fluid is modeled using the Navier-Stokes equations linearized about a turbulent mean state, while the solid is represented by a through-thickness Galerkin discretization of the elastodynamic equations. The solid response is condensed into a spectral surface-impedance operator at the fluid-solid interface. At $Re_\tau = 180$, stiff panels approach the rigid-wall response, whereas more compliant panels modify the low-rank response associated with the near-wall cycle. A Reynolds-number study shows that panels with fixed nondimensional material stiffness can produce different responses depending on whether their thickness scales with inner or outer flow length scales. The influence of viscoelastic damping is examined across low- and high-frequency regimes, where stiffness-proportional damping alters the high-frequency fractional-energy distribution, while the low-frequency distribution remains relatively insensitive to damping. For multilayer panels, the fluid-facing material determines the interfacial wave speed, while the subsurface stiffness distribution modifies the panel's effective thickness. Temporal stability analysis identifies regions of parameter space where a steady harmonic response is relevant and regions where instabilities grow. Finally, a leading-order, covariance-based drag-estimation framework relates the coupled response to changes in the mean flow and to the estimated skin-friction drag. Together, these tools provide a basis for screening coating designs and selecting candidates for high-fidelity simulations and experiments.

papers.title: Pre-amplification for Preserving Quantum Resources Through an Open-Air, Room-Temperature Microwave Channel
papers.abstract: We model a scenario where the pre-amplified signal mode of a two-mode squeezed vacuum (TMSV) state generated by a Josephson parametric converter (JPC) is transmitted through a room-temperature, open-air channel, while the idler is retained at low temperature. Before transmission, the state contains three quantum resources: (1) entanglement, (2) non-classicality, and (3) sub-vacuum conditional prediction of the signal quadrature. To preserve these resources through noise and loss, we consider two forms of quantum-limited pre-amplification of the signal mode: phase-preserving amplification (PPA) and phase-sensitive amplification (PSA). We identify three thresholds for a fixed amount of loss as noise increases from zero marking the loss of (1) entanglement, (2) non-classicality, and (3) sub-vacuum conditional prediction of the signal quadrature, respectively. We find first that entanglement is fatally sensitive to the noise and loss in our channel model and neither form of pre-amplification protects it. On the other hand, phase-sensitive pre-amplification is shown to significantly raise the thresholds at which non-classicality and sub-vacuum conditional prediction are destroyed. For a 3-meter link between room-temperature horn antennas at 5 GHz, the noise thresholds for these resources can be orders of magnitude above the thermal background. Further analysis shows that these conclusions are robust to limited phase misalignment and pre-amplifier-added noise, with the latter having the stronger effect. These surviving non-classical resources may support quantum-enhanced sensing, illumination, and metrology protocols even in regimes where entanglement itself is destroyed. Our results suggest that protocols that exploit these quantum phenomena are the most likely to succeed in microwave applications.

papers.title: Functional Information, Optimal Channel Simulation and Lossy Source Coding
Visual Marking as a Native Reasoning Capability for Multimodal LLMs
A Bleichenbacher bit-by-bit oracle attack from partial message knowledge
Medicaid Quality Disparities: Domain-Specific Performance Analysis and Approaches for State-Level Improvement
papers.abstract: Medicaid covers nearly 78 million people, yet care quality varies across states, programs, and clinical domains. Using the 2024 CMS Child and Adult Core Sets (9,781 usable state-measure observations from 11,100 records), this study combined descriptive statistics, benchmark-gap analysis, correlation, and OLS regression to find where shortfalls cluster. Disparities were strongly domain-specific. Maternal and Perinatal Health scored lowest (28.0%), followed by Dental and Oral Health (38.5%) and Behavioral Health (44.4%), while Long-Term Services and Supports (82.8%) and Experience of Care (67.8%) scored highest. State performance correlated strongly with national benchmarks (r = 0.77, approximately), so rates should be read against each measure's benchmark. Domain was the strongest predictor, and the model explained 31.2% of variance. Because of heteroscedasticity and influential observations from mixing bounded and utilization measures, estimates are descriptive. Quality improvement should be targeted by domain, prioritizing maternal health, behavioral health network adequacy, and dental provider participation.

papers.title: The Manifold-Index Model: provably and efficiently avoiding the statistical and computational curse of dimensionality
Beyond AUC: Do Mammography Risk Models Predict When Cancer Occurs?
DexFormer 2.0: Towards a Cross-Embodiment Foundation Policy for Dexterous Grasping
Canonical metrics on punctured spheres, I: the mass matrix and the polygon model
papers.abstract: A canonical metric $g_{\mathfrak{p}_{\ell}}$ on $S^n \setminus \mathfrak{p}_{\ell}$, where $\mathfrak{p}_{\ell}=(p_1,\ldots,p_{\ell})$ and $n \ge 3$, is a metric conformal to the round metric that is complete, scalar-flat, and asymptotically flat at each puncture $p_i$. For $n=3$ these metrics are the Brill--Lindquist time-symmetric initial data for $\ell$ black holes, and their ends carry ADM masses. In this paper we study the masses, through the mass matrix, as functions on the conformal moduli space $M_{\ell}(S^n)$. The mass matrix $\eta =(\eta_{ij})$ is a symmetric matrix with zero diagonal and vanishing row sums (these matrices form the space $H_{\ell}$), and it determines the \emph{normalized ADM mass} at the $i$-th end via $\hat{\mathfrak{m}}_i=\sum_{j\ne i}e^{\eta_{ij}}$. We prove that the mass map $\Xi\colon M_\ell(S^n)\to H_{\ell}$ is a homeomorphism onto its image. On the other hand, the moduli space $\mathcal{M}_\ell(S^n)$ is homeomorphic to the moduli space of those equilateral $\ell$-gons in the hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^{n+1}$ whose sides, extended to infinity, end at distinct points (the Gauss map). By a theorem of Kapovich--Leeb--Millson and Balser, every polystable configuration is the Gauss image of such a polygon, and the Gauss map identifies the space of all equilateral $\ell$-gons with a natural compactification of $M_\ell(S^n)$. In particular, the mass matrix has an explicit description in terms of the pairwise vertex distances of the polygon. The mass matrix diverges as punctures collide. The degeneration, its renormalization, and the resulting compactification of the moduli space are the subject of a sequel to this paper.

papers.title: ANNA: Attention-Free Neural Neighborhood Aggregation for Channel Estimation on Regenerative NTN Payloads
papers.abstract: Accurate deep learning (DL)-based channel estimation (CE) for non-terrestrial network (NTN) uplinks must meet the processing, power, and latency constraints of regenerative payloads. We propose Attention-free Neural Neighborhood Aggregation (ANNA), a lightweight architecture combining per-resource block (RB) pilot projection, convolutional neighborhood aggregation, and shared reconstruction, with dense-grid expansion only at the output. Evaluation against learned and classical estimators uses paired waveform-generated datasets with receiver frequency correction enabled and disabled. With correction enabled, 16-bit floating point (FP16) deployment on a 10 W Jetson Orin NX achieves 0.372 ms 99th-percentile (P99) latency and 2.15 dB lower mean normalized mean-squared error (NMSE) than the fastest learned baseline at 29.6% higher latency. Relative to the most accurate learned baseline, ANNA is 4.08 times as fast and consumes 80.5% less module energy per sample, with a 1.14 dB accuracy penalty. It meets the adopted 0.5 ms P99 target in all 100 benchmark runs, demonstrating a favorable accuracy-latency-energy trade-off for embedded uplink CE.

papers.title: Ramsey sets are canonically Ramsey
papers.abstract: A set $A$ of points is called Ramsey if, for each $r$, every $r$-coloring of a sufficiently high-dimensional Euclidean space contains a monochromatic congruent copy of $A$. We show that for each Ramsey set $A$, every $r$-coloring of a sufficiently high-dimensional Euclidean space, regardless of the number of colors used, contains a monochromatic or a rainbow congruent copy of $A$. This answers a question raised in virtually every paper on the topic.

papers.title: Self-supervised learning for zebrafish embryo phenotype evaluation: Systematic comparison of algorithms, label-efficient classification, and transfer learning
GNN-Based Deep Reinforcement Learning for Coastal Emergency Response under Extreme Water Levels
Borel combinatorics of $\mathbb{N}^{\ell}$-shift actions and hypersmooth equivalence relations
papers.abstract: We conjecture that for each integer $\ell\geq 2$, the equivalence relation arising from the shift action of $\mathbb{N}^{\ell}$ on $2^{\omega^{\ell}}$ is hypersmooth. We prove this conjecture for $\ell=2$, reduce the general case to a problem in Borel graph colorings, and establish the general case in measure. We also show that under certain mild hypotheses on a hypersmooth equivalence relation $E$, every finite-index Borel super-equivalence relation of $E$ is hypersmooth.

papers.title: Three-Dimensional Impact Angle Control Guidance Law with Field-of-View Constraint
Geometry-Derived Capacitance Dyadics with Floquet Sideband Correction for Anisotropic Periodic Patch Metasurfaces
papers.abstract: Homogenised sheet models describe periodic metallic patch layers using a scalar sheet capacitance, which is only valid when the effective response is isotropic. An isotropic response exists for unit cells with patch geometries that have rotational symmetry of order three or higher. Lower-symmetry unit cells with irregular or random geometries generically require a full 2 x 2 surface-capacitance dyadic. We present a framework that computes this dyadic directly from the arbitrary gap-connected patch geometry on a unit cell of a hexagonal lattice. The two-dimensional Bravais periodicity fixes the two independent macroscopic loading directions, the connectivity of the gap ensures a full-rank response for the geometries considered here, and the point-group symmetry of the patch constrains the form of the dyadic. A quasi-static boundary value problem on a single periodic cell then determines its independent entries. We use the surface-capacitance dyadic in the anisotropic surface- wave dispersion relation, which includes the leading spatially-dispersive first shell Floquet-sideband correction. For each new patch geometry, the dyadic and the first-shell correction are obtained from a single quasi-static cell problem and from the reconstructed boundary. So anisotropic surface- wave dispersion follows without a per-geometry full-wave eigenmode band sweep or sheet-tensor retrieval. We validate this geometry-to-dispersion chain against full-wave eigenmode simulations across six representative symmetry classes, showing that the correction captures band flattening near the Brillouin-zone boundary and improves agreement relative to the local dyadic model.

papers.title: Global dynamics of large smooth solutions to the two-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes system with Navier-slip boundary conditions
papers.abstract: We establish global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions containing vacuum to the two-dimensional barotropic compressible Navier-Stokes equations with bulk viscosity depending on the density, in smooth bounded simply connected domains, subject to the Navier-slip boundary conditions. Without any restriction on the size of initial data, we obtain time-uniform density and velocity bounds and exponentialconvergence to equilibrium in Sobolev spaces for the density and velocity. Moreover an initial vacuum point will persist and force the exponential growth of density gradients.

papers.title: Self-doped correlated adatom lattices on cubic boron nitride
papers.abstract: We survey triangular adatom lattices on the (111) surfaces of cubic boron nitride (cBN) for strongly correlated two-dimensional electron systems. Using density functional theory combined with the constrained random phase approximation and charge self-consistent dynamical mean-field theory, we identify twelve promising candidates. Group-III (group-V) adatoms on the N- (B-)termination realize clean one-band Hubbard systems, while group-III and transition-metal (V, Cr, Mn) adatoms on the B-termination realize two-band Hubbard systems. Importantly, the polar III-V character of cBN induces self-doping by $\pm 1/4$ electron away from integer filling. With strong Hubbard (and Hund's) interactions and small hoppings, most systems are doped Mott insulators. Heavy quasielectrons with mass renormalizations up to 4 and strong local moments up to 2.5 $\mu_B$ put our systems into a regime where unconventional superconductivity on the triangular lattice has been predicted.

papers.title: A counterexample to the subgraphings approximate the cost problem
papers.abstract: We prove that for every $k\ge 2$, the free group $\mathbb{F}_k$ on $k$ generators admits a finite generating set $S$ such that the Schreier graphing of the Bernoulli action of $\mathbb{F}_k$ with respect to $S$ does not admit spanning subgraphings that would approximate the cost of the action. In particular, this gives an example of a graphing that spans a treeable countable pmp equivalence relation, but does not admit a spanning subtreeing.

papers.title: Estimating Outpatient Visit Prices from Hospital Price Transparency Data using Large Language Models
Oxygens breathe, electrons jump
papers.abstract: Electronic transport in polyanionic battery cathodes proceeds through small-polaron hopping between transition-metal sites and is commonly assumed to be tightly coupled to the motion of charge-compensating mobile ions. Using olivine Li$_x$MnPO$_4$ as a prototypical platform, we use first-principles molecular dynamics with extended Hubbard functionals to follow, in real time and at finite temperature, the adiabatic evolution of Mn oxidation states and atomic sublattices. We find that polaron hopping and cation migration are dynamically decoupled: Mn$^{2+}$/Mn$^{3+}$ valence exchanges occur frequently while the intercalated ions remain confined to their sites, and hopping is gated by the local oxygen framework. Freezing the six oxygen atoms of an individual MnO$_6$ octahedron excludes that site from the hopping network, while increasing the fictitious oxygen mass slows down electronic transport. Each valence exchange coincides with a concerted breathing of the donor and acceptor octahedra ($\Delta V \simeq 2$ $Å^3$), with their volume asymmetry crossing zero at the transition, consistent with the Holstein-Marcus coincidence condition. The hopping rate yields an activation energy of $E_a = 0.20 \pm 0.03$ eV, closely matching the elastic energy scale of the two coordination cages ($\lambda_V/4 \approx 0.20$ eV). These results identify the oxygen coordination cage, not the mobile cation sublattice, as the dynamical gate for small-polaron transport: a site can accept the electron only if its cage can breathe, and the barrier is governed by cage elasticity. Selective constraints and mass scaling applied to first-principles dynamics provide a general route to link electronic and lattice degrees of freedom in redox-active materials, opening the door to framework engineering in intercalation and mixed ionic-electronic conductors.

papers.title: Scaling large language model-assisted line-of-therapy adjudication with human-in-the-loop evidence-calibrated selection
Microfitting: Continual Learning via Cached Test-Time Training
Tight Bounds for Non-Monotone Submodular Maximization under a Cardinality Constraint with Constant Recourse
Continuous-Time Stochastic Contraction Induced by Common White Noise
Deep Sequence Model for Genome Wide Discovery of Coding and Regulatory Element Signatures
VoxMel TTS Technical Report
papers.abstract: Continuous autoregressive TTS relies on an acoustic target that enables stable next-latent modeling while preserving fine-grained acoustic details. While existing approaches employ learned compressed representations (e.g., continuous VAE latents) to render prediction tractable, they rely on complex neural encoders that often cap generation fidelity. Conversely, training-free targets like mel-spectrograms eliminate encoder overhead, yet their potential for autoregressive generation remains largely underexplored. In this work, we propose VoxMel, a tokenizer-free framework for autoregressive TTS that makes stable mel modeling tractable through a fixed, exactly invertible two-axis Haar transform. The transform first decomposes each mel spectrogram along frequency into local averages and a frequency residual, then splits the averaged component along time into Coarse-Mel and a temporal residual. A language-model backbone with a flow-matching head autoregressively generates Coarse-Mel. Non-autoregressive residual tiers then predict the temporal residual from Coarse-Mel, followed by the frequency residual conditioned on the reconstructed Frequency-Averaged Mel. Neither residual is fed back into the autoregressive history. Trained on 100K hours of Emilia, the supervised 0.6B model obtains 1.51\% WER and 0.738 speaker similarity (SIM) on test-en, and 1.29\% CER and 0.755 SIM on test-zh. GRPO improves these results to 1.15\% WER / 0.753 SIM and 1.17\% CER / 0.776 SIM, respectively. We also distill the guided flow head into two- and four-step students, requiring 2 or 4 head evaluations per coarse frame. The four-step student retains competitive SIM and nearly matches the supervised model in WER/CER.

papers.title: Integrating Latent Block Models into Variational Autoencoders for Disentangled Representation Learning
Contraction Analysis and Control of Polynomial Dynamical Systems
Improving Tropical Cyclone Forecasts through Objective Ensemble Track-Error Reduction
papers.abstract: Accurate tropical cyclone (TC) track guidance is essential for warnings, evacuation planning, and risk communication, but outlying members and distinct track scenarios can degrade raw ensemble forecasts. Statistical and machine-learning (ML) methods proposed to improve ensemble guidance are difficult to compare because previous studies often use different forecast systems, basins, periods, and verification methods. Using a common verification framework, this study compares six objective methods (four statistical trimming and two ML methods) with the full ensemble mean for 138 TCs forecast by GEFS, MOGREPS-G, and IFS during 2016-2024. Dynamic trimming (DT) is the most consistent statistical method, reducing mean total track error by 8.0%, 13.4%, and 16.1% at short, medium, and long ranges. Its largest benefits occur in high-spread cases, where it can reach 70% of the low-error bound. Short-lead-error trimming (SLET) provides useful delayed guidance after early observations become available, but its improvement decreases with lead time. Regression-mixture clustering (RC) shows potential in low-spread cases and provides the largest improvement over the control run. The gradient boosted tree (GBT) produces the largest medium-range improvement and exceeds the theoretical trimming bound, suggesting strong potential, particularly when the observed track is poorly represented by the ensemble family. However, its 12.8% short-range degradation and gains concentrated in a small subset of cases indicate overcorrection when the ensemble mean is already accurate, highlighting the need for additional constraints. These results provide a consistent basis for using objective error-reduction methods to strengthen TC track guidance for operational decision-making.

papers.title: Asymptotic radial symmetry of $p$-Ginzburg-Landau minimizers on the disk
papers.abstract: We solve the minimizer case of Brezis's Open Problem~2.3 for every fixed $p>2$. For $\varepsilon>0$, let $\mathbf{u}_{\varepsilon}\in W^{1,p}(B_1;\mathbb{R}^2)$ be a global minimizer of the $p$-Ginzburg--Landau energy \[ \int_{B_1} \left( \frac{|\nabla\mathbf{u}|^p}{p} +\frac{(1-|\mathbf{u}|^2)^2}{4\varepsilon^2} \right)\,dx \] with prescribed trace $\mathbf{u}_{\varepsilon}|_{\partial B_1}(x)=x$. We prove that, as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$, $\mathbf{u}_{\varepsilon}(x)\to x/|x|$ at every point $x\in B_1\setminus\{0\}$. The convergence is strong in $W^{1,p}_{\mathrm{loc}}(B_1\setminus\{0\};\mathbb{R}^2)$ and hence uniform on every compact subset of the punctured disk. On each such compact subset, the potential energy tends to zero and the total energy converges to the $p$-Dirichlet energy of the radial map. No symmetry or uniqueness of the minimizers is assumed. The proof combines whole-plane concentration, a strict exterior filling estimate, and quantitative convexity to locate the concentration point and identify the limiting map.

papers.title: Uniform compactness in a family of $\bar{\partial}$-Neumann problems
papers.abstract: In their paper on non-coercive boundary value problems, Kohn and Nirenberg show that a priori estimates for all forms satisfying $\bar{\partial}$-Neumann boundary conditions follow from a compactness estimate. Inspired by Hamilton, we show that these a priori estimates are stable under deformations of the complex structure, the hermitian metric and the volume form of the underlying manifold. We use a parameter $m$ to encode a deformation of this data. We show that if a family of $\bar{\partial}$-Neumann problems depends smoothly on $m$ and the compactness estimate(s) hold (with constants uniform in $m$), then the family of solution operators also depends smoothly $m$. As a consequence we obtain sufficient conditions for the Bergman kernel to vary smoothly in a family of domains. We also provide a sufficient condition for the uniform compactness estimate(s) to hold in a family of domains.

papers.title: Logarithmic thermodynamic cost of prediction from rare observations
papers.abstract: A memory predicting changes in its environment from rare observations must spend energy on sampling and recording. We consider autonomous chemical memories driven by a sample-and-hold sensor observing an environment that switches at rate gamma, with sampling frequency f<<gamma. An ideal observer with access to the full observation history can retain predictive information proportional to f. However, retaining a finite fraction of this information in an autonomous physical memory requires work of order kBT ln(gamma/f) per sensor change. This additional thermodynamic cost arises from the competing requirements of suppressing false records during long intervals between observations and responding rapidly to new observations. We establish a universal low-power bound on predictive information, which grows at most as P/ln(P_ref/P) with power budget P, uniformly over any finite number of memory states and independently of network topology and memory relaxation times. We further demonstrate that memory architecture determines the attainable scaling. With bounded transition rates and readout from the memory alone, two-state memories are limited to P^2 scaling, whereas a three-state memory is sufficient to attain the optimal logarithmic scaling. Our results establish a fundamental thermodynamic distinction between acquiring information and maintaining a useful record of a changing environment.

papers.title: Machine Learning the $GW$ Self-Energy Operator for Real Materials
papers.abstract: Machine learning of $GW$ in solids has largely focused on prediction of scalar quasiparticle energy corrections. Here, we introduce a phase-aware many-body transformer that predicts the full $\mathbf{k}$-resolved complex self-energy matrix. As a proof of principle, we apply the model to predict quasiparticle energies before and after diagonalization of the quasiparticle Hamiltonian, obtaining a test set mean absolute error (MAE) of 29 meV for a dataset of 1745 2D materials in the static COHSEX approximation and 60 meV for a more limited dataset of 433 materials calculated within a plasmon-pole model. COHSEX pretraining followed by finetuning reduces this MAE to 42 meV. The predicted matrices also accurately reproduce QP wavefunctions.

A Proof of Stein's Equidissection Conjecture
papers.abstract: In 1970 Monsky showed that a square cannot be dissected into an odd number of equal-area triangles. His proof used an ingenious colouring of the plane based on a 2-adic valuation on $\mathbb{R}$ together with Sperner's lemma. Subsequent work established similar results for regular polygons, centrally symmetric polygons, and polyominoes. In 2000, Stein proposed a common generalisation of the centrally symmetric and polyomino cases to balanced polygons. In 2014, Rudenko introduced a new perspective on the problem and proved Stein's conjecture for dissections with rational vertex coordinates. Building on and streamlining his approach, we resolve the conjecture in full.

papers.title: A Polynomial Time Approximation for the Minimization of Implication Systems and Horn CNFs
Torsion phenomena in symplectic capacities via Clarke duality
papers.abstract: We study Gutt--Hutchings capacities with finite cyclic coefficients and show that torsion in positive $S^1$-equivariant symplectic homology detects new obstructions to symplectic embeddings between convex toric domains. Prime-field coefficients give no additional obstructions in this class, while the torsion responsible for the new obstructions already appears over $\mathbb Z/p^{p+2}$ for every prime $p$. We prove a stabilization theorem for these capacities on convex bodies with arbitrary commutative coefficients, yielding a sharp stabilized embedding obstruction in an explicit example. Clarke duality makes these phenomena accessible to computation. We extend the filtered equivariant Clarke--Floer comparison to arbitrary commutative coefficient rings and compute the capacities using models of dual action sublevels built from representation spheres. The circle-action weights encode orbit covering multiplicities, whose products govern the new obstructions.

papers.title: Positivity of simplicial volume of convex projective manifolds
papers.abstract: Let $\Omega$ be an irreducible properly convex projective domain admitting a discrete cocompact group action of projective automorphisms. We prove that the Holmes--Thompson volumes of projective simplices with vertices in $\Omega$ are uniformly bounded. As a consequence, we prove that a closed properly convex projective manifold of dimension at least two has positive simplicial volume if and only if it is irreducible.

papers.title: Unveiling the Multi-Phase Outflow in NGC 4151 with JWST Observations - I. Integrated Properties of the Outflow
papers.abstract: The biconical outflow of the nearby Seyfert 1.5 AGN NGC 4151 has been studied across the electromagnetic spectrum, yet mapping its multiphase structure with a single facility has remained challenging. Leveraging the broad wavelength coverage of the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), we present new near- and mid-infrared observations tracing the ionization stratification of these outflows with a unified dataset. We analyze emission lines originating from molecular gas to highly ionized plasma and analyze the ionized gas using a 5-component Cloudy photoionization model covering three primary phases. Applying the footprint line method to characterize the X-ray emitting gas, we find that it holds the largest share of the total mass, suggesting that it is a primary candidate for driving AGN feedback in this system.

papers.title: Optical spin Edelstein response of d-wave altermagnets
papers.abstract: The momentum-dependent spin splitting and compensated magnetic order in altermagnets offer opportunities for electrical control of spin polarization. We explore the spin Edelstein effect in the frequency domain of a two-dimensional d-wave altermagnet with Rashba spin-orbit coupling. We calculate the spin-velocity susceptibility response function beyond the intraband response regime and find that the interband longitudinal and transverse Edelstein responses are governed by the Zeeman quantum metric and Zeeman Berry curvature, respectively. The density of states presents a logarithmic van Hove singularity at exactly the negative value of the energy below which four disconnected Fermi contours emerge. This defines three distinctive regions for the position of the Fermi level, through which the Edelstein susceptibility tensor displays characteristic spectral features, reflecting the topological change of the Fermi surface. The resulting spin magnetization shows a strong dependence on the driving frequency and on the orientation of the in-plane external electric field. Our results highlight new possibilities for electrical and optical control of the spin Edelstein effect in altermagnets that could find spintronic applications.

papers.title: Impatience Makes Matching NP-Hard
Local Limit Theorems and Edgeworth Expansions for some classes of inhomogeneous Markov chains
papers.abstract: In this note, we prove local central limit theorems and expansions in the central limit theorem for inhomogeneous Markov chains satisfying a one-step lower ellipticity condition. As for the local limit theorem, in the general inhomogeneous case, compared with \cite{DS}, we are able to prove results without two-sided ellipticity, although only in the one-step case. Compared with \cite{PeligradLLT1,PeligradLLT2}, we are able to prove local limit theorems without a lower $\psi$-mixing condition. Concerning Edgeworth expansions, compared with \cite{DHPTRF1}, we are able to get results without two-sided ellipticity (under some sequential Diophantine conditions). Our conditions are then verified for Markov chains in a random dynamical environment with a one-sided Doeblin condition under very mild assumptions. For Markov chains in a random environment, we also consider the more general case of $\phi$-mixing chains and then, under some mild periodicity assumptions on the environment, we prove local central limit theorems and first-order Edgeworth expansions (without any ellipticity assumptions), matching the results for deterministic homogeneous chains. When the chain is driven by a topologically mixing subshift of finite type, we obtain high-order expansions for $\phi$-mixing chains under some Diophantine conditions of a deterministic system generated by a periodic point. We then apply our results to bounded additive functionals of posterior states in disordered quantum trajectories and establish local central limit theorems and first-order Edgeworth expansions.

papers.title: Approximate $K$-Conjugacy of Minimal Cantor--Circle Extensions I: The Rigid Case
papers.abstract: We study approximate $K$-conjugacy for minimal Cantor--circle extensions with arbitrary circle homeomorphism cocycles, allowing orientation reversal. Under the assumption of classical rigidity, we show that two such systems are approximately $K$-conjugate if and only if there exists an ordered unital graded $K$-theory isomorphism satisfying the finite coefficient $K$-condition. Our approach combines dynamical corrections along Kakutani--Rokhlin towers with the classification and uniqueness theory of $C^*$-algebras. Moreover, the crossed-product isomorphisms implementing approximate $K$-conjugacy can be chosen as inner perturbations of a fixed isomorphism and its inverse.

papers.title: $p$-ellipticity for systems of elliptic equations with complex coefficients
papers.abstract: We extend the concept of $p$-ellipticity for (single) elliptic operators, that we introduced in arXiv:1611.00653 , to the case of systems of elliptic equations with complex coefficients. The $p$-ellipticity condition from this paper turns out to be equivalent, up to a factor depending on $p$, to a condition for systems introduced (and equally named) by Dindoš, Li and Pipher in arXiv:2007.13190 . We prove several key properties of $p$-ellipticity akin to those that have been known to hold in the scalar case ( arXiv:1611.00653 ). In some respects, however, the vector case fundamentally differs from the scalar one. As an application we establish the contractivity on $L^p$ of the operator semigroup generated by systems of elliptic equations with complex coefficients and subject to Dirichlet, Neumann or mixed boundary conditions.

papers.title: Zeeman-Doppler imaging of active young Suns. New surface magnetic field maps for BE Cet, HN Peg, and kappa1 Cet
papers.abstract: Studying the magnetic activity of young solar analogues is important for understanding the dynamo mechanisms of the Sun and other late-type stars. We aimed to determine the surface magnetic field topology of four stars, analogues to the young Sun. This will contribute to long-term studies of the evolution of magnetic activity on different timescales of these targets. We obtained high resolution spectropolarimetric measurements with the HARPSpol instrument mounted at the ESO 3.6m telescope in the epoch 2021.6, and the SOFIN instrument, mounted on the 2.56m NOT telescope in epochs 2017.4 and 2021.5. The signal-to-noise ratio of the observations was boosted with least squares deconvolution. The surface magnetic field maps were calculated with the Zeeman-Doppler imaging technique. The magnetic field is decomposed into spherical harmonic expansions, allowing us to quantify the contributions from the axisymmetric and non-axisymmetric components, as well as the poloidal and toroidal fields. Out of the four stars observed (BE Cet, HN Peg, kappa1 Cet, V1358 Ori), three (BE Cet, HN Peg, kappa1 Cet) show clear signs of magnetic fields. Only one star, BE Cet shows clear evidence for the dominance of non-axisymmetric modes and the poloidal field being more dominant than the toroidal. HN Peg also shows signs of a stronger poloidal than a toroidal field, indicating an {\alpha}^2 dynamo, where the convective turbulence effects dominate over the differential rotation. The magnetic field of V1358 Ori could not be reliably reconstructed.

papers.title: On the relation of secondary motions to large- and very-large-scale motions
papers.abstract: The coexistence of secondary motions with large-scale and very-large-scale motions (LSMs/VLSMs) is investigated by direct numerical simulations of turbulent open-channel flow over streamwise-aligned Gaussian ridges, varying the ridge spacing $S$ and height $h$. First, the ridge height controls the secondary-motion strength and thereby the coexistence with VLSMs. VLSMs are suppressed for $h \geqslant 0.05\delta$, with $\delta$ the open-channel height, and re-emerge at $h = 0.025\delta$, where the mean secondary motions are comparable in strength to those over strip-type surfaces. Previously reported differences between strip- and ridge-type surfaces thus reflect secondary-motion strength rather than surface type. Second, proper orthogonal decomposition and conditional averaging reveal instantaneous secondary motions that span approximately $2\delta$, fill the channel height irrespective of $S$ and $h$, and are stronger than their mean. These are identified as LSMs spatially locked and amplified by the ridges. Over dense ridges, their alternation between neighbouring ridges yields weak, near-wall confined mean secondary motions, although VLSMs are suppressed over the full channel height. The ridge height thus sets the strength of the locked LSMs, whereas the ridge spacing sets where and for how long they persist. For weak locked LSMs, ridges spaced at their natural spanwise extent increase the VLSM energy, indicating that persistent locked LSMs concatenate into VLSMs. Third, large-scale instantaneous secondary motions persist over dense ridges in the absence of long streaks. This suggests that secondary motions are driven by intermittent cross-sectional motions rather than by long streaks, similar to the streak-less bursts in near-wall turbulence.

Averaging for multi-scale McKean-Vlasov equation
papers.abstract: We consider a system of Stochastic Differential Equations with two time scales, so called slow-fast system of SDEs. As customary when studying slow-fast dynamics, we seek a coarse grained description of the system, obtained, in the limit of scale separation, by 'averaging out' the fast component of the dynamics (so-called averaging limit). We study slow-fast systems where the fast variable is described by a process which is non-linear in the sense of McKean i.e. by an SDE whose coefficients depend on the law of the process itself, while the slow variable is a linear SDE (linear in the sense of McKean). We show that, when the fast variable is a McKean-Vlasov process and, additionally, the coefficients of the SDE depend on the position of the slow process, the limit of scale separation is not provided by the usual ansatz which one would expect by applying classical averaging paradigms. We identify the limit and provide complete proof.

papers.title: Understanding Users' Security, Privacy, and Trust Concerns in Healthcare AI Systems
feedback-grape: A JAX-based Python Package for GPU-Accelerated GRAPE with Feedback
papers.abstract: Modern quantum technology applications require accurate control of quantum systems, including a feedback loop in the control process. While open-loop control can be performed using well established gradient methods like GRadient Ascent Pulse Engineering (GRAPE), it was until recently unclear how to combine these with feedback from measurements, which are inherently non-differentiable. Recent work has successfully demonstrated how feedback can be incorporated into GRAPE using machine learning, resolving this issue. Following this progress, we have developed an efficient Python package implementing the method of ``feedback GRAPE''. In this hands-on tutorial, we discuss the package in detail based on concrete examples. Built on the GPU-accelerated JAX platform, our package offers a user-friendly interface inspired by the widely-used QuTiP library, including simplified treatment of multi-component systems.
