The boundary integral equation is discretised by a spectrally accurate Nyström scheme on a graded parametrisation, and the pressure jump follows from the zero-wavenumber limit of the streamwise momentum balance. A single linear system yields the full resistance matrix and pressure-jump coefficients for an eccentric cylinder; an additional right-hand side treats imposed net flux. For nonzero coefficients, comparisons with independent COMSOL finite-element simulations show relative differences below \(0.1\%\) for the resistance coefficients and at most \(0.0122\%\) for the pressure-response coefficients and excess hydraulic resistance. Reciprocity, symmetry constraints, and lubrication asymptotics provide additional checks on the numerical results. We track the coupling between rotation and translation and the pressure generated by the cylinder from the channel scale into the lubrication regime, and determine the pressure--flow relation, driving torque and efficiency of the rotating-cylinder pump for asymmetric clearances.

papers.title: What Matters for Cross-Modal Alignment
MOBO-CAPS: Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization with Cardinality-Aware Pareto Selection
MoViC: Real-Time Humanoid Whole-Body Control from Monocular Video Streams
Linearization and local controllability of nonautonomous differential inclusions
papers.abstract: In this paper we study the linearization of nonautonomous differential inclusions, whose right-hand side is integrably Lipschitz in the state variable and measurable in time. We establish measurability results for time-dependent graphs and identify the Clarke tangent cone to the set of their measurable selections in $L^\infty\times L^1$. Combining this characterization with a subtransversality argument, we obtain a lower estimate for the Clarke tangent cone to the set of all admissible trajectories starting from a fixed set. As an application, we give sufficient conditions for local controllability around a closed terminal set.

papers.title: The ordered sum-rank metric and linearized multiplicity codes: NRT meets sum-rank
Two Quintic Diophantine Equations and Fifth Powers in Fibonacci Sums at Distance Five
papers.abstract: Let $F_n$ denote the $n$th Fibonacci number. We study the Diophantine equation $$ F_{n+5}+F_n=y^5 $$ in positive integers $n$ and $y$. We prove that this equation has no solutions. The proof uses a recurrence identity to reduce the problem to the two equations $$ X^2-5Z^5=44,\qquad X^2+44=5Z^5. $$ We show that the first equation has exactly the solutions $(X,Z)=(\pm7,1)$ for $Z>0$, and that the second has no such solutions. To obtain these results, we use ideal factorization in $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{11})$ and $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-11})$ and reduce the problem to six quintic Thue equations. Their complete solution sets are computed with the Magma Online Calculator and independently verified with PARI/GP.

papers.title: Efficient AOD-Transport Compilation for Neutral-Atom Arrays
papers.abstract: Neutral-atom quantum computers execute two-qubit gates by shuttling atoms between storage and entanglement zones with acousto-optic deflectors (AODs). The efficiency of these movements determines circuit fidelity via transport overhead, idle-atom crosstalk, and atom-transfer errors. Additionally, AOD hardware constraints limit parallel atom movements, so efficient qubit placement and routing are essential. We present NEAT (Neutral-atom Efficient AOD-Transport compiler). Its transport-informed placement evaluates each decision by its incremental equivalent time, a single cost combining transport time, atom-transfer loss, and crosstalk. Its partial-progress routing allows conflicting moves to advance concurrently via intermediate waypoints. NEAT also schedules gates to maximize parallelism and uses a staggered atom array whose trap geometry preemptively avoids AOD violations without extra moves. On standard benchmark circuits, NEAT outperforms state-of-the-art (SOTA) compilers in fidelity, circuit duration, and compilation time. On scalability benchmarks of up to 1,000 qubits, it shortens circuits by 1.9x, reduces the negative log-fidelity by 1.5x, and compiles 6.6x faster than SOTA compilers on average. Overall, NEAT is a lightweight yet effective compiler for efficient and scalable neutral-atom quantum computing. The code is available at this https URL .

papers.title: Angular dependence of the low-temperature skyrmion state in Cu$_2$OSeO$_3$
papers.abstract: In the cubic chiral magnet Cu$_2$OSeO$_3$, a low-temperature skyrmion state (LTS) and a metastable tilted conical state emerge for magnetic field along $\langle 100\rangle$, both stabilized by magnetocrystalline anisotropies. We report how these states evolve when the magnetic field is rotated from $\langle 100\rangle$ via $\langle 111\rangle$ to $\langle 110\rangle$. Measurements of the magnetization and the AC susceptibility are combined with broadband microwave spectroscopy on the same cuboid sample at 5\,K. In the microwave spectra, the characteristic gigahertz excitations, notably the counterclockwise gyration mode of the skyrmions, provide a direct indicator of the character of the magnetic states and a qualitative measure of their volume fractions. Both techniques consistently show that signatures of the LTS decrease in strength under rotation and are observed only for field directions within ${\sim}20^{\circ}$ of $\langle 100\rangle$. In this range, the field values at which the skyrmions unwind remain essentially unchanged. In contrast, signatures of the tilted conical state persist up to ${\sim}40^{\circ}$, beyond which the conventional sequence of helical, conical, and field-polarized states is recovered. Thus, the tilted conical state, while being a prerequisite for the nucleation of the LTS under field sweeps, is not sufficient for its formation.

papers.title: Two-Robot Evacuation from a Unit Disk in the Segment Visibility Model
Unstable Periodic Orbit Localization in a Nonlinear System-Environment Model
papers.abstract: The role of unstable periodic orbits (UPOs) is investigated in the chaotic dynamics of a nonlinear system-environment model composed of a central two-level system coupled to an environment of two-level systems. Families of UPOs embedded in chaotic regions are identified and their local instability is characterized. Their behavior is examined under variations of the environment size, energy, and system symmetry, allowing the model to serve as a controlled testbed in which the dimensionality and dynamical conditions can be systematically modified. Characteristic UPO-based dynamical quantities are used to assess the influence of these periodic orbits on nearby chaotic trajectories, including occupation of the UPO tube, its persistence at late times, return fidelity enhancement, and recurrence timing. Across the different model variations considered, trajectories initialized close to the UPOs retain statistically detectable spatial and temporal signatures associated with the periodic orbits. These results indicate that unstable periodic orbits can retain a measurable organizing influence on surrounding chaotic trajectories across changes in dimensionality, energy, and system symmetry, giving rise to scar-like dynamical signatures in a simple nonlinear system--environment model.

papers.title: Subwavelength resonances and localization in finite resonator chains with a size defect
papers.abstract: We study subwavelength resonances of a finite chain of $N\ge2$ close-to-touching spherical resonators in three dimensions with a single radius defect of relative size $\tau\in(0,1]$ and gap width $\varepsilon$. Taking the high-contrast limit before the narrow-gap limit, we prove that the positive generalized eigenvalues of the weighted chain coupling matrix with respect to the volume matrix determine the leading relative resonant frequencies. After eliminating the finite tails, we obtain an exact characteristic determinant and identify a unique critical ratio $\tau_*\in(0,1)$ at which the largest eigenvalue crosses the upper edge of the homogeneous recurrence band $[0,4]$. For every $0<\tau<\tau_*$, exactly one eigenvalue lies above this band, and its eigenvector decays geometrically along the tails. As $\tau\to\tau_*^-$, its recurrence decay length diverges like $(\tau_*-\tau)^{-1/2}$. As $\tau\to0$, exactly one eigenvalue diverges like $\tau^{-2}$ and its eigenvector concentrates at the defect; if the defect is interior, one additional positive eigenvalue has order $\tau$. For suitably normalized relative resonant modes, the sequential limit of the $\varepsilon$-scaled gradient supremum in each gap equals the absolute difference between adjacent reduced amplitudes. For the largest-eigenvalue mode, this yields defect-adjacent gradient concentration as the defect shrinks.

papers.title: Large-Scale Cosmic-Ray Anisotropy in the TeV Regime: Peak Observables and a Propagation-Model Interpretation
papers.abstract: In recent years, cosmic-ray observations have entered a stage of high-precision measurements, but the phases of large-scale anisotropy reported by different experiments differ significantly, partly because the first harmonic cannot fully describe non-dipolar structures. In this work, we process the one-dimensional relative-intensity distributions from ARGO-YBJ, Tibet AS$\gamma$, and HAWC using a unified procedure, perform multi-harmonic fits, and reconstruct the distributions, with the global maximum of each distribution used to define the peak amplitude $A_{\max}$ and the peak right ascension $\alpha_{\max}$. The results show that, in the common energy range of 11--22~TeV covered by the three experiments, the range of the published first-harmonic phases is $22.6^\circ$, whereas the range of $\alpha_{\max}$ is reduced to $7.5^\circ$; $\alpha_{\max}$ evolves overall from $60^\circ$--$70^\circ$ at the low-energy end to $250^\circ$--$300^\circ$ at the high-energy end, while $A_{\max}$ exhibits a local minimum and $\alpha_{\max}$ changes rapidly in the phase-flip region. At the low-energy end, $\alpha_{\max}$ lies between the right-ascension projections of the direction toward the Geminga supernova remnant and the direction of the local interstellar magnetic field. Accordingly, we construct a spatially dependent propagation model that includes Galactic background sources, a Geminga-related nearby source, and anisotropic diffusion along the direction of the local interstellar magnetic field. Within a unified framework, the model reproduces the energy spectra of P, He, C, O, and Fe, as well as the energy evolution of $A_{\max}$ and $\alpha_{\max}$, providing a self-consistent explanation for the origin of large-scale anisotropy in the TeV to tens-of-TeV energy range.

papers.title: KneeFS-Net: A Lightweight Deep Learning Model for Knee Osteoarthritis Severity Assessment with Cross-Domain External Validation
Twister After Dark: Diagnosing a Damaging Nocturnal Tornado in Iloilo, Philippines (08 August 2026)
papers.abstract: (Abridge) At ~1430 UTC (2230 LST) on 08 August 2026, a significant tornado struck the Mandurriao and Jaro districts of Iloilo City, Philippines. Its parent supercell developed within the southwest monsoon enhanced by Typhoon Dolphin, under weak synoptic forcing, as a nocturnal low-level jet of ~40 kt near 1.5-3 km advected warm, moist marine air onshore. ERA5 depicted MUCAPE of ~2000 J/kg, negligible inhibition, an LCL below 300 m, and nearly purely streamwise low-level vorticity, but deep-layer shear (DLS, 0-6 km bulk wind difference) below 3 m/s. Hodographs from the newly operational Iloilo S-band dual-polarization radar (S-ILO), ~5-7 km from the storm, revealed low-level shear (LLS, 0-1 km bulk wind difference) of ~16 m/s and 0-1 km storm-relative helicity of 124-211 m^2/s^2. The storm exhibited a hook echo with a weak echo hole, a $Z_{DR}$ arc and ring, an elevated 55-60 dBZ rear-flank core consistent with a descending reflectivity core, and a ~50 dBZ ring interpreted as a debris ball. A survey of 31 damage indicators documented a ~2.9 km long and up to ~340 m wide path rated IF2 on the International Fujita Scale. Processor smoothing of the radial velocity and a $\rho_{HV}$ threshold for rainfall estimation masked any tornadic vortex or debris signature, although a radial velocity simulation shows that a narrow vortex (core radius ~50-100 m) with a rotational velocity of ~35-45 m/s could have been concealed. This case shows that significant tornadoes can develop at night during the Philippine monsoon season and that operational radar quality control should be revised to retain severe-storm signatures.

papers.title: Pulse-timing errors in exchange-only spin qubits: how one control imperfection propagates to VQE, QAOA and fault-tolerance primitives
papers.abstract: In an exchange-only (EO) spin qubit every gate is a sequence of Heisenberg exchange pulses whose only continuous parameter is the pulse area. We ask how an error in that area propagates to an algorithm's result. On up to six encoded qubits we compile VQE for H$_2$ and LiH, QAOA MaxCut, Grover search, phase estimation and a distance-3 repetition code into exchange pulses and perturb every pulse with a systematic fractional error $\varepsilon$, an offset or per-pulse jitter. For circuits whose first-order response is negligible at the threshold, the useful regime ends at $\varepsilon$ of a few $10^{-3}$: chemical accuracy is lost at $\approx6\times10^{-3}$ for both molecules and 5% of success probability between 3 and $9\times10^{-3}$ for 498-1216 pulses. A systematic error accumulates as the square of the depth and biases the answer; jitter accumulates linearly and, within statistics, does not bias phase estimation. Leakage from inter-block pulses is a third of the CNOT error, survives variational re-optimisation and a leakage-controlled entangler, and makes a leakage-blind repetition-code round worse than its uncorrected data by a factor 38-93 at $\varepsilon=10^{-2}$ in three of four compilations; in the fourth the uncorrected data already fail. The compilation moves the thresholds by a factor of two to eight. Measured over-rotation and exchange noise put devices at the edge of this regime, and with the measured 3.5 $\mu$s $T_2^*$ a quasi-static magnetic gradient limits thousand-pulse circuits unless $J/h$ reaches several hundred MHz with continuous areas, because a duration grid of 2-5% of the SWAP time starts to cost chemical accuracy. As a bit budget, a common-mode area error needs 8-10 significant bits and a 6-bit significand for the durations suffices in the tested circuits; half-precision words and picosecond timers exceed this; older devices had 6-8 bits of analog stability.

papers.title: When Zero Is Competitive: A Descriptive Pilot of Transformer and Gate-Graph Surrogates on Random-Angle Quantum Circuits
VoiceGuard: An Audio-Native LLM-VLA Pipeline for Wheelchair-Mounted Assistive Manipulation
Giant Raman Optical Activity in Chiral and Polar Ni$_3$TeO$_6$
papers.abstract: Raman optical activity (ROA) measures the difference in Raman scattering intensity for right- and left-circularly polarized light and reflects the chirality of excitations. In solids, ROA is commonly very weak. For the phonons of chiral and polar Ni$_3$TeO$_6$, we find a giant ROA with magnitude 100 times higher than commonly reported for molecules. The systematic analysis based on phonon selection rules allows the chiral and achiral scattering channels to be separated. First-principles calculations of the Raman tensor at finite phonon momentum relate the effect to the phonon modulation of the band-geometric and band-dispersion contributions to optical gyrotropy. This establishes Raman optical activity as a probe of electron--phonon modulation of the band geometry in an insulator.

papers.title: Autonomous Multi-modal Agents for ITOps Observability
Morphology-Decoupled Segmentation for Multiple Tunnel Defects Under Complex Environments
orderStatMoments: Exact Means, Variances, and Covariances of Order Statistics in R
papers.abstract: Calculating the moments, i.e., means, variances, and covariances, of the order statistics of a sample is critical, as they are foundations for order-statistics-based estimation and inference problems. In the early literature, the exact covariance matrices were tabulated only up to the sample size of 50 under normality. Recent software either provides exact calculation only for the means and variances of single order statistics, or obtains the covariances by approximations. We create the R package orderStatMoments to calculate the exact values of these moments for any ranks and any sample size. It covers thirteen built-in distribution families, specified by name and parameters as in R, and allows for continuous distributions defined by the user under relatively weak conditions. It also calculates the moments of any linear combination of order statistics, including sample quantiles, and Lloyd's best linear unbiased estimators with their variances. The work makes two contributions. First, the package provides the exact covariances between order statistics, which no software we found does. Second, we design methods based on the statistical properties of order statistics critical for ultra accurate computing at large sample sizes and various distributions. The accuracy is verified against closed forms at sample sizes up to $n = 10^6$, against the permutation identities on full matrices, and against 556 cells tabulated in seven publications, where it identified some errors far beyond the stated accuracy. A comparison with five R packages and Python's SciPy shows advantages of this package. Computing is efficient, with a time nearly independent of the sample size.

papers.title: Practice Is Not Free: Measuring the Embodied Cost of Reset-Free Robot Practice
GPROF V08: Improving Satellite Precipitation Estimates Across a Heterogeneous Constellation of Passive-Microwave Sensors
papers.abstract: Precipitation estimates from the passive microwave observations (PMW) of the Global Precipitation Measurements (GPM) mission serve a wide range of scientific, societal, and economic applications. The Goddard Profiling Algorithm (GPROF) is the operational retrieval used to produce the precipitation estimates for all GPM PMW sensors. This study presents the implementation GPROF V08 -- the most recent version of GPROF and a major update aimed at improving the accuracy of precipitation estimates from the GPM constellation. GPROF V08 replaces the conventional Bayesian scheme used by earlier GPROF versions by a convolutional neural network (CNN). The first part of this two-part study described a novel ML framework for generating synthetic observations required for training CNN retrievals for all GPM sensors. This second part describes the final, operational implementation, which adds a second finetuning stage to the this http URL from the new GPROF V08 algorithm for all principal GPM sensors are validated against reference precipitation estimates from various sources. Our results show that, while the magnitude of improvements vary by sensor and surface type, they are robust across sensors and metrics and can be as high as 40 \% for the linear correlation coefficient for precipitation estimates from SSMIS and ATMS over ocean compared to combined radar and radiometer retrievals from GPM. While some challenges remain -- such as an increased sensitivity to sensor degradation and the persistence of climatological biases, which remain of the same order as for GPROF V07 -- GPROF V08 constitutes a substantial advancement in spaceborne precipitation monitoring. Since the improvements are robust across all sensor of the constellation, the update is expected to improve the full record of GPM precipitation estimates and thus benefit a wide range of downstream datasets and applications.

papers.title: Variants of Expansivity, Shadowing and Spectral Decomposition
papers.abstract: In this paper, we first distinguish a very recently introduced notion of mean asymptotic expansivity from asymptotic expansivity. Then, we extend the spectral decomposition theorem due to Smale to bi-mean asymptotically expansive homeomorphisms with the shadowing property. We also extend a measurable spectral decomposition theorem due to Shin to shadowable measures for bi-mean asymptotically expansive homeomorphisms. Each of the chain transitive sub-systems obtained by Shin can be further decomposed into chain mixing systems by using the ideas of Richeson and Wiseman. Next, we use a probabilistic argument to recover both Smale-like and Bowen-like spectral decompositions for expansive homeomorphisms with the shadowing property. Moreover, we investigate inter-relations among several variants of the shadowing property including the eventual shadowing property, the thick shadowing property, the ergodic shadowing property, the mean ergodic shadowing property and the $M_{\alpha}$-shadowing property.

papers.title: CreaTrace: Video Creative Plagiarism Detection and Evidence Tracing
Federated Dataset Simulation: Inducing Label-Free Heterogeneity Across Tasks
Take a Step Back: A Dual-Granularity Raw Feature Empowered Intermediate Fusion Graph Convolutional Network for Multimodal Recommendation
Fano blowups of Grassmannians along sub-Grassmannians
papers.abstract: Let $\tilde X$ be the successive blowup of the Grassmannian $\operatorname{Gr}(d,n+1)$ with $n\ge3$, in arbitrary characteristic, along sub-Grassmannians of codimension $r_1,\dotsc,r_s\ge2$ that meet transversely. We prove that, if $d\ne2$, then $\tilde X$ is Fano if and only if $\sum_i(r_i-1)\le n$, and we give a similar criterion for $d=2$. As applications, we prove that the successive blowup of $\mathbb{P}^4$ along $s$ planes that meet transversely is Fano if and only if $s\le4$. We also determine when the successive blowup of a smooth quadric fourfold along planes of one family that meet transversely is Fano.

papers.title: The structure of variational autoencoder latent spaces and its consequences for representation and optimization
Boundary singularities for weak solutions of semilinear elliptic problems throughout the subcritical range
papers.abstract: Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^N$ ($N \ge 2$) be a bounded domain with smooth boundary $\partial \Omega$. We construct positive very weak solutions for the problem $\Delta u + u^p = 0$ in $\Omega$ for all $p \in [(N+1)/(N-1),(N+2)/(N-2))$ when $N \ge 3$ and for all $p \ge (N+1)/(N-1)$ when $N = 2$. These solutions vanish in a suitable trace sense on $\partial \Omega$ but are singular at prescribed isolated points. This gives a completely affirmative answer to a conjecture of del Pino-Musso-Pacard.

papers.title: Physics-Informed Fractional Load Forecasting With Memory-Aware Break Detection for Reserve Scheduling
Value and Policy Calibration from Execution Feedback for Socially Compatible Driving
RADISH: A Robust Covariate-Adaptive Trial Design with Historical Control Borrowing
papers.abstract: Incorporating historical controls into randomized clinical trials can improve statistical efficiency and alleviate enrollment challenges by reducing the need for concurrent controls, particularly when their recruitment is ethically or logistically challenging. These gains depend on comparability between the historical and concurrent controls. Many dynamic borrowing methods assess compatibility for the overall study populations and apply the same borrowing decision to every participant, even when comparability varies with participant covariates. We propose RADISH, Robust Adaptive Discrepancy-Informed Shrinkage for Historical Borrowing, a covariate-adaptive design that assesses compatibility at the individual participant level and incorporates robust borrowing into sequential randomization and final inference. Under the stated regularity conditions, the RADISH estimator is asymptotically normal and supports asymptotically valid Wald inference. Simulation studies, including semi-synthetic simulation studies based on the two real-world randomized trials, show that RADISH improves efficiency and assigns fewer participants to the control group when the historical and concurrent controls are compatible. As incompatibility increases, RADISH progressively reduces borrowing and approaches a concurrent-only design and analysis.

papers.title: DetouR: Plugging Association Routes into Search Agents for Multi-hop Question Answering
Towards GPROF V08: A Machine-Learning Framework for Simulating Passive Microwave Observations of Precipitation
Evaluating Near-Perfect Accuracy Claims in Machine-Learning-Based Leak Detection for Two-Phase Pipelines: A Condition-Blocked Audit
Darcy plume oscillations at low injection velocities
papers.abstract: We numerically investigate miscible buoyancy-driven Darcy plumes at low injection velocities. Below a critical injection velocity, the steady plume becomes unstable and develops periodic oscillations. Approaching the critical velocity, the oscillation amplitude vanishes while the frequency remains finite at the critical point, consistent with a supercritical Hopf bifurcation, whereas at lower injection velocities increasingly complex dynamics emerge. Unsteadiness also strongly enhances lateral mixing, increasing the mixing-layer thickness by a factor of approximately 2-3 compared with a steady plume. These findings reveal a previously unexplored dynamical regime of Darcy plumes with important consequences for subsurface transport and leakage.

papers.title: Diagnosis and Recovery in AI Workflows with Scarce Expert Capacity
papers.abstract: We study sequential decisions in AI workflows and other automated execution systems where failures of uncertain origin require recovery under limited shared expert capacity. Recovery choices affect future diagnostic demand, while expert availability changes which recovery actions are worthwhile. We coordinate diagnostic requests, expert dispatch, and checkpoint-based recovery to maximize expected net operating value. A finite-horizon model tracks uncertain error locations, remaining time, and shared expert capacity. Structural analysis shows how competition for diagnosis changes unaided recovery. When a full rebuild from checkpoint 0 is the best unaided fallback after failure, a larger expert pool can justify retaining more work despite a lower chance of immediate success. Capacity can also raise net operating value before fixed staffing costs while reducing diagnostic hours when advice is requested only after a failed trial. Our Diagnosis-Resource-Recovery Control (DRRC) policy coordinates these decisions through local recovery lookahead and estimates of service requirements and remaining time; its learning-augmented variant uses task-specific quality and duration estimates. In controlled simulations, larger pools draw more requests before repair, and selective diagnosis raises net value chiefly by reducing recovery costs. In a digital twin based on 177 software defects, DRRC with reference-assisted diagnosis increases mean timely completion by 3.27 percentage points and mean net value by 1.85% relative to automated recovery, although the net-value advantage remains uncertain across repositories. Expert capacity changes when workflows seek advice and how much work they preserve. Expansion may raise or lower diagnostic hours, so capacity and recovery design should be assessed jointly by their contribution to net operating value.

papers.title: All unital reversible nonsymmetric rings of order 256
papers.abstract: A ring is reversible if $ab=0$ implies $ba=0$, and symmetric if $abc=0$ implies $acb=0$. Szabo proved that the smallest order of a unital reversible nonsymmetric ring is $256$. We classify all such minimal rings: up to isomorphism there are exactly $186$ of them, $19$ of characteristic $2$ and $167$ of characteristic $4$, and there are none of characteristic $8$ or higher. All of them are local with residue field $\mathbb{F}_2$, the nilpotency index of the Jacobson radical is $4$ or $5$, and $120$ of them form $60$ pairs $R$, $R^{op}$ of non-isomorphic rings. The classification is obtained by a general method of deformation of graded algebras over $\mathbb{Z}/2^e\mathbb{Z}$, whose completeness is proved, and it is checked against the known examples: $\mathbb{F}_2Q_8$, Szabo's example and the ten rings in the family of generalized quaternion rings studied by Grau, Oller-Marcén and Szabo. The presentations of the $186$ rings and the code are provided as ancillary files.

papers.title: Concircular Sections Along Submanifolds
papers.abstract: We introduce an equation which generalises that of a concircular vector field to sections of the ambient tangent bundle along submanifolds. Totally umbilic hypersurfaces and various overdetermined systems (such as Obata's and Tashiro's equations) are obtained as specific cases. Given an ambient manifold $M$ and a connected submanifold $P$ of dimension at least $2$, the solution space $W(P;M)$ is shown to have dimension at most $\mathrm{dim } M+1$ with all solutions being of `special type' whenever it exceeds $\mathrm{codim } P+1$. This bound is shown to be sharp. When the submanifold $P$ is simply connected we show the maximum dimension is attained exactly when $P$ has constant sectional curvature $\kappa$ relative to the ambient manifold $M$. In the case of maximum dimension we introduce a bilinear form $\mathbb{I}$ on $W(P;M)$ which is Riemannian, degenerate or Lorentzian, depending on the sign of $\kappa$ and show $P$ immerses into $(W(P;M),\mathbb{I})$'s unit quadric. Hence our main result shows that whenever $P$ is simply connected, has dimension of at least $2$, and has constant curvature $\kappa\neq0$ relative to its ambient manifold $M$, there is an isometric immersion (which we construct explicitly) of $P$ with its metric induced from $M$, into the $\mathrm{dim } M$-dimensional space form of curvature $\kappa$.

papers.title: Anatomy of an Agent Harness: Decisions, Invariants and Corner Cases
Sparse Rotatable Arrays (SRAs) for Cell-Free MIMO: Network-Wide Design of Antenna Activation and Panel Orientation
Multimodal AI in Healthcare: Review of Vision-Language Foundation Models for Real-World Medical Applications
On the richness of metamaterials generated by recursive cell division
papers.abstract: Scale-rich metamaterials are one member of a family of recursive cell divisions, which differ in which cell is cut, where the cut passes and at what angle. We characterise six members of this family through three network mappings, the cell tree, the dual graph of ligaments and junctions, and the frame graph of spans, and through their elastic-wave properties: the effective refractive index n, its isotropy and the band over which it holds. The dual-graph degree law, the mean degree and the age law of the ligaments hit by new ones are the same for every rule, so they cannot distinguish the materials. The cell tree and the cell shapes do differ, and one consequence of them explains the physics: the tail of long spans in the frame graph. With the longest spans as the length scale, the bending part of the inverse squared index follows a single power law across rules, densities and numbers of ligaments, and the same spans set the lowest local resonance and the band edge. The stretching part, which caps the index, is carried by the straight frame lines of the tiling rather than by the division. Random cut angles produce elongated cells and long spans, hence high index and a narrow band; cuts perpendicular to the long axis of the cell keep the cells compact, giving low index and a wide band. Cutting through the centroid instead of a random point bounds the split fraction between 4/9 and 5/9, which removes the area hierarchy without changing the index. The cut angle interpolates continuously between these limits, and the isotropy peaks where the ligament orientations become isotropic while the cells are still compact. In three dimensions the plate and strut divisions are stretching dominated and the index stays low for every rule.

papers.title: FinVision: Multimodal AI for Visualizing Financial Narratives
Equal Dose, Different Coverage:Tracing Rate and Duration in Image Editing
Quantum teleportation with photons from remote quantum dots emitting at telecom C-band
papers.abstract: Employing quantum teleportation to increase the communication distance in quantum channels requires distinct quantum light sources, preferably operating at telecommunication wavelength. Here we utilize two semiconductor In(Ga)As quantum dots, strain engineered to emit in the telecom C-band, as sources of single- and entangled-photons, respectively. This enables a full-photonic quantum teleportation experiment, achieving a maximum teleportation fidelity of 92.7(5)%. Owing to state-of-the-art source brightness, and high time resolution, it is here possible to employ the three-photon coincidences to fully quantify the time-dependence of the process. In this way, we highlight current limitations and implement an optimization in the data-processing which leads to the maximization of achievable teleportation fidelity and coincidence rates. These results constitute a step forward in practical implementations of quantum teleportation in future fiber-based quantum networks.

papers.title: Neumann zero modes and the locality of the derivative expansion
papers.abstract: The derivative expansion (DE) provides a useful approximation to the Casimir interaction energy between two close surfaces. It has the form of a local functional, obtained from a zero momentum expansion. However, when the system involves a massless field satisfying Neumann conditions, that expansion may develop nonanalytic terms. We present here a study on how this property reflects itself in the need to add to the DE some novel, nonlocal terms. These are, we argue, akin to the ones introduced in effective theories because of the presence of massless particles in loops. We pinpoint the mode responsible for this effect, and construct the effective action due to its fluctuations, showing that it reproduces known nonanalytic contributions, and present the corresponding nonlocal addition to the DE. We also predict a new nonanalyticity: Neumann conditions in $3+1$ dimensions at zero temperature produce a term of order $|{\mathbf k}_\shortparallel |^3$, with a parameter-free coefficient, between the (local) second and fourth orders of the expansion. We show that, for a cylinder in front of a plane, the zero-mode loop adds to the local expansion a term of relative order $(L/R)^{3/2}$, with a coefficient that we compute explicitly, showing that it accounts for the behaviour of the existing numerical fits for that geometry.

papers.title: CRAFT: A Robot-Agent Harness with Scope-Aware Adaptation
Discovering Programmatic Policies from Reinforcement Learning-Based Traffic Signal Controllers
Towards a foundation model for Type IIB flux vacua
papers.abstract: Progress in characterising the Type IIB flux landscape requires scalable methods for constructing flux vacua. In this work, we investigate generative models as a framework for sampling vacua across multiple Calabi-Yau geometries and for directing searches towards specified physical properties. We compare transformers and diffusion models trained to generate quantised fluxes together with approximate values of the complex structure moduli and axio-dilaton. We exploit a staged training procedure comprising pre-training, and post-training via reinforcement learning, and assess how each stage improves the generated distributions and enables targeted sampling. We further examine whether structures learned from geometries with smaller $h^{1,2}$ can be transferred to geometries with larger $h^{1,2}$ through fine-tuning on specialised datasets. Our results provide evidence that generative models can learn distributions of flux vacua across distinct compactifications, improve searches for vacua with selected properties and transfer information between geometries. This establishes a concrete basis for developing a foundation model of the Type IIB flux landscape.

papers.title: Counting integral points of fixed degree and given height over function fields
papers.abstract: Let $k$ be a finite extension of the rational function field in one variable over a finite field, and let $\mathcal{O}_k$ be its ring of integers. Let $\overline{k}$ be an algebraic closure of $k$. For integers $e \geq 2$ and $n \geq 1$, we study the number of points in the affine space $\overline{k}^n$ whose coordinates are integral over $\mathcal{O}_k$, have absolute logarithmic Weil height equal to $m \geq 0$, and generate an extension of degree $e$ over $k$. More precisely, we derive an asymptotic formula for this quantity as $m \rightarrow \infty$ whenever $n > e$, except in the cases $(n,e)\in \{(3,2),(4,3),(5,4)\}$. When $k$ is the rational function field, however, we use Weierstrass semigroups to obtain asymptotic formulas for the cases $(n,e)\in \{(1,2),(2,2),(3,2)\}$, thereby completing the picture in the setting $e=2$. As an application, we also derive asymptotic estimates for the number of certain decomposable forms with coefficients in $\mathcal{O}_k$.

papers.title: Finite sums of weighted composition operators on the Fock space
papers.abstract: We study finite sums of weighted composition operators on the classical Fock space. We show that no cancellation phenomenon occurs when the composition symbols are pairwise distinct: such a sum is bounded, compact, or belongs to the Schatten class S_p, 0<p<\infty, if and only if each summand has the corresponding property. We also obtain two-sided essential norm estimates and quantitative Schatten norm comparisons for fixed distinct nonconstant symbols. As an application, we obtain corresponding boundedness, compactness, and Schatten-class results for finite sums of generalized Volterra-type integral operators.

papers.title: Multi-year forecasting of F10.7 and F30 solar radio flux using an adaptive Kalman filter and hemispheric solar activity
papers.abstract: The F10.7 and F30 radio flux indices drive thermospheric and radiation-environment models, and long-term predictions are needed for satellite mission planning, orbital-lifetime estimates, and re-entry assessments. We develop multi-year predictions of both indices for lead times of 1 to 84 months using three complementary contributions. First, we apply the McNish-Lincoln (M&L) method and demonstrate its predictive skill over multi-year horizons, with RMSE of 11-22 sfu for F10.7 and 7-14 sfu for F30. RMSE largely stabilizes after roughly 36 months, indicating near-constant forecast skill over the seven-year horizon. Accuracy also depends strongly on the solar-cycle phase at which the forecast is issued, with the most favorable starting intervals occurring progressively earlier in the cycle for longer lead times. Second, we update the initial predictions using an adaptive Kalman filter with noise statistics identification, which assimilates the latest monthly observations to reconstruct the current smoothed flux, remove the delay introduced by centered smoothing, and improve solar-cycle state estimation, reducing forecast errors by up to 70%. Third, we introduce synthetic hemispheric components of solar radio flux to account for the separate evolution of the northern and southern hemispheres, and incorporate them into a hemispheric M&L formulation. Compared with the initial M&L predictions, it reduces RMSE by up to 55% for F10.7 and 58% for F30, showing that hemispheric asymmetry contains predictive information lost in the full-disk index. These results extend solar-cycle forecasting to multi-year timescales relevant for long-term space-weather applications and operational planning.

papers.title: CoSyDelay: Cognitive Symbolic Regression for Traffic Delay Estimation
A new formula for Moore-Penrose inverses of rank-deficient Toeplitz matrices
Exhaustive Evaluation of Fixed-Point Reciprocal Architectures for FPGAs
Character variety of the punctured sphere and the determinantal variety
papers.abstract: We show that the SL(2;C) character variety of the n-punctured sphere is described via the determinantal variety defined by an n x n symmetric matrix of rank at most 4 whose entries are the traces of simple closed curves on the surface. This result generalizes the Fricke-Klein-Vogt relations to arbitrary n, and we determine the structure of the kernel of the associated matrix.

papers.title: How ready is the United States commercial building stock for artificial intelligence? A national estimate from energy codes and survey data
Magnetic control of hydrodynamic spin coupling between rotors: Ferrohydrodynamic effects in the two-rotor problem
authors: Efstratios E. Tzirtzilakis (University of the Peloponnese
papers.abstract: The hydrodynamic spin coupling between two rotors ("fluid gears") is investigated numerically for a magnetic fluid in non-uniform magnetic fields. An active cylinder drives a torque-free passive one inside a circular corral, with one rotor heated. The model combines magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) and ferrohydrodynamics (FHD), with the full Kelvin force and temperature-dependent Langevin magnetisation. For the oil-based ferrofluid EFH1 the Lorentz force is negligible, and the Kelvin force drives thermomagnetic convection from the heated rotor. Steady torque-free states are computed with Taylor-Hood finite elements, the gear ratio $\Gamma$ being an additional unknown. Without a field the results agree within 1-8% with published planar simulations up to $\mathrm{Re}\approx 50$. About 17,000 steady states cover 34 arrangements of wires, NdFeB rods and magnet cores, gaps $G=0.1$-$0.7$, $\mathrm{Re}=10$-$40$ and heating of 5-20 K. Because the coupling is weak, fields of 1-2 mT change $\Gamma$ by an amount comparable to $\Gamma$ itself. At 2 mT it is reversed, strengthened or weakened in nine cases out of ten. The outcome is set by the source position: at the experimental gap and $\mathrm{Re}=20$ a source below the corral or behind the active rotor strengthens the gear-like counter-rotation up to 2.7-fold, and a source above the corral reverses it into belt-like corotation. Several sources do not act additively, and a magnet core inside the active rotor raises $|\Gamma|$ at small gaps to seven times the largest hydrodynamic value. At fixed geometry and Reynolds number, field strength and heating act approximately through a single thermomagnetic source parameter.

papers.title: Strong Standard Completeness of a Hypersequent Calculus for Cyclic Involutive Residuated Lattices
papers.abstract: We present a hypersequent calculus $H_R$ for cyclic involutive residuated lattices and prove strong standard completeness for arbitrary theories in a fixed countable propositional language. Standard models are chains on $[0,1]$; neither commutativity nor equality of the monoid unit and the dualizing constant is assumed. The chain semantics is the class $K_R$ defined by unit cyclicity and all ordered finite-history conditions. Every countable member of $K_R$ embeds into a standard chain preserving the entire signature. The construction combines central-support reconstruction, gap insertion and relative contraction. A relative comparison construction supplies the required chain countermodels. We also prove admissibility of the unrestricted density rule for theoremhood and effective elimination from finite proofs without additional assumption leaves. Elimination uses terminating enumeration of density-free proofs; ordinary Cut is retained, and no complexity bound is claimed. Further constructions give bounded standard embeddings for nontrivial countable chains of involutive uninorm logic and pseudo-uninorm logic with weak commutativity. Using ordinary chain completeness for arbitrary theories, these yield strong standard completeness for both logics. A companion Lean~4 development formalizes the main results, with its scope and external inputs stated explicitly.

papers.title: Two-Stage Prompt Learning: A Unified Framework for Person ReID without Clothing Hypothesis
Geomagnetic Q-Response Inversion as a Calderón-Type Inverse Boundary Value Problem
papers.abstract: Whether electrical conductivity can be uniquely determined from magnetic measurements alone is a fundamental question in geomagnetic induction sounding. For a spherical conductor in the magnetoquasistatic model, we establish an equivalence between the complete Q-response and a restricted magnetic boundary operator, connecting geomagnetic induction to Calderon-type inverse boundary value theory. For axisymmetric conductivities, we derive exact representations of the zero-frequency zonal response derivatives as conductivity-weighted spatial moments. These formulas give an explicit interpretation of individual response derivatives, and completeness of the moment family yields conductivity uniqueness. For layered axisymmetric models with known shell interfaces and piecewise-constant radial dependence, we further establish uniqueness at a single nonzero frequency. Finite-dimensional subclasses also admit uniqueness and stability estimates from finitely many response coefficients at sufficiently low nonzero frequencies. These results identify complementary mechanisms for conductivity recovery from magnetic-only observations, while uniqueness for general three-dimensional scalar conductivities from ideal magnetic-only Q-response data remains unresolved.

papers.title: AllocFlow: End-to-End Portfolio Trading Action Generation from Raw Market Data
Far-field prediction of algebraic curves via generalized asymptotes
papers.abstract: The asymptotic behavior of algebraic curves is classically described by means of linear asymptotes. However, many infinite branches exhibit a non-linear behavior that cannot be represented accurately by straight lines. In this paper we propose a computational framework for far-field prediction of algebraic curves based on generalized asymptotes. Starting from the asymptotic expansion of a real branch at infinity, we retain its non-decaying terms in order to construct an algebraic surrogate, which is then used as an adaptive far-field model outside a sufficiently large compact region. We introduce explicit discrepancy indicators and a switching radius that determine when the exact branch may be replaced by its generalized asymptotic predictor. The framework recovers the classical linear asymptote whenever the latter exists, while remaining effective for branches with polynomial or Puiseux-type dominant behavior. In the implicit setting, we prove algebraicity and compatibility properties of the predictor and derive asymptotic error estimates from the first neglected term of the expansion. A residual certificate distinguishes guaranteed finite-tail replacement from asymptotic radius estimates. Tangential tails, slow decay, and a smooth transition rule clarify the limitations of truncation. Reproducible finite-window tests compare the predictors with fitted polynomial baselines; these tests are not a benchmark of a complete plotting system.

papers.title: Quasinormal Modes and Environmental Trapping around Charged Letelier Black Holes with Perfect-Fluid Dark Matter and Quintessence
papers.abstract: We compute the massless scalar quasinormal spectra of charged Letelier black holes surrounded by logarithmic perfect fluid dark matter (PFDM) and quintessence, for $\Lambda=0$ and for asymptotically anti-de Sitter (AdS) spacetimes, together with the test Maxwell spectra for $\Lambda=0$. For $\Lambda=0$, sixth order WKB values with Padé resummation agree with independent time domain evolutions to within $0.06\%$ for the fundamental modes. Stronger string cloud and quintessence lower both the oscillation frequencies and the damping rates, while a larger charge or a larger positive PFDM parameter $\beta$ raises both. In our convention $\beta>0$ means negative PFDM energy density; negative $\beta$ gives a positive density and reverses the shift. The angular frequency and Lyapunov exponent of the unstable circular null orbit reproduce the eikonal trends and approximate the $\ell=2$ WKB frequencies at the percent level. For $\Lambda<0$ the scalar potential diverges at the AdS boundary and the single barrier WKB formula does not apply. We therefore solve the eigenvalue problem with a Chebyshev pseudospectral method in ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein coordinates, with regularity at the horizon and a Dirichlet condition at the boundary, and check the modes against time domain evolutions and Schwarzschild-AdS benchmarks. The AdS spectrum contains long-lived modes trapped between the photon sphere barrier and the reflecting boundary, with damping rates spanning about five orders of magnitude. The damping correlates with the ratio of the oscillation frequency to the barrier top frequency, consistent with leakage through the barrier. No growing modes are found in the test field sectors and parameter ranges studied, which does not establish the stability of the fully coupled system.

papers.title: Calabi flow in the controlled Kähler cone
papers.abstract: We prove that the geometric limit of a global Calabi flow in a real class of the controlled Kähler cone is independent of the initial metric. Under cohomological K-polystability, the limit is a smooth cscK metric in the original class and complex structure. We also establish varying-class closedness and an equivariant continuity method. We apply this method to construct a smoothly varying family of cscK metrics throughout an explicit interval of symmetric real Kähler classes on the blow-up of the projective plane at four points in general position.

papers.title: SAGE-VQA: A Training-Free, Self-Evolving Agentic Framework with Grounded Evidence for Knowledge-Based Visual Question Answering
From Companion to Guardian: Designing an Emergency Support System Using a Quadruped Robot for Older Adults
Does synthetic pre-training pay off on a microcontroller? Accuracy, latency and energy across two MCUs
Subarchetypal Analysis: A Semi-Supervised Framework for Archetypal Analysis
papers.abstract: In this work, we introduce subarchetypal analysis, a new semi-supervised framework for Archetype Analysis (AA) and Archetypoid Analysis (ADA) based on subsets of observations from which archetypal profiles are generated. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first subset-constrained framework for archetypal analysis. Classical AA and ADA are recovered as special cases, and the location result for archetypes is extended to the proposed framework. The generating subsets may be defined a priori by the user to incorporate external knowledge, or determined from intrinsic properties of the data or the underlying problem structure. As an illustration of the latter, we consider efficient subarchetypes within Data Envelopment Analysis, where the subsets are determined by the geometry of the efficient frontier. We develop and implement algorithms for subarchetypal analysis in both multivariate and functional settings, available in an R package. The proposed methods are compared with constrained clustering, group-wise archetypal analysis, and classical unconstrained AA and ADA, and their practical usefulness is demonstrated through applications to business, sports analytics, and human development data.

papers.title: Spectral Moments of the Projected Hubbard Configuration Graph: Connectivity, Exchange, and Virtual Doublons
papers.abstract: At strong on-site repulsion, the lowest band of $n$ lattice fermions is the spectrum of the hopping projected onto configurations without double occupancy, $H_\infty=P_0H_tP_0$. We study its moments, for few fermions in the square-lattice Hubbard model and, where the arguments allow, on any finite graph. (1) For spin-independent Hermitian hopping (no on-site terms) on any $N\geq2$-site graph, $\mu_2=\frac{n(N-n)}{N(N-1)}\sum_{i\neq j}|t_{ij}|^2$, for any spin composition. (2) On any finite graph, $\mu_4$ is exactly linear in the same-spin pair count, as four hops permute particles by at most a transposition or 3-cycle; for uniform hopping on a simple graph with $N\geq4$ the slope is $\alpha(N,n)=-8C_4(N-n)(8N-11n-2)/[N(N-1)(N-2)(N-3)]$, fixed by the number $C_4$ of 4-cycles. (3) At large finite $U$, the second-order Schrieffer-Wolff correction is Hilbert-Schmidt orthogonal to $H_\infty$ on every triangle-free graph, so the band variance has no $1/U$ term; its $U^{-2}$ coefficient, an exact trace checked by exact diagonalization, is negative at the low fillings computed. (4) Under a Peierls flux, the exchange slope $\alpha(N,2,\Phi)=-\frac{64}{N-1}\cos\Phi_\square$ ($L\times L$ tori, $L=3$ or $L\geq5$) carries the ordinary charge-$e$ harmonic, while the doublon (bound-pair) hopping acquires a doubled phase, $t_de^{2iA_{ij}}$: the second-order single-doublon Hamiltonian is exactly $\pi$-periodic ($h/2e$) under a boundary twist, and the exact two-electron U-band follows numerically, up to $O((2\lambda)^L/U^{L-1})$. Result (1), the permutation bound, the orthogonality in (3) and the doubled phase are machine-checked in Lean 4. Repulsive binding and the pair charge $2e$ are known; new are the exact moment structure and the derivation of the doubled phase. We make no claim about many-pair phase stiffness, off-diagonal long-range order or superconductivity.

papers.title: Characterisation of first passage locations for two-dimensional lattice random walks
papers.abstract: Consider a diagonal random walk $(X_n,Y_n)$ on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ with transition probabilities depending only on the second coordinate. We characterise the distributions of first passage locations, $X(\tau_a)$, where $\tau_a$ is the first time $Y_n$ reaches level $a$. We obtain a necessary and sufficient condition for a given distribution to be realised as a rescaled first passage location from some starting level. The proof extends Bondesson's method for one-dimensional first passage times. It combines a transformation of generating functions based on Pick functions with a construction using barriers. We also study maximal representations of generating functions of first passage locations and show that analogous converse results for standard and honeycomb random walks require additional restrictions.

papers.title: Deterministic preparation of squeezed Schrödinger cat states with arbitrary size and squeezing
papers.abstract: We introduce a scheme for the deterministic preparation of squeezed Schrödinger cat states based on reservoir engineering. Our proposal relies on the linear and quadratic coupling of an oscillator mode to an auxiliary mode that decays into a vacuum reservoir. For suitable couplings, we show that the system unconditionally relaxes into a pure steady state. We derive an analytical expression for the steady state in terms of the coupling constants, and show that it corresponds to a displaced and squeezed finite superposition of Fock states. Numerical simulations further confirms that this state is reached with unit fidelity from a thermal initial state, without measurement, feedback or post-selection. Additionally, we derive analytical expressions for the non-Gaussianity and the Wigner function of the steady state. Our results reveal that states exhibiting maximal non-Gaussianity are excellent approximations of squeezed Schrödinger cat states, with fidelities exceeding $0.996$. The optimal squeezing stays close to 3dB, while the squared cat size scales proportionally with the highest Fock state occupation number in the finite superposition of the steady state. These maximally non-Gaussian states also maximise the Wigner logarithmic negativity. Finally, by selecting the appropriate ratios of the couplings, our scheme can generate cat states subject to arbitrary squeezing and displacement.

papers.title: A Demonstration System for Faithful Temporal Question Answering
Learning When to Continue and When to Stop: Termination-Aware OPSD
Count Constraints and Conditional Benchmarks for Roster-Based Network Reconstruction
papers.abstract: When everyone reports contact counts for known groups, roster-based aggregated relational data (ARD) can determine individual links. In our sparse circular design with 40 nodes and eight groups, the complete counts fix 35.6% of realized edges on average. Zero counts alone exclude 91.1% of nonedges on average, and the full set of counts raises that share to 91.7%. We assess ranking on the unresolved pairs by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Uniform weighting of compatible graphs yields higher mean AUC than the direct scores from either a circular latent-position fit or a nuclear-norm fit. In a follow-up analysis, using the same fitted probabilities to weight compatible graphs reverses the comparison for the circular fit. With the generating circular form and interaction strength supplied, its mean AUC exceeds uniform by 0.016-0.019 across three paired density settings. The gain is 0.007 under a stochastic blockmodel, where the circular form is misspecified. Nuclear-norm plug-in scores remain below uniform in mean AUC. For independent Bernoulli edges with fixed probabilities strictly between zero and one, we characterize when an oracle using the true probabilities gives the same edge marginals as uniform weighting for every feasible count array. This occurs exactly when the conditional graph law is uniform on every such array, or equivalently when log odds are additive in node-by-group effects. We recommend reporting fixed edge states, ranking on unresolved pairs, and generating-probability error separately.

papers.title: Bowed-String-Mechanism-Inspired Quantum Dissociation Control of Molecules
papers.abstract: Inspired by Guettler's mechanics of accelerating Helmholtz motion, we present a predictive laser pulse-shaping strategy to rapidly initiate the multiphoton dissociation of vibrationally excited diatomic molecules. In intense infrared fields, NO molecules often exhibit unpredictable control windows due to the chaotic fragmentation of intensity thresholds. By incorporating a bowing-analogue transient shaper enforced by a boundary-matching constraint with symmetric derivative slope transitions and vanishing initial boundary conditions ($T(0) = 0, T'(0) = 0$), we demonstrate that a pulse engineered with non-linear front-flank acceleration reduces the multi-valued threshold topology into a single, predictable linear dissociation corridor. Wigner quasiprobability distributions confirm that this temporal acceleration trajectory opens cantori bottlenecks and suppresses wave-packet fragmentation, restricting the quantum non-classicality index to $M_{\text{nc}} \le 0.15$. Our simulations verify that this trajectory engineering preserves wave-packet localization and maintains high dissociation yields ($P_{\text{diss}} > 0.95$) even under Markovian thermal dephasing ($\delta/\omega_0 = 10^{-4}$) and frozen rotational variations up to $J = 5$. Comparison with contemporary ultrafast spectral phase modulation protocols demonstrates that conventional smooth pulse envelopes, despite advanced phase-chirping, exhibit limitations in restricting non-hyperbolic cantori stickiness due to insufficient sub-picosecond acceleration. In contrast, our boundary-constrained shaper enforces a deterministic, single-valued dissociation corridor under equivalent few-picosecond control windows.

papers.title: Lao Siji: Adapting openpilot to Closed-Loop End-to-End Driving in Neural Reconstruction
Wideband Hybrid Beamforming via Programmable Unitary Mixer--TTD RF Networks
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a wideband hybrid beamforming architecture whose analog front-end consists of fixed unitary mixers interlaced with programmable diagonal phase-shift/true-time-delay (TTD) layers. Under ideal passive-component assumptions, the analog beamformer is semi-unitary on every OFDM subcarrier, so the injected RF-chain power reaches the antenna ports without analog-network loss. We design the phase shifts and delays of the programmable diagonal phase-shift/TTD layers for OFDM sum-rate maximization. Numerical results show that increasing mixer--TTD depth improves the sum rate under ideal component assumptions and a common injected RF-power budget. With component losses included, a shallow design retains an advantage over the evaluated hybrid baselines at low-to-moderate powers, motivating deeper implementations with low accumulated loss.

papers.title: Quantum Gromov--Hausdorff Convergence of Spectral Truncations for Amenable Discrete Quantum Groups with Modified Rapid Decay
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be an amenable discrete quantum group with the modified rapid decay property relative to a proper central length $\ell$. We construct a modularly corrected commutator seminorm on $C_r^*(G)$ and prove its right invariance. Averaging over the coproduct yields a regular bi-invariant Lip-norm. For the spectral projections $P_R=\chi_{[0,R]}(D_\ell)$, we equip the finite-dimensional operator systems $A_R=P_RC_r^*(G)P_R$ with the Lip-norms induced by the compressed left and right coactions. We prove quantum Gromov--Hausdorff convergence and obtain an explicit approximation estimate. These spectral compressions are length-filtered Peter--Weyl truncations of the compact dual. The resulting regular bi-invariant Lip-norm also places the family within Leimbach's operator Gromov--Hausdorff convergence theorem. The construction applies to non-unimodular discrete quantum groups, including discrete duals of standard deformations of compact semisimple Lie groups.

papers.title: Schatten isometries of Grassmann spaces
papers.abstract: We characterize all (not necessarily surjective) Schatten $p$-isometries of the Grassmann space of rank $k$ projections on a complex Hilbert space for every $p\in(0,\infty]$. We prove that every such isometry is induced by a linear or conjugate-linear isometry of the underlying Hilbert space $\mathcal H$, with the additional possibility of composition with orthocomplementation when $\dim \mathcal H = 2k > 2$. Our result generalizes Wigner's theorem, which plays a central role in the mathematical foundations of quantum mechanics. It also extends previous results on Schatten $p$-isometries of Grassmann spaces, including characterizations of surjective isometries by Gehér and Šemrl for $p=\infty$ and by Qian et al. for $0<p<\infty$ and that of not necessarily surjective isometries by Gehér for $p=2$.

papers.title: A hybrid log-likelihood-ratio statistic for single-detector SPIIR gravitational-wave searches
papers.abstract: Periods with only one detector operating accounted for 13.3 percent of the third LIGO-Virgo observing run (O3) and 29.7 percent of the first part of the fourth observing run (O4a). We present the first dedicated single-detector implementation of the Summed Parallel Infinite Impulse Response (SPIIR) pipeline for binary neutron star (BNS) and neutron star-black hole (NSBH) merger searches. Our hybrid log-likelihood ratio combines signal-consistency models for non-Gaussian glitches with a profile likelihood ratio for the signal-to-noise ratio under a Gaussian-noise model. We calibrate the glitch model by source category and trigger-rate class. We assign false alarm rates (FARs) using the measured background from the same detector and analysis chunk, extrapolating its high-ranking tail. We check the FAR assignments by comparing observed and expected cumulative background counts for BNS in O3a and NSBH in O3b at LIGO Hanford (H1) and LIGO Livingston (L1). Using O3 data and the GWTC-3 injection set, we find that, at a threshold of one false alarm per two months, the BNS sensitive distances are $136.5^{+2.9}_{-3.0}$ Mpc in L1 and $120.2^{+3.1}_{-3.3}$ Mpc in H1. These central estimates are approximately 24 and 38 percent higher, respectively, than the GWTC-3 GstLAL values of $110.5^{+3.2}_{-3.4}$ Mpc and $87.2^{+3.6}_{-3.9}$ Mpc over the same data and injection parameter ranges. GstLAL provides the only published single-detector results in GWTC-3. For NSBH, SPIIR reaches $164.1^{+6.7}_{-7.3}$ Mpc in L1 and $134.9^{+6.3}_{-7.0}$ Mpc in H1, compared with $165.1^{+6.7}_{-7.3}$ Mpc and $156.0^{+5.9}_{-6.4}$ Mpc for GWTC-3 GstLAL, respectively. Targeted searches recover triggers associated with GW190425, GW200105_162426, and GW230529_181500 with assigned FARs below the same threshold.

papers.title: Delayed Heuristic-Behavior-Target Coupling for Off-Policy Reinforcement Learning in Inventory Control
Basic introduction to Freidlin-Wentzell theory
papers.abstract: Freidlin-Wentzell theory provides the quantitative foundation for rare, noise-induced transitions in stochastic dynamical systems, predicting optimal transition pathways, the exponential scaling of mean escape times, and the long-term occupancy of competing attractors in metastable systems. Here we present a pedagogical, physics-oriented review built around a unified Hamiltonian framework: starting from the infinitesimal generator of a continuous-time Markov process, we derive the local Hamiltonian, obtain the Lagrangian and action functional via Legendre-Fenchel duality, and construct the quasi-potential landscape. We apply this streamlined formalism across weak-noise diffusions, Markov jump processes, weakly interacting particle ensembles, and nonequilibrium stochastic fields, alongside exact conditions for macroscopic coarse-graining. Along the way, we highlight how broken detailed balance drives forward and reverse transition paths apart, explain where local linear stability and Gaussian approximations break down, and assemble multi-attractor landscapes using combinatorial $W$-graphs. Finally, we bridge the analytical theory to modern numerical solvers, including ordered upwind methods, geometric minimum action algorithms, and neural-network parameterizations, and provide an accompanying GPU-accelerated Python package.

papers.title: CHERI under Fault Injection: An Emulation-Based Security Evaluation of Capability Hardware Enhanced RISC Instructions
Uniqueness of invariant measures for mean-field stochastic damped wave and heat equations
papers.abstract: We study invariant measures for a Wick-renormalized mean-field stochastic damped wave equation on the two-dimensional torus and for the corresponding stochastic heat equation. With Wick ordering relative to the massive Gaussian free field with covariance $(1-\Delta)^{-1}$, we prove uniqueness among invariant laws whose renormalized second moment belongs to $H^{-\sigma}(\mathbb T^2)$, where $0<\sigma<\tfrac12$. Stationarity reduces the mean-field equation to a linear equation with a deterministic distribution-valued potential. We show that self-consistency forces this deterministic potential to vanish. The damped wave equation therefore has invariant law $\mathcal N(0,(1-\Delta)^{-1})\otimes\mathcal N(0,\varepsilon^{-2}I)$, with covariance understood distributionally, while the heat equation has the Gaussian free field as its invariant law. This resolves self-consistency for spatially varying distribution-valued potentials and establishes uniqueness in the specified class. As the inertia parameter tends to zero, the position marginal remains equal to the invariant law of the corresponding stochastic heat equation, whereas the velocity marginal assigns vanishing probability to every bounded subset of $H^{-1-\sigma}(\mathbb T^2)$, establishing Smoluchowski-Kramers type behavior.

papers.title: The Vocabulary Tax: Safely Trimming Unused Tokens from LLMs for On-Device Use
AgenticJevNav: Agentic Object Search and Navigation via Event-Driven Verification
"Don't Leave the Task Unfinished": Persistence-Driven Violations under Quiet Oversight
Chirality-polarized superradiance induced by quantized orbital-angular-momentum transfer in a ring cavity
papers.abstract: We investigate a spin-$1/2$ Bose-Einstein condensate coupled to two counterpropagating modes of an optical ring cavity and driven by Laguerre-Gaussian Raman beams carrying quantized orbital angular momentum (OAM). We demonstrate that competition between OAM-selective Raman scattering channels controls collective superradiance through self-consistent atom--cavity feedback, linking atomic orbital motion to cavity-chirality selection. For unequal OAM transfer, one cavity mode dominates the superradiant response, with its chirality switchable by the Raman pump strengths. In contrast, equal OAM transfer allows both counterpropagating modes to coexist. The resulting chirality-polarized phases support distinct vortex and vortex--antivortex configurations with reconstructed synthetic gauge-field textures. Remarkably, contact interactions can reshape the vortex topology without changing the dominant cavity chirality, revealing distinct responses of atomic and photonic degrees of freedom. The predicted mode switching and vortex ordering can be probed through cavity output and spin-resolved imaging in a proposed $^{87}$Rb implementation. Our results establish quantized OAM transfer as a mechanism for controlling collective cavity emission beyond conventional atomic SOAMC.

papers.title: Variance Stable Gaussian Smoothing Estimator for Arbitrary High-order Derivatives
The maximum length of a Hamiltonian path in the grid graph $P_m \times P_n$
papers.abstract: Label the $mn$ vertices of the grid graph $P_m \times P_n$ bijectively by $1, \dots, mn$ and read the labels in increasing order; this produces a Hamiltonian path whose length in the Manhattan metric is denoted $M(P_m \times P_n)$. McNeil conjectured, on the basis of computer evidence, that $M(P_n \times P_n) = n^3 - 3$ for even $n$ and $n^3 - n - 1$ for odd $n$. Fried recently determined $M(P_m \times P_n)$ up to an additive error of one. We determine it exactly, which settles McNeil's conjecture. The proof rests on the cut-counting bound for multisets. Fried states that bound for multiplicities at least two; we give a form valid for every multiplicity, with a correction term that is invisible in the planar case but not in higher dimensions.

papers.title: A remark on the entropy numbers of mixed smoothness classes
papers.abstract: We find the right orders of both the entropy numbers and the Kolmogorov widths of classes of multivariate functions with bounded mixed derivative, when the class is defined by the restriction in the uniform norm and the error of approximation is measured in the uniform norm. The case of functions of two variables was settled about 30 years ago and the case of three or more variables stayed open.

papers.title: Magnetic fields in blazar jets derived from synchrotron self-absorption
papers.abstract: Context. Magnetic fields are believed to play a crucial role in the launching, acceleration, and evolution of blazar jets. However, direct measurements of the magnetic field strength in the radio-emitting regions of blazar jets remain limited. Aims. We aim to estimate the magnetic field strengths in the synchrotron self-absorption (SSA) regions of blazar jets and investigate their connections with the properties of the jet and central engine. Methods. We compiled multifrequency radio data for 143 blazars and fitted their radio spectra with a combined power-law and SSA model to derive the turnover frequency and turnover flux density. The magnetic field strengths were then calculated by combining the SSA parameters with the very long baseline interferometry (VLBI) measured angular sizes and Doppler factors compiled from the literature. Results. The SSA-derived magnetic fields are systematically lower than those obtained from broadband spectral energy distribution modeling, suggesting that the two methods probe different regions of the jet. We further investigated the correlations between the SSA magnetic field strength and the apparent knot speed, {\gamma}-ray luminosity, black hole mass, and accretion disk luminosity. Only a weak correlation is found between the SSA magnetic field strength and {\gamma}-ray luminosity, while the best-fit relations with the other investigated parameters also exhibit negative slopes, suggesting a common tendency that is qualitatively consistent with magnetic energy being progressively converted into bulk kinetic energy during jet propagation. Conclusions. Our work presents a large statistical studies of SSA-derived magnetic fields in blazars and provides new observational constraints on the magnetic evolution of relativistic jets.

papers.title: HEmIF-Bench: Benchmarking H&E-to-mIF Models BeyondVirtual-StainFidelity
DiffWAM: Learning World Action Model from Consecutive Visual Difference
Dynamic Spatio-Temporal Graph Attention Networks with Nested Clustered Optimization for Multi-Asset Portfolios
A simple proof of the characterization of $\ell_\infty^n$ by norm-one projections and a stability estimate
papers.abstract: We give a short and elementary proof of a classical fact that an $n$-dimensional real or complex normed space with the absolute projection constant equal to one is linearly isometric to $\ell_\infty^n$. The proof uses only finite-dimensional convexity and linear algebra, with no infinite-dimensional ingredients. The same approach yields a quantitative stability estimate of order $\varepsilon^{\frac{1}{3}}$ when the absolute projection constant is at most $1+\varepsilon$. This improves Zippin's estimate of order $\varepsilon^{\frac{1}{8}}$ in each fixed dimension as $\varepsilon \to 0$. The real and complex cases are treated by the same arguments.

papers.title: Remember, Replay, Adapt: Learning from Past Experience in Online Vision-and-Language Navigation
Attribute or Abstain: Evaluating Evidence-Grounded Retrieval on the Low-Resource African Business Web
Towards the LSST DESC pipeline for cosmology with galaxy clusters -- design and validation on simulations
papers.abstract: We present the current implementation of an automated framework developed within the Legacy Survey of Space and Time Dark Energy Science Collaboration (LSST DESC) for galaxy cluster cosmology, in preparation for the first LSST data releases of the NSF-DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory. The cluster cosmology pipeline integrates DESC-developed tools dedicated to galaxy/cluster catalog ingestion, cluster number count and weak lensing measurements, modeling, and parameter inference through posterior sampling, enabling reproducible end-to-end cluster cosmology analyses. We test and validate the pipeline using synthetic mock datasets and the LSST DESC cosmoDC2 simulation, performing a joint analysis of redMaPPer cluster abundance and stacked weak lensing profiles measured in bins of redshift and richness. We constrain two cosmological parameters, $\Omega_c$ and $\sigma_8$, along with six cluster mass-observable relation parameters. Our baseline analysis recovers the fiducial cosmoDC2 values of $\Omega_c$ and $\sigma_8$ within $0.51\sigma$ and $0.34\sigma$, respectively. We also showcase the flexibility of the overall pipeline by assessing the impact of fiducial cosmology and alternative modeling prescriptions on the parameter constraints. Lastly, we also discuss the current limitations of the pipeline and the developments needed for LSST data.

papers.title: Minimal sets of countable group actions on regular curves
papers.abstract: We study minimal sets of countable groups acting by homeomorphisms on regular curves. If the ambient action has a finite orbit, every infinite minimal set is an equicontinuous Cantor system. If there is no finite orbit, the minimal set is unique and remains minimal for every finite-index subgroup. A minimal set supporting an invariant probability is a finite orbit, an equicontinuous Cantor system, a circle isometry action, or a Cantor extension obtained by splitting a countable invariant subset of such a circle. Without an invariant probability, infinitely many nondegenerate components can occur. Their homeomorphism types determine the underlying space, and every nonempty countable family of types is realized. The two-generator free group admits an example with arc components on a dendrite, whereas its restricted wreath product with the integers admits none on any regular curve.

papers.title: HIVE-ECIA: Identity-Aware Historical Evidence Acquisition for Bandwidth-Efficient Multi-Object Tracking
LoopSkim: Lossless Multi-Depth Speculative Decoding for Looped Language Models
Diagonal and Fine Tower Dimensions for Minimal Circle Homeomorphisms and Product Actions
papers.abstract: We study minimal circle homeomorphisms and their products with Cantor systems, and show that these actions have diagonal dimension at most two and fine tower dimension at least two. Consequently, diagonal dimension, fine tower dimension, and tower dimension are all equal to two for minimal circle homeomorphisms. We also obtain a strict separation between tower dimension and fine tower dimension on a one-dimensional space.

papers.title: EasyNav: A Modular Architecture for Real-Time Navigation Across Heterogeneous Robot Environments
Restoring Fair Hrtick Re-arming After Same-Task Repicks in the Linux EEVDF Scheduler
Frege's logic in Grundgesetze is nonclassical
papers.abstract: I show that the axioms and rules of inference about the horizontal in the subsystem of Grundgesetze without value-ranges fail to capture its intended interpretation. That is, I build a nonstandard model in which $-a$ is the true iff $a$ is not the false, thereby confirming a conjecture made by Landini that $a \to (-a) = a$ is not provable in this subsystem. This motivates our main result, namely, soundness and completeness proofs for the first-order fragment without value-ranges with respect to a new nonclassical semantics of boolean truncation. Simply put, the widespread assumption that Grundgesetze's first-order logic is classical first-order logic is mistaken.

papers.title: Exact multiplicity for a Minkowski-curvature Neumann problem with a step weight
papers.abstract: The DEG1 challenge asks whether positive solutions of a super-exponential Minkowski-curvature equation are unique for step weights with a single sign change and negative mean. In this paper, we give a Neumann counterexample by studying $\left(\frac{u'}{\sqrt{1-(u')^2}}\right)' + \lambda a_{\mu,h}(t)(e^{u^2}-1)=0$ with $u'(0)=u'(2h)=0$, where $a_{\mu,h}=1$ on $(0,h)$ and $a_{\mu,h}=-\mu$ on $(h,2h)$, with $\mu>1$. Using the shooting method, we prove that the positive solution curve has exactly two nondegenerate folds for $(\lambda,h)$ in a nonempty open region. As $\mu$ increases through the corresponding critical values, the number of positive solutions is successively $1$, $2$, $3$, $2$, and $1$.

papers.title: Antisymmetry Breaking for Critical Poincaré-Sobolev Extremals in the Three Dimensional Ball
papers.abstract: We study extremal functions for Poincaré-Sobolev inequalities in the unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^3$. At the critical exponent $q=6$, we prove that no minimizer is antisymmetric with respect to any hyperplane through the origin. We obtain a positive gap between the general and antisymmetric optimal constants. Continuity of these constants yields antisymmetry breaking for exponents sufficiently close to $6$. We introduce two critical indices to describe the onset of antisymmetry breaking and prove that global minimizers are antisymmetric at both indices.

papers.title: Illusion of Explainability: A Sanity Check for Spectral Band Attribution in Satellite Time-Series Crop Classification
Metallic or insulating magnetic phases of transition-metal oxides in light of the Slater vs Mott controversy
papers.abstract: Magnetic d-electron oxides usually have a long-range-ordered ground state and an above-ground-state disordered para phase.
