The historical Slater-Mott controversy still reverberating to date pertains to understanding the origin of the insulating vs metallic nature of these two phases. Slater suggested that the insulating character evolved from the long-range order (LRO) antiferromagnetic (AFM) cell-doubling, leading to energy band repulsion and thus to forming a band gap. The reliance on LRO to explain gapping suggests that the absence of LRO in the spin-disordered para-phase would deprive the system from band repulsion, thus predicting a metallic paramagnetic (PM) phase. This, however, conflicts with numerous current observations. The alternative Mott-Peierls-Hubbard view abandons the mean-field-like band structure view emphasizing instead the local interelectronic repulsion U as a strong correlation signature of gapping both at the presence or absence of LRO. However, U is not an easily measured or calculated quantity in periodic systems, a situation often leading in practice to treating U as an adjustable parameter. The current work uses a parameter-free mean-field-like approach (Density Functional Theory, DFT), allowing energy-lowering symmetry breaking. This is done by considering local magnetic motifs as building blocks of the macroscopic AFM or PM phases. It is found that even when such motifs are isolated electronically from each other (i.e. vanishing LRO) by embedding them in quantum barriers (such as magnetic NiO6 octahedra surrounded locally by wide-gap MgO) they exhibit an intrinsic band gap. Thus, the origin of the band gaps in AFM or PM phases need not be LRO or strong correlation and can be understood within the mean-field-like band structure approach with symmetry breaking.

papers.title: First-order smoothed exact-penalty methods for equality-constrained regularized nonconvex optimization
Recovery Gone Too Far: Understanding and Repairing Risky Fallback in LLM Agents
An Exploration of Physical and Chemical Representation in Coarse-Grained, Machine-Learned Protein Models
papers.abstract: Machine-learned coarse-graining has emerged as a reliable framework for building protein models that accurately and efficiently sample their relevant conformational landscape. Existing studies assume a predefined map from full- to coarse-grained resolution. However, the choice of map strongly affects the quality of the models. Here, we study the dependence of system-specific machine-learned coarse-grained (MLCG) models across 7 mapping choices, spanning different resolutions and embedding types for coarse-grained beads. We show that resolution and chemical diversity do not always correlate with accuracy, and that accurate protein-specific models can be generated using minimal chemical diversity if the latent space representation of the system has high enough dimensionality.

papers.title: Mock Observations: Morphological Analysis of Galactic Bars in IllustrisTNG Simulations
papers.abstract: Galactic bars are important tracers of disk-galaxy evolution, yet reported bar fractions vary among observational studies and between observations and cosmological simulations. We compare bar statistics and properties in the IllustrisTNG simulations(TNG100 and TNG50 at z~0.1) with Sloan Digital Sky Survey(SDSS) galaxies at0.1<=z<=0.1264. We generate synthetic r-band TNG images,match SDSS observational conditions,and analyze mock TNG and real SDSS images using a common image-based framework of source segmentation,morphological classification, and isophotal ellipse fitting. For face-on late-type galaxies with log(M*/Msun)>10,the global bar fractions are 26.68+/-0.23%,24.96(-.76/+.78)%, and 13.42(-1.07/+1.15)% for SDSS,TNG100,and TNG50,respectively. TNG100 broadly agrees with SDSS over 10^10<~M*<~10^11.2Msun but shows a higher fbar at higher masses, whereas TNG50 remains lower than SDSS over most of10^10<~M*<~10^11.7Msun. Bulge-disk decompositions show fewer high-n bulges in TNG100 than in SDSS,particularly at high masses,but more in TNG50. These differences in bulge concentration may contribute to the different bar fractions. Bar length generally increases with stellar mass,and this trend depends little on the adopted bar-length definition. However, the outer ellipticity-decline estimator(R0.85max) yields systematically larger bar lengths than the ellipticity-peak estimator (R(eps,max)^bar). Massive TNG100 galaxies have more extended stellar disks than SDSS,which may contribute to their smaller relative bar lengths(Rbar/Re). Our results indicate that observational conditions,sample selection,and bar-identification methodology can affect the inferred bar fraction,emphasizing comparable observational conditions and analysis procedures in simulation-observation comparisons. Our SDSS measurements may underestimate the bar fraction relative to observations with higher spatial resolution.

papers.title: Growing length scales while approaching the glass transition
papers.abstract: Even after decades of research, the nature of the glass transition is controversially debated: Kinetic freezing phenomena, purely local strain-mediated effects, or collective phenomena including a hidden phase transition are usually discussed. In this work, we check reports on clusters of correlated particles in supercooled liquids which grow upon approaching the glass-transition. We specifically focus on dielectric studies providing approximate access to the four-point correlation function, which allows insight into the evolution of so-called amorphous order. Existing temperature-dependent data derived from the three-point correlation function or higher-order dielectric susceptibilities are modeled using the random first-order transition theory combined with the Vogel-Fulcher-Tammann law. This ansatz enables detailed predictions concerning normalized correlation lengths or the number of correlated particles as function of temperature and fragility. It provides a good fit to the experimental data for all materials investigated, including network and molecular glass formers and polymers. We conclude that length scales and corresponding particle numbers determined by the different methods used are at least similar and closely related to those considered by the theory. Moreover, the model predictions on the fragility dependence of the number of correlated molecules are at least approximately fulfilled. Existing criticism concerning an apparent lack of criticality in the temperature dependence of experimental correlation lengths is discussed in terms of this fragility dependence: All available data are well consistent with a hidden phase transition which is best revealed for the most fragile liquids.

papers.title: Certified Algorithms for Gaussian Location Mixture NPMLEs via Discretized Gradient Flows
papers.abstract: We study the computation of approximate nonparametric maximum likelihood estimators (NPMLEs) for Gaussian location mixtures in arbitrary dimension $d\ge 1$ via the Fisher-Rao gradient flow. We provide a certified algorithm based on an entropic proximal discretization of the flow which, given a sufficiently small $\varepsilon > 0$, returns an absolutely continuous mixing measure $\tilde\mu$ admitting an exact finite-dimensional representation and satisfying $\hat L_n-L_n(f_{\tilde\mu})\le\varepsilon$. For almost every dataset $X_1,\cdots, X_n \in \mathbb{R}^d$ satisfying $n>2(d+1)(m+1)^2$, where $m$ is the number of support points of the NPMLE, the algorithm requires $O(n\varepsilon^{-1}\log^{d+2}(1/\varepsilon))$ time. En route, we also establish results on the well-posedness and convergence properties of the continuous-time Fisher--Rao flow. In particular, initializing the flow at the uniform probability measure on a ball containing the convex hull of the observations, we show that $\hat L_n-L_n(f_{\mu_t})=O(\log t/t)$. We also establish that, for almost every dataset satisfying the same condition on $n$ as above, the set of global maxima of the optimal score is the same as the support of the NPMLE, and the Hessian of the optimal score is nondegenerate at these points, extending a result of (Polyanskiy-Sellke, 2025) to higher dimensions.

papers.title: Weighted bisections of triangle-free subcubic graphs
papers.abstract: We prove a conjecture of Gerke, Gutin, Yeo, and Zhou: for every finite triangle-free subcubic graph other than the claw and every nonnegative edge weighting, there is a bisection whose weight is at least $11/15$ of the total edge weight. This bound is best possible, as shown by the Petersen graph. The proof uses matching-based local distributions, weighted induction, and convex separation to establish the edgewise cut guarantees while maintaining global balance.

papers.title: Instability of non-minimal critical points of Newton's equation with real analytic potentials
papers.abstract: We prove that any non-minimal critical point of a real analytic potential on a finite-dimensional Euclidean space possesses a nonconstant zero-energy Newton trajectory that converges to the equilibrium as \(t\to+\infty\). By time reversibility, this yields forward Lyapunov instability. We do not assume the critical point is isolated. The proof constructs angular minima via quadratic regularization, matching the regularization coefficient to the leading inertial term. A free forcing coefficient allows continuation past bounded accumulations of correction orders. For polynomial potentials, this produces a complete Hahn-series solution, and differential algebraicity gives a common Puiseux denominator. A fixed-denominator continuation estimate together with a finite Taylor transfer extends the construction to analytic potentials. The realization theorem for the resulting invariant formal phase curve then yields a genuine trajectory. We also exhibit an isolated polynomial singularity for which an exact Euler-field identity admits no relatively differentiable solution on the negative set of the potential.

papers.title: Exciton-polarons in monolayer semiconductors with drifting electrons
papers.abstract: Recent work has demonstrated that the optical absorption of moderately doped two-dimensional semiconductors can be described in terms of exciton-polarons. In this picture, interactions between a photoexcited exciton and a Fermi sea of excess charge carriers split the exciton spectrum into a lower-energy attractive polaron branch and a higher-energy repulsive polaron branch. Due to the negligible in-plane momentum of photons, however, optical measurements probe only exciton-polarons near zero momentum, leaving their finite-momentum physics largely unexplored. Here we propose accessing this regime by measuring the absorption in the presence of an electric bias current. In effect, this displaces the electronic Fermi sea in momentum space, such that an optically active exciton-polaron at rest acquires finite momentum relative to the charge carriers. Using a diagrammatic formulation of the exciton-polaron problem, we derive exact relations between the spectral and quasiparticle properties of current-biased exciton-polarons and their finite-momentum counterparts in an equilibrium Fermi sea. These relations show that absorption measurements with drifting electrons can reconstruct the momentum dependence of the quasiparticle properties for both branches. We estimate that experimentally accessible currents can probe a broad momentum range while remaining within the linear-response regime.

papers.title: Quantum Startup, Recoil Statistics and Collective Gain in Free-Electron Lasers
papers.abstract: We examine the conditions under which quantum signatures can be distinguished from classical dynamics and statistical fluctuations in a free-electron laser. Starting from minimal coupling and the Bambini--Renieri frame, we derive the momentum-photon exchange Hamiltonian and its Raman-Nath ladder. An interaction-picture expansion retains detuning exactly and organizes recoil corrections through the mismatch between neighboring orders. Its validity depends on the accumulated recoil phase over the populated ladder, rather than on elementary recoil alone. Numerical checks and Gaussian entrance packets illustrate the effects of preparation and resonance averaging. We distinguish number-state exchange amplitudes from predictions for a coherent optical seed, and joint electron-field coherence from reduced radiation coherence. The Wigner representation connects finite recoil translations with classical transport and identifies the information required for bunching. A cavity channel then provides the basis for comparison with the recoil-resolved oscillator proposed by Kling and Giese, including the optical-undulator preparation, stimulated back-action and narrow resonance acceptance. Space charge, spontaneous diffusion and FEL-induced energy spread are compared with recoil and high-gain bandwidth scales. The coherent undulator pump is essential to exclude artificial zero-recoil antibunching from a number-state preparation. Startup and excess photon variance alone do not establish a quantum signature: the specified observable must remain distinguishable from a classical stochastic baseline under compatible preparation, propagation and detection conditions.

papers.title: Free energy profile computations for force-induced melting of a short B-DNA using Jarzynski equality
papers.abstract: We initially equilibrate a system of solvated 12-base pair canonical B-DNA of a specified sequence in a state of no external force acting on it (state $A: f=0$). A switching experiment is then performed by pulling one end of the DNA while restraining its other end. The pulling force is taken up to a maximum of 400 pN (state $B$), at a specified constant rate. The non-equilibrium work done W associated with this finite-time process is determined by integrating the extension of the DNA molecule with respect to the applied force. The distribution of the work values $P(W)$ is obtained by repeating the pulling process several times, wherein each time, the process is started with macroscopic state $A$. The free energy profile $\Phi(f)$ is obtained by a suitably devised method from the Jarzynski equality. The conformational space of the DNA is also sampled in an equilibrium method of umbrella sampling by considering the end-to-end length $\xi$ as the reaction coordinate. The associated potential of mean force (PMF) $\Phi(\xi)$ is then computed by invoking the weighted histogram analysis method (WHAM). From the results, we observe that the equilibrium free energy difference between two states, $A$ and $B$, $\Delta F_{AB} ~(=F_B -F_A)$ obtained through both methods, is in close agreement with each other, despite the differences along the profiles $\Phi(f)$ and $\Phi(\xi)$, attributed to their distinct pathways of unzipping.

papers.title: Large Language Model-based Optimization for Wireless Communication: A Survey
Let Execution Do the Teaching
A Negative Answer to a Variant of the Lins-de Melo-Pugh Conjecture
papers.abstract: We study the polynomial Liénard system $$\dot x=y-(a_1x^{2m+1}+a_2x^{2n+1}+x^{2N}),\qquad \dot y=-x,$$ where $0\leq m< n<N$ are integers and $a_1a_2<0$. The supremum of the numbers of limit cycles in this family is at least two for every integer $N\geq3$ and at least three for $N=5$. These results disprove Conjectures 1.5 and 1.6 of Cen et al. [Sci. China Math. 69 (2026)].

papers.title: Uniqueness of limit cycle{s} in a class of classical trinomial Liénard systems
papers.abstract: This paper studies the number of limit cycles of the polynomial Liénard system $\dot x=y-F(x)$, $\dot y=-x$, where $F(x)=a_1x^{2N}+a_2x^{2m+1}+x^{2n+1}$, with integers \(N,m,n\) satisfying $2\le N\le m<n$, $a_1\ne0$ and $a_2\neq 0$. It is proved that this system has exactly one limit cycle and that every periodic orbit is hyperbolic and attracting for $a_2<0$; this system has no limit cycles for $a_2>0$. The uniqueness proof compares the widths and relative midpoints of the two scalar arcs obtained in potential coordinates. This result gives a positive answer to Conjecture 1.4 of Cen et al. (Sci. China Math., 2026).

papers.title: Who Writes the Codebook? An Eight-Step Framework for Auditing LLM-Generated Category Systems
Interactive Structured Environment Scaling for Large Language Model Agentic Reasoning
Toward an Admissibility Theory of Aharonov--Bohm Arbitrage
papers.abstract: This note develops a provisional admissibility framework for Aharonov-Bohm type arbitrage. Starting from a categorical filtration $F:\mathcal T_{\mathrm{mic}}^{\mathrm{op}}\to \mathsf{Prob}$ and its distortion on microscopic histories, we ask when a favorable closed microscopic loop can be realized as an executable relative ordinal arbitrage over an open macro-time interval. The history endofunctor $\mathsf{Hist}$ retains the staged decomposition of economic activities, while the twisted-arrow category $\operatorname{Tw}(\mathsf{Hist}(\mathcal T_{\mathrm{mic}}))$ represents a microscopic loop as an arrow between distinct histories. An observable clock $\Pi: \mathsf{Econ} \to \mathcal T_{\mathrm{mac}}$ and a microscopic realization functor $J: \mathsf{Hist}(\mathcal T_{\mathrm{mac}}) \to \operatorname{Tw}(\mathsf{Hist}(\mathcal T_{\mathrm{mic}}))$ connect economic histories with their microscopic geometry. Executability is treated separately through configuration histories, capacity constraints, observations, and policies. This yields pathwise and almost-sure notions of execution. A finite foreign-exchange model illustrates stochastic execution, capacity failure, terminal settlement, and comparison with a benchmark strategy. A parameterized finite filtration is constructed whose nontrivial statewise distortion agrees exactly with the relative FX settlement multiplier. Hence the resulting filtration--policy model satisfies the bridge $V_*(\pi^q)=dF(\gamma)V_*(\pi^p),$ and, under order compatibility, realizes relative ordinal arbitrage. The remaining problem is to identify the filtration parameters from independent market primitives and to study stability under refinement.

papers.title: Theory of anisotropic magnetotransport beyond the constant relaxation-time approximation in multi-Weyl semimetals
papers.abstract: Multi-Weyl semimetals, characterized by Weyl nodes carrying higher monopole charges, provide a platform for exploring topological magnetotransport beyond the conventional Weyl paradigm. Here, we develop a generalized semiclassical Boltzmann framework for multi-Weyl semimetals with arbitrary monopole charge $N$, incorporating the orbital magnetic moment (OMM) into the quasiparticle dispersion and Berry-curvature-modified dynamics, together with a momentum-dependent collision integral accounting for intra- and intervalley scattering. We investigate the longitudinal magnetoconductivity (LMC) and planar Hall conductivity (PHC) for $N=1$, $2$, and $3$, considering both nonmagnetic and magnetic impurity scattering. In the absence of OMM, the LMC remains positive and quadratic in the magnetic field throughout the investigated scattering regime, consistent with conventional chiral-anomaly-assisted transport. Including OMM, however, leads to a sign reversal of the LMC under sufficiently strong intervalley scattering for the $\sigma_0$ and $\sigma_z$ impurity channels. Remarkably, the critical intervalley scattering strength decreases systematically with increasing monopole charge, indicating an enhanced tendency toward negative LMC in higher-charge Weyl systems. Furthermore, we find that the PHC also undergoes a sign reversal for $N=2$ and $N=3$ in the same impurity channels, while remaining positive for $N=1$ within the investigated parameter range. The angular dependences retain their characteristic $\sin^2\gamma$-like and $\sin2\gamma$ profiles for LMC and PHC, respectively, even across the sign reversal. Our results demonstrate that the interplay of Berry curvature, OMM, monopole charge, and impurity scattering can produce qualitatively distinct weak-field magnetotransport responses beyond the conventional chiral-anomaly picture.

papers.title: HalluProbe: Exploiting VLM Hallucinations for Backdoor Detection
Stripped White Dwarfs as Spectroscopic Clocks: Abundance Transitions in Partial Tidal Disruptions
papers.abstract: We investigate partial tidal disruptions of He and CO white dwarfs (WDs) by a $10^{4}\,M_{\odot}$ intermediate-mass black hole (IMBH) using three-dimensional hydrodynamic simulations. We construct realistic WD structures and abundance profiles with MESA and map them into FLASH to follow the remnant response and the time-dependent composition of the fallback debris in single pericentre passages on tightly bound orbits ($e=0.9$). The element-specific fallback rates exhibit pre-peak compositional transitions that trace the WD's stratified layers. In the grazing encounter ($\beta=0.55$), hydrogen dominates the earliest returning debris, followed by helium, showing a H$\rightarrow$He transition. Deeper encounters ($\beta=0.7$ and $0.8$) penetrate the CO core and produce a He$\rightarrow$C transition, that occurs earlier relative to peak fallback and is stronger in the deeper encounter. These signatures provide a potential spectroscopic diagnostic for identifying CO-WD tidal disruption events (TDEs). We then develop a semi-analytic model for repeated tidal stripping and predict passage-to-passage compositional evolution, in which the stripped material becomes progressively enriched in heavier elements as deeper layers are exposed, leading to stronger and earlier abundance transitions in later flares. We find that WDs can survive several dozen ($\sim 30$-$80$) passages, depending on their initial mass and compactness. Our results link time-dependent abundance signatures to repeating WD disruptions and provide testable observable predictions for identifying IMBH-powered transients.

papers.title: Uniquely balanced polyhedral complexes are highly connected
papers.abstract: We establish higher connectivity of polyhedral complexes admitting a unique positive balanced top cycle. Our main result shows that, after quotienting by common lineality, every skeleton satisfies the corresponding higher connectivity property. The proof bounds the number of connected components surviving facet deletions by the dimension of the top-cycle space using homological and linear-algebraic arguments. As applications, we prove higher connectivity for all skeleta of arbitrary pointed polyhedral structures on tropical linear spaces of valuated matroids and Bergman fans including nonrealizable cases. These results answer questions raised by Maclagan and Yu.

papers.title: Max-Min Throughput in RSMA-Aided SWIPT for Sustainable Internet of Underground Things: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach
Local Order Matters: A Lightweight CPU-Trainable CNN for Website Fingerprinting on Defended Tor Traffic
Velocity weakening and stick-slip in mean-field depinning with stress overshoots
papers.abstract: We study a fully connected depinning model with transient stress overshoots of strength $M$, driven through a spring of stiffness $k_0$. Combining exact stationary relations, linear stability analysis, direct simulations, and population dynamics, we connect the force--velocity characteristic to stick-slip motion and quasistatic avalanche statistics. For $M>1$, two distinct stiffness scales organize the response. At $k_0=k_{\rm w}\equiv M-1$, the stationary characteristic first develops a velocity-weakening branch, whereas $k_0=k_{\rm q}\equiv(M-1)^2/(4M)$ marks the onset of finite-amplitude stick-slip in the quasistatic limit. Their separation produces an intermediate regime in which the quasistatic force converges to a stationary value, whereas finite-velocity driving produces stick-slip below a critical velocity. Quasistatic avalanches in this regime undergo transient amplification and display an excess of large, asymmetric events---"ghost kings"---that remain finite. By contrast, at and below $k_{\rm q}$ the same amplification produces system-spanning "genuine kings" and a finite quasistatic force cycle. These results show how elastic loading dynamically selects among the branches of a reentrant force--velocity relation and clarify the connection between velocity weakening, stick-slip, and runaway avalanches.

papers.title: Bioformer-RetroMAE: retrieval-oriented pretraining of a compact biomedical language model for literature search
HBF-EventLab: A Discrete-Event Simulator for Studying Host-Device Coordination in High Bandwidth Flash
Optimisation of gas mixture for charge and light readout with Micromegas detectors
papers.abstract: Optical readout of Micromegas detectors is a promising technique for neutron and charged-particle imaging, offering high spatial resolution while reducing the complexity of electronic readout. Within the framework of the development of optical-readout Micromegas detectors, different noble-gas-based mixtures have been investigated to optimize charge amplification and scintillation yield. Argon-, neon-, and helium-based mixtures with various quenchers were characterized using X-ray irradiation. The detector gain, energy resolution, and optical light intensity were measured simultaneously over a wide range of amplification fields. Unprecedented energy resolutions were achieved over a large detection area (several cm$^2$) with He/\CF and Ne/\CF (90/10) mixtures, reaching 10.5\% and 13.3\% (FWHM), respectively, with the He-based mixture delivering particularly remarkable performance. Simultaneous charge and optical measurements further reveal that high charge gain does not necessarily translate into a strong optical response: while He- and Ne-based mixtures achieve effective charge gains of the order of 10$^5$, Ar/\CF mixtures produce the strongest detected light signals. Among the investigated mixtures, the ternary Ar/\CF/Isobutane (95/3/2) mixture stands out as particularly promising, combining high effective charge gain, a comparatively strong optical response, and more stable detector operation.

papers.title: When Facts Change, Which Decisions Break? Dependency-Aware Context Graphs for Agents
Bridging the Terminology Gap: A Data-Centric Alignment Framework for Multilingual Translation in Cross-Border Corporation
PanDWM: Panoramic 4D Driving World Models
On $ι$Quiver (BPS) Algebras and (Strict) Partitions
papers.abstract: We consider the $\iota$quiver algebras of split type associated with the quiver BPS algebras of affine type A. They are supposed to give twisted affine Yangians and (elliptic) $\iota$quantum toroidal algebras that could possibly arise from D-branes on $\mathbb{C}\times\mathbb{C}^2/\mathbb{Z}_n$ with orientifolds. We mention some properties of these algebras, such as the minimalistic presentations in the rational cases and the coideal structures. We also investigate how one might identify these algebras from the quiver theories with orientifold actions. Moreover, we discuss some representations with combinatorial bases of these algebras. In particular, the algebras with $n=1,2$ in certain limits of the parameters have representations labelled by (coloured) strict/symmetric partitions, which in the case of $n=1$ recovers the known BPS counting of certain theories.

papers.title: Scaling Fourier Inequalities for Locally Compact Quantum Groups
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study Fourier and convolution inequalities on locally compact quantum groups in the presence of the scaling group. For $1\le p\le 2$, we investigate a family of scaling Fourier transforms and the associated norms $H_{p,\theta}(\mathbb G)$, and we show that $H_{p,\theta}(\mathbb G)<1$ for the real quantum $az+b$ group and $0<\theta<1$, $1<p<2$. We also investigate scaling convolution for locally compact quantum groups and, by extending the ordinary convolution, obtain the corresponding scaling Young inequality in four different regions. In Young Region~II, under $1<p,s<2$ and $2\leq r<\infty$, we construct sequences proving norm one at every effective vertex and prove strict inequality at every other effective point.

papers.title: Indication of demographic and epidemiological data on early-stage risks and long-term epidemic burden
papers.abstract: This study investigates the relationship between age-specific cumulative infection burden and the probability of triggering a major outbreak in heterogeneous populations. We develop two modeling frameworks that incorporate empirical age-stratified contact matrices: a deterministic framework for deriving the final size relation and a stochastic framework based on a Continuous-time Markov chain epidemic model, for which a multi-type branching-process approximation is used to characterize early-stage outbreak risk. The framework is illustrated using empirical social contact data from Guangzhou, Foshan, and Zhuhai, China, under two disease-motivated scenarios representing COVID-19 and hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD). The illustrative analyses indicate that the relationship between cumulative infection burden and early-stage outbreak risk depends on both epidemiological characteristics and population contact patterns. In particular, age groups with the highest final attack rates do not necessarily have the highest probability of triggering a major outbreak. These findings highlight the complementary nature of the two measures and the value of considering both when assessing age-specific epidemic risks in practice.

papers.title: Electrical transport of surface-bound electrons on annealed solid neon
papers.abstract: We study the dc transport of electrons bound to the surface of solid neon using the conventional Sommer-Tanner method. First, we find that the capacitive cross-talk for the thickness of solid samples on the order of a millimeter varies substantially with the temperature and is strongly affected by the sample annealing. Second, we find that, even for the annealed samples, the observed response of electrons differs significantly from that of the surface-bound electrons on liquid helium and cannot be satisfactorily described by conventional models. Despite this, we managed to extract the resistance of the electron system from its in-phase response and investigate the temperature dependence in a wide range between 1.4 and 20 K. In a high-temperature range between 16 and 20 K, the resistance behavior is found to agree very well with the vapor-atom scattering mechanism, while at lower temperatures it is consistent with temperature-dependent scattering by surface roughness. Our analysis indicates a high electron mobility of electrons on solid neon but two orders of magnitude lower density than expected. These results suggest surface electrons as a suitable probe for studying the morphology of the neon surface but call for a better understanding of the experimental method applicable to such systems.

papers.title: Sparse Stabilization of Continuous-Time Linear Dynamical Systems
Record-proof optical communication enabled by a quantum receiver with lossless optical decryption
papers.abstract: We propose record-proof physical-layer encryption (PLE) based on quantum-optimal reception. Unlike conventional symmetric-key encryption algorithms, the proposed scheme prevents decryption of recorded signals even if the secret key is disclosed after transmission. Existing PLE schemes rely on practical limitations of the eavesdropper's receiver in pursuing record-proof security; ours instead exploits the noncommutativity of conjugate optical quadratures to give the legitimate receiver an intrinsic sensitivity advantage. A phase-controlled Kennedy receiver performs lossless optical decryption and near-optimal binary-state discrimination. We demonstrate record-proof security with a 3.0-dB channel-loss budget, showing that quantum receivers offer cryptographic functions beyond sensitivity enhancement.

papers.title: Sharp Gaussian Approximation for Q-Learning
NoLBERT-Calls: Reading Earnings Calls Without Hindsight
A phase diagram for training and inference in language models
papers.abstract: A language model is a complex system whose behavior is determined jointly by the Transformer and the corpus, yet how the representation geometry in the Transformer relates to the actual behavior of language models remains open. We analyze how the representation geometry changes along the forward propagation of actual language models and characterize the representation geometry of a document at a given layer by two collective coordinates, document distinguishability and document dimension. On the phase diagram spanned by these collective coordinates, inference is represented as a flow along depth. We find that, for untrained models, depending on their initialization scale, most of the 156 inference flows move toward the collapse and noise regions of the phase diagram. By contrast, the inference flows of 8 trained models from 5 architecture families all enter and reside in the central region of the phase diagram. Describing the evolution of the flows with a discrete Langevin equation, we find that the difference between the inference flows of untrained runs and those of trained models reduces to whether the effective force on the flows in this region is of saddle or stable-node type. On Pythia-1.4B, we interpret the training process as a phase transition. These results give a unified gateway to the relation between representation geometry and language-model behavior.

papers.title: Reflection Is Not Always Worth It: Budgeted Reflection Allocation for Recommendation Agents
Borel $(2n+1)$-coloring for bounded degree function graphs
papers.abstract: Let $G=(X,E)$ be a Borel graph generated by $n$-many bounded-to-one Borel functions. We show that $G$ admits a Borel proper $(2n+1)$-coloring, which answers a problem of Kechris, Solecki and Todorčević.

Splitting of separatrices in generalized standard maps
papers.abstract: We consider generalized standard maps, that is, maps $F_h:(x,y) \mapsto (x+y+f(x;h),y+f(x;h))$ under quite general assumptions. These maps are area preserving. In particular, the Chirikov standard map, the area preserving Hénon map and the case $f(x;h)= \varepsilon(x-x^n)$, $n\ge 2$, where $\varepsilon = 4 \sinh^2(h/2)$ satisfy our hypotheses. For all these cases, the problem of the existence of transverse homoclinic points arises. We prove that, for a wide class of generalized standard maps, the primary homoclinic points are transverse, provided that some constant is different from 0.

Quantum state tomography with measurement-conditioned diffusion models
papers.abstract: We introduce Diff-QST, a measurement-conditioned diffusion model for quantum state tomography that learns from an ensemble of input states and reconstructs a physical density operator from noisy, possibly incomplete Pauli measurements in two or three denoising steps. In simulations of two to five qubits, Diff-QST has higher mean fidelity than maximum-likelihood estimation (MLE) and a semidefinite-programming least-squares estimator (SDP) in all 120 tested conditions at nominal noise. After training, GPU reconstruction is faster than both in condition-averaged time at every system size and, at four and five qubits, in every condition. At four and five qubits, though not at two and three, Diff-QST also has higher fidelity than an architecture-matched regression baseline trained without diffusion. At five qubits, over the tested numbers of observables and shots per observable, it reaches a specified fidelity with 25%-67% fewer total shots than this baseline. Under state and noise distributions that differ from those used in training, Diff-QST retains its fidelity advantage over MLE and SDP in most tested conditions, although it can reverse. Diff-QST is therefore suited to fast tomography from noisy, incomplete Pauli measurements of states represented by its training ensemble.

papers.title: Counterexamples to Ecker's Conjecture
papers.abstract: Analogous to Perelman's W-entropy defined for Ricci flow, K. Ecker defined a functional W for the mean curvature flow in R^{n+1} and the region it encloses, and made the conjecture that this functional is monotonically increasing in time. In this paper, we give a negative answer to Ecker's conjecture.

papers.title: AGPF: Dynamic Source Selection for Feature Pyramid Fusion
Saturation and Semi-Saturation Numbers of Joins with Complete Graphs
papers.abstract: For a nonempty family $\mathcal F$ of graphs, a graph is $\mathcal F$-semi-saturated if adding any missing edge creates a copy of some member of $\mathcal F$ containing the added edge, and is $\mathcal F$-saturated if it is also $\mathcal F$-free. The minimum numbers of edges in such graphs of order $n$ are denoted by $\operatorname{ssat}(n,\mathcal F)$ and $\operatorname{sat}(n,\mathcal F)$, respectively. We study these parameters for families of graphs obtained by taking the join of a fixed complete graph with each member of a given graph family. Assume that every member of $\mathcal F$ has at least $8$ vertices, minimum degree at least two, and no triangle containing two vertices of degree two. We give explicit sufficient conditions under which $\operatorname{sat}(n,K_t\vee\mathcal F) =\binom{t}{2}+t(n-t)+\operatorname{sat}(n-t,\mathcal F),$ and characterize all extremal graphs. For the family $\mathcal C_{\ge r}=\{C_\ell:\ell\ge r\}$ of subdivisions of $C_r$, this identity holds for fixed $t\ge1$ and $r\ge4t^2+8t+29$ and all sufficiently large $n$. For $K_t\vee C_k$ with $k\ge2t^2+3t+4$, we establish the corresponding identity for saturation when $n\ge2(k+t-2)^3$ and for semi-saturation when $n\ge56k^3+t-1$.

papers.title: Asymptotics of the three-color Hadwiger-Ramsey numbers
papers.abstract: The Hadwiger-Ramsey number $R_h(k;\ell)$ is defined as the smallest integer $n$ such that for any edge coloring of a complete graph on $n$ vertices in $\ell$ colors at least one of the color classes induces a graph with a $K_k$ minor. We show that $R_h(k;3) = \left(\beta^{-1} + o(1)\right)k \sqrt{\ln k}$, where $\beta^{-1} = 2/\sqrt{-\ln(10-4\sqrt6)} = 1.58149\ldots$. This resolves the first open case of a problem by Axenovich and Steiner, who determined the asymptotic behavior of $R_h(k;2)$ and asked about the asymptotics of $R_h(k;\ell)$ for $\ell \geq 3$.

Exploring X17 Couplings through Meson Dalitz Decays
papers.abstract: The ATOMKI collaboration has reported anomalous $e^+e^-$ pair production in a series of nuclear transitions, which has been interpreted as a possible signature of a new light boson, X17. Meson Dalitz decays provide a complementary probe of the X17 interaction structure. However, the widely studied vector coupling scenario is in tension with the combined constraints from existing $D^{*0}\to D^0e^+e^-$, $D_s^{*+}\to D_s^+e^+e^-$ measurements and nuclear transition analyses. In this work, we investigate the X17 contributions to meson Dalitz decays within a framework incorporating both vector and axial-vector couplings, employing the Bethe--Salpeter approach to calculate the hadronic transition matrix elements. With $u$ and $d$ quark couplings taken from previous analyses, we identify allowed regions for the charm and strange quark couplings, which require the axial-vector coupling strength $|g_{c,s}^A|\sim10^{-3}$. We obtain four degenerate best-fit solutions, one of which is $(g_c^V,g_c^A,g_s^V,g_s^A)=(8.32,1.09,-2.62,1.36)\times10^{-3}$, and estimate the decay ratio $R^{\mathrm{th}}(D^{*+}\to D^+e^+e^-)$, which significantly exceeds the Standard Model prediction.

The Erdős similarity problem for polynomials and analytic maps
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the Erdős similarity problem by replacing affine copies with images of polynomial maps or analytic maps. This is inspired by a connection between a partial converse of Szemerédi's theorem and the Erdős similarity problem and its variants, as well as a version of polynomial Szemerédi's theorem by Bergelson and Leibman. In particular, we strengthen several known results in the literature. We show that a large class of sequence are not polynomially universal in this sense. First, for sequences satisfying suitable gap hypotheses, an explicit Cantor-type witness is constructed. Second, for sets satisfying certain growth conditions, a random Cantor-type witness is constructed, extending work of Kolountzakis. This also extends certain results in recent work of Cuéllar-Iosevich-Kulkarni-Aravena-Yavicoli to the polynomial setting. Finally, we show for arbitrary sequences $A$ with zero as an accumulation point that the $(d+3)$-fold sumset $(d+3)A$ is not polynomially universal when restricted to polynomials of degree at most $d$; this complements classical work of Bourgain.

Quark + diquark description of nucleon gravitational form factors
papers.abstract: We present parameter-free predictions for the nucleon gravitational form factors (GFFs) using a Poincare-covariant quark+diquark Faddeev equation. We provide the full GFFs ($A$, $J$, $D$, and $\bar{c}$) along with their species decompositions into quark and gluon contributions. Based on the diquark breakdown, we find that while the scalar diquark component dominates the nucleon's energy, spin, and mechanical properties, the axial-vector component plays an indispensable role. The GFF $B(Q^2)$ is predicted to be vanishingly small but nonvanishing at finite $Q^2$; its physical origin is deeply rooted in the nucleon' s internal structure through cancellations in both the diquark content and the $u/d$ flavor sectors. Furthermore, our results for $\bar{c}(Q^2)$ confirm the fundamental symmetry requirements of the approach. Compared with lQCD, our calculated $D$-term and various spatial radii are somewhat smaller in magnitude. This systematic underestimation is primarily driven by the gluon sector and can be attributed to the omission of meson cloud effects, suggesting that these effects impact the gluon distribution more significantly than the quark distribution. Finally, our analysis of the energy density based on two extrapolation schemes reveals that the presence of a negative central energy density is highly model-dependent.

papers.title: Drone Navigation for Fast, Safe Emergency Response
Optimal first order global regularity for fractional harmonic maps into spheres
papers.abstract: This paper is a continuation of our previous work on global regularity theory for the sphere-valued fractional harmonic maps which was initialized by several authors such as Millot-Pegon-Schikorra and Millot-Sire. By adapting the powerful quantitative stratification approach developed by Naber-Valtorta on harmonic mappings, we establish a corresponding stratification theory for fractional harmonic maps, from which an optimal first order global regularity theory and the rectifiable structure of singular sets follow.

papers.title: An improved lower bound for piercing the chessboard by lines
papers.abstract: Let $p_n$ be the least number of lines meeting the interior of every cell of an $n\times n$ board. We prove that $\liminf_{n\to\infty}p_n/n\ge0.7520517>\frac34$. The previous bound was $0.7$. The proof is computer-assisted. It identifies a non-negative polynomial on the unit square and bounds its integral along every line.

papers.title: Conditional Optimal Transport and Triangular Maps for Imitation Learning
Efficient numerical measurement design and certified risk bounds for multiparameter quantum estimation
papers.abstract: Multiparameter quantum estimation requires efficient measurement design and reliable bounds on the attainable precision. We present Q-StARC, a numerical framework that combines measurement optimization with certified lower bounds on the weighted variance of locally unbiased estimators. The measurement search parameterizes rank-one measurements on a complex Stiefel manifold and combines projected ambient Adam updates, QR retraction, and Riemannian conjugate-gradient refinement. Independent risk bounds are obtained from a denominator-based matrix sum-of-squares hierarchy. When its support coefficients are optimized jointly, the hierarchy starts at the weighted Nagaoka-Hayashi (NH) bound and converges to the optimal locally unbiased risk, including for singular states. Numerical applications certify that the NH bound is unattainable for several finite-copy qubit models and two full eight-parameter qutrit models. For the qutrit examples, the certified relative gaps above the NH bound exceed $14\%$ and $11\%$, while the level-$m=1$ lower bounds agree with the best numerical measurement costs to relative differences of $4.5\times10^{-7}$ and $2.2\times10^{-6}$, respectively.

papers.title: Cyclic Hasse diagrams of manifolds and noncommutative path cohomology
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a connected oriented closed manifold of dimension $d\geq 2$, equipped with a regular CW structure, and let $P$ be its face poset. We consider the cyclic Hasse diagram $G_P^{\mathrm{cyc}}$, obtained from the directed Hasse diagram $G_P$ by adding an arrow from each maximal cell to every $0$-cell of $M$. Over an arbitrary field $\mathbb K$, we completely describe the path cohomology algebra $PH^*(G_P^{\mathrm{cyc}})$ in terms of the $\mathbb K$-Betti numbers of $M$. In particular, this algebra is not graded commutative whenever the dimension of $H^*(M)$ over $\mathbb K$ is at least 4. This disproves Grigor'yan's conjecture on graded commutativity. Moreover, as $M$ ranges over connected oriented closed surfaces, the even subalgebras $PH^{\mathrm{even}}(G_P^{\mathrm{cyc}})$, regarded as ungraded associative unital $\mathbb K$-algebras, satisfy no common algebraic identity beyond those satisfied by all associative unital $\mathbb K$-algebras. These results distinguish GLMY path cohomology from classical cohomology, whose cup product is graded commutative and whose even subalgebra is commutative. As an application, we construct a digraph $G$ for which the Künneth formula for the categorical product $G\times G$ fails, answering a question of Pinto negatively and disproving another conjecture of Grigor'yan.

papers.title: Reasoning in the loop: antibody lead optimization by probing mechanism and measurement
Polarization of Fast Radio Bursts due to Propagation in Magnetized Plasma
papers.abstract: Polarization measurements of radio transients, particularly their frequency dependence, shed light on the magnetic environments of these sources. We extend the analytical solution of radiative transfer of the polarization properties of such transients to both a cold magnetized plasmas beyond the high-frequency approximation and a relativistic plasma with synchrotron emission. The Faraday mixing coefficients are enhanced makes Stokes parameters $Q$, $U$, and $V$ to exhibit a more rapid and complex frequency-dependent evolution. A relativistic plasma medium can also generate both Faraday roataion and conversion with a smaller magnetic field. The relativistic plasma is investigated as a persistent radio source (PRS) associated with FRB, and it is found that, although the observed PRS luminosity can be accounted for, an FRB can propagate out only under certain special parameter conditions. We apply the model to fit the polarization profile of GPM J1839$-$10 and revisit some FRBs. All sources with Faraday conversion require that the environment's magnetic field not exceed 100~G. The magnetic field of FRB 20180301A and GPM J1839$-$10 are almost perpendicular to the light of sight for at least some times.

papers.title: Developing JEEVHITAA: Designing and Evaluating a Human-Centered AI Ecosystem for Collective Care
No complete set of mutually unbiased bases in C^6 without Fourier vanishing
papers.abstract: A recent exact certificate shows that C^6 admits no seven mutually unbiased bases, hence at most five (OpenAI, 2026). That argument has two parts. The first proves the Fourier-vanishing conjecture of Matolcsi, Ruzsa and Weiner for every complex Hadamard matrix of order six other than Tao's cubic matrix, and excludes the cubic matrix separately. The second feeds this vanishing into a positivity certificate on mixed moments of a hypothetical complete family. We show that the first part is not needed. We keep the same six families of test functions and the same linear identities, but we never set a moment to zero because of Fourier vanishing. New positive definite integer matrices still give the contradiction. The only inputs are orthonormality, unbiasedness, the second-moment (2-design) identity of a complete family, and the trivial bound |moment| <= 1. A standard-library program checks the certificate in exact integer and rational arithmetic in under a minute and a half. We also record computational observations that are not part of the proof: a systematic S_6-symmetric family of test functions appears to close the argument with relations of total order at most 7 instead of 11, and at order 9 two orbit types of test charges appear to suffice. In the prime-power dimensions 4,5,7,8, where complete families exist, the same pipeline finds no certificate, as it must.

papers.title: Multi-throat generalized Ellis--Bronnikov wormholes with asymptotic string-cloud behavior
papers.abstract: We study an ultrastatic, spherically symmetric family of traversable wormholes obtained by locally deforming a generalized Ellis--Bronnikov areal-radius profile in a spacetime with an asymptotic angular deficit. Depending on the deformation parameters, the same analytic family contains one, two, three, or four throats. The corresponding bifurcation curves are obtained in dimensionless form, and the resulting geometries are regular and asymptotically conical. We also reconstruct a source in General Relativity using a canonical scalar, a shift-symmetric phantom scalar, and a magnetic nonlinear electromagnetic field coupled to the canonical scalar. In the reference multi-throat geometry, the coupling removes a branch obstruction of an uncoupled single-valued nonlinear electrodynamics (NED); the same obstruction occurs whenever equal values of the magnetic invariant require different values of $\mathcal G_F$. For $\mathcal G(F)=F+\lambda\sqrt F$, the NED sector carries the leading asymptotic stress, which scales as $r^{-2}$ and approaches the string-cloud equation of state. The total stress tensor satisfies pointwise energy conditions in finite belly-centered regions of representative two- and four-throat solutions, while the throats violate the radial null energy condition (NEC) and the violation extends into integrable asymptotic tails. The Nandi--Zhang--Kumar covariant volume integral of $\rho+p_r$ is quadratic in the deformation amplitude; its zero is distinct from the bifurcation curves. Away from saddle-node boundaries, each throat supports a radially unstable background-metric light ring, and each intermediate belly supports a radially stable one, with an internally trapped null family in the double-throat case. These results place the topology, source reconstruction, integrated NEC content, and background-metric circular-orbit structure in a common parameter-space description.

papers.title: MAPS: A Multimodal Agentic Framework for POI Data Production Based on Crowdsourced Street-view Imagery
Field-Driven Active Matter Physics and Material Applications
papers.abstract: Active matter consists of energy-consuming units that generate motion, making it a powerful platform for exploring nonequilibrium physics and engineering adaptive materials. Robotic active matter brings this physics into programmable, macroscopic agents with controllable actuation, sensing, and response, but its scalability is limited by onboard power, communication, and control complexity. Field-driven active matter addresses these limitations by shifting part of the control burden from individual agents to external or environmental fields, such as magnetic, electric, acoustic, optical, and fluidic fields, which can power, guide, and couple many agents simultaneously. Beyond applications in targeted navigation, adaptive collaboration, and flexible transport, field-driven robotic active matter offers a controllable testbed for nonequilibrium phenomena that are difficult to isolate in molecular or colloidal active matter, including tunable interactions, programmable phase transitions, solid-fluid switching, hyperuniform order, and reconfigurable collective motion. Here, we present field-driven active matter as a bridge between active matter physics and functional material engineering, organized through a unified field-to-information-to-physics-to-function framework that links field-mediated interactions, information processing, and memory to collective transport, reconfiguration, and mechanical performance. By distributing control between agents and fields, field-driven active matter offers a pathway toward intelligent materials capable of sensing, adaptation, computation, reconfiguration, and performing complex tasks, while expanding both the scientific scope of nonequilibrium physics and the practical capabilities of engineered matter.

papers.title: Word complexity cutoffs for mixing properties of subshifts
papers.abstract: Investigating word complexity cutoffs for partial and light mixing in subshifts, we construct partially mixing rank-one subshifts whose word complexity functions $p(q)$ satisfy $ \liminf_{q\to\infty}\frac{p(q)}q<2+\epsilon $ for any prescribed $\epsilon>0$ and, conversely, we prove that every lightly mixing rank-one subshift satisfies $ \liminf_{q\to\infty}\frac{p(q)}q>2, $ establishing $2$ as the optimal limiting threshold in the rank-one setting. More quantitatively, we show that every $\alpha$-partially mixing rank-one subshift satisfies $ \liminf_{q\to\infty}\frac{p(q)}q\geq 2+\frac{\alpha}{(1+\alpha)}. $ Our constructions are a combination of staircase and Chacon-like rank-one stages; we introduce the independently interesting notion of mixing spans and meshes to establish partial mixing while retaining low word complexity.

papers.title: Spectroscopic evidence for unconventional surface magnetism in the Kondo insulator FeSb$_2$
authors: Erin E. Fleck Jonathan A. Sobota
papers.abstract: Kondo insulators have a non-magnetic bulk due to many-body screening of local moment by conduction electrons. However, the surface of these systems has reduced density of itinerant electrons and may experience a Kondo breakdown, leading to recovery of non-zero local moments and possible magnetic order. Here we use angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy to investigate the (010) surface of a $d$-$p$ electron Kondo insulator FeSb$_2$, which is predicted to host a bulk $d$-wave altermagnetic state in the absence of Kondo screening. We find anisotropic splitting on the surface states with a maximum in the $k_z$ direction and a minimum in the $k_x$ direction. The splitting is apparently suppressed with increasing temperature or with Te doping, suggesting that the splitting arises from a magnetic order rather than Rashba effects. Considering the proximity of the bulk to a $d$-wave altermagnetic state and considering the symmetry of the crystal on the surface, we postulate that our observations may be consistent with an emergent surface altermagnetic order. Such an unconventional 2-dimensional magnetic order naturally hosted on an insulating, non-magnet bulk substrate may offer a promising platform for versatile applications.

papers.title: Pros4D: Modeling Evolving 4D Worlds in Latent Space for Dynamic Spatial Reasoning
Machine interpreting competitiveness: a discourse-sensitive comparison of meaning and target-language quality in English-Chinese simultaneous interpreting
Exact environment checkpointing for memory-limited DMRG and TDVP
papers.abstract: Finite matrix-product-state sweep algorithms, such as the density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) and the time-dependent variational principle (TDVP), store one environment tensor per site. At the bond dimensions needed for frustrated and two-dimensional systems this stack, rather than the state itself, exhausts the memory of the device. We adapt checkpointing to these sweeps: every $k$-th environment is kept, with $k\approx\sqrt{N}$ for $N$ sites, and the blocks in between are rebuilt when the sweep returns to them. The rebuild repeats the original contractions, so energies and states are reproduced bit for bit when the contractions are deterministic. Environment memory falls by 4.6-10x on cylinders of 96-384 sites. Bond-dimension searches with an implementation that rebuilds checkpoints at each half-sweep give gains of 1.77 for one level and 2.07 for two levels with eight contraction chunks on a single 141 GB GPU, using a 144-site triangular $J_1$-$J_2$ cylinder and stored baselines with matching chunking. Separate timings with checkpoints retained across half-sweeps give a one-level overhead of 6-15%, depending on the local eigensolver. At $D=1536$ the two-level schedule with eight chunks takes 1.42 times the sweep time of the equally chunked stored baseline, or 1.79 times that of the unchunked stored baseline. Simple models of the memory and the run time reproduce the measurements to within a few per cent. Unlike offloading, the method needs no host memory or disk, and the two can be combined. Implementations are provided for this http URL , TeNPy, this http URL and quimb.

papers.title: Multi-Branch Transformer
Mixed-Sign Kitaev Exchange in Jahn-Teller-Distorted CrI$_2$
papers.abstract: Kitaev couplings with ferromagnetic (FM) or antiferromagnetic (AFM) character shape magnetic frustration and phases differently in real materials, yet their coexistence within a single material remains unexplored. Here, we propose Jahn-Teller distortion as a route to realizing such coexistence on inequivalent bonds. First-principles calculations identify monolayer CrI$_2$ as such a system, with AFM and FM Kitaev couplings on the short and long bonds, respectively. These opposite signs are robust against variations in Hubbard $U$, functionals, and strain. A minimal tight-binding model links this sign contrast to Jahn-Teller-split $t_{2g}$ orbitals and their hopping to $e_g$ orbitals. We further adopt the cluster expansion method and develop a realistic machine-learned spin Hamiltonian, which reproduces the experimentally observed proper-screw geometry and propagation direction and reveals highly nonuniform spin rotation, with turning angles ranging from $48.0^\circ$ to $93.9^\circ$. Both proper-screw anisotropy and strong anharmonic spin rotation arise from the mixed-sign Kitaev interaction. These findings not only establish Jahn-Teller distortion as a microscopic route to mixed-sign Kitaev exchange, but also open a new avenue for exploring novel magnetic phases.

Stability of the tangent bundle on del Pezzo surfaces
papers.abstract: In this article, we study the Bridgeland stability of the tangent bundle on del Pezzo surfaces. We obtain a complete description of the region where the tangent bundle is (un)stable with respect to the standard Bridgeland stability conditions associated to the anticanonical polarization.

IANN: A Unified Framework for Equivariant InterAtomic Neural Networks with User-Friendly Implementation
papers.abstract: Machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) now approach density functional theory (DFT) accuracy at a fraction of its cost, but the practical benefit is limited by software fragmentation: each state-of-the-art architecture is released as a separate codebase, with its own data format, configuration system, training loop and molecular-dynamics interface. Comparing two architectures on the same dataset, or moving a trained model into a production simulation, therefore requires substantial re-engineering. We introduce IANN (InterAtomic Neural Network), an open-source PyTorch framework that reimplements equivariant graph neural networks - PaiNN, NequIP, MACE, Allegro, EquiformerV2, EquiformerV3 and UMA - behind a unified data object, a unified trainer and a single deployment route, so that the architecture is a one-word change in a configuration dictionary. Forces, stresses and virials are obtained for every architecture from one analytic differentiation of the energy with respect to the edge vectors of the atomic graph, exact under periodic boundary conditions. Distributed training is configured automatically from the SLURM, PBS or MPI environment, so the same script runs unchanged from a workstation to a multi-node GPU allocation. Self-describing checkpoints serve directly as ASE calculators, as ensembles reporting uncertainties, or as TorchScript models run inside LAMMPS through bundled C++ pair styles with single- and multi-GPU inference. Trained on a common dataset of millions of structures, the architectures can be compared under identical conditions. We further release PaiNN foundation models trained on 41.9 million curated DFT structures from MPtrj, Alexandria, OMat24, MatPES, OC20, OC22, OC25, MPr2SCAN and MatPESr2SCAN, spanning the PBE, RPBE and r2SCAN functionals. Additionally, IANN provides an agent interface to facilitate integration with autonomous agents.

papers.title: PIRanNN: Random-Feature Pricing and Calibration under Jump-Diffusion and Stochastic-Volatility Models

Compact Projected Pfaffian States for Rydberg-Blockaded Quantum Spin Systems
papers.abstract: We numerically demonstrate that a compact projected Pfaffian ansatz effectively describes the ground state of the nonintegrable PXP model. The variational wave function is obtained by applying separate Gutzwiller and Rydberg-blockade projectors to a general fermionic paired state, and each blockade-allowed configuration has an amplitude given by the Pfaffian of a configuration-selected pairing matrix. The exact blockade-projected product state of a known frustration-free deformation of the PXP model lies within the variational manifold and provides a physically motivated initial state for the variational Monte Carlo optimization toward the ground state of the pure PXP model. For a one-dimensional system of $N$ sites, optimizing all symmetry-allowed pairings in an $O(N)$-parameter wave function yields a near-exact ground state with a normalized energy variance (V-score) of order $10^{-9}$ despite the exponentially large blockade-constrained Hilbert space. On the square lattice, an $O(N)$-parameter wave function with the same amplitude structure yields relative energy errors below $0.2\%$ for clusters accessible to exact diagonalization and produces magnetizations consistent with available benchmarks. These results show that the same projected Pfaffian construction can be applied to blockade-constrained systems in both one and two dimensions.

papers.title: Charm quark energy loss fluctuations in clumpy color string medium
papers.abstract: We simulate charm quark propagation through an ensemble of color flux tubes formed between receding color charges in proton-proton collisions. Under the assumption of sharp string boundaries and a localized nature of the overlap regions, high flux tube densities lead to the formation of string clusters. We convert the local energy density of the superposed color field into an effective temperature of an ideal gluon gas and study the dependence of charm energy loss on its spatial inhomogeneities. By comparing different energy-density extraction prescriptions, we show that both elastic and inelastic momentum damping mechanisms are sensitive to the medium properties. However, the collisional channel is an order of magnitude smaller in absolute terms (up to $\sim0.15$~GeV) compared to the radiative loss (up to $\sim1.5$~GeV). Overall, the results demonstrate that the spatial overlap of individual strings generates a complex local energy density pattern, which predominantly governs the medium-induced quenching of charm quarks.

papers.title: Distance-Certified Polyak-type Stepsizes for Subgradient Methods under Hölder Growth
Rethinking Post-Training for Expressive Zero-Shot Text-to-Speech
papers.abstract: Zero-shot voice cloning typically emphasizes preserving the timbre and prosodic characteristics of a reference speaker. However, in real-world use, speech should adapt its delivery to the target text rather than remain tied to a fixed speaking style. In this work, we formulate this problem as text-adaptive prosody synthesis for zero-shot voice cloning and study how post-training can endow a cloning model with this capability. We develop a three-stage framework. First, Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) provides a cold start by aligning the model with text-appropriate expressive speech. Second, Group Sequence Policy Optimization (GSPO) jointly optimizes prosodic expressiveness, acoustic quality, intelligibility, and speaker similarity. Finally, context-conditioned On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) enables self-improvement by transferring expressive behavior from strong-reference to weak-reference conditions. On Qwen3-TTS, our framework improves Emotion from 18.5 to 81.2 and Paralinguistics from 38.4 to 73.9. Extensive ablations validate the role of each stage.

papers.title: Fine-Grained RLAIF for Visual Safety: Learning to Zoom into Hazards for Multimodal Safety Alignment
DynLimit: A Simulation Benchmark for Dynamics-Critical Planning and Control
How Should Parallel Langevin Chains Share Noise?
Conditional Asset Pricing Transformer
Efficient Recursive Evaluation of Gaussian, Gamma, and Inverse Gaussian Tail Probabilities
Charge-Transfer Energy Governed by $f$-$d$ Coulomb Interaction in Rare-Earth Systems
papers.abstract: The $f$-$d$ Coulomb interaction ($U_{\rm fd}$) plays a central role in low-energy theories describing valence fluctuations and quantum valence criticality in rare-earth systems. In contrast, core-level spectroscopies have conventionally been analyzed using the phenomenological charge-transfer energy ($\Delta$), and the relationship between these two descriptions has remained unclear. Here, we develop a spectroscopic framework demonstrating that the charge-transfer energy contains an $f$-$d$ Coulomb contribution $U_{\rm fd}n_d$ arising from the $d$-electron occupation ($n_d$), leading to the charge-transfer energy $\Delta'$. We apply this framework to the prototypical valence-transition compound YbInCu$_4$ and demonstrate, from combined analyses of core-level photoemission and $L$-edge x-ray absorption spectroscopy, that the observed spectroscopic evolution across the first-order valence transition is consistently interpreted in terms of the variation of $\Delta'$.

papers.title: A Threshold-Free Visual-Semantic Matching Metric for Evaluating Consistency in Subject-Driven Image Generation
Read Before You Fit: Text-Derived Constraints for Discovering Differential Equations from Noisy Biological Data
Wilsonian renormalization group flow in QED with the Pauli term
papers.abstract:
We study the renormalization group (RG) flow of quantum electrodynamics (QED) with a Pauli term, $\kappa_	au\Bar{\psi}\sigma_{\mu
u}F_{\mu
u}\psi$, by using the gradient flow exact renormalization group (GFERG). In the GFERG, the gauge Ward--Takahashi identity takes the conventional form and is exactly preserved, and the gauge coupling flows only through the photon anomalous dimension~$\gamma_A$. In the leading large-$N_f$ approximation, the vacuum polarization induced by the Pauli coupling yields a nontrivial fixed point with~$e_*=0$, $\kappa_*
eq0$, and~$\gamma_A=-1$. This fixed point has three relevant directions, as does one of the fixed points of the asymptotically safe QED proposed by Gies and Ziebell. At finite~$N_f$, however, the $N_f$-independent one-loop effects on the fermion line, in particular the additive mass renormalization proportional to~$\kappa^2$, eliminate this fixed point unless $N_f$ is at least several tens; for~$N_f=1$ there is no fixed point at weak Pauli coupling. Along the full flow for~$N_f=1$, $\kappa_	au$ is irrelevant and is attracted to an induced value~$\kappa_{	ext{ind}}(e_	au)$, which is proportional to~$e_	au^3$ at weak coupling, while $e_	au^2$ is marginally irrelevant as in QED without the Pauli term.

papers.title: Who May Release, Who Must Repair: Separating Authorization from Report Accountability in Personalized Services
Hidden Heat-Current Transport Channels Behind Observable Temperature Dynamics
papers.abstract: Diffusive decay and wave-like oscillations in temperature dynamics are commonly used to characterize heat conduction, yet these signatures do not uniquely identify the underlying heat-current transport mechanisms. Here we reveal a spectrum of constitutive heat-current channels whose microscopic organization can change without a corresponding qualitative change in observable temperature dynamics. We develop a two-level spectral theory that first resolves the finite-wave-vector constitutive response into relaxational and streaming channels characterized by their poles and heat-current residues, and then connects their combined response to equilibrium temperature fluctuations through energy conservation. First-principles calculations for NaF at 17~K reveal that the same streaming-induced mode coupling responsible for the perturbative nonlocal correction in the Guyer--Krumhansl (G--K) reduction drives a nonperturbative transformation of the isolated momentum-organized relaxational channel into a dominant complex-conjugate streaming pair. This transformation breaks down the single-relaxational-channel constitutive structure of G--K, while oscillatory temperature dynamics persist below the short-period boundary of its predicted oscillatory window. At shorter periods, heat-current weight redistributes among multiple collision-coupled streaming channels before approaching independently damped phonon streaming. Increasing temperature provides a distinct route beyond hydrodynamics by eliminating the isolated momentum-organized sector, even as oscillatory temperature dynamics persist. Thus, the breakdown of a hydrodynamic constitutive description can reflect a reorganization of heat-current transport rather than the disappearance of oscillatory temperature dynamics, and agreement with temperature measurements alone does not validate the constitutive structure of a reduced theory.

papers.title: Recovery-Guided Model-Based Diffusion for Safety-Critical Legged Locomotion
When Backdoors Can Be Switched Off: Suppression-Aware Backdoor Attacks on Vision-Language-Action Models
SemLite-GS: Semantic-Selective Parallel Gaussian Splatting for Lightweight Building Reconstruction from UAV Oblique Imagery
Tight Sequential Confidence Intervals for Online Kernel Regression
JEPA4R: Embodied JEPA World Models with 4D Point Planning
Exact Sparse Assignment with Costly Target Embeddings: Fixed-Realization Certificates and an Empirical Audit
Moderate deviations for semilinear stochastic evolution equations in fast Markovian environments
papers.abstract: This work establishes moderate deviation principles for semilinear stochastic evolution equations with coefficients depending on fast Markov environments. The environment is either an exponentially ergodic Markov process on a Polish space, independent of the noise, or a finite-state Markov chain whose transition rates depend on time and on a finite-dimensional observation of the state. The rate function is quadratic in the residual of the linearized dynamics. Its covariance is the sum of the averaged covariance of the Wiener noise and the asymptotic covariance generated by the environment, given by a Green--Kubo formula in the independent case and by a Poisson equation in the switching case. The rate function is written with the Moore--Penrose inverse of the square root of this covariance and requires the residual to lie in its range, not merely in the closure. This allows degenerate covariances and nonclosed ranges. In the switching case, the dependence of the invariant distribution on the slow state adds an extra term to the linearized drift. Since the stochastic convolution is not a semimartingale, the proofs combine the regeneration split chain technique with Galerkin approximation. The assumptions are verified for stochastic reaction--diffusion equations, including space-time white noise in one spatial dimension.

papers.title: PISG: Constraint-Aligned Signal Amplification for Diffusion-Based Combinatorial Optimization
Logical AI OS: A Training-Free Governance Layer Outside the Model for Instruction Following -- Benefits, Costs, Failures, and the Calibration of the Measuring Instrument Itself
Routing Information and Stationary Limits in Many-Server Load Balancing
papers.abstract: We study how routing information determines stationary congestion in many-server systems with Poisson arrivals and homogeneous exponential servers. We consider policies that prioritize idle servers and select a queue stochastically no longer than a uniformly sampled queue. In nondegenerate slowdown, where spare capacity is fixed, we identify population laws from the fraction of queues with waiting jobs at each population level. We establish these laws for one-job priority, join-idle-queue, and idle-first sampling. One-job priority attains the join-the-shortest-queue population law and mean delays; further queue information can improve limiting delays in convex order without changing their means. In the super-Halfin-Whitt and Halfin-Whitt regimes, every such policy has the same stationary limits. Our estimates bound idleness-weighted occupancy tails in terms of ordinary tails, uniformly over queue-length thresholds and policies. They also yield process convergence and limit interchange for initial laws uniformly dominated by stationarity, with convergent scaled initial states.

papers.title: M-CROSS: A Multisensor Simulation Dataset for SLAM across Water--Land Transitions
Compositional Exploits in Autonomous Coding Agents: Attack Mechanics and Ephemeral Defense
Ambiguous Examples Help, But Full Data Wins: Revisiting Dataset Cartography for Extractive Adversarial QA
When Does an AUROC Comparison Survive a Change in Population Mix?
Algebraic instantons and non-Gaussian vacuum in quantum mechanics
papers.abstract: The standard instanton calculus in quantum mechanics is based on harmonic minima in the potential. When the perturbative vacuum is anharmonic, $V\simeq\lambda x^{2n}$ with $n\ge2$, the standard construction fails. We study this problem for a particle on a circle and subject to a potential $V(x)=16\lambda\sin^4(x/2)$. The instanton and its fluctuation operator are known in closed form, but they differ qualitatively from the familiar ones. Because $V''=0$ at the minimum, the classical vacuum is gapless, the instanton decays algebraically (an algebraic instanton), the zero mode is located at the threshold of a continuous spectrum, and the one-loop determinant is infrared divergent. Quantum mechanics generates a non-perturbative gap $E_q\propto\hbar^{4/3}\lambda^{1/3}$, and the instanton is embedded in a vacuum that is dynamically gapped, similar to what happens in Yang--Mills theory. We show that the one-instanton amplitude can be computed by matching the instanton trajectory to the exact vacuum part of the path integral. The resulting prefactor scales as $\hbar^{4/3}$, and this expression agrees with the numerical spectrum to a very high accuracy. The classical interaction between instantons decays as $T^{-3}$, whereas the correct result is an exponential decay controlled by the dynamically generated gap, beyond the quantum time scale. We provide an alternative derivation of this result based on a sum over intermediate states.

papers.title: The Fourier Ratio on Resistance Spaces and Applications to Electrical Networks
papers.abstract: We study the Fourier Ratio for spectral expansions of nonnegative self-adjoint operators. Weighted Cauchy--Schwarz estimates turn eigenvalue counting bounds into Fourier Ratio bounds for spectrally regular functions. On a compact measured resistance space, Kasue's identity expresses the reciprocal eigenvalue sum as one half of the average resistance distance. We use this identity to obtain a sharp coefficient estimate for every finite-energy function, with no spectral cutoff. Bounded orthonormal system recovery theorems then yield reconstruction estimates whose sample counts depend on both the Fourier Ratio and the pointwise size of the chosen eigenfunctions. We distinguish these estimates from the weaker diameter-only bounds and give an interval example with a sample count logarithmic in the dimension of the spectral subspace for fixed accuracy and energy ratio. Resistance also controls errors caused by displaced sensors. We apply the estimates to standard self-similar fractals and finite electrical networks, where the geometric constant becomes the normalized square root of the Kirchhoff index. A separate observation describes Fourier Ratios of coefficient families with a limiting distribution.

papers.title: Isolated Singularities Not Resolved by Iterated Nash Blowups
papers.abstract: Castillo, Duarte, Leyton-Álvarez, and Liendo asked whether iterating ordinary Nash blowups in characteristic zero or normalized Nash blowups in arbitrary characteristic can fail to resolve isolated singularities arXiv:2511.17862 . We answer this question affirmatively with two constructions of isolated singularities, one nonnormal and one normal, both giving counterexamples to normalized Nash iteration in every characteristic.

papers.title: Fate of chiral and $U(1)_A$ symmetries in hot QCD matter under background magnetic fields
papers.abstract: We summarize our recent lattice QCD study of chiral and singlet $U(1)_A$ symmetry breaking in background magnetic fields. The magnetic field explicitly reduces the non-singlet flavor symmetry through the unequal light-quark electric charges. We therefore study two neutral-channel susceptibility differences: $\chi_{\pi^0}-\chi_\sigma$ for chiral symmetry breaking and $\chi_{\pi^0}-\chi_{\delta^0}$ for singlet $U(1)_A$ symmetry breaking. The calculation uses fixed-scale $(2+1)$-flavor HISQ ensembles with $m_l=m_s^{\mathrm{phys}}/10$, corresponding to a zero-field pion mass of $M_\pi\simeq220\,\mathrm{MeV}$. Magnetic fields enhance both susceptibility differences at low temperatures. Near the crossover, sufficiently strong fields instead suppress both differences. The suppression sets in at larger magnetic fields and is milder for the singlet-axial susceptibility difference than for the neutral chiral susceptibility difference.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal Reconstruction of Auroral Precipitations with Neural Fields
Drift-Conditioned Structural Replay for Continual Cardiac Ultrasound Segmentation
Fourier Ratio Bounds and Sensitivity to Sensor Placement
papers.abstract: We study how the regularity of a continuous function controls the Fourier ratio of its sampled values, and how errors in sensor placement affect recovery from incomplete measurements. For a periodic function on the square sampled on an $N$ by $N$ grid, we show that Hölder regularity $C^{0,\gamma}$ with $0<\gamma<1$ leads to a bound of order $N^{1-\gamma}$, that Lipschitz regularity leads to the critical bound $\sqrt{1+\log N}$, and that fractional Sobolev regularity $W^{s,p}$ with $0<s<1$ and $sp>2$ leads to a bound of order $N^{1-s}$, where both polynomial exponents are sharp. A common translation of the grid removes the hypothesis on the sampled mass needed on a fixed grid and yields an estimate in terms of the $L^2$ norm of the gradient, and with two derivatives the bound is independent of the grid size. We extend the energy argument behind these results to compact Riemannian manifolds and prove that the critical square-root logarithm is necessary on every compact surface.
