Explicit constructions and computational certificates show that these bounds are attained for several cases, including grids of dimensions $5\times5\times100$, $5\times6\times75$, and $6\times6\times75$. For the grid of dimension $5\times7\times c$, we construct a box-free coloring with $c=50$, while our counting bound gives $c\leq 52$. This gap suggests that the counting bound may not always be sharp. We also investigate the largest $n\times n\times n$ cube admitting a box-free 2-coloring. We found box-free colorings of the $n$-cube for $n\leq 10$, and colorings of the $11\times11\times11$ cube with only eight monochromatic boxes. On the other hand, we show that every 2-coloring of the $21\times21\times21$ cube contains at least 21 monochromatic boxes. Thus the largest box-free cube has side length between 10 and 20, inclusive. We conclude with conjectures and open problems.

papers.title: Multi-Objective Causal Bandits: Minimal Intervention Space and Policy-Level Learning
Probability of Success under Population Shift for Phase III Trial Planning
papers.abstract: Probability of success (PoS) is widely used to inform go/no-go decisions for phase III trials based on phase II evidence. Conventional PoS calculations, however, implicitly assume that baseline covariate distributions are identical across phases. When covariate shift exists between phase II and phase III populations, unadjusted PoS may be biased and lead to miscalibrated decision-making. We propose a Bayesian framework for PoS evaluation that explicitly accounts for covariate shift between phase II and III population prior to phase III initiation. The method adopts a transportability perspective, adjusting phase II evidence to reflect an anticipated phase III target population using available target covariate information. The framework accommodates both individual-level and aggregate-level phase III covariate data. Simulation studies demonstrate that, compared with the conventional approach, the proposed method improves PoS accuracy and decision calibration when covariate shift is present, while maintaining comparable performance when populations are aligned. We illustrate the proposed methodology using clinical trial data from systemic lupus erythematosus.

papers.title: Ramsey Numbers of Most Even-Linked Double Stars
papers.abstract: For $n \geq m$, the linked double star $S_c(n, m)$ is the graph formed by taking two disjoint stars $K_{1, n}$ and $K_{1, m}$ and linking their centers with a path on $c$ vertices. In this paper, we investigate the Ramsey numbers of even-linked double stars, that is, where $c = 2p$ for some $p \in \mathbb{N}$. Determining the Ramsey numbers of the $p = 1$ case (classical double stars) is a longstanding open question; the $p = 2$ case was resolved by Burr and Erdős in 1976, and Liu and Chen made progress for general even-linked double stars in 2026. We extend Burr and Erdős' formula for $p = 2$, proving that the Ramsey number of $S_{2p}(n, m)$ is given by \[r(S_{2p}(n, m)) = \max(2n + 2p - 1, n + 2m + 3p - 1),\]when $m \geq p -2 \geq 0$. Our upper bound argument hinges upon the existence (or nonexistence) of an object that we call a polarized pair. We also establish a matching lower bound that applies for all $n, m, p \geq 2$, and as such, we conjecture that this formula applies for all even-linked double stars where $p \geq 2$.

papers.title: Orion I: Discovery of an Isolated dE,N Galaxy at 60 Mph
papers.abstract: Inspection of deep JWST images centered on the lensing cluster of galaxies MACS J0454.1-0300 reveals a small, well resolved stellar system that is clearly in the foreground. Photometric measurements including a color-magnitude diagram and radial profile show that it is a nucleated dwarf early-type galaxy (dE,N) at a distance of ~60 Mpc and with structurally normal properties. This object (J04:54:07.39-02:59:22.5, referred to as Orion I for shorthand) may be an outlying member of a previously known small galaxy group, or may be simply an isolated field galaxy depending on the accuracy of its distance estimate. The discovery of Orion I suggests that other small stellar systems in the nearby universe might be found through a search of the many deep \jwst imaging fields that are now being accumulated.

papers.title: Where slide-level foundation-model classifiers fail on atypical breast lesions
Conic Frames, Cosine Measure, and Gaussian Frames
papers.abstract: Conic combinations play an important role across mathematics in areas such as optimization, non-negative matrix factorization, and sparse coding. Frames which span their underlying space using only conic combinations, known as positive spanning sets or conic frames, are of special interest in derivative free optimization. In particular, sets with large cosine measure, a measure of how spread out the vectors are, are favored. We focus on the asymptotics of the cosine measure of Gaussian frames and present tail bounds in a variety of regimes.

papers.title: Comparative Analysis of Influences of Magnetic Field Inputs on Simulating the 2017 September 10 Solar Energetic Particle Event
papers.abstract: Physics-based solar energetic particle (SEP) models simulate the ambient solar wind, coronal mass ejections (CMEs), and SEPs using photospheric magnetic field maps as the inner boundary condition. In this study, we select the 2017 September 10 SEP event, which produced the first ground level enhancement observed on the surfaces of both Earth and Mars, to examine how these inputs influence the modeled results. We use the SOlar wind with FIeld lines and Energetic particles (SOFIE) model suite, driven independently by the GONG and ADAPT-GONG magnetic field maps, to simulate the solar wind, CME, and SEPs from the low corona to beyond Mars' orbit. The two maps yield different open flux regions and hence different solar wind conditions, both globally comparable to in situ observations at Earth, STA, and Mars, with the GONG-driven results performing slightly better. We find that in the ADAPT-GONG-driven run, a more energetic CME flux rope propagates into a slower, wider stream, producing broader CME expansion and a more extended shock, which reaches both planets within ~4 hours of the observed arrival, while the GONG-driven run misses both arrivals. Both simulations reproduce the observed SEP fluxes at Earth within a factor of ~3, while the ADAPT-GONG-driven results compare better with observations at Mars, which connects magnetically to the shock flank. Therefore, for this event, the relative performance of the two simulations depends on the observer and observable, with SEP fluxes shaped by CME propagation through the ambient solar wind and by magnetic connectivity to the evolving shock.

papers.title: A Recursive Construction of Perfect and Odd Perfect Sequences of Unbounded Length over the Unit Quaternions
Spectral action in Betti metaplectic Langlands
papers.abstract: We construct the spectral action in the context of Betti metaplectic Langlands theory. More precisely, we prove that the category of twisted sheaves on $\text{Bun}_G$ with nilpotent singular support admits a canonical action by the symmetric monoidal category of quasicoherent sheaves on the moduli of twisted $H$-local systems, where $H$ is the metaplectic dual group. This confirms the Betti version of the conjecture of Gaitsgory--Lysenko, originally formulated in the de Rham setting under the name ``metaplectic vanishing conjecture". Given a symmetric monoidal category with suitable symmetry, we develop a categorical framework by introducing a notion of twisted factorization homology and studying its categorical action. We show that the category of quasicoherent sheaves on the moduli of twisted local systems can be realized as a twisted factorization homology. Using metaplectic factorizable Satake we further prove that the metaplectic Hecke action naturally fits into our categorical framework. Combining these results, we obtain the desired spectral action.

papers.title: Robust Well-Log Reconstruction Across Point Gaps and Whole Wells via Boundary-Gated Soft-Thresholding Kalman Fusion
Well-Log Reconstruction with Pre-trained Geological Knowledge: A Knowledge-Conditioned Large-Language-Model Generative Agent
Data-Driven Heuristic-Guided Business Process Redesign
Integrability of the Schrödinger Equation for a Mie-type Potential via the NU Method and Appell-type Hypergeometric Polynomials
papers.abstract: We establish a formal correspondance between the Appell-type hypergeometric polynomials $\widetilde{e}_n$, rectently introduced in [1], and the exact solutions od the radial Schrödinger equation for a family of Mie-type potentials. Using the Nikiforov-Uvarov (NU) method, we show that the radial equation reduces to an hypergeometric differential equation with a parameter $N$, which plays the role of an effective principal quantum number. A careful analysis of th asymptotic behavior of the solutions reveals a dual structure: the confluent hypergeometric function of the second kind $U$ yields square-integrable bound states, for which the condition $N\in \mathbb{N}$ provides a quantization condition of Diophantine type, and a discrete energy spectrum. In contrast, the generalized Laguerre function $L$, of a certain type, yields non-normalizable scattering states. In the particular case of vanishing angular momentum $(l=0)$, these scattering stetes truncte into the Appell-type polynomial $\widetilde{e}_n$, which thus characterize the s-wave scattering of the Mie-type potential. This work therefore provides a unified algebraic framework for both bound and scattering states, and clarifies the physical scope of the Appell-type polynomials.

papers.title: Toward Planning Representations That Separate Task Structure from Visual Content
Braid monodromy and the Cartwright--Steger surface
papers.abstract: Building on the Livne-like construction of Cartwright, Koziarz and Yeung, we construct a closed smooth 4-manifold with a map to the two-sphere whose generic fiber has genus 109 and whose four exceptional fibers are determined by explicit braid and permutation data. A pencil of four-pointed spheres realizes the same global braid monodromy and makes the covering holomorphic. We show that the contraction of its thirty-six exceptional curves is the Cartwright-Steger surface, hence our smooth construction gives a topological description of this complex surface.

papers.title: On the boomerang spectrum of the APN power function $x^{q+2}$ over $\F_{q^2}$
Latency-Preserving Rewrites and Translation Validation for Dynamic Quantum Circuits
Sharp fill-in inequalities and rigidity for spin initial data sets
papers.abstract: We prove sharp fill-in inequalities for compact spin initial data sets satisfying the dominant energy condition. The inequalities relate the spacetime mean curvature of the boundary to its hyperspherical radius and stable one-systole. Equality characterizes spacelike graphs of constant boundary height over round Euclidean balls and, in the systolic case after passing to the universal cover, over products of a round disk with Euclidean space. We also prove rigidity under comparison with strictly convex Euclidean domains, using normalized boundary metrics. The proofs use a modified Dirac operator with a chiral boundary condition.

papers.title: Towards Probabilistically Safe Reinforcement Learning: Theory and Deployment on Humanoid and Aerial Robots
The $J$-Homomorphism From Localising The Cobordism Hypothesis
papers.abstract: Lurie's cobordism hypothesis classifies fully extended framed topological field theories valued in a symmetric monoidal $(\infty,n)$-category $\mathcal{C}$ with duals by the $\infty$-groupoid $\mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{fd}}$ of fully dualisable objects. This classification results in an $O(n)$-action on $\mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{fd}}$, where $O(n)$ acts on the framed bordism category by change of framing. Lurie observed that for a connective spectrum, this action is ``a version of the classical $J$-homomorphism.'' We make this identification explicit: with respect to the right action of $O(n)$ on framings, the $O(n)$-action on the localisation $L(\mathrm{Bord}_n^{\mathrm{fr}}) \simeq S$ is precisely $\ominus J_n$, the inverse of the unstable $J$-homomorphism $J_n \colon O(n) \to \mathrm{GL}_1(S)$. The identification of the action with the unstable $J$-homomorphism in the setting of smooth stacks is due to Grady--Pavlov; we give an independent proof in Lurie's original formulation of the cobordism hypothesis, using the abstract Pontryagin--Thom construction. The sign (i.e.\ whether the action is $J_n$ or $\ominus J_n$) depends on the convention for the $O(n)$-action on framings, and is relevant for $\mathrm{pin}^\pm$ theories and hence for quantum systems with time-reversal symmetry. We compute the induced action on homotopy groups of the sphere spectrum in low degrees, yielding explicit invariants for invertible TFTs in dimensions $1$, $2$, and $3$, and connect these to the Kitaev chain, the framing anomaly, the spin-statistics theorem, and anomaly inflow. We recover the Galatius--Madsen--Tillmann--Weiss theorem as a consequence of the cobordism hypothesis and relate the homotopy fixed-point and mapping-spectrum perspectives on invertible TFTs via the duality between tangential and normal framings.

papers.title: A Hierarchical Statistical Framework for Evaluating Agent Reliability
papers.abstract: Agents operating in complex scenarios often face uncertainty due to incomplete information about the environment they operate in, ambiguous user queries, complex business rules and the inherently stochastic dynamics of the governing policy. Several new benchmarks have been proposed to evaluate LLM-based agents on complex tasks in multi-tool environments, including settings with policy constraints and varying levels of intent ambiguity. These conditions make it important to evaluate agentic systems systematically and quantify their performance under different conditions to assess their reliability in production. This need is evident in the recently introduced Thinkingbox benchmark, where even the strongest models struggle to perform consistently across diverse business scenarios. This paper presents a statistical framework for evaluating uncertainty and reliability in agentic systems. We define a hierarchy of scenarios, instances, and samples to assess model performance and variability systematically. We apply this framework to common metrics found in the literature: mean pass rate, $pass@k$, and $passhat^k$, with uncertainty estimates for each metric. Aggregating metrics at different levels of the hierarchy reveals different structures and properties of the policy model; we connect this hierarchical aggregation with the known process of \emph{coarse-graining} as intended in the physics and statistical literature. We independently derive exact finite-sample expressions for the sampling variances of the unbiased $pass@k$ and $passhatk$ estimators; related results also appear in recent submissions. Our central contribution is a constructive derivation of hierarchical uncertainty propagation, making explicit its correspondence with coarse-graining and separating execution noise from task heterogeneity.

papers.title: Towards Understanding the Complexity of CAQE: A Proof-Theoretic Analysis of its Core Procedure
Discovery of Ultra Fast Outflows in the Narrow Line Seyfert 1 Galaxy Mrk 110 with XMM-Newton and NuSTAR
papers.abstract: We present an X-ray analysis of XMM-Newton and NuSTAR spectra of the Narrow-Line Seyfert 1 (NLS1) galaxy Mrk 110. Our analysis reveals the intriguing presence of a multi-component ultra fast outflow (UFO) both in the grating spectrum and the NuSTAR data. The moderate UFO significance (3-4$\sigma$), in the grating and CCD data indicates a shallow absorber, consistently with the absence of previous such claims in this source. The two components (UFO1 and UFO2) in the grating spectrum show a fairly wide range of velocities (0.05-0.06c), as their respective ionization state (Log U = -1.43 and -1.82), however they share the same column density (Log N$_H$ $\sim$ 19.7). In the NuSTAR spectrum, we found a much faster wind component with a velocity of $\sim$ 0.21c (UFO3). We show that, in an energy-driven wind scenario, UFO3 might carry enough energy to produce significant feedback on its host galaxy. Considering its known radio properties, Mrk 110 is therefore another Narrow-Line Seyfert 1 with stratified ultra-fast outflows co-existent with a pc-scale jet/outflow radio structure.

papers.title: Nonsmooth Convex and Strongly Convex Optimization from Noisy Comparisons
papers.abstract: We study nonsmooth convex and strongly convex optimization problems using only noisy pairwise comparisons: each query specifies two points and returns a single binary response indicating which point has the smaller function value, subject to noise. We distinguish two observation models: Stochastic Order Oracles, which compare two evaluations of the same random loss, and Preference Oracles, whose conditional response mean is a transfer function of the objective difference. For Stochastic Order Oracles, we prove that no comparison-based algorithm can guarantee vanishing expected suboptimality in general, even when sample losses are convex and Lipschitz and the mean objective is strongly convex. Under a normalized probit calibration, we recover convergence and establish matching upper and lower rates for convex and strongly convex objectives. For Preference Oracles with a linear response model, the binary response $O \in \{\pm1\}$ satisfies $\E[O\mid y,z]=\lambda(f(y)-f(z))$, with $\lambda>0$. In dimension $d$, we obtain an upper bound of $\widetilde (d^{3/2}/(\lambda\sqrt N))$ and establish, to our knowledge, the first minimax lower bound of $\Omega(d/(\lambda\sqrt N))$, matching the optimal budget $N$ exponent, for both convex and strongly convex nonsmooth objectives. Beyond exact linearity, we analyze a simple projected comparison method for nonlinear transfer functions and establish convergence rates that depend on how accurately these functions can be approximated by a linear model near zero. Our analysis requires neither oddness nor twice differentiability of the transfer function.

papers.title: On the number of elite primes
papers.abstract: A prime $p$ is elite if all sufficiently large Fermat numbers $F_n=2^{2^n}+1$ are quadratic nonresidues modulo $p$. Let $E(x)$ be the number of elite primes up to $x$. The best published bounds are $E(x)\ll x/(\log x)^{3/2}$ unconditionally and $E(x)\ll x^{5/6}$ under the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH), both due to Just. Just and Pollack remarked, without a written proof, that sorting primes by the exact power of $2$ dividing $p-1$ should give $x/(\log x)^{2-\varepsilon}$ and $x^{3/4+\varepsilon}$. We give complete proofs of slightly sharper statements: $E(x)\le(16+o(1))x\log\log x/(\log x)^2$ unconditionally, and $E(x)\ll x^{3/4}(\log x)^{1/2}$ under GRH. We also recall, with short proofs, known facts about the period of $(F_n\bmod p)$ that go back to Aigner: every elite prime $p$ satisfies the defining condition from the index $v_2(\operatorname{ord}_p 2)$ onwards, and the period is even unless $p\in\{3,5\}$. Finally, we show under GRH that, when the moduli involved are at most $x^{1/3}$, the set of primes bounded by the sieve argument has size $\asymp x\log\log x/(\log x)^2$. This indicates that the remaining factor $\log\log x$ cannot be removed by this method alone. All theorems of the paper have been formalized in the Lean 4 proof assistant, with the Brun--Titchmarsh inequality and two standard consequences of GRH as explicit hypotheses.

papers.title: Before the Word: Name Information in Description-Derived States of Small Language Models, With and Without Naming Failure
Impact of Wind-Solar-Battery Growth on Electricity Prices: Reserve Scarcity and Transmission Congestion
Symbolic Powers and Asymptotic Invariants of Invariant Ideals in Determinantal Rings
papers.abstract: Let $A$ be the coordinate ring of a bounded-rank locus of generic, symmetric, alternating, or Hankel matrices. Thus $A$ is the quotient of a polynomial ring by a generic determinantal, symmetric determinantal, generic Pfaffian, or Hankel determinantal ideal. In each case there is a nested family of rank primes ${\mathfrak p}_1\supset {\mathfrak p}_2\supset\cdots\supset{\mathfrak p}_q$ and a standard-monomial basis whose shapes are diagrams with parts at most $q$. We isolate the common properties of these four straightening theories and use them to give a uniform treatment of products $D_\sigma={\mathfrak p}_{\sigma_1}\cdots{\mathfrak p}_{\sigma_s}$ in the quotient ring $A$, extending analogous results over suitable polynomial rings. In all four cases the shape $\sigma$ must have parts of size at most $q$. We determine their primary decompositions and associated primes in the rank-$q$ quotient, compute all symbolic powers with respect to the full set of associated primes, and prove that their symbolic Rees algebras are finitely generated. In the generic, symmetric, and alternating cases the respective symbolic Rees algebras are also normal, and Cohen--Macaulay. We also determine the asymptotic resurgence $\widehat\rho$ and Waldschmidt constants of these ideals and prove they are related by $\widehat\rho(D_\sigma)=\alpha(D_\sigma)/\widehat\alpha(D_\sigma)$.

papers.title: The $E_6$-Grassmannian, its minuscule Coxeter matroids, and the lines on a cubic surface
papers.abstract: We study the minuscule Coxeter matroids of type $E_6$, whose ground set is the set of 27 lines on a smooth cubic surface. We characterize them by a tritangent exchange property and classify them into 230 orbits under the Weyl group. Every nonempty matroidal stratum of the $E_6$-Grassmannian is an open subscheme of a torus, and all orbits but one are realizable over every infinite field. Finally, we compute the tropical $E_6$-Grassmannian and its 60 classes of toric degenerations. This is an extended abstract for a forthcoming paper.

papers.title: Quantum sine imaginary-time evolution: sequential and QSVT implementations of a probabilistic ground-state filter
papers.abstract: We propose quantum sine imaginary-time evolution (QSITE), a quantum algorithm for preparing ground states of a Hamiltonian. QSITE approximates imaginary-time evolution through an exact sine filter. We give two circuit implementations of this operator: a sequential one that applies it as a concatenation of linear combinations of unitaries (LCU), reusing two ancilla qubits across steps via mid-circuit measurement, and a coherent one based on the quantum singular value transformation (QSVT). A telescoping identity shows the two prepare the same state and succeed with identical probability, differing only in how that probability can be boosted. QSITE belongs to the family of ancilla-based probabilistic imaginary-time filters and we state rigorous convergence guarantees: we prove that the QSITE operator converges uniformly to the exact ITE operator, that the prepared state converges to the ideal ITE state, and that the filter probability increases monotonically with each concatenation step. Although the construction applies to an arbitrary Hamiltonian, we specialize it to optimization Hamiltonians, and this specialization is what exposes its structure more easily. Since MaxCut eigenvalues are integers, the probability of failure is periodic in the evolution time, yielding safe zones, the first located analytically and the second numerically. For MaxCut we further show that, when the tolerated energy error is a fixed fraction of the ground-state energy, the probability of failure can be bounded below 1/2 with concatenation steps growing linearly with the number of qubits in the first safe zone. We present numerical results for random Erdös-Rényi instances with up to 24 qubits and benchmark QSITE against QAOA.

papers.title: Positivity and Boundedness of Solutions to the Guyon-Lekeufack Volatility Model with General Kernels
papers.abstract: We study nonnegativity of the volatility in the continuous-time Guyon-Lekeufack model, in which volatility is an affine function of the convolution of past returns with a kernel $K_1$ and the square root of the integral of past squared returns weighted by a kernel $K_2$. We show that, when volatility is nonnegative and $K_1$ admits a resolvent of the first kind, uniform boundedness of integrals of $K_2$ with respect to this resolvent yields a deterministic upper bound for the asset price, which is then a bounded martingale on every finite time interval. This result is the counterpart of the strict local martingality criterion for negative volatility in Guyon, Jeannin and Jourdain (2026, Corollary 2.6(ii)). We also derive such bounds for popular stochastic volatility models when the Brownian motions driving the asset price and volatility have correlation $-1$. We give sufficient conditions for nonnegative volatility with a completely monotone return convolution kernel $K_1$, and necessary conditions when $K_1$ and $K_2$ are respectively $M$- and $N$-exponential kernels. For $M=1$, we obtain a necessary and sufficient condition.

papers.title: NAP-Wave: A Neural Adaptive Plane-Wave Architecture for High-Frequency Helmholtz Problems
AC Assessment of DC Power Flow Screening for Data Center Hosting Capacity and Siting
Are Average Estimates in Line Graphs Biased Toward Areas of Higher Variability?
The Deepest Pairs of Points Are Not as Deep as Conjectured
The Dedekind-MacNeille Completion as a Functor
papers.abstract: We study the Dedekind-MacNeille completion through representable functors on the wide subcategory $\mathbf{Pos}_{\mathrm{cl}}$ of posets and lower cut-continuous (closed) maps. On this category the completion is contravariantly functorial and naturally isomorphic to $\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf{Pos}_{\mathrm{cl}}}(-,[1])^{\mathrm{op}}$, via $A\mapsto\chi_A$ and its inverse $f\mapsto f^{-1}(\{0\})$. The naturality of this identification makes the Yoneda lemma applicable: uniqueness of the representing object and the endomorphism monoid of the completion follow formally. We also show that $\mathbf{CLat}_\vee$ is full in $\mathbf{Pos}_{\mathrm{cl}}$, that $\mathbf{CLat}_\wedge$ is equivalent to a full subcategory of $\mathbf{Pos}_{\mathrm{cl}}^{\mathrm{op}}$, and that the covariant adjunction refines to a $2$-adjunction whose idempotent monad has Eilenberg--Moore algebras equivalent to $\mathbf{CLat}_\vee$.

papers.title: Protecting the System, Stranding the User: The Limits of Multi-Agent Authorization
Synthetic Neurosymbolic Task Generation with Controlled Constraint Complexity
Scaling laws in machine learning on non-ideal experimental data enable inverse design of radiative-cooling coatings
papers.abstract: Materials informatics increasingly targets multicomponent materials, yet experimental datasets inevitably contain non-ideal variations arising from imperfect uniformity and reproducibility in composition, coating formation, and measurement. Whether machine-learning prediction accuracy scales with amount of data under these conditions remains unclear. Here, we develop an automated platform that produced and optically characterized 11,520 radiative-cooling coatings spanning nine material and processing parameters. Forward and inverse neural networks, and a spectrum-conditioned diffusion model were trained on subsets of 10 to 10,000 samples. All models exhibited power-law scaling, with prediction errors decreasing with dataset size. Experimental inverse-design validation showed that larger datasets produced spectra closer to a broadband-emitter target. The diffusion model generated multiple candidate parameter sets, allowing selection among alternative solutions based on ease of fabrication, cost, and scalability. These results demonstrate predictable learning-curve scaling in non-ideal experimental data and provide a quantitative basis for estimating the benefit of additional experimental data, and thus the cost-effectiveness of materials-informatics.

papers.title: Chiral Majorana Charge Kondo Criticality
papers.abstract: Unambiguous identification of chiral Majorana edge modes remains challenging because the transport signatures proposed for them can also arise from conventional mechanisms. Here we identify the chiral Majorana charge Kondo (CMCK) critical point as a more discriminating many-body route to detect chiral Majorana edge modes. This criticality arises in a charged island hosting a single chiral Majorana edge mode, where Majorana self-conjugacy locks normal and anomalous tunneling amplitudes, so that each physical lead provides two Kondo screening channels without fine tuning. Ordinary subgap states generically break this locking and drive the system toward conventional charge Kondo (CK) behavior. In the simplest two-terminal geometry, CMCK and conventional CK share the critical conductance $G^*=e^2/2h$, but their leading conductance corrections scale as $T^{1/3}$ and $T$, respectively. Their residual entropies also differ, as do the crossover exponents under gate detuning and contact asymmetry. For $N$ leads, CMCK conductance corrections scale as $T^{1/(N+1)}$, and for $N\geq3$ even the critical conductance differs from that of conventional CK with the same number of leads. These universal signatures are testable using established charge-Kondo measurement techniques.

papers.title: A New Record for the Katz-Tao Sum-Difference Exponent
papers.abstract: We prove the record bound $C_{3b}\le 209357544569848128/114631769327023765=1.8263483657186\ldots$ for the Katz-Tao sum-difference exponent, valid in every abelian group without $2$-torsion. Using only Shannon inequalities, conditional copies and Katz-Tao's original directions, whose classical single-grid argument gives $11/6$, we break $11/6$, obtaining $2762/1509$ and $152/83$. For every abelian group we prove the universal bound $C_{\mathrm{all}}=10304335425987192362/5641833174538280329=1.8264161855212\ldots$, which is below the previous record for the real Katz-Tao constant. In the AlphaEvolve study ( arXiv:2511.02864v3 ), the search for extremal distributions improved this constant's lower bound in the eighth decimal place and left its upper bound at $11/6$. Our upper bounds are proofs discovered by CASPAC, the computational mathematics engine of the CASP research system, and certified by independent exact checkers. The proofs use stacked entropy certificates; we supply the complete rational identities, proofs of every auxiliary inequality, and exact verification over the stated group classes.

papers.title: Learning Spatially Aware Audio-Visual Features from Videos with Mono Audio
Computing Independent Sets of Size Three in Disk Graphs
Extracting Damping Ratio and Shear Wave Velocity through Joint Inversion of Rayleigh Wave Attenuation and Phase Velocity Data
papers.abstract: Methods for reliable in-situ estimation of small-strain damping ratio remain far less developed than those for in-situ shear wave velocity (Vs) measurements. For surface wave-based approaches, challenges with extracting damping ratios are caused by both difficulties associated with developing attenuation coefficients from recorded wavefields and complexities involved when interpreting their multimodal irregularities during inversion. This study presents a joint inversion framework for extracting shear damping ratio (Ds0) and Vs profiles from Rayleigh-wave attenuation and phase velocity data using a viscoelastic predominant-mode approach. Unlike conventional inversion, the proposed formulation identifies the mode contributing most strongly to the measured wavefield, allowing multimodal attenuation and dispersion data to be incorporated without explicit modal indexing. This approach has significant benefits for inverting attenuation data, whose modal behavior is much more irregular than phase velocity. A coupled inversion strategy is adopted to jointly estimate the Vs and Ds0 while addressing their different sensitivities to phase velocity and attenuation. The predominant-mode attenuation concept is first validated against two synthetic ground models of increasing complexity. The synthetic inversion results demonstrate the framework's ability to recover the Ds0 and Vs profiles and capture modal transitions associated with a low-velocity layer. The framework is then applied to active-source field data from Mirandola, Italy, where the fundamental mode dominates, and Bird's Landing, California, where a soft peat layer produces significant higher-modes. At both sites, the inverted Vs profiles agreed well with independent site characterization data, while the damping estimates exhibit physically plausible trends and provide site-specific information that complements empirical estimates.

papers.title: Splitting and Mixed Deformations of Toric Generalized Kähler Potentials
papers.abstract: We study splitting phenomena for extremal toric generalized Kähler structures on products of compact toric manifolds. We prove that every extremal symplectic potential splits when the skew-symmetric parameter $B$ is block diagonal, without any restriction on $A$. We also construct two types of non-splitting examples on $\mathbb{CP}^1\times\mathbb{CP}^1$: an explicit constant-generalized-scalar-curvature structure with a splitting potential but a non-product generalized Kähler structure, and a deformation family of constant-generalized-scalar-curvature structures with genuinely non-splitting potentials.

papers.title: On the false discovery rate of one-sided p-values under Gaussian dependence
papers.abstract: We study the false discovery rate (FDR) of the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure for $K$ hypotheses at nominal level $q$ under Gaussian dependence of one-sided p-values. We ask whether the global null is least favorable after optimizing over correlation matrices. We show that the global null attains the worst-case FDR for $K\le3$ at every level. In dimension eight, an explicit mixed-null construction has FDR $21q/20$ for $0<q<1/2$. It exceeds the global-null maximum for all sufficiently small $q$, by a uniform extension of the known fixed-matrix small-level Simes bound. For $0<q<1/2$, we identify eight as the first inflation dimension in the monotone rank-one class and prove that $21q/20$ is its exact eight-dimensional maximum. In the same level range, the sharp multiplicative bound over all dimensions in this class is twice the omega constant $w = W(1)$, where $W$ is the Lambert $W$ function. This bound is approached as the dimension increases. We also give scale conditions for stability around the independence benchmark $m_0q/K$, where $m_0$ is the number of true nulls, and obtain a dimension-free upper bound of $q+q^2/2+O(q^3)$ at small levels under the global null with nonpositive correlations.

papers.title: PBit1: One Programmable P-Bit per Parameter - A Finite-Control Representation of Pretrained Networks
Explicit Regularization for Flow Matching
SLiDE: Structured Linear Dynamics for Forecasting with Exogenous Inputs
The stable false discovery rate
papers.abstract: When a discovery depends on analysis choices, a list of selected hypotheses that controls the false discovery rate (FDR) gives little indication of how easily the finding could change: the selected set may be very sensitive to a variety of analyst choices, like the target FDR level, which machine learning algorithms are used in the pipeline, the choice of test statistics, and so on. We propose that scientists should measure and control a new metric called the \emph{stable FDR} (sFDR), and give methods to control it, including simple wrappers around existing FDR analysis pipelines. sFDR is a natural continuous extension of the FDR: we assign each hypothesis an allocation between zero and one, and the sFDR equals the expected fraction of null allocation to total allocation. If one runs multiple analyses of the same data by varying different reasonable choices, allocations can be determined by simply dividing each run's selection indicators by its discovery count, then averaging across analyses and rescaling. The resulting sFDR equals the average of the ordinary FDRs of the runs, even though the runs are dependent: thus sFDR control holds under the same assumptions that the original FDR control held. (In contrast, naively reporting just fractions of times each variable was selected need not control the sFDR.) It is interpretable: hypotheses that were always selected are allocated 1 and those never selected are allocated 0. In leukemia expression and neuroimaging analyses, findings with larger allocations were more often supported in separate samples. We also develop procedures that can assign stable allocations directly from p-values, e-values, or knockoff statistics, resulting in stable-BH, stable e-BH and stable knockoff procedures. A representation by e-values describes which allocation rules control the error rate and gives ways to optimize allocations for different follow-up goals.

papers.title: Diagnosis as Percolation on an Evidence Graph: Root-Cause Recoverability in Network Fault Diagnosis
Finite-summability in the noncommutative geometry of crossed products
papers.abstract: We study finite-summability of unbounded representatives of $K$-homology classes for crossed-product $C^*$-algebras associated with actions on compact spaces. Using Kasparov's Dirac--dual-Dirac method, we isolate geometric conditions on the $\gamma$-element under which elements of $K$-homology can be transferred to a crossed product associated with a proper action and represented by finitely summable unbounded cycles defined from Dirac-type operators with an unbounded potential. We relate finite-summability of these operators to integrability properties of the potential by spectral estimates for Schrödinger operators on manifolds of bounded geometry. In particular, for finitely generated nilpotent groups this leads to finitely summable, unbounded representatives of all $K$-homology classes. We also give examples showing that representability of $K$-homology classes by finitely summable unbounded cycles is not invariant under $KK$-equivalence.

papers.title: Field-Effect Magnon Transistor
papers.abstract: Antiferromagnetic magnons offer a promising platform for highspeed, energy-efficient information processing. Intrinsic odd-parity spin splitting in a cycloidal magnetic order offers a route to nonvanishing magnon transport in compensated magnets. Here, we propose a magnonic field-effect device (akin to a transistor) based on a ferroelectric antiferromagnet BiFeO3 in which a gate electric field reconfigures domain boundaries to amplify/modulate magnon transport. These boundaries switch the nonlocal inverse-spin-Hall response between low- and high-signal states, with a pronounced dependence on the direction of magnon propagation. Source-drain reversal, magnetic-field measurements, symmetry analysis, and first-principles calculations reveal nonreciprocal magnon transport associated with the reversal of spin angular momentum across the domain boundaries. Our results establish an electrically programmable, non-volatile magnon transistor.

papers.title: High-inclination Centaur or Captured Halley-Type Comet? Observational and Dynamical Characterization of C/2024 L1 (PANSTARRS)
papers.abstract: The high-inclination (`high-i') Centaurs of the middle and outer Solar System are of uncertain origin. While many have been captured directly from the Oort Cloud, making them less-evolved analogues to the Halley-Type Comets, this process alone cannot produce the number of observed objects. The most discussed alternate origin is direct excitation of trans-Neptunian Objects into high-i orbits by the action of some unfound massive planet beyond Neptune. It is thus critical to find ways to discern the origins of these objects to provide new constraints on the various unfound planet hypotheses. This work assesses the only known active high-i Centaur: C/2024 L1 (PANSTARRS). Our dynamical investigations show that L1 has not decreased its semimajor axis in at least the past 1810 years, unlike all known TNO-derived active Centaurs at lower-i whose activity initiates after orbital changes. We also imaged L1 on five nights in the year before its April 2025 perihelion and found its brightness and optical colors to be stable and that its tail grew steadily. While this is like many Halley-type comets, few active low-i Centaurs have such stable activity. We thus propose that L1 is a captured Oort Cloud comet analogous to lower perihelion Halley-types and is thus a highly attractive target for large aperture follow up. The number and active fraction of these high-i objects should help us discern their origins and survey telescopes like Roman and Rubin could help us figure out where in the Outer Solar System the mystery lies.

papers.title: Log Hodge-de Rham degeneration beyond the toroidal case
papers.abstract: Let $\phi\colon X \to S$ be a flat and proper one-parameter degeneration of algebraic varieties with a single degenerate fiber $X_0$. If $\phi\colon (X|X_0) \to (S|0)$ is log smooth and saturated, the log Hodge-de Rham spectral sequence is known to degenerate at the page $E_1$. Adding to that some further well-known related properties, we say that the log de Rham complex $\Omega^{\bullet,\mathrm{log}}_{X/S}$ is cohomologically flat as a filtered complex, short cffc. Furthermore, if $\phi\colon (X|X_0) \to (S|0)$ has only toroidal log singularities, it is known that the reflexive log de Rham complex $\mathcal{W}^\bullet_{X/S}$ is cffc. A major motivation to study this property is that in the Calabi-Yau case, $\mathcal{W}^\bullet_{X/S}$ being cffc implies that a certain logarithmic deformation functor for $\phi_0\colon X_0^\partial \to S_0^\dagger$ is unobstructed. In this article, we develop a computational criterion to determine, under very mild assumptions on $\phi\colon X \to S$, whether the reflexive log de Rham complex $\mathcal{W}^\bullet_{X/S}$ is cffc. Applying this criterion, we found many explicit examples of degenerations of surfaces where $\mathcal{W}^\bullet_{X/S}$ is cffc, even though the log singularities are worse than toroidal. We did not find any new examples of degenerations of threefolds such that $\mathcal{W}^\bullet_{X/S}$ is cffc.

papers.title: The Lukashian Calendar: A universal calendar mechanism using variable-duration years and days for any human colony or settlement
papers.abstract: Existing calendars, in particular the Gregorian calendar, have a complex structure which requires constant adjustment in the form of leap days and leap seconds in order to remain synchronized to the position of a planet in the Solar System. In addition, mean solar days can deviate up to 16 minutes from true solar days on Earth. On other planets, this discrepancy can be far greater: on Mars, it can be up to 51 minutes. Numerous Martian proposals ranging from Aitken (1936) to Gangale (1986) to Silin (2025) mimic the Gregorian calendar and do not address these issues. Moreover, many do not include a system for telling the time of day, or stretch the second beyond the standard SI second. This paper proposes a calendar mechanism that uses years and days with a variable duration, in order to accurately represent true solar years and days. In this mechanism, time of day is expressed as a proportion, rather than a number of fixed units, such as hours and minutes. This results in a simple and consistent structure that can universally be applied to any planet, moon or space station with a human presence. Furthermore, it allows analog missions on Earth to use the same calendar mechanism as future missions in space. This paper will outline the principles and details of this mechanism, using Earth and Mars as illustrative examples. Also discussed is the implementation of the mechanism on actual computers, which have a Unix time system clock based on discrete milliseconds.

papers.title: EndoComparer: Comparative Surgical Video Question Answering with Pseudo-Siamese Visual Adaptation and Perceive-then-Compare Reasoning
ElevatorII: High-Performance Fully-Static Cross-ISA Binary Translation
Consistency-Aware Map Generation at Multiple Zoom Levels Using Aerial Image
Risk-Averse Decision-Focused Learning: Minimizing CVaR of Regret
Current-driven chiral RKKY interaction in altermagnets
papers.abstract: The Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya (DM) interaction between magnetic moments usually requires spin--orbit coupling and broken inversion symmetry. We show that in a spin-split metal without spin--orbit coupling a charge current generates a DM interaction between localized spins. Using Keldysh Green's functions (GFs) with a drifting Fermi sea, we compute the Ruderman--Kittel--Kasuya--Yosida (RKKY) interaction between two magnetic impurities in a two-dimensional $d$-wave altermagnet with an additional exchange splitting. To linear order in the current, the correction is a Fermi-surface term, and all its components are obtained in closed form in terms of Bessel functions, valid for arbitrary values of the two independent spin splittings, $\beta$ and $J_\perp$. The induced DM vector points along the spin-quantization axis, which in the present model is the out-of-plane direction $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$. At long distance it decays as $1/R$, one power more slowly than the equilibrium coupling. In the altermagnet it vanishes for bonds along the nodal directions, where the two spin bands are degenerate, and, for a diagonal current, has opposite signs on bonds along the two crystal axes. This $d$-wave signature reverses with the Néel vector and with the current, and distinguishes the altermagnet from a ferromagnet. The current also generates symmetric couplings that are odd in the impurity separation. In low-density two-dimensional conductors, the DM coupling can reach a few percent of the equilibrium exchange.

papers.title: The Contingent HOD Dichotomy
papers.abstract: The axiom V = HOD, referring to the class of hereditarily ordinal-definable sets, is contingently contingent by forcing---it holds contingently in the generic multiverse of some models of set theory but not others. Thus we introduce and investigate the \emph{contingent HOD dichotomy}, according to which either (1) the set-theoretic universe V is close to HOD by forcing---HOD is a ground, V = HOD is forceable, the universe is ordinal-definable from a set parameter $V=\text{HOD}_b$, the blurry HOD hierarchy collapses to kappa-HOD for some cardinal kappa, and furthermore these features are invariant by forcing and hold throughout the generic multiverse; or (2) the universe V is far from HOD by forcing in all those respects, so $V\neq\text{HOD}$, but also HOD is not a ground, V = HOD is not forceable, the set-theoretic universe is not ordinal-definable from a set, the universe is not kappa-HOD for any kappa, and these features hold invariantly throughout the generic multiverse. We investigate the nature of the dichotomy in connection with large cardinals, with set-theoretic geology, with the iterated $\text{HOD}^\alpha$ classes, and with the maximality principles MP and MP(R), showing generally that both prongs of the dichotomy occur with diverse set-theoretic phenomena.

papers.title: Spectral Steering: Local Inverse Geometry for Frozen Diffusion Generators
Orbital graph structure of alternating full groups and simple torsion amenable groups of exponential growth
papers.abstract: We develop a framework for constructing simple alternating full groups A(G, X), associated with finite fragmentations of minimal expansive dihedral Cantor actions, with controlled orbital-graph codings and purely non-Hausdorff singularities. We also prove that positive entropy of a naturally labeled admissible orbital line forces exponential word growth of the acting group. As an application, we construct continuum many pairwise abstractly nonisomorphic, finitely generated, infinite, simple, torsion, amenable groups of exponential word growth. They arise as alternating full groups of fragmented minimal expansive dihedral Cantor actions with linearly repetitive generic regular orbital graphs and purely non-Hausdorff singularities. Under the same minimality, expansivity, linear repetitivity and singularity assumptions, if every finite clopen coding is determined by a bounded fragmentation window, the alternating full group has intermediate word growth.

papers.title: Linear-optical nonlocality without postselection
papers.abstract: Linear optics is one of the major platforms for quantum information processing and experimental tests of quantum foundations. This motivates a thorough exploration of its capabilities and limitations. In this paper we investigate the extent to which passive linear optics, when fed with single-photon Fock states and followed by postselection-free number-resolving measurements, can demonstrate nonlocality. These resources define BosonSampling, a computational model believed to have intermediate computational power, being neither classically simulable nor quantum universal. We prove that, when restricted to only two input photons, this system also has intermediate nonlocality capabilities, achieving a violation of the CHSH inequality no higher than $1+\sqrt{2}$. Although this value has appeared frequently in the literature as achievable, to our knowledge this is the first proof that it is maximal. We show that, as we increase the number of available photons, linear optics can produce violations arbitrarily close to Tsirelson's bound of $2\sqrt{2}$. Finally, we extend the analysis to tripartite nonlocality, leveraging well-known interferometric suppression laws to show how several tripartite inequalities can be violated in this setup beyond their bipartite bounds.

papers.title: Learning from Mutants: Teaching Small Language Models to Synthesise Loop Invariants
Tracking gas-solid hydration kinetics by non-contact in situ transflection micro-FTIR spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Gas--solid reaction kinetics is important in applications such as thermochemical heat storage (TCHS), but experimental evaluation remains a bottleneck in materials development. This study evaluates non-contact \textit{in situ} transflection micro-Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy for tracking hydration reactions between water vapor and inorganic solids. Powder layers of La$_2$(SO$_4$)$_3$, CaSO$_4$, and CaO, exhibiting different hydration mechanisms and kinetics, were deposited on an Au-coated glass substrate and exposed to humidified N$_2$. Evolution of water- and hydroxyl-related IR absorption band areas was compared with thermogravimetry (TG)-derived hydration numbers. The FTIR band-area profiles were broadly consistent with the TG-derived hydration trends, showing close agreement for La$_2$(SO$_4$)$_3$ and CaSO$_4$. For CaO, some differences were observed between the FTIR and TG results, possibly because CaO is sensitive to differences in gas-phase conditions, particularly the initial increase in humidity, between the two measurements. The spectra distinguished molecular-water uptake in La$_2$(SO$_4$)$_3$ and CaSO$_4$ from hydroxide formation in CaO. They also detected carbonate formation during CaO hydration. Thus, \textit{in situ} time-resolved FTIR separately monitored individual chemical reactions, whereas TG recorded only their combined effect on the sample mass. These results demonstrate the potential of transflection micro-FTIR for chemically selective monitoring of gas--solid reactions in small localized samples.

papers.title: Disentangling Magnetospheric and Colliding-Wind X-ray and Radio Emission in the Post-Mass-Transfer Magnetic Massive Binary Plaskett's Star
papers.abstract: Plaskett's star is an O+O binary system harboring a kG-order magnetic field associated with the broad-lined secondary. It is the only O-type star believed to host a centrifugally supported magnetosphere. We present orbital- and rotational-phase resolved X-ray and low-frequency radio observations of Plaskett's star. X-ray observations were taken with Chandra using the High Energy Transmission Grating Spectrometer (HETGS), while the radio observations come from uGMRT and VLA. The X-ray light curve shows rotational modulation according to the magnetic component's rotation period, with maximum flux near magnetic minima. We confirm the decline in flux near orbital phase 0.5 where the slow rotator primary is in front of its magnetic companion. We used the $f/i$ ratios of Si XIII and Mg XI from high-resolution X-ray spectroscopy to infer the location of the plasma emitting X-rays. We find no statistically significant variation in line widths or centroid shifts with either orbital or rotational phase; however, given instrumental limitations, this non-detection may partly reflect observational constraints, while still suggesting a complex and extended X-ray emitting plasma distribution. We could not detect the star in the low-frequency radio bands (0.6--1.5 GHz). Re-analysis of existing Very Large Array data reveals an additional detection at 3 GHz, consistent with a nonthermal contribution predicted by magnetospheric models, although no direct signature was obtained. At low frequencies, nonthermal emission from the magnetosphere and the colliding-wind region is likely suppressed by free-free absorption in the winds of one or both components.

papers.title: Bellman Residual Bracketing: Resolving the Sample Complexity of Discounted and Average-Reward RL
Conditional Stochastic User Equilibrium as a Gibbs Distribution: Tractable Flow Laws and Exact Path-Free Sampling
papers.abstract: Treating traffic counts as data calls for the joint distribution of link flows. Stochastic user equilibrium (SUE) gives a single flow vector, and independent route choice at fixed probabilities ignores congestion feedback between travelers. Conditional stochastic user equilibrium (CSUE), in which each traveler of a finite population chooses a route by logit conditional on the routes of all others, contains this feedback but has been hard to compute with at scale. Under separable link costs and a common route-choice precision, the CSUE conditionals are those of a unique Gibbs distribution whose energy is a left-endpoint discrete congestion potential, and for continuous nondecreasing costs the law concentrates on deterministic logit SUE in the large-population limit. When the routes of each origin are the paths of an acyclic bush, retaining origin- or OD-level labels gives an unnormalized layered link-flow law with an explicit product-form multiplicity. On this representation we build a block Metropolis-Hastings sampler whose proposal is an integer version of Dial's loading under frozen costs. It leaves the CSUE law on the bush route sets invariant without enumerating paths or storing individual routes, and at stationarity the mean rejection rate of a block lies between one and two times the total variation distance between its proposal and exact conditional. In experiments, the sampler reproduces reference laws from exact enumeration and traveler-level Gibbs sampling, whereas independent route choice at frozen costs reproduces mean flows but overstates link-flow standard deviations by up to 48% and distorts correlations. On Sioux Falls, the block sampler attains 76.1 times the minimum effective sample size per CPU second of traveler-level Gibbs sampling, and on Chicago Sketch, with over one million travelers, its sampled covariance is used to assess traffic-count locations.

papers.title: Behavioral Assurance for Socially Deployed AI Agents
Sharp First-Hit Identification from Finite Depth Samples
Negative and Positive Saddle-Selection Ambiguities in the HTEE
papers.abstract: The holographic timelike entanglement entropy (HTEE), computed via complexified extremal surfaces, suffers from a saddle-selection ambiguity: for sufficiently small time intervals (\(\Delta t\to0\)), both a vacuum-connected and a vacuum-disconnected complex extremal surface contribute, and the minimal-real-part criterion and the vacuum-reduction criterion can favor different saddles. We study this ambiguity in strongly coupled field theories whose dual geometries are hyperscaling-violating Lifshitz backgrounds, in which conformal symmetry and Lorentz invariance are broken by the Lifshitz exponent and the hyperscaling-violation parameter. Working in \(2+1\)- and \(3+1\)-dimensional dual field theories, we derive general expressions for the HTEE in the vacuum-connected and vacuum-disconnected saddles, \(s_{v.c.}\) and \(s_{v.d.}\), respectively, and compare their real parts. We find that the two criteria agree everywhere except at the first accidental zero. The ambiguity appears in two distinct forms. In the \emph{negative} family, \(\operatorname{Re}(s_{v.c.})=0\) and \(\operatorname{Re}(s_{v.d.})<0\), whereas in the \emph{positive} family, \(\operatorname{Re}(s_{v.c.})>0\) and \(\operatorname{Re}(s_{v.d.})=0\). The latter shows that the ambiguity survives even in the conformal \(3+1\)-dimensional case. It therefore seems that the saddle-selection ambiguity is a generic feature of the complexified-geometry prescription.

papers.title: Read, Then Shade? How Visual Evidence Changes Incentive-Driven Misreporting in Vision-Language Advisors
SemMask: Semantic-Prioritized Progressive Masking for Diffusion Language Models
ResWAM: Learning What Changes, Not What Stays, for World-Action Models
A proof of Nakamura's conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove Nakamura's conjecture on the relation between the 2D Toda model and solutions of the Ernst equation, using the Pfaffian solutions obtained in our previous work arXiv:2610.27420 .

papers.title: Steering Bayesian Inference and Decisions through Data Poisoning
An Explicit Version of Serre's Open Image Theorem for Galois Number Fields
papers.abstract: In 1971, Serre showed that the mod $p$ Galois representation associated to a non-CM elliptic curve over a number field is surjective for all but finitely many primes $p$. That is, there exists a constant $c(E,K)$, for $E$ a non-CM elliptic curve over a number field $K$, such that $\rho_{E,p}:\mathrm{Gal}(\overline{K}/K)\to \mathrm{Aut}(E[p])$ is surjective for all primes $p>c(E,K)$. We give a bound for this constant using an effective version of the Faltings isogeny theorem for specific number fields. We show that, for $K=\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{D})$ with $|D|<50$ and $K$ a formally real number field, given a non-CM elliptic curve $E$ over $K$ we have $c(E,K)\le 2C_1(K)\log N_{K/\mathbb Q}\operatorname{rad}\left( 2\mathcal O_K\mathfrak N_{E}\right )+2 C_2(K)$, where $\mathfrak N_E$ denotes the conductor ideal of $E$, and the constants $C_1(K)$ and $C_2(K)$ can be described explicitly. We also show that for primes greater than this bound, the image cannot be contained in the normalizer of a non-split Cartan subgroup. This works for any Galois number field. Our proof assumes the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH).

papers.title: Counterexamples to Strichartz estimates for general irrotational compressible Euler backgrounds and positive estimates for a spherical isotropic background solution
papers.abstract: We consider the free boundary problem for the irrotational compressible Euler equation in a physical vacuum setting. By using the irrotationality condition in the Eulerian formulation of Ifrim and Tataru, we previously showed that the problem can be rephrased in terms of the velocity potential function as an acoustic wave equation that turns out to be widely used in solar seismology. This paper is another step towards understanding what Strichartz estimates are achievable for the aforementioned equation. Our object of study is the corresponding linearized problem. In a previous work, we constructed a class of gallery modes in a model stationary case, which turned out to be counterexamples to Strichartz estimates, forcing a loss of derivatives. By a careful regularization of the domain defining function, we transplant these counterexamples to general Euler backgrounds, and obtain general counterexamples in the same range. On the other hand, we also prove that for the background corresponding to a concrete affine isotropic spherical solution for the irrotational compressible Euler equations, one has Strichartz estimates up to the aforementioned threshold, which shows that they are optimal for at least some explicit Euler backgrounds. To the best of our knowledge, these are the first results of this kind for explicit solutions of the irrotational compressible Euler equations in a physical vacuum.

papers.title: Inquest: Log-Guided Root-Cause Code Localization with a Staged Agent
A Neural Density Functional for Spatial Structure and Orientational Ordering in Two-Dimensional Lattice Hard Rods
papers.abstract: We study spatial structure and orientational ordering of horizontal and vertical hard rods on a two-dimensional square lattice using neural classical density functional theory. We construct two convolutional architectures that exploit the symmetry relating the rod orientations: a direct-$c^{(1)}$ network (learning the map between the first functional derivative of the excess free energy and the inhomogeneous density, $c^{(1)} \leftrightarrow \rho$) and a $\Phi$-network (learning directly the map between free energy and density, $F_\text{ex} \leftrightarrow \rho$). Both networks use exactly the same inhomogeneous grand-canonical Monte Carlo density profiles and one-body direct correlation targets. Both neural representations substantially improve the predicted density profiles relative to the Lafuente--Cuesta lattice functional. The resulting free energy landscapes, however, differ between the two representations. Furthermore for the direct-$c^{(1)}$ network the integration along different density paths produces different free energies. As a result, the transition to nematic ordering for rods with aspect ratio 8 is strongly first order for the direct-$c^{(1)}$ network while only weakly discontinuous for the $\Phi$-network. The latter is a reasonable approximation to the continuous transition found in simulations, demonstrating that subtle entropic free energy differences are accessible in neural cDFT.

papers.title: Determinateness in a classical theory of nonclassical truth
papers.abstract: Recent theories that take determinateness as primitive are either nonclassical theories of nonclassical truth, like Field's INT, or classical theories of classical truth, like Fujimoto and Halbach's CD and CD^+. This paper develops a third option: a classical theory of nonclassical truth. The theory, KFDcs, extends the Kripke-Feferman theory KFcs with a primitive determinateness predicate. Unlike CD^+, KFDcs keeps the iteration of truth unrestricted and gives up its completeness. With or without a consistency axiom, KFD is proof-theoretically equivalent to the theory \widehat{ID}_2 of twice iterated fixed points, with ordinal {\varphi}({\varphi}({\varepsilon}_0, 0)0), thus stronger than CD^+. It is also shown that replacing full induction with internal induction yields ordinal {\varphi}({\varphi}({\omega}, 0)0), and restricting internal induction to total formulae yields {\varphi}({\varepsilon_0},0), the ordinal of KF.

papers.title: TrustBound: Mechanized Completeness for Payment Epochs Initiated by AI Agents
Lesion-Aware Explainable AI for Diabetic Retinopathy Grading from Fundus Images
Beyond Prompts: Runtime Contracts for Coding Agents
Random Cut Forests, Games and Diffusion over Approximately Nested Anisotropic Local Geometry
Affordable Analytic Gradients for G0W0-BSE Excited States for Multiple GW Variants via Back-Propagation
papers.abstract: We derive, implement and validate analytic nuclear gradients for three variants of $GW$ self-energies---the contour-deformation (CD), the analytic continuation (AC), and the contour deformation with $W$-analytic-continuation (CD-WAC)---and for the Bethe--Salpeter equation (BSE) built on top of them. All gradients are expressed as contractions of a set of covectors connected to derivatives of primitive quantities in SCF calculations. The derivation of these covectors is a back-propagation procedure through the $GW$ and BSE equations. Central finite differences confirm the correctness of all implemented gradients. With the AC-$GW$-BSE gradient we optimize the excited-state geometries of carbon monoxide, a donor-acceptor dye labelled as DA1, and DMABN, a typical model system for twisted intramolecular charge-transfer phenomena (TICT), and have obtained results that successfully reproduce observations from experiments or high-level calculations. We also performed trajectory surface hopping (TSH) simulations of nonadiabatic molecular dynamics (NAMD) of DMABN using the SHARC NAMD package, showing the capacity of our method to simulate NAMD problems. We performed timing and memory scaling tests, demonstrating that the gradient calculations of both $GW$ and BSE scale asymptotically as $N^4$ for timing and $N^3$ for memory. All source codes used in the present work, including the REST program package and the modified SHARC NAMD package that supports REST as the quantum chemistry backend, are available on Gitee this https URL and this https URL

papers.title: Evidence-Conditioned Completion and Synthesis of Electronic Health Records
Sharp condition for the existence of wave operators
papers.abstract: We study the wave operators for a Jacobi matrix whose spectral measure satisfies the Szegő condition. We formulate a sufficient condition in terms of the associated Verblunsky parameters and show that it is sharp.

papers.title: DT-MATCH: Defect- and Topology-Aware Chiplet Matching for Yield Optimization in Heterogeneous Integration
Large caps in $\mathbb{F}_3^9$ and $\mathbb{F}_3^{11}$
papers.abstract: We construct sets of $1104$ points in $\mathbb{F}_3^9$ and $5744$ points in $\mathbb{F}_3^{11}$, each containing no three distinct collinear points. A reflection lift sends the Calderbank--Fishburn $236$-cap to a cap with three parallel layers of sizes $512,80,512$; both outer layers are linearly equivalent to the FunSearch $512$-cap. A coordinate substitution in Hill's $112$-cap uses replacement sets of sizes $80,32,32$ for the three values of one scalar coordinate. Assigning the $80$-point set to a noncentral $45$-point section gives $5744$, gaining $240$ points over the $5504$ construction obtained from a central $40$-point section.

papers.title: Func-JEPA: Learning a Sobolev Space of Functions as Latent Vectors
Second-Order Threshold and Value Asymptotics in Multiple-Stopping Secretary Problems
papers.abstract: We study the classical secretary problem with a fixed number of selection opportunities. We derive explicit corrections to the limiting thresholds and to the optimal success probability. A cancellation identity removes the influence of later threshold rounding from the first correction, while a Poisson representation explains its probabilistic meaning. Every bounded rounding of the limiting thresholds shares the first value correction. We obtain integer rounding laws, eventual threshold identities along continued-fraction convergents, and joint rounding frequencies. Rigorous rational bounds show that the first eleven corrections are positive and the twelfth is negative, producing the first shifted convergent identity.

papers.title: Chang's Omitting Types Theorem in Lukasiewicz Logic
papers.abstract: We prove Chang-style omitting types theorems for standard first-order Lukasiewicz logic. Starting from a prescribed model $M$, we obtain an extension that omits higher-complexity types while preserving lower-level types already realized in $M$. If $T$ is a $\Pi_{n+2}$-theory, every model of $T$ has an exact extension that preserves its realized $\Sigma_{n+1}$-types and omits every $\Sigma_{n+2}$-type not generated by a $\Sigma_{n+1}$-type. An iterated construction also omits infinity-universal types, whose unbounded quantifier complexity cannot eventually be generated by the corresponding lower-complexity fragments of a single type. The main tool is a refinement of Robinson's infinite forcing sensitive to the quantifier complexity of formulas.

papers.title: Weak-type $(p,p)$ inequalities for Riesz transforms
papers.abstract: For $1\le p\le2$, we obtain the sharp weak-type $(p,p)$ inequality for each classical Riesz transform on real-valued functions on $\mathbb R^n$, with the same optimal constant as for the Hilbert transform. The proof combines the Bellman function method of \cite{BHV} with Janakiraman's sharp strip potential \cite{Janakiraman}.

papers.title: Tight Bounds for Differentially Private Cut Release
Continuation-Guided LLM Evolution of Program Policies and Goal Compilers in Craftax
Agent Authenticator: Passkey-Grade, Hardware-Bound Authentication for AI Agents
Cooperative Gradient Estimation for Multi-Robot Source Seeking with Heteroskedastic Measurements
Depth-Aware Path Planning and Collision Avoidance for Robotic Nursing Assistants Using Real-Time 3D Vision
Compiling Imperative Hardware Protocol Specifications to Hardware
On the Cauchy problem for $σ$-evolution equations with time-dependent coefficients via upper decay indicators
papers.abstract: In this paper, the first main goal is to investigate the Cauchy problem for the linear $\sigma$-evolution equation $$u_{tt}+a^2(t)(-\Delta)^\sigma u+b(t)u_t+m^2(t)u=0, $$ where propagation speed, damping term and mass are time-dependent functions. Under suitable assumptions on the interaction among these coefficients, we not only derive decay estimates for the solution and its derivatives in terms of the effective parabolic time scale $\mathcal{V}_{a,b}(s,t):=\int_s^t a^2(\tau)/b(\tau) d\tau$, but also conclude the additional decay induced by the mass term and the upper decay indicators of the initial data. Especially, one can recognize that the time-derivative estimate for solutions exhibits a competition between $m^2(t)$ and $a^2(t)\left(1+\mathcal{V}_{a,b}(0,t)\right)^{-1}$. For the corresponding semi-linear problem with the nonlinear term $|u|^p$, we also establish global (in time) existence of small data solutions fulfilling decay estimates, coming from the mass factor $\exp\left(-\int_0^t m^2(\tau)/b(\tau)d\tau\right)$, under the same assumptions on these coefficients.

papers.title: Geometrically formal Hermitian metrics on compact complex surfaces
papers.abstract: We classify compact complex surfaces admitting either a geometrically Dolbeault formal or an ABC-geometrically formal Hermitian metric. Furthermore, we prove that on a compact Kähler surface, every ABC-geometrically formal metric is Kähler, whereas, for geometrically Dolbeault formal Hermitian metrics, Gauduchon, LCK, and Kähler conditions are equivalent. On non-Kähler surfaces, an ABC-geometrically formal Hermitian metric is LCK and, except on Inoue surfaces, Vaisman.

papers.title: LLM Trading Agents Earn Beta, Not Alpha: A Look-Ahead-Free Benchmark
Ultra-CAN: A Lightweight Blind ISAC Receiver for Chaos-Based Telemetry and Local-Seed Ranging in the Internet of Drones
Edgeworth expansion on sums of Wiener chaos
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study Edgeworth expansions for random variables belonging to a fixed finite sum of Wiener chaoses. Building on the work of Mansanarez, Poly and Swan ( arXiv:2510.14002 ) for a single Wiener chaos, we investigate the extension of their approach to functionals $F$ living in a finite sum of Wiener chaoses $\mathcal{W}_{\leq d}$. Within the Malliavin--Stein framework, we bound the total variation distance between the law of $F$ and its Edgeworth approximation of order $2dm$ by $(\sum_{p,q}^d \operatorname{Var}\Gamma(F_p,F_q))^{m/2}(\operatorname{Var}\Gamma(F,\operatorname{L}^{-1}F))^{1/2}$, where $F_p$ denotes the projection of $F$ onto the $p$-th Wiener chaos. The presence of several chaotic components introduces additional interactions, since these components are orthogonal but generally dependent. Since our proof relies on the integration-by-parts formalism and the spectral properties of the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck operator, this result extends naturally to the broader framework of Markov chaoses.

papers.title: PathLoop: Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Reasoning for Evidence-Grounded Whole-Slide Image Analysis
Accounting for Attrition in Respondent-Driven Sampling Cohort Studies
papers.abstract: Respondent-driven sampling (RDS) is widely used to recruit populations lacking conventional sampling frames. Because RDS oversamples well-connected individuals, weights are commonly applied to improve representativeness. Although methods for cross-sectional RDS analyses are well developed, guidance for longitudinal studies is limited, despite additional selection bias from missed visits and dropout. We develop a framework that jointly accounts for unequal inclusion probabilities at recruitment and attrition during follow-up. The approach combines baseline RDS weights with inverse-probability-of-non-response weights estimated from observed follow-up histories, producing visit-specific weights for estimating prevalences, means, and regression parameters. We clarify when the RDS design should inform attendance models rather than being addressed only during outcome analysis. Using simulations of RDS recruitment, we assess prevalence and standardized prevalence differences under varying recruitment and attrition mechanisms, focusing on bias, variance, and confidence interval coverage. Weighting the response model by baseline RDS weights was important when an unmeasured determinant of degree also predicted response, even when it did not predict the outcome. We illustrate the framework using data from the Montreal site of Engage, a multisite RDS cohort of sexual minority men in three Canadian cities, from 2017-2023. Follow-up involved intermittent missed visits, attrition, and terminal dropout that was more common among participants with smaller networks. Our findings provide practical guidance for combining design-based and attrition adjustments to support valid inference in longitudinal RDS studies.

papers.title: Objectify, Don't Delete: Complaint-Derived Evaluation of Ambient Clinical Notes
Geodesics and a Hubble Relation in Nonstationary Thermodynamic Geometry
papers.abstract: Thermodynamic geometry offers a versatile lens from equilibrium to nonequilibrium, yet typically assumes a stationary metric. Here we study nonstationary thermodynamic geometry, where the metric evolves even at fixed control parameters. The resulting temporal connection generalizes the geodesic equation and redistributes dissipation along optimal control paths. We further establish a thermodynamic Hubble relation that distinguishes relaxation toward equilibrium from geometric expansion or contraction. Brownian examples demonstrate that externally modulated friction can reduce minimum dissipation, while heat exchange with a finite reservoir can induce geometric contraction and Mpemba-type relaxation. Our framework lays a geometric foundation for understanding complex evolving nonequilibrium systems.

papers.title: Geometric Stability and Sample Complexity for Compositional Function Priors
Scalable composite likelihood inference for directed probit networks
papers.abstract: We develop scalable estimation and inference for directed probit networks with correlated sending and receiving effects and residual reciprocity. An incomplete composite likelihood in two stages combines exact bivariate margins of sampled dyads and triples, avoiding integration in high dimensions and cubic enumeration. For fixed parameter dimension, criterion evaluation is linear in the number of draws. Averaging a fixed number of fits from independent index samples reduces sampling variation and allows parallel computation. We establish consistency and joint asymptotic normality with different directional rates, allowing a singular node projection when draw counts lie between the node and dyad scales. An overlap covariance accounts for network and index variation and is consistent relative to each directional variance. Independent index samples stabilize covariance estimation without refitting. The resulting procedure provides standard errors, mapped joint regions and score tests for zero variance components. Simulations show improved estimation from averaging and substantially lower computation times than default Bayesian fitting. An application to a fly brain network with 21,738 neurons demonstrates estimation and inference at a scale relevant to modern network data.

papers.title: A note on distributive lattices with a commutative generalized implication
papers.abstract: We study distributive lattices with an ideal-valued generalized implication satisfying a commutativity identity. This class extends commutative weak Heyting algebras by allowing implication values to be non-principal ideals. We characterize its intersection with several known classes of gi-lattices, study gi-deductive systems and their relationship with gi-filters and gi-congruences, and extend the relational characterization of commutativity to this setting. The resulting correspondence yields a Priestley-style duality by restricting the established duality for gi-lattices.

papers.title: Simulations of turbulent heat and particle transport in stellarator plasmas
papers.abstract: Achieving sustained energy production in magnetic confinement fusion reactors requires a deep understanding of turbulent transport of heat and particles. This thesis investigates turbulent transport with a particular emphasis on stellarators, using simulations with the $\delta f$ gyrokinetic code stella for the W7-X, LHD, TJ-II and NCSX stellarators, the ASDEX Upgrade (AUG) tokamak and the Cyclone Base Case (CBC). It addresses two questions: how do density gradients affect turbulent heat transport, and can turbulence help retain particles in the plasma core? In the first part, an inter-machine study shows a strong reduction of the ion heat flux in NCSX and W7-X with increasing density gradients, attributed to the stabilization of ion-temperature-gradient-driven modes without significantly destabilizing trapped-electron modes or universal instabilities. This beneficial effect is absent in tokamaks, where the heat flux increases with the density gradient, highlighting the role of magnetic geometry. The ion heat flux in stellarators does not follow the growth rate of the fastest-growing linear mode, underscoring the importance of nonlinear effects. Trapped-electron modes dominate in CBC, AUG, TJ-II, LHD and NCSX, while passing-particle-driven universal instabilities contribute significantly in W7-X. The second part addresses the long-standing discrepancy between the strongly hollow density profiles predicted by neoclassical theory in large stellarators and the flat or weakly peaked profiles measured in W7-X. Nonlinear simulations and a particle balance analysis show that turbulence provides a robust inward particle flux, driven by finite ion and electron temperature gradients, that can account for the observed profiles: the sign of the turbulent particle flux matches the sign of the discrepancy between the experimental and neoclassical fluxes across the entire plasma radius of W7-X.

papers.title: Confinement--Higgs Complementarity Viewed through Relative Quantum Reference Frames
papers.abstract: We formulate confinement--Higgs complementarity in terms of the relative orientation between two independently constructed quantum reference frames (QRFs): one derived from the gauge field and the other from the scalar field.
