Exact continuum and lattice identities give a relational interpretation of the scalar--color observables used in recent gauge-fixing-free $SU(2)$ simulations. In particular, we provide a QRF interpretation of the additional gauge-invariant nonlocal separation line obtained from the Cho--Duan--Ge (CDG) reduction reported in lattice simulations of the radially fixed fundamental $SU(2)$ gauge--scalar model. We explain why such a candidate nonlocal boundary is compatible with Fradkin--Shenker continuity and Osterwalder--Seiler analyticity for the appropriate class of local gauge-invariant observables. Separately, we show that a Wilson-rooted control observable admits an exact results at zero plaquette coupling and that it does not cause such a nonlocal separation line.

papers.title: Equilibrium measures for anisotropic exponential interaction energies with applications to transformers
Renormalization Group Flow from 4d Chern-Simons Theory
papers.abstract: The four-dimensional Chern-Simons theory coupled with surface defects is known to realize two-dimensional integrable quantum field theories (QFTs). We discuss the renormalization group (RG) flow of such two-dimensional integrable QFTs from first-principles Feynman diagram computations intrinsically in the four-dimensional framework. We first derive the one-loop RG flow of two-dimensional QFTs realized by the four-dimensional Chern-Simons theory on $\Sigma \times C$ coupled with the order surface defects supported on $\Sigma $. Here, the affine Kac-Moody symmetry of the defects underlies the one-loop RG flow. We then derive the one-loop RG flow of the principal chiral model (PCM) without Wess-Zumino term, which is realized using disorder surface defects, within the Batalin-Vilkovisky formalism. We obtain the nontrivial one-loop RG flow of the PCM, reproducing its known asymptotically-free beta function, using two complementary methods: by explicitly evaluating one-loop Feynman amplitudes, and by computing an analogue of analytic torsion for four-dimensional Chern-Simons theory.

papers.title: Denoising-Induced Recovery of Effective Dynamics
papers.abstract: Recovering dynamical equations from data is a central problem in nonlinear science. In practice, measurements are corrupted by noise and often contain fast oscillations that are not part of the slow dynamics of interest. For this reason, data are typically pre-processed before model recovery or classsification. Here, we reveal the effects of filtering, a specific denoising technique, on recovery. Our analysis show that equation discovery performed on filtered data recovers, up to a fixed precision, the normal-form (effective) equations rather than the original system.

papers.title: Over-the-Air Semantic Alignment via Dual Stacked Intelligent Metasurfaces
Homomorphisms between Weyl modules for $\mathrm{GL}_3$ in characteristic $2$
papers.abstract: We classify the homomorphism spaces between Weyl modules for the general linear group $\mathrm{GL}_3$ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $2$. We prove that these spaces have dimension at most one and give an explicit recursive procedure that determines when they are nonzero and constructs generators in terms of semistandard tableaux. As a consequence, we determine the dimensions of certain homomorphism spaces between Specht modules in characteristic $2$.

papers.title: Local field shifts and the Gribov-Zwanziger horizon functional
papers.abstract: We study a Maggiore-Schaden-like re-centering of the Gribov-Zwanziger action using a smooth compactly supported profile. At fixed background and finite cutoff, under the stated coercivity and contour hypotheses, this transformation preserves the original horizon functional with no residual dependence on the profile. The extension to gauge-field integration requires additional domination assumptions. Near a self-adjoint first Gribov horizon, the response depends on both the lowest Faddeev-Popov eigenvalue and its source weight. We extend this visibility analysis to non-self-adjoint compressions, separating source darkness from truncation-induced shielding, and recall continuum transverse $SU(2)$ examples. Transporting the composite insertion preserves the regulated Gaussian and resolvent structure. A separate free-space tree-level check reproduces the auxiliary-mass denominator of the RGZ propagator, without determining condensate dynamics

papers.title: Sada-ASR: A Production Multidialectal Arabic Speech Recognition System
DBHiCo: Dual-Branch Hierarchical Contrastive Learning for MRI Image Classification
Scalar charge of neutron stars and accreting black holes in Starobinsky gravity: quasi-universal relations, the trace anomaly and gravitational-wave sensitivity
papers.abstract: The Starobinsky scalaron is sourced by the trace of the stress--energy, so its exterior charge is set by the matter around an object and not by the object's vacuum geometry. We derive a master formula for that charge for any static, spherically symmetric source, evaluate it first for neutron stars, where the interior is known, and then for accreting black holes, where it is not. For a star the pressure subtracts: on the interior metric with the Eardley sensitivity, and the charge is a quasi-universal function of the compactness. Six realistic equations of state confirm the relation but lie above the coefficient calibrated on polytropes; the refit reproduces their mean to 0.007. The trace $\rho-3p$ changes sign in the cores of massive stars, and the charge also tracks the tidal deformability and the moment of inertia to a few parts in 1000 and 100. Solving the Einstein-frame structure equations self-consistently moves a star along this relation and leaves its charge at fixed compactness within 4 per cent of the test-field value. We compare the charge with NICER radii and the GW170817 tidal deformability, and use the published massless dipole constraint from GW230529 to calibrate a Fisher estimate of the sensitivity of a similar binary to a finite scalaron range, projected to the Einstein Telescope and Cosmic Explorer; the range is a free parameter, and the laboratory bound on pure $R+\alpha R^2$ is confronted explicitly. A vacuum black hole has q=0; a hole with a disc has $q=\sinh(m_\phi r_d)/(m_\phi r_d)$, controlled by the disc's outer edge, which makes it the counterpart in which the same integral is dominated by matter far from the centre; light is blind to the charge at leading order, and the correction beyond it is negligible for any self-consistent disc.

papers.title: Formalizing Formal Semantics: The Formal Atlas
An asymptotic resolution of the Gao--Thangadurai conjecture on the Harborth constant
papers.abstract: The Harborth constant $\mathsf g(G)$ of a finite abelian group $G$ of exponent $n$ is the least integer $k$ such that every subset of $G$ of size at least $k$ contains $n$ elements whose sum is zero. Let $C_n$ be a cyclic group of order $n$. Gao and Thangadurai \cite{gt} in 2004 conjectured that $\mathsf g(C_n\oplus C_n)=2n+(-1)^n$ for all integers $n\ge3$. We prove this conjecture for all sufficiently large integers $n$.

papers.title: Evaluating and Improving Natural Language Autoencoders
Quantum periods and threefold flips
papers.abstract: We study regularized quantum periods under birational contractions involving threefold flips. Let $g:X \dashrightarrow X'$ be a birational map between Fano threefolds with terminal quotient singularities which contracts exactly one prime divisor $E$ and extracts no divisor. We prove that $$ \lim_{r \rightarrow +\infty}\widehat{G}_{X,rE}(t) =\widehat{G}_{X'}(t). $$ The proof uses logarithmically smooth degenerations and positive discrepancies on good resolutions. Compatibility with orbifold invariants is proved using successive quotient-point extractions and the two-component orbifold degeneration formula. We also define stationary descendant invariants of projective terminal Fano threefolds by good resolutions and prove compatibility with a given projective $\mathbb{Q}$-smoothing. The period comparison extends to projective $\mathbb{Q}$-factorial terminal Fano endpoints under the same hypothesis on the birational map. Its proof compares the endpoints on a common resolution.

papers.title: Formalizing $\mathsf{einsum}$ with Named Tensor Notation
Spaces with maximal monotone convex subdifferentials
papers.abstract: We characterize the real Hausdorff locally convex spaces on which every proper lower semicontinuous convex function has a maximal monotone convex subdifferential. Equivalent conditions are given in terms of the portability of closed convex sets and identities involving upper envelopes. Among normed spaces, this property is equivalent to completeness; among Fréchet spaces, it is equivalent to normability. We also prove that the property is preserved under products with finite-dimensional spaces.

papers.title: A Compact Single-Flange Low-Energy Inverse Photoemission Spectrometer with Elliptical-Mirror Photon Collection
papers.abstract: Low-energy inverse photoemission spectroscopy (LEIPS) is limited by weak photon emission, so photon collection optics largely determine its sensitivity. We compare four photon-collection configurations, each addressing a limitation of its predecessor: a detector beside the sample without collection optics (no-mirror), an off-axis parabolic (OAP) mirror delivering a collimated beam to a head-on photomultiplier tube (PMT), external optics coupling the OAP output to a side-on PMT with about twice the quantum efficiency (OAP-external), and an in-vacuum elliptical mirror focusing the emitted light onto the detector (elliptical). Ray-tracing shows that the elliptical mirror delivers 91.9% of the emitted photons to the detector, compared with 63.3% for the OAP mirror and 3.06% without a mirror, while a plane mirror folding the light path by about 90$^\circ$ allows the electron gun, collection optics and detector to fit on a single 8-inch flange. For C$_{60}$ films, the elliptical configuration gives the highest lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) intensity of the four, 271 counts per second per $\mu$A of sample current, 1.74 and 3.23 times those of the OAP and OAP-external configurations and about 45 times that of the no-mirror configuration. The gain over the OAP configuration is comparable to the 1.45-fold increase predicted by ray-tracing, but the filter and detector also differed, so the geometric contribution could not be isolated. The OAP-external configuration gave only 0.54 times the OAP signal despite its higher quantum efficiency. High sensitivity therefore requires both a large collection solid angle and a short optical path kept inside the vacuum.

papers.title: Relativistic precession around rotating neutron stars. I. Slow rotation: Hartle--Thorne spacetimes, particle orbits and the QPOs of atoll and Z sources
papers.abstract: We study the relativistic precession model (RPM) of quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) in the spacetimes of slowly rotating neutron stars computed from the equation of state (EOS). For four EOSs (WFF1, G3, FSUGarnet and IOPB-I) we solve the Hartle--Thorne equations to second order in the angular velocity and compute the orbital and epicyclic frequencies of the exterior metric without expanding in the spin or the quadrupole. At $1.9\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$ the spin-induced quadrupole is 2--4 times that of a black hole with the same spin; it lowers the nodal precession frequency by up to 25 per cent near the innermost stable circular orbit and limits the nodal frequency that any spin can produce. An eccentric, tilted geodesic around a $1.92\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$ star spinning at 363~Hz precesses at the epicyclic rates, and the power spectrum of a hot spot on it peaks at the orbital, periastron and nodal precession frequencies. Applied to the atoll sources 4U 1636$-$53 and 4U 1728$-$34, the RPM gives masses of 2.02--$2.15\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$ and 1.88--$1.92\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$. For 4U 1728$-$34 the low-frequency QPO favours stars with large moments of inertia, $I\simeq2.5\times10^{45}$~g\,cm$^{2}$. Without an EOS the QPOs give $M=1.920^{+0.014}_{-0.012}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$, $j=0.162^{+0.023}_{-0.011}$ and $\bar Q=2.2^{+1.1}_{-0.8}$; a Kerr spacetime with the same nodal frequency would underestimate the moment of inertia by 22 per cent. For the Z sources GX 5$-$1 and GX 340+0 the horizontal-branch oscillations cannot be twice the nodal precession frequency for any of the four EOSs: the fits are driven to spins of 730--745~Hz and to the maximum mass.

papers.title: Latent Molecular Rollout Towards Causal World Models: Direction is Learnable, Amplitude Control is Readout-Dependent
papers.abstract: A molecular world model should predict how structural changes alter physical properties, not merely assign labels to static molecules. We build a latent molecular rollout system on an 8B Qwen3 backbone, trained on 9,202 aqueous experimental pKa pairs from iBonD, and assess its progress toward causal control by auditing three often-conflated capabilities: predictive fidelity through the intended molecular pathway, directional learnability versus amplitude calibration of target-conditioned displacements, and transfer of latent control to decoded structures. After removing textual shortcuts, continuous latent inference achieves a test MAE of 2.087, significantly outperforming direct molecular feature readout (MAE difference -0.276, 95% CI [-0.352, -0.203], p<0.001). A target-conditioned policy reliably learns displacement directions, with a median cosine of 0.577 and 62.8% of 43 held-out pairs exceeding the 0.3 threshold. Amplitude conclusions are strictly readout-dependent. A frozen linear readout yields near-zero amplitude correlation (-0.020), while a nonlinear gradient-based readout recovers relative amplitude ordering (correlation 0.585, sign accuracy 0.744-0.767) with compressed absolute scale. At the decoded structure level, neither input-slot editing nor direct final-state injection produces meaningful changes across 80 test sources, bounding the tested control surfaces rather than indicating a universal decoder bottleneck. Generation fine-tuning shows relative improvement under internal oracle evaluation but does not surpass a simple constant baseline in single-sample settings. These results delineate the capability frontier of fixed-scale latent molecular interfaces: directional control is robustly achievable, but calibrated amplitude control and decoded structural transfer remain open challenges on the path to causal molecular world models.

papers.title: Black holes in Myrzakulov $F(R,T)$ gravity
papers.abstract: We investigate vacuum black-hole solutions in metric-affine Myrzakulov $F(R,T)$ gravity (MG-I), where $R$ is the affine Ricci scalar and $T$ is a quadratic torsion invariant, not the trace of the matter energy-momentum tensor. For the polynomial model $F(R,T)=\alpha R+\beta T+\gamma T^3$, with $\alpha\neq0$, we first vary the metric and all components of the independent affine connection, and only then specialize to metric-compatible geometry with totally antisymmetric torsion. Nonzero axial torsion admits an exceptional branch $\alpha+\beta+3\gamma T_*^2=0$, on which the metric satisfies the Einstein equations with effective cosmological parameter $\Lambda_*=\gamma T_*^3/\alpha$. We establish a local existence result and construct torsionful Schwarzschild-(anti-)de Sitter representatives that are smooth through a selected future Killing horizon. Within the spherically symmetric axial ansatz, we characterize Ricci-symmetric affine connections by the condition $(fV-U)'=0$ and compare a constant-$W=fV-U$ family with a constant-$U$ family. Although these connections share the same metric and torsion scalar, their affine curvature invariants generally differ. Independent coordinate-level curvature contractions and component tests of the unrestricted metric and connection variations corroborate the identities used in the construction; these checks complement the analytic variational derivation. Finally, we identify null directions of the restricted axial quadratic form and distinguish this degeneracy from a complete metric-affine stability analysis. Our conclusions are local and do not establish global extendibility, physical inequivalence of all torsion profiles, or dynamical stability.

papers.title: Do Probing and Steering Favor the Same Directions Within and Across Language Models?
$K_1^*(1870)$ and $3S$-$2D$ mixing in the strange meson sector
papers.abstract: Very recently, the BESIII Collaboration reported the first observation of a $J^P=1^-$ strange resonance in the $K\eta'$ system, the $K_1^*(1870)$. We examine whether this state can be accommodated in the kaon meson family. Although it cannot be assigned as a pure $3^3S_1$ or $2^3D_1$ state, we show that it can be described as the lower state of $3S$-$2D$ mixing, whose mass agrees with the measured value, and we predict its higher-mass partner. Using the quark pair creation model, we calculate the OZI-allowed decay properties of both \textcolor{black}{mixed} states; the total decay width of the lower state is consistent with the measured width of the $K_1^*(1870)$. We note that the subordinate $K\eta'$ decay mode of this state appears to contradict its observed $K\eta'$ decay channel, which calls for further study. We further investigate the production of these two states via the $Kp$ reaction, which may provide valuable information for future experimental searches.

papers.title: Asymptotic Divergence-Based Monitoring for Data Drift in Production AI Systems: A Discrete Case Approach
papers.abstract: We develop a complete asymptotic theory for monitoring data drift in production artificial intelligence (AI) systems whose inputs take values in a finite set of categories. The framework combines two complementary inferential tools. Under the no-drift hypothesis $H_0$, the two-sample likelihood-ratio statistic $G$ of Wilks follows a universal Chi_{r-1}^2 law, independently of the divergence chosen and of the sample sizes; the calibrated Population Stability Index (PSI) of Yurdakul and Naranjo (2021) shares the same Chi_{r-1}^2 limit and is asymptotically equivalent to the $G$-test under $H_0$. Under the drift hypothesis $H_1$, the plug-in phi-divergence is asymptotically normal with a variance computed in closed form for the one-sample, two-sample and symmetrized configurations, yielding standardized $Z$-statistics, detection boundaries, power functions and sample-size planning rules. We supply a per-category decomposition that localizes the drift on specific categories, a Benjamini--Hochberg procedure for monitoring many features simultaneously, and an explicit comparison with the heuristic PSI cut-offs of industrial practice. Two fully worked simulation examples - one one-sample with the Rényi divergence and multiple testing, one two-sample with the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence and sample-size planning - illustrate every notion of the paper on realistic production data.

papers.title: Maximality of the Došen--Petrić Boolean Category
papers.abstract: We prove that the zero-identity Boolean category of Došen and Petrić, freely generated by a nonempty set of propositional variables, is maximal. Adjoining any equation between parallel morphisms that does not follow from the defining equations, and closing under the operations on morphisms and uniform formula substitution, collapses this category to a preorder. This disproves their conjecture that the category is not maximal. The proof uses Boolean Coherence to select a pair of variable occurrences on which the two morphisms differ. Composition with morphisms selecting these occurrences, uniform substitution and two isomorphisms yield equality of the product projections. We prove that any zero-identity Boolean category satisfying such an additional equation under every interpretation of the variables is a preorder. We also give a Lean formalization of these proofs and their dependencies. It includes Boolean Coherence and the correspondence between substitution on tagged occurrence sets and substitution on finite ordinals.

papers.title: Vegetation Health Classification for Low-Data and Edge Hardware Deployment
A quantitative measure of predictability for surface gravity waves
papers.abstract: We introduce a Bayesian inference framework to characterize the predictability of a one dimensional ocean surface wave field given surface elevation measurements from a sensor. Unlike the classical theories that only sketch the boundary of a predictable zone based on group velocity, we use the Bayesian posterior uncertainty of surface elevation to quantify the local predictability at every spatiotemporal location. Our approach first constructs a prior distribution to encode existing knowledge of the wave field such as the spectrum and propagation direction. By conditioning on the (possibly noisy) measurement data, we infer the posterior distribution of the wave field, from which a spatiotemporal uncertainty map is extracted. This map agrees well with the group-velocity-based classical predictable zone theory when the frequency spectrum has bounded support. Meanwhile, it also demonstrates predictability even for a spectrum with unbounded frequency support where the classical predictable zone degenerates. A refined analysis of posterior uncertainty using observability Gramian matrix reveals a `data-informed' part and an `un-informed' part of the wave field, with the latter being fundamentally un-predictable. Furthermore, nonlinear effects can be naturally introduced into the Bayesian framework by incorporating the nonlinear ocean surface wave equations. This is the first time that nonlinearity is rigorously treated in the predictable zone problem. We perform numerical tests using both bounded, piecewise constant spectrum and unbounded JONSWAP spectrum. The numerical results confirm the proposed advantages of our method for linear waves and reveal how wave steepness affects the predictability of nonlinear waves. Nonlinear modal interactions redistribute uncertainty between the inside and the outside of the predictable zone with an amount proportional to the wave steepness.

papers.title: Beyond Paired Inputs: Learning to Leverage RGB-T Cross-Modal Relations in Multimodal Large Language Models
Quaternion Matrix Tuples with Common Invariant Subspaces: Dimension and Nonuniqueness
papers.abstract: Let $M_n(\mathbb{H})$ denote the algebra of $n\times n$ quaternion matrices. We study common invariant right subspaces of tuples in $M_n(\mathbb{H})^r$ and determine exact real semialgebraic dimensions for two associated sets. If $n_1,\ldots,n_s$ are positive integers, $n=n_1+\cdots+n_s$, and $q=\sum_{1\leq a<b\leq s}n_an_b$, the set of tuples preserving at least one nested chain with successive increments $n_1,\ldots,n_s$ has dimension $4rn^2-4(r-1)q$. For $r\geq2$ and $1\leq k<n$, the set of tuples with at least two distinct common $k$-dimensional right invariant subspaces has dimension $4rn^2-4(r-1)(k(n-k)+n-1)$. The proofs use finite right-module coordinates and a common local-rank argument.

papers.title: Unbound matter in the circum-halo medium: a common mediator of halo secondary bias
papers.abstract: Halo secondary bias describes the dependence of halo clustering on properties beyond mass. Here we report that a new environmental metric, the unbound matter fraction ($f_{\rm un}$) in the $2$--$3\,R_{\rm vir}$ shell around a halo, can largely account for secondary bias. Using haloes with $M_{\rm vir}=10^{10.5}$--$10^{14.5}h^{-1}{\rm M_\odot}$ at $z=0$ obtained from TNG300-1-Dark, we find that controlling for $f_{\rm un}$ reduces the secondary bias of formation time, concentration, spin, shape and velocity anisotropy to a residual correlation of $\lesssim 4\%$, outperforming other environmental metrics such as the tidal anisotropy for spin and velocity anisotropy. Applying a stacking method to the circum-halo medium (CHM), we identify two distinct flow patterns: low-$f_{\rm un}$ haloes co-move with coherent flows, with the CHM converging onto the haloes; in contrast, high-$f_{\rm un}$ haloes move through dynamically hot, partially virialized structures, with the CHM passing by rather than being accreted. This dichotomy points to two distinct regimes of secondary bias, a `cold' regime and a `hot' regime, in which tidal and inertial forces act as the main drivers, respectively, with the dominant mechanism migrating from the former to the latter as haloes assemble into massive structures. At fixed large-scale environment, $f_{\rm un}$ further indicates the presence of nearby neighbours and the competitive accretion. Our results highlight the role of unbound matter as a mediator of environmental effects on haloes, and reveal the physical mechanisms that shape the CHM pattern through which these effects are mediated.

papers.title: Fixed-space indices and symmetry breaking in variational problems
papers.abstract: We establish a quantitative criterion for variational bifurcation with prescribed exact stabilizers under finite group actions. Combining scalar spectral flow on fixed spaces with overgroup nullities, we bound the number of bifurcation parameters when the restricted singular set is finite. The theorem allows strongly indefinite Fredholm Hessians and singular ambient endpoints, without parameter differentiability or regular crossings. Finite Morse index reduces the inputs to indices and nullities; extensions cover varying form domains and regular matrix Sturm--Liouville systems. For a Newtonian nine-body family containing a reported counterexample to Moeckel's stability conjecture, we prove analytically that two nonconjugate exact reflection types bifurcate at a common central mass, displacing the central body. Positivity excludes larger stabilizers, while a scalar Schur complement synchronizes the bifurcations, independently of the reported stability assertion.

papers.title: Sustaining In-Network Computation in Satellite Networks: An Architecture for Semantic Continuity
Ship-as-a-buoy for Phase-resolved Reconstruction of Surface Waves
Self-similarity of axisymmetric Marangoni flows on a deep viscous subphase
papers.abstract: Local gradients of surface tension caused by inhomogeneous distributions of surfactant molecules are known to generate Marangoni flows, the mechanics of which have important consequences in various areas of science and engineering. In this paper, we investigate the deposition of insoluble surfactants on the surface of a deep, viscous subphase, which propagate axisymmetrically without diffusing. We study these flows from the perspective of self-similarity, i.e., seeking solutions which show universal features on appropriate length and time scales. We first present a closed form, self-similar solution of the first kind for the axisymmetric spreading of surfactants, which is globally valid at long times. We then numerically study `filling' flows of surfactant, where the surfactant distribution is locally depleted such that inward flows are generated to `fill' the surfactant-free area. These flows have the special feature of forming cusp-like structure in finite time, which have been studied extensively in the literature of self-similarity of the second kind. We show that these flows admit a countably infinite number of stable similarity solutions based on the local behavior of the initial surfactant concentration profile. We remark on a few unique features of these results in contrast to filling flows in other physical limits.

papers.title: Galerkin methods for unconventional superconductors with long-range interactions on 3D lattices
papers.abstract: We develop an analysis and a B-spline Galerkin method for the matrix-valued Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer (BCS) gap equation of unconventional superconductors with general long-range interaction kernels on arbitrary Bravais lattices. We define the BCS free energy functional on lattices, show that it is bounded from below, and characterise solutions of the gap equation as its stationary points. For non-repulsive kernels, we prove that fixed-point iteration never increases the free energy and drives the residual to zero. The algebraically decaying tails of the interaction are described by Epstein zeta functions, so the method applies to any power-law exponent $\nu>0$, including exponents at or below the lattice dimension such as dipolar interactions in three-dimensional lattices. In the B-spline Galerkin basis, the singular convolutions correspond to block-circulant matrices whose eigenvalues are lattice sums, applied without quadrature at FFT cost. Each iteration takes log-linear work and linear memory, and Broyden updates accelerate convergence. By engineering a suitable dispersion for a prescribed gap, we obtain non-trivial analytic singlet and triplet solutions of the gap equation with power-law interactions on the integer lattice at zero temperature, to our knowledge the first ones. Benchmarks against these solutions and against highly resolved numerical data show convergence rates determined by the B-spline degree and the regularity of the solution. Finally, we compute a nodal superconductor with long-range interactions on the three-dimensional fcc lattice: a chiral state with a line node and two topologically non-trivial Weyl point nodes. On 16 cores, the method reaches a residual of $1.5\times10^{-13}$ for 6.3 million complex unknowns in less than two minutes.

papers.title: PALIN: Pixel-Aligned LiDAR-NIR Multimodal 3D Object Detection with Benchmark
Leveraging Dual-Process Theory for Multimodal Multiparty Turn-Taking Prediction
Bright-Dark State Interplay Governs Vibronic Decoherence in Molecular Aggregates
papers.abstract: In this study, we establish a spectroscopy-driven framework that connects optically bright vibronic eigenstates to their subsequent decoherence dynamics in excitonic molecular aggregates. Combining the Multiparticle Holstein Formalism with explicit system--bath interactions, we demonstrate that relaxation-induced purity loss is governed by three interconnected factors: (i) the bath spectral window, which determines the accessibility of intra- and interband relaxation pathways; (ii) the local network of dark vibronic states surrounding the optically prepared bright state; and (iii) the energetic placement of the bright state, which controls downhill relaxation. Remarkably, states with different excitation energies exhibit nearly identical purity dynamics when their local relaxation networks are similar. The resulting H--J asymmetry further reveals the importance of energetic directionality. These findings establish a reliable connection between optical spectroscopy, vibronic band structure, and state-selective loss in purity.

papers.title: UACS: Uncertainty-Aware Clustering and Sparse Parameter Estimation for Multi-Condition Wheel Center Force
Computing rare events in Lévy-driven systems via optimal control
papers.abstract: We extend the optimal control formulation of sample path large deviation theory, which has proven effective for numerical computation of instantons and sharp probability estimates in stochastic differential equations with Gaussian noise, to systems with light-tailed Lévy noise. In the scaling limit of small jumps and high intensity, such systems satisfy a large deviation principle of Freidlin-Wentzell type, with a running cost given by the Legendre transform of the noise cumulant generating function. We propose to numerically minimize this cost over noise realizations subject to the system dynamics, which yields the instanton without having to solve Hamilton's equations, and naturally handles degenerate and multiplicative noise. When the cumulant generating function has a bounded domain, the cost grows only linearly for large noise, and instantons can contain jumps. We analyze when jumps are not only admissible but optimal, depending on the subleading behavior of the cost and on the drift, and show how jumps can be resolved numerically through a time reparameterization that freezes physical time. For continuous instantons, we derive Riccati and Fredholm determinant expressions for the leading-order prefactor, and we discuss the modifications needed when the instanton jumps. We illustrate and validate our methods against Monte Carlo simulations in several examples: a two-dimensional nonlinear model, an active run-and-tumble particle with non-Gaussian tumbling noise, and the Ghil-Sellers energy balance climate model with Lévy-perturbed solar forcing.

papers.title: Probing SAM Perturbations Through Statistical Replay
Local asymptotic normality for Cox-Ingersoll-Ross drift parameters under high-frequency sampling and the strict Feller condition
papers.abstract: For the ergodic Cox--Ingersoll--Ross (CIR) diffusion with known diffusion scale and a fixed initial value, we prove local asymptotic normality (LAN) of the exactly sampled experiment for the drift parameters whenever the Feller index exceeds $1$, assuming only a vanishing mesh and a diverging observation horizon. This improves the previously known condition that the index exceed $(11+\sqrt{89})/2$. The proof cuts off the continuous score near $0$, recovers the remainder by exact conditional centering on each sampling interval, and transfers LAN by a conditional-likelihood argument.

papers.title: Generic finiteness of rotating relative equilibria in the planar $N$-vortex problem
papers.abstract: For every $N\ge2$, we prove that Zariski-generic nonzero real circulations, with any prescribed signs, admit at most $N^{2N}$ labeled, collision-free rotating relative equilibria modulo translations, rotations in $SO(2)$, and positive scaling. The excluded parameters lie in an explicit finite union of quadratic hypersurfaces. The proof combines a logarithmic-residue obstruction to positive-dimensional complex solution sets with Bézout degree bounds.

papers.title: Grokking Can Be Steered: Selecting Desirable Solutions By Choice Of Learning Rule
Team Stability: Theory and Evidence
StyleJudge: A Human-Validated, In-Context-Learning Vision-Language Evaluator for Artistic Style Transfer
Towards Informed Autonomy Design: Understanding the Interplay of Function Characteristics and Autonomy Preferences in Automotive Agents
A Proof of The Twin-Star Hypothesis in Dimension Five
papers.abstract: It was recently shown that the question of whether the determinant-like map \(\det^{S^2}\) is unique up to multiplication by a scalar is equivalent to a combinatorial conjecture regarding cycle-free \(d\)-partitions of the complete graph \(K_{2d}\), known as the twin-star hypothesis. This hypothesis asserts that every cycle-free \(d\)-partition of \(K_{2d}\) is weakly equivalent to one that contains a component isomorphic to the twin-star graph \(TS_d\). This hypothesis was previously established for \(d\le4\). In the present paper, we prove it for \(d=5\). Consequently, the associated determinant-like map \(\det^{S^2}\) is unique up to a scalar in dimension \(5\).

papers.title: InvarOrd: Self-Supervised Ordinal Knowledge Distillation with Rank-Invariant Alignment for Label-Efficient Cross-Species Hyperspectral Fish Freshness Assessment
Interpreting Random Forests: Comparing Surrogate Models and Rule Extraction Methods
A Universal Algebraic Construction of Hilbert-Space Fragmentation
papers.abstract: We present a mechanism for obtaining Hilbert-space fragmentation from arbitrary quantum lattice Hamiltonians acting on finite-dimensional local spaces. We first express the Hamiltonian in an algebraic form using supersymmetry (SUSY) and parasupersymmetry (paraSUSY) generators. Enlarging their representations defines a lifting procedure, which we study in two forms, site-wise and bond-wise lifting. Site-wise lifting introduces immobile zero modes that generate exponentially many invariant sectors while retaining the original dynamics in the fully active sector. We determine the sector structure and establish strong fragmentation for uniform lifts at fixed intermediate zero-mode density. For nearest-neighbor chains, correlation functions reveal restricted propagation and, in the mixed-field example, persistent local memory. Bond-wise lifting produces mobile conserved strings, pair-flip dynamics and fluctuating dimers, and extends to fragmented unitary circuits. Different representations and embeddings realize different fragmentation mechanisms. Some of the fragmented models obtained by this method include lifted permutation and Ising spin chains, a lifted toric code, the \(XXC\) families of spin chains, and fragmented extensions derived from the integrable \(H_{1,11}\) and \(H_{1,3}\) seed densities. The last two models are derived from Hietarinta's classification of constant $4\times 4$ Yang-Baxter solutions.

papers.title: Representing Differential Inclusions as Monads: A Framework for Compositional Controller Synthesis
Deep Nonlinear Sufficient Dimension Reduction for Discretely Observed Functional Data
papers.abstract: We develop a modular framework for deep nonlinear Sufficient Dimension Reduction (SDR) of discretely observed functional predictors with Euclidean or metric-space-valued responses. A presmoothing encoder converts the functional input into finite-dimensional coordinates, and a neural network learns a sufficient representation from them. The framework separates the choice of encoder from that of the SDR criterion. We study kernel embedding and discrete functional principal component analysis, each combined with either a generalized martingale difference divergence network or a Fréchet cumulative covariance network. These combinations share objectives of the martingale difference divergence form. {Under input smoothness and general Hölder regularity of the target operator, we establish approximation and generalization bounds that jointly account for functional truncation, network approximation, statistical estimation, numerical integration, measurement noise, and encoder estimation. The complete theoretical analysis rigorously demonstrates how errors in the encoded coordinates propagate through the network to the deep nonlinear SDR estimator, and quantifies the final estimation error in relation to observation frequency and model complexity.} Simulations and an application to satellite-derived vegetation trajectories and crop-composition responses illustrate the statistical and computational advantages over RKHS-based nonlinear functional SDR methods.

papers.title: Link Spectra of Lorenz-like Templates and the Horseshoe
papers.abstract: We give a complete classification of the inclusion relations between the link spectrum of the horseshoe template $L(0,1)$ and those of the nonnegative Lorenz-like templates $L(0,a)$. For a template $T$, its link spectrum $\mathscr L(T)$ consists of the link types carried by $T$, allowing parallel strands along its strips. For integers $a\geq0$, the spectra of $L(0,a)$ and $L(0,1)$ are comparable under inclusion if and only if $a\notin\{0,2\}$. More precisely, \[ \mathscr L(L(0,a))=\mathscr L(L(0,1)) \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad a=1, \] while \[ L(0,a)\prec L(0,1) \qquad (a\geq3). \] For $a=0$ and $a=2$, the two spectra are incomparable. The main new containment is \[ L(0,2n)\preceq L(0,1)\qquad(n\geq2), \] which goes beyond the classical parity-preserving nesting relations. A key ingredient is a braid-theoretic criterion: every $T$-link \[ T((r_1,s_1),\ldots,(r_k,s_k)) \] with $s_k\geq2r_k$ is a horseshoe link. This gives a large explicit family belonging to both the Lorenz and horseshoe spectra. In the reverse direction, we construct a horseshoe link outside the Lorenz spectrum. For each integer $m\geq6$, we obtain infinitely many horseshoe links of braid index $m$ excluded from every other nonnegative $L(0,a)$. These examples give infinitely many links with any prescribed number of components at least three. In the other direction, for each positive number of components, we give infinitely many links carried by both $L(0,0)$ and $L(0,2)$ and excluded from the horseshoe spectrum.

papers.title: Successive Convexification in Learned World Models for Safe Offline Planning
VAST: Compiling Grounded Vulnerability Scenarios into Verifiable, Multi-Step Environments for Evaluating LLM Red-Team Agents
The Goldstone--Wilczek Charge on the Rim
papers.abstract: A solenoid flux $\Phi=2\pi\alpha$ threaded through the center of the Kaplan--Sen lattice disk binds a ground-state charge $Q_{\rm core}=\alpha-\mathrm{round}(\alpha)$, and the edge carries exactly the opposite charge. The edge charge is the Goldstone--Wilczek charge of the edge ladder, $Q_{\rm edge}=-\tfrac12\eta$, with $\eta$ its spectral asymmetry. At $\Phi=\pi$ one unit of charge crosses the disk. We ask how the rim operator, the Schur complement of the disk Hamiltonian on its boundary sites, registers this transfer. Its count of negative eigenvalues never changes over the flux cycle. Instead, the unit of charge enters the rim through a simple pole: the extremal eigenvalue of the rim operator passes through infinity in the same flux interval as the charge jump, with $\Delta Q_{\rm edge}=\tfrac12\Delta\,\mathrm{sign}\,\lambda_{\rm ext}$. The residue factorizes into the coupling of the inner edge mode to the rim and the inverse slope of that mode's level, and grows linearly with the radius. All statements are checked numerically on disks of radius $R=11$, $19$ and $34$.

papers.title: Semantics First, Pixels Later: Mission-Driven Event Streams for Drone Video over Bandwidth-Starved Links
Rigidity of complete self-shrinkers
papers.abstract: Let $X:M^n\to\R^{n+1}$ be an $n$-dimensional complete self-shrinker with constant squared norm $S$ of the second fundamental form. For $n=4$, we prove that if $f_3=\sum_i\lambda_i^3$ is constant, where $\lambda_i$ denotes principal curvatures, then $S=0$, or $S=1$ and the image $X(M^n)$ in the rigid cases is one of the hyperplane, the sphere or the standard generalized cylinders. In every dimension, under assumption of sub-exponential growth we prove the same conclusion. Without assumption of sub-exponential growth, we prove if $S\leq 3+1/\sqrt n$, then the same conclusion holds.

papers.title: Program Distillation: Transferring LLM Capability from System 2 to System 0
Fluctuation modes in the initial state of heavy-ion collisions: from 2D to 3D hybrid simulations
papers.abstract: This dissertation investigates how the initial stages of relativistic heavy-ion collisions shape the evolution of the quark-gluon plasma (QGP) and the observables measured experimentally. Particular attention is given to the initial state and pre-equilibrium dynamics, which constitute the main sources of uncertainty in hybrid simulations. The first part of the dissertation reviews the framework underlying state-of-the-art hybrid simulations and the numerical tools used in phenomenological analyses. The second part studies the matching between pre-equilibrium evolution and viscous hydrodynamics. Since commonly used conformal kinetic-theory descriptions are inconsistent with the non-conformal hydrodynamic equation of state, an entropy-density matching prescription is proposed. This prescription reduces the artificial bulk pressure generated at the switching time and improves the consistency of the hybrid framework. The third part develops a mode-by-mode decomposition of initial energy-density profiles to isolate fluctuation modes and quantify their contributions to final observables. Applied to Pb-Pb collisions across centrality classes and extended to a fully three-dimensional O-O collision system, the method shows that initial fluctuations survive hydrodynamic evolution and leave measurable imprints on final observables. In O-O collisions, fluctuations can dominate over geometric effects from the impact parameter, demonstrating that intermediate-sized systems are not simply scaled-down versions of large systems. Overall, these results provide tools for constraining the early stages of heavy-ion collisions and for understanding how fluctuations propagate through the QGP evolution.

papers.title: An $(\infty,1)$-category of conically smooth stratified bordisms
papers.abstract: To study derived defect topological quantum field theories, we construct an $(\infty,1)$-category of stratified bordisms and sketch its $(\infty,d)$-dimensional analogue. In the first chapters we develop a method for constructing symmetric monoidal $(\infty,1)$-categories, inspired by Segal spaces but better suited to geometric inputs, which we call interval Segal spaces. Using this framework, we construct the $(\infty,1)$-category of $d$-dimensional smooth manifolds via smooth $\infty$-sheaves thereof, in an attempt to address fibrancy issues present in prior work on this subject. We further equip this category with a symmetric monoidal structure, compute its homotopy 1-category, and extend the construction to manifolds endowed with tangential structures, obtaining the interval Segal space of $d$-dimensional bordisms with tangential structure. To model the stratifications supporting topological defects, we work with conically smooth stratified spaces, a suitably smooth framework for conical stratifications. We define stratified topological manifolds as stratified $\mathcal{B}$-manifolds for a suitable $(\infty,1)$-category of basics $\mathcal{B}$. Using these, we construct an interval Segal space whose objects are compact closed stratified topological $(d-1)$-manifolds and whose 1-morphisms are stratified $d$-dimensional bordisms, and we endow it with a symmetric monoidal structure. We also use tangential structures on conically smooth stratified spaces to formulate a notion of defect labels, aiming toward bordisms with labeled defects in the style of Carqueville et al. Finally, we sketch a higher-dimensional generalization of the interval category to a category of $d$-cubes for $d>1$, conjecturally presenting $(\infty,d)$-categories, and outline how stratified factorization homology may be used to produce derived stratified defect TQFTs.

papers.title: A full-wave ICRH solver with full kinetic accuracy using only first order differential equations
papers.abstract: Accurate full-wave computation of ion cyclotron resonance heating (ICRH) typically requires solving the computationally demanding integro-differential dielectric tensor of the hot plasma. Based on the method in [Phys. Plasmas 32, 082110 (2025)], we develop BO-FW1D, a 1D frequency domain finite difference full-wave solver which generates full kinetic, accurate and efficient simulations utilizing a fluid plasma model. To accurately convert the conductivity tensor in phase space into a first-order differential equation, we introduce a mathematically rigorous framework using pseudodifferential operator theory based on Kohn-Nirenberg ordering. Benchmarks with an all-orders 1D full-wave solver show high consistency in critical kinetic effects and electric-field distributions, while substantial computational acceleration is achieved. This work could lay the foundation for developing full-wave solvers that combine full kinetic accuracy with high computational efficiency.

papers.title: Predicting, Fast and Slow: SSD Already Knows Which Guess Is Wrong
Characterization of an Optical Time Projection Chamber prototype with Ar:CF$_4$ at atmospheric pressure
papers.abstract: We report on the characterization of an Optical Time Projection Chamber (OTPC) developed as a prototype for neutron-induced reaction studies at Soreq Applied Research Accelerator Facility (SARAF). The prototype was operated with Ar:CF$_4$ (95:5) at 1 bar, using parallel mesh electrodes for charge multiplication and electroluminescence, and alpha particles from a $^{241}$Am source. Both induced charge and light signals were recorded. A systematic characterization was carried out to study charge multiplication and scintillation yield. We present the results of these measurements in single-gap amplification configurations, along with two-gap operation and a demonstration of synchronized optical readout.

papers.title: Text Speeding Itself Up: Recency and Restraint in Session-Local Drafting
Critical corner angles and defect exchange in confined nematics with splay-bend anisotropy
papers.abstract: In confined nematics, the director turning imposed by the walls is absorbed by defects, and we show that the corners exchange these defects with the liquid. A tangentially anchored corner of opening angle $\omega$ takes one of several types, labelled by the number $m$ of half-turns of the director relative to the radius; neighbouring types differ by a bound defect of index $\pm\frac12$, and logarithmic energies decide when the corner sheds or absorbs it. For equal elastic constants the critical angles are $72^\circ$, $120^\circ$, $216^\circ$ and $360^\circ$, with windows of bistability between them, explaining the hidden defect near $72^\circ$ vertices and selecting the equilibria of polygons and discs. We introduce unequal splay and bend constants through the cubic invariant $Q_{lk}\,\partial_lQ_{ij}\,\partial_kQ_{ij}$ in reduced Landau--de Gennes theory; bounding the order by its bulk value makes the problem well posed, without further elastic terms, whenever both Frank constants are positive. At first order only the splay corner feels the anisotropy; other corner and defect energies are even in it and follow exactly by quadrature. The anisotropy moves the angle above which a splay corner sheds a $+\frac12$ defect from $104^\circ$ to $136^\circ$ as $K_3/K_1$ rises from $0.54$ to $1.86$, and so predicts which polygons prefer splay corners and which interior defects. Finite-element computations for polygons of three to eight sides and the disc confirm this: the exchange occurs within the predicted range by migration of $+\frac12$ defects into the corners, near which states with zero, one and two splay corners are nearly degenerate.

papers.title: A Quantum Metric Approach to Stabilizer Codes
papers.abstract: We associate a spectral triple with each stabilizer code in a projective error model arising from a nice error basis and equipped with a length function. The spectral triple records the dimension of the code as well as the minimum code distance. For Pauli stabilizer codes of dimension greater than one with Hamming weight, Latrémolière's dual propinquity provides a pseudometric which allows us to compare codes of different physical and logical dimensions. We show that in the resulting topology, minimum distance of a code is locally constant for qubits and for qudits of dimensions three and five. Thus correction of all errors up to a prescribed weight is a local property in these cases. Moreover, for each prime $p$, we classify the underlying $C^*$-algebras in the metric closure as a subclass of AF algebras, namely those arising as tensor products of $C((\mathbb{Z}_p)^r)$, for $r \in \{0,1,2, \ldots , \infty\}$, with matrix algebras of $p$-power order or the UHF algebra of type $p^\infty$. Every such $C^*$-algebra not isomorphic to $M_{p^k}(\mathbb{C})$ for any $k\geq 1$ occurs as the underlying algebra of a point in the metric boundary. In particular, we obtain the CAR algebra as a metric limit of qubit stabilizer codes.

papers.title: Time-Varying Recalibration of Forecast Distributions
papers.abstract: Combined density forecasts are often miscalibrated, and the miscalibration can change over time. We propose a time-varying framework that recalibrates any combined forecast through applying a monotone map to its probability integral transform. We consider a Beta CDF or a rational quadratic spline as the map, and their parameters are updated either via score-driven filters combined with dynamic model averaging, or by a convolution-based update that additionally conditions on features of the forecast distribution. In simulations, the spline map corrects multimodal miscalibration that the Beta map cannot, and the convolution update achieves the highest log score when the miscalibration switches between regimes. We apply the method to nine G10 exchange rates and US inflation, recalibrating forecast distributions from both a loss-discounting linear pool and Bayesian predictive synthesis. In both applications, recalibration improves PIT uniformity, with gains in forecast accuracy most evident when the original forecasts are miscalibrated.

papers.title: Efficient and Accurate Causal Validation of Training Data Attribution
Counting real meromorphic differentials on $\mathbb{CP}^1$
papers.abstract: The counting problem for meromorphic differentials on $\mathbb{CP}^1$ with fixed orders of zeros and poles and vanishing residues at some specific poles, up to the action of $\mathrm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{C})$ and the multiplication by a nonzero constant, was completely solved before by several authors. In all the cases when there are finitely many such meromorphic differentials, an explicit formula for their number was found and also, in the case of residueless meromorphic differentials with two zeros, a link to the WDVV equations and the KP hierarchy was established. We consider a real analog of these counting problems by requiring that a meromorphic differential is preserved by a real structure on $\mathbb{CP}^1$. Our real counting problems admit refinements, obtained for example by specifying the orders of poles and zeros that are fixed by the antiholomorphic involution. We obtain explicit formulas for all our real counting problems and also, in the case of real meromorphic differentials with two complex conjugate zeros and residueless poles, establish a link to the open WDVV equations and the system of equations for the wave function of the KP hierarchy. An application to real Hurwitz numbers is also presented.

papers.title: Cotorsion pairs in $η$-extensions with applications to $θ$-extension rings and tensor rings
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal B$ be an abelian category with enough projective and injective objects, and let $\mathcal B\ltimes_\eta F$ be an $\eta$-extension of $\mathcal B$ with $\eta$ associative. Given a cotorsion pair $(\mathcal X, \mathcal Y)$ in $\mathcal B$, we show that the cotorsion pair $(\Delta(\mathcal X),\Delta(\mathcal X)^\perp)$ exists for arbitrary associative $\eta$, removing the square-zero assumption $F^2=0$ from Hu's construction. When $(\mathcal X, \mathcal Y)$ is hereditary, the heredity of $(\Delta(\mathcal X),\Delta(\mathcal X)^\perp)$ is characterized by the first left derived functor of a canonical defect functor $\delta$. We also remark that Hu's construction and hereditary result for the cotorsion pair $({}^\perp U^{-1}(\mathcal Y), U^{-1}(\mathcal Y))$ remain valid without the nilpotence assumption on $\eta$. Under nilpotence hypotheses, we establish a completeness criterion for $(\Delta(\mathcal X),\Delta(\mathcal X)^\perp)$ using the Beligiannis radical functor $\mathfrak r$. And we also provide a completeness criterion for $({}^\perp U^{-1}(\mathcal Y), U^{-1}(\mathcal Y))$ if $\mathcal B\ltimes_\eta F$ has enough injective objects. We give sufficient conditions for their coincidence. Dual results are obtained for $\zeta$-coextensions. Finally, we specialize the theory to $\theta$-extension rings and tensor rings, where the abstract conditions admit explicit module-theoretic descriptions.

papers.title: CLEW: Log-Anchored Backward Tracing for Root-Cause Code Localization
Cogirth-Strength Ratios and Matroid Rank Reduction
Architectures and KV Replay for Depth-Recurrent Language Models
PopulationBalanceModels.jl: An Extensible Framework for Deploying Population Balance Models
Hilbert-Kunz Multiplicity and Smirnov's conjecture
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study Smirnov's conjecture: Let $(R,\mathfrak{m})$ be a Noetherian local ring of characteristic $p>0$ and dimension $d$. Let $I$ be an $\mathfrak{m}$-primary ideal. If $R$ is weakly $F$-regular, analytically unramified and Cohen-Macaulay, then $\displaystyle L_1(I)=e(I)-e_{\mathrm{HK}}(I)$ if and only if $I$ is stable. Here, $e(I)$ and $e_{\mathrm{HK}}(I)$ denote the Hilbert-Samuel multiplicity and the Hilbert-Kunz multiplicity of $R$ with respect to $I$, respectively. Moreover, $\displaystyle L_1(I)=\lim_{q\to\infty}\frac{e_1(I^{[q]})}{q^d},$ where $q=p^e$ and $e_1(I^{[q]})$ denotes the first Hilbert coefficient of $R$ with respect to the $q$th Frobenius power of $I$. We prove the conjecture when $R$ is either excellent and strongly $F$-regular, or excellent of dimension $3$.

papers.title: Powers of projective lines inside full flag varieties
papers.abstract: Up to now, symplectic foliations of Poisson varieties have been primarily studied from a set theoretic perspective by describing their symplectic leaves individually as orbit closures. In the direction of obtaining algebro-geometric characterizations, for the standard Poisson structure $\pi$ on the full flag variety $G/B_+$ of a complex semisimple algebraic group $G$, we prove that the irreducible components of the reduced part of the 0-degeneracy locus of $(G/B_+, \pi)$ are precisely the inclusion-maximal $T$-stable complete Poisson submanifolds of $(G/B_+, \pi)$ that are isomorphic to powers of $\mathbb{P}^1$. This characterization is based on a theorem that explicitly classifies the closed Richardson varieties of $G/B_+$ isomorphic to $(\mathbb{P}^1)^d$. In turn, this theorem is based on a general theorem for arbitrary $T$-stable subvarieties of full flag varieties $G/B_+$ isomorphic to $(\mathbb{P}^1)^d$.

papers.title: Dressed higher-form symmetries in mixed state quantum matter
papers.abstract: We describe how to construct emergent strong higher-form symmetries in mixed quantum states that act unitarily on Hilbert space. Our construction uses (quasi-)local recovery channels from quantum error correction to some nearby simple (stabilizer) model. We prove that when the recovery is done in an appropriate (deterministic) manner, the resulting operators continue to be unitary. When applied to operators acting on topologically non-trivial sub-manifolds (loops, surfaces), the resulting unitaries inherit the logical algebra of the fixed point model. More generally, the unitarity of the emergent symmetries allows one to define emergent excitations whose statistics follow those of the fixed point limit.

papers.title: GRASP: Query-Adaptive Graph Retrieval framework with Cross-Attention Scoring and Path Sufficiency Verification for Question Answering
Few-Shot Visual Concept Extraction for Steering Diffusion Transformers
Do Rule-Based Tools Help LLMs Translate Endangered Uralic Languages in the Prompt or over MCP?
Radial Evolution of a Corotating Interaction Region from a High-Resolution MHD Simulation
papers.abstract: Corotating interaction regions (CIRs) are large-scale structures formed by fast--slow solar wind interaction, playing a crucial role in heliospheric dynamics and space weather. However, the evolution of individual CIRs and their full three-dimensional morphology remain poorly understood. We investigate the radial evolution of a single CIR using a high-resolution simulation combined with a backmapping method. The simulation reproduces the major plasma and magnetic signatures observed by Wind at 1~AU and by MAVEN and Tianwen-1 at $\sim$1.6~AU. The CIR exhibits a warped, shell-like spiral structure tilted relative to the heliospheric current sheet, consistent with theoretical predictions. During its developing stage, geometric changes are modest, and the radial scalings of velocity ($V_r \propto r^{0.02}$), density ($N \propto r^{-2.00}$), magnetic field ($B_{\rm total} \propto r^{-1.74}$), and temperature ($T \propto r^{-0.97}$) are comparable to those of the background solar wind. In the mature stage, the CIR drifts in longitude and expands toward high latitudes, while its longitudinal and latitudinal widths decrease with distance. The full-domain scalings change markedly to $V_r \propto r^{0.13}$, $N \propto r^{-1.91}$, $B_{\rm total} \propto r^{0.35}$, and $T \propto r^{-0.52}$, differing from both the background wind and the ecliptic-plane CIR. This study quantifies the radial evolution of a CIR from formation to maturity and highlights the importance of its three-dimensional structure in characterizing its morphology and dynamics.

papers.title: On $z_{2M}(21,4)$: the Hole Extensions of the Chen--Chen Configuration Are Reducible, and the Extremal Configurations of $z_2(21,4)$ Are Not Unique
papers.abstract: The second order extended Zarankiewicz number $z_{2M}(m,n)$ of Qi and Yu allows a secondary half of a $2$-edge to be shared, while the $1$-edge graph stays $C_4$-free and extremal and $1$-edges and main halves stay exclusive. Whether $z_{2M}(21,4)=55$ is open. Since deleting a $2$-edge removes exactly one displayed square, $z_{2M}(21,4)=55$ if and only if there is no irreducible admissible configuration with exactly $56$ displayed squares, and by the cell count of Qi and Yu and the heredity of irreducibility such a configuration without empty cells is an extremal $55$-square configuration of $z_2(21,4)$ plus one $2$-edge at its hole. For the extremal configuration of Chen and Chen we show, by certificates verified in exact rational arithmetic, that all $56$ such extensions have SOS rank at most $55$: $32$ by product relations and $24$ by contraction certificates of Xu--Yan type. We also show, with computer-assisted certificates and an exhaustive isomorphism search, that the extremal configurations of $z_2(21,4)$ fall into at least six isomorphism classes; Chen and Chen leave the structural classification of extremal augmented graphs open. Finally we prove a six-to-four reduction. For irreducible configurations whose $1$-edge graph is $C_4$-free with $m+\binom n2$ edges it bounds the multiplicity of a shared half by $n(n-1)$ ($12$ at $21\times4$), and it applies directly to an explicit number of the extensions of any extremal configuration of $z_2(21,4)$, eight for that of Chen and Chen, bringing each to at most $54$ squares, in agreement with the certificates. The cell count, the heredity lemma, the rows lemma, the six-to-four identity and a $2\times2$ example are checked in Isabelle/HOL; the remaining arguments are written proofs.

papers.title: $Q$-operators, cluster mutations, and flavored Toda chain
papers.abstract: We construct Baxter $Q$-operators for a family of quantum cluster integrable systems, that we call the flavored Toda chains, associated with quivers $\mathcal{Q}_N[F]$, where $F\subseteq\{2,\dots,N\}$ specifies data of $\vert F \vert$ additional nodes compared to $\mathcal{Q}_N[\varnothing]$ for the ordinary $N$-particle open $q$-deformed Toda chain. A distinguished sequence of quantum cluster mutations yields an ordered product of Faddeev's quantum dilogarithms. We prove that these operators form a commuting family and that their shifted quotients are transfer matrices whose coefficients are commuting Hamiltonians. We identify these transfer matrices with matrix elements of products of explicit local Lax matrices of rank two. Local cluster transformations move flavor insertions along the chain while preserving their ordered flavor parameters and the transfer matrix together with the canonical transformation. We also derive integral kernels for the $Q$-operators and evaluate an associated Fourier transform as a factorized scalar $Q$-function. Finally, we relate the quivers to the BPS quivers of five-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=1$ gauge theories in the decoupling limit and identify the normalized scalar $Q$-function with the perturbative contribution of a canonical codimension-two defect wrapping a squashed three-sphere.

papers.title: Security Authentication as Protective Friction: Understanding the Dual Effects of Authentication Measures in e-Government Platform
Ramsey goodness of large generalized fans
papers.abstract: Given graphs $G$ and $H$, the Ramsey number $r(G,H)$ is the smallest integer $N$ such that any red-blue edge coloring of $K_N$ contains a red copy of $G$ or a blue copy of $H$. If $H$ is connected, Burr's lower bound gives $r(G,H)\geq (\chi(G)-1)(|V(H)|-1)+s(G)$, where $s(G)$ is the minimum size of a color class over all proper $\chi(G)$-colorings of $G$. The graph $H$ is called $G$-good if equality holds in this bound. Liu and Li [J. Graph Theory, 2025] characterized the graphs $G$ with $s(G)=1$ for which $K_p+nH$ is $G$-good for $p\geq 2$ and sufficiently large $n$, and posed the corresponding problem for $p=1$. We solve this problem by showing that for a graph $G$ with $\chi(G)=k+1\geq 2$ and $s(G)=1$, a graph $H$ of order $h$ and sufficiently large $n$, $K_1+nH$ is $G$-good if and only if $G\subseteq mK_2+K_{k-1}(m)$ when $nh$ is odd, or $G\subseteq (mK_2\cup K_{1,2})+K_{k-1}(m)$ when $nh$ is even, for some positive integer $m$.

papers.title: Existence of alternating Hamiltonian paths on specific bicolored point sets
papers.abstract: Consider a bicolored point set $P$ in general position in the plane consisting of $n$ blue and $n$ red points. We show that if $P$ can be partitioned into bicolored pairs $(a_i,b_i)$ such that, for every $i$, $a_i$ and $b_i$ have different colors and the sets $P\setminus \{a_i\}$ and $P \setminus \{b_i\}$ have the same order type, then there exists a noncrossing alternating Hamiltonian path on $P$. We also investigate the case when $P$ lies on the circle, and every interval along the circle contains at most $c$ more points of one color than of the other. For $c=2$, we show that there exists a noncrossing alternating Hamiltonian path on $P$. For $c=3$, we show that there exist configurations of points for which the longest noncrossing alternating path on $P$ has size at most $(2-1/25)n + O(1)$.

papers.title: Cluster-Robust Inference in Small Samples Using Bias Corrections
papers.abstract: This paper derives an exact expression for the bias of the linearized estimator of the variance for cluster-robust inference, which generalizes an earlier result derived by Bell and McCaffrey (2002). Both cases of continuous and binary treatments are discussed. Under the former it is shown that the bias of the linearized variance estimator and its jackknife variant are of order $G^{-1}$ relative to the true variance, where $G$ denotes the total number of clusters. A bias-corrected variance estimator (BCCV) is then proposed and shown to have a relative bias of order $G^{-2}$. In the case of models with binary treatments the orders of the bias of standard estimators and the proposed bias-corrected one are shown to be $\max (G_{1}^{-1},G_{0}^{-1})$ and $\max (G_{1}^{-2},G_{0}^{-2})$, where $G_{1}$ and $G_{0}=G-G_{1}$ are the numbers of treated and untreated clusters. Scale and degrees of freedom adjustments to the $t$-statistic computed using bias-corrected standard errors are also proposed. Small sample properties of the proposed BCCV test are investigated using Monte Carlo experiments. It is shown that the proposed test generally outperforms tests based on conventional and jackknife cluster standard errors, and performs comparably to wild bootstrap inference and the recent jackknife distribution-adjusted testing procedure by \cite{hansen2026jackknife}. The utility of the proposed test is illustrated\ using three empirical applications from the literature.

papers.title: From Objective Compromise to Structure-Enabled Intelligence: Reshaping the Scientific Paradigm of AI
papers.abstract: Mainstream artificial intelligence systems, particularly Large Language Models (LLMs), are fundamentally constructed upon the Optimization-Driven (OD) paradigm. This paradigm can be characterized as an ill-posed optimization problem within a high-dimensional parameter space. When confronted with real-world scenarios characterized by noise and conflicting constraints, the logic of global error minimization inherently induces a strong smoothing effect. Consequently, this yields statistical compromise solutions that flatten local features, making it arduous to overcome the inherent bottleneck of Out-of-Distribution (OOD) generalization. Existing AI models generate outputs purely based on statistical probabilities. They lack the capacity to autonomously discern truth from falsehood or establish causal logic, thereby lacking genuine cognitive intelligence. To address the ontological limitations of the OD paradigm, this paper proposes a novel paradigm termed \textit{Structure-Enabled Intelligence}. This approach abandons the conventional path of relying solely on computing power scaling and data fitting to achieve emergent intelligence. Instead, it embeds mathematical structures and physical mechanisms as underlying priors into the algorithmic architecture, constraining the model's solving process with structured scientific rules. Through this paradigm shift from ``data-driven objective fitting'' to ``mechanism-structure dominance,'' the proposed approach fundamentally mitigates the issue of statistical compromise, enhances the model's extrapolation and generalization capabilities, and simultaneously reshapes human-AI synergy by upholding human subjectivity in scientific cognition.

papers.title: DyTransRM: A Unified Simulation-to-Real Framework for Dynamic Radio Map Prediction
papers.abstract: Dynamic radio map (RM) prediction enables proactive wireless network control by forecasting future propagation conditions from historical observations. However, collecting temporally continuous and spatially dense real-world RMs is prohibitively expensive, while models trained on large-scale simulated data often suffer from limited transferability to real environments. To address this issue, we propose DyTransRM, a unified simulation-to-real framework for dynamic RM prediction under sparse real-world measurements. DyTransRM first introduces RadioCLIP to learn physics-semantic representations by aligning environmental evolution with the corresponding propagation evolution, thereby improving both prediction accuracy and cross-domain transferability. To further bridge the simulation-to-real gap, SparseUOT employs sparse-mask simulation refinement to mimic realistic measurement patterns and unbalanced optimal transport to selectively align compatible propagation representations across domains. Experiments on RadioMapMotion and real-world datasets demonstrate that RadioCLIP achieves an NMSE of 0.0018 and an RMSE of 0.012 in simulation-domain prediction. After sparse real-domain adaptation, DyTransRM achieves an NMSE of 0.023, RMSE of 0.079, and MAE of 0.064, outperforming representative adaptation baselines without requiring spatially complete real RMs. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of DyTransRM for transferring simulation-learned dynamic propagation knowledge to practical sparse-measurement scenarios.

papers.title: Prepare Lighter and Faster for Open-Vocabulary Queries: A Query-Wise 3D Segmenter for Gaussian Splatting
Hydrogen in Practice: A Global Review of Demonstration Projects from Production to Integration
Memorization Lives in a Few Attention Heads: Mitigating Memorization in Diffusion Models via Projection-Based Suppression
Fault Diagnosis and Fault-Tolerant Operation Strategy for Triple-Port Hydrogen Production System
Ultrastrong coupling between magnetoplasmons and higher cyclotron-resonance harmonics induced by spatially inhomogeneous electromagnetic fields in two-dimensional electron systems
papers.abstract: Finite-wave-vector electromagnetic fields provide a route to accessing nonlocal collective dynamics in two-dimensional electron systems. Here, we theoretically investigate the magnetoplasmon response of a two-dimensional electron system subjected to a spatially nonuniform electromagnetic field in a perpendicular magnetic field. By combining Maxwell's equations with the Kubo formula, we derive the nonlocal magnetoconductivity tensor and obtain the self-consistent dispersion relation for collective modes. We show that a finite in-plane wave vector enables higher-order cyclotron transitions, allowing higher harmonics of the cyclotron resonance to contribute to the nonlocal conductivity. These harmonics hybridize with the magnetoplasmon mode, producing avoided crossings in the collective-mode spectrum characteristic of Bernstein modes. To quantify this hybridization, we establish a correspondence between the Maxwell-Kubo dispersion relation and a Hopfield-type Hamiltonian and derive an analytical expression for the effective coupling strength between the magnetoplasmon and the n-th cyclotron-resonance harmonic. Our analysis reveals that the normalized coupling strength exhibits a nonmonotonic dependence on the in-plane wavelength, reaching a maximum that becomes nearly independent of electron density in the high-density regime. These results establish a quantitative connection between nonlocal magnetoconductivity, Bernstein-mode physics, and effective collective-mode coupling, providing design guidelines for realizing ultrastrong coupling in terahertz magnetoplasmonic systems.

papers.title: On the Waldschmidt constant of monomial ideals
papers.abstract: We investigate a conjecture proposed by Cooper et al. in 2017 regarding a lower bound for the Waldschmidt constant of monomial ideals. We first show that this conjecture does not hold in general by explicitly computing the Waldschmidt constant for a family of monomial ideals. Also, we identify a class of monomial ideals for which this conjecture holds by proving a containment between symbolic and ordinary powers. For a monomial ideal, we provide a new lower bound for the Waldschmidt constant, which modifies the conjectured lower bound under a certain condition.

papers.title: Smoothing of the Coupled KdV System on \mathbb{T}
papers.abstract: We study the nonlinear smoothing properties of the Coupled KdV system posed on the torus. This system arises as a particular case of the four-parameter family of Boussinesq systems studied by Bona, Chen and Saut, corresponding to the choice $\eta^{2}=\frac{2}{3}$, $b=d=0$ and $a=c=\frac{1}{6}$. Although the similarities with the periodic KdV equation and the favorable resonance structure of the Majda-Biello system for the coupling parameter $\alpha =-1$ might suggest that smoothing can be established by a relatively straightforward adaptation of existing techniques, the nonlinear interactions in the Coupled KdV system introduce additional difficulties. In particular, certain mixed interactions lead to degeneracies in the associated resonance functions, resulting in a loss of frequency decay that restricts the attainable smoothing gain. By combining normal-form reductions, duality arguments and Bourgain-space estimates, we establish a smoothing gain of any order $ a< \min \{1,\frac{2}{3}(2s+1)\} $ for $s>-\frac{1}{2}$. Our result demonstrates that the interplay between nonlinear interactions and resonance structures plays a decisive role in determining the smoothing properties of coupled dispersive systems.

papers.title: Hydration-induced local diffusivity heterogeneity modulates aqueous $H_2+OH$ reaction kinetics
papers.abstract: At room temperature, a Kramers reaction rate calculated with homogeneous solvent friction exceeds the measured rate of the aqueous reaction $H_2 + OH -> H + H_2O$ by about an order of magnitude. We show that spatially correlated hydration-induced diffusivity fluctuations increase effective friction and suppress the predicted escape rate. Estimates based on hydration-shell properties bring the theoretical rate closer to experiment. The suppression weakens with increasing temperature, linking local solvent heterogeneity to activated aqueous reaction kinetics.

papers.title: Federated versus Centralized PV Capacity-Factor Forecasting: A Non-Inferiority Study Across Seven Stations in North Macedonia
Food co-purchasing networks encode geographic disparities in cardiometabolic health
Do Pretraining Optimizer Gains Transfer to KL Distillation?
Real-World End-to-End Product Entity Resolution
Are Revealed Preferences All You Need for AI Alignment?
papers.abstract: AI agents learn what principals want from what principals choose. We offer a criterion for when a principal's decisions, at every belief an AI might hold, are all the AI needs. For acting, they are. Cautious actions, such as deferring to a person, typically divide the principal's actions into blocks, and for choosing costless evidence, decisions are enough exactly when the same evidence is best in every block. Otherwise, the AI acts as its principal would yet can gather the wrong evidence, and greater capability can turn that error into incorrect actions. Choices between two mistakes reveal what decisions miss.

papers.title: Constraining neutrino masses with localized fast radio bursts: Current bounds and future prospects
papers.abstract:
The dispersion-measure (DM)--redshift relation of fast radio bursts (FRBs) provides independent low-redshift cosmological information for neutrino-mass inference. In this work, we perform joint analyses with cosmic microwave background (CMB) data, using 120 localized FRBs with reliable host-galaxy redshifts and larger mock samples, to investigate the effects of sample size and the dark-energy model on constraints on the sum of neutrino masses, $\sum m_
u$. In the $\Lambda$CDM+$\sum m_
u$ model, CMB+FRB gives $\sum m_
u<0.21\,\mathrm{eV}$, substantially relaxed relative to the current CMB+DESI result. With 1000 simulated events, CMB+FRB1(mock) gives an upper limit of $0.12\,\mathrm{eV}$, which decreases to $0.035\,\mathrm{eV}$ for CMB+FRB2(mock) with 10000 events. The latter is more stringent than the CMB+DESI limit, demonstrating the potential of large localized FRB samples to constrain neutrino mass. When the model is extended to $w_0w_a$CDM+$\sum m_
u$, both the observed and mock samples yield upper limits of approximately $0.3$--$0.4\,\mathrm{eV}$, indicating that the assumed dark-energy model remains a dominant factor in these constraints. As localized FRB samples grow and the modeling of the individual DM contributions becomes more accurate, FRBs may provide further independent low-redshift information for constraining neutrino mass.

papers.title: Universal Analytical Description of Magnetoexcitons in Two-Dimensional Semiconducting Materials
papers.abstract: Matching the Coulomb and logarithmic limits of the Rytova--Keldysh model gives a universal zero-field spectrum for monolayer exciton $s$ states, $E_n\simeq-\mathrm{Ry}^*/[n-1/2+f_n(\xi)]^2$, where $\xi$ is the screening parameter. Analytical radii determine diamagnetic coefficients and the magnetic crossover scale. Zero-field deviations peak near $1\%$ across the full screening range $0\leq\xi\leq100$. For the sampled hBN-encapsulated monolayers, magnetoexciton energies agree with numerical spectra to sub-meV rms up to $100\T$ and capture the measured orbital shifts. Shared parameters link optical and magneto-optical spectra.

papers.title: First-order convergence of finite-difference approximations to the minimum action for diffusions with multiplicative noise
PMR: MoE Routing with Shared Prototypes and Congestion Pricing
A Hierarchical Group Factor Model with Characteristic-Driven Global and Local Factors
papers.abstract: We propose a Hierarchical Group Factor Model (HGFM) for jointly estimating global and group-specific factors with characteristic-driven portfolio weights. Both factor types are constructed from contemporaneous returns, producing endogeneity that we address by quasi-maximum likelihood estimation. Conditional on the interaction matrices, we separate the global and local coefficient components and normalize their factor representations.
