FundingClaw: Automated Grant Proposal Writing Agents System
From zero-target transfer to target-site personalization: multi-source training across fall-detection models
Personalized Language Models for One-to-Many Private Communications
GENMETA-Lite: A Fast and Flexible Approach to Federated Learning with Disparate Covariate Information Across Studies
papers.abstract: Meta-analysis is foundational to federated learning, where one learns parameters by combining information across studies without sharing individual-level data. Handling missing and disparate covariates across studies is a major issue due to potential introduction of bias and decreased efficiency. We previously proposed a generalized meta-analysis estimator (GENMETA) to build a unified regression model using information on parameter estimates from sub-models and a reference population to estimate the joint covariate distribution. Building on that work, we present a linear estimator (GENMETA-Lite) as a practical, non-iterative method for multivariate meta-analysis, extended to handle heterogeneity in covariate distributions across studies, coarsened covariates, and model selection. Simulations demonstrate that our estimator has robust performance compared to estimates from naïve inverse-variance weighted meta-analysis or multiple imputation with individual-level data (approximately 4 to 100-fold reduction in mean squared error), even when underlying assumptions of linearity and homogeneous distributions are violated. We apply the method to fit a breast cancer risk prediction model with data from five studies (N = 313,851). Our study shows GENMETA-Lite is a robust federated learning approach for building regression models by combining information across disparate studies. An R package implementing these methods is made publicly available.

papers.title: ImpedanceMimic: Learned Impedance as Action Space for Force-Accurate Motion Imitation
Exact mobility edges in high-dimensional quasiperiodic networks
papers.abstract: Inspired by the one-dimensional hidden self-duality [Phys. Rev. Lett. 134, 246301 (2025)], we establish a generalized theoretical framework for a specific class of high-dimensional quasiperiodic network models. Specifically, as long as the periodic network acts as bond-decorating links and the quasiperiodic potentials are spatially separable, the system can be mapped onto an effective high-dimensional generalized Aubry-André equation by integrating out the periodic sites. This mapping restores the hidden self-duality symmetry in these complex models, thereby yielding exact mobility edges. Taking two-dimensional and three-dimensional models as examples, we demonstrate the consistency between the theoretical prediction and the numerical results. This paper establishes a clear paradigm for mapping high-dimensional quasiperiodic networks to high-dimensional Aubry-André models, providing a systematic pathway for the construction and exploration of the exact mobility edge in high-dimensional systems.

papers.title: MarineSparkLM-4B: A Lightweight Language Model for Marine and Offshore Engineering Built by Parameter-Efficient Adaptation
Normalized ground states of Kirchhoff equation on waveguide manifolds
papers.abstract: We study the nonlinear Kirchhoff equation on the waveguide manifolds $\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{T}^n$: \begin{align*} -\left( a+b \int_{\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{T}^n}|\nabla_{x,y}u(x,y)|^2\,dxdy\right) \Delta_{x,y}u+\omega u=|u|^\alpha u, \end{align*} where $a,b>0$, $\omega\in \mathbb{R}$, $\alpha\in(0,2^*)$. We first establish existence of the normalized ground states when $\alpha\in(0,2^*)$. To precisely characterize the $y$-dependence of ground states, we apply a scaling argument to handle the integral term $ \int_{\mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{T}^n} |\nabla_{x,y} u(x,y)|^2 dxdy$. To this end, we construct two distinct modified energy functionals, through which we establish the $y$-independence and $y$-dependence of the ground states in two specific regimes: $(i)$ $ d + n \leq 4$ and $\alpha \in (0, \frac{8}{d+n})$; $(ii)$ $d = n = 1$ and $\alpha \in (8, \infty)$.

papers.title: Classification of ${\rm GL}_1(D)\times {\rm GL}_{n-1}(D)$-distinguished representations
papers.abstract: Let $D$ be a quaternion division algebra over a non-Archimedean local field $F$ of characteristic zero. We prove the conjecture of Dagar, Sharma, and Verma classifying irreducible smooth representations of $\mathrm{GL}_n(D)$ distinguished by $\mathrm{GL}_1(D)\times\mathrm{GL}_{n-1}(D)$ for $n>2$. These are precisely the trivial representation and the irreducible normalized parabolic inductions $\one_{n-2}\times\tau$, where $\tau$ is an infinite-dimensional irreducible representation of $\mathrm{GL}_2(D)$ distinguished by $\mathrm{GL}_1(D)\times\mathrm{GL}_1(D)$. The proof combines a choice of cuspidal inducing factor with orbit conditions and multisegment methods.

papers.title: HDR-DTCP: High-Dynamic-Range Differential Tissue-Coupled Wireless Powering for Tunable Biphasic Stimulation in Injectable Implants
A Bias-Variance Framework for Estimating Stochastic Speed-Density Relationship Considering Constrained Sample Size
papers.abstract: Accurate calibration of traffic speed-density fundamental diagram models is essential for freeway traffic flow analysis, yet existing approaches estimate parameters from fixed datasets without examining how estimates evolve as data availability increases. This study develops a comprehensive Bayesian stochastic calibration framework integrating sequential Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) estimation via a Metropolis-Hastings within Gibbs sampling scheme with a novel Bias-Variance Cone analysis for asymptotic parameter identification. The framework is applied to 17 macroscopic speed-density models using one full year of 5-minute PeMS loop detector data from three California freeway stations. Sequential MCMC progressively increases the number of randomly sampled days from 1 to 365, enabling systematic evaluation of parameter stability and convergence as a function of data availability. Among the 17 models, nine achieved stable posterior convergence with physically interpretable estimates, while four exhibited catastrophic structural failures due to logarithmic singularities, unit incompatibilities, and initialization sensitivity. The Bias-Variance Cone framework, representing the first application of asymptotic bias-variance decomposition to fundamental diagram calibration, establishes that free-flow speed parameters are reliably identified within approximately 30 days, whereas density and shape parameters require 100 to 182 days, providing the first quantitative minimum data requirements in the literature. Collectively, the findings provide an empirical identifiability ranking of 17 fundamental diagram models, a validated minimum data sufficiency framework, and a replicable, automated platform for large-scale stochastic fundamental diagram calibration.

papers.title: Puzzle: One Pass Is Not Enough for Open-Vocabulary Remote Sensing Segmentation
A Systematic Study of Cross-Token Transfer for Data-Efficient Non-Verbal Text-to-Speech
Large-$N$ expansion in SU($N$) Yang-Mills-like theories
papers.abstract: It has been known for fifty years that bare U($N$) pure Yang-Mills (YM) theory admits the large-$N$ 't Hooft expansion for the $n$-point connected correlators of gauge-invariant single-trace operators, where the corresponding Feynman diagrams are topologically classified by the sum over the genus $g$ of $n$-punctured smooth orientable closed Riemann surfaces. In fact, 't Hooft expansion extends verbatim to U($N$) YM-like theories whose Lagrangians only involve fields valued in the U($N$) Lie algebra - including supersymmetric (SUSY) extensions of pure YM theory such as $\mathcal{N}=1,4$ SUSY YM. The aim of the present paper is to systematically work out the topology of the large-$N$ expansion in SU($N$) - as opposed to U($N$) - YM-like theories, where a number of subtleties inevitably arise. Indeed, since the U($1$) inside the U($N$) YM-like theories decouples, the large-$N$ U($N$) and SU($N$) expansions should either essentially coincide or intrinsically differ - in the latter case necessarily by extra - possibly singular - topologies, as the 't Hooft expansion in U($N$) YM-like theories already exhausts all the smooth topologies. In fact, we demonstrate that 't Hooft smooth topologies are actually generically incomplete in the large-$N$ expansion of both the SU($N$) and renormalized U($N$) YM-like theories, where renormalization inevitably separates the SU($N$) sector that is interacting from the U($1$) sector that is free. Specifically, we interpret the extra topologies that arise in SU($N$) theories for correlators of higher-twist quasi-partonic operators as singular pinched closed surfaces, thus extending our previous investigation of correlators of twist-$2$ operators for which extra pinched tori arise.

papers.title: Live Noise Fingerprints for Quantum Program Analysis
Excitation-Selective Control of Protected Subradiant Antiresonances
papers.abstract: Subradiant cavity antiresonances exhibit narrow spectral features, yet controlling their nonlinear response without perturbing the protected resonance remains challenging. Here we demonstrate excitation-selective control of a subradiant antiresonance in a driven two-emitter cavity-QED system. An auxiliary collective channel leaves the antisymmetric single-excitation state unaffected while shifting the doubly excited state, introducing tunable excitation anharmonicity without altering the linear antiresonance. This separation enables control of two-photon excitation pathways and photon correlations. Independently, a spatial coupling phase tunes optical access to the subradiant state without changing its intrinsic decay rate. We find that the interferometric phase information per incident photon is optimized when cavity-induced readout approximately matches intrinsic subradiant decay, while steady-state atomic entanglement peaks at an intermediate coupling phase. We further extend phase-selective optical control to collective subradiant modes in correlated emitter arrays. These results establish collective symmetry and spatial mode matching as distinct controls of nonlinear photon correlations, optical phase information, and atomic entanglement.

papers.title: Asymptotic efficiency of tests for quantum statistical models
papers.abstract: In classical statistics, local asymptotic normality provides a general framework for characterizing optimal testing power and constructing asymptotically efficient procedures. Extending this framework to quantum statistical models introduces additional challenges arising from the noncommutativity of observables and the need to optimize over quantum measurements. In this paper, we develop a theory of asymptotic efficiency for quantum hypothesis testing using quantum local asymptotic normality and the asymptotic representation theorem. We establish sharp nuisance-maximin power bounds for one-sided tests and two-sided tests within the unbiased class by reducing the corresponding classical--quantum Gaussian shift experiments to classical testing problems. This reduction is justified through a quantum Hunt--Stein argument that accommodates both commuting and noncommuting Gaussian coordinates. Under suitable asymptotic invariance conditions, the resulting bounds transfer to the original quantum experiments and are attained by scalar symmetric logarithmic derivative tests. We further develop a two-stage adaptive construction that achieves the same local asymptotic power without knowledge of the reference parameter. As an application, we study testing of smooth spectral functionals of quantum states. We compare scalar symmetric logarithmic derivative tests with the weak Schur sampling plug-in test and with optimally weighted linear statistics of its fluctuations. This comparison distinguishes loss from the plug-in weighting from a gap between the best such spectral statistic and the scalar score procedure. We characterize equality of the corresponding variances and illustrate the two gaps through explicit examples.

papers.title: When the Mythical Man-Month Meets Agentic Web Systems: Structured Coordination for Scalable Development
Spontaneous Chiral Superradiance of a Spin-1 Condensate in a Ring Cavity
papers.abstract: We investigate superradiant phase transitions in a spin-$1$ Bose-Einstein condensate coupled to a ring cavity, where two symmetry-related Raman processes couple the atomic spin states to counterpropagating cavity modes. Above the superradiant threshold, we find that the symmetry between the two Raman channels is spontaneously broken, giving rise to a chiral superradiant (CSR) phase. Despite the exchange symmetry of the Hamiltonian, the CSR state spontaneously selects one of the two propagation directions, with one cavity mode becoming macroscopically occupied while its counterpropagating partner remains dark. Spin-dependent collisions further reshape the superradiant phase diagram by selectively shifting the boundaries between the chiral and symmetric superradiant phases, a feature intrinsic to the multicomponent spin-$1$ manifold. For sufficiently negative spin-dependent interactions, the interaction-induced modification of the atomic level structure gives rise to a reversed plane-wave phase characterized by an inverted internal-state occupation. These results identify spontaneous selection between symmetry-related superradiant channels as a mechanism for generating chirality in many-body cavity QED and demonstrate how spin-dependent collisions control the resulting superradiant phase structure.

papers.title: SuperGlance: Driving at a Glance with a Vision-Language Model
Intervals in affine Bruhat order
papers.abstract: Let $(W,S)$ be an irreducible affine Coxeter system. We study Bruhat intervals in $W$ via the well-known characterization of Bruhat order in terms of galleries. We start by using folded galleries to formulate an analogous order on the coweight lattice, which we call Iwahori order. This allows us to reduce the description of certain Bruhat intervals to that of the corresponding Iwahori intervals. We next give closed-form descriptions of all Iwahori intervals, using the quantum Bruhat graph (QBG). More precisely, we show that lower Iwahori intervals saturate pseudo-Weyl polytopes (that is, certain intersections of negative cones), and upper Iwahori intervals saturate certain unions of positive cones, with the cone points given by explicit formulae involving paths in the QBG. We then describe arbitrary Bruhat intervals by partitioning them into their core, a large region which is (in most cases) completely determined by an Iwahori interval, and their crust, the complementary boundary region. We conclude by proving that, under a super-regularity assumption, the crust is covered by certain locally-defined tesselating shapes. All statements and proofs are rank- and type-free.

papers.title: Low-Latency LLM-Based Streaming Multi-Talker ASR with Verifiable Rewards
How Much Determinism Can Fine-Tuning Buy? Margin Regularisation Against Batch-Induced Token Flips
OGLE-2018-BLG-0829L: A Microlensing System with a Planet Orbiting a Star Possessing a Brown-Dwarf Companion
papers.abstract: We analyze the microlensing event OGLE-2018-BLG-0829, whose light curve exhibits a weak short-term anomaly in addition to the prominent caustic-crossing features of a binary lens. The anomaly cannot be explained by a binary-lens single-source (2L1S) model. We therefore investigate both binary-lens binary-source (2L2S) and triple-lens single-source (3L1S) interpretations and find that both models reproduce the additional anomaly, with the 3L1S model being favored by $\Delta\chi^2=15.1$. Under the favored 3L1S interpretation, the anomaly arises from a caustic induced by a planetary-mass companion, whereas the prominent caustic-crossing features are produced by the underlying binary lens. Combining the measured event timescale, $t_{\rm E}=7.55\pm0.30$ days, and angular Einstein radius, $\theta_{\rm E}=0.325 \pm 0.059$ mas, with a Bayesian analysis, we infer a lens system consisting of an M dwarf of mass $0.193^{+0.300}_{-0.098}\,M_\odot$, a possible brown-dwarf companion of mass $0.068^{+0.105}_{-0.034}\,M_\odot$, and a Saturn-mass planet of mass $0.337^{+0.522}_{-0.171}\,M_{\rm J}$. The companions have projected separations of approximately 3.6 au and 1.6 au from the primary, respectively. However, the physical interpretation remains tentative because potentially important higher-order effects have not been considered, and the dynamical stability of the proposed configuration remains uncertain. If confirmed, this would be the third star--brown dwarf--planet system identified through microlensing, highlighting the potential of microlensing to detect planets in complex multiple systems.

papers.title: Psyquandle Fares
papers.abstract: We introduce a new infinite family of invariants of singular knot and links and of pseudoknots by extending the biquandle fares construction to the case of psyquandles. We give the axioms explicitly for four cases of fare-based invariants: 1-fares, signed crooked 2-fares, signed through 2-fares and signed complete 2-fares. We provide examples of each type, illustrating the method of computation and collecting some results for toy examples using small-cardinality psyquandles and abelian coefficient groups.

papers.title: The Race between Protection and Control: Fast Reactive Reserves Against Overvoltage Cascade
Wireless Edge-Assisted Adaptive Latent Reasoning for Vision-Language-Action Models in Physical AI
Accurate qLDPC decoding under real-time constraints
papers.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires reconciling the computational demands of accurate decoding with the stringent timing constraints of real-time error correction. We present Spatiotemporal Covariance-Optimized Parallel Ensemble (SCOPE), a physics-informed framework for real-time decoding of quantum low-density parity-check codes (qLDPC). By exploiting the spatial symmetries of bivariate-bicycle (BB) codes and the temporal regularity of repeated syndrome extraction, SCOPE uncovers a spatiotemporally covariant decoding structure and organizes the circuit-level problem into a layered decoding strategy. We further compress the high-dimensional evolution of belief propagation (BP) into a low-dimensional dynamical representation, revealing distinct signatures of successful and failed decoding and enabling early detection of unpromising trajectories. Guided by these dynamical signatures, SCOPE explores multiple perturbed decoding trajectories in parallel, enabling early termination and reseeding within a fixed serial iteration budget, with message-passing parameters optimized offline by simulated annealing. Circuit-level simulations of the $[[144,12,12]]$ BB code yield a logical error rate of $p_L=4.82\times10^{-10}$ at a physical error rate of $p=10^{-3}$. We further realize a pipelined two-arm memory-augmented BP (Mem-BP) core at the register-transfer level. Functional simulations at a 250 MHz clock yield a 16 ns BP iteration interval per arm and a mean input-to-result latency of 173.8 ns at $p=5\times10^{-3}$.

papers.title: Classification of Conformal Ising/Tricritical Ising Interfaces Preserving $\mathcal{W}_3^{\mathbb{Z}_2}$ Symmetry
papers.abstract: We classify conformal interfaces between the Ising and tricritical Ising models that preserve the chiral algebra $\mathcal{W}_3^{\mathbb{Z}_2}$. Using the folding trick, we formulate the problem in terms of boundary states satisfying the Cardy condition and determine the unique NIM-rep compatible with the bulk partition function. We obtain a complete set of 24 fundamental boundary states, of which 18 correspond to factorized interfaces preserving the full product Virasoro symmetry, while the remaining six break this symmetry. We construct these six interfaces explicitly and determine their annulus partition functions. They are related by topological defect line dressings, and one coincides with the RG domain wall proposed by Gaiotto.

papers.title: Efficient simulation of the generalized Langevin equation using a basis of dynamically relevant histories for memory and noise
papers.abstract: The Generalized Langevin Equation (GLE) is a cornerstone for modeling non-Markovian dynamics, but its numerical solution remains challenging due to the history-dependent convolution and the need to generate colored noise with a prescribed correlation function. We introduce a forward construction that addresses both challenges within a single framework. We represent an arbitrary trajectory as sum of relevant and irrelevant parts, where relevant part can be decomposed into a small number of characteristic history patterns that make the main contribution to future dynamics. It allows to reduce numerical cost to \(O(d^2)\) for $d$ chosen patterns instead of full history. The same construction applies to colored noise generation, where the causal filter plays the role of the memory kernel. We demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the method for several representative kernels, including long-range kernels with power-law tails.

papers.title: Empowering Masked Diffusion Models to Self-Correct with Leave-One-Out Transformers
A Nonlinear Abstract Domain for Bayesian Neural Networks
AI Inference-Aware Optimal Power Flow: Converting Token Requirements into Grid Flexibility
ANCHOR: A Port-Hamiltonian Model for Forecasting Team Dynamics in Human-in-the-Loop Systems
Beyond Plain MCP: Do Decision Models and Code Mode Make Tool Use Cheaper and Faster?

Joint RF-VLP Position and Velocity Tracking: Bayesian Estimation and Performance Analysis
papers.abstract: Visible light positioning (VLP) provides accurate indoor positioning through optical received signal strength (RSS) measurements, while radio-frequency (RF) delay and Doppler measurements offer complementary range and velocity information. Motivated by this complementarity, we investigate joint RF--VLP position and velocity tracking, addressing both recursive state estimation and its fundamental performance characteristics. We formulate a Bayesian maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimation problem that combines optical RSS, RF delay and Doppler measurements, and motion prediction, and develop a Gauss--Newton-based algorithm for recursive tracking. To characterize the estimation limits and the benefits of RF--VLP integration, we derive the Bayesian information matrix and the corresponding Bayesian Cramér--Rao lower bound (BCRLB). We further introduce a state-conditioned information matrix (SCIM), whose inverse coincides with the MAP estimator's mean-squared error matrix under a first-order observation model, enabling tractable analysis of RF-induced information gains. The analysis quantifies the distinct contributions of RF delay and Doppler measurements and reveals different asymptotic estimation-error behaviors with respect to RF and VLP signal-to-noise ratios. Numerical results demonstrate improved position and velocity tracking over the considered baselines, with substantial velocity gains from RF sensing. The results also validate the theoretical asymptotic predictions and show that the inverse of the SCIM closely captures the estimator's error trends.

Testing General Relativity by Reconstructing Dark Energy and the Growth Index with Physics-Informed Neural Networks
papers.abstract: We extend the Cosmo-PINN, a physics-informed neural network for model-independent cosmological reconstruction, to reconstruct the dark energy equation of state parameter $w_{\mathrm{DE}}(z)$ and the growth index $\gamma (z)$ of matter perturbations. The reconstruction is performed through three modules: the background module, the matter growth module, and the growth index module. The background module learns the dark energy density $\rho _{\mathrm{DE}}(z)$ from cosmological observations, and $w_{\mathrm{DE}}(z)$ is reconstructed through the residual of the conservation equation. The reconstructed background is then passed to the other two modules, which reconstruct the observables $f(z)$ and $f\sigma _{8}(z)$ either directly from the linear perturbation equation of General Relativity or through an independently reconstructed growth index $\gamma (z)$. Comparing the two reconstructions on the same background provides a consistency test of the underlying physical framework. The network is trained on the DESI DR2 Baryon Acoustic Oscillations, Cosmic Chronometers, Type Ia Supernovae, and redshift-space distortion data. Posterior uncertainties for the reconstructed cosmological parameters and functions are obtained through Hamiltonian Monte Carlo sampling. For the different data combinations, the posterior median of the present-day dark energy equation of state lies within the range $w_{\mathrm{DE,0}}\in \lbrack -0.930,-0.867]$, while the phantom divide crossing takes place at $z\simeq 0.41$--$0.53$. The posterior median of the present-day growth index reconstructed from the data lies within $\gamma _{0}\simeq 0.60$--$0.62$, indicating suppression of the growth of cosmic structure.

The Contact Process with Temporary Immunity on $\mathbb{Z}$
papers.abstract: We develop a regeneration scheme for the one-dimensional contact process with temporary immunity, also known as the spatial SIRS process, a non-attractive interacting particle system. The key ingredient is a one-sided space-time shielding mechanism, constructed from infinite infection paths of an auxiliary process. These paths separate the evolution of the infection front from the configuration and graphical history left behind, allowing us to construct regeneration times without relying on attractiveness. The same shielding mechanism also provides coupling arguments for processes started from different initial configurations. Using this approach, we establish a law of large numbers and a functional central limit theorem for the right edge, existence and uniqueness of an invariant law for the process seen from the edge, and complete convergence. We also prove survival from every nonempty finite infected set for sufficiently large immunity-loss rates and derive an explicit extinction criterion.

papers.title: Decoupling Data Layouts from Algebraic Data Types
How to Agree Without Agreeing
papers.abstract: Consensus lets institutions decide without a central authority, but a record of agreement reveals neither its basis nor its credibility. We model support, standing aside and veto as responses to a proposal. A proposal can pass without active support, and the member least willing to allow passage limits what can be adopted, however many members oppose the proposal. Letting proposers moderate their demands can ease agreement while undermining the prescribed punishment. Proposal restrictions or deviation costs can preserve that threat. Across the initialisations tested, learning agents agree frequently even though many reconstructed rules allow profitable departures. In our sample of Antarctic Treaty working papers, 80% of proposals revising existing arrangements were adopted at submission, against 38% of new proposals. Consensus can keep producing agreement on what already exists while new protection waits.

NS-bialgebras, the NS-Yang-Baxter equation and dendriform D-bialgebras
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop a bialgebra theory for NS-algebras via the Manin triple approach. We first study representations of NS-algebras and establish an equivalence among NS-bialgebras, matched pairs and Manin triples of NS-algebras. We then introduce the NS-Yang-Baxter equation (NS-YBE) and show that its symmetric solutions induce triangular NS-bialgebras. We further investigate the relationship between symmetric solutions of the NS-YBE and $\mathcal O$-operators of NS-algebras, and characterize pre-NS-algebras in terms of invertible $\mathcal O$-operators. As an application, we investigate the relation between NS-bialgebras and dendriform D-bialgebras via double constructions of Connes cocycles. In particular, we show that every NS-bialgebra induces a dendriform D-bialgebra structure on the direct sum of two copies of its underlying vector space.

The first-order theory of the ring of integers of any abelian extension of $\Q$ is undecidable
papers.abstract: We show that any ring of totally real abelian integers has a JR-number and therefore the first-order theory of every ring of totally real abelian integers is undecidable. It then follows that the first-order theory of the ring of integers of any abelian extension of $\Q$ is undecidable and that there is one formula without parameters defining $\Z$ in any such ring. The main arithmetic input is a recent paper of Bajpai, Das, Kedlaya, and Mello proving that the houses of cyclotomic integers form a well-ordered subset of $\R$.

papers.title: Stability of Self-Similar Expansions for Self-Gravitating Hyperelastic Bodies
papers.abstract: We consider the three-dimensional elastodynamics system with nonlocal gravitational coupling and nonlinear traction-free boundary conditions, modeling an isolated self-gravitating hyperelastic body, where the strain-energy function is assumed to be objective, isotropic, and homogeneous of degree $-1$. We prove nonlinear stability of a self-similarly expanding separable solution, recently constructed by the authors [JangLeslie2025], under radial perturbations satisfying the codimension-one constraint of zero total energy. Using a self-similar reformulation analogous to that developed for the mass-critical Euler--Poisson system in [HadzicJang2018CPAM], we recast the perturbed equation as a scalar nonlinear five-dimensional radial wave equation and the nonlinear traction-free boundary condition as a homogeneous Neumann condition. A key is to identify a quasilinear form of the leading-order spatial operator that is compatible with this boundary condition and yields coercive energy estimates. Our energy estimates capture the stabilizing effect of the background expansion and yield global existence and nonlinear codimension-one stability in self-similar variables.

Drift of a Charged Particle in a Black Hole Magnetosphere: the Effect of Black Hole Spin
papers.abstract: Sparse plasma immersed in a strong magnetic field is common in astrophysical scenarios, for which a collisionless description is more appropriate. The guiding-center approximation serves as an effective tool for describing the motion of charged particles in a strong magnetic field, revealing the drift, a sub-leading order motion that causes particles to deviate from the magnetic field lines. It is widely accepted that the charged particles drift under the induction of gravity in Newtonian framework. However, a covariant formulation of the guiding-center approximation, as well as the drift of a charged particle induced by strong gravitational field, has yet to be fully explored. As a preliminary study, we aim to analyze the drift of a single charged particle in a black hole magnetosphere via a covariant approach. Particularly, we focus on the effects of black hole spin. We first examine the drift caused by the rotation of a massive object in the Newtonian regime using the language of gravitoelectromagnetism. A covariant formula of drift is derived, which is confirmed to reduce to the Newtonian results in the weak gravitational field and low speed limit. The impact of BH spin on the drift is analyzed in detail in Kerr spacetime specifically, for which we define the drift rate whose value quantifies the significance of the drift. Our results indicate that the impact of BH spin on the drift of a charged particle in a BH magnetosphere can be comparable to that of other factors in some extreme cases.

papers.title: Conditional Principle of Least Action: Gauge Algebra and Noether's Second Theorem
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of a conditional extremum of an action within a class of fields constrained by differential equations. For this setup, we establish the interconnection between the gauge symmetry algebra of the equations constraining the admissible fields and that of the action restricted to this class of fields. Based on this relation between the two gauge algebras, we derive an extension of Noether's second theorem and its converse. The general method is illustrated by the example of linearized gravity with the Einstein-Hilbert action and the class of admissible metrics restricted by the Cotton equation.

ASASSN-15af: An Eclipsing Cataclysmic Variable above the Period Gap Showing Both Positive and Negative Superhump-like Signals
papers.abstract: We present a photometric study of ASASSN-15af (TIC~231050794), combining TESS full-frame-image photometry from the TEQUILA project with 2-minute SPOC light curves and archival ASAS-SN and ATLAS monitoring over 4400~d. The long-term light curve shows recurrent dwarf-nova outbursts, establishing ASASSN-15af as a high-inclination eclipsing dwarf nova above the canonical period gap. From 391 quiescent eclipses, we derive the working ephemeris $T(E)=2139.76108(3)+0.14982063(2)\,E$ (BTJD), corresponding to $P_{\rm orb}=3.596$~hr. A quadratic fit is formally better, but the timings sample only three widely separated epochs, so we regard the apparent O--C curvature as tentative. In quiescence, the out-of-eclipse waveform is dominated by a stable $2f_{\rm orb}$ component, consistent with a substantial ellipsoidal contribution from the donor; during the Sector~96 outburst, its fractional amplitude decreases by $\simeq66\%$, consistent with dilution by the brightened disk. The outburst-only signals occur at periods $\sim1.6\%$ shorter than $P_{\rm orb}$ in Sector~2 and $\sim3.1\%$ longer in Sector~96, consistent with negative- and positive-superhump-like modulations, respectively. Because each is detected in only one outburst, their recurrence remains to be established. Their period-offset ratio, $\phi\simeq0.51$, is consistent with empirical trends among systems showing both modes, while the inferred superhump-based mass ratios span $q\simeq0.06$--$0.24$. During the Sector~96 outburst, the eclipse deepens by $\Delta D=0.196\pm0.028$ and its centroid shifts earlier by $\Delta t_{\rm c}=-66.6\pm7.3$~s, indicating a redistribution of accretion-powered light. These results identify ASASSN-15af as an above-gap eclipsing dwarf nova with a dynamically variable accretion disk; spectroscopy is needed to constrain the mass ratio.

papers.title: Constrained Adiabatic Quantum Programming
papers.abstract: To find a $k$-clique in a graph, adiabatic quantum computation (AQC) evolves a quantum system from the minimum of an initial cost function to the minimum of a problem cost function that penalizes non-cliques. Existing AQC languages fix the initial cost function, so the search ranges over all $2^n$ subsets of the $n$ vertices, although only the subsets of size $k$ can be answers. We present ENQ+, an AQC language in which the programmer writes both cost functions. Data constraints define the problem cost function. Relational constraints, a new construct, declare the moves the search may make between configurations and define the initial cost function. For the clique, a single relational constraint, which exchanges a chosen vertex with an unchosen one, confines the search to the subsets of size $k$. ENQ+ thereby turns constrained quantum annealing, which physicists set up by hand for individual problems, into a programming construct. We give ENQ+ a semantics in many-world configuration (MWC) graphs, whose nodes are configurations and whose edges are moves, and derive from it a step-wise semantics of adiabatic evolution. We prove that a run stays within the component of the MWC graph that contains its initial state, and that a run from an approximate initial state still reaches the answer, with probability equal to its squared overlap with the exact one. We compile ENQ+ to quantum circuits, prove the compilation correct with respect to the semantics, and use ENQ+ to program the Three-Dimensional Matching, Hamiltonian Cycle, and Traveling Salesperson problems.

papers.title: On the Flucher--Rumpf isoperimetric question for the interior Bernoulli free boundary problem: a conformal reformulation, quantitative bounds and the second variation at the disc
papers.abstract: Let $c(\Omega)$ be the Bernoulli constant of a bounded domain $\Omega\subset\R^N$, that is, the infimum of the parameters $\lambda$ for which the interior Bernoulli free boundary problem $\Delta u=0$ in $\Omega\setminus K$, $u=0$ on $\partial\Omega$, $u=1$ and $|\nabla u|=\lambda$ on $\partial K$ admits a classical solution. Flucher and Rumpf asked whether $c(\Omega)\ge c(\Omega^*)$, where $\Omega^*$ is the ball of the same volume. The variational analogue was settled by Daners and Kawohl, but the variational constant differs from $c$ already for the ball, and the original question remains open. We prove the following. (i) Through a conformal parametrisation of $\Omega\setminus K$ by an annulus, every classical solution in a simply connected planar domain with connected, filled free set satisfies $\lambda\ge\mu/R$, where $\pi R^2=|\Omega|$ and $\mu\approx 2.485268$; hence $c(\Omega)\ge 0.9142\,c(\Omega^*)$ for every bounded planar convex domain of class $C^1$. (ii) In this class, the Flucher--Rumpf inequality is equivalent to an area inequality for analytic functions in an annulus, which also provides an explicit generator of exact solutions. (iii) A Rellich--Pohozaev identity yields, in every dimension $N\ge2$ and for every strictly star-shaped domain, $c(\Omega)\ge\max\{\sqrt{\theta(\Omega)},\kappa_N\}\,c(\Omega^*)$, where $\theta(\Omega)\in(0,1]$ is an explicit geometric quantity equal to $1$ only for balls and $\kappa_N$ is an explicit constant with $\kappa_3\approx0.650$ and $\kappa_N\to1$ as $N\to\infty$.

The fate of hidden symmetries under magnetic Harrison transformations
papers.abstract: Solution-generating transformations construct new geometries from known seeds, raising the question of whether and to what extent the resulting solutions inherit the hidden symmetries underlying the seeds' integrability and separability. We have established universal perturbative inheritance laws for CKTs and massless scalar separability directly at the level of magnetic Harrison transformations, encompassing both magnetization of Carter-type seeds and demagnetization of conformal Carter-type seeds. In both magnetized Kerr and demagnetized Kerr-Bertotti-Robinson, this perturbative inheritance coexists with the loss of exact Carter-type separability, while seed-connected conformal Killing-Yano structures are already obstructed at the same perturbative order. These results reveal a hierarchy in the perturbative survival of hidden symmetries and provide a framework for investigating their inheritance in more general theoretical settings and under other solution-generating transformations.

A proof of Schmeisser's conjecture
papers.abstract: In 1977, Schmeisser proposed a strengthening of Sendov's conjecture: if all zeros of a polynomial $p$ of degree $n\ge2$ lie in the closed unit disk, then for every point $\xi$ in the convex hull of the zeros of $p$, there exists a critical point $\zeta$ of $p$ such that $ |\xi-\zeta|\le 1.$ We prove this conjecture in every degree. The proof combines a covering of the convex hull by diameter disks, inequalities for reflected polynomials, and quantitative estimates for centred products, supplemented by rigorous computer-assisted verification in a finite range of degrees.

papers.title: Stochastic gauge fixing from the holographic renormalization group
papers.abstract: We extend the dictionary between stochastic quantization and holographic Wilsonian renormalization to Yang-Mills theory in four-dimensional anti-de Sitter space at tree level. The radial component of the bulk gauge field is Zwanziger's gauge-fixing function; radial gauge is Parisi-Wu quantization, whose random walk of gauge modes is the longitudinal bulk propagator. We obtain the triple- and quadruple-trace couplings of gluons at finite cutoff in closed form. On transverse data, their dependence on the bulk gauge resides in a single zero mode, which drops out of the flat-space limit.

papers.title: CONTEXT-PCa: Evaluating the role of clinical context in MRI-based AI for detecting clinically significant prostate cancer (study protocol)
RoboCoEvo: Expanding Robot Capabilities through Agent-Policy Co-Evolution
AI climate trajectories shaped by growth, power choices and decarbonization
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is emerging as a major source of electricity demand, yet its operational greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions remain difficult to resolve geographically. We develop a facility-level global inventory of AI-oriented data centers and extend it to 2030 using documented expansion plans and grid-policy scenarios. Under Current Policies, emissions increase from 20.4 MtCO$_2$e in 2024 to 68.7 MtCO$_2$e in 2030, with parameter-side Monte Carlo 5th--95th percentile ranges of 19.3--21.0 and 60.8--73.9 MtCO$_2$e, respectively. Only six geographies, representing less than 3% of projected capacity, avoid rising emissions. Grid decarbonization consistent with net zero by 2050 lowers projected 2030 emissions to 48.3 MtCO$_2$e, but fossil-based behind-the-meter generation erodes this benefit. Under that scenario, the U.S. behind-the-meter emissions penalty exceeds the combined AI-data-center emissions outside the United States. These findings support coordinated capacity planning, faster access to low-carbon electricity and limits on routine fossil-based behind-the-meter supply.

Stokes Waves in a Finite-Depth Fluid via a Conformal Transformation
papers.abstract: Euler equations for a spatially periodic surface in a two-dimensional fluid of a finite depth are reduced to a system of evolution equations after a conformal transformation. Compared to the previously developed formal approach, we show that the system of evolution equations is complemented by two constraints which determine the new depth in conformal variables and the Bernoulli integration constant. A locally unique continuation of the traveling Stokes waves with respect to the wave speed is studied by using arguments based on the implicit function theorem. We show that the constraints on the traveling wave profile recover the correct small-amplitude expansion of Stokes waves in physical variables. We also prove for the co-periodic stability problem that the real unstable eigenvalues may bifurcate from the zero eigenvalue only at a critical point of the wave energy. Finally, we perform numerical approximations of the wave profiles for both small and large amplitudes and illustrate different bifurcations along the solution family.

papers.title: Corporate Stances on Societal Issues in the US
papers.abstract: When do firms take public positions on divisive societal issues and why? We assemble a comprehensive dataset on corporate stance-taking in the United States, using large language models to read 52,000 news articles and press releases about 836 companies that belonged to the S&P 500 at any point between 2008 and 2025. We identify 9,917 stances on nine partisan issues such as climate change, abortion, and racial discrimination. We show that stance-taking increased fourfold after 2008 and peaked in 2021. It is overwhelmingly liberal and concentrated among the largest firms. A quarter of stances give no explicit business justification. Stance-taking is only weakly related to lobbying and campaign contributions and, unlike them, does not follow the electoral cycle. Instead, firms tend to speak when media coverage and public interest in an issue peak. Together, these findings suggest that stance-taking can be understood as a contribution to broad policy debates rather than a strategy to shape policies that affect firms' core business. Finally, we investigate whose views corporate stances represent. Consumer-facing firms take more stances, and firms whose consumers lean Democratic take more liberal stances on issues other than climate. Companies with larger shares of Democratic employees, executives, and board members also take more liberal stances. Exploiting within-firm variation, we find that having more Democrats among a company's leadership increases liberal stance-taking, while having more women increases stance-taking on gender-related issues and abortion.

papers.title: Classification of critical points of heat kernels on flat tori and Riemann theta functions
papers.abstract: For any two-dimensional flat torus $E_\tau:=\mathbb{C}/(\mathbb Z+\mathbb Z\tau)$ and any $t>0$, we prove that the heat kernel $p_{\tau}(z,t)$ has either four or six critical points on $z\in E_{\tau}$ (i.e., including four trivial critical points and at most one pair of nontrivial critical points). This is interestingly consistent with Lin-Wang's remarkable result (Ann. Math. 2010) for the Green function. The key idea is to show that any nontrivial critical point (if it exists) is a nondegenerate global minimum point. Furthermore, we classify the types of all critical points, as well as the splitting phenomena that occur when the number of critical points changes. Applications to Riemann theta functions are also given.

papers.title: Midsagittal Corpus Callosum Parameterization: A Framework for Spatially Detailed Diffusion MR Imaging Analysis
papers.abstract: The corpus callosum (CC) is the largest white matter structure in the human brain and plays a central role in interhemispheric communication. Diffusion MR imaging is widely used to investigate microstructural organization, but commonly used analysis approaches have important limitations. Voxel-based methods rely heavily on accurate inter-subject registration and smoothing choices, tract-based spatial statistics (TBSS) restricts the analysis to a narrow white matter skeleton, and parcellation approaches reduce spatial detail by averaging diffusion measures over relatively large regions. In this work, we introduce a parameterization framework for the analysis of the midsagittal CC that resamples the structure using a standardized grid of points, establishing a geometric correspondence across individuals without explicit inter-subject registration. In a test-retest dataset, the method provided stable measurements while covering most of the midsagittal CC, and sensitivity analyses showed that results in the central CC changed little under perturbations of the input CC mask, whereas peripheral regions were more sensitive. The framework was further evaluated in group analyses of aging and Alzheimer's disease in datasets that differ in acquisition protocol and spatial resolution. Effect-size maps and quantitative comparisons showed that its results were largely consistent with TBSS and parcellation-based analyses in the overall spatial pattern of effects, while also revealing additional spatially localized differences. These findings suggest that the parameterization provides a simple, computationally efficient, and spatially detailed approach for investigating midsagittal CC microstructure, offering a structure-specific complement to whole-brain and region-based methods.

papers.title: A Fast Algorithm for the Familywise Loss
Policy Optimization With Multiple Verifiers via Pareto Rankings
Detection of CH$_2$NH on Titan
papers.abstract: Saturn's moon, Titan, presents a chemical environment where abiotic synthesis of organics essential for life -- including amino acids and nucleotide bases -- may naturally occur. The assessment of Titan's organic content begins with characterizing its atmospheric chemical inventory, where many predicted molecular species remain unidentified. Here, we present the definitive spectroscopic detection of CH$_2$NH (methanimine) on Titan from observations with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array. CH$_2$NH represents the first stable imine (C=N) to be detected on Titan, and may be integral for further biomolecule formation as a precursor to glycine and adenine. We find abundances of CH$_2$NH at the 0.1--1 ppb level in Titan's mesosphere through multiple valid vertical profile configurations, yielding total column densities ranging from $\sim0.9$--$3\times10^{13}$ cm$^{-2}$. Middle-atmospheric abundances are commensurate with recent photochemical model predictions. However, models with parameterized galactic cosmic ray (GCR) fluxes, which exhibit a secondary, stratospheric formation site, are shown to provide poor fits to the data. Thus, our results provide confirmation of predicted formation and destruction pathways for CH$_2$NH in the upper atmosphere, and demonstrate secondary formation mechanisms in the lower atmosphere require adjustments. The latter presents an important barrier for fully estimating Titan's lower atmospheric composition, as enhanced production by GCR is predicted for additional N-bearing species, such as NH$_3$ and CH$_3$NH$_2$ (methylamine). The detection of CH$_2$NH provides the motivation to search for additional species fundamental for prebiotic molecule formation, which will dramatically improve our understanding of complex molecular synthesis of relevance to astrobiology in CH$_4$-rich environments.

papers.title: Log-optimal two-sample testing by betting
Large Language Models for AI Infrastructure
Interplay of interfacial energetics and selective Ni segregation in the morphology of co-precipitates in low-alloy steels
papers.abstract: Coupled precipitation and interfacial segregation in low-alloy steels change precipitate stability and morphology, which influence strengthening and embrittlement. Cu-rich precipitates (CRPs) and Mn-Ni-Si-rich precipitates (MNSPs) frequently form core-shell or appendage morphologies, but the interfacial energetics controlling this change are not well quantified. We combine a density-functional-theory-trained cluster expansion with lattice Monte Carlo simulations to evaluate the Fe/CRP, Fe/MNSP and Cu/MNSP interfaces within one Hamiltonian. The three coefficients based on excess internal energy follow gamma_Cu/MNSP < gamma_Fe/CRP <~ gamma_Fe/MNSP and give a positive work of adhesion and a negative spreading parameter, consistent with favorable Mn-Ni-Si attachment to a CRP and partial coverage. Only Ni segregates to the Fe/CRP boundary. Mn and Si segregate weakly on their own but become more enriched when Ni is present and co-segregate with Ni at the boundary. Ni forms an interfacial layer about one monolayer thick with an excess of 7.4-9.6 atoms/nm^2, develops B2-like local order and shows an energy reduction that increases with Ni coverage. At 1 at.% matrix Ni, a Gibbs adsorption analysis gives a Fe/CRP free-energy reduction of about 0.15 J/m^2. These interface coefficients and segregation trends connect segregation, interface energy and co-precipitation and support compositional optimization in low-alloy steels.

papers.title: High-dimensional limit theorems for adaptive variants of SGD I: Ballistic limits
Projected DKP spin-1 sectors in a $(2+1)$-dimensional static wormhole: Self-duality, helicity content, and spectral correspondence
papers.abstract: We use the projected spin-1 Duffin--Kemmer--Petiau (DKP) equation in $2+1$ dimensions to clarify the physical content of the irreducible $3\times3$ representations. The projected antisymmetric tensor is algebraically dual to the projected vector, and the two twin representations select conjugate self-dual covariant-curl sectors, which reduce to opposite massive helicities in the flat-space limit. We then apply this structure to the static wormhole problem previously studied with a single irreducible representation. The first-order radial DKP system contains an exceptional normalizable bound-state branch at $\omega^2=M^2$ that is absent from the master-variable reduction, whereas the generic master and circular sectors are related by a Darboux transformation. The latter preserves the transmission and reflection probabilities, while the quasinormal modes are organized into two pole families in the complex radial-momentum plane, leading to the physical pairing $(\omega,-\omega^*)$ rather than a global $\pm\omega$ prescription.

papers.title: Non-Uniform Array Configuration and Antenna Deactivation for Energy-Efficient Sensing
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a non-uniform array design framework for energy-efficient multi-target sensing by jointly optimizing the antenna configuration and the transmit covariance matrix (TCM). To begin with, a limited number of antennas are selected from a set of antenna locations to maximize the minimum mainlobe-to-peak-sidelobe-level ratio (MMPSR) over a sensing region. Next, the antenna configuration is optimized using a simulated annealing (SA)-based search, while a TCM optimization problem is formulated using Charnes-Cooper transformation and solved as a convex semidefinite program for each fixed configuration. Subsequently, an adaptive antenna deactivation strategy is developed to determine the maximum number of antennas that can be switched off while satisfying an MMPSR requirement. Finally, simulation results demonstrate that the proposed non-uniform array design outperforms fixed uniform and non-uniform array benchmarks and requires fewer active antennas to achieve a required sensing performance, thereby supporting energy-efficient sensing.

Aspirational Identities: How VTubing Affords New Modes of Digital Embodiment

Quasi-particle sector hybridization and the onset of chaos in spin ladders
papers.abstract: How quasiparticle numbers influence the emergence of quantum chaos is a fundamental question in interacting many-body systems. We investigate this interplay in a spin-$1/2$ XXZ ladder, where the strong-rung regime supports an approximate organization of many-body eigenstates into quasi-particle(triplon) number sectors. Using spectral statistics, triplon-based observables, and von Neumann entanglement entropy, we characterize the microscopic hybridization of triplon-number sectors as the leg coupling increases. We find that the crossover toward Gaussian orthogonal ensemble statistics shifts to weaker couplings with increasing system size, whereas the characteristic crossover scale associated with triplon-sector hybridization exhibits a much weaker size dependence. Furthermore, eigenstate-to-eigenstate fluctuations exhibit scaling consistent with the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis even while remnants of the strong-rung structure persist, suggesting that spectral chaos does not necessarily require complete sector hybridization.

Slow and rapid mixing in $\mathbb{Z}_2$ hyperlattice gauge theory
papers.abstract: The Ising model under Glauber dynamics on the torus is known to exhibit a phase transition in its mixing time. The mixing is exponentially slow when $\beta >\beta_c$ and logarithmically fast when $\beta <\beta_c$. In this paper, we generalize the slow-mixing result to $\mathbb{Z}_2$ hyperlattice gauge theory when $\beta$ is large enough. This is a higher-dimensional analogue of the Ising model, with spins on $k$-cells. Specifically, on the torus of any dimension $m \ge k+2$, we prove explicit exponential lower bounds on the mixing time of Glauber dynamics when $\beta$ is sufficiently large. More precisely, we prove that the result holds for a broader class of dynamics, allowing more than one $k$-cell to change its value at each step of the algorithm. Finally, we show that there are distinct slow and rapid mixing regimes, as for sufficiently small $\beta$ the Dobrushin condition is satisfied for Glauber dynamics under the heat-bath rule, which implies logarithmic mixing.

papers.title: SPARC: Evidence-guided adaptive model composition for materials discovery
papers.abstract: Closed-loop experimentation requires more than selecting the next experiment. It must also determine which existing measurements and model-derived relationships are sufficiently supported to influence that decision. Here we introduce SPARC (Sparse Predictive Aggregation of Regression Components), a framework that continually revises this support as experimental evidence accumulates. Competing model families are evaluated through out-of-fold predictions, so that each model is tested on observations not used in its corresponding fit. Sparse posterior composition assigns model influence according to predictive contributions supported by the out-of-fold evidence, retaining complementary contributions from several model families. Candidate-dependent predictive dispersion and residual variability define trust, which modulates exploration alongside the predicted response. Independent diagnostics also prioritize existing measurements for prospective verification, with model-derived trust reported alongside them. Across eight published materials datasets, SPARC achieved higher $R^2$ than the corresponding literature-reported values in six, with relative gains of up to 77% without the density-functional-theory- or experiment-derived descriptors used by several published pipelines. In an automated alkaline oxygen-evolution-reaction campaign, 8 of 11 SPARC-selected experiments reached overpotentials below 300 mV, with a best value of 242 mV, compared with 18 of 125 initial experiments. Measurements prioritized for verification before repetition subsequently deviated by 76 mV on average, compared with 27 mV for matched controls. SPARC therefore turns experimental evidence into a basis for revising model influence, directing exploration and identifying measurements that warrant verification.

papers.title: Machine-learned active spaces enable quantum calculations of spin-state energetics of transition-metal complexes on quantum hardware
papers.abstract: Multireference calculations on transition-metal complexes, on classical or quantum hardware, depend on the choice of active space. The orbitals that belong in it are those that are strongly entangled in the correlated wavefunction, but measuring this entanglement requires the very correlated calculation that the active space is meant to make affordable. Here we present SpinAware, a machine-learning model that predicts density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) single-orbital entropies and orbital-pair mutual information from the unrestricted Hartree-Fock (UHF) solution of each spin state, without any correlated calculation. Each of the 20 highest occupied and 20 lowest unoccupied orbitals is described by 60 descriptors computed from the UHF solution, among them the differences between its alpha and beta occupations and energies, its metal-d and ligand character, and its exchange coupling to the other orbitals, and a transformer predicts the entropy of each orbital in the context of all others. Trained on 3454 spin-pure DMRG calculations on mononuclear Cr-Ni complexes, the model transfers to experimentally characterized complexes with ligands, binding topologies, oxidation states and metals absent from training. Over 11 spin states it reproduces the DMRG entropy profiles with a mean absolute error of 0.027, and combining the predicted entropies with the predicted mutual information gives a candidate pool that contains 99% of the DMRG-active orbitals of the benchmark spin states while keeping, on average, only 15 of the 40 orbitals. Natural-orbital occupation scans then select compact active spaces from this pool for a nickel and a cobalt complex. Sample-based quantum diagonalization with samples from IBM quantum processors reproduces the exact CASCI energies of these spaces to within 0.3 kcal/mol and their spin-state gaps to within 0.10 kcal/mol for up to 32 qubits.

papers.title: Nearby M&M Binaries Uncovered with the Gaia Multipeak Fraction and Speckle Interferometry
papers.abstract: Multipeak fraction is a strong indicator of stellar multiplicity with subarcsecond angular separation in the Gaia DR3 catalog. We select 18 sources with multipeak fraction above 5% among stars possibly in the 20 pc solar neighborhood with as yet unconfirmed binarity. We successfully resolve eleven systems of M-type dwarf components in speckle interferometric observations with a 2.5 m telescope at the Caucasian Mountain Observatory of Sternberg Astronomical Institute, Moscow State University. The tentatively estimated companion masses lie in the 0.09 -- 0.23 $M_\odot$ range. All six sources with a multipeak fraction of 6--8% are unresolved, suggesting an observational bias that affects nearby stars.

papers.title: Certify, Then Select: Viability-Aware Runtime Steering of Frozen Diffusion Policies
Model-Free UPS Control Tuning for Improved Low-Voltage Ride-Through in AI Data Centers
Emergence of Anisotropic Defect Networks in Shocked Diamond
papers.abstract: Predicting failure after shock loading requires understanding how the structures created during compression evolve as the material unloads. In diamond, both crystal plasticity and localized amorphization have been reported to accommodate shock-induced shear. However, it remains unresolved how the resulting defect structures organize in three dimensions during compression and how this organization influences where tensile damage localizes during release. Here we couple phase-contrast-enhanced radiography at an X-ray free-electron laser with simulations to address this question in single-crystal diamond. By combining radiographs at multiple pump-probe delays with hydrodynamic calculations, we show that linear features first become visible behind the plastic wavefront while material near the front remains highly compressed. By rotating the viewing direction about the shock axis, we find that the projected feature angles favor finite $\{111\}$ sheets elongated along in-plane directions close to $\langle112\rangle$. Molecular dynamics simulations show that an interconnected network of amorphous bands and stacking faults forms during compression, preferentially on $\{111\}$ variants with larger in-plane shear traction. Projections of this network qualitatively reproduce the observed loss of feature visibility with rotation. During simulated release, tension opens local cracks within these pre-existing amorphous bands. These results support a pathway in which the crystallographically organized defect network formed during compression provides preferred sites for tensile damage during release. This pathway may also operate in other strongly covalent solids.

papers.title: Hard or Mislabeled? Failure Screens Enrich Vision Benchmarks for Label Errors
More Context, Mixed Results: Evaluating LLMs for Identifier Recovery and Code Deobfuscation
Understanding the Role of Reasoning Data in Pretraining
Learning-Enhanced Reduce-Repair-Refine-Optimize Framework for Real-Time Train Platforming
papers.abstract: Real-time train platforming under disruptions requires rapid revision of routing, platforming, and timing decisions. Dense traffic and shared infrastructure create tightly coupled conflicts, making real-time optimization computationally demanding. This paper proposes a learning-enhanced Reduce-Repair-Refine-Optimize framework that reduces and selectively relaxes the routing search space to balance computational efficiency, feasibility, and solution quality. The reduction stage constructs a restricted MILP by fixing selected routing decisions using route-specific predictive models and thresholds, thereby accounting for heterogeneity across routes. Two adaptive mechanisms subsequently modify the reduced search space: repair selectively releases route fixings to restore feasibility, while refinement releases additional fixings to recover routing alternatives and improve solution quality without reverting to the unrestricted problem. Computational experiments on real-life disrupted station-area instances show that the framework matches or improves upon a recent rTPP heuristic in more than 80% of instances within 60~s. Under the common 180~s budget, the framework obtains strictly better terminal incumbents than the unrestricted MILP in 56.7% of all instances and 77.4% of hard instances. Moreover, it obtains better terminal incumbents than an otherwise identical variant without refinement in 71.9% of hard instances. The results demonstrate that learning-based search-space reduction is most effective when the reduced search space remains adaptable during optimization, enabling high-quality feasible solutions within the real-time computation budget.

papers.title: Delay Closure of Observable Dynamics for the Heat Equation
Flat-band driven bipolar anomalous Nernst effect towards volt-scale transverse thermoelectric conversion
papers.abstract: Unipolar anomalous Nernst thermopiles are critically plagued by metallic interconnects, which induce heavy Joule dissipation and compromise the module's packing density, ultimately capping voltage generation. Here, we circumvent these limitations by establishing an intrinsic bipolar anomalous Nernst effect (BANE) paradigm, enabling seamless series integration analogous to Seebeck n-p pairs without passive metallic bridges. Focusing on flat-band topological systems, through machine learning assisted screening across multiple target properties, we identified 249 BANE materials, exhibiting near-room-temperature polarity switching. Guided by this predictive framework, we experimentally realized this phenomenon in single crystals of the Weyl ferromagnet, Co$_2$TiGe. Strikingly, while its intrinsic anomalous Hall conductivity (AHC) remains rigorously temperature-invariant up to the Curie temperature, the anomalous Nernst signal undergoes a sharp polarity inversion across $T \approx 225$ K. First-principles calculations attribute this behavior to the interplay between flat bands and Weyl nodes, where thermal depopulation shifts the chemical potential across the band edge, inverting the sign of $\partial \sigma_{xy} / \partial \epsilon$ via the Mott relation. This work opens an avenue toward compact, monolithic transverse thermopiles capable of volt-scale generation free from interfacial parasitic dissipation.

papers.title: Spacer-Engineered Spectral Selectivity in Metal-Carbon Solar-Thermal Absorbers
papers.abstract: Spectrally selective solar-thermal absorbers must capture sunlight while limiting emission at operating temperatures where the Planck spectrum overlaps the solar band. We connect this trade-off to a controlled optical mechanism in a metal-carbon metasurface. A radiative-limit calculation using AM1.5D illumination identifies how cutoff wavelength, infrared absorptivity and concentration together constrain equilibrium temperature, while the metasurface calculations reveal the additional role of a sharp spectral transition. We then separate the dielectric gap from the absorbing carbon layer in a gold--carbon architecture. Frequency-domain fields and material-resolved dissipation show that the spacer controls the overlap of a gap-localised mode with carbon, extending the high-absorptivity band and sharpening its infrared roll-off. A thickness sweep demonstrates that the spectrum with the strongest visible absorption need not give the highest radiative-limit equilibrium temperature. Polar-angle- and polarisation-resolved calculations demonstrate the angular robustness of the proposed plasmonic metasurface and assess the extent to which normal-incidence spectra approximate hemispherical emission. The calculated high-temperature values are benchmarks for the fixed-geometry, fixed-optical-constant model, not operating temperature predictions for the gold structure. The study establishes spacer-controlled loss partitioning as a route to shaping solar-thermal spectra and distinguishes optical selectivity from materials durability and useful heat output.

papers.title: The Critic Can Hurt: On the Safety of Critics in LLM-Guided AutoML Search
B2G-Agent: An LLM-Based Multi-Agent Tool for End-to-End Building-Grid Interactions
A Bound on Wormhole Probing Time from Holographic Multi-Entropy
papers.abstract: Bipartite entanglement entropy eventually saturates and therefore cannot track the continued growth of an eternal wormhole. Recently, it was shown that genuine tripartite multi-entropy can probe wormhole growth even after bipartite entanglement entropies have saturated. This naturally raises the question: can increasing the number of parties extend the probing time indefinitely? Adopting the multiway maximin prescription and assuming that its selected representatives are regular spacetime-stationary networks, we prove that the answer is no for nonrotating BTZ black holes. We establish a common finite upper bound on the probing time for every fixed finite boundary partition, independent of the number, sizes, and arrangement of its parties. For any network on any Cauchy slice, there exists a comparison network that assigns the entire central region containing the wormhole interior to a single party. A network longer than this comparison network cannot minimize length on that slice. The central length required by a stationary network connecting the two boundaries grows with time, whereas the central length of the comparison network remains uniformly bounded. At sufficiently late times, such a network therefore cannot minimize length on any Cauchy slice containing it and is excluded from the maximin prescription. Consequently, beyond this bound, no network selected by maximin enters the black-hole interior.

papers.title: Refinement vs. Replanning: Inference Compute Allocation in Robot Policies
Control of Non-Markovianity via Channel Exceptional Points in a Driven-Dissipative Kerr-Cat Qubit
papers.abstract: Exceptional points (EPs) in open quantum systems are conventionally defined at the Liouvillian level, making them representation-dependent and often requiring auxiliary degrees of freedom. We study EPs directly at the quantum-channel level in a driven-dissipative Kerr-cat qubit, in which dissipation drives bidirectional jumps between its two basis states. Interpolating two Markovian channels yields single EPs when the endpoints straddle a spectral-phase boundary and, remarkably, double EPs within the same phase. The interpolated EPs map out a Markovian--non-Markovian phase diagram: the parameter plane separates certified non-Markovian and Markovian domains, with domain boundaries switching the channel between the two characters. Three spectral criteria certify every domain. As the evolution time advances, the domains drift, split, and partially shrink, making the switching increasingly sensitive to parameters and time. This establishes a representation-independent paradigm for classifying and switching quantum memory effects, applicable to continuous-variable, discrete-variable, and hybrid systems.

papers.title: A Multigrid Finite State Projection Algorithm For The Solution Of The Reaction-Diffusion Master Equation
Early Spectroscopy of the Type II SN 2024phv Suggests Short-Lived Circumstellar Interaction
papers.abstract: We present the high-cadence light curve and rapid spectroscopy of the Type II SN 2024phv, discovered just 16.8 hours after the estimated explosion time. The early light curve exhibits a rapid 2 mag rise over the first day of observation, and spectra at 1.7 and 2.6 days reveal weak, narrow emission lines, suggesting moderate interaction with circumstellar material during the first few days after explosion. Models of shock-cooling emission provide a reasonable fit to the light curve after day 2, implying minimal interaction at later epochs, and yield a best-fit progenitor radius of $R=390\pm90\,R_{\odot}$. We also compare our earliest spectra with radiation hydrodynamical models of exploding red supergiants to measure circumstellar densities of ${\sim}10^{-12}$ g cm$^{-3}$ within a few stellar radii of the progenitor, followed by a sharp dropoff in the density profile. This rapidly decreasing profile leads us to conclude that the progenitor of SN 2024phv had an extended atmosphere and/or closely confined circumstellar material, likely from rapidly increasing or eruptive mass loss prior to explosion. In the context of other supernovae discovered at similarly early phases, SN 2024phv points to a diversity in the mass-loss rates of red supergiant stars in their final years.

papers.title: Beyond Controllability: Speaker Diversity in Instruction-Guided Text-to-Speech
SurveyWeave: An Agentic Framework for Automated Survey Generation
Optimal Capital Injections in a Microlending Group under External Shocks
papers.abstract: Motivated by static models of group default in microlending, we study a dynamic problem in which the members of a lending group are exposed to external shocks, such as droughts or floods, and the manager of a common emergency fund decides at each shock how much capital to inject into the members who were hit. Shocks arrive at random times, the set of members that a shock hits may depend on which members the previous shock hit, and the losses may spill over to members who were not hit directly. Between shocks, the members' wealth follows a linear stochastic differential equation in which members support each other, and the fund grows with interest and member contributions up to a cap. The cost balances the members' shortfall below a poverty line, a welfare measure that contains a standard poverty measure as a special case, against the administrative cost of the injections and the benefit of keeping money in the fund. We formulate the problem as a Markov decision process embedded at the shock times and prove that the embedded process is Markov with a weakly continuous transition kernel. When the discount rate exceeds a growth rate determined by the wealth dynamics, we show that the expected total cost is finite under every policy, that the finite-horizon optimal values converge to the infinite-horizon one at an explicit rate, and that there exists a stationary optimal injection policy, which can be chosen independent of calendar time.

papers.title: HeteroWear: Sensor-Aware Self-Supervised Learning for Heterogeneous Wearable Activity Recognition
The Stability Frontier of Interacting Binary Stars
papers.abstract: We derive a conservation based dynamical stability frontier for interacting binary stars that distinguishes stationary mass transfer from the restoration of a perturbed contact state. We apply the formalism to conservative white dwarf binaries with direct impact accretion, coupling Roche overflow, stream angular momentum, gravitational radiation, and both stellar spin reservoirs. From the contact equations, we obtain the required orbital return torque, and an exact Jacobian identity yields the restoring gradient and an oscillatory stability boundary in the computed white dwarf domain. A dimensionally normalized quadrupolar tide reveals separate equilibrium fold and oscillatory thresholds, including coexisting stable and unstable stationary branches. Finite donor synchronization introduces an additional oscillatory stability frontier. The model recovers the classical Roche and gravitational radiation limits, while the calculated orbital period derivatives are consistent with published binary timing measurements within their combined observational and model uncertainties. These results specify the torque amplitude, restoring stiffness, and synchronization rate needed for local stability, providing quantitative targets for stellar tidal calculations and the interpretation of interacting binaries in the millihertz gravitational wave band.

papers.title: Distance-Certified Safe Control in Unknown Environments via Spatio-Temporal Composition of Gaussian Processes
Spherical functions of the quantum symmetric pair of type FII
papers.abstract: We prove Schlösser's conjecture relating quantum FII spherical functions to Askey--Wilson polynomials for equal left and right coideal parameters and determine the corresponding radial operator. An explicit transport formula gives the shifted restrictions for arbitrary nonzero parameters.

papers.title: Adaptive nonorthogonal atomic orbitals refine charge transfer and bonding descriptors
papers.abstract: First-principles calculations implicitly encode bonding and charge transfer, but converting periodic electronic structure into interpretable and transferable descriptors remains challenging. Recently, we introduced Crystal Orbital Guided Iteration To atomic-Orbitals (COGITO), a tool for mapping plane-wave DFT back to an interpretable, minimal basis of adaptive atomic orbitals. Here, we show how the high-dimensional bonding information from COGITO can be reduced into chemically useful descriptors of covalent bonding, charge transfer, and crystal-dependent atomic chemistry without collapsing the real-space origin of the interactions. Compared to methods that use static or orthogonal orbital bases, COGITO descriptors of short- and long-range bonding show more stability and a better ability to distinguish between ionic, covalent, and metallic bonding regimes. Lastly, COGITO reliably decomposes band dispersion into range-resolved contributions, allowing us to verify and add to the orbital origins of silicon's low-symmetry conduction band minimum. Overall, the adaptive COGITO-based descriptors encode electronic structure, offering a well-structured route to expose the orbital interactions and charge transfer responsible for electronic properties.

papers.title: Finite-time quenches across first-, second-, and infinite-order transitions in XXZ spin chains
papers.abstract: We investigate how equilibrium quantum phase transitions manifest themselves in small systems driven out of equilibrium by quantum quenches. We consider linear ramps of the anisotropy in spin-1/2 and spin-1 XXZ chains, which host transitions of first, second, and infinite (Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless, BKT) order. We consider system sizes available in current quantum simulators and investigate how the order of the transition, the symmetries, and the ramp duration affect the decomposition of the time-evolved state into the instantaneous eigenbasis. The order of the transition determines the dynamics: across the BKT transition, moderately slow ramps already keep the system close to its ground state, corresponding to an adiabatic evolution, whereas for the second-order Haldane-Néel transition a ramp roughly three times slower is required to reach the same regime. Across the first-order transition, since the dynamics conserves the magnetization of the initial state, we observe the formation of ferromagnetic domains, separated by a single domain wall for slow ramps and by multiple walls for faster ones. Interestingly, shortly after the transition, the state evolves as a coherent beating between domain-wall states, a behavior captured by the recently proposed quantum-state texture.

papers.title: Aggregating Rankings of Coalitions to Rank Individuals
papers.abstract: We develop an ordinal framework for aggregating a profile of rankings of coalitional performances to determine the ranking of individuals. From university ratings to the assessment of team-sports players, we often evaluate individuals based on their coalitional performances. Although such evaluation has been addressed by cooperative game theory, it is only recently that its ordinal counterpart, social ranking theory (Moretti, 2015), has emerged. As most of the literature considers a single coalitional ranking (which corresponds to a real-valued characteristic function), we extend the model to allow a profile of coalitional rankings (which corresponds to a multidimensional characteristic function).
