papers.abstract: Threshold crossings in exponentially relaxing shot noise depend on the interplay between incoming impulses and the residual signal left by earlier arrivals. For renewal input, existing high-threshold product approximations of the mean first-passage time (MFPT) leave open when evaluation at a single index preserves the mean with vanishing relative error. Here we derive an exact finite-threshold MFPT series for exponentially marked renewal shot noise and recast it as an average over an auxiliary Poisson index. When the waiting-time density exhibits short-time power-law behavior, $w(t)\sim ct^{\kappa-1}$, the dominant series contributions shift from the Poisson center by an amount of order $x^{1-\kappa}$, whereas the averaging kernel has a fluctuation width of order $\sqrt{x}$, with $x=\lambda b$. The competition between these scales yields a crossover at $\kappa=1/2$, where the deterministic-index product is asymptotically exact in ratio above this boundary, requires a finite multiplicative correction at criticality, and exhibits a growing logarithmic discrepancy below it. A moving-saddle approximation also yields an asymptotically exact MFPT ratio under general strictly positive, finite-mean waiting times. Numerical comparisons across Gamma, Weibull, and generalized-Gamma renewal laws illustrate the approximation regimes and their finite-threshold accuracy. Together, these results provide an exact finite-threshold benchmark for the mean first-passage time and reveal how short-gap renewal statistics determine the asymptotic accuracy of high-threshold approximations.

From Twelve Leads to Single: Cross-Lead Knowledge Distillation for Domain-Generalized Atrial Fibrillation Detection
papers.abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) detection from long-term ambulatory electrocardiography (ECG) is critical because AF is a leading cause of stroke yet is frequently missed by conventional diagnostics, particularly in wearable settings that demand strong cross-domain generalization. Deep learning has improved AF identification by exploiting rhythm patterns, but methods such as BMIRC and SJTU-ECGNet still struggle to generalize across heterogeneous single-lead wearable datasets. To address this issue, we propose X-LeadGen, a two-stage cross-lead distillation framework for single-lead ECG AF detection that explicitly targets domain generalization. First, a 12-lead teacher network distills rich multi-lead information into a single-lead student through cross-lead knowledge transfer and a simulated self-distillation branch within the teacher, improving cross-lead representation alignment and AF discrimination. Second, we introduce a domain-generalization strategy that applies domain-adversarial training in both teacher and student stages, complemented by GANs-based augmentation in the student phase to learn domain-invariant features and enhance robustness to distribution shifts. Across seven public ECG datasets under real and simulated Lead-I settings, X-LeadGen consistently outperforms existing approaches in accuracy and F1-score, demonstrating strong generalization for real-world wearable AF monitoring. Our implementation is publicly available at this https URL , enabling further research and validation in the ECG community.

papers.title: Inside the Brain Tumor: What MRI-Defined Habitats Exist Within Glioblastoma, How Are They Spatially Organized, and What Molecular Processes Are Associated with Them?
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma exhibits substantial spatial heterogeneity, but MRI studies often emphasize tumor extent rather than the organization of imaging phenotypes. We investigated whether multiparametric MRI identifies reproducible habitats and whether habitat abundance and spatial architecture provide distinct information. Preoperative T1, contrast-enhanced T1, T2, and FLAIR scans with manual segmentations from 97 TCGA-GBM patients were analyzed. Unsupervised clustering of normalized voxel intensities identified two habitats. An Interface Ratio quantified the observed H1-H2 boundary relative to abundance-preserving spatial randomization. Molecular associations were assessed using matched Affymetrix U133A expression data and seven prespecified transcriptional programs. H2 showed higher T2 and FLAIR signal, while habitat distributions corresponded poorly to conventional segmentation compartments. Among 66 mixed-habitat tumors, Interface Ratio varied substantially and was independent of H2 abundance (rho = 0.074, p = 0.555). Molecular data were available for 89 patients, including 60 mixed-habitat tumors. Higher H2 abundance was nominally associated with hypoxia-program scores after adjustment for Interface Ratio (beta = 0.337, 95% CI 0.089-0.584; p = 0.0077), but not after multiple-testing correction (FDR = 0.108). No Interface Ratio association survived correction. Habitat composition and spatial organization represent two complementary dimensions of glioblastoma heterogeneity. The H2-hypoxia relationship remains exploratory and requires independent, spatially resolved validation.

The effect of policy cancellation on the risk of an insurance portfolio
papers.abstract: For an insurance portfolio modelled by a large number of i.i.d. losses, the average loss converges to its expected value by the law of large numbers, reflecting the diversification effect of pooling risks. Policy cancellations reduce the portfolio size and thereby weaken this effect. We quantify the resulting increase in risk by applying risk measures to the average loss before and after the cancellation of policies. For a portfolio of size $n$, we show that the impact of cancelling a single contract is of order $n^{-3/2}$, while the cancellation of a fixed proportion of contracts has an effect of order $n^{-1/2}$. We further extend the proportional cancellation regime to heterogeneous portfolios with different cancellation rates and risk characteristics across segments. These asymptotic results provide a quantitative basis for assessing surrender fees and cancellation costs from the insurer's perspective. We complement the theoretical analysis with numerical results for representative life insurance products, illustrating the magnitude of cancellation costs and the effect of portfolio aggregation. The two regimes require different techniques. For the cancellation of a fixed proportion of contracts, we employ central limit theorems in Wasserstein distance. For the cancellation of a single contract, we combine Kantorovich-Rubinstein duality with higher-order distributional approximations based on the Edgeworth and Cornish-Fisher expansions.

papers.title: Automated detection of wild and cultivated plants in citizen science records
papers.abstract: Citizen science plant occurrences may help the early detection of naturalisations of alien species, yet they are affected by misclassifications of cultivated plants as wild occurrences. To differentiate cultivated from wild observations, we proposed a decision framework for the manual annotation of records. We annotated this cultivation status for 1,491 iNaturalist records in Cape Town, comprising 12 invasive alien plant species. To automate the classification, we trained algorithms on annotated records based on 39 predictors from split into 4 sets: (i) basic record and observer features, (ii) visual features extracted from images, (iii) geographic features, and (iv) iNaturalist observer statistics. 11 Classification algorithms were trained on 8 combinations of predictor sets, to assess predictors importance, yielding 88 models evaluated with crossvalidation. 25.2% of all annotated records were cultivated, and 21.2% among Research Grade records, while 24.8% of annotated records were doubtful. Automated classification yielded an accuracy in distinguishing cultivated from wild records reaching 87%, improving over the iNaturalist cultivation tag (74%), and the accuracy was robust when predicting on new species (85%). Model performance was overall highest when combining iNaturalist-specific, geographic and visual predictors, but visual predictors alone performed better for certain species. Our results highlight the potential to automatically distinguish cultivated and wild-growing plant records to support invasion risk assessments and sanitise ecological analyses currently contaminated by cultivated records. Our framework is transferable to other crowdsourcing platforms, even though the manual annotation capacity can limit transferability.

Trusted financial data for agentic commerce: A multi-agent framework for credit risk, fraud detection, and secure payment decisions
papers.abstract: Financial institutions increasingly require intelligent risk-management systems that combine predictive performance with data reliability, interpretability, and adaptable decision policies for emerging agentic commerce environments. This study proposes a Trusted Financial Data (TFD) Multi-Agent Framework that integrates predictive risk modeling, behavioral intelligence, data-trust assessment, explainable artificial intelligence, and uncertainty-aware decision orchestration for credit-default and payment-fraud management. The framework translates heterogeneous risk and trust signals into interpretable Approve, Review, and Decline decisions using fixed and adaptive decision policies. Experimental evaluation was conducted on the Home Credit Default Risk and IEEE-CIS Fraud Detection datasets against five machine-learning baselines: Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, and Multi-Layer Perceptron. Adaptive TFD achieved recall values of 0.6234 and 0.9366, with ROC-AUC values of 0.7584 and 0.9474 on Home Credit and IEEE-CIS, respectively. Adaptive orchestration consistently improved minority-class risk detection relative to fixed TFD policies, although at the cost of increased false-positive interventions. SHAP-based global and local explanations further enhanced transparency into model predictions and decision behavior. Overall, the findings demonstrate the potential of TFD as a trust-aware multi-agent decision-orchestration layer that combines predictive, behavioral, uncertainty, and data-quality signals to support configurable, explainable, and adaptive financial risk management across heterogeneous operational environments.

papers.title: Random matrix discrepancy -- CLuP algorithm and parametric RDT approach
papers.abstract: We study information-theoretic and algorithmic aspects of random matrix discrepancy in proportional regime. The problem amounts to finding $\kappa=\min_{\x\in\mB^n}\|\sum_{i=1}^{n}\bar{A}_i\x_i\|_2$, where $\bar{A}_i\in\mR^{d\times d}$ is a collection of $n$ iid GOE matrices, $\mB^n$ are vertices of the unit cube in $\mR^n$, and $\alpha=\lim_{n\rightarrow \infty}\frac{n}{d^2}$ is a proportionality constant. Strong progress is made in several directions: (i) We develop a Random duality theory (RDT) framework and utilize its a lifted variant to establish lower bounds on $\kappa$, which precisely match the bounds obtained via the first moment in [81]. (ii) To address analytical challenges, we propose a negative Hopfield model as a proxy for implementation of a fully lifted RDT. On the 2nd lifting level, this model fits remarkably well between the information-theoretic lower bounds from [81] and the algorithmic upper bounds from [38]. (iii) On the 3rd and 4th lifting levels, parametric RDT concepts predict a sizeable computational gap for lower $\kappa$ values in the proxy model. Extending proxy information-theoretic fitting to algorithmic suggests a similar computational gap for matrix discrepancy in low $\kappa$ regime, aligning with [73]. (iv) We design a Controlled Loosening Up (CLuP) algorithm for matrix discrepancy. Its performance strongly matches our analytical results -- closely approaching information-theoretic predictions in lower $\alpha$ ranges (indicating a small or nonexistent computational gap) and following the proxy model's algorithmic predictions in higher $\alpha$ ranges (indicating a sizeable computational gap). Both the information-theoretic and algorithmic predictions match the corresponding phenomenologies of the symmetric binary perceptron (SBP) vector analogue in the entire $\alpha\in(0,\infty)$ range [1,2,14,31,51,92,111].

Automating literature screening and knowledge synthesis with large language models
papers.abstract: Scientific literature is expanding rapidly, yet much of its knowledge remains difficult to organize and reuse due to the substantial workload needed to navigate large, heterogeneous literature corpora. Here, we develop a generalizable large language model (LLM)-powered framework that automates literature screening, structured information extraction, and knowledge synthesis within a unified workflow. We benchmarked 11 state-of-the-art proprietary and open-weight LLMs across three materials science screening tasks differing in scope, corpus size, and class imbalance. Seven LLMs achieved balanced accuracies above 0.90 across all tasks, with the best-performing LLM reaching 0.96--0.98, demonstrating the potential of LLMs to accurately screen large, highly imbalanced scientific corpora. The framework also substantially reduces manual effort, screening 10,000 records within four minutes compared with approximately 83 person-hours for manual screening. Beyond literature screening, the framework extracts structured information from full-text articles, enabling content-level quantification of research landscapes that extends traditional bibliometric analysis based on publication metadata. This capability reveals methodological trends and underexplored directions, as shown for machine learning in concrete materials science. We further demonstrate its utility for information and data discovery by identifying publications containing silicate glass density data that are difficult to retrieve using conventional search strategies, which can support downstream hypothesis development, research design, and data-driven scientific discovery. Overall, these results demonstrate the broad applicability of LLM-powered literature analysis across scientific domains and its potential to transform large, unstructured literature corpora into structured, analyzable knowledge at scale.

Powering the Space Elevator
papers.abstract: Powering the Space Elevator is a report on the work of an International Space Elevator Consortium study group tasked with determining the technology options for delivering power to the climbers on the space elevator at any altitude above Earth. The book covers options such as laser power beaming, microwave beaming, a solar-powered climber, and delivering power through the electrical conductivity of the tether. This report starts with the reference conceptual design of a climber from the 2023 study report, "The Climber/Tether Interface of the Space Elevator," and adds features to the climber that allow it to ascend or descend the elevator tether. The strengths and limitations of current technologies are identified, along with areas for future research.

papers.title: DecompJSCC: Joint Source-Channel Coding With Decoupled SNR and Rate Adaptation
papers.abstract: Deep joint source-channel coding (DeepJSCC) for image transmission must adapt to changes in the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and available transmission resources. However, some existing joint-adaptive methods condition the encoder on the requested rate, while others apply static masks after encoding. The former couples latent formation to the rate request, whereas the latter cannot adapt channel selection to image content. To address these limitations, we propose DecompJSCC, which decomposes joint adaptation into SNR-conditioned latent formation and post-encoding rate control within a single model. The encoder applies SNR-conditioned block attention residuals across all stages, aggregating intra-stage and cross-stage semantic representations. At the receiver, an adapter performs SNR-conditioned affine correction. We introduce a post-encoding rate-adaptive channel semantic budgeting (RCSB) module whose shared gate selects channels of the formed latent by image content, adjusts their gains, and keeps exactly the requested count. This keeps the encoder output independent of the rate request for a fixed image and SNR. Experimental results show that DecompJSCC outperforms SwinJSCC and SA-RA-JSCC in peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) across a range of SNR and rate settings, by 0.64 dB and 1.00 dB over SwinJSCC and by 0.97 dB and 0.96 dB over SA-RA-JSCC on Kodak and CLIC2021, while using only 7.5% of SwinJSCC's Adaptive ModNet parameters.

papers.title: Bäcklund transformations of the fifth Painlevé equation
papers.abstract: In this paper Bäcklund transformations of the fifth Painlevé equation are discussed. The Bäcklund transformations are applied to rational solutions of the fifth Painlevé equation, which are expressed in terms of the generalised Laguerre polynomials and generalised Umemura polynomials. Using appropriate Bäcklund transformations, we derive non-unique solutions of the fifth Painlevé equation in terms of modified Bessel functions. Further it is shown that there are also rational solutions in terms of generalised Umemura polynomials for the same values of the parameters, which are not special cases of the modified Bessel function solutions. The relationship between solutions of the fifth Painlevé equation and solutions of the third Painlevé equation is also discussed.

papers.title: Zeeman-Doppler imaging of V889 Her: Surface spots and magnetic field topology 2017 - 2023
papers.abstract: The surface magnetic field of the young solar analogue V889 Her is studied using Zeeman-Doppler imaging (ZDI). This well-studied star has previously been reported to have an exceptionally high differential rotation and show abrupt changes in the surface magnetic field and spot configuration. Our aim is to study the evolution of the magnetic field topology in V889 Her. This will contribute to understanding dynamo action in young solar-type stars. We also want to constrain the surface differential rotation curve of the target star. We employ the ZDI method on observations collected with the SOFIN spectropolarimeter mounted at the Nordic Optical Telescope. We test differential rotation parameters previously reported in studies of the star. We observe significant changes in the radial field near the rotational pole throughout the whole span of the observations. Specifically, the polarity of the radial field is reversed around 2021. The large-scale magnetic field also contains a persistent strong azimuthal component at high latitudes. We detect abrupt changes in the spot configuration in June 2018 on the time scale of a week. The observations favour a solar type differential rotation. The different rotation parameters influence the brightness map more than the magnetic field topology. We cannot link the observed changes in the magnetic field topology with the evolution of the long-term spot activity. The abrupt changes observed in 2018 confirm previous reports that the surface magnetic field and spot configuration may undergo rapid evolution on short time scales. This complicates the estimation of the surface differential rotation.

papers.title: Syzygy matrices and higher extensions over string algebras
papers.abstract: Over a finite-dimensional string algebra, higher extension dimensions may eventually vanish, become periodic, or grow without bound. We show how their behaviour can be read from a finite directed graph. Second syzygies split into uniserial modules from a finite family; their syzygies define a nonnegative integer matrix, so higher extension dimensions become weighted counts of walks. Only the part of the graph relevant to the chosen pair of modules contributes. This gives four growth regimes: eventual vanishing, periodicity, quasi-polynomial growth, and exponential growth. We derive the construction from projective covers, give explicit extension formulas over truncated cycles, and illustrate the growth regimes with examples.

papers.title: The Capillary Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski Problem
papers.abstract: We study the Capillary Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski Problem on an acute spherical cap. For $1\le k\le n-1$, the equation is \[ h\,\varphi(\ell/h)\,\bar\sigma_k(\nabla^2h+h\sigma)=f, \qquad \nabla_\mu h=\cot\theta\,h, \] where $\ell$ is the support function of the unit capillary spherical cap. For $1\le k\le n-1$, this includes the capillary Christoffel--Minkowski and capillary $L_p$ Christoffel--Minkowski problems; the same density formally recovers the capillary Orlicz--Minkowski endpoint when $k=n$. We organize the theory in five parts. After recalling the elementary symmetric functions and the capillary support-function formalism, we review the capillary Orlicz--Brunn--Minkowski framework and introduce the intermediate-order Orlicz $k$-mixed functional and its Euler--Lagrange equation. In the supercritical regime \[ a_\varphi(t):=\frac{t\varphi'(t)}{\varphi(t)}\ge k+1+\delta, \] we derive uniform $C^0$, $C^1$ and $C^2$ estimates for positive $k$-admissible solutions. The same supercritical index produces a strictly coercive second variation and a spectral gap for the linearized Neumann operator. These facts lead to existence and uniqueness by a continuity method, quantitative stability of the solution map in both the datum and the Orlicz weight, and an open perturbative class of strictly convex non-power solutions. Under an additional capillary Orlicz-convexity condition on the datum, a full-rank argument upgrades the global admissible solution to a strictly convex capillary support function.

papers.title: The Capillary Dual Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski Problem
papers.abstract:
We study a capillary dual Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski problem on a spherical cap. For $2\le k\le n$, $1<p<k+1$, and $0<	heta<\pi/2$, we consider \[ \sigma_k(
abla^2h+h\sigma) = f(\xi)h^{p-1} rac{ho^{k+1}}{\varphi(ho)}, \qquad ho=(h^2+|
abla h|^2)^{1/2}, \] with the capillary Robin condition $
abla_\mu h=\cot	heta\,h$. Assuming that $f$ is positive, smooth and horizontally even, $g=f^{-1/(p+k-1)}$ satisfies the capillary spherical-convexity and boundary compatibility conditions, and $H(r)=\varphi(r)/r^p$ is strictly increasing and proper with $Q_\varphi(r)\le k+1$, we prove the existence of a smooth, positive, horizontally even solution that is strictly capillary convex. The proof uses an Orlicz homotopy, uniform a priori estimates, a viscosity constant-rank argument when $k<n$, global oblique regularity, and degree theory.

papers.title: The Capillary Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski Flows
papers.abstract: We study a capillary Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski flow on a non-obtuse spherical cap for $1\le k\le n-1$: \[ \partial_t h= \frac{h^2\varphi(\ell/h)}{f}\, \bar{\sigma}_k(\nabla^2h+h\sigma)-h, \qquad \nabla_\mu h=\cot\theta\,h. \] In the supercritical regime \[ a_\varphi(s)=\frac{s\varphi'(s)}{\varphi(s)} \ge k+1+\delta, \qquad s a_\varphi'(s)\ge0, \] we obtain time-uniform $C^0$ and $C^1$ estimates and a closed scalar equation for the speed ratio. A dynamic Orlicz square-completion identity, combined with inverse-concavity, yields a viscosity estimate for the minimum principal radius. Under a strict dynamic Orlicz-convexity condition and \[ \frac{f_\mu}{f}\ge\frac{n-k}{n}\cot\theta, \] we prove time-uniform two-sided principal-radius bounds on every smooth existence interval for $0<\theta\le\pi/2$ and deduce long-time existence and smooth convergence to a stationary solution. The boundary regularity step uses a quantitative interior concave estimate through Neumann reflection and a concave uniformly elliptic extension. Under the weaker condition $(f\ell^{k-1})_\mu\ge0$, strict convexity is preserved on every smooth existence interval. For $k=1$, the transformed scalar equation is uniformly parabolic for every $0<\theta<\pi$. Classical parabolic estimates then give an all-angle scalar flow theorem, without asserting geometric convexity preservation in the obtuse range.

papers.title: An Incomplete-Preference Quantum Anscombe--Aumann Representation
papers.abstract: By dropping the idea that completeness is a mandatory prerequisite for agents' rationality, this work shows how classical and quantum subjective probability attributions represent suitable preference orderings. To do so, we develop an extension of the Anscombe--Aumann framework in which acts map a finite set of states of the world into the effect interval of a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, while preferences need not be complete. The construction keeps three logically distinct questions separate. First, an incomplete-preference multi-utility theorem supplies affine utility functionals. Second, finite-dimensional operator geometry determines the form of each affine functional. Third, admissibility identifies which normalised probability--state pairs are compatible with the full preference. We introduce behavioural state-independence as the natural Anscombe--Aumann interpretation of the idea that the identity of the states of the world should not affect how quantum consequences are compared. Because an incomplete preference makes this aggregate behavioural condition weaker than a utility-by-utility condition, the factorisation theorem requires a stronger, explicitly operational representation-level condition. Under that condition and Loewner monotonicity, every affine utility functional is positively affinely equivalent to a normalised utility of the form $ U_{p,\rho} (f)= \sum_{s} p(s) Tr( \rho f(s) )$. Consequently, a suitable incomplete preference relation is represented by a family of admissible pairs in $\Delta(S)\times D(H)$. We then identify a canonical maximal compatible family and show that the scalar-effect subspace carries an ordinary classical multi-utility representation, with scalar events appearing as the vertices of the scalar-act cube.

papers.title: Exponential Lower Bounds for the Spherically Averaged Density of Atoms
papers.abstract: We study the asymptotic behavior of the spherically averaged density $\widetilde \rho$ for fermionic bound states of the $N$-electron atomic Hamiltonian $H_{N,Z}$ with nuclear charge $Z$. For the density associated with an eigenfunction satisfying $H_{N,Z}\psi=E\psi$, we show that if the energy $E$ is below the bottom of the essential spectrum $\Sigma:=\inf\mathop{\rm ess. spec} (H_{N,Z})$, then $\lim_{r\to\infty}\frac{\ln \widetilde \rho(r)}{r} =\lim_{r\to\infty}\frac{d}{dr}{\ln \widetilde\rho(r)} =-2\alpha_0$, with $\alpha_0=\sup\{\alpha \ge 0\colon e^{2\alpha r}\widetilde \rho \in L^1(\mathbb{R}_+,r^2dr)\}$. The same is true at threshold in certain cases. Moreover, we prove $\alpha_0^2=\Sigma-E$ for the ground states of $H_{3,Z}$ with sufficiently large $Z$.

papers.title: Hybrid Uncertainty in the Real Forms of $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb C)$
papers.abstract: An optimized commutator bound can lie strictly below the quantum infimum even when its minimizing mean is realized by a quantum state. We study hybrid uncertainty, defined as the sum of pairwise products of standard deviations. For any spanning list of nonzero real linear combinations of the generators in a positive discrete series representation of $\mathfrak{su}(1,1)$, the commutator bound has a unique minimizing mean, realized by a Perelomov coherent state. We prove that the optimized bound equals the infimum over states with finite second moments if and only if the symmetrized covariance matrix of the prescribed observables is diagonal in this state. When this condition fails, the quantum infimum is strictly greater than the bound; for a nonorthogonal list, we obtain an explicit positive lower bound on this gap. For irreducible spin-$j$ representations of $\mathfrak{su}(2)$, we derive the exact minimum of the spectral hybrid uncertainty over states for any spanning list of spin observables. For a fixed state, we compare separate measurements made before a random target is disclosed with direct measurement of the target known in advance. For these protocols, the excess mean squared error coefficient equals twice the listed hybrid uncertainty, and its minimum over orthogonal combinations of the observables equals twice the spectral hybrid uncertainty.

papers.title: An accelerated multiobjective gradient flow with implicit Hessian-driven damping
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose an accelerated multiobjective gradient flow with implicit Hessian-driven damping for unconstrained convex multiobjective optimization problems in a real Hilbert space. The continuous flow is formulated as a system of two first-order equations involving only a single multiobjective projection operator and suitable time-scaling factors. Formally, it can also be expressed as a second-order system with explicit multiobjective Hessian-driven damping, which corresponds to the usual Hessian-driven damping introduced by Alvarez et al. [J. Math. Pures Appl., 81(8):747--779, 2002]. The first-order formulation, however, involves no Hessian term and can be regarded as an extension of the Hessian-driven Nesterov accelerated gradient flow by Chen and Luo [ arXiv:1912.09276 , 2019]. Assuming that the objective gradients are Lipschitz continuous on bounded sets and that the common lower level sets are bounded, we establish global existence in finite dimensions under suitable time-scaling conditions. An a priori energy estimate confines the solutions to a fixed bounded set, and a Lyapunov argument yields fast decay of a merit function and the KKT residual. Under an additional bound on the time-scaling factors, the trajectory of every global solution converges weakly to a weak Pareto point. Numerical tests illustrate the rapid residual decay and reduced oscillations.

papers.title: An AI-enabled high-resolution chlorophyll-a forecasting model that outperforms the operational global biogeochemical system
papers.abstract: Surface chlorophyll-a concentration is a key indicator of marine phytoplankton variability, and short-term forecasts of its distribution provide advance information for marine ecosystem monitoring and management. However, interactions between physical transport and biological processes complicate chlorophyll-a forecasting, and simulating these coupled processes with conventional numerical models imposes substantial computational demands. Here we introduce ChlCast, an AI model that generates daily forecasts of surface chlorophyll-a concentration over a 10-day horizon at approximately 4-km resolution between 60$^\circ$S and 60$^\circ$N. ChlCast combines factorized spatiotemporal convolutions with a multiscale architecture to learn from historical chlorophyll-a fields and climatological information. Compared with the operational 0.25$^\circ$ Copernicus global ocean biogeochemical forecasting system, ChlCast reduces mean absolute error and root mean square error by 70.74% and 47.63%, respectively, against satellite-derived Level-4 chlorophyll-a fields, and by 35.03% and 13.07% against independent BGC-Argo in situ observations. Coastal case studies further show that the 4-km forecasts retain coastal gradients and localized concentration maxima that are weakened by coarse-grid averaging. These results demonstrate the potential of observation-driven deep learning for high-resolution forecasting of surface chlorophyll-a variability at the near-global scale.

papers.title: Foundation Tensor Networks Generalize Across Lattice Hamiltonians
papers.abstract: Neural quantum states and tensor networks have emerged as leading techniques for simulating quantum many-body systems. However, disordered systems remain extremely challenging in both frameworks as they require computation of the ground state for every realization of the disorder. Recently, neural quantum states have been used to construct foundation models that generate the ground state directly from the Hamiltonian. Still, they are hindered by the need to perform extensive sampling to estimate observables. To address these difficulties, we introduce the foundation tensor network (FTN), which uses a neural network to generate the tensor network representation of the ground-state wavefunction from the Hamiltonian. To accelerate training, we develop a technique, called \texttt{GridBP}, based on iterated one-dimensional belief propagation that reduces the cost of computing the energy expectation value to just two tensor contractions. We use FTNs to calculate the critical parameters of the glass transition in the quantum Edwards-Anderson model via finite-size scaling analysis. To facilitate rapid averaging, we use a moment-generating function to evaluate the order parameter, lowering the cost to a single tensor contraction. We obtain high-fidelity estimates for the critical parameters by averaging over 500,000 disorder realizations.

papers.title: DART ejecta reveal the recoil momentum budget of a kinetic impact
papers.abstract: Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) demonstrated that ejecta recoil enhances asteroid deflection, but the ejecta processes generating and distributing this recoil remained unclear. We reconstruct three-dimensional ejecta evolution from time-resolved morphology and brightness observations, recovering previously missing constraints on momentum transfer and material transport. Integrating reconstructed momentum yields momentum enhancement factors $\beta_\mathrm{D}=2.13 \pm 0.19 (1{\sigma})$ for Dimorphos and $\beta_\mathrm{sys}=2.04 \pm 0.19 (1{\sigma})$ for the Didymos system. Combined with the measured deflection, the reconstructed recoil constrains Dimorphos's bulk density to $1435.18_{-153.71}^{+112.59} \mathrm{kg m^{-3}}$ without assuming its mass. By linking observed orbital deflection to the released material, this reconstruction provides ejecta-based constraints for assessing kinetic-impact effectiveness and investigating how natural collisions drive mass loss and debris transport among small Solar System bodies.

papers.title: The retarded interaction and non-scattering for 3D Maxwell--Dirac system
papers.abstract: We prove an a priori obstruction to linear scattering for the massive Maxwell--Dirac system in three space dimensions. A global solution with nonzero charge cannot scatter linearly in $L^2$ if its full and homogeneous potentials are $O(t^{-1})$, and the homogeneous potential is $o(t^{-1})$ in compact timelike cones. No nonlinear asymptotic expansion is assumed in this non-scattering theorem. We also identify the exact leading interaction when the nonlinear current approaches a free Dirac current in $L^1$. Its coefficient is a positive quadratic form in the velocity density and is bounded below by the square of the charge divided by $4\pi$. The proof uses free Dirac asymptotics and an estimate for retarded source errors after pairing with a smooth free current.

papers.title: Weak Generators in Stable Module Categories
papers.abstract: The aim of this note is to show that the existence of weak generators in the stable module category of a ring, or equivalently, of $p$-indigent modules in the terminology of Holston et al., depends on the underlying model of set theory.

papers.title: QuantumInputOutput.jl: A Julia framework for input-output theory with quantum pulses and the SLH formalism
papers.abstract: The interaction of traveling photonic pulses with quantum systems is a fundamental process for many quantum technologies such as quantum communication, control, and measurement protocols. The so-called SLH formalism, named for the triple of operators that parametrize the dynamics, in combination with virtual emission and absorption cavities provides a general toolbox to describe such processes. However, modeling open quantum systems driven by propagating quantum pulses becomes cumbersome once several components, channels, and temporal modes are involved. Here we present QuantumInputOutput, an open-source framework that automates this derivation process: first, symbolic expressions for the Hamiltonian and Lindblad operators are derived using predefined SLH rules and symbolic quantum algebra. Next, the obtained operators are converted to (time-dependent) numerical matrices or are used to obtain higher-order mean-field equations. The numerical expressions are presented in a form immediately suitable for solving the time evolution of the master equation and analyzing the output modes via correlation functions. Besides its usefulness for numerical simulations, the framework also provides a convenient tool to derive symbolic expressions for one-dimensional quantum systems such as multilevel emitters in cavities or waveguides.

papers.title: Fast mixing and thermal phases from strong decay of correlations
papers.abstract: We show that a strong form of correlation decay in quantum Gibbs states has far-reaching dynamical consequences. For a smooth path of geometrically local commuting Hamiltonians whose Gibbs states satisfy strong decay of correlations, we construct $\mathrm{O}(1)$-time quasi-local Lindbladian evolutions exactly connecting these states in both directions, together with $\mathrm{O}(1)$-time quasi-local Hamiltonian evolutions exactly connecting their canonical purifications. These quasi-local connections strengthen previously known quantum-channel circuit constructions based on the decay of connected correlation functions [R. Ma, V. Khemani, and S. Sang, PRX Quantum 7, 033052 (2026)], which approximately connect states within the same phase but have depths that grow logarithmically with system size. Furthermore, if the Gibbs-state path contains a product state, we prove that the single-site Glauber dynamics has a $\Omega(1)$ spectral gap independent of the system size throughout the path. This establishes Glauber-dynamics fast mixing for models that may violate the strong spatial mixing condition used in prior proofs, including (1) the $q$-state Potts model throughout the high-temperature phase for any $q$ and any finite dimension; (2) the Ising model with a longitudinal field at low temperature, with frustrating perturbations that destroy monotonicity of the dynamics; and (3) the three-dimensional $\mathbb{Z}_2$ lattice gauge theory at low temperatures comparing to a field perturbation, even though the model supports classical memories at intermediate temperatures. Intriguingly, we establish fast mixing of these classical Markov chains using tools from quantum physics like Lieb-Robinson bounds.

papers.title: Microcausality Bounds on Dispersion Laws
papers.abstract: Microcausality holds in any state, including those that spontaneously break Lorentz invariance, and requires the poles (and other singularities) of the retarded Green's function to satisfy $\mathrm{Im}\,\omega \le |\mathrm{Im}\,k|$ throughout the complex plane. Building on the work of Heller, Serantes, Spaliński and Withers, we study its consequences for dispersion relations that are linear at small $k$, like Goldstone bosons, assuming tree-level, non-dissipative dynamics. We show that microcausality is equivalent to requiring that $k \pm \omega(k)$ be typically real functions. This yields two-sided bounds on all higher-order coefficients of $\omega(k)$ in units of its radius of convergence $R$, the scale at which the linear Goldstone description breaks down. The optimal constraints are characterised by an infinite hierarchy of Toeplitz determinants. We derive analogous bounds on $\omega^2(k)$, whose radius of convergence $\tilde R$ marks the scale at which new states must appear. The bounds shrink to zero as the sound speed $c_s$ approaches 1: for a fixed higher-derivative correction, both $R$ and $\tilde R$ become parametrically smaller than naive dimensional analysis suggests. In particular, in the EFT of Inflation all higher-derivative quadratic operators must vanish as $c_s \to 1$. We test the bounds in several models: a $U(1)$ superfluid, light in a dielectric medium, photon propagation in a strong magnetic field, colour-flavour-locked quark matter, and a homogeneous solid. Finally, we extend the bounds to gapped modes.

papers.title: Counting Second-Order Schreier Sets with Minimum 2
papers.abstract: A finite nonempty subset of the positive integers is first-order Schreier if the minimum element of that set is greater than or equal to the size of the set. We can generalize the first-order Schreier sets recursively to higher orders, and we specifically investigate the second-order Schreier sets. We show a combinatorial relationship between the count of second-order Schreier sets with minimum element $2$ and the index shift of a convolution of the Fibonacci numbers (given by Sequence A023610 in the OEIS).

papers.title: Composition-dependent ultralight dark matter detection with a tetrahedral superconducting gravity gradiometer
papers.abstract: Tetrahedral superconducting gravity gradiometers designed as full-tensor gravitational-wave detectors, such as the ground-based mSOGRO design and the proposed lunar LANGO observatory, reconstruct the acceleration-gradient tensor from four test masses. We show that giving the four test masses two compositions in a $2+2$ arrangement adds a composition-dependent ultralight dark matter (ULDM) channel to that same tensor readout, with no separate dark-matter sensor and no dark-matter-specific readout. A coherently oscillating scalar accelerates each mass in proportion to its dilaton charge, and the tensor reconstruction leaves the charges only in a mean, rejected with the common mode, and a single vector $\qv$ proportional to the charge contrast $\Delta\abaralpha_{AB}$ between the two materials. The response is the rank-one tensor $\K_{\ULDM}(t)=\gv_\phi(t)\otimes\qv$, whose amplitude is set by the halo, independent of $m_\phi$. The axis of $\qv$ is fixed in advance by the material assignment, so the response obeys the null condition $\K_{\ULDM}(\mathbf{I}-\Pq)=0$ at every instant, for any $\gv_\phi$ including a virialized field with a stochastic gradient---an exact tensor discriminator against gravitational-wave signals; for a single composition $\qv=0$. With the gravitational-wave noise model, the coupling sensitivity for copper and lead test masses reaches $d_{\hat m}-d_g\simeq3.4\times10^{-8}$ for the baseline instrument and $4.9\times10^{-10}$ with upgraded accelerometers. The rank-one factorization and the null condition are summarized in a companion Letter; the present paper gives the derivations and the detector-level analysis.

papers.title: Bound States of Two D0-Branes and the Three-Graviton Coupling
papers.abstract: We numerically solve for the ground state of the $SU(2)$ BFSS matrix model for M-theory. This state corresponds to the zero-energy bound state of two D0-branes or, by the BFSS conjecture, to the eleven-dimensional graviton with two units of momentum along the M-theory circle. The wavefunction exhibits a strongly coupled core, as well as an asymptotic power-law tail where the D0-branes are well separated. The coefficient of this power-law decay is the three-graviton coupling, previously computed by Herderschee and Maldacena, which our numerical solution reproduces with high accuracy. We also show that this coupling is protected by supersymmetry in the matrix model, and derive its value from the non-renormalized one-loop interaction of the two D0-branes. Lastly, we provide a simple representation-theoretic argument regarding the recently proposed excited bound states of the model.

papers.title: Simulation-Based Priors and BAO Shifts from the Lyman-$α$ Forest at the Field Level
papers.abstract: We present an analytic forward model for the Lyman-$\alpha$ (Ly-$\alpha$) forest flux field based on cubic-order large-scale structure perturbation theory (effective field theory) calculations. We validate our cubic model on two sets of hydrodynamic simulations spanning $2 \leq z \leq 4$: the small-volume CAMELS suite, which spans a wide range of cosmological and astrophysical parameters, and the large-volume, high-resolution Sherwood simulations. We find qualitatively similar results for both at the power-spectrum level. The perturbative model reproduces the three-dimensional flux power spectrum of the simulations to $\sim 5\%$ down to $k \simeq 1$-$1.5\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$, depending on the redshift. This improves compared to previous quadratic perturbative forward models by up to 40%. Exploiting cosmic-variance cancellation in the field-level approach, we carry out precision measurements of the Lyman-alpha forest bias parameters from the CAMELS simulation suite. We use these measurements to analytically predict the shifts in the Baryon Acoustic Oscillations (BAO) scaling parameters induced by nonlinearities in the three-dimensional Lyman-alpha forest clustering as a function of cosmological parameters. We find sub-percent shifts in both the radial and transverse directions with a noticeable dependence on cosmology and redshift. Finally, from the field-level fits we construct simulation-based priors that can be used for cosmological analyses of the Lyman-alpha forest with the currently observing Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI). In addition, our cubic model captures the connected four-point function (trispectrum) of the forest, which opens up novel opportunities for accurate covariance matrix estimation for DESI and its successor, DESI-II.

papers.title: Sharp Uniform Fisher Information Bounds from Projective Designs
papers.abstract: Fixed measurements for multiparameter pure-state metrology must remain informative without knowing the input state. We quantify this requirement by the Fisher floor, the smallest fraction of the quantum Fisher information that a measurement retains over all pure states and tangent directions. We determine the Fisher guarantees, namely lower bounds on Fisher floors, implied by projective design order alone in every dimension $d\ge 2$. These guarantees are sharp at order $t=2$ and every odd order $t\ge 3$, and finite weighted designs attain them; at even orders, our bounds are nearly tight. As the order increases, the guarantees approach one half, the single-copy quantum limit. Sampling and spectral completion of any 3-design yield, with probability $1-O(1/d)$, a measurement with linearly many outcomes and a dimension-independent Fisher floor. Such a measurement separates all pure states in Hellinger distance, so pure-state maximum-likelihood estimation from $N$ copies attains mean infidelity $O(d/N)$ uniformly over pure states, optimal up to a universal constant factor.

papers.title: Global Fit Inference for LISA with samsara++
papers.abstract: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) will observe a superposition of gravitational-wave signals, requiring joint inference of an unknown number of sources, parameters, and instrumental noise. To disentangle these contributions, that overlap in both time and frequency, a Global Fit (GF) analysis is needed. We present samsara++, a C++/CUDA sampler designed to address this trans-dimensional GF problem. Building on the continuous-time MCMC framework of samsara, the algorithm combines birth-death processes for adding and removing sources, with mutation moves for parameter estimation. Birth and death are selected through posterior-dependent rates. Shared-memory parallelism, incremental likelihood updates, and indexed storage reduce the computational and memory costs, while parallel tempering improves the exploration of multimodal posteriors. We assess the performance using simulated one-year LISA datasets containing Galactic double white dwarf binaries and stationary Gaussian instrumental noise. Analyses of populations containing 143 and 866 binaries start from empty source models, without preliminary searches or proposals tailored to the injected population. These tests demonstrate source reconstruction and catalog generation, highlighting, at the same time, the importance of source-count, overlapping signals, and incomplete mixing on joint source and noise inference. Then we perform a separate stress test, initialized at the injected parameters, exploring a population of 16,435 binaries, corresponding to 131,480 source parameters. This run completes 15 million iterations in approximately 16 hours using about 3 GB of RAM. All together, these benchmarks show the computational feasibility of birth-death sampling for large Galactic-binary populations, and provide a foundation for extending samsara++ toward a comprehensive LISA global fit.

papers.title: Gauge aspects of teleparallel gravity and Noether's second theorem
papers.abstract: We examine the gauge structure of the Teleparallel Equivalent of General Relativity (TEGR) from the perspective of Noether's second theorem. We show that diffeomorphisms and local Lorentz transformations are the gauge symmetries of TEGR, as these are the only variational symmetries that give rise to Noether identities. We then discuss the distinct roles of these two symmetries and their implications for the gauge-theoretic interpretation of gravity. Finally, we discuss consequences of these observations for the role of translations in gauge theories of gravity and the coupling of matter in TEGR. In particular, we demonstrate that the matter coupling prescription is uniquely determined and coincides with that of general relativity, including in the case of spinor fields.

papers.title: ISLA: A Coordinate-Free, Measure-Weighted Transformer for Boundary-Driven PDEs
papers.abstract: Symmetry is a foundational principle of physics: the behavior of a PDE-governed system does not depend on the coordinate frame, unit system, or mesh used to write it down, and neither should a surrogate model. Yet today's leading neural surrogates lack these invariances and fail under simple transformations of the same problem: for models trained on PDEs of cars in one pose (i.e., translation and rotation), rotating the full PDE raises the surface-pressure error from 4% to more than 100%, and re-sampling its boundary raises it to about 30%. We introduce ISLA (Invariant Slice Attention), a slice-attention transformer for steady, boundary-driven PDEs. Because the boundary determines the interior solution, ISLA encodes the posed boundary once into learned slices and evaluates arbitrary interior points independently through a tree-accelerated learned boundary kernel. Inputs are nondimensionalized in scales computed from the boundary, sums over boundary cells are area-weighted quadratures that converge under mesh refinement, and geometry enters only as distances and relative angles to equivariant slice anchors, making the model equivariant to rigid motions and reflections up to optional token subsampling and tree clustering. On AeroZoo, 2,816 3D flows spanning diverse geometries, poses, physical scales, and boundary conditions, ISLA's mean reference-scaled velocity and pressure errors are at least 1.9 and 2.2 times lower than any baseline's. On full AirfRANS, ISLA is second only to an explicit boundary-integral network (GLOBE), with errors at least 1.6 times lower than Transolver's and GeoTransolver's in every field.

papers.title: UV and deep-UV ultrafast harmonic generation enhanced by resonant gold nano-pillar metasurface
papers.abstract: We report experimental observations and full-vector numerical simulations of second and third-harmonic generation from a two-dimensional periodic gold nano-pillar metasurface, for efficient ultrafast light conversion from near-infrared to the UV and deep-UV spectral ranges. The metasurface is designed to support an angle-tunable plasmonic resonance in the near-infrared spectral range, with its resonance wavelength shifting as a function of the pump angle of incidence. Under resonant conditions, strong electromagnetic-field confinement near the nano-pillar corners enhances the nonlinear light-matter interactions. Compared with a flat gold mirror, the nanostructured metal exhibits enhanced nonlinear frequency conversion, with conversion efficiencies of second and third-harmonic generation increased by two and three orders of magnitude, respectively. Full-wave theoretical modeling of linear and nonlinear light-matter interaction in nanoscale structures validates the experimental results. We demonstrate that periodically arranged square gold pillars can be engineered to achieve enhanced second and third-harmonic generation at wavelengths that can be tailored through the structural design, without requiring complex geometries or hybrid structures that pose fabrication challenges. The close agreement between theoretical predictions and experimental measurements further advances our understanding of surface-mediated nonlinear optical processes in metals and highlights the potential of metallic nanostructures as ultrafast light sources in the UV and deep-UV.

papers.title: Temporal Regularized Learning: Self-Supervised Learning Local in Space and Time
papers.abstract: Self-supervised objectives such as VICReg learn representations by making related inputs similar, while variance and covariance penalties prevent collapse. These penalties are statistics over a batch of samples, so layer-local variants, too, are typically local in space but not in time. We introduce Temporal Regularized Learning (TeReL), which optimizes a VICReg-style objective one sample at a time with purely local updates: each update uses only the current activity of its own and the preceding layer and a fixed-size running state. Temporally adjacent inputs serve as positive pairs, which makes the objective a soft form of Slow Feature Analysis (SFA). Running estimates of each neuron's mean and variance, together with one lateral matrix per layer, replace the batch statistics; held fixed during differentiation, they turn the gradient into a Hebbian feedforward update and an anti-Hebbian lateral update. We show that a two-layer network trained with batch size one on an MNIST stream of class-homogeneous chunks reaches 96.48% linear-probe accuracy, above random features (95.09%) and classical SFA, and that the temporal order and each loss term contribute to this result. With both locality constraints relaxed, the same objective matches supervised backpropagation. TeReL thus shows that the collapse-preventing statistics of modern self-supervised learning can be held as running state at each neuron, which brings these objectives closer to what brains and neuromorphic hardware can implement.

papers.title: Real log canonical thresholds and real log canonical thresholds with signs
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the properties of the real log canonical threshold $\text{rlct}(X,Y)$ associated with a pair $(X,Y)$ and the real log canonical thresholds with signs $\text{rlct}^{\pm}(f)$ associated with a polynomial function $f: \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$. In particular, we relate these invariants to other invariants arising from the theory of motivic integration. We also show how to compute these invariants in several particular cases, including the Newton non-degenerate case and the case of analytically irreducible plane curve germs.

papers.title: Margin-Inducing Optimal Guidance and Control for Atmospheric Entry
papers.abstract: A method is presented for margin-inducing optimal guidance and control with application to atmospheric entry. The method induces margin in state inequality path constraints during entry while simultaneously retaining a large portion of the non-margin-inducing performance. The margin in the guidance trajectory is based on a differentiable approximation of the maximum of a continuous function. This differentiable approximation is derived from the Kreisselmeier-Steinhauser (KS) function, where the KS function is defined for a function over sampled data. The KS function is first modified into a weighted form where the data points and weights are associated with a multiple-interval Legendre-Gauss-Radau quadrature. This weighted form is then shown to be an approximation of a logarithmic integral. This smooth approximation of the maximum function is then used to formulate a margin-inducing optimal control problem, and this margin-inducing optimal control problem is re-solved at specified guidance update times. The method is applied to a reusable launch vehicle atmospheric entry problem subject to heating rate and dynamic pressure constraints. It is found that the method of this paper produces a guidance trajectory that remains a significant distance from the path constraint limits while maintaining a large portion of the performance of the constrained optimal control problem.

papers.title: Numerical tests of chiral fermion weights with $η$-invariant phases in the 3450 model
papers.abstract: We test numerically a recently proposed prescription for coupling continuum chiral fermions to interpolated lattice gauge fields, in which the fermion weight has a Pauli-Villars (PV) regularized magnitude and a phase given by an Atiyah-Patodi-Singer (APS) $\eta$-invariant in one higher dimension. We use the anomaly-free two-dimensional $U(1)$ theory with left-handed charges $3,4$ and right-handed charges $5,0$, whose torus determinant is known exactly. At zero magnetic flux, with gauge fields interpolated from lattice links, the Polyakov loops evaluated on a $16\times16$ grid of flat connections agree with the exact values within $0.04\%$, whereas omitting the APS phase substantially reduces them to about $3\%$ of the exact result. The vacuum-polarization response yields an induced mass $m/e=2.82089$, close to $5/\sqrt{\pi}=2.82095$. At unit flux, where zero modes make the determinant vanish, we calculate a twelve-point correlator on a cylinder with the generalized APS boundary condition. For three smooth backgrounds its magnitude agrees with the exact result within $0.8\%$. Without the $\eta$-invariant its phase deviates by $1.8$-$3.0$ mrad, and with it by $0.2$-$0.5$ mrad. The phase of each charged fermion changes by $15$-$46$ mrad when the gauge field is extended differently into the third dimension, but the change cancels to below $0.2$ mrad in the anomaly-free combination.

papers.title: Uniqueness of addition in Schrödinger algebras
papers.abstract: We obtain a criterion for the uniqueness of addition in Schrödinger Lie algebras, applicable to both bijections and injections. This allows us to construct the first example of a Lie algebra with unique addition and a non-trivial center over a field of characteristic zero. Furthermore, a necessary and sufficient condition is established for the Schrödinger algebras to have bracket width one.

papers.title: Classification and Geometry of Loxodromic Curves on Surfaces of Revolution in Three-Dimensional Euclidean Space
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the global geometry of loxodromes and loxodromic curves on surfaces of revolution in $\mathbb{R}^3$. A loxodrome is a regular curve avoiding the poles and making a constant directed angle with the meridians. To allow curves to reach or pass through poles, we introduce loxodromic curves, whose pole-free interior portions are loxodromes. The directed azimuths of these portions agree modulo $\pi$. We classify surfaces of revolution into four types based on the number of poles and whether the profile curve is closed: cylinder-like, torus-like, paraboloid-like, and sphere-like. For cylinder-like surfaces, every maximal loxodromic curve other than a parallel is non-self-intersecting. For torus-like surfaces, nonparallel maximal loxodromic curves are closed or dense according to the rationality of their rotation numbers. For paraboloid-like and sphere-like surfaces, only maximal meridians can pass smoothly through poles, while nonmeridional, nonparallel maximal loxodromic curves have poles as endpoints. We derive the differential equations for arc-length-parametrized loxodromes and introduce coordinates in which they are represented by straight lines. We solve the direct and inverse problems for loxodromic segments on all four surface types and give criteria for maximal loxodromic curves to be geodesics. We show that diffeomorphisms preserving maximal loxodromic curves preserve surface type and that their inverses preserve such curves. These maps preserve maximal meridians and parallels on surfaces with poles, but need not do so on pole-free surfaces. We characterize azimuth-consistent diffeomorphisms and, for cylinder-like surfaces, establish criteria for conformality and isometry. In particular, azimuth-consistent diffeomorphisms are conformal when both surfaces have poles.

papers.title: Boundary Actuation of a Chain Fountain - Physically Admissible Tracking, Stochastic Limits and Zero-Gravity Circulation
papers.abstract: This paper was inspired by a post on Twitter and by the eight months the author spent at the AASS Centre at Orebro University in 2007. This phenomenon is interesting not only to a physicist, but also to someone like me working in control theory, because of its potential relevance to stabilizing drones and similar flying machines subject to random velocity fluctuations while hovering. A chain fountain can settle without an engineered controller, yet its natural height is selected by transport and boundary forces. We ask how an ideal boundary traction force can sustain a prescribed height or motion. Within an established three-state model, we connect feedback design to force and energy balances and derive sufficient conditions for nominal tracking that preserve the model's mechanical constraints. We also bound the deviations caused by bounded pickup uncertainty. The resulting framework explains how feedback can shape a naturally regulated process and identifies physical limits on the motions it can sustain: stabilizing a mathematical trajectory is useful only if the corresponding motion remains mechanically admissible. This is a preliminary step towards stabilization of the chain in three dimensions.

papers.title: Near-Threshold Kink Trapping Enhances Defect Healing in an Adaptive $\boldsymbol{ϕ^4}$ Chain
papers.abstract: We study the scattering of topological kinks in a discrete $\phi^4$ chain with a localized, adaptive defect, motivated by autonomous self-healing mechanisms in fibrous and polymeric chains. The defect represents damaged flanking bonds whose coupling stiffness evolves dynamically via an internal healing variable, driven by the local energy density and moderated by a viscoelastic relaxation rate $\beta$. Using high-resolution numerical simulations, we identify a sharp transition at a critical impact velocity $v_c$ separating kink reflection from transmission ($v_c \simeq 0.4183$ for the benchmark initial defect stiffness $C_{\min} = 0.2$). While subcritical kinks ($v_i < v_c$) bounce back with little energy deposition and supercritical ones ($v_i > v_c$) cross the defect too quickly to induce noticeable recovery, kinks near the threshold ($v_i \simeq v_c$) undergo resonant trapping. This prolonged dwell time transfers substantial vibrational energy into the defect, driving the healing variable to nearly full restoration ($h_{\max} \approx 0.98$). Notably, while $v_c$ and the peak defect energy $E_{d,\max}$ depend strongly on $C_{\min}$ and are largely unaffected by $\beta$, non-zero relaxation ($\beta > 0$) shortens the trapping window and reduces the final recovery efficiency. Our results show that energy-driven self-healing in discrete lattices is controlled by the cumulative dwell time and time-integrated energy excitation rather than the instantaneous impact peak alone.

papers.title: On the Difficulty of Sequence-Level Supervised Learning for Autoregressive Language Models
papers.abstract: During the supervised learning phase, autoregressive language models are typically trained by minimizing the negative log-likelihood of the training data, which decomposes as a sum of token-level cross-entropies via teacher forcing. This objective is simple and efficient but potentially suffers from so-called exposure bias: a mismatch between the way the model is trained and the way it is used at inference time. Can we instead design sequence-level loss functions that incorporate inference-time decoding procedures, such as greedy decoding or autoregressive sampling? We show that two natural attempts lead to loss functions that are fundamentally flawed: unbounded below. We further show that these two flawed loss functions are intimately connected: using autoregressive Gumbel tricks, the sampling based loss is the expected greedy loss under Gumbel perturbations. Since the pathology stems from the dependence of the decoded sequence on the model parameters, we analyze the update direction obtained by applying a stop gradient on the sampling procedure, leading to a moment matching direction. While it is not the gradient of any loss function, we prove that it defines a valid descent direction in function space for the autoregressive negative log-likelihood. Despite these theoretical insights, the moment matching direction suffers from high variance. We conclude that teacher forcing may well be ``all you need'' for supervised learning of autoregressive models.

papers.title: Proof of the Quasi Riemann Hypothesis using $\mathbb Q[i]$
papers.abstract: Using quartic Gauss sums in place of the cubic Gauss sums in OpenAI's original proof, we prove that the Dedekind $\zeta$-function $\zeta_{\mathbb Q(i)}(s)$ of $\mathbb Q(i)$ has no zeros in the half-plane $\Re s>599/600$, thereby obtaining the same zero-free half-plane for the Riemann $\zeta$- this http URL obtain the upper bound for the smoothed sum by applying Poisson summation twice and using the functional equation of the quartic Kubota series of angular weight $1$.In the Mellin representation, a zero-density bound for the family of quartic characters controls the terms from nonprincipal characters,and a residue and a lattice average over fourth powers give the main term.

papers.title: Information Spectrum Methods for MUltiple-Access Channels--Part III : The Strong Converse in the $K$-User Gaussian Case
papers.abstract: This paper, Part III of a series, treats $K$-user multiple-access channels (MACs). Its starting point is a pair of fundamental lemmas, a random-coding lemma of Feinstein type and a converse lemma of Verdú--Han type, which are the $K$-user extensions of the two lemmas underlying Han's information spectrum approach to the general two-user MAC. From them we derive the capacity region of the general $K$-user MAC with cost constraint and show that it contains the polymatroid capacity region of the $K$-user Gaussian MAC. We then prove, by an elementary information spectrum calculation that adapts a diffuse--exceptional subspace decomposition used in recent second-order converses for the Gaussian MAC, that for every subset $\cS$ of users and every independent input satisfying the power constraints, the conditional information spectral-sup rate of the $K$-user Gaussian MAC does not exceed $\frac12\log(1+P_\cS/N)$, where $P_\cS$ is the total power of the users in $\cS$, with a probability bound that does not depend on the input. Consequently, the strong converse for the $K$-user Gaussian MAC, in the sense that the error probability tends to one for every rate tuple outside the capacity region, follows directly from the converse lemma, without the wringing technique and without hypothesis-testing meta-converses. This strong converse was first established by Fong and Tan, whose per-blocklength bounds yield it, through wringing and quantization. It is the key ingredient in the converse parts of the coding theorems for mixed Gaussian MACs in Part I, where the $\varepsilon$-strong converse would not suffice.

papers.title: Information Spectrum Methods for Multiple-Access Channels --Part II : $\varepsilon$-Capacity Regions in the Mixed Finite-Alphabet Case
papers.abstract: In a nonergodic channel such as a slowly fading link, the channel law is drawn once and held fixed for the whole codeword, and the relevant performance measure is the $\varepsilon$-capacity. We study the $\varepsilon$-capacity regions of two-user mixed multiple-access channels (MACs) with finite alphabets, additive cost constraints and an arbitrary mixing measure. The direct parts are derived from a single information spectrum formula; the converse parts use, in addition, Fano's inequality and Ahlswede's strong converse applied to each component. Without knowledge of the realized component, we prove a single-letter inner bound for every $0\le\varepsilon<1$, in which one input serves all components; for $\varepsilon=0$ it is tight, and the capacity region is given by the essential infima of the component mutual informations. We prove a single-letter outer bound, the outage region, in which each component may use its own input; it holds with or without channel state information (CSI) at either terminal, and it is the $\varepsilon$-capacity region when the encoders know the component and the parameter space is countable. Both bounds coincide, in all four CSI scenarios, for well-ordered mixed MACs, which include degradedly ordered families and mixtures with a common optimal input, such as mixed additive MACs. Without CSI the outer bound can be strictly loose, and the no-CSI $\varepsilon$-capacity region for $0<\varepsilon<1$ remains open in general. Finally, we extend Ahlswede's strong converse to $K$ users with cost constraints and show that most of these results extend to $K$-user mixed MACs.

papers.title: Dynamics and Statistical Mechanics of Born-Oppenheimer Auxiliary Velocities
papers.abstract: In Born-Oppenheimer (BO) dynamics, auxiliary variables such as electron densities, induced polarization and electrode charges follow stationarity conditions, yet their time derivatives, such as currents, are physical observables. Using Mass-Zero constrained dynamics, we interpret these derivatives as explicit dynamical variables and derive the invariant measure giving their equilibrium statistical properties. We illustrate the framework in constant-potential molecular dynamics, where the electrode-charge velocities reproduce BO current fluctuations and the frequency-dependent admittance.

papers.title: Low-lying doubly charmed strange baryons via QCD sum rules
papers.abstract: We systematically investigate the masses of the low-lying doubly heavy baryons and their $B^*(3/2^+)\to B(1/2^+)\gamma$ radiative transitions within QCD sum rules and light-cone sum rules (LCSR). By constructing mixed interpolating currents, we obtain $M_{\Xi_{cc}}=3.62^{+0.14}_{-0.15}$ GeV, $M_{\Xi_{cc}^*}=3.72^{+0.14}_{-0.13}$ GeV, $M_{\Omega_{cc}}=3.72^{+0.13}_{-0.15}$ GeV, and $M_{\Omega_{cc}^*}=3.82^{+0.13}_{-0.15}$ GeV, together with their doubly bottom partners around $10.27$--$10.34$ GeV. The extracted masses are compatible with the observed $\Xi_{cc}$ and $\Omega_{cc}$ states and predict hyperfine splittings of about $101^{+27}_{-11}$ MeV and $99^{+11}_{-12}$ MeV for the $\Xi_{cc}$ and $\Omega_{cc}$ systems, respectively. Using these inputs, we derive the LCSR for the electromagnetic form factors and obtain radiative widths $\Gamma(\Xi_{cc}^{*++}\to\Xi_{cc}^{++}\gamma)=5.25^{+8.57}_{-3.62}$ keV, $\Gamma(\Xi_{cc}^{*+}\to\Xi_{cc}^{+}\gamma)=0.31^{+0.84}_{-0.25}$ keV, and $\Gamma(\Omega_{cc}^{*+}\to\Omega_{cc}^{+}\gamma)=0.41^{+0.67}_{-0.30}$ keV, while the corresponding doubly bottom widths are at the $0.002$--$0.01$ keV level. We find that the magnetic-dipole contribution dominates, whereas the electric-quadrupole form factor is numerically small. The light- and heavy-quark photon-emission terms can interfere or enhance significantly, and the heavy-quark contribution cannot be neglected in radiative transitions. These results provide useful theoretical guidance for future searches for spin-$3/2$ doubly heavy baryons through radiative decay modes at LHCb, Belle II, and other experimental facilities.

papers.title: TAPES: Terminal Adjoint-Propagated Error Scheduling for Financial Diffusion Samplers
papers.abstract: Financial diffusion samplers are often reused with a small number of function evaluations (NFE) inside scenario and risk pipelines, where numerical time-grid error can distort terminal quantities such as covariances, tails, and drawdown proxies. We study offline grid construction for a frozen probability-flow ODE: the score network, conditioning, Euler solver, report normalization, and deployment NFE remain fixed. TAPES (Terminal Adjoint-Propagated Error Scheduling) estimates signed local defects by Richardson comparisons, transports them through the remaining discrete flow and a terminal-report adjoint, and optimizes the squared norm of their sum before a capped direct refinement. We show that this transported signed sum is the first-order terminal-report error and quantify, under an aligned-defect model, the inefficiency of diagonal criteria. Across six budgets on a regime-switching simulation and chronologically held-out Mag7 contexts, TAPES gives the lowest design- and audit-report errors in all 24 dataset--budget--report rows within the reported five-pipeline panel. Cross-budget mean relative audit-error reductions are about 10--11% on Regime-SV and about 1% on Mag7, with Bonferroni intervals excluding zero; all displayed winners persist under a doubled-resolution reference, and a small Regime-SV Heun probe preserves the TAPES-first audit ordering. TAPES changes only the offline schedule and retains the prescribed deployment NFE; claims concern numerical fidelity to frozen generators.

papers.title: Why "quantum spin liquids" are quantum singlet liquids
papers.abstract: The last couple of decades have seen enormous theoretical and experimental research efforts aimed at finding quantum spin liquids (QSLs) in geometrically frustrated (GF) magnetic materials. Experimental demonstrations of QSLs are challenging due to the indirect character of possible QSL signatures and the presence of impurities in materials, which may destroy or obscure a QSL. At the same time, the theoretical literature often lacks consensus about the ground states of quantum spins on even the simplest GF magnetic lattices. We summarize experimental evidence that in the impurity-free limit, available GF magnetic materials that do not develop magnetic order at low temperatures would form {\it a quantum singlet liquid}, i.e. a disordered state of non-magnetic excitations. We further confirm with theoretical arguments the existence of such a singlet liquid and its gapless character in materials with half-integer spins per primitive magnetic cell. Such a liquid manifests itself in the thermodynamics of GF magnets while having no magnetic features at low temperatures.

papers.title: No Convergence in Learned Eavesdropping-Detection Dynamics for BB84 Quantum Key Distribution
Polynomial Swap Coboundary Expansion with Applications to LTCs and PCPs
Integral Exponential Series: Fibonacci Weights and Implicit Equations
papers.abstract: We apply classical prime-power congruence criteria to two families of exponential series. For the Fibonacci numbers $F_n$, we characterize the polynomials $P\in\Z[T]$ for which $\exp(\sum_{n\ge1}P(F_n)x^n/n)$ has integer coefficients: this holds if and only if $P$ is even and $P(0)\equiv P(1)\equiv P(2)\pmod5$. In particular, $5$ is the least positive multiplier for each positive even power of $F_n$, and the series with weights $5F_n^{2k}$ has degree $5^{k-1}$ over $\Q(x)$ for $k\ge1$. For $R_n(y)\in\Z[y]$ satisfying $R_{pn}(y)\equiv R_n(y)\pmod p$ for every prime $p$ and every $n\ge1$, we prove that $H(x,y)=\exp(\sum_{n\ge1}R_n(y)^n x^n/n)$ belongs to $\Z[y][[x]]$ and that $A(x)=H(x,A(x))$ has a unique integral solution. For $q\in \Z$, taking $R_n(y)=q^n+y$ proves the conjecture in OEIS A163138; the Fibonacci result proves the conjecture in A207969 and A207970. For the implicit family with indeterminate $q$, the coefficient of $x^n$ has degree $n^2$, leading coefficient $1/n$, and nonnegative integer coefficients in the binomial basis, for every $n\ge1$.

papers.title: Learning memory forces and bounding frequency errors in fractional Kuramoto grids
papers.abstract: Missing history creates two different demands on a forecaster for a fractional grid: predicting frequency accurately and reconstructing memory well enough to bound the prediction error. We connect these demands through the hereditary force that remains after an integral observation correction. A compact decoder retains the directions most relevant to that force, and an exact decomposition separates omitted directions from coefficient error. A response-trained linear predictor and neural refinement learn the coefficients for frequency prediction. A separate force reconstruction supplies the reference for a nonlinear energy bound for the specified finite relaxation model, accounting for numerical propagation defects and the difference between the reference and point forecasts. For the outage transients studied here, refinement improves on the linear predictor across the time steps and memory parameters tested. Replacing the noisy origin states reveals why this gain can coexist with greater memory reconstruction error: the learned correction partly compensates for observation error. Separating prediction from reconstruction enables frequency bounds in cases where the point predictor alone cannot support them. A critical radius compares calibrated uncertainty with the angle margin available along the reference trajectory, explaining both issuance and abstention. Under jointly exchangeable calibration and test events, the calibrated guarantee bounds the marginal probability of issuing an invalid envelope. Together, these results connect uncertainty about history outside the observation window to frequency forecasts and explicit conditions for bounding their errors.

papers.title: Chimera states in a network of firefly oscillators
papers.abstract: We investigate chimera-like states in a network of identical firefly oscillators with nonlocal delayed coupling. For a uniform communication delay, the network exhibits a breathing phase-frequency chimera, characterized by the coexistence of frequency-locked and frequency-drifting populations and an oscillating incoherent-domain width. We then introduce heterogeneous pairwise communication delays to investigate a numerical analogue of the Sarfati-Peleg phenomenon observed in natural firefly swarms. In this regime, a recurring collective chorus coexists with character oscillators that flash persistently before or after the chorus. Cycle-resolved delay maps, role rasters, character probabilities, and spatial covariance diagnostics demonstrate the persistence and collective organization of these chorus-character roles. Although the uniform-delay and heterogeneous-delay states represent different forms of partial synchronization, the same firefly-oscillator framework supports both regimes. Finally, we construct a reduced analytical description in terms of a chorus-relative delay field and a memory field. The local dynamics is organized around a saturated subcritical pitchfork structure, producing a stable chorus equilibrium together with two stable character equilibria. The reduced model therefore provides a phenomenological description of the tri-stable chorus-character organization and its characteristic delay scale. Our results show that heterogeneous delayed interactions among identical relaxation oscillators can generate persistent temporal identities analogous to those reported in synchronous firefly swarms.

papers.title: Connecting Electroweak Fine-Tuning, Tens-of-GeV Dark Matter, and Exotic Higgs Decays in the GNMSSM
