papers.abstract: In the general next-to-minimal supersymmetric standard model (GNMSSM), we connect electroweak fine-tuning, a singlino dark matter candidate with mass around tens of GeV, and Exotic Higgs Decays, identifying a natural region characterized by the mass hierarchy $m_{\tilde{S}}<m_{\tilde{B}}<m_{\tilde{H}}$ and $\mu_{\rm tot}\in [200, 500]$ GeV. For fine-tuning measure $\Delta \leq 40$, the branching ratio $\mathrm{Br}(h\to a_sa_s)$ falls in the range 7\%$-$25\%, with the pseudoscalar mass $m_{a_s}$ lying mostly between 10 and 20 GeV. This region splits into two viable scenarios consistent with LZ 2024 direct detection: one where the lightest CP-even Higgs $h_1$ is SM-like ($h_1$ case), and another where the second-lightest $h_2$ is SM-like ($h_2$ case). LHC searches for $h\to a_sa_s \to b\bar{b}\tau^+\tau^-$ exclude 12\% (10\%) of samples with 12 GeV $\leq m_{a_s} \leq$ 15.5 GeV in the $h_1$ ($h_2$) case, while a substantial fraction remains accessible at the HL-LHC in the $h_2$ case. Our analysis unifies naturalness, dark matter, and observable exotic Higgs decays, yielding concrete targets for future experiments.

papers.title: Congruence density under sublattice inclusion
papers.abstract: Following Gábor Czédli, the \emph{congruence density} of a finite lattice $A$ is $\cd(A)=|\Con A|/2^{|A|-1}$, where $\Con A$ is its congruence lattice and $|A|$ is its number of elements. Czédli proved that density cannot increase under several kinds of sublattice extension and asked whether this holds for every sublattice inclusion. For a sublattice $S$ of $L$, we prove the stronger inequality $\cd(L)\leq2^{-d}\cd(S)$, where $d$ is the larger of the increases in the numbers of join-reducible and meet-reducible elements. The proof follows congruence labels along the chains into which prime intervals of $S$ split in $L$. We also prove that $\cd(L)=\cd(S)$ if and only if every element of $L-S$ is comparable with every element of $L$. The theorem of G. Czédli and L.~Szabó relating compatible quasiorders to pairs of congruences gives the corresponding quasiorder-density results.

papers.title: The limit point set of real roots of random polynomials: a resolution of erdős problem 521
papers.abstract: We resolve Erdős Problem~521 by proving that the normalized real-root count $N_n/\log n$ of Rademacher polynomials almost surely has no limit. More generally, consider the Kac polynomials \[ P_n(x)=\sum_{j=0}^{n}\xi_jx^j \] with i.i.d.\ real coefficients of mean zero, variance one, and a finite absolute exponential moment. Let $N_n$ denote the number of distinct real roots of $P_n$. We prove that, almost surely, \[ \liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{N_n}{\log n}=\frac1\pi, \qquad \limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{N_n}{\log n}=\frac1\pi+C_*, \] and the set of subsequential limits is exactly \[ \left[\frac1\pi,\;\frac1\pi+C_*\right]. \] Here $C_*>1/\pi$ is a constant uniquely determined by an equation. The lower-limit identity remains valid under the weaker assumption that $\mathbb{E}|\xi_0|^{2+\delta}<\infty$ for some $\delta>0$.

papers.title: A Probabilistic Characterization of the Ideals of Resolvent Algebras
papers.abstract: We characterize the ideal theory of Buchholz for resolvent algebras in probabilistic terms. Regarding closed two-sided ideals as kernels of representations, we pass from representations to the Gelfand--Naimark--Segal representations of states, and describe the singular, trivially regular, and regular parts, which Buchholz gives through the one-particle space, by the behavior of the corresponding probability measures of the fields. On an isotropic subspace, the resolvent algebra is a commutative $C^{\ast}$-algebra whose states correspond to probability measures, and this correspondence carries the description further to sub-$\sigma$-algebras. Starting from Bose--Einstein condensation of the free Bose gas with its direct integral representation and from the treatment of the infrared singularity of the van Hove model, we connect the ideal-theoretic and the probabilistic arguments. Since the ideals carry physical information in these arguments, we show that the corresponding sub-$\sigma$-algebras and their inclusions carry this information in correspondence with the ideals.

papers.title: Pyramidal Columns Acting as Attention Heads
papers.abstract: Can the functional architecture of a Transformer attention head be given a biological construction? More specifically, could a suitable group of pyramidal columns in posterior temporal language regions (PTLRs) constitute the biological construction of a neuromorphic mechanical realization of an attention head, under a mathematical instantiation that need not coincide with its standard Transformer instantiation? This paper investigates this hypothesis by examining possible correspondences between the functional organization of attention heads and neurophysiological mechanisms operating within and across pyramidal columns involved in human language processing. Our analysis builds on a mechanical-structural description of Transformer attention heads as systems of simple neural networks linked through output-input and output-weight interconnections. We examine the functional organization of an attention head and the input-dependent transformations it produces, and ask how the corresponding processing relations could be constructed in biological neural tissue. We then identify candidate neural mechanisms of signal transmission and modulation within and across pyramidal columns that may jointly support such a construction. On this basis, we propose that a suitably organized group of pyramidal columns in PTLRs could constitute a biological construction of a neuromorphic mechanical realization of an attention head. Whether the required functional organization actually exists in PTLRs remains an open empirical question. The hypothesis does not require the biological system to reproduce the standard mathematical instantiation of Transformer attention: the same functional architecture may be mechanically realized and mathematically instantiated in a different way, consistent with its biological construction.

papers.title: Improved Elastic Weight Consolidation as an Optimization Constraint for Continual Learning
papers.abstract: Regularization-based continual learning reduces catastrophic forgetting by penalizing changes to parameters that mattered for earlier tasks. Elastic Weight Consolidation (EWC), a standard instance, weights its quadratic penalty by the empirical Fisher, usually justified as approximating loss curvature. We instead derive the penalty from what training on a new task should preserve. In this formulation, Continual Learning as an Optimization Constraint (CLOC), new training must keep chosen functionals of learned behavior unchanged, and the local approximation of this constraint is the stored penalty. We show that EWC's empirical Fisher is exactly the first-order form of this constraint when the preserved functional is each old sample's loss. The derivation exposes a flaw: EWC weights each sample by the scale of its loss gradient, so samples the model fits well barely contribute, although later training can still forget them. Improved EWC (IEWC) instead penalizes how far each old output moves off its loss level set, rather than how much its loss changes, which removes this weighting for any differentiable loss and output geometry. Across classification, segmentation, language, forecasting, and diffusion, IEWC variants match or improve on EWC and outperform EWC-DR, a classification-specific correction. In a held-out evaluation with validation-selected hyperparameters, removing this weighting alone raises ImageNet-R accuracy over EWC by 2.00 percentage points (95% CI 0.93-3.07). More broadly, CLOC turns the design of continual-learning penalties into a choice of what to preserve, from which a principled penalty follows by derivation.

papers.title: On the Broué--Digne--Michel conjectures: disjointness of the cohomology groups
papers.abstract: The goal of this paper is to start proving the Broué--Digne--Michel conjectures concerning the cohomology of Deligne--Lusztig varieties attached to roots of the full twist. The main result establishes that the $\mathrm{Ext}$-algebras of the cohomology complexes attached to roots of the full twist are concentrated in degree $0$. The main idea is to reduce the problem to a calculation in the Hecke category. The resulting argument is essentially topological and applies to all realizations of the Hecke category.

papers.title: Communication inequalities: robust quantum advantage, measurement testing and dimension witnessing with minimal setups
papers.abstract: Communication scenarios (CS) are arguably the simplest setting in which quantum behaviors can be observed. Yet, in contrast to Bell scenarios or prepare-measure scenarios with shared randomness, no general method is known to separate classical and quantum statistics. Here we close this gap by deriving dimensional inequalities to separate classical and quantum statistics in CS. These depend only on four parameters of the input-output statistics, corresponding to correlated and anticorrelated events. Under dimensional assumptions, saturating one of the inequalities certifies SIC-POVMs with analytical noise robustness. The inequalities also yield a dimension witness for both correlated and anti-correlated statistics, without the need of measurement incompatibility.

papers.title: The multiplicative complexity of the three-bit low-half multiplier
papers.abstract: We prove that the multiplicative complexity of the three-bit low-half multiplier is six, giving a structural, enumeration-free lower-bound proof valid against unrestricted nonlinear reuse in Boolean XOR-AND circuits. The value was first established by SAT searches of the first author and independently confirmed by the second author. An explicit six-AND circuit supplies the upper bound. The lower bound combines derivatives, quadratic products, complementary minors, and extraction modulo a Boolean ideal. Independent finite checks accompany the arguments. $\mathrm{MC}(M_3)=6$ is fully formalized in Lean 4, using only Lean's three standard axioms (propositional extensionality, choice and quotient soundness).

papers.title: Flow Structure in Idealized Rotating Detonation Combustor with Supersonic Inflow
papers.abstract: The work presented investigates the flow structure and stability of an airbreathing rotating detonation engine (RDE) in an idealized combustor. The presented derivation of a modified pressure cutoff injection scheme allows for supersonic injection in an idealized two-dimensional RDE as a function of a specified design Mach number and the pressure ratio across the injection surface. Numerical simulations are conducted using a compressible reacting flow solver with finite-rate chemistry built on an Adaptive Mesh Refinement (AMR) framework. The fuel mixture is set to a stoichiometric hydrogen-air mixture for all simulations. Stable operation occurs for a wide range of inflow conditions with inflow Mach numbers up to 4. The increased total temperature associated with increasing Mach numbers causes burning at the injection surface during the injector recovery process, resulting in unstable operation. Meanwhile, increasing total pressure facilitates sustained supersonic injection. Analysis of the steady flow structure shows a familiar structure with significant changes to the detonation structure when compared with a rocket RDE. With supersonic inflow, an oblique detonation wave (ODW) forms along the injection surface connected to the moving detonation through a slip line. Changes in the oblique detonation wave and normal detonation angle occur with changes in the inflow Mach number, however the overall detonation structure remains similar when supersonic injection occurs.

papers.title: The norm formula in a Banach space and in its complete theory
papers.abstract: Let $h$ be the Hilbert norm on the real space $\ell_2(\mathbb{N})\oplus_2\ell_2(\mathbb{N})$, and put $q(u,v)=\sup_{i<j}|u_i+v_j|$. For each of Bollobás's additive norms $h+\varepsilon q$, $\varepsilon>0$, and for the quadratic norm $\sqrt{h^2+q^2}$, the norm formula $\lVert x+y\rVert$ is unstable on the renormed space and has no independence property in its complete theory. We approximate $q(x+y)$ uniformly on bounded Hilbert balls by truncating small coordinates. For $n$ fixed test vectors and thresholds, the number of threshold patterns of $q(x+y)$ as $y$ varies is bounded by a polynomial in $n$ when the support sizes of the test vectors and of $y$ are bounded. These estimates give finite fat-shattering dimension for the translates of $q$ at every positive scale. The norm formula on a space can be stable, unstable without the independence property, or have the independence property. We give an example in each of these three cases where the formula has the independence property in the complete theory, and an example in each of the first two cases where it lacks that property in the complete theory. All five spaces satisfy a common midpoint estimate for uniform convexity, and each admits an isomorphism to Hilbert space of distortion at most $\sqrt3$.

papers.title: Boij-S"oderberg and Harder-Narasimhan polygons of vector bundles on projective space
papers.abstract: Eisenbud and Schreyer proved that the cohomology table of a vector bundle $F$ on $\mathbb{P}^n$ is a unique positive combination of supernatural tables along a chain of root sequences. The slopes of the pieces, weighted by their ranks, form a concave polygon $\Psi_F$, the Boij-Söderberg polygon, with the same endpoints as the Harder-Narasimhan polygon $P_F$. We prove that $P_F\leq\Psi_F$, in any characteristic, by testing subsheaves against sheaves with pure resolutions on thickened lines; the bound is optimal among bounds depending only on the ray of the table. The chain majorizes every other supernatural decomposition, and $\Psi$ is monotone under cancellations, hence upper semicontinuous in flat families. The comparison extends to coherent sheaves and, by linear projection, to sheaves of positive dimension. On $\mathbb{P}^2$ the defect is a sum of four cohomological terms; we characterize equality and show that the inequality survives the large volume limit of Bridgeland stability. For a smooth projective variety $X$ of dimension $n\geq2$ in characteristic zero, with $H$ ample and base-point-free, the mean normalized squared spread $G(\mathcal{E})$ of the roots in the cohomology table of every vector bundle $\mathcal{E}$ satisfies $G(\mathcal{E})\geq(K_X^2-2c_2(X))\cdot H^{n-2}/((n+1)H^n)$, a bound independent of $\mathcal{E}$. Since $G(\mathcal{E})=1$ exactly for arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay bundles, when this bound exceeds $1$ it is a uniform form of their absence.

papers.title: CCGeant4: charge-state-resolved transport and energy-loss fluctuations of relativistic heavy ions in Geant4
papers.abstract: CCGeant4 models energy-loss fluctuations of heavy ions in Geant4, accounting for both charge exchange and relativistic corrections to electron scattering beyond the first Born approximation. We use GLOBAL cross sections for electron capture and loss, ATIMA equilibrium stopping powers and charge-dependent delta-electron spectra calculated from the Dirac equation in a frozen-shell potential. The package also supports tabulated elastic ion-nucleus scattering. The silicon example includes interference between Coulomb and nuclear scattering amplitudes. We compare charge evolution with GLOBAL and energy-loss spectra with MOCADI for matched beams and targets. Experimental comparisons cover published energy-loss measurements and several measurements of energy deposited by xenon ions in silicon. For uranium at 800 MeV/u, the energy-loss variances from our Dirac configuration agree with published screened-ion calculations to within 4% in Be, Al and Pb. Both calculations lie within the reported experimental uncertainties for all three targets, while calculated bismuth spectra in silver are narrower than measured. Calculations in thin silicon layers show that delta-electron escape can make deposited-energy distributions substantially narrower than primary-ion energy-loss distributions, highlighting the importance of secondary-electron transport for detector-response modelling. The distribution includes the Geant4 source patch, the transport tables and their converters, and a runnable example.

papers.title: Relaxation of Quantum Observables in a 4D Black Hole that forms from Collapse of a Null Shell
papers.abstract: The vacuum polarization and luminosity are computed in a four-dimensional spacetime where a spherically symmetric null shell contracts to form a black hole. This is done by computing the contribution of the spherically symmetric modes of a massless minimally coupled scalar field to the quantities $\la \phi^2 \ra_{\rm in} - \la \phi^2 \ra_U$ and $L_{\rm in} - L_U$. Here the subscript ``in'' denotes the {\it in} vacuum state for the null shell spacetime and the subscript ``U'' denotes the Unruh state in Schwarzschild spacetime. The computation is done outside the null shell and outside the event horizon where the spacetime geometry is the Schwarzschild geometry. It is found that, as expected, these differences approach zero at late times. However, they do so significantly more slowly than in the two-dimensional case where there is no scattering of the mode functions. In both cases, the difference is dominated by a quasinormal mode at intermediate times and a tail term at late times that decays quartically in time. For the luminosity difference, an analytic calculation verifies the late-time result for the tail term.

papers.title: Xenon energy-deposition widths in silicon: measurements and Geant4 comparisons
papers.abstract: Energy-deposition fluctuations determine the isotope-separation capability of multilayer silicon detectors. We measure the central peak widths of $^{124}$Xe signals in 300- and 675-micrometre silicon layers at incident energies of approximately 152-274 MeV per nucleon and compare them with Geant4 11.4.0 electromagnetic option 4 (emopt4) and a calculation with explicit charge exchange. In the 300-micrometre detector, the emopt4 relative width of 1.844% exceeds the unselected experimental width of 1.407% by 31% and the selected width of 1.060% by 74%. For the 675-micrometre detector, selection windows around the downstream-signal peak, each approximately ten fitted first-plane standard deviations wide, give experimental upper estimates of 0.66-0.74%, compared with emopt4 predictions of 1.01-1.24%. Explicit charge-state transport gives widths of 0.889-0.932% for the thinner layer, depending on the incident charge distribution, and 0.59-0.63% for the thicker layer. These predictions are consistent with the experimental upper estimates, while emopt4 overestimates the widths for both thicknesses throughout the studied energy interval.

papers.title: Exact transformation-optics representation of the Ellis wormhole and limits of finite-device scattering emulation
papers.abstract: We derive a global isotropic representation of the ultrastatic Ellis wormhole and establish which features of its electromagnetic response can, and cannot, be reproduced by a finite device. An orientation-preserving coordinate map sends the signed proper-radial line to a punctured Euclidean chart with refractive index $n(\rho)=1+a^2/(4\rho^2)$. Through the Plebański correspondence, this gives the exact impedance-matched continuum medium $\varepsilon_r=\mu_r=n(\rho)\mathbf{I}$ and its full vector-Maxwell operator. For the ideal two-ended geometry, we derive the electromagnetic radial operator, establish its spectral properties, and express its scattering amplitudes through Jost solutions and Wronskians. Nonzero transmission into the second asymptotic end implies $|R_{\rm id}|<1$ at every real frequency, whereas a regular, lossless finite one-port has unit-modulus reflection. The reverse triangle inequality therefore yields a strictly positive lower bound on the complex reflection-amplitude mismatch. This theorem applies to the stated lossless single-port class and is not extended to lossy or multiport realizations. We compute converged multipole scattering data and establish the low-frequency threshold scaling $|T_L|^2\propto(\omega a/c)^{4L+2}$, with coefficients independently validated for $L=1,2,3,4$. The transmission cross section tends to $\pi a^2$, while the ideal profile's total scattering cross section has a logarithmic forward divergence. We also construct a smooth finite-shell target and derive an exact finite-band constitutive-error formula for a calibrated passive Lorentz model. The constitutive benchmark is kept distinct from scattering equivalence throughout.

papers.title: Holographic dual of the 2d Ising model
papers.abstract: We propose a holographic dual of the 2d Ising model on a torus as the Turaev-Viro TQFT on a solid torus. The bulk spacetime is divided into the ``core'' region and the ``sandwich'' region. The core region prepares a defect state $|\mathcal{D}\rangle$ on the topological boundary $\mathbb{D}$. The sandwich region computes the Turaev-Viro state sum $\langle\mathcal{D}|\Pi|\mathcal{F}\rangle$ between the state $|\mathcal{D}\rangle$ on $\mathbb{D}$ and the state $|\mathcal{F}\rangle$ on the physical boundary $\mathbb{B}$. The fusion diagram (or string-net) $\mathcal{F}$ on $\mathbb{B}$ is given by the Aasen-Fendley-Mong construction. There is also a ``bedding surface'' $\mathbb{S}$ between $\mathbb{D}$ and $\mathbb{B}$, and the height variables (or Ising spins inside/outside of the domain wall) are naturally living on $\mathbb{S}$. The bulk spacetime is discretized by the 2-skeleton $P$ which interpolates $\mathcal{D}$ and $\mathcal{F}$. When the defect $\mathcal{D}$ is absent, the 2-skeleton $P$ ends on the bedding surface $\mathbb{S}$ and $P$ is interpreted as the bulk worldsheet of the string-net $\mathcal{F}$.

papers.title: An Analytical Model for Fast Design Optimization and Performance Studies of nuSTORM
authors: J. P. A. M. de André
papers.abstract: The concept of generating neutrino beams from stored muons (nuSTORM) has been explored for several decades. A few nuSTORM facilities have been designed for GeV muons, and a design of a sub-GeV nuSTORM, proposed for the European Spallation Source, is now underway. At low energy, the much larger beam divergence can significantly reduce the neutrino flux reaching the detector. Therefore, optimization of facility parameters is essential to avoid additional flux losses. This optimization, however, is not trivial due to the interdependency of the parameters. In this paper, we derive an analytical expression for the absolute neutrino flux incident on the detector front face and show how it can guide the optimization of a nuSTORM facility. The analytical expression is furthermore validated with published data and Monte Carlo simulations from five separate cases. In addition, we show how it can be extended to also predict the neutrino energy distribution at the detector, thus offering a convenient method to estimate the facility performance without time-consuming Monte Carlo simulations of particle transport and decay.

papers.title: Hybrid Machine Learning for Physically Consistent Prediction of Mutual Diffusion Coefficients in Binary Liquid Mixtures
papers.abstract: Experimental data on mutual diffusion coefficients in liquid mixtures are scarce, and existing prediction methods are unreliable for non-ideal mixtures. Building on HADES, our hybrid model for self-diffusion coefficients, we introduce the Enhanced Vignes Equation (EVE), which augments the Vignes equation with a deep-set model. Its inputs are molecular descriptors derived from SMILES and activity-coefficient information from HANNA, a machine-learning model for activity coefficients. EVE predicts Maxwell-Stefan diffusion coefficients; the corresponding Fickian coefficients follow from the thermodynamic factor, likewise obtained from HANNA. Trained and evaluated on 2106 experimental data points for 123 binary mixtures, EVE outperforms all available semi-empirical models, halving the mean absolute relative error for mixtures without experimental infinite-dilution diffusion data. Combined with HADES, EVE yields the complete set of self- and mutual diffusion coefficients of a binary mixture from SMILES and pure-component viscosities alone. EVE and HADES are available at this https URL , and the code is fully disclosed.

papers.title: Novel method for measuring the isovector partner of X(3872)
papers.abstract: The predicted isovector partner of the $X(3872)$, denoted as $W_{c1}$, is expected to produce only a relatively weak structure near the charged $D \bar{D}^*$ threshold, making its experimental identification challenging. In this work, we explore the triangle singularity (TS) mechanism as a means of enhancing the sensitivity to the $W_{c1}$ in the decays $B^0 \to \pi K \bar{D}^0 D^{*0}$. We investigate the $D_{s1}(2536) \bar{D}^*$ triangle rescattering mechanism, incorporating the coupled-channel $D \bar{D}^*$ scattering amplitudes obtained from the Lippmann-Schwinger equation. The interplay between the TS and the coupled-channel dynamics produces characteristic structures in the $K \bar{D}^0 D^{*0}$ invariant mass distributions associated with the $X(3872)$ and its isovector partner $W_{c1}$. In particular, the charged-channel contribution exhibits a distinct structure sensitive to the nearby $W_{c1}$ pole. Our results demonstrate that the TS mechanism provides a promising way to probe the otherwise weak manifestation of the $W_{c1}$, offering a complementary experimental strategy for searching for this predicted state at Belle II and LHCb.

papers.title: Affine Combiners for Reed-Solomon Proximity Gaps
papers.abstract: Reed-Solomon proximity gaps establish soundness guarantees for protocols that test received words through random combinations. For length-$n$ codes over $\mathbb{F}_q$, classical scalar combiners achieve error $O(n/q)$ in the unique-decoding regime, with larger known bounds near the Johnson radius. We prove smaller error bounds using affine combiners, which combine two received words $f,g$ as $f(x)+(\alpha+\beta x)g(x)$, where $\alpha,\beta$ are independent uniform elements of $\mathbb{F}_q$. For output degree bound $d=\rho n$, fixed $\rho\in(0,1)$ and $0<\eta<1-\sqrt{\rho}$, and sufficiently large block length $n$, we prove mutual correlated agreement (MCA) with one coordinate of agreement loss at threshold $A=\lceil(\sqrt{\rho}+\eta)n\rceil$, with error $O_{\rho,\eta}\left(\frac{1}{q}+\frac{n^2}{q^2}\right)$. The result holds over arbitrary evaluation domains in every finite field, including prime and binary extension fields. The agreement threshold can approach the Johnson threshold, beyond unique decoding. For $q\ge n^2$, our error is $O_{\rho,\eta}(1/q)$, an asymptotic factor-$n$ separation from scalar combiners: we prove that their worst-case MCA error is $\Omega_{\rho,\eta}(n/q)$ at the same agreement threshold and with the same one-coordinate loss. We also prove that affine combiners incur worst-case error $\Omega_{\rho,\eta}(n/q)$ when no agreement loss is allowed. Thus one coordinate of agreement loss is necessary for our guarantee; this relaxation of standard MCA reduces the guaranteed common agreement fraction by at most $1/n$. We also extend the result to $k$-variate Reed-Muller codes on subfield grids, obtaining MCA error $O_{\rho,\eta,k}(q^{-k})$ for fixed $\rho,\eta,k$, sufficiently large $n$, and $q\ge n^{k+1}$, with agreement loss $n^{1-1/k}$.

papers.title: Computing extensions of flag-jump t-modules
papers.abstract: We study Anderson t-modules whose positive-degree coefficient matrices admit a flag-jump basis and extend the t-reduction algorithm to this setting. We prove that these t-modules are abelian, with motive rank equal to the sum of their jump degrees. If $\Phi$ has jump degrees $j_1,\ldots,j_d$ and $deg_\tau\Psi<\min_s j_s$, we compute the t-module structure on ${\mathbf{Ext}}^1_\tau(\Phi,\Psi)$, its subgroup ${\mathbf{Ext}}_{0,\tau}(\Phi,\Psi)$, and the associated exact sequence. The construction allows nonzero nilpotent constant terms and includes the strictly pure case. When $\Psi$ is the Carlitz module, $N_\Phi=0$, and all jump degrees are at least two, the construction yields a dual t-module. We give complexity bounds for the algorithms and implementations in SymPy and Mathematica.

papers.title: Data-driven non-contiguous photon-energy groups for fast multigroup radiation transport in line-dominated plasmas
papers.abstract: Radiation transport in line-dominated plasmas, such as extreme ultraviolet (EUV) light source plasma, laser-fusion hohlraums, and stellar interiors, needs too many photon-energy groups for accurate radiation-hydrodynamic simulations. Our data-driven method assigns the bins of an opacity table to $K$ non-contiguous groups with fixed spectral shapes that never couple. Existing multigroup codes can use it by replacing the opacity this http URL a radiation-hydrodynamic code, 30 such groups replaced 151 conventional groups; the energy conversion efficiency from laser to EUV changed by less than 0.5\% in absolute value.

papers.title: Sensing frequencies at the discrete Grover-Heisenberg limit using a single qubit
papers.abstract: We consider a fundamental quantum sensing task: detecting weak oscillating fields with unknown strength and frequency. Recent work by Allen et al. established a fundamental lower bound on the required sensing time, which they named the "Grover-Heisenberg limit", and gave a protocol attaining this limit. The protocol relies on auxiliary qubits, which are used to run Grover's algorithm as a subroutine, leaving open the question of whether a single sensing qubit can achieve the same scaling. We show that a single qubit suffices for a discrete version of this problem in which the frequency belongs to an arbitrary, but known, finite set of candidate frequencies. Our protocol's sensing time grows only as the square root of the number of candidate frequencies. We prove that this square-root dependence, which we refer to as the "discrete Grover-Heisenberg limit", is optimal in the worst case.

papers.title: Three-dimensional dopant depth determination from momentum-resolved core-loss 4D-STEM data
papers.abstract: Moving beyond specimen-projected micrographs in scanning transmission electron microscopy to determine a three-dimensional distribution of dopants is of vital importance for materials characterization and development. Within the Born approximation, Fourier transformation over probe position of a momentum-resolved core-loss 4D-STEM dataset reveals fringes whose frequency encodes the dopant's distance from the focal plane. We address two principal challenges which arise under experimental circumstances. First, fringe contrast is degraded by dynamical scattering, but can be partially recovered by acquiring off major zone axes. Second, the excessive doses typical of core-loss scattering can be alleviated using a Bayesian framework which, on a simulated Fe-doped strontium titanate, achieves nanometre to sub-nanometre depth precision from 100 to 1000 core-loss counts, depending on the signal-to-background.

papers.title: Spectra of gcd-graphs over a matrix ring
papers.abstract: In this short note, we calculate the spectra of gcd-graphs defined over a matrix ring. Using character sums, we show that this calculation can be reduced to certain counting problems. In particular, when the underlying ring is a matrix ring with coefficients in a finite field, we calculate these spectra explicitly. We will also show that two gcd-graphs over the same matrix ring are isospectral if and only if they have the same generating set.

papers.title: Discovery of a likely supermassive neutron star in a remarkably wide binary
papers.abstract: Supermassive neutron stars ($M \gtrsim 2\ M_{\odot}$) provide stringent constraints on the equation of state of dense matter. We report the discovery of a wide binary system composed of a red giant star and an invisible companion with an orbital period $P\approx 1218\pm3$ days and a comparatively low eccentricity $e\approx 0.09\pm0.01$ (with $1 \sigma$ uncertainty). By combining radial velocity measurements from the Large Sky Area Multi-Object Fiber Spectroscopic Telescope and the Apache Point Observatory Galactic Evolution Experiment (APOGEE) with astrometric data from {\it Gaia} DR2 and DR3 catalogues, we derive a Keplerian orbit with an inclination angle $i\approx73^{\circ}\pm11^{\circ}$. The unseen companion has a mass in the range of 1.8--2.8 $M_{\odot}$ (spanning the full spread of all estimates), with a best-fit value of $2.20^{+0.14}_{-0.13}$ $M_{\odot}$. This potentially places the unseen companion within the mass gap between neutron stars and black holes. Spectral disentangling using high-resolution near-infrared APOGEE spectra shows no absorption features from an additional component, suggesting the presence of a compact object: either a supermassive neutron star or a low-mass black hole. The wide, low-eccentricity orbit is difficult to explain through standard binary evolution channels, pointing to the need for improved theoretical models to account for such systems.

papers.title: Feedback-induced mechanical bistability and perpendicular-domain formation in active elastic tissues
papers.abstract: Contractile fibers in muscle tissues are highly aligned over the scale of many cells. Muscle layers surrounding organs with an inner lumen are often arranged in orthogonal directions. Here, we study a minimal mechanism of how structural order and its patterning into orthogonally aligned domains can emerge from mechanical feedback alone. The central idea is that contractile fibers align in the direction of the local active and elastic stresses, a feedback motivated by the maturation of muscle fibers under tension. We thus model muscle tissue as an active nematic solid with stress feedback: an elastic medium with embedded contractile fibers that are reinforced along the directions of the local tissue stresses. We find that the feedback from the contractile fiber stress is self-amplifying and drives spontaneous fiber alignment. Feedback from the elastic stress couples the alignment to the mechanical boundary conditions and tissue geometry. Depending on the mechanical boundary conditions, the elastic-stress feedback stabilizes two orthogonally aligned tissue states, resulting in a structurally and mechanically bistable tissue that shows a hysteretic stress-strain response. In spatially extended tissues, this bistability gives rise to orthogonally aligned domains separated by domain walls. Our results show that stress feedback can pattern structural order by coupling spontaneous alignment to the tissue geometry. Our mechanism thus provides a purely mechanical route to orthogonal fiber patterning in muscle tissues.

papers.title: Spontaneous mechanical patterning in active elastic tissues with stress feedback
papers.abstract: The active mechanics of biological tissues is often governed by embedded active contractile fibers responding to mechanical feedback. We introduce a minimal model of a solid-like tissue where the mechanics is controlled by feedback of local active and elastic stresses on fiber organization. The resulting tissue generically exhibits a bistable response to external strain and spontaneously segregates into domains of orthogonally aligned fibers. Our theory thus provides a minimal mechanical feedback mechanism generating orthogonal structural alignment ubiquitous in biological tissues.

papers.title: Golod thresholds of ideals and products of ideals in dimension 3
papers.abstract: Let $I$ be a proper ideal in a standard graded polynomial ring $P$ with homogeneous maximal ideal $\m$. We show that there exists $k_0\in \mathbb{N}$ such that $\m^kI$ is Golod for all $k\geq k_0$. The smallest such $k_0$ is denoted $\mathrm{gt}_{\m}(I)$, and we call it the Golod threshold for $I$ over $\m$. We give an explicit formula for $\mathrm{gt}_{\m}(I)$ in the case when $I$ is a monomial complete intersection and bounds for $\mathrm{gt}_{\m}(I)$ for other classes of ideals. We also show that when $I$ is homogeneous, under a suitable degree condition, $\m^k I$ is Golod if and only if $k\geq \mathrm{gt}_{\m}(I)$, i.e., once Golodness is achieved, it cannot be lost. In the last section, we work in the setting of a regular local ring of dimension 3, and show that the product of any two proper ideals is Golod; this resolves a question posed by Dao and De Stefani \cite[Question 4.5]{dao2022monomial} and VandeBogert \cite[Question 4.11]{vandebogert2022products}.

papers.title: Cubic fourfolds with a symplectic involution from finite Prym data
papers.abstract: We reconstruct smooth cubic fourfolds with a symplectic involution through classical interpolation of smooth plane conics from five distinct points, or four with their cross-ratio. If the quadratic coefficient map has rank three and the fixed cubic surface has trivial automorphism group, five polarized anti-invariant Jacobian factors of smooth Eckardt sections suffice, or four with their parameters. Both bounds are optimal. By contrast, in rank two we construct two-dimensional families of equivariantly nonisomorphic fourfolds with the same entire unparametrized Prym image. The factor family also has an integral projective Lagrangian closure in an associated OG10 compactification.

papers.title: Tracing Galactic Dust Reddening with Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbon Emission: SPHEREx Observations of the North Ecliptic Pole
papers.abstract: We investigate the ability of SPHEREx observations of the $3.3$ $\mu$m polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) emission feature to trace Galactic dust reddening. Applying a spectral template-based method to SPHEREx data, we measure the strength of the $3.3$ $\mu$m PAH feature in each $6''.2$ pixel of a $22^{\circ}$ by $22^{\circ}$ region centered on the north ecliptic pole (NEP). We convert the PAH feature strength to reddening by applying a radiation field correction and a linear scale factor. The resulting $E(B-V)$ map is consistent with far-infrared, stellar, and HI-based reddening maps at arcminute scales, exhibiting a typical $E(B-V)$ difference of $\lesssim 7$ mmag. A galaxy count test finds that all reddening maps have a dispersion of $\approx11$ mmag in $E(B-V)$ relative to what would be needed to produce spatially uniform galaxy counts. While there is some evidence that reddening is overestimated by our map at high PAH abundances, this effect is smaller than the uncertainties on the applied radiation field corrections and limited to $\sim$10 mmag in the most extreme regions of the NEP. For a diffuse, high Galactic latitude region like the NEP and at the sensitivities of our validation metrics, the SPHEREx PAH-emission based reddening map matches the accuracy of existing reddening maps while being capable of accessing a higher angular resolution of $\sim6''$.

papers.title: Additive Relations and Betti Growth in Goldbach Rings
papers.abstract: The binary Goldbach ring over a field $k$ is the quotient of $R=k[x_p:p\text{ an odd prime}]$ by the relations $x_px_q=x_{p'}x_{q'}$ whenever $p+q=p'+q'$, with $\mathrm{deg}( x_p )=(p,1)$. We prove that if $g$ is a map from the odd primes to an abelian group and $g(p)+g(q)$ depends only on $p+q$, then $g(p)=g(3)+\frac{p-3}{2}(g(5)-g(3))$ for every odd prime $p$. This settles Kátai and Phong's conjecture on shifted prime arguments and proves, for odd primes, the affine classification they conjectured for binary sums. The universal group of binary prime relations is free of rank two. We obtain a minimal bigraded free resolution from compatible resolutions of finite truncations and determine the growth of its linear Betti numbers in two regimes. For fixed monomial degree $d\ge3$, as the Goldbach degree $n\to\infty$ through $n\equiv d\pmod2$, we prove $\beta_{d-1,n,d}\sim(d-1)T_d(n)/d!$, where $T_d(n)$ counts ordered representations by $d$ odd primes. Explicit Koszul cycles from common prime shifts span a positive fraction of this strand. For finite supports $\mathcal{A}_m=\{p\le m:p\text{ an odd prime}\}$, fix the homological degree $i\ge1$ and sum over all Goldbach degrees. As $m\to\infty$, the linear-strand totals are asymptotic to $i|\mathcal{A}_m|^{i+1}/(i+1)!$ when all binary relations on $\mathcal{A}_m$ are retained, and to $(1-2^{-i})|\mathcal{A}_m|^{i+1}/(i+1)!$ when only relations of common weight at most $m$ are retained. These leading estimates are uniform over fields. The interpolation theorem gives eventual depth at most two for the variable truncations; both truncation families have asymptotically maximal projective dimension.

papers.title: A Neural Physics Solver for Richards Equation
papers.abstract: A new approach to discretise and solve Richards equation based on the finite element method (FEM) is presented. The novelty of the approach, called the Neural Physics method, is that it expresses the discretisation as a convolution neural network (CNN) whose weights are predetermined by the integrals of the basis functions in the FEM. The Neural Physics method is physically consistent as it represents a discretisation of the governing equation and can run on CPUs, GPUs and the latest AI accelerators, resulting in an increase in computational speed. The Neural Physics method is demonstrated for two different discretisations of Richards equation, including a multigrid method that is realised through a U-Net architecture. The accuracy and speed of these methods is tested on a problem with a known analytical solution and compared to a standard FEM, and shows that the Neural Physics method is almost an order of magnitude faster than a comparable FEM. Finally, the Neural Physics method is applied to a real-world test case with integrated experimental data and simulates the infiltration of water through a rain garden. This new approach therefore provides a route to efficiently and accurately solve Richards equation for a wide array of hydrological applications.

papers.title: Low-energy spectral-window truncation for compact U(1) lattice gauge theory
papers.abstract: We establish a nonasymptotic electric-flux truncation bound covering the entire vacuum-relative low-energy spectral window of the original pure compact $U(1)$ lattice Hamiltonian. Formulated on a three-dimensional periodic cubic lattice with $N\geq3$ sites per direction at $\theta=0$ in the gauge-invariant zero-global-flux sector, our factorial-squared tail-norm estimate applies uniformly to every normalized vector in the window without requiring physical eigenvalue isolation, a window-edge gap, or nondegeneracy, and carries no window-dimension factor. This uniform control bounds ordered low-energy eigenvalue and excitation-energy errors while governing finite-time hard-wall evolution initialized from each state's normalized projection. Within this model, an analytic finite-volume strong-coupling construction certifies a nonvacuum band and an order-one coherent plaquette signal change that persists under a specified finite cutoff. The window estimate further provides precision-dependent sufficient cutoffs, a polar-decomposition linear isometric encoding for reference-entangled inputs, and readout bounds for the local electric square. Under lattice refinement at fixed positive bare coupling, physical volume, window width, and evolution duration, cutoffs scaling as $\beta\log N/\log\log N$ with $\beta>2$ drive the state and bounded-readout truncation errors to zero.

papers.title: Zero-sum Ramsey numbers of forests, cycles and complete bipartite graphs
papers.abstract: For a graph $G$ and $m\ge2$ dividing $e(G)$, the zero-sum Ramsey number $R(G,\mathbb Z_m)$ is the least $N$ such that every $\mathbb Z_m$-labeling of $E(K_N)$ contains a copy of $G$ whose edge labels sum to zero. We disprove the Bialostocki--Dierker asymptotic conjecture for forests by constructing trees for every sufficiently large edge count whose ratio of zero-sum to two-color Ramsey numbers has lower limit at least $554/553>1$. For powers of two $q\ge2$, we characterize all $s,k\ge1$ satisfying $R(K_{s,kq},\mathbb Z_q)=s+kq$ and prove $R(mK_{q,q},\mathbb Z_m)=2qm+m/\gcd(m,q)-1$ for every $m\ge2$. The packing upper bound combines Caro's transfer inequality with our spanning result and sharpens earlier bounds when $\gcd(m,q)\ge4$. The formula also gives exact values for counterexamples to Caro's defect conjecture, whose failure was already implicit in earlier work of Caro and Caro--Provstgaard. For every integer $m\ge2$ and every multiple $\ell$ of $m$ with $\ell\ge100m^3$, we also prove $R(C_\ell,\mathbb Z_m)=\ell+m/\gcd(m,2)-1$ for the cycle $C_\ell$ on $\ell$ vertices, determining the eventual value left by the bounds of Chi and He for even moduli $m\ge4$.

papers.title: NuSTAR view of the NGC 4151 corona: thermal balance and astroparticle constraints
papers.abstract: I present a comprehensive analysis of all publicly available NuSTAR observations of the nearby Seyfert galaxy NGC 4151 (2012--2024). The hard X-ray continuum is well described by thermal Comptonization in a hot corona, with electron temperatures $kT_{\rm e} \approx 40-125$ keV and optical depths $\tau \approx 0.4-1.2$ (slab geometry). A clear anti-correlation between $kT_{\rm e}$ and $\tau$ is observed, consistent with a thermostat behavior with constant Compton parameter $\gamma \approx 3.12$ calculated according to Sunyaev and Titarchuk (1980). Variability on timescales of hours constrains the size of the emitting region to $R \approx 250-1200 r_{\rm g}$, corresponding to moderate compactness values $\ell \lesssim 4$. The source occupies the same region of the compactness--temperature plane as other local Seyferts, with no evidence for pair runaway. I then explore two astroparticle implications. The IceCube neutrino excess reported toward NGC 4151 corresponds to $L_\nu/L_X \approx 0.3\%$, an energetically negligible contribution that does not alter the observed coronal energy balance. An additional injection of pairs from the hypothetical X17 boson cannot produce significant changes, unless the injection rate exceeds the photoproduction one, but no anomalies were found in the present data set. The NuSTAR data thus provide no evidence for either a significant neutrino cooling channel or an X17-related pair injection in the corona of NGC 4151.

papers.title: On Algebraic LNE models of complex affine algebraic curves
papers.abstract: We give a sufficient condition for an affine complex curve to have an algebraic complex LNE model.

papers.title: Accelerating matrix-free fast diagonalization and preconditioned linear solvers for high-order finite element discretized elliptic problems on distributed GPUs
papers.abstract: The time to solution of an iterative solver depends on the number of iterations and the cost per iteration. This paper develops algorithms that reduce both for elliptic problems discretized with high-order continuous finite elements on distributed GPUs, implemented in a unified matrix-free code supporting CUDA, HIP and SYCL. A distributed direct fast-diagonalization (FD) Poisson solver provides exact solutions on tensor-product meshes with direction-wise grading and coefficients varying along one coordinate direction. Its tensor data remain distributed, moved between slab layouts using collective transposes or kept in place by a Schur-complement approach. A two-level hybrid Schwarz preconditioner with FD cell solves (HS-FD) is extended to 2:1 hanging-node octrees with exact local cell inverses, while a p-multigrid preconditioner with Chebyshev--Jacobi smoothing (CJ-pMG) resolves hanging-node constraints at every level within fused kernels. Both approaches exploit FP32, where cell shapes and coefficients allow, within an FP64 conjugate-gradient iteration, adaptively select replicated or distributed coarse levels, support block solves for multiple right-hand sides and determine all parameters from the operator without case-specific tuning. Comparisons with Jacobi-preconditioned conjugate gradients (Jacobi PCG), MFEM, nekRS and this http URL span uniform, graded and octree meshes, layered coefficients, and four applications across NVIDIA, AMD and Intel GPUs. The direct solver is two to three orders of magnitude faster than Jacobi PCG on uniform meshes. HS-FD converges in 11 iterations for the generalised Poisson problem on octree meshes across 8 to 1024 MI250X graphics compute dies. These results provide practical guidelines for solver selection based on mesh structure and coefficient characteristics.

papers.title: Ultra-high-energy cosmic rays require metal-rich sources
papers.abstract: The elemental composition of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays (UHECRs) must be evaluated at a given rigidity rather than energy to compare with candidate elemental abundances, such as those of low-energy cosmic rays seeding the acceleration of UHECRs. We determine the UHECR composition from fits to Pierre Auger Observatory data and evaluate the resulting abundances at fixed rigidity. We identify two classes of solutions consistent with measurements above $10^{17.8}$ eV: one in which the hydrogen flux at Earth is dominated by secondary nucleons produced by photodisintegration of heavier nuclei in extragalactic photon fields, and a second in which this contribution is less pronounced. Only the latter, which yields a mixture of primary and secondary protons at Earth, allows a hydrogen abundance at the source comparable to that of low-energy cosmic rays. However, both classes of solutions require an overabundance of nuclei in the silicon-iron group. Other source models from the literature also fail to reproduce the full elemental composition. The metallicity of UHECRs thus differs markedly from that of all candidate seed populations considered, leaving the origin of the heavy-element excess unresolved.

papers.title: Maximal Violation of Mermin Inequality for Commuting von Neumann Algebras and Multipartite Vacuum Entanglement in QFT
papers.abstract: Summers and Werner proved that Bell inequalities are violated maximally and generically in the vacuum of a relativistic quantum field theory in [S. J. Summers and R. Werner, Commun. Math. Phys. 110 (1987), 247-259]. Their criterion concerns two-party case, that is, there are two algebras of quantum observables: one algebra and its commutant. In this case, the maximal CHSH value is converged to in every normal state exactly when the algebra is strongly stable. In the paper, we study the corresponding question for three and more mutually commuting von Neumann algebras. We focus on the multipartite Mermin inequalities instead of CHSH ones. For the tripartite Mermin functional we show that maximal violation in every normal state is equivalent to the existence of a common sequence of asymptotic GHZ stabilizers. Strong stability of each local factor is an necessary condition for maximal violation, and a joint embedding of an infinite GHZ tensor product is sufficient. Counterexamples show that strong stability and type III_1 of the individual algebras, even together with tripartite duality, do not suffice to arrive at the maximal violation. The results are also extended to n>=3 parties.

papers.title: The distribution of $αp$ modulo one in short intervals
papers.abstract: For any real number $x$, let $\|x\|$ denote the distance from $x$ to the nearest integer, and let $\alpha$ be any irrational number. We prove that there exist infinitely many $X$ such that for $Y=X^\gamma/2$ with $7/12<\gamma\le 1$ and $0<\theta<\min \{(12\gamma-7)/24, 1/9\}$, there is a prime $p$ satisfying $$ \|\alpha p\|<X^{-\theta},\quad X-Y<p<X. $$ Moreover, we obtain an asymptotic formula for the number of such primes. In particular, if $\alpha$ has a continued fraction expansion with bounded partial quotients, then this asymptotic holds for all sufficiently large $X$. Our result extends the admissible range of short intervals in the corresponding theorem of Baier and Roy from $2/3<\gamma\le 1$ to $7/12<\gamma\le 1$, reaching Huxley's classical range for primes in short intervals, and also improves the exponent $\theta$ for $2/3\le \gamma\le 3/4$. The improvement is obtained by adapting a recent result of Maynard, Pandey, and Radziwiłł on exponential sums over primes.

papers.title: Sample complexity of learning fermionic and bosonic Gaussian states with single-copy and entangled measurements
papers.abstract: With single-copy measurements, every mixed fermionic Gaussian state on $m$ modes, pure modes included, is learned to trace distance $\epsilon$ from $\Theta(m^3/\epsilon^2)$ copies, with no logarithmic factor, against the known $\Theta(m^2/\epsilon^2)$ for collective measurements. We prove the upper bound, resolving Conjecture 10.1 of arXiv:2609.23189 (lower bound for $\epsilon\le1/3600$), and fill most open entries of the sample-complexity table of fermionic and bosonic Gaussian states, for single-copy, $k$-copy and collective measurements. With blocks of $k$ copies, the covariant highest-weight measurement of arXiv:2611.07271 , read out through the Weyl-shift estimator, is exactly unbiased for every state; it gives $\Theta(\max\{m^3/k,m^2\}/\epsilon^2)$ in Frobenius norm on all states and in trace distance on every class at a fixed distance from the pure boundary. The gain $1/k$ ($k\le m$) away from the pure boundary, against $1/\sqrt k$ on cold number-conserving states, is therefore attained. Learning a quadratic fermionic Hamiltonian in Frobenius norm from its Gibbs state at bounded $\beta\|h\|$ has the same rate. For bosonic Gaussian states with bounded covariance, any displacement and squeezing, and occupations $n_1\le\dots\le n_m$, $O((m^2+r^3+\sum_{i,j>r}1/(n_i+n_j))/\epsilon^2)$ single-copy measurements suffice, $r$ the largest index with $r\,n_r\le2$; this is the minimax rate on dyadic-interval classes, with no spectral gap or cold-mode count assumed, and holds with no covariance bound for displaced passive states. With no bound on energy or squeezing, non-Gaussian measurements learn centred one-mode states, mixed included, from $O(\epsilon^{-2})$ and centred pure $m$-mode states from $O(m^2/\epsilon^2)$ single copies, free of the $\log\log E$ term of Gaussian measurements, and $m$-mode states from $O(m^3/\epsilon^2)$ copies, entangled only in a first round on blocks of $4m+6$.

papers.title: A dual-moment phenomenological framework for gravitational,electromagnetic and strong interactions
papers.abstract: The unification of fundamental interactions remains an outstanding open problem in fundamental physics. Most existing unification schemes rely on extra dimensions, exotic symmetries, or unobserved dynamical degrees of freedom. Here we construct a minimal classical phenomenological framework built on primitive charges and motion-induced kinetic dual moments. Gravitational, electromagnetic, and strong interactions are coherently formulated within a unified inverse-square-law structure. We postulate a universal coupling relation connecting source-charge couplings and moment-mediated couplings across these interaction sectors. Although weak-charge degrees of freedom can be formally accommodated within the formalism, full quantitative treatment of weak-interaction dynamics is left for future work. The model recovers well-established low-energy limits for planetary orbits, atomic systems, and heavy-quark hadrons. Importantly, it yields distinguishable corrections to light deflection by rapidly spinning compact objects, and three independent experimental schemes are proposed to test these predictions.

papers.title: AHEADance: Anticipatory Humanoid Dance from Streaming Audio
papers.abstract: A humanoid that dances to streamed music must commit each motion chunk before it has heard the music that chunk accompanies, and must continue from motion it has already committed. We present AHEADance, a robot-native streaming dance generator executed on a humanoid robot by a whole-body tracker. ListenAhead conditions each chunk on heard music and a frozen music model's forecasts of the coming music, aligned to their target times and weighted by reliability. The forecasts carry the timing of upcoming beats almost as well as the actual future; with them, the generator is better synchronized with the music and concentrates more motion energy at its song's beat frequency. Commit Forcing trains continuation from the model's own committed chunks, updating both the latent history and the decoded boundary of the next chunk; it reduces low activity from 83.5% to 10.3%, the level of real dance. Three music evaluators, each validated on real G1 dance, test synchronization, song and style. On a physical Unitree G1, it dances while the music plays and comes to rest when it stops, without a fall. Project page: this https URL

papers.title: Challenging the hoop conjecture with spinning pancakes and baguettes
papers.abstract: Understanding when gravitational collapse produces a black hole remains a central challenge in general relativity. Black-hole uniqueness results characterize the stationary endpoint under suitable assumptions, while singularity theorems establish geodesic incompleteness in the presence of trapped surfaces and appropriate energy and global conditions. Neither, however, provides a general criterion for horizon formation. The hoop conjecture offers such a criterion by relating the enclosed mass to the compactness of a matter distribution in every direction. We construct axisymmetric families of initial data describing rotating dust and test a formulation of the conjecture adapted to this setting. We explore highly prolate and oblate configurations with both constant and differential rescaled angular-velocity profiles, including configurations near the threshold for apparent-horizon formation. We find that the conjecture holds for rotating configurations, with a coefficient within 14% of unity as in the nonrotating case, provided the quasilocal mass includes the rotational energy. If the irreducible mass of the apparent horizon is used instead, the deviations grow with spin, as they do for Kerr black holes. For horizonless configurations, the conjecture likewise holds when the mass is restricted to the energy enclosed by the matter surface, whereas using the ADM mass, which also includes rotational field energy outside the matter, leads to apparent violations of up to $\approx$25%. We also discuss the possible evolution of compact configurations without apparent horizons, their relation to weak cosmic censorship, and their implications for horizonless compact objects.

papers.title: Patch LegONet: Resolving Localized High-Frequency PDE Dynamics with Low-Frequency Operator Blocks
papers.abstract: Localized interfaces, layers, and shocks can require high spatial resolution even when most of a partial differential equation (PDE) solution remains smooth. In global spectral methods, resolving these features requires increasing the approximation order across the entire domain. LegONet builds PDE solvers from reusable mechanism blocks, but its global coefficient representation faces the same limitation. We introduce Patch LegONet, which reuses pretrained mechanism blocks on smaller physical patches to resolve localized fine scales. The solution consists of a global background and local corrections. Mapping a fixed reference representation onto smaller patches increases local resolution without enlarging the blocks. The corrections join smoothly to the global background at patch boundaries. Differential operators are rescaled analytically to account for each patch's physical size. Nonlinear mechanisms are evaluated on the combined solution to include interactions between the background and local corrections. Patches can move, merge, or be removed during rollout while the pretrained patch blocks remain frozen. Six experiments on Allen-Cahn and viscous Burgers equations assess static, multiple, and moving patches in one to three dimensions. At comparable numbers of degrees of freedom, Patch LegONet consistently lowers the final relative solution error compared with global refinement. The reduction is approximately one order of magnitude in most tests. These results extend mechanism reuse across spatial scales and provide a practical route to local refinement in learned PDE solvers.

papers.title: marineGeochemFoam: A multipurpose framework for simulating reactive transport and biogeochemical cycling in marine sediments and at seawater-groundwater interfaces
papers.abstract: We present marineGeochemFoam, an open-source reactive transport modeling framework for simulating early diagenesis, sediment burial, submarine groundwater discharge, and biogeochemical cycling in marine sediments and groundwater-seawater transition zones. The code is implemented in the widely used numerical toolbox OpenFOAM and extends the capabilities of the existing diagenetic models by supporting, among other features, i) coupled reactive transport of dissolved solute and solid species, (ii) a flexible native reaction package, supporting arbitrary reaction networks with n-th order and Monod-type kinetics, and (iii) coupling with an external geochemical code, PHREEEQC, providing access to a wide range of thermodynamically based geochemical processes. We benchmarked different features of the code across various examples with increasing complexity. Successively, the code was applied to two case studies reproducing field observations from the Hanko groundwater discharge site, Finland, and the Santa Barbara Basin, California. Beyond diagenetic applications, the code also serves as a general-purpose reactive transport simulator.

papers.title: Distributed Global Pose Synchronization for Heterogeneous Multiple Rigid Body Systems on SE(3)
papers.abstract: This paper addresses the problem of global pose synchronization for heterogeneous multiple rigid-body systems evolving on the matrix Lie group $\SE(3)$. We first construct a new potential function on $\SE(3) \times \mathbb{R}$ with a generalized non-diagonal weighting matrix, together with a set of switching variables governed by continuous-discrete hybrid dynamics. Based on this new potential function and these switching variables, we propose a distributed hybrid feedback control scheme that uses relative pose on $\SE(3)$ and group velocity measurements, endowed with global asymptotic stability guarantees. We then further propose a distributed velocity-free hybrid feedback control scheme that uses relative and absolute pose measurements, without requiring group velocity measurements, while preserving global asymptotic stability. Numerical simulations are presented to demonstrate the performance of the proposed distributed hybrid control schemes.

papers.title: Adding unbounded and not bounded sets to a singular cardinal
papers.abstract: This paper solves a problem (SP) attributed to Solovay in the 1960s, which is to add an unbounded sequence to a singular cardinal $\kappa$ without adding bounded subsets to $\kappa$, while preserving $\kappa^+$. The solution applies to any cofinality of the singular cardinal, with the assumption that $\kappa$ is a strong limit needed for the case of uncountable cofinality. Unsuccessful attempts to solve (SP), mostly for the countable cofinality, have appeared in published papers by various authors.

papers.title: The Cool Circumgalactic Echo of the Stellar-to-Halo Mass Relation
papers.abstract: The stellar-to-halo mass relation (SHMR), a key prediction of galaxy formation models, peaks at $M_* \sim 3 \times 10^{10}\,M_\odot$. This scale is often attributed to circumgalactic baryonic feedback processes, however, direct observational evidence linking the two remains scarce. Using Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) galaxy--quasar pairs, we map the cool circumgalactic medium (CGM) using Mg II $\lambda\lambda2796, 2803$ absorption with stacking technique across nearly three decades in stellar mass. The radial Mg II absorption equivalent-width profile, $W_{\rm MgII} \propto D^k$, becomes progressively shallower with increasing stellar mass, following $k = 0.70\log(M_*/M_\odot)-9.12$. Crucially, we find that the $W_{\rm MgII}$ in the CGM scales tightly with the SHMR. The $W_{\rm MgII}$ peaks at the same characteristic mass as the SHMR, coinciding with a transition of the cool CGM from super-virial to sub-virial kinematics. Low-mass halos show excess non-gravitational motions consistent with recycled accretion and feedback-driven circulation, whereas massive halos show halo-centric heating that may maintain star formation quenching. This study bridges the gap between cool CGM and SHMR, showing that peak star formation efficiency coincides with the most abundant cool CGM reservoirs.

papers.title: Thermodynamics of Kerr-Newman-Bertotti-Robinson black holes from background subtraction
papers.abstract: The non-asymptotic flatness of the charged rotating black holes immersed in the Bertotti-Robinson magnetic field causes the ambiguity in the gauge choice for the time generator and the electric potential. By using the newly established form of the integrability condition together with the gauge choice for the asymptotically flat charged rotating black holes as the initial condition, we have found that the gauge can be uniquely fixed. With this fixed gauge, we further obtain the mass and angular momentum by the background subtraction method with the Minkowski spacetime as the reference spacetime. As a result, not only is the first law of black hole thermodynamics as well as the quantum statistical relation automatically satisfied, but also both the Christodoulou-Ruffini relation and the Smarr formula are obeyed.

papers.title: Shape Holomorphy of the Calderón Projector on Lipschitz Surfaces: Frequency-Explicit Bounds for the Helmholtz Operator
papers.abstract: We establish the holomorphic dependence of the Calderón projector for the Helmholtz operator upon shape boundary deformations of a family of bounded Lipschitz domains in two and three spatial dimensions, with bounds explicit in the wavenumber and the size of the holomorphic extension. More precisely, after transporting the four boundary integral operators contained in the Calderón projector to a fixed reference boundary, we prove that the resulting parameter-to-operator maps admit bounded holomorphic extensions in their natural fractional Sobolev spaces. Unlike approaches that require boundary regularity of class $\mathscr C^{1,1}$ or higher, our argument traces the holomorphic dependence on the shape by transferring elliptic estimates to the boundary through the fundamental solution and the Dirichlet and conormal trace operators. This construction is the key step that allows us to treat Lipschitz-regular boundary deformations. Furthermore, we show that the domain of holomorphy can be chosen independently of the wavenumber $\kappa$, while the operator bounds in the corresponding fractional Sobolev spaces contain algebraic factors in $\kappa$ multiplied by $\exp(C\kappa\delta)$. In particular, for real domains, corresponding to $\delta=0$, our single layer estimate recovers, to our knowledge, the best available frequency dependence on general Lipschitz boundaries. For the double layer, adjoint double layer, and hypersingular operators, we obtain novel frequency-explicit bounds. The results proved in this work provide the analytic foundation for frequency-explicit uncertainty quantification, model order reduction, and high-dimensional approximation of boundary integral operators, their Galerkin discretizations, and the resulting boundary densities and quantities of interest on families of parametrically varying boundaries.

papers.title: Harmonic origin of local symmetry breaking in PbTe revealed using machine-learned potentials
papers.abstract: We use machine-learned interatomic potentials combined with higher-order interatomic force constant models to show that finite-range polar correlations in PbTe are driven by long-range harmonic interactions rather than lattice anharmonicity. Our molecular dynamics simulations reveal a spatial polar correlation range exceeding 50 Å at low temperatures and decreasing with increasing temperature. Selective interatomic force constant mapping demonstrates that crystal anharmonicity usually associated with the formation of polar nanoregions suppresses polar correlations. Instead, long-range harmonic interactions extending to 13 Å are necessary to reproduce the spatial coherence of local dipoles. In reciprocal space, these extended harmonic interactions correspond to high curvature of the transverse optical (TO) phonon branch at the $\Gamma$ point. Comparison with isostructural NaCl connects these extended interactions to local underscreening of predominantly Coulombic forces. Our results provide a key microscopic description of finite-range polar correlations and a framework for understanding local symmetry breaking in centrosymmetric materials.

papers.title: That Time of the Year Again: Government Pay Revisions in the Aggregate Economy
papers.abstract: Public pay is set by law in nominal terms, so inflation erodes its real value between legal acts until the government revises it. I model each revision as the choice of a forward-looking government, shaped by two costs that push in opposite directions. A fixed cost of acting makes revisions large and rare, whereas a convex cost of financing the increase at once makes them small and frequent. Through the budget, each revision also moves debt and the risk of fiscal stress under which the next one is made. In the documented pay decisions of eleven countries, pay set at discretion erodes against prices and private earnings and is restored in discrete steps, every cut was decided during market stress or an adjustment program, and court rulings drove a wedge between the cuts legislated, the cuts paid and the cuts that lasted. Estimated on the legal acts, the model reproduces the documented paths of pay in most countries when data and simulations are measured the same way. In Portugal's estimated model, the savings that the Treasury requires once spreads rise produce the cuts, the debt overhang holds pay down after the crisis, and a court that strikes cuts after they take effect invites cuts it will strike. Review of cuts before they took effect would have lowered the social cost of Portugal's crisis relative to review after the fact, and partial indexation would have paid in Bangladesh unless its automatic increases were costly to finance.

papers.title: Distinguishing thyroid nodule malignancy using digital palpation
papers.abstract: Accurate pre-operative diagnosis of thyroid nodules remains a major clinical challenge. Current diagnostic techniques rely on fine-needle aspiration and demonstrate high rates of inconclusive results, often leading to avoidable thyroidectomies with lifelong implications. Here, we introduce a mechanics-based diagnostic method that leverages Digital Palpation to determine malignancy and identify tissue subtypes in human thyroid nodules. From a cohort of patients undergoing thyroidectomies, we evaluated ex vivo thyroid specimens and processed the resulting mechanical data from 36 tests in 10 thyroid nodules. Principal Component Analysis reveals that these experimental results are distributed within a three-dimensional space of interpretable scalar features reflecting tissue grittiness, strength, and toughness, which map closely to descriptions of malignant and benign nodules given by clinicians. Our results further demonstrate that malignant nodules exhibit distinct mechanical signatures compared to their benign counterparts. This revealed a statistically significant difference (p = 9 x 10^-4) and separability (95% lower-bound Hedges' g = 1.08) between benign and malignant nodules along a direction in principal component space representing effective stiffness. Preliminary clustering patterns were also observed among malignant subtypes, including follicular, oncocytic, and papillary thyroid carcinomas. Together, these results highlight the potential of Digital Palpation as a novel mechanics-based method for tissue characterization and motivate its further development toward diagnostic applications.

papers.title: Direct product geometries in $n$-dimensional linear and quadratic gravity
papers.abstract: Direct-product spacetimes offer a tractable route to exact solutions in gravity theories beyond general relativity. We study $n$-dimensional direct-product spacetimes of $(m_1+m_2)$, $(2+m)$, and $(2+\ldots+2)$ type in linear gravity and general pure quadratic-curvature gravity, allowing the two-dimensional subspaces to have nonconstant curvature. We classify the resulting solution spaces and determine how the allowed geometries depend on the gravitational theory, the dimension, and the curvature couplings. Metrics containing two-dimensional part(s) of nonconstant curvature are governed either by algebraic conditions on a curvature profile, or, in one special class of quadratic gravity, by a differential equation. Relations governing metrics with only constant-curvature $m$ dimensional subspaces are purely algebraic. We compare the two considered theories and study relations between their solution sets. We further examine conformal relations, generalized Petrov types, and compatibility with electromagnetic sources. Four- and six-dimensional cases are analyzed in detail, and so is the Weyl squared action (that reduces to Weyl conformal gravity in $n=4$), as a particular example of quadratic gravity couplings. Explicit analytic solutions illustrating the resulting structure are presented whenever possible.

papers.title: Forelli--Rudin Type Operators in Infinite Dimensions, I
papers.abstract: We introduce Forelli--Rudin-type integral operators on the open unit ball of \(\ell^2\). We completely characterize the boundedness of these operators between weighted \(L^p\) and \(L^q\) spaces for all \(p,q\in[1,\infty]\), as well as their membership in every Schatten class of operators between the corresponding weighted \(L^2\) spaces. We also establish trace formulas for these operators that cannot be obtained from their finite-dimensional counterparts by a formal passage to the limit as the dimension tends to infinity. Our results are not merely infinite-dimensional extensions of those obtained by Cheng, Fang, Wang, and the second author (2017), Zhao and Zhou (2022), and Ding (2022). Rather, they reveal new phenomena that are unique to infinite dimensions and arise from the fundamental geometric and measure-theoretic differences between finite- and infinite-dimensional spaces. A key ingredient in our proofs is the establishment of new Forelli--Rudin-type asymptotic estimates in infinite dimensions. These estimates also provide new insights into the development of function theory on the infinite-dimensional unit ball.

papers.title: An iterated-logarithm price of anytime validity for log-optimal e-processes
papers.abstract: Log-optimal e-variables at fixed horizons, also called numéraires, have been conjectured to ``almost'' form an e-process for exponential-family null hypotheses. A related open question is whether an e-process can attain the optimal e-power at every horizon up to a bounded loss. Given a final horizon, we study the minimax regret of e-processes relative to the numéraires at all times up to it. For the Gaussian location null and the composite alternative of Gaussian distributions with a smaller variance and an unknown location, we show that the minimax regret in the worst case over the location grows like the iterated logarithm of the final horizon. A single e-process attains this rate at every horizon. This growth answers the question negatively. It also refutes the conjecture if ``almost'' means a regret bounded uniformly over horizons. For this Gaussian location problem, we thus exhibit the frontier precisely: the minimax regret is bounded if and only if the alternatives have at least the variance of the null.

papers.title: Thermochemical Rossby waves in rapid rotation: from swallowtail geometry to nonlinear selection
papers.abstract: When heat and solute both destabilise a rapidly rotating fluid, do their buoyancies add? Codensity models assume so, giving a straight onset diagonal; spherical shells show curved and kinked thresholds. We study the Busse-Simitev rotating annulus, whose normal modes obey an exact complex cubic dispersion relation. Combining the Bilharz criterion with the neutral-curve envelope yields, in the rapid-rotation limit, an explicit swallowtail wave front, in Arnold's sense, that bends the codensity diagonal into smooth and then kinked thresholds as the diffusivity ratio decreases. Its cusp edges lie inside the unstable domain and its exposed kink ends at the swallowtail singularity; these are singularities of wave-number selection, without coalescence of temporal eigenvalues, and the swallowtail diffusivity ratio has analytical small- and large-Prandtl-number limits. At a kink, broad, fast thermal and narrow, slow compositional Rossby waves become neutral together; hidden arcs mark the birth and merger of unstable wave-number bands. The same geometry enters nonlinear selection: mean-scalar feedback factors through neutral-arc normals and scalar responses, so the mean-profile coexistence margin is positive at every corner of the leading front and vanishes quadratically with the kink angle as the waves merge. Complete cubic coefficients predict robust coexistence at a reference corner and a narrow bistable interval near merger. Periodic-cell simulations away from merger confirm the coexisting waves and their invasion thresholds.

papers.title: Derived invariance of holomorphic two-forms and homological motives of stably holomorphically symplectic varieties
papers.abstract: Let $\Phi:D^b(X)\to D^b(Y)$ be a derived equivalence between smooth projective complex varieties, and let $h=c_1(L)$ for an ample line bundle $L$ on $X$. For $z\in\mathbb C$, transporting the cup-product action and evaluating at $e^{zh}$ gives a homomorphism of graded algebras $\Theta^\bullet_{F,z}:H^\bullet(Y,\mathcal O_Y)\to H^\bullet(X,\mathcal O_X)$, where $F$ is the cohomological transform of $\Phi$. We prove that $\Theta^\bullet_{F,i}$ is an isomorphism in degrees one and two. In particular, $X$ and $Y$ have the same number of holomorphic two-forms. The proof in degree two uses the Hodge-Riemann bilinear relations on $X$ and on $X\times X$. We also prove that being stably holomorphically symplectic is a derived invariant, where a smooth projective variety is called stably holomorphically symplectic if it is a direct factor of a smooth projective holomorphic symplectic variety. For derived-equivalent varieties in this class, we construct an isomorphism of rational homological motives as unital algebra objects. In particular, their graded rational cohomology algebras are isomorphic compatibly with the Hodge structures.

papers.title: Combinatorial Invariants for Metacyclic Groups
papers.abstract: We study product-one invariants of finite metacyclic groups, with particular attention to metacyclic $p$-groups. For semidirect products $C_n\rtimes C_m$ such that $\operatorname{ord}_n(\ell)=m$ and $\operatorname{ord}_q(\ell)=m$ for every prime divisor $q$ of $n$, we give a short proof of the known formula for the small Davenport constant and determine the exact value of the $\eta$-constant.
