We also develop a fast cross-validation approach for model selection and calibration of predictive uncertainty for treatment effects. We use simulations to examine when pooling helps or harms imputation and cross-validation to assess whether probabilistic modeling improves accuracy in multiple empirical applications.

papers.title: Does the Escape Fraction Prescription Shape Reionization History and Morphology?
papers.abstract: The escape fraction of ionizing photons, $f_{\rm esc}$, is among the least constrained quantities of the Epoch of Reionization (EoR), and intergalactic opacity prevents its direct measurement at high redshifts. We constrain three power-law parameterizations, $f_{\rm esc}(z)$, $f_{\rm esc}(M_{\rm h})$, and $f_{\rm esc}(z, M_{\rm h})$, against JWST UV luminosity functions and EoR observables (ionizing emissivity, neutral hydrogen fraction, and Thomson optical depth) using Markov Chain Monte Carlo, with priors allowing $f_{\rm esc}$ to increase or decrease with redshift and halo mass. We propagate the best-fit models into the semi-numerical simulation SimFast21 and compare their ionization morphology and 21 cm power spectra with a constant-$f_{\rm esc}$ model. All models reproduce the observations with nearly identical global reionization histories. The data favor $f_{\rm esc}$ decreasing with redshift, from $\approx 0.8$ at $z = 5$ to $\approx 0.35$ at $z = 15$. The halo-mass-only model prefers $f_{\rm esc}$ increasing with halo mass, but this trend is a proxy for redshift evolution. When both dependencies vary jointly, the data prefer a mass-independent $f_{\rm esc}$. At matched global neutral fraction, all four prescriptions yield similar ionization morphology, and the 21 cm power spectra agree to within $\approx 10\%$. Thus, once calibrated against the same observations, the details of the $f_{\rm esc}$ prescription, set by interstellar medium physics, largely average out in both global observables and the 21 cm power spectrum. Distinguishing them may require statistics beyond the power spectrum, such as Ly$\alpha$ and 21 cm forest sightline statistics, or forecasts that exploit their small differences in reionization timing.

papers.title: Minimal Alt(6)-modules with additive dimension on characteristic not 3
papers.abstract: This article takes place in the extension and generalization proposed by Corredor, Deloro and Wiscons of the works of Dickson and Wagner regarding the Classification of minimal $\text{Sym}(n)$- and $\text{Alt}(n)$-modules. In particular, we classify the minimal faithful $\text{Alt}(6)$-modules with an additive dimension in characteristic not 3. We also highlight the remaining work needed to complete the classification of minimal faithful $\text{Alt}(n)$- and $\text{Sym}(n)$-modules with an additive dimension.

papers.title: Holographic Approaches to Hadron Structure
papers.abstract: We give an introduction to and an overview of holographic approaches to QCD and hadron structure. After an introduction to the string-theoretic foundations of holographic QCD, we review the predictions of top-down and bottom-up models for the phenomenology of mesons, baryons, and glueballs. We focus on the top-down model following from probe flavor branes in the Witten model of low-energy Yang-Mills theory and, in the more phenomenological approach of bottom-up models, mostly on minimal models based on five-dimensional anti-de Sitter space, which also implement global symmetries and their anomalies consistently, but allow the high-energy behavior to better match real QCD.

papers.title: 2-generation of Chevalley Lie algebras over finite fields
papers.abstract: In this article, we prove that every split simple Chevalley Lie algebra over a finite field of characteristic $p\neq 2$ of classical types $B_n$, $C_n$, and $D_n$, and exceptional types $G_2$, $F_4$, $E_6$, $E_7$, and $E_8$, is $2$-generated. Combined with the result of Cantor, Jezernik, and Zozaya for the classical type $A_n$ [Two-generation of traceless matrices over finite fields, Linear Algebra Appl. (2025)], this establishes $2$-generation for all split simple Chevalley Lie algebras over finite fields of characteristic $p\neq 2$.

papers.title: A discontinuous Galerkin method for biharmonic Dirichlet control problems with patch reconstruction
papers.abstract: In this paper, we present and analyze an interior penalty discontinuous Galerkin method for Dirichlet boundary control problems governed by the biharmonic equation, with the control imposed through the normal derivative. The method is based on a reconstructed discontinuous approximation that admits an arbitrarily high-order approximation space with only one unknown per element. We construct a discretization that approximates the state and adjoint state in this space and derive a priori error estimates in the energy and $L^2$ norms. The analysis is carried out under the limited regularity available on polygonal domains by means of a medius argument. Numerical experiments are provided to support the predicted convergence rates.

papers.title: Bayesian Model Comparison for Nonlinear State Space Models without Posterior Sampling
papers.abstract: Marginal likelihoods are central to Bayesian comparison of nonlinear state space models, but commonly used estimators require posterior simulation for each model, with computational costs that grow with the sample size $T$. We propose a deterministic estimator that requires no posterior simulation. A grid filter integrates out the latent states, and a Laplace approximation with a second-order correction integrates over the static parameters. Under derivative-growth and posterior-concentration conditions, the corrected Laplace approximation has error $O(T^{-2})$, and the size of the correction indicates the error that remains. In stochastic volatility experiments, the estimator is more accurate than Chib's method, the Gelfand--Dey estimator and importance sampling with a fitted proposal at equal computing time for $T\geq 2{,}000$. Applications to two exchange rates and to $T=19{,}266$ five-minute stock returns provide the strongest support for heavy-tailed observations and a transitory volatility factor.

papers.title: Results for distinct covering systems with a prime minimum modulus $q \ge 11$
papers.abstract: We prove that if the smallest modulus of a covering system is a prime $q \ge 11$, then the sum of the reciprocals of the moduli is at least $1+10^{-33}$. This improves on a previous more general bound of the first two authors in this particular case. We also show that it is impossible to construct a covering system using distinct multiples of $q$ as moduli. Finally, we show as a corollary that it is impossible to construct $10$ distinct covering systems with the property that no modulus is used in more than one of the covering systems.

papers.title: Minimum Extension Degrees for Reed-Solomon Codes:Exact Values and a Quadratic Transition
papers.abstract: We study the minimum extension degree of Reed-Solomon codes admitting exact linear repair of every failed coordinate from any $d$ surviving coordinates at the cut-set bound. Write $s=d-k+1$, and let $Q_s(n)$ be the minimum product of $n$ pairwise coprime integers, each at least $s$. We locate the transition for the formula $sQ_s(n)$ near $n=d^2$: for every fixed $0<\varepsilon<1$ and sufficiently large $d$, the formula is exact up to $(1-\varepsilon)d^2$, whereas strict improvement is possible at every length at least $(1+\varepsilon)d^2$, uniformly over the base field and code dimension. The lower bound follows from an inequality for the cost of residual prime powers; the upper bound follows from an existing affine-plane construction. We also show that the full-helper coordinate-count bound is attained over sufficiently large base fields. Finally, nonlinear repair at cut-set equality induces linear repair over the prime field. Thus the degree bounds over that field remain valid, and the same transition holds when the repair base field is prime.

papers.title: On the Characterization Problem for Krull Monoids with Homocyclic Class Group
papers.abstract: This paper addresses a central problem in the factorization theory of Krull domains in which every class contains a prime divisor. It is well-known that the system of length sets depends on the class group only and the question is whether this system carries enough information to recover the underlying class group. We give an affirmative answer for all homocyclic class groups $C_n^r$. More precisely, let $D$ be a Krull domain with class group $C_n^r$, with $n, r \in \mathbb N$, and suppose that each class contains a prime divisor. If the system of length sets $\mathcal L (C_n^r)$ is equal to a system of length sets $\mathcal L (G)$, for any finite abelian group $G$ with $\mathsf D (G) \ge 4$, then $G \cong C_n^r$. The central tools are cross numbers of (minimal) zero-sum sequences over the class group.

papers.title: Yb/Sr optical clock comparison at 2.08E-18 uncertainty over a 1350-km fiber link
papers.abstract: Redefining the International system of Units (SI) second requires independent frequency-ratio measurements between clocks based on different laboratories, with an overall uncertainty below 5E-18, to validate individual clock evaluations through consistency checks. Reaching this uncertainty over long distances has remained challenging. So far, comparisons at this level have been achieved only a few times, between co-located clocks, and their results disagree markedly. Previous high-precision comparisons have therefore been limited to local or kilometre-scale links. Here we compare a ytterbium optical lattice clock in Wuhan with a strontium optical lattice clock in Shanghai over a phase-stabilized fiber link spanning 1350 km, and determine the Yb/Sr frequency ratio to be 1.207 507 039 343 337 716 0(26), with a Bayesian statistical uncertainty of 1.14E-18 and a total uncertainty of 2.18E-18. To our knowledge, this is the first intercity long distance frequency-ratio measurement, whose total uncertainty reaches the level required by the redefinition roadmap. The measured ratio exhibits a significant correlation with Earth tides and its response agree with the model within the statistical uncertainty. At intercity scale, this comparison demonstrates the capability of an optical-clock network for frequency comparison and Earths gravitational-potential sensing, a key step toward a wide-area optical-clock network.

papers.title: Symplectic capacities and Weyl laws from Abelian Higgs min max theory
papers.abstract: For a Hermitian line bundle $E\to Y$ over a Riemannian manifold $(Y^n,g)$, the self-dual Abelian-Higgs energy is defined by $\mathcal{E}^Y_{\varepsilon,g}(u,a)=\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_Y \left(|\nabla_a u|_g^2+\varepsilon^2|F_a|_g^2+ \frac{(1-|u|^2)^2}{4\varepsilon^2}\right)dV_g$, where $u$ is a smooth section of $E$, $a$ is a unitary connection, and $F_a$ is its curvature. Pigati and Stern studied the energy as a codimension-two analogue of the Allen-Cahn energy to study minimal submanifolds in a Riemannian manifold. In this paper, we use this functional to define a nondecreasing sequence of symplectic capacities $\{c_k^{\mathrm{AH}}\}_{k\ge1}$ in dimension four by a min-max construction. In particular, we prove that $c_1^{\mathrm{AH}}$ is normalized on the ball and the cylinder. For the upper bound on the cylinder, we combine Gromov's theory of families of $J$-holomorphic spheres with Taubes's planar vortex. For the lower bound on the ball, we use the properties of the Abelian-Higgs theory developed by Pigati-Stern, together with a geometric estimate on smooth approximations to the double of the ball and an equivariant deformation of low energy sublevels. These estimates give the normalization without Seiberg-Witten theory. We then use Seiberg-Witten moduli spaces on $\mathbb{CP}^2$ and $S^2\times S^2$ to prove an upper bound on the higher capacities of balls and the formula $c_k^{\mathrm{AH}}(Z^4(a),\omega_0)=ka$. We also prove Weyl laws for domains in $\mathbb{R}^4$, both for the capacity sequence and for the min-max sequence with the standard Euclidean metric. For these results, we construct AH sweepouts from moduli spaces of the solutions to the perturbed Seiberg-Witten equations.

papers.title: Extrinsic Curvature Estimation by Closest Point Projection of Rays
papers.abstract: We propose a parametrization-free method that estimates the principal curvatures and principal directions of a submanifold of $\mathbb{R}^d$ from the closest point projections of a few random rays, without coordinate charts or local fitting. The projection of a ray induces a curve on the submanifold, which is a geodesic only in special cases, so its curvature is in general not a curvature of the submanifold. The velocities of these curves, however, relate to the derivative of the closest point projection, whose eigenpairs carry the information of the principal curvatures and directions. Finite differences along $d$ rays can estimate them without relying on the normal information at a cost of $\mathcal{O}(d^3)$ besides the projections, and we provide error bounds. The method extends to submanifolds of any codimension and to point clouds, and experiments confirm the predicted rates in up to $128$ dimensions.

papers.title: Magnetic billiards: duality and magnetic Radon property
papers.abstract: We study Birkhoff magnetic billiards inside convex planar domains for a constant weak magnetic field. We prove that there exists a functional family of centrally-symmetric convex billiard tables satisfying the so-called magnetic Radon property. These are tables which have a rotational invariant curves consisting of $4$-periodic orbits with the rotation numbers either $1/4$ or $3/4$. These billiard tables can be constructed in a neighborhood of circles. However in our construction we do not use perturbation methods but rather some topological argument for the system of ODEs governing the magnetic Radon property. In contrast with this result we consider the magnetic billiard tables having discrete rotational symmetry for the angle $2\pi/k, k\in\mathbb{Z}$. We prove that in this case a rotational invariant curve consisting of $k$-periodic orbits exists, if and only if the billiard table is circular. We develop several tools, which, we believe, are important for other aspects of magnetic billiards. The first is the "magnetic duality" which enables to work with the dual object---the outer magnetic billiard. Secondly, we find the generating functions of outer magnetic billiard, both the ''standard" and the "non-standard" ones.

papers.title: Maximizing Measures for Subadditive and Almost-Additive Potentials on Countable-Alphabet Subshifts
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of maximizing measures for subadditive and almost-additive families of upper semicontinuous, bounded-above potentials $\mathcal F=\{f_n\}_{n\geq1}$ on closed subshifts over countable alphabets. Under a coercivity condition on $f_1$, we prove that every maximizing sequence, that is, $\{\mu_k\}_{k\geq1}\subset\mathcal M_\sigma(X)$ satisfying $\bar{\mathcal F}(\mu_k)\to\beta(\mathcal F)$, is uniformly tight, preventing mass from escaping to arbitrarily large symbols. As a consequence, a maximizing measure exists. We apply these results to matrix cocycles, establishing the existence of invariant measures that realize the joint spectral radius for countable families of matrices.

papers.title: Agent-guided epitope excision enables economical de novo binder design
papers.abstract: De novo protein design campaigns remain bottlenecked by the inference compute time required to generate and rank candidates, limiting wider functional exploration. Here, we introduce and evaluate an epitope excision approach that truncates targets to local interface windows to accelerate both backbone diffusion and structure prediction. Across 15 targets and 3,666 designs, excised windows closely reproduced full-target binding interfaces (median C\alpha RMSD of 0.37 Å) and made it practical to design binders against the 719-residue extracellular domain of fibroblast activation protein alpha (FAP) by cutting RFdiffusion and AlphaFold3 GPU time by ~ 88% in one of the epitopes. Pairing this workflow with an agentic optimization loop allowed the system to autonomously identify catalytic-site targeting strategies. Under a fixed compute budget, a human-in-the-loop (HITL) workflow raised the computational hit rate from 5.06% to 9.33% while further cutting GPU hours by ~ 42%. We also found that omitting target multiple sequence alignments during refolding roughly substantially increased the apparent yield. Wet-lab validation with yeast display identified nanomolar binders from the generated designs with the HITL and the fully autonomous agent (human-out-of-the-loop, HOOTL) arms recovering more enriched designs than the PI-alone baseline. Together, target excision and agent-guided search offer a practical way to scale de novo binder design to large, therapeutically relevant proteins.

papers.title: Pesin's entropy formula on attractors with continuous invariant splittings
papers.abstract: We consider an attractor $\Lambda$ of a $C^1$ diffeomorphism of $\mathbf M^d$ with a trapping neighborhood $U$ and an extendable continuous invariant splitting $T_{\overline U}\mathbf M^d=E\oplus F$. Under quantitative asymptotic hyperbolicity assumptions, we prove the existence of hyperbolic ergodic invariant probability measures on $\Lambda$ that satisfy Pesin's entropy formula and have negative Lyapunov exponents on $E$ and positive exponents on $F$. No dominated splitting is required on the attractor. Our results apply to mostly expanding partially hyperbolic systems and to systems with separated Lyapunov exponents under suitable statistical assumptions. For $C^{1+\alpha}$ diffeomorphisms, the resulting measures are SRB measures, and the corresponding sets of asymptotically hyperbolic points are covered, modulo Lebesgue null sets, by the basins of at most countably many such measures. We give necessary and sufficient criteria for the existence of ergodic SRB measures with these exponent signs in terms of derivative growth and orbit statistics, and characterize the relationship between physical measures, strongly observable measures, physical-like measures and such SRB measures. We also construct examples with unique hyperbolic SRB measures of full support on attractors admitting no nontrivial dominated splitting, demonstrating the applicability of our criteria beyond results that require domination.

papers.title: Corner Regularity and Asymptotics for the Two-Dimensional Radiation Transport Equation
papers.abstract: The regularity of solutions to the two-dimensional radiation transport equation plays a central role in understanding the behavior of scalar flux near geometric corners. In a previous study of Kaper's corner singularity problem, the physical transport kernel was decomposed into its principal inverse-distance singularity and a lower-order remainder, reducing the corner asymptotic analysis to the question of whether the scalar flux possesses sufficient continuity to justify differentiation of the associated singular potential. The required regularity, however, remained unresolved. In this paper, we establish a sharp modulus-of-continuity estimate for the scalar flux generated by the physical transport kernel and prove the estimate $\omega_{\phi}(h)=O\!\left(h\log(D/h)\right)$, which implies Dini continuity. This estimate yields absolute convergence of the fluctuation term arising in the differentiated principal potential and permits a rigorous differentiation formula for transport solutions. Using this regularity framework, we derive the fixed-angle asymptotic behavior of the scalar flux and its first derivatives near a rectangular corner. For every fixed interior ray, the gradient exhibits logarithmic growth, while the scalar flux admits an $r\log(1/r)$ correction with an explicitly identified coefficient determined by the corner values of the flux and source. The analysis shows that a rectangular corner does not generate a singularity stronger than the logarithmic first-derivative singularity already present in smooth-boundary transport theory. Numerical calculations on benchmark problems are consistent with the theoretical predictions. These results provide a rigorous resolution of the regularity issue underlying Kaper's corner singularity problem and establish a mathematical framework for corner asymptotics in two-dimensional radiation transport.

papers.title: Off-diagonal hypergraph Ramsey numbers
papers.abstract: For $n,r\in\mathbb{N}$ with $r\geq 3$ and an $r$-graph (i.e., an $r$-uniform hypergraph) $H$, the Ramsey number $R(H,n)$ is the smallest $N\in\mathbb{N}$ such that every red/blue coloring of the hyperedges of the $N$-vertex complete $r$-graph $K_N^{(r)}$ contains either a red copy of $H$ or a blue copy of $K_n^{(r)}$. For every integer $r\geq 3$, we characterize all $r$-graphs $H$ for which $R(H,n)$ is polynomial in $n$. Explicitly, we prove a conjecture of Conlon, Fox, Gunby, He, Mubayi, Suk, Verstraëte, and Yu, that $R(H,n)$ is polynomial in $n$ if and only if $H$ is isomorphic to a subgraph of a lexicographic power of $K_r^{(r)}$. This concludes an extensive line of work initiated by Erdős and Hajnal in 1972 on characterizing the polynomial growth of off-diagonal hypergraph Ramsey numbers.

papers.title: Physics-informed neural network (PINN) approximations of capillary menisci in polygonal channels
papers.abstract: A capillary interface must satisfy both its curvature equation and the contact angle at the container walls. We study how strong-form physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) approximate these conditions when the prescribed equilibrium is geometrically incompatible. In zero gravity, the Concus-Finn critical contact angles for spanning graphs in square and equilateral-triangular cross-sections are respectively 45 degrees and 60 degrees. Below these angles, classical subdomain flux balance yields a certified lower bound on the continuous combined interior and wall residual loss, retaining the sampling densities and wall weight. The subdomain bounds and their sums over disjoint regions tend uniformly to zero as the contact angle approaches the threshold from below at fixed wall weight. The computed PINNs return smooth graphs with finite axial extent in the nonexistence regime: small interior residuals coexist with corner wall-flux deficits, where the adjoining contact-angle conditions demand more flux than a finite-slope graph can supply. At the default wall weight, several degrees into this regime, neural losses computed by quadrature are 1.6-1.8 times the bound from one cut per corner, with higher ratios occurring near the critical angle. Polynomial least-squares comparisons support the same geometric interpretation in a second smooth trial family. The bound supplies a physical scale for the residual compromise and explains why residual assessment must include wall flux and continuum compatibility.

papers.title: Evidence for Kaluza-Klein excitations of the graviton, gluon and quark at LHC
papers.abstract: Following our paper showing evidence for a tower of Kaluza-Klein gravitons, we interpret the massive 4 jet excesses observed by CMS. They could come from the decay of two heavy KK gluons gkk(3.6TeV) and gkk(8.6TeV) into pairs of KK quarks qkk(1TeV) and qkk(2.1TeV). Present limits on gkk into top pairs seem to exclude gkk(3.6TeV) but these limits assume a dominant decay into top pairs, which can be questioned as was the case in our study of KK graviton decays. The cross section predicted for gkk(8.6) requires a BR into a pair of qkk(2.1TeV) or order 10% which is not unlikely. We also discuss the issue of a hierarchy between the KK graviton masses and the vector boson masses and the solution provided by the RS multi-brane models. Prospects for reaching a 6 s.d. level local evidence with RUN3 data are promising for 3 channels. KK excitations of the Z boson are discussed and appear also promising. Indirect evidences for these particles are also presented.

papers.title: Adaptive Local Proper Orthogonal Decomposition via Graph Partitioning and Provable Error-Bounded Lossy Compression for Parametric Series in Finite-Dimensional Function Spaces
papers.abstract: We introduce a spatially adaptive proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) method for error-bounded lossy compression of snapshot data in finite-dimensional function spaces. The method combines hierarchical graph partitioning with independent low-rank approximations on spatial subdomains, allowing the local approximation ranks to adapt to the spatial distribution of information in the data. For partitions that are orthogonal in the discrete inner product, we establish an exact decomposition of the global squared weighted reconstruction error into local contributions and characterize the weighted-norm optimality and coefficient-space quasi-optimality of local POD approximations for fixed partitions and ranks. These results provide a rigorous mechanism for allocating a prescribed global error tolerance among subdomains and selecting the smallest admissible local ranks. We further develop a sufficient error bound for the coefficient-space normalized root-mean-square error (NRMSE). A greedy hierarchical refinement algorithm accepts a spatial subdivision only when it reduces the storage required by the local low-rank factors while preserving the prescribed reconstruction-error bound. The method is assessed using synthetic data and snapshot sequences from two- and three-dimensional compressible-flow simulations. The numerical results illustrate how spatially adaptive ranks and partitioning can improve compression relative to global POD and fixed spatial partitions, particularly when the data exhibit spatially heterogeneous dynamics.

papers.title: Conditional Reset-Enhanced Dissipative Quantum Metrology
papers.abstract: Open quantum sensors work either in a transient regime with finely timed readout or in a steady-state regime with robust but weaker sensitivity. To overcome this trade-off, we ask whether repeatedly resetting a probe to a fixed state, even a suboptimal one, can outperform the optimal single-shot transient protocol. We prove that blind resets, triggered by an external clock, cannot do so even with memory. Conditional resets, triggered by the probe's own state, break this no-go result by capturing parameter-dependent quantum jumps or by recycling heralded losses, for parameters encoded in dissipative rates and Hamiltonians alike. A three-level thermometer capturing thermal excitations outperforms the optimal no-reset protocol in both transient and steady-state regimes, even with a $40\%$ preparation error. Conditional resets can even saturate the ultimate bound of nonequilibrium thermometry with a single readout. Heralded recycling enables steady-state frequency estimation to outperform optimal transient Ramsey interferometry. The advantages extend to interacting probes and to elapsed-time estimation, and both mechanisms can be realized using established experimental techniques.

papers.title: Automated generation and execution of large-scale semidefinite programs for variational two-electron reduced density matrix theory
papers.abstract: The variational two-electron reduced density matrix (v2RDM) method provides a wave-function-free approach to the description of strong electron correlation whose computational cost scales polynomially with the number of correlated orbitals. Here, we present an automated pipeline for the generation and execution of semidefinite programs (SDPs) associated with the v2RDM problem. Algebraic constraints encoding ensemble $N$-representability conditions are generated via the p$^\dagger$q second-quantized algebra package, and the p$^\dagger$q-generated expressions are automatically translated into a sparse-matrix representation that can be digested by an appropriate SDP solver. We have implemented a boundary-point SDP (BPSDP) solver in the libsdp package that can execute the v2RDM SDPs on either CPU or GPU hardware. We apply the code in several contexts. First, two-particle conditions are used to describe the 76-orbital model of the iron-molybdenum cofactor (FeMoco) of nitrogenase, the simulation of which requires roughly 25 hours of compute time on a single Nvidia H100 GPU. Second, the performance of high-order (four-particle positivity) conditions is evaluated on a challenging two-dimensional H$_{10}$ cluster problem. Lastly, new classes of positivity constraints for mixed fermion-boson systems are generated and applied within the context of ab initio cavity quantum electrodynamics simulations.

papers.title: Resonant-pair energy return beyond the early Green-Kubo plateau in a quartic chain
papers.abstract: The Green-Kubo formula gives the thermal conductivity as the long-time limit of the running Green-Kubo integral, the time integral of the equilibrium heat-current autocorrelation function. In simulations, this integral often approaches a plateau at finite time. We study how it evolves after such an early plateau in a weakly coupled chain of quartic oscillators, where the plateau value is close to the rate at which independent neighboring cells exchange energy. Two neighboring cells with nearly equal frequencies form a resonant pair: their relative phase oscillates like a pendulum, and energy that has crossed the bond between them flows back. We show that, at weak coupling, the running integral of such a pair follows the pendulum trapping response of nonlinear Landau damping. For the quartic potential, the small-oscillation period of this pendulum, $T_{\rm lib}\propto\varepsilon^{-1/2}$ with intercell coupling $\varepsilon$, does not depend on energy, so all resonant pairs share one time scale. Without fitted parameters, the theory predicts that the running integral of an isolated pair falls to a negative first minimum of $-0.74$ times the plateau value at $0.952\,T_{\rm lib}$. Simulations of isolated pairs approach this prediction as the coupling decreases. In chains, the first minimum occurs on the same time scale but is shallower, and a small positive value can remain much later. Chains of strongly chaotic cells show no comparable decrease, and energy-conserving noise much faster than $1/T_{\rm lib}$ largely removes the decrease. The pair response provides a quantitative finite-time reference for interpreting early Green-Kubo plateaus in such chains.

papers.title: No braiding for quantum sl2 reps - A short proof
papers.abstract: We give a short and self-contained proof that the category of all finite dimensional representations of quantum sl2 is not braided. Moreover, we show that it is a braided module category over a suitable monoidal subcategory.

papers.title: Sparse-grid discretizations of BGG sequences
papers.abstract: For Bernstein--Gelfand--Gelfand (BGG) complexes, we develop the first sparse-grid finite element discretizations, for dramatically reducing the number of degrees of freedom used in tensor-product finite elements. Alpert wavelets and their first and second primitives yield compatible hierarchies of discontinuous, continuous, and continuously differentiable piecewise polynomials, that serve as one-dimensional ingredients of BGG sparse-grid finite elements. For the three-dimensional Hessian, elasticity, and div-div complexes, we construct a bounded commuting sparse-grid projection that yields stable discrete potentials, exactness and uniform inf-sup stability of associated mixed methods. Under mixed Sobolev regularity, we also prove sparse-grid approximation estimates with dimension-independent algebraic convergence rates in the number of degrees of freedom. Experiments for a three-dimensional incompatibility problem and a two-dimensional biharmonic problem on an annulus illustrate the efficiency of sparse grids relative to tensor-product finite elements.

papers.title: Low-field dephasing time of an optically polarized NV$^-$ spin bath beyond the P1 limit in diamond: a cluster-correlation-expansion and exact spin-bath study
papers.abstract: Dense ensembles of nitrogen-vacancy (NV$^-$) centres in nitrogen-rich diamond dephase on the electron spins of the substitutional nitrogen (P1) centres. If the paramagnetic nitrogen is instead converted into NV$^-$ centres, the laser that initializes the sensor also pumps the bath into $m_s = 0$, a state with no moment along its own axis. Using cluster-correlation-expansion (CCE) calculations with a dynamical mean field, combined with an exact solver for probe-bath exchange and with no adjustable parameter, this paper asks whether such an optically polarized NV$^-$ bath dephases a sensor more slowly than a P1 bath of the same density. The answer is set by the field. In a field along [111], three quarters of the bath centres lie off the field axis, and the moment of their $m_s = 0$ state along the field grows from 0.04 at 25 G to 0.46 at 300 G and 0.81 at 800 G. At 25 G the polarized bath is therefore nearly silent: at 0.57 ppm the dephasing time $T_2^*$ of a separately addressed $^{15}$NV$^-$ probe is 112 $\mu$s, six times the 18.0 $\mu$s of a P1 bath, and still 2.4 times at 90% polarization; an ensemble measurement gains a factor of two. At 300 G the advantage over P1 shrinks to 1.4, and at 800 G the polarized bath dephases faster than P1. The field dependence of every bath, P1 included, follows the mean moment of its centres along the field. For the Hahn echo, bath relaxation ($T_1$ = 6 ms) caps the gain: a $^{15}$NV$^-$ probe in a polarized bath reaches 1.5 times the P1 value at 25 G and 1.14-1.16 times at 300 and 800 G. Driving a single $^{14}$N hyperfine line at 25 G lengthens the ensemble $T_2^*$ to 38 $\mu$s ppm, four times the experimental P1 value, implying a 3.5-12-fold dc sensitivity gain over conventional diamond with 10-30% NV$^-$ conversion. Optical polarization of an NV$^-$ bath at low field therefore offers dephasing times beyond the P1 limit of nitrogen-rich diamond.

papers.title: A New Modifications of the Milstein and Euler Methods and the Taylor-Ito Expansion for Ito Stochastic Differential Equations with Drift and Diffusion Coefficients Having Non-Differentiable or Singular Time-Dependent Multipliers
papers.abstract: The article presents a new modifications of the Milstein and Euler methods for systems of Ito stochastic differential equations with drift and diffusion coefficients having differentiable and non-differentiable or singular power-law time-dependent components (the latter depending only on the time variable). By iteratively applying Ito's formula to the mentioned differentiable components of the drift and diffusion coefficients, a new modification of the Milstein method is derived in the paper. A key feature of this modification of the Milstein method is the presence of time-dependent weight functions in the iterated Ito stochastic integrals of the second and first multiplicity (the specified weight functions are identically equal to unity in the classical Milstein method). To approximate the specified iterated Ito stochastic integrals (with respect to the components of a multidimensional Wiener process) that involve time-dependent weight functions, the paper proposes using the method of generalized multiple Fourier series, introduced by the first author in 2006. The article also provides a modification of the Euler method and the Taylor-Ito expansion for Ito SDEs with non-differentiable or singular drift and diffusion coefficients. The convergence rates of the proposed modifications of the Milstein and Euler methods are established. A series of numerical experiments has been performed to confirm the theoretical results of this paper.

papers.title: JaxMARL-BC: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Macroeconomic Modelling, in Seconds
papers.abstract: Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) offers a principled way of populating simulated economies with many heterogeneous decision makers. Its adoption, pioneered in finance, has nonetheless been slow in macroeconomics because of two main limitations: the lack of a shared frame of reference connecting MARL systems to dynamic stochastic general equilibrium (DSGE) models the profession already trusts, and the very long training times. The first limitation was recently addressed by the Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Business Cycle (MARL-BC), which places deep RL households in a real business cycle economy and reduces to classic DSGE models in specific limits. Here we address the second limitation. We present JaxMARL-BC, a JAX-accelerated simulator that trains MARL-BC economies in seconds (between 75x and 724x faster than the reference implementation), and scales to 200,000 independent learning households. We verify its correctness against the known DSGE limits, characterise its scaling through a simple cost law, and demonstrate its value by a proof-of-concept calibration of an extended model with heterogeneous returns on capital, in a two-hour experiment that would previously have taken over a month. We release JaxMARL-BC as open source.

papers.title: CRAFT-ε: A Conformer-Resolved Atom- and Fragment-based Theory for the Static Relative Permittivity of Pure Organic Liquids
papers.abstract: The static relative permittivity is an important property in thermodynamic modeling, electrochemistry, and solvent design, but predicting it directly from molecular structure remains challenging because both electronic polarization and molecular dipole orientation contribute to the measured response. Here, we introduce CRAFT-{\epsilon} (Conformer-Resolved Atom- and Fragment-based Theory for {\epsilon}), a conformer-resolved molecular descriptor model for predicting the static relative permittivity of neutral pure liquids. Conformer free energies, molecular dipoles, and atom-resolved polarizabilities are obtained from a GFN2-xTB/ALPB 10 workflow. The molecular dipole is decomposed into chemically defined polar-fragment vectors, allowing fitted corrections to retain both the magnitude and relative orientation of local dipolar contributions. Electronic and orientational polarization are combined with a group-contribution molar volume in the Onsager-Kirkwood-Fröhlich relation. A staged parameterization with 41 parameters is applied to nonpolar, polar, and hydrogen-bonding compounds. For 1393 liquids with permittivities between 1.5 and 183, CRAFT-{\epsilon} reaches a five-fold cross-validated average absolute deviation of 2.40 ({R^2} = 0.93). Conformational averaging 15 is essential for liquids with several polar groups. Compared with an established fragment-based model with 139 parameters, it reaches a similar cross-validated RMSE (3.65 versus 3.41) with about a quarter of the parameters and applies to every liquid of the dataset. The resulting framework provides a computationally inexpensive route from molecular structure to liquid dielectric response and forms a basis for later application to solvent mixtures and electrolyte systems.

papers.title: Half-delocalization for semiclassical measures of split higher-dimensional quantum cat maps
papers.abstract: We study quantum cat maps on multidimensional tori and prove an optimal lower bound for the Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy of their semiclassical measures under the hypothesis that the dynamics splits over the rationals. This is the first instance of such a bound for a dynamical system with multiple positive Lyapunov exponents. The proof is based on a new notion of conditional quantum dynamical entropy and a careful study of the multiple Ehrenfest time adapted to the dynamics.

papers.title: Single-photon time qubit: Quantum-vacuum control and complementarity of the arrow of time
papers.abstract: Treating the arrow of time as a controllable quantum variable rather than a fixed external parameter is a central challenge in quantum physics. Recently, Bloch~\cite{Bloch2025} proposed the theoretical concept of a \emph{time qubit}, a two-level control space $\mathcal{H}_T=\mathrm{span}\{\ket{+},\ket{-}\}$ that selects between opposite Hamiltonian evolutions $\hat{H}_{\pm}=\hat{H}_0\pm\hat{V}$, but this paradigm has remained experimentally unrealized. Here we formulate the quantum-optical theory of a single-photon time qubit---uncovering quantum-vacuum control and complementarity of the arrow of time---and experimentally probe and validate its predictions using phase-resolved single-photon interferometry from two coherently seeded entangled nonlinear biphoton sources~\cite{Lee2018,Yoon2021}. First, we show theoretically and verify experimentally that a controlled $\pi$ pump--seed phase inversion during pair creation from the quantum vacuum flips the stimulated displacement generator $\hat{V}\to -\hat{V}$ on top of the spontaneous two-mode squeezing background $\hat{H}_0$, reversing the stimulated evolution time [$\hat{U}_{\mathrm{stim},-}(t)=\hat{U}_{\mathrm{stim},+}(-t)$] and enabling universal single-qubit $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ control and postselection-free first-order tomography on the temporal Bloch sphere. Second, we prove that spontaneous idler vacuum fluctuations record complete which-branch (temporal-direction) information whereas the shared coherent seed erases it without cascading or aligning the idler beams, establishing an exact wave--particle complementarity law $|\bm{r}|=\mathcal{V}=|\alpha|^2/(1+|\alpha|^2)$ for the purity of the arrow of time and enabling direct first-order measurement of the Loschmidt time-reversal echo.

papers.title: Graphexon Mean Field Games on Large Network Limits
papers.abstract: This paper analyzes graphexon mean field games (GXMFG) on large network limits. By considering edge distributions of a sequence of finite graphs, we define the empirical graphexon measures and study their subsequential weak limits in a graphexon space consisting of all symmetric probability measures on $[0,1]^{2d}$. This concept of network limits extends graphon theory to general, not necessarily dense, networks. To formulate the game using the graphexon limit, we exploit a useful property that a probability measure on a product space is the product of a probability kernel and a marginal distribution. Based on such graph limits and the probability kernel of the associated graphexon measure, we derive the GXMFG equations, and present a detailed analysis for the linear-quadratic case. For linear-quadratic models with finite populations residing over large networks, we use the GXMFG equations to construct decentralized strategies, for which an $\epsilon$-Nash equilibrium property is established.

papers.title: High-cadence GW astrometry in the $μ$Hz gap
papers.abstract: We forecast the sensitivity of a dedicated, fast-spinning astrometric survey to a stochastic gravitational-wave background (SGWB) in the microhertz gap between pulsar timing arrays (PTAs) and LISA. Spinning the satellite faster samples each star more often, raising the Nyquist frequency and opening higher frequencies at no cost in noise: the shorter, noisier exposures are exactly compensated by their number, so the white-noise floor of each position stream is independent of cadence. High frequencies are where astrometry is most competitive, because the deflection measures the strain directly: its strain noise is white, whereas the equivalent noise of pulsar timing grows as $f^2$. With a cross-correlation estimator over $N$ reference stars and the astrometric overlap computed in the distant-source limit, we find that a Gaia-like satellite scanning the ecliptic poles, with $N\sim10^4$ bright stars over $10$~yr, falls short of the background measured by PTAs by a factor $\sim\!60$. A larger, $8$-m-class aperture, or a constellation of satellites covering the whole sky, reaches it, while extending the reach continuously across the $\mu$Hz band.

papers.title: Mutually touching cylinders: Littlewood's seven, and at most ten in general
papers.abstract: We give a computer-assisted proof that at most seven congruent infinite circular cylinders in $\mathbb{R}^3$ can touch pairwise. This answers a question of Littlewood from 1968. For cylinders of arbitrary radii we prove the upper bound ten. Whether ten can be attained remains open.

papers.title: An Inverse Problem for the Moore Gibson Thompson Equation: Injectivity and Stability
papers.abstract: We study an inverse problem for the variable coefficient Moore Gibson Thompson (MGT) equation in a bounded domain, where the objective is to recover an unknown initial acceleration from boundary measurements of the acoustic field. We establish both injectivity and stability of the associated measurement operator. Injectivity is established through a unique continuation property by applying a theorem of Tataru for analytically principally normal operators. The argument relies on a factorization of the third order operator into wave type components, combined with Carleman estimates and propagation techniques in the spirit of Tataru. Stability is derived through a microlocal analysis of the forward operator, based on the construction of geometric optics approximate solutions and the identification of an elliptic pseudodifferential operator arising from microlocal back propagation of the data. These results connect the MGT inverse problem with the classical theory of hyperbolic inverse problems, such as photoacoustic tomography, while highlighting new features induced by the third order dynamics and damping.

papers.title: Vacuum-Field Squeezing by Molecules in Optical Cavities: An Exact Bound and Linear-Response Theory
papers.abstract: The ground state of a molecule coupled to an optical cavity contains virtual photons, and squeezing of the photonic field has been found in exactly solvable models, perturbation theory, and numerical calculations. Here, two exact sum rules for the field quadratures show that, within the dipole approximation, the vector-potential fluctuations of a linearly polarized mode never exceed their vacuum value in the ground state of any molecule at any coupling strength. Consequently, the field is squeezed whenever the mode couples to a dipole-allowed transition from a nondegenerate ground state, and the cavity-induced ground-state energy shift cannot increase with the cavity frequency at a fixed coupling vector, which is an exact constraint on approximate methods. Moreover, the incoherent photon statistics, which exclude the coherent part of the field, are never sub-Poissonian. At weak coupling, an exact resolvent expression reduces the squeezing and the ratio of the anomalous to the normal photon moment to linear-response properties of the isolated molecule, with the ratio set by a mean excitation energy. Time-dependent density functional theory with CAM-B3LYP and PBE0 reproduces exact and QED coupled-cluster references for both quantities to within 5% at 45 benchmark points. A survey of 29 molecules gives mean excitation energies of 9.5-21 eV at a cavity frequency of 2 eV and shows that the most polarizable molecules squeeze the field the most.

papers.title: The Exhaustive Peres Transform: Extraction and Universal Coding
papers.abstract: Run to exhaustion, Peres's iteration of von Neumann's procedure yields a bijection of {0,1}^N that splits every string into fair bits and a residual. The residual is self-delimiting and determines the number of ones, so the fair bits are exactly uniform given the residual under every exchangeable law. Each residual one accounts for a power of two of the weight of the input, and the residual of every input of length N has fewer than sqrt(3) N^0.793 ones. This sparsity gives a short proof, with an explicit remainder, that the fair bits per symbol tend almost surely to the entropy for Bernoulli sources and every finite alphabet. The Bernoulli likelihood factorises along the recursion, and code B, which codes the residual at plug-in biases, has the length of the two-part code. Code G gamma-codes the gaps of the residual, with no estimate and no arithmetic coder: on every string its length is at most the logarithm of the type class plus O(N^0.793 log N). What is more, a concatenation of J pieces costs its piecewise empirical entropy plus a term that is sublinear when J = o(N), without the cuts being sent. After a Burrows-Wheeler transform of the reversed string, both codes are universal for stationary ergodic sources: code B through a context tree of growing depth, with regret O(2^k log N) against Markov sources of order k, and code G with no tree, competing on every individual sequence with the empirical conditional entropy of every order. For laws invariant under permutations inside the pieces of a partition, the fair bits not mixed across the pieces are exactly uniform given everything else; after the BWT, the fair bits of every stationary source fall short of their length by o(N) bits of entropy, with an exponential tail for Markov sources. Experiments measure the finite-length price of these guarantees.

papers.title: Motility-Induced Phase Separation of Run-and-Tumble Particles under Local Stochastic Resetting
papers.abstract: We investigate the non-equilibrium stationary states of a one-dimensional active gas composed of run-and-tumble particles (RTPs) undergoing motility-induced phase separation (MIPS) and subjected to local stochastic resetting at the origin. Unlike global resetting, local resetting maintains a mass-injection flux at the origin while preserving large-scale spatial self-organization. We demonstrate that above a critical resetting rate $r_c$, the active system undergoes a transition toward a stationary two-phase state featuring a dense liquid droplet centered at the origin coexisting with a surrounding gas phase. Using kinetic evolution equations, we derive the exact steady-state density profile expressed in terms of the Lambert function. The size of the droplet has a non-monotonic dependence on the resetting rate $r$, and attains its maximum. Furthermore, we analyze the dynamical stability of the supersaturated gas phase and show that a nucleated droplet relaxes exponentially toward its steady-state size with a relaxation timescale of $1/r$. We extend our framework to model a finite resetting velocity, proving that the stationary droplet size is invariant with respect to the resetting velocity.

papers.title: Generalised Fluctuating Dynamic Density-Functional Theory: Derivation and Applications
papers.abstract: Classical density-functional theory (DFT) determines the equilibrium density distributions of complex many-body systems by bridging microscopic and macroscopic fluid descriptions via a free-energy variational principle. For time-dependent settings, dynamic DFT (DDFT) extends this formalism to govern the evolution of relevant order parameters, typically the number density. However, deterministic DDFT fails for mesoscopic systems far from equilibrium, where non-negligible thermal fluctuations require a stochastic extension: fluctuating DDFT (FDDFT). Here, we derive a generalised FDDFT from first principles, starting from microscopic Hamiltonian dynamics via systematic coarse-graining and Zwanzig's projection operator formalism. The resulting equations govern arbitrary observable fields driven by thermodynamic forces from a general entropy functional. These dynamics decompose into reversible, dissipative, and stochastic contributions, explicitly linked to microscopic mechanics via the Liouville operator, Green-Kubo relations, and the fluctuation-dissipation theorem, respectively. To delineate these coarse-grained descriptions, we show that ensemble averaging over fluctuations reduces our framework to a generalised macroscopic DDFT. Finally, we demonstrate the breadth of our formalism by applying it to two prototypical fluid classes. In the colloidal regime, it recovers the recently established colloidal FDDFT. For simple atomic and molecular fluids, we derive the non-isothermal Landau--Lifshitz fluctuating Navier-Stokes equations, providing a first-principles foundation for this classical phenomenological model and clarifying its statistical-mechanical assumptions.

papers.title: Uniform Confinement for One-Dimensional Pressureless Euler--Poisson: Existence and Asymptotics
papers.abstract: One-dimensional Euler-Poisson-type systems with interaction potentials that are attractive at long ranges serve as simplified models that describe aggregation phenomena. We prove uniform bounds on the positions and velocities of discrete sticky-particle solutions to such a system where the potential satisfies certain coercivity growth conditions, requiring the potential be only $C^{0, 1}_{\mathrm{loc}}$. When the potential is semiconvex, these bounds yield compactness of time-translated trajectories, which converge to a solution on all of $\mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R}$ of a simpler equation. Often, these limiting solutions possess substantial rigidity that determines the asymptotic behavior of the original solution, which we explore in a few applications. This method is robust with respect to the choice of potential, and in contrast to previous work does not require the solution operator to have a closed-form expression. As a corollary of our uniform bounds, we also obtain existence of solutions for non-semiconvex potentials, although such solutions may not retain stickiness.

papers.title: On The Manin Constant
papers.abstract: We prove the Manin constant conjecture for every optimal elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$ and Stevens' Conjectures I and II. Our method adapts Hongbo Yin's congruence argument for cubic roots of modular functions to lifts of modular parametrizations through isogenies, using the unbounded denominators theorem of Calegari, Dimitrov and Tang.

papers.title: Shifted quantum affine symmetric pairs: finite presentations and graded coideal structures
papers.abstract: Shifted quantum affine symmetric pair algebras were recently introduced as a trigonometric analogue of shifted twisted Yangians, whose truncations are expected to quantize fixed point loci in generalized affine Grassmannian slices. They are defined via a loop presentation with infinitely many generators and relations. In this paper, we consider anti-dominantly shifted quantum affine symmetric pair algebras of simply-laced split type. Our main result is a construction of a finite presentation à la Levendorskii. We apply it in type $\mathsf{A}$ to construct an embedding of a shifted quantum symmetric pair algebra into the corresponding shifted quantum affine algebra, yielding a graded coideal structure.

papers.title: The genus of a curve on Calabi-Yau threefolds
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth projective Calabi-Yau variety of dimension $3$, with Picard number one. Let $n$ be the self-intersection of the ample generator of the Néron-Severi group of $X$. Let $\mathsf{GV}_{g,d}$ be the Gopakumar-Vafa invariant of $X$ of genus $g$ and degree $d$. It is conjectured that {\it if $g>\frac{d^{2}}{2n}+\frac{d}{2}+1$, then $\mathsf{GV}_{g,d}=0$}. In this paper, we prove the implication when $d\gg n$ and $X\subset \mathbb P^r$ is a complete intersection in projective space. The vanishing follows by proving that if $C$ is a closed subscheme of $X$ of dimension $1$, arithmetic genus $p_a(C)$, and degree $d\gg n$, then $p_a(C) \leq \frac{d^2}{2n}+\frac{d}{2}+1$. Actually, we prove a somewhat more general result. In particular, we prove that $C$ is an extremal curve if and only if $C$ is the complete intersection on $X$ with a hyperplane $H$ and a hypersurface $F$, namely $C=X\cap H\cap F$. When $X\subset\mathbb P^r$ is not necessarily a complete intersection, assuming that the Picard group of $X$ is generated by the hyperplane section class, we obtain the coarse bound $p_a(C)\leq \frac{d^2}{2n}+\frac{d}{2}+\left(\frac{11}{24}n+4\right)$ for $d\gg n$.

papers.title: Topological Splitting of Sondheimer Oscillations in Thin-Film Weyl Semimetals
papers.abstract: We discuss topological effects on Sondheimer oscillations in the magnetoresistance of thin-film Weyl semimetals. The Sondheimer oscillations are periodic in magnetic field and originate from the commensurability between the film thickness and the cyclotron-orbit pitch. Using Boltzmann transport theory, we investigate the effects of Berry curvature and orbital magnetic moment on the oscillations. We find that the Sondheimer oscillations split into two branches with different frequencies and that each branch becomes chirped because its frequency depends on magnetic field. These features originate from the orbital-Zeeman-induced deformation of the Fermi surface. The same mechanism also applies to Dirac semimetals.

papers.title: Self-organizing recruitment cascades couple Levy search to a clustered maximum-entropy resource field
papers.abstract: Foraging recruitment is modeled as a contagion: an agent finding a resource triggers a linear-threshold cascade on the group's communication network. Because activation is degree-normalized, crowding shuts the cascade off, causing the swarm to aggregate on a resource and then disperse to explore again. Acting on the cascade moves agents in space, rewiring the network; recruitment and exploration are thus one coupled process, and removing this coupling alone abolishes self-limitation. Recruitment spreads only within a connectivity window bounded below by percolation onset and above by degree-blocking. The swarm self-organizes to the near-critical edge of this window--self-organized quasi-criticality--hovering near but below the critical point without settling onto a size-invariant critical state, with a finite-correlation-time activity spectrum (Lorentzian-like, not 1/f) consistent with local criticality. Recruitment raises harvest up to 2.7x over solitary search on sparse, clustered fields and loses (down to 0.37x) on abundant or uniform ones; because resources generically aggregate, the favourable regime is the common one. The Levy search and resource field are both least-committal: a maximum-caliber walk coupled to a maximum-entropy point process whose generic sign is clustered, with the optimal search exponent tracking the field's fractal dimension. Heavy-tailed Levy exploration crosses sparse voids while recruitment cascades exploit clusters by switching agents to short local steps, binding exploration and recruitment into a single self-organizing cycle.

papers.title: Interior caustics and rigidity near noncircular ellipses
papers.abstract: We prove local rigidity near every fixed noncircular ellipse from integrable rational caustics in an arbitrary nonempty open interval $I\subset(0,1/2)$ of rotation numbers. For each fixed $r>11/2$ and bound on the $H^r$ norm of the elliptic graph displacement, every sufficiently $C^1$-small positively curved perturbation admitting such caustics at all rational rotation numbers in $I$ is an ellipse. It suffices to assume these caustics at a suitably chosen family of rotation numbers in $I$ with any prescribed rational point of $I$ as its unique accumulation point. The key linear result classifies real $L^2$ displacements with phase-independent orbit sums at every rational rotation number in $I$ as infinitesimal ellipse deformations.

papers.title: Commutative exact superalgebras and super-modular tensor categories
papers.abstract: We consider the theory of commutative exact algebras in braided finite tensor categories to superalgebras, motivated by extensions of vertex operator (super)algebras. For a braided category $\C$ let $\B=\C^{\gr}$ be the category of $\mathbb Z/2$-graded objects with the Koszul-signed braiding. Its even-morphism part is the underlying category of the supercategory of Creutzig-Kanade-McRae. A supercommutative superalgebra $A=A_0\oplus A_1$ in $\C$ is the same as a commutative algebra $\bA$ in $\B$, and super-local modules are the local $\bA$-modules. Hence, rigidity, pivotality and ribbon statements are instances of the ordinary theorems of Shimizu-Yadav, with the ribbon condition $\theta_{A_0}=\id$, $\theta_{A_1}=\varepsilon\,\id$, where $\varepsilon=\pm1$ is fixed by the statistics of the odd part. For $\C$ non-degenerate and $\bA$ haploid and exact we prove that the category of super-local modules is a braided finite tensor category whose Müger center is $\mathsf{sVect}$. It is the centralizer of a fermion in a non-degenerate category obtained by condensing in $\C\boxtimes(\text{toric code})$. If $\C$ is ribbon and $\bA$ is symmetric Frobenius it is ribbon. We give a self-contained treatment of graded simple current algebras and of the free fermion (Ising) example. We compare our formulation with Creutzig-Kanade-McRae and Creutzig-McRae-Shimizu-Yadav.

papers.title: Optimal robust single-qubit gates in superconducting quantum processors
papers.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires high-fidelity quantum gates that are resilient to control errors and device imperfections. Here, we develop energy-optimal control pulses for single-qubit gates that are simultaneously robust against frequency detuning and waveform inhomogeneities while also suppressing leakage outside the computational subspace. Combining the optimized pulse envelopes with an adaptive control scheme, we experimentally demonstrate optimal robust gates on a superconducting quantum processor. For a gate duration of 90ns, we achieve fidelities above 99.9% for the X gate and 99.6% for Hadamard-type gates. For the X gate, we maintain fidelities above 99.5% for simultaneous drive-amplitude variations up to 20% and qubit detuning up to 4 MHz. This robustness outperforms that of conventional Gaussian pulses by an order of magnitude, without much difference in peak gate fidelity. These results establish a route towards robust single-qubit control in large-scale quantum processors, advancing the development of fault-tolerant quantum computing.

papers.title: Designing Robust Quantum Gates
papers.abstract: For given control channels, quantum control theory determines whether quantum gates can be realized, but not their resilience to errors. We address this problem by establishing existence criteria for robust gate implementation in $d$-level systems. Our criteria reveal that implementability of all gates is not enough: a universal family of robust gates exists if and only if, in addition, the driven Hamiltonian operators share no common symmetry. When these criteria hold, we can make every gate resilient to any combination of static perturbations, uniform Hamiltonian rescaling, perturbations at a finite set of selected frequencies, and perturbations with arbitrary selected waveforms. We can impose robustness conditions broadly with limited information about errors, e.g., against any static perturbations; we can also tailor these conditions to the platform, e.g., against environment-induced noise with dominant spectral peaks, requiring no spectral details beyond the peak frequencies. We numerically construct explicit protocols for robust gates, reducing average gate infidelity by approximately two to seven orders of magnitude under Hamiltonian perturbations and environment-induced noise. Together, our existence criteria and numerical constructions provide practical guidance for evaluating the potential of quantum platforms and designing robust quantum gates.

papers.title: Announced Breaks Separate Conformal Reliability from Frequency Calibration
papers.abstract: When the process behind a time series changes on an announced date, like Australia's switch to five minute electricity settlement on October 1, 2021, intervals calibrated before it can stop covering at their stated level. Whether a forecaster needs the next interval to cover or a finished period's share of misses on target decides the restart. We recompute the next conformal interval from post-break forecast errors, and for n independent ones from the same continuous law, its expected coverage error is $O(n^{-1/2})$, the optimal order in a fixed class among methods told the date. For a finished period's share of misses to match its target, we restart adaptive conformal inference (ACI), which on bounded errors brings that share within $O(n^{-1})$ of target if its corrections at a lower limit stay bounded in total, for that period only. After a simulated mean jump of 5.0 standard deviations, recomputed 90% intervals lie an expected 3.5 percentage points from target at the 50th forecast, a third closer than the 5.2 of the best of five adaptive methods. Of 9 announced changes in Texas, Australian and PJM power markets and a Federal Reserve decision, only Australia's switch moves the errors enough for a 5% test at 80% power to resolve a gain from restarting ACI, and dates help restarted ACI only after large changes.

papers.title: Holographic two-point functions across a PT symmetry-breaking transition
papers.abstract: In parity-time (PT)-symmetric non-Hermitian systems, an exceptional point, where eigenvalues and eigenvectors coalesce, typically separates a real spectrum from complex-conjugate eigenvalues. In logarithmic conformal field theories (LCFTs), such an exceptional point appears in the spectrum of scaling dimensions. Holographic models of LCFTs, such as the dipole model, are built exactly at this point. Here, we deform the holographic dipole model so that its two coalescing scaling dimensions split into either two real ones or a complex-conjugate pair. We obtain the renormalized two-point functions in closed form. They change continuously from a linear combination of two power laws, through the logarithmic form of the LCFT at the exceptional point, to log-periodic oscillations. For any pair of scalar primary operators with real mixing under dilatations, the conformal Ward identities fix this form up to two normalization constants, which the holographic dictionary determines. In PT-symmetric theories with such a dilatation operator, real and complex-conjugate scaling dimensions correspond to the PT-unbroken and PT-broken phases. In the BTZ black hole at finite temperature, the difference between the quasinormal frequencies associated with the two scaling dimensions changes from purely imaginary to purely real across the real-to-complex spectral transition. Correspondingly, the linear response changes from overdamped to underdamped, with critical damping at the exceptional point. Direct experimental observation of the two-point functions across the exceptional point could be achieved in two hyperbolic electric circuits with a non-reciprocal coupling, through the voltage response between their edge nodes.

papers.title: Complete solutions and subharmonic functions
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a Riemann surface, $K_X \rightarrow X$ the canonical bundle, and $T_X\coloneqq K_X^{-1}\rightarrow X$ the dual bundle of the canonical bundle. For each integer $r \geq 2$, each $q \in H^0(K_X^r)$, and each choice of the square root $K_X^{1/2}$ of the canonical bundle, we canonically obtain a Higgs bundle $(\K_r,\Phi(q))\rightarrow X$, which is called a cyclic Higgs bundle. A diagonal solution $h = (h_1, \dots, h_r)$ to the Hitchin equation on a cyclic Higgs bundle yields $r-1$ Hermitian metrics $H_1, \dots, H_{r-1}$ on $T_X\rightarrow X$, defined as $H_j \coloneqq h_j^{-1} \otimes h_{j+1}$ for each $j=1,\dots, r-1$, while $h_1$, $h_r$, and $q$ yield a Hermitian metric $H_r$ on $T_X \rightarrow X$ which is degenerate at the zero set of $q$. A diagonal solution is said to be complete if the Kähler metrics induced by $H_1,\dots, H_{r-1}$ are all complete. Li--Mochizuki established a theorem stating that, for any Riemann surface $X$ and any $q$ that is non-zero unless $X$ is hyperbolic, there exists a unique complete solution $h$ to the Hitchin equation for the cyclic Higgs bundle $(\K_r,\Phi(q))$ with $\det(h)=1$. The holomorphic section $q$ induces a subharmonic weight function $\phi_q=\frac{1}{r}\log|q|^2$ on $K_X\rightarrow X$, and the Hitchin equation depends on $q$ only through this weight function. In previous work, the author introduced a variant of the Hitchin equation associated with an arbitrary subharmonic weight function $\varphi$. In this paper, we extend the Li--Mochizuki theorem to complete solutions of the extended Hitchin equation associated to any subharmonic weight function $\varphi$ that is not identically $-\infty$ unless $X$ is hyperbolic.

papers.title: Computing S(X) for Ruled Surfaces Defined on Curves of Genus 2
papers.abstract: This paper discusses the algebra of symmetric tensors for ruled surfaces defined by rank 2 stable vector bundles on curves of genus 2. The algebra is computed for special bundles $E$ when $S^2 E$ is destabilized by a line bundle and when $S^3 E$ is destabilized by a bundle of rank 2. A strategy for computation is discussed in regards to the other special bundles $E$. This paper also discusses the generalization of these strategies to higher genus and gives a computation when $E$ is not stable and may be written as a direct sum of line bundles.

papers.title: Four colours are needed for closed-neighbourhood conflict-free colouring of planar graphs
papers.abstract: A colouring of the vertices of a graph is conflict-free with respect to closed neighbourhoods if every closed neighbourhood contains a colour that appears on exactly one of its vertices. The colouring need not be proper. Every planar graph has such a colouring with four colours. Fabrici, Lužar, Rindošová and Soták [Proper conflict-free and unique-maximum colorings of planar graphs with respect to neighborhoods, \emph{Discrete Appl.\ Math.}\ \textbf{324} (2023) 80--92] conjectured that three colours always suffice. We disprove this conjecture. We give a simple gadget construction that turns every planar graph of chromatic number four into a planar graph with no conflict-free colouring with three colours. This also shows that it is NP-complete to decide whether three colours suffice for a planar graph. We also give a critical planar graph on $25$ vertices and $51$ edges that needs four colours, with a proof that can be checked by hand. Finally, we give an infinite family of plane triangulations that need four colours, and an infinite family of critical examples.

papers.title: AdvDyn: An Emissivity-based Physical Adversarial Patch for Dynamic Infrared Attack
papers.abstract: With the widespread application of infrared object detection technologies in military domains, intelligent infrared adversarial camouflage capabilities have become critical. Existing physical attack methods predominantly employ static thermal suppression strategies, suffering from limited environmental adaptability, insufficient attack robustness, and inadequate visual concealment. This study proposes AdvDyn, an emissivity-based physical dynamic adversarial patch that achieves paradigm-shifting advancements from static to dynamic attacks through algorithm-material co-innovation. First, a multi-level loss function based on feature confusion mechanisms is designed to deceive detectors by attenuating target saliency and enforcing background feature alignment. Second, adaptive physical transformations and differentiable binarization optimization are integrated to address physical robustness and realizability constraints. A 6*4 array of reversible electrochromic emissivity device is developed and tested across a range of background scenarios, enabling scene-adaptive dynamic adversarial attack through independent unit control. Experiments demonstrate that this method achieves 95.59% attack success rate (ASR), reducing average precision (AP) by 60.51%. Physical validations show that static adversarial patches attain 76.55% average ASR under multi-view, multi-range, and multi-spectral conditions, while dynamic patches enhance ASR up to 91.55% in complex environments (wilderness/urban) through adaptive switching. The seamless digital-to-physical transfer via tunable emissivity devices transcends the limitations of traditional static adversarial attack by establishing a dynamic infrared regulation capability. This advancement enhances the battlefield survivability of military assets and demonstrates transformative potential for adaptive adversarial attack in practical combat scenarios.

papers.title: Thermal activation of photon catalysis in difference-intensity Mach-Zehnder interferometry with squeezed thermal light
papers.abstract: Realistic non-Gaussian operations, which can be implemented by mixing a nonclassical Gaussian state with a Fock state at a beam splitter and then heralding on a photon-number-resolving detector, are known to improve phase estimation in a Mach-Zehnder interferometer. The existing studies have considered the single-mode squeezed vacuum for difference-intensity and parity detection, and the two-mode squeezed thermal state for parity detection alone as the initial Gaussian resources. However, a real squeezer in the lab actually produces single-mode squeezed thermal light, which has not been studied in a coherent-plus-resource interferometer. We take up this case and using the phase space Wigner picture, we obtain the heralded state produced by photon subtraction, addition and catalysis on a single-mode squeezed thermal resource, and evaluate the corresponding phase sensitivities. Single-photon catalysis, which is useless on squeezed vacuum, becomes a useful operation for any thermal occupation above $\nth\simeq0.2$, and since it heralds with a probability near one-half, it turns out to be the best success-weighted operation over the whole thermal range. In the vacuum limit our results reproduce the known hierarchy, where two-photon catalysis is the best operation. The quantum Fisher information computations confirms that thermal noise enhances the phase information encoded in the catalyzed state, demonstrating that difference-intensity detection closely approaches the ultimate precision bound across most operational regimes, and, together with a loss analysis, verifies the robustness of the effect.

papers.title: On the location of mass concentration for attractive Bose-Einstein condensates with a ring-shaped potential in bounded domains
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the ground states of attractive Bose-Einstein condensates in a bounded domain $\Omega\subset \mathbb R^2$ under the ring-shaped trapping potential $$ V(x)=(|x|-1)^2. $$ Letting $\Gamma=\{x\in\mathbb R^2:|x|=1\}$ be the ring of global minima of $V(x)$, we focus on a unified geometric setting $\Gamma\cap \Omega\not=\emptyset$, which allows $\Gamma\subset \Omega$ or $\Gamma\cap\partial\Omega\neq\emptyset$. In this setting, we determine the precise location of mass concentration for ground states as the interaction strength approaches the critical value. More precisely, we prove that the mass concentrates at a point $x_0\in\Gamma\cap \Omega$ that has maximal distance from $\partial\Omega$. Our method relies on exponential upper and lower bounds on the difference between the minimal energies in the bounded domain and whole space. The essential lower bound follows from a uniform quadratic-growth estimate near the ground state manifold of the whole space problem, which is established by combining the nondegeneracy of the optimizer for the Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality with a Lyapunov-Schmidt reduction.

papers.title: On the Complexity of Finding Stationary Points in Stochastic $(L_0, L_1)$-Smooth Nonconvex Optimization
papers.abstract: We study the stochastic first-order oracle (SFO) complexity of finding $\epsilon$-stationary points of $(L_0,L_1)$-smooth nonconvex functions. Under bounded-variance noise, existing analyses of normalized and clipped stochastic gradient descent (SGD) establish optimal dependence on $\epsilon$ and $L_0$, but the jointly optimal dependence on $L_0$, $L_1$, and $\epsilon$ remains unclear. We resolve this question for an unbiased SFO whose gradient noise has a $p$th central moment bounded by $\sigma^p$ for some $\sigma\geq 0$, where $p\in(1,2]$.Specifically, we establish an SFO lower bound of $\Omega\big(\big(\sigma^{\frac{p}{p-1}}\epsilon^{-\frac{p}{p-1}}+1\big) (L_0 \Delta\epsilon^{-2}+L_1\Delta\epsilon^{-1})\big)$, where $\Delta>0$ is the initial optimality this http URL bound identifies an unavoidable contribution proportional to $L_1\epsilon^{-1}\Delta$. We also prove that mini-batch (smoothed) normalized SGD can attain a matching upper bound, thereby establishing the optimal SFO complexity.

papers.title: Cooperation Dynamics with Environmental Feedback: Steady States and Transitions
papers.abstract: Cooperative behavior and its regulatory mechanisms are central to complex systems and evolutionary game theory. In natural populations, strategy updates and endogenous payoff environments interact bidirectionally, shaping cooperation. We propose a strategy-payoff environmental-feedback model for four canonical games: Prisoner's Dilemma, Snowdrift, Stag-Hunt, and Harmony. Mathematical derivation reduces the high-dimensional coupled system to an analytically equivalent canonical replicator equation. Bifurcation diagrams, phase portraits, and simulations show how initial cooperation, temptation to defect, and punishment jointly regulate cooperation. Stag-Hunt and Harmony display bistability and initial-state dependence; Prisoner's Dilemma exhibits robust dynamics with stable mixed equilibria. Temptation and punishment drive sequential cross-type game transitions at critical thresholds. Sufficient punishment suppresses defection, shifts bifurcation thresholds, delays destabilization of cooperative steady states, and reshapes these transitions. Numerical tests confirm equivalence and stability switching. Spatial lattice simulations agree with theoretical predictions, supporting robustness. This work reveals regulatory mechanisms from endogenous payoff feedback and initial-condition sensitivity, providing a basis for understanding and optimizing collective prosocial behavior.

papers.title: Brezis--Nirenberg-type results for coupled critical elliptic systems with sign-changing perturbations
papers.abstract: We establish Brezis--Nirenberg-type existence results for elliptic systems with symmetric linear coupling, a radial critical nonlinearity and a subcritical potential. For any dimension $N\ge3$, the potential may change sign, with its negative part bounded by a subquadratic power for some exponent $q_1\in(1,2)$ and no smallness restriction on the coefficient. Under coercivity and suitable near-zero and subcritical growth assumptions, we obtain a nontrivial weak solution if the largest eigenvalue of the coupling matrix is positive when $N\ge4$, or exceeds a positive constant depending on the domain when $N=3$. No homogeneity, convexity or monotonicity along rays is required of the perturbation potential, and either sign of the linear coupling is allowed. The proof combines a variational criterion below the critical Sobolev energy level with estimates showing that the negative part of the potential contributes less than the linear energy decrease. On star-shaped domains, we also obtain a Pohozaev nonexistence criterion.

papers.title: Evolution Toward Sensing-Enabled RAN: Practical Bistatic Sensing via Uplink
papers.abstract: This paper considers uplink channel state information (CSI)-based sensing as an opportunistic approach to enabling sensing in cellular networks, with minimum required modifications to the infrastructure. A practical sensing signal processing procedure is presented, combining 5G positioning function with multi-antenna array processing for passive target localization.
