This paper is concerned with the time-periodic solutions of the Vlasov-Poisson-Boltzmann (VPB) system with a given time-periodic external force in the whole space $\mathbb{R}^3$, where the force is allowed to be non-potential. For the purpose, we first study the Cauchy problem around global Maxwellians, proving the global existence of small-amplitude solutions in a hybrid function space that combines the low-frequency Besov framework for the forced Boltzmann equation with a corresponding control of the self-consistent electric field. One key point occurs to the nonlinear Vlasov force $-
abla_{x}\phi \cdot 
abla_{v}f +  rac{1}{2}v \cdot 
abla_{x}\phi f$ at low frequencies. Rather than treating it as a generic source term, we exploit the Poisson equation and macroscopic balance laws to recover the structural cancellation required for the VPB semi-group estimates, which combined with high-frequency energy estimates and weighted microscopic propagation, yields a closed global well-posedness theory. We further prove uniform stability of the difference of two small-amplitude solutions driven by the same force with respect to distinct initial data. As a consequence of those results, for the time-periodic problem where the external force is time-periodic, we are able to make use of Serrin's method to establish the existence of a unique time-periodic solution of the same period together with its large time asymptotic stability. Our result also gives the existence and stability of stationary solutions when the external force is time-independent.

papers.title: The Zero-Age Massive Stellar Population of W49A from VLA Observations
papers.abstract: We use all-configuration VLA data at 3.3 cm with a physical resolution of ~2000 AU to infer the embedded zero-age massive stellar population of the W49A protocluster, as traced by its compact, ultracompact (UC), and hypercompact (HC) H II regions. Our method consists of visual source identification, the derivation of stellar ionizing-photon rates from the observed emission measure, and the further derivation of stellar masses and luminosities using state-of-the-art stellar calibrations. Considering the 101 robust detections, maximum-likelihood estimation fitting of the high-mass end (M > 10.9 M_\odot) of the sample yields power-law slopes Gamma >= 2.40 for the logarithmic representation of the stellar initial mass function (IMF): dN/d(log M) proportional to M^{-Gamma}. The result is robust considering different assumptions for the ionizing stellar systems. The slopes remain at Gamma >= 1.88 after correction for optical depth effects at 3.3 cm. Therefore, the inferred distribution of stellar masses presents a clear deficit in the high-mass end as compared to the standard stellar IMF (Gamma = 1.35). We propose that this is due to a shorter lifetime of the radio-detected H II regions produced by higher-mass stars, but evolutionary effects in the mass distribution of star formation within embedded protoclusters cannot be discarded.

papers.title: Interacting Galilean and Finite-Energy Carroll Fermions
papers.abstract: We develop a common similarity-transformation framework for Galilean and Carrollian Dirac contractions, encompassing Lévy--Leblond and magnetic Carroll spin-half systems. Explicit field maps relate free formulations with different mass and energy parametrizations. We obtain the complete five-parameter family of derivative-free Hermitian quartic potentials for a pair of Grassmann-odd Pauli spinors, invariant under rotations, a common $U(1)$, and triangular boosts. Higher-order and color-mixed interactions admit exact classical solutions. An independent pairing channel generates derivative interactions upon exact auxiliary elimination and sources otherwise absent Carroll spinor components. Quartic deformations of a Galilean fermionic gauge theory yield algebraic or spatial differential equations while preserving a local phase symmetry. Nambu--Jona-Lasinio contractions provide relativistic origins for selected channels.

papers.title: Kinetic Lifshitz invariants and dynamics of nonreciprocal fluctuations in superconductors
papers.abstract: We derive the generalized time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau theory of a disordered noncentrosymmetric superconductor from the Keldysh nonlinear sigma model, using a two-dimensional electron gas with Rashba spin-orbit coupling and an in-plane Zeeman field as a minimal model. On the thermodynamic side we construct the Lifshitz invariants of the free energy, the linear and cubic gradient terms and the momentum-odd part of the quartic vertex, and trace their dependence on disorder. The couplings of the quadratic sector are governed by a single closed-form kernel controlled by the ratio of the Dyakonov-Perel spin-relaxation rate to temperature. It interpolates between the weak-relaxation regime, where the invariants are suppressed, and the relaxation-dominated regime, where the helical modulation of the order parameter saturates at a universal, disorder-independent value. This crossover reconciles known results for the magnetoelectric couplings of disordered Rashba superconductors. Because the theory is formulated on the Keldysh contour, it also determines the dissipative dynamics: the relaxation rate of a fluctuation with pair momentum $q$, and hence the Langevin noise power, acquires a term odd in $q$ and odd in the magnetic field. The structure of this kinetic Lifshitz invariant is dictated by Onsager reciprocity: friction and noise change together, so that equal-time fluctuations remain Gibbsian while the relaxation dynamics becomes nonreciprocal. As applications we compute the superconducting diode efficiency near $T_c$, where the cubic invariant competes with the quartic vertex and with higher-gradient terms, reversing the sign of the diode coefficient. We also consider fluctuation-induced magnetochiral anisotropy above $T_c$, which grows as the inverse square of the distance to $T_c$ and is suppressed in the relaxation-dominated regime.

papers.title: Hidden Supersymmetry in Wigner-Yang Quantum Mechanics
papers.abstract: We consider a quantum system on the real line obeying a deformed Heisenberg algebra. This deformation was originally proposed by E.P. Wigner in 1950 when establishing the non-uniqueness of the canonical commutation relations implied by the equations of motion. An explicit coordinate representation was subsequently provided by L.M. Yang in 1951 and in essence is identical in form with Dunkl's difference-differential operator introduced in 1989 in connection with root systems of reflection groups when limited to the group $Z_2$ acting on the real line. Under certain conditions such quantum systems exhibit a supersymmetric (SUSY) structure where the reflection operator acts as the grading operator. We present a generalisation of Yang's representation by first considering only one of the two equations of motion in phase space. The corresponding non-interacting system is found to represent Witten's model of SUSY quantum mechanics. Imposing also the second equation of motion the original result of Wigner and Yang is reconsidered by extending their discussion to general symmetric potentials on the real line. As explicit example we discuss the harmonic oscillator and an attractive Coulomb-like potential $V(x) = - \gamma / |x|$. We also establish a Hooke-Newton duality between this Coulomb-like system and the original Wigner-Yang harmonic oscillator system.

papers.title: Detecting non-Gaussianity and quantum non-Gaussianity via multicopy interference
papers.abstract: We develop tests of non-Gaussianity for bosonic systems based on interference between identically prepared copies of the state. The tests use real orthogonal transformations that mix the copies while preserving their collective mode. These transformations commute with identical Gaussian unitaries applied to each copy, allowing us to derive exact Gaussian benchmarks. For single-mode states, purity alone determines the Gaussian reference value, and any discrepancy certifies non-Gaussianity. A two-copy SWAP measurement supplies the purity calibration, while informative tests within this family begin at three copies. We describe a measurement protocol with finite-sample error bounds that use passive interferometry and photon-number-resolving detectors. We also derive purity-dependent inequalities, including joint constraints on higher-power real moments, whose violation excludes convex mixtures of Gaussian states (thus certifying quantum non-Gaussianity). Finally, we extend the reference formulas to multimode systems and prove completeness of the covariance-calibrated hierarchy for states with finite mean photon number.

papers.title: New gravitational instanton: shadow of an extra dimension
papers.abstract: We present an exact gravitational instanton solution on a five-dimensional, conformally invariant, Kerr-like warped Riemannian brane-world manifold. The geometry can be described as the Kähler manifold $\mathbb{C}^1\times\mathbb{C}^1\times \mathbb{R}$. By applying a double cover of $S^3$ through stereographic projection onto $\mathbb{C}P^1\times \mathbb{C}P^1$ of the effective four-dimensional manifold, together with the Klein surface construction, we exploit the underlying $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry. The instanton is then obtained by fibering over the antipodal $S^2$. The metric is determined by a first-order differential equation containing an integer parameter, while the equation governing the angular momentum component decouples from the remaining field equations. Finally, we show that our solution admits an analytic complex transformation to a locally conformally related Kähler manifold possessing a Kähler potential, thereby making the self-dual structure manifest.

papers.title: Tomographer: End-to-end Redshift Distribution Estimation for Source Catalogs and Intensity Maps
papers.abstract: Redshift information is central to nearly every extragalactic and cosmological application of sky surveys, yet only a small fraction of cataloged sources, and none of the photons forming diffuse backgrounds, have spectroscopic redshifts. Clustering-based redshift inference estimates the redshift distribution of an arbitrary dataset through spatial cross-correlation with a reference sample of known redshifts. It relies only on positional information, making it applicable to any tracer of large-scale structure, including source populations and diffuse intensity maps. Its broader adoption, however, has been limited by technical barriers: assembling and characterizing spectroscopic references, expensive pair-counting computations, theoretical corrections, and systematic control. To remove these barriers, we introduce Tomographer, an end-to-end clustering-redshift framework. The key design feature is a set of precomputed "activation maps" encoding the spatial pair information of 3 million Sloan Digital Sky Survey spectroscopic galaxies and quasars up to $z\sim4$ over $10{,}000\,{\rm deg}^2$. This eliminates user-end pair counting, reducing computational scaling from $O(N\log N)$ to $O(1)$ map multiplications. Given a source catalog or intensity map, Tomographer returns the bias-weighted redshift distribution, $b(z)\,{\rm d}N/{\rm d}z(z)$ or $b(z)\,{\rm d}I/{\rm d}z(z)$. We validate the framework against samples with known redshifts, demonstrate accurate uncertainty estimates, and show robustness to survey footprint, spatially varying selection functions, beam smoothing, and foreground contamination. We showcase applications to source catalogs selected by flux, color, photometric redshift, morphology, or variability, and to intensity maps from radio to X-rays. Future Tomographer releases will incorporate additional wide-field spectroscopic reference samples as they become available.

papers.title: Stochastic partial differential equation model for environmental DNA dynamics in river environments
papers.abstract: Environmental DNA (eDNA) has emerged as a novel tool for quantifying the seasonal abundance of aquatic species in water bodies; however, its mathematical modeling is still at a germinating stage because of its mechanistic uncertainties. We propose a first-step mathematical and computational framework for the eDNA dynamics of migratory fish based on a novel stochastic partial differential equation model with a delayed source input. The model governs spatiotemporal eDNA concentration in rivers where the source comes from a stochastic differential equation for the migration dynamics of the fish. The affine nature of the model facilitates its theoretical analysis, including the guarantee of well-posedness and the closed-form derivation of the Laplace functional despite the proportionality coefficient of the multiplicative noise term being non-Lipschitz. We also propose a discretization scheme for the model that theoretically generates nonnegative numerical solutions. We finally apply the proposed model to eDNA concentration data sampled from midstream reaches of a river system and perform sensitivity analysis.

papers.title: Nonlocality relates cuprate photoemission $ω/T$ scaling to a broad dielectric loss peak
papers.abstract: Photoemission spectroscopy on high $T_c$ cuprates reveals a puzzling nodal self-energy with $\omega/T$ scaling and an exponent varying continuously with doping. Meanwhile, electron energy loss spectroscopy finds a broad $\sim 1$eV peak whose physical origin remains debated. We propose they share a common origin by introducing a phenomenological model of nonlocal screening in a many-body charged fluid. The model's key feature is spatially nonlocal effective repulsions between carriers $V_{\alpha}(r) \sim 1/r^\alpha$, with doping-dependent $\alpha$. The model predicts a falsifiable relationship between independently measured self-energy exponent $\gamma$ and loss function peak dispersion exponent $\alpha$, as $\gamma = 2-\frac{1}{\alpha}$. This can be tested using modern ARPES and EELS. Nonlocality provides an alternative route to $\omega/T$ scaling in observables, although it is conventionally regarded as a signature of quantum criticality.

papers.title: Speculative Successive Cancellation Decoding of Polar Codes
papers.abstract: Polar codes achieve channel capacity as block length increases, but this asymptotic advantage comes at the cost of decoding speed: the conventional \ac{SC} algorithm is inherently sequential, which limits its practicality for high-throughput applications. This work addresses that limitation by introducing the \emph{\ac{Spec-SC}} framework, which incorporates speculative execution into the \ac{SC} decoding process. While \ac{sp-node}-based decoders enable partial parallelism for specific, predefined structures, \ac{Spec-SC} extends this capability by permitting parallel execution in general nodes that do not match any \acs{sp-node} pattern. A built-in verification mechanism ensures that this speculation does not compromise decoding correctness. Simulation results show that \ac{Spec-SC} achieves the same \acs{BER} and \acs{FER} performance as conventional \ac{SC} decoding, while reducing the average number of sequentially traversed nodes by up to $69\%$ for a polar code of length $N=4096$. A cycle-level analysis further shows that, for $\Pc(4096,3584)$ at $5\,\mathrm{dB}$, a heterogeneous four-core configuration achieves a $1.57\times$ decoding speedup using a total of $2944$ processing lanes, representing a $43.75\%$ increase over the $N_{\mathrm{lane}}=2048$ one-core \ac{SC} baseline. The speedup increases to $2.5\times$ at $7\,\mathrm{dB}$, demonstrating the increasing effectiveness of speculation at higher $\EbNo$. These results demonstrate that \ac{Spec-SC} enables additional algorithm-level parallelism beyond conventional \ac{sp-node}-based decoding, motivating its further investigation for high-throughput and high-reliability communication systems. achieve, paving the way for speculative hardware decoder implementations.

papers.title: A fast dynamo with zero topological entropy
papers.abstract: We construct an autonomous Lipschitz fast dynamo on the flat three-torus whose particle flow has zero topological entropy and whose ideal induction equation has no exponential growth. We perform a multiscale construction starting from the Ponomarenko flow. For every sufficiently small positive magnetic diffusivity, the induction operator on $\mathbb{T}^3$ has an eigenvalue with real part bounded below by a positive constant independent of the diffusivity. A corresponding non-zero real-valued magnetic field satisfies an exact exponential growth law in $\mathrm{L}^2$. For the same velocity field, every solution of the ideal problem grows at most linearly in $\mathrm{L}^2$. Moreover, the particle flow and its inverse have Lipschitz constants growing at most linearly in time and thus zero topological entropy. The velocity field is real-valued, divergence-free, differentiable everywhere and smooth away from one circle, but is not $\mathrm{C}^1$.

papers.title: Thermal Stability of Two-Dimensional Crystals with Extended OH Hydrogen-Bonded Chains
papers.abstract: Numerical simulations of the dynamics of monolayer structures of molecules deposited on a sheet of hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) have been performed. It is shown that molecules containing benzene rings and hydroxyl groups can form stable two-dimensional crystals with linear hydrogen-bonded chains OH$\cdots$OH$\cdots$OH$\cdots$. Such structures are formed by the following molecules: phenol (C$_6$H$_5$OH), hydroquinone (C$_6$H$_4$(OH)$_2$), 4-phenylphenol (C$_6$H$_5$-C$_6$H$_4$OH), 4-(4-phenylphenyl)phenol (C$_6$H$_5$-C$_6$H$_4$-C$_6$H$_4$OH), paracetamol (CH$_3$C(O)NHC$_6$H$_4$OH), 4-hydroxybenzanilide (C$_6$H$_5$C(O)NHC$_6$H$_4$OH) and 4,4$^\prime$-dihydroxybenzanilide (C$_6$H$_4$OHC(O)NHC$_6$H$_4$OH). On the one hand, the benzene rings in these molecules ensure their strong interaction with the flat substrate; on the other hand, they do not hinder the formation of long hydrogen-bonded chains. The monolayer structures of these molecules exhibit high thermal stability: the onset melting temperatures of their 2D crystals are 112, 257, 237, 337, 277, 407, and 483$^\circ$C, respectively. The simulations suggest that structures composed of h-BN sheets and molecules of hydroquinone, paracetamol, 4-hydroxybenzanilide and 4,4$^\prime$-dihydroxybenzanilide can be used for the development of novel proton-exchange membranes capable of operating at elevated temperatures.

papers.title: AI Governance for Institutional Readiness in Finance
papers.abstract: Agentic AI is gaining acceptance in asset management, but governance has not kept pace: 88\% of surveyed finance professionals report no operational governance framework for agentic AI, and only 24 of 75 large U.S. money managers disclosing AI use in Form ADV filings report a formal governance policy. We argue this gap is architectural: governance built for static validation does not survive continuously retrained agentic policies. We propose a four-layer framework (Policy, Engineering, Composition, Systemic) grounded in two distinct kinds of evidence, kept explicitly separate: two calibrated synthetic illustrations (a regret-covariance drift monitor; a crowding simulation showing joint drawdown risk rising from 39.2\% to 79.3\%), and three real, documented cases (a deployed LLM-embedding trading strategy, a \$45 billion discretionary fund's forced-deleveraging blowup, and a tribunal ruling holding an airline liable for its chatbot). The synthetic examples demonstrate computability from observable data; the cases demonstrate that the failure modes are not hypothetical. We provide a 90-day implementation sequence spanning trading and payments/customer-facing systems.

papers.title: Valley-controlled chiral magnetism in transition metal dichalcogenide monolayers
papers.abstract: We put forward the Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida (RKKY) interaction in transition metal dichalcogenide monolayers as a tool to create and control a chiral magnetic texture. We show that in the spin-valley locking regime, the RKKY interaction acts as a Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya coupling with an effective spin rotation period exactly equal to the tripled lattice constant. Using mean field theory and classical Monte Carlo simulations, we demonstrate that this interaction qualitatively reshapes the phase diagram of atomically thin antiferromagnets. It destroys the chirality-related phase transition by selecting a single chirality value even when the RKKY interaction is small. At the same time, it shifts the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transition associated with spins orientation to higher temperatures. We argue that the valley degree of freedom of electrons mediating the RKKY interaction provides a powerful control knob for exploring non-universal phase transitions and quantum spin liquid states in two-dimensional van der Waals heterostructures.

papers.title: Proximity effects of chiral magnetization on transition metal dichalcogenides monolayers
papers.abstract: We consider the proximity effects of a commensurate chiral $120^{\circ}$ Néel magnetic structure on the transport and optical properties of a transition metal dichalcogenide monolayer (TMD ML). The enlarged magnetic unit cell leads to the folding of the Brillouin zone and enables efficient intervalley spin-flip scattering. Starting from a six band tight binding model, we develop an effective $k\cdot p$ model, which describes the coupling between charge carriers in the TMD ML and the chiral magnetization. We predict the anomalous antiferromagnetic Hall effect (AHE) for conduction electrons and describe it accounting for the interplay between anomalous velocity, side jump, and skew scattering contributions. The proximity of the chiral magnetization also leads to the mixing and splitting of the exciton resonances in the two valleys which are related by the time reversal symmetry despite zero net magnetization. Finally, we demonstrate the possibility to measure the distribution of in-plane orientation of the chiral magnetization through Faraday rotation and the ellipticity of incident linearly polarized light.

papers.title: Approximate Message Passing with Random Initialization for Phase Retrieval
papers.abstract: Randomly initialized first-order iterative algorithms are simple, widely used, and empirically effective across many high-dimensional inference problems, yet their theoretical behavior remains far less understood than that of algorithms started from more elaborate, problem-specific initializations such as spectral initialization. This paper takes a step toward closing this gap by studying randomly initialized approximate message passing (AMP) for noiseless phase retrieval, a canonical nonconvex inference problem. We give a non-asymptotic, growing-horizon characterization of the AMP trajectory from random initialization, and show that it achieves both the information-theoretic weak recovery threshold $\delta_{\rm weak}=1/2$ and the AMP strong recovery threshold $\delta_{\rm str}\approx1.13$, matching the recovery thresholds established for spectrally initialized AMP. The key technical ingredients are twofold: (i) a non-asymptotic coupling that decomposes the AMP iterates as a signal component, a linear combination of independent Gaussian vectors, and an approximation error, and (ii) a second-order analysis of the Onsager correction error built around a non-asymptotic version of Bolthausen's condition. These allow us to analyze the $O_\delta(\log n)$ steps required for weak recovery, and to faithfully track the asymptotic state evolution up to $n^{1/3}/\operatorname{polylog}(n)$ steps in the intermediate recovery regime $\delta\in(\delta_{\rm weak},\delta_{\rm str})$, both beyond the $O(1)$-iteration horizon of classical AMP theory. Above the strong recovery threshold, AMP reaches any prescribed fixed recovery accuracy within $O_{\delta,\varepsilon}(\log n)$ iterations. Both the coupling and the error analysis are developed for a broad class of generalized AMP dynamics and may be of independent interest for general single-index models.

papers.title: Control variates with neural surrogates for uncertainty quantification in kinetic equations
papers.abstract: Efficient uncertainty quantification for kinetic equations with random inputs is challenging because it requires repeated simulations of high-dimensional models, such as the Boltzmann, Landau, and related collisional equations, whose computational cost can quickly become prohibitive. Multifidelity control variates address this difficulty by coupling a small number of high-fidelity simulations with many evaluations of lower-complexity reduced models. In this work, we analyze the case in which the reduced model is replaced by a neural surrogate rather than evaluated through a classical numerical scheme. We show that the resulting estimator remains unbiased and that the change in the optimal variance induced by the neural approximation is controlled by the error between the exact low-fidelity observable and its neural approximation. This estimate is then combined with residual stability estimates for inhomogeneous Fokker--Planck and Bhatnagar--Gross--Krook surrogates. We also extend the analysis to several control variates and to an asymptotic-preserving (AP) hierarchy containing the limiting Euler observable. In the fluid limit, the optimal hierarchical variance converges to the variance associated with the limiting Euler control, while the contribution of the intermediate kinetic correction vanishes. Numerical tests based on micro--macro neural surrogates illustrate the predicted variance stability and the behavior of the AP hierarchy.

papers.title: Thermal Evolution and Hydrodynamic Filtering of Pseudoscalar Dark Matter
papers.abstract: Filtered dark matter provides a mechanism for producing massive dark matter particles during a first order phase transition. The resulting abundance can be modified by plasma hydrodynamics. We investigate this effect in a complex singlet extension of the Standard Model, focusing on the deflagration regime. The entropy normalized dark matter abundance $Y_\chi$ is calculated using both analytic and numerical methods. As the dark matter mass increases, we identify three patterns of abundance evolution before nucleation, ranging from thermal equilibrium to thermal suppression and freeze-out. For $\xi_w=0.01$, the numerical results show that hydrodynamic effects increase the final $Y_\chi$ by factors of approximately $4.1$, $5.7$, and $31.6$ for $m_\chi=1.78$, $2.30$, and $5.03~\mathrm{TeV}$, respectively. For the two lighter masses, the numerical and analytic results agree within $5\%$, and the difference is reduced to about $1\%$ or less when hydrodynamic effects are included. The heaviest case requires a numerical treatment because dark matter freeze-out before nucleation. Our results show that hydrodynamic reheating can enhance $Y_\chi$ even when dark matter has already frozen out before the phase transition. In this regime, $Y_\chi$ is determined by the dark matter abundance established before nucleation and hydrodynamic filtering at the bubble wall.

papers.title: Mechanistic bridges from receptors to whole-brain dynamics: promise and limits of master-equation mean-field models
papers.abstract: Drug and disease perturbations often arise at molecular, synaptic or cellular scales, yet are often observed in population and whole-brain signals. Which microscopic mechanisms stay explicit, interpretable and testable through tractable reductions, and what can whole-brain models claim? We follow the master-equation lineage of receptor-aware adaptive mean fields, from finite-size statistics and semi-analytical transfer functions to connectome-coupled conductance-based adaptive nodes. Re-deriving its moment equations, we correct the covariance equation, which omitted a curvature term of the same order as those kept. We compare this strategy with phenomenological neural masses, exact low-dimensional and population-density reductions, large-scale spiking models and learned or hybrid surrogates. We find that effective excitatory/inhibitory synaptic kinetics, conductance state and spike-frequency adaptation can stay manipulable across scales, enabling interpretable, pharmacology-informed perturbations with testable meso- and macroscopic effects. Yet this requires coarse-grained Markovianity, population homogeneity, quasi-stationary transfer functions, moment closure, regional uniformity and measurement-specific observation models. Moreover, first-order whole-brain models discard covariance dynamics, and macroscopic fits do not identify a unique molecular cause. In compute and memory traffic, node-local detail mainly changes prefactors, while dense global covariance propagation changes the scaling class. Cross-scale models should therefore be judged by the intervention pathways and observables they preserve, validity domain, identifiability, empirical adequacy and cost. Receptor-aware mean fields are thus neither universal nor a mere realism-cost compromise, but a transparent, tractable strategy for selected mechanistic questions, provided each reduction step is independently validated.

papers.title: FDIR: Fidelity-Anchored Decompressed Image Restoration for Human and Machine Perception
papers.abstract: Evaluating restored images requires considering pixel fidelity, human perception, and machine preference. However, existing compressed image restoration methods rarely satisfy all three criteria at once. Regression models preserve pixel fidelity but often produce overly smooth results. Conversely, generative models create realistic textures but tend to drift from the ground truth. To address this trade-off, we propose FDIR (Fidelity-Anchored Decompressed Image Restoration), a framework that uses generative priors while preserving strong pixel fidelity. FDIR works in two stages. First, a quality-guided one-step flow model (QO-Flow) adapts a pretrained latent flow backbone with LoRA to generate a structural prior in a single forward pass. Second, rather than outputting this generated image directly, a flow-conditioned detail refinement network (FCDR) uses it to predict a pixel-space residual on the decompressed input. This design brings in perceptual details while keeping the final output faithful to the original image. We evaluate FDIR on LIVE1 and DIV2K under severe compression at quality factors 1 and 5. Across all four settings, FDIR achieves the highest PSNR among the seven compared methods and beats the strongest perceptual baseline, CODiff, by 1.3 to 2.1 dB. It also ranks second on LPIPS in all four settings and on FID and DISTS on DIV2K-Val, right behind CODiff. For downstream detection, segmentation, and retrieval at quality factors 20 and 30, FDIR ranks second on every individual metric and achieves the best average rank across all ten metrics. Overall, FDIR is the only method to maintain a top-two average rank across fidelity, perception, and machine preference.

papers.title: Revisiting Stress Analysis in a Three-Dimensional Elastic Hollow Sphere under Uniaxial Compression via the Inverse Laplace Transform Expressions within an Elastodynamic Framework
papers.abstract: The stress analysis of a three-dimensional elastic hollow sphere subjected to uniaxial compression is revisited, employing an elastodynamic framework. Through the application of the Laplace transform, the scalar and vector potentials of displacement are expanded, facilitating a detailed exploration of the system's mechanical behavior. The static solutions for displacement and stress distributions are derived in the long-time limit, which reveal key insights into the response of the elastic hollow sphere. Notably, on the inner surface, certain quantities exhibit a peak at the point where the angle between the compressive force and the point on the surface becomes perpendicular, indicating localized stress concentration. These findings provide a robust analytical approach for understanding and predicting the behavior of elastic hollow spheres under uniaxial loading, with implications for material science and structural engineering.

papers.title: An Adjusted Ersatz Discrepancy for Global Sensitivity Analysis: Theory and Benchmarks
papers.abstract: In given-data sensitivity analysis, the analyst holds only a fixed sample of model inputs and outputs. We revisit the ersatz discrepancy of Puy, Roy, and Saltelli (2024), a grid-occupancy statistic read from the scatterplot of an input against the output, and propose two modifications: a rank transformation of the output and a deterministic Moore-neighbourhood fill of isolated empty cells. We derive the asymptotic theory of the resulting adjusted ersatz under simple random sampling. Without the fill, the rank-transformed statistic is exactly a histogram estimator of Borgonovo's moment-independent measure ($\delta$). At its resolution, however, it converges to $e^{-1}$ plus a different $f$-divergence, so that its value under independence is $0.37$. With the fill, the limit lies between $\delta - 0.141$ and $\delta + 0.048$ for every dependence structure, and its value under independence drops to $0.047$. The theory explains the type I errors observed at screening thresholds of $0.01$, $0.05$, and $0.10$, the dominant role of the grid resolution, and when rankings by $\delta$-type measures and by total-order Sobol' indices agree. In replicated benchmarks, Becker metafunctions and the HYMOD model, a degree-adaptive polynomial chaos expansion estimates total-order indices most accurately, whereas the adjusted ersatz differs from $\delta$ by $0.02$-$0.08$ on average, as the theory predicts, and improves markedly on the original measure. It is best used as a fast, assumption-free screening statistic.

papers.title: The eROSITA X-ray luminosity function of active galactic nuclei
papers.abstract: The X-ray luminosity function (XLF) of active galactic nuclei (AGN) provides an observational probe of the growth of supermassive black holes (SMBHs) across cosmic time. With its large survey grasp, Spectrum Roentgen Gamma (SRG)/eROSITA samples the luminosity--redshift plane with a depth--area balance complementary to pencil-beam surveys, providing the volume needed to detect rare luminous AGN, previously limited by small-number statistics. We measure the soft XLF, leveraging an eROSITA sample spanning approximately eight orders of magnitude in luminosity out to $z\simeq6$. This enables us to study luminosity-dependent evolution with improved constraints, and to infer both the SMBH accretion history and optical/UV missed AGN population. We introduce a new redshift-dependent smoothly broken power-law parameterisation in which all XLF model parameters are allowed to evolve continuously with redshift. We find lower space densities for moderately and very luminous AGN at low redshift, while the abundance is higher than previously found at the highest redshifts. Comparisons to optical/UV quasar LFs converted to rest-frame $2\!-\!10\,\mathrm{keV}$ show that the UV-missed fraction decreases with luminosity, and, in the most luminous bin, increases with redshift. Integrating the XLF yields a black-hole accretion-rate density peaking at $z \simeq 1.5$, with the corresponding cumulative black-hole mass density indicating $\sim80^{+11}_{-23}\%$ obscured growth relative to locally-inferred BH mass estimates derived from scaling relations and missed by the soft X-ray selection of our sample. With this work, we release the eROSITA DR2 AGN catalogue, including counterparts and their redshift information. We then discuss how these results can inform future spectroscopic, photometric, and X-ray survey strategies aimed at improving AGN demographic constraints.

papers.title: Unbiased Data-Driven Determination of the Nuclear Dipole Amplitude in the Color Glass Condensate
papers.abstract: Gluon saturation limits the growth of parton densities at small Bjorken-$x$ and is expected to be most pronounced in heavy nuclei. Yet quantitative extractions of the nuclear gluon dipole amplitude have long relied on parametrized initial conditions, introducing uncontrolled model dependence that obscures genuine nuclear effects. We introduce a physics-informed neural-network framework that embeds the collinearly improved Balitsky-Kovchegov evolution equation directly into the training objective, allowing the impact-parameter-averaged dipole amplitude to be determined from data without assuming a functional form for its initial condition. Applying this framework to forward-hadron nuclear-modification-factor and coherent $J/\psi$ photoproduction data, we extract the $^{208}$Pb dipole amplitude at $x_0=0.01$ with QCD evolution and momentum-space positivity enforced throughout training. The evolved amplitude reproduces the measured cross sections across the available kinematic range and yields a saturation-scale ratio $Q_{s0,\mathrm{Pb}}^2/Q_{s0,p}^2 = 3.17^{+0.17}_{-0.10}$, consistent with simple geometric scaling. The extracted Pb initial condition is well described by a McLerran-Venugopalan-type form, in contrast to the proton, reflecting the higher color-charge density of a large nucleus. Using the same amplitude, we predict the rapidity dependence of the transverse-momentum ratio in $pp$, $p$Pb, and Pb$p$ collisions, finding agreement with recent LHCb measurements at low multiplicity without any system-dependent parameters. This work provides the first unbiased, data-driven determination of nuclear structure in the saturation regime and establishes a general strategy for embedding nonlinear evolution equations into machine-learning extractions of dynamically constrained observables.

papers.title: Uniform Airy expansions for Ramanujan's function and the Stieltjes--Wigert edge kernel
papers.abstract: For $q=e^{-\varepsilon}\to1^-$, we obtain an Airy expansion for Ramanujan's entire function $A_q(\sqrt q\,x)$, uniformly for $x$ in a sufficiently small fixed complex neighborhood of $1/4$. After an explicit exponential normalization, the expansion has analytic coefficients and a nonlinear Airy argument. We calculate the first corrections and bound the remainder by $\varepsilon^2$ times an Airy envelope. The estimate is valid at Airy zeros and retains exponential decay on the real interval below $1/4$. The proof uses a Gaussian integral representation and an odd analytic change of variable that reduces the phase to cubic form. The compact turning-point expansion follows as a corollary. For each fixed positive zero $\rho_n(q)$, we obtain an expansion of $\log(4\rho_n(q))$ through order $\varepsilon^2$, with remainder $O_n(\varepsilon^{8/3})$. A zero-free interval identifies the zeros by their global indices. We also calculate the $\varepsilon^{2/3}$ correction to the known Airy limit of the Stieltjes--Wigert edge kernel, with an $O(\varepsilon^{4/3})$ remainder uniformly on compact sets, including the diagonal.

papers.title: Counterexamples, Spectral Obstructions, and Deletion Stability for WOW-284
papers.abstract: WOW-284 is a Graffiti conjecture asserting that every connected graph of order at least three and girth at least five has minimum dual degree at most $-\lambda_{\min}(D)$, where $D$ is the distance matrix and the dual degree of a vertex is the average degree of its neighbors. We refute it with exact counterexamples on $38$, $39$, $40$, $42$ and $50$ vertices and study the structure of regular counterexamples. For a connected $k$-regular graph $G$ of girth at least five and diameter three, we prove that $\delta^*(G)+\lambda_{\min}(D)=2k-2-\max_\theta(\theta+1)^2$, the maximum being over the nonprincipal adjacency eigenvalues, so strict failure is a spectral window condition. The closed window $|\theta+1|\le\sqrt{2k-2}$ alone, without any diameter assumption, forces $|V(G)|<(k+2)(k^2+3)/6$ when $k\ge4$, and an integral excess matrix derived from the optimal polynomial sharpens this bound for diameter-three counterexamples. Every regular strict counterexample has degree at least six and diameter at most four, and in degree six it has at most $50$ vertices. Under vertex deletion, the Hoffman-Singleton graph remains a strict counterexample after the removal of any five vertices, while an explicit six-vertex deletion destroys strictness. A degree-$57$ Moore graph, if one exists, remains a connected strict counterexample after the removal of any $56$ vertices. Every strict counterexample has at least $15$ vertices, and an exhaustive search excludes orders up to $19$. The strict induced subgraphs of the Hoffman-Singleton graph of orders $36$ to $50$ are classified up to automorphism; among them are three further irregular counterexamples of order $40$.

papers.title: PANTERA. I. Hunting for the Most Metal-Rich Stars in the Solar Neighborhood with High-Resolution Spectroscopy
papers.abstract: We present PANTERA (Project for Astrophysical Nucleosynthesis and Targeted Exploration of metal-Rich Abundances), a high-resolution spectroscopic survey of the most metal-rich stars in the solar neighborhood. In this first paper, we report iron abundances for 56 metal-rich stars, selected from Gaia DR3 XP spectrophotometric metallicities. These targets were observed with the PEPSI spectrograph on the Large Binocular Telescope (LBT), the Levy spectrograph on the Automated Planet Finder (APF) telescope, and the HIRES spectrograph on the Keck telescope. We derive [Fe/H] from an equivalent-width analysis of iron lines, with the effective temperature taken from photometry and the surface gravity from the Gaia parallax. We verify our measurement using Gaia benchmark stars, observing some sources with more than one spectrograph, using a second synthesis code, and an independent equivalent-width measurement. We find that the Gaia-XP metallicities over-predict [Fe/H] for part of our sample: they agree with our values for the dwarfs, though a selection bias limits what this agreement can show, and exceed our [Fe/H] by $0.15\pm0.02$ dex on average for the cool giants. We attribute the over-prediction in part to the strong blue line blanketing of the cool metal-rich giants and to the survey labels on which the XP metallicities were trained. We find that 25 of the 56 stars have [Fe/H] $> +0.4$, with the most iron-rich stars reaching [Fe/H]$=+0.58$. We discuss the implications of our result on studying metal-rich populations.

papers.title: Structure-Property Correlation of Cr/Cu-MnFeCoNi High-Entropy Alloys for Alkaline Water Electrolysis
papers.abstract: High-entropy alloys (HEAs), with their unique compositional-complexity and tunable surface chemistry, have emerged as promising electrocatalysts for energy conversion. The catalytic activity of HEA often arises from the interplay between the intrinsic activity of the individual elements and the synergistic effects generated at the interfaces. Even a single-element substitution in a multicomponent HEA can substantially alter the surface-chemistry and electrochemical kinetics of the active surface. Here we investigated the structure-property relationship of CrMnFeCoNi (HEA-Cr) and MnFeCoNiCu (HEA-Cu) HEAs by comparing the alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and oxygen evolution reaction (OER) activity. Under the same experimental condition, HEA-Cu outperforms HEA-Cr towards both HER and OER. Substituting Cr with Cu significantly enhances the bifunctional activity, where HEA-Cu achieved a lower overpotential (538 mV) and Tafel slope (165 mVdec-1) when compared with HEA-Cr. Computational analysis corroborates these findings, showing that Cu substitution modulates the electronic-structure to provide favorable binding energies for reaction intermediates (H*, O*, OH*, and OOH*). Interestingly, unlike HER, recovered HEA-Cu after OER showed migration of Cu forming a Cu-rich outer layer shell with a multimetallic core. These findings demonstrate the potential of single-element substitution in HEAs as a strategy for designing high-performance, cost-effective catalysts for efficient water electrolysis.

papers.title: Electronic and magnetic properties of small one-dimensional Wigner crystals from an ab initio approach
papers.abstract: We present an ab initio method to study the electronic properties of small one-dimensional Wigner crystals. In particular, we focus on the calculation of the electronic charge distribution. Our theoretical studies are motivated by the experimental observation of few-electron Wigner crystals in a carbon nanotube [Science 364, 870 (2019)]. We model the experimental setup by confining electrons in a one-dimensional potential well with hard-wall boundary conditions. We represent the Hamiltonian of the system in a basis of Slater determinants and perform full configuration interaction to ensure we capture all the electron correlation for a given basis set. As the one-particle basis set we use particle-in-a-box wave functions which by construction satisfy the boundary conditions. With our approach, we obtain accurate electronic density profiles of small one-dimensional Wigner crystals. These profiles clearly show the localisation of the electrons. Moreover, we calculate the exchange coupling constant of the Wigner dimer by mapping our ab initio method on a Heisenberg Hamiltonian. We obtain a reasonable agreement with a result in the literature.

papers.title: Quasi-SVD: Learning a Lie-constrained matrix factorisation for real-time imaging
papers.abstract: Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) underlies matrix factorisation tasks across many fields, with imaging applications demanding cost-efficient processing. Yet SVD algorithms are inherently sequential, constraining GPU throughput and limiting online deployment in imaging pipelines. This study introduces a fully parallelized matrix factorization framework for GPUs by enforcing matrix orthogonality on left singular vectors via Lie-parametrised algebra and recovering the remaining components through soft constraints. This asymmetric constraint design enables an efficient parallel decomposition with an orthogonal left factor, achieves high reconstruction fidelity and substantially accelerates computation relative to the exact SVD, with high throughput exceeding standard video frame rates. Performance is evaluated on multiple imaging tasks spanning complementary computational regimes: (1) an MNIST denoising benchmark at an intermediate scale with known ground truth, (2) Mueller matrix polarimetry for neurosurgical tissue characterisation, requiring massive batch processing of small matrices, and (3) spatio-temporal background subtraction for ultrasound localisation microscopy, requiring high-dimensional matrix separation. Across regimes and instruments, the proposed framework demonstrates robust domain transfer at various matrix scales and 2.6--67$\times$ speed-ups over the exact GPU SVD, and, unlike randomised SVD, accelerates large batches of small full-rank matrices. By prioritising downstream reconstruction fidelity over exact spectral recovery, the proposed SVD framework enables GPU-friendly matrix factorisation.

papers.title: An infinite family of minimally nonperfectly divisible graphs with a bisimplicial vertex
papers.abstract: We construct an explicit infinite family of minimally nonperfectly divisible graphs $G_t$, each with a bisimplicial vertex $v_t$ of degree four and a cutvertex. Thus the same family disproves Hoàng's conjectures excluding bisimplicial vertices and clique cutsets from such graphs. For every integer $t\geq1$, the graph $G_t$ has clique number three and satisfies \[ |V(G_t)|=93+30(t-1),\qquad |E(G_t)|=320+104(t-1). \] Deleting $v_t$ gives a perfectly divisible graph $H_t$ with an edge whose endpoints both lie outside the perfect part of every perfect division. This gives a negative answer to the prescribed-vertex question of Hu, Xu and Zhuang. The same graphs answer their second question affirmatively: each $H_t$ is perfectly divisible but not perfectly weight divisible. The cutvertex and weighted consequences were pointed out by Hu, Xu and Zhuang, who also observed that replacing one endpoint of the edge by two adjacent twins gives a minimally nonperfectly divisible graph with a homogeneous set.

papers.title: Form-Factor-Constrained Non-Factorized Transition-GPD Tomography of $N\toΔ(1232)$ Multipole Structure
papers.abstract: A form-factor-constrained non-factorized transition-GPD reconstruction is developed for the $N\to\Delta(1232)$ electromagnetic transition. The production input consists of the published CLAS magnetic multipole amplitude and electric and scalar/Coulomb quadrupole ratios. Additional external low-$Q^2$ ratio data are retained only as a separate ratio-sector diagnostic. The electroproduction quantities are propagated replica by replica and converted to the dimensionless Jones--Scadron transition form factors $G_M^*$, $G_E^*$, and $G_C^*$. AICc model selection yields a modified dipole for $G_M^*$, a dipole for $G_E^*$, and a cubic $z$ expansion for $G_C^*$. These fits define the imposed positive-$x$ normalization $F_\alpha(t)=2G_\alpha^*(-t)$ for factorized, correlated exponential, Regge-like, and double-distribution-inspired transition-GPD profiles. The upper boundary of the impact-parameter transform is fixed by the largest measured absolute-form-factor point, $Q^2=6~\mathrm{GeV}^2$, so that no high-$Q^2$ continuation beyond the measured range enters the production reconstruction. The primary transverse localization observable is therefore defined from the small-$Q^2$ slope of the modeled transition GPD, with finite-window radial moments retained only as secondary core-shape diagnostics. For the slope-defined width, the transition form factor contributes an $x$-independent channel-dependent offset, while the entire $x$ dependence is fixed by the chosen longitudinal--transverse profile ansatz. The factorized profile is $x$-independent and the three non-factorized families generate distinct modeled $x$ dependences. The resulting reconstruction separates measured transition-form-factor information from model-dependent longitudinal structure and provides a controlled framework for assessing structural and covariance sensitivity in $N\to\Delta(1232)$ transition tomography.

papers.title: Causal-TS: A Python Library for Causal Discovery in Stationary and Nonstationary Time Series
papers.abstract: We describe Causal-TS, an open-source Python library that provides a common interface and lagged-graph representation for causal discovery (structure learning) from stationary and nonstationary multivariate time series. It learns lagged and contemporaneous causal graphs with constraint-based (CDNOTS, CDNOTS+, Cedar), score-based (LGES, TGES, GES, LASSO-VAR, VARLiNGAM, Granger) and hybrid (GRACE, REAP) methods. The constraint-based methods share 17 linear and nonlinear conditional independence (CI) tests, nine with PyTorch implementations. It also provides candidate-regime detection with per-regime discovery, latent-confounder correction (LUCID), missing- and mixed-data support, a data-driven configuration recommender, a command-line interface, and an optional DoWhy bridge from a discovered graph to causal effect estimates and counterfactuals. The library is pip-installable, tested on Python 3.10-3.14, and available at this https URL .

papers.title: Reframing the coupling force of adaptive resolution simulation in terms of the Liouville-type hierarchy for open systems
papers.abstract: In this work, we present a novel perspective on the coupling force employed to compensate the interface artifacts prevalent in adaptive resolution simulations (AdResS) of open many-particle systems. We show that a substantial part of this "thermodynamic force" can be framed in terms of the theoretical model of the Liouville-type hierarchy for open systems. The correspondence is made explicit for the case of a simple atomistic fluid, for which a one-dimensional integral expression is derived. This enables the analysis for dependencies of the thermodynamic force on important simulation parameters, which is taken to inspire both simplifications for the numerical calculation of the thermodynamic force and new criteria for its validation that are adequate to the interfacial nature of the problem. The theoretical claims are then verified in a simulation study of the atomistic supercritical Lennard-Jones fluid at different thermodynamic states.

papers.title: Observer-Assisted Relative-Velocity Compensation with LPV-$H_\infty$ Robust Correction for 3D Trajectory Tracking of Underactuated Non-Minimum-Phase AUVs under Ocean Currents
papers.abstract: This paper develops an observer-assisted control architecture for 3D trajectory tracking of torpedo-type underactuated AUVs with non-minimum-phase sway/heave dynamics under unknown ocean currents. A three-stage state-current observer provides relative-velocity estimates to a nonlinear feedforward term for dominant current rejection and to an LMI-certified LPV-$\mathcal{H}_\infty$ correction layer. Feedback-linearising cancellation yields a constant input matrix, enabling convex synthesis without pairwise cross terms. A residual-level break-even law shows that the effective surge disturbance depends on current-estimation error, while a singular-perturbation analysis proves local practical uniform ultimate boundedness on the embedded LPV model. REMUS simulations over three trajectories and four current scenarios show 89-96% current-estimation reduction, about 99% translational residual reduction, and RMS tracking-error reduction from 4.04 m to 0.24 m.

papers.title: A Maximum Entropy Implementation of Differential Privacy Under Linear Invariants
papers.abstract: Differential privacy is the standard for ensuring data privacy and is widely used in major data publications, including reporting results from the U.S. decennial census. Common implementation of differential privacy uses independent Gaussian or Laplace noise addition to the database. However, there could be aggregate (linear) queries to the database that are excluded from the privacy budget, for example, state totals that can not be perturbed due to constitutional mandates. Any implementation of a differential privacy is required to honor these constraints, also referred to as invariants. Under aggregation constraints, the noise vector is no longer independent and the traditional differential privacy guarantees have to be re-evaluated. We propose a high entropy differential privacy implementation that maintains the aggregation invariants with probability one or exponentially close to one and derive the privacy guarantees for the implementation under the invariants. The theoretical proof also gives a solution to an open question about the null space of correlation matrices. Moreover, the methodology has general use in the context of sampling from normal mixture models under linear equality constraints.

papers.title: First Lattice Calculation of Structure-Dependent Radiative Corrections to Lepton-Flavor-Universality Ratios in Leptonic Decays
papers.abstract: The ratio of electronic to muonic leptonic decay widths, $R_{e/\mu}$, for the light mesons $\pi$ and $K$, provides a clean test of lepton flavor universality (LFU) and a sensitive probe of physics beyond the Standard Model. Its Standard-Model prediction is exceptionally precise, with the leading uncertainty associated with the structure-dependent (SD) radiative correction of $O(0.1\%)$. As experiments such as PIONEER and NA62 aim for unprecedented precision, this SD correction has become an essential ingredient in precision experiment--theory comparisons. We present the first lattice QCD$+$QED calculation of this SD correction at the physical pion mass and in the continuum limit. We employ the infinite-volume reconstruction (IVR) method with Coulomb-gauge photons, significantly reducing both statistical errors and finite-volume effects. We obtain the Standard-Model predictions, $R_{e/\mu}=1.23516(10)\times10^{-4}$ for $\pi$ and $R_{e/\mu}=2.47661(31)\times10^{-5}$ for $K$. Our results reduce the hadronic uncertainty in $R_{e/\mu}$, provide the most precise Standard-Model predictions to date, and establish first-principles benchmarks for future high-precision tests of LFU.

papers.title: Load-induced Taylor-Aris dispersion in compliant electroosmotic pumps with viscoelastic electrolytes
papers.abstract: We investigate the dispersion of a passive, neutral solute in a compliant slit, in which electroosmotic flow drives a viscoelastic electrolyte against an outlet pressure load. The electrolyte is modelled using the simplified Phan-Thien-Tanner model with an inviscid Newtonian solvent. Combining lubrication theory, Debye Huckel linearisation and a local elastic-foundation model, we determine the loaded flow and quantify solute dispersion. A central finding is that hydraulic loading fundamentally alters the thin-electric-double-layer limit of shear dispersion. It was observed that shear dispersion vanishes under free-flow conditions, but an adverse pressure gradient continues to support core shear under load, resulting in a finite dispersion plateau even without flow reversal. This plateau increases with hydraulic loading and is further enhanced by viscoelasticity at a fixed throughput fraction. For Newtonian flow, wall expansion leaves the plateau unchanged under constant-current conditions but increases it under constant-voltage conditions. At finite EDL thicknesses, opposing electroosmotic and pressure-driven shear can partially cancel, improving the plate number despite reduced throughput. The combined effects of shear dispersion, molecular diffusion and transit time produce an optimal EDL thickness at prescribed throughput. Joint optimisation shifts the optimum towards free-flow conditions and thinner EDLs for the range of parameters considered. The predicted plate numbers agree closely with Brownian-dynamics simulations for six benchmark cases. These results establish the role of hydraulic loading and wall compliance in controlling the trade-off between pressure delivery and band broadening in compliant electroosmotic pumps.

papers.title: Diagonally gauged anomaly-free 6D supergravities and their vacua
papers.abstract: We study anomaly-free six-dimensional $N=(1,0)$ supergravities with $n_T=1$ and diagonal $U(1)_{R+}$ or $Sp(1)_{R+}$ gauging. The diagonal group combines R-symmetry with a commuting action on hypermultiplets. We perform bounded searches for anomaly-free models with one or two additional simple gauge group factors of rank at most 30, impose string-charge lattice and positive kinetic term conditions, and tabulate the resulting spectra. The main scans cover $q_{\max}\leq2$ and $d_{\max}\leq3$, where $q_{\max}$ is the largest absolute hyperino charge and $d_{\max}$ the largest diagonal $Sp(1)$ representation dimension, with supplementary searches at larger values. Every hypermultiplet block is required to be nontrivial under at least one additional simple gauge factor. The search has led to a large number of models. Here we give the details of 93 models with $G_+= U(1)_{R+}$ and $q_{\rm max}\le 2$, and 26 models with $G_+=Sp(1)_{R+}$ and $d_{\rm max}\le 3$, and one or two simple group factors. Additional 1341 and 494 models with $G_+=U(1)_{R+}$ with $q_{\rm max}=2$ and $Sp(1)_{R+}$ with $d_{\rm max}=3$, respectively, are posted to the GitHub repository. We establish the existence of supersymmetric Minkowski vacua for all the anomaly free models we have found with $q_{\rm max}=2$ and $d_{\rm max}=3$. We find that such vacua require $q_{\max}>1$ for $U(1)_{R+}$, and $d_{\max}>2$ for $Sp(1)_{R+}$. We also show that every Minkowski vacuum breaks R-symmetry, with the connected unbroken gauge group contained in the additional gauge factors. At two-derivative order, while our anomaly free models do not admit AdS$_6$ solutions, all those with $q_{\rm max} = 2$ and $d_{\rm max}=3$ have non-supersymmetric and unstable dS$_6$ vacua as well.

papers.title: On the effects of emulated quantum layers on CNN performance and explainability for OCT and dementia imaging
papers.abstract: Hybrid quantum-classical convolutional neural networks have been proposed as an alternative to classical deep learning models. However, executing network components on quantum hardware imposes fundamental limitations, such as gradient estimation through repeated measurements, and increasing the number of qubits can lead to trainability problems such as barren plateaus. Moreover, the reported success of these hybrid networks has been linked to quantum architectures that can be efficiently simulated on classical computers. We investigate whether small, classically simulated quantum circuits can serve as useful components within larger models, as a substitute for purely classical layers. We present a systematic comparison between a Hybrid Quantum-inspired CNN (HQiCNN) and standard CNN architectures, where the models differ only in a single intermediate layer: an emulated quantum circuit in the HQiCNN and classical counterparts in the CNN. The models are evaluated on two medical imaging datasets while varying training set size, learning rate, batch size, circuit entanglement and observable se. Under a strict parameter budget, the HQiCNN outperforms the classical baselines. When the classical layer is given more parameters, overall performance becomes comparable, with the HQiCNN showing improvements only in the intermediate-data regime. Removing entanglement yields comparable performance and richer observable sets yield no performance improvement. Finally, we introduce two SHAP-based metrics for comparing model explanations, $|$SHAP$|$IoU and EMD$_{\mathrm{pos}}$. They show that all architectures attend to anatomically plausible regions, and that the spatial attention agreement between them increases with training set size. These results indicate that, under specific data regimes, quantum-inspired hybrid models are a competitive alternative to classical CNNs for medical image classification.

papers.title: Static spheres in black hole spacetimes: pairing, energy conditions, and an upper bound on the innermost radius
papers.abstract: Static spheres---spherical surfaces, located outside the event horizon, on which massive test particles can remain at rest with zero angular momentum relative to asymptotic static observers---have recently attracted some attention. In this work, we investigate their existence, relation to the energy conditions, and radial bounds in general static, spherically symmetric, asymptotically flat black hole spacetimes within general relativity. By analyzing the behavior of a radial function constructed from the mass and radial pressure functions, we prove that, under the weak energy condition (WEC), a static sphere necessarily requires negative radial pressure (tension). Furthermore, for non-extremal black holes satisfying the WEC, we show that any exterior static spheres, if present and non-degenerate, occur in pairs, each consisting of an inner unstable sphere and an outer stable one. Assuming the WEC holds throughout the exterior, the inner static sphere is characterized by a violation of the strong energy condition (SEC), with $\rho+p+2p_T<0$, where $\rho$, $p$, and $p_T$ denote the energy density, radial pressure, and tangential pressure, respectively; the SEC is restored ($\rho+p+2p_T>0$) at the outer sphere; a degenerate static sphere satisfies $\rho+p+2p_T=0$. In addition, focusing on the innermost static sphere and assuming that the WEC holds while the SEC is uniformly violated between the event horizon and this sphere, we derive a rigorous upper bound on its radius. These results establish a direct, analytic link between the energy conditions and the existence of static spheres, and provide a quantitative constraint on the matter environment of black holes possessing such orbits.

papers.title: Spectrogram-Based Joint Detection, Localization, and Classification of Events in Continuously Recorded IBR Waveforms
papers.abstract: Continuously recorded high-resolution power system waveforms capture fast dynamics and transient events. However, extracting actionable insights from these large volumes of data requires automated event detection, temporal localization, and classification. This paper proposes a spectrogram-based framework that jointly detects, localizes, and classifies events in voltage and current waveforms at the terminal of an inverter-based resource (IBR). We recast this problem as a temporal object detection problem using time-frequency representations that explicitly reveal transient and harmonic signatures. The short-time Fourier transform is applied to each waveform channel, and the resulting log-spectrograms are stacked into a multi-channel tensor and processed by a U-Net architecture to jointly estimate event occurrence, temporal boundaries, and event type. A network of the same depth and width operating on raw waveform samples serves as a baseline. Experiments on synthetic single-phase disturbances and three-phase faults in IBR terminal recordings demonstrate that the proposed approach substantially improves event detection and temporal localization compared with the raw-waveform baseline, particularly at finer time-frequency resolutions, while also improving classification accuracy.

papers.title: First-principles calculation of electron-phonon spectral functions for defects using phonon interpolation
papers.abstract: Accurate optical lineshapes of point defects require dense sampling of lattice vibrations, which is challenging for direct first-principles supercell calculations. We introduce a phonon-interpolation method for calculating Huang-Rhys spectral densities and optical lineshapes within the harmonic Franck-Condon framework. By exploiting the spatial localization of transition-induced forces, the method obtains electron-phonon coupling from a tractable defect supercell and samples its vibrational response on dense reciprocal-space grids, avoiding explicit construction and diagonalization of large hypercell dynamical matrices. Applied to the negatively charged nitrogen-vacancy center in diamond, the method resolves low-energy acoustic contributions, the dominant phonon sideband structure, and finer optical-phonon features. The resulting temperature-dependent photoluminescence lineshapes reproduce the main features of experimental spectra after accounting for additional broadening. The approach offers an efficient route to high-resolution defect spectra and can, in principle, complement embedding and machine-learning methods.

papers.title: Model inference from fluid flow in continuum theories of active matter
papers.abstract: Active matter systems are driven out of thermodynamic equilibrium by localized, microscale energy dissipation. While active field theories are highly successful at simulating these non-equilibrium phenomena (the forward problem), characterizing real-world active materials is fundamentally bottle-necked by the difficulty of measuring active stresses directly. This paper addresses the inverse problem using deep learning: model inference and model selection from observable flow field data of active fluids. We formulate an inversion framework applied to two cornerstone paradigms of active continuum physics: Active Model H (representing scalar active matter) and Active Nematics (representing active systems with orientational order). We demonstrate that the kinetic energy spectrum obtained from the fluid flow field preserves a high-fidelity signature of activity to infer parameters of active model H and active nematics. The classification of the models requires comparison using conventional numerical work against predicted parameters. Our deep learning method presents a principled way to bear upon questions of model inference and selection given the flow field data in continuum models of active matter.

papers.title: Band Engineering of Exciton Polaritons in Resonant Polaritonic Metasurfaces
papers.abstract: Polaritonic metasurfaces provide a versatile platform for engineering hybrid light-matter states through the interplay of optical resonances and excitonic excitations. Yet, predictive models often remain phenomenological and rely on coupled-mode equations. Here, we develop an effective Hamiltonian framework for exciton polaritons in resonant polaritonic metasurfaces, derived from a semiclassical single-pole description of excitonic polarization and a Green's-function description of guided-mode resonances. The resulting non-Hermitian Hamiltonian rigorously incorporates resonant photonic harmonics, multiple excitonic degrees of freedom, and radiative losses. The model establishes selection rules for photonic-excitonic coupling governed by orbital multipole index and polarization and identifies one bright excitonic degree of freedom per retained guided harmonic. We apply the framework to a bulk van der Waals WS$_2$ metasurface patterned into a hexagonal lattice of triangular holes and uncover a new geometry-controlled topological transition driven by dipole-quadrupole band inversion, distinct from the conventional breathing-honeycomb-lattice transition. Full-wave simulations confirm the predicted topological phase diagram and the emergence of photonic and polaritonic edge states at a topological interface. Our results establish a theoretical multimode framework for geometry-controlled bandstructure engineering in polaritonic metasurfaces, with applications in topological, chiral, and quantum integrated photonics.

papers.title: The Liouville equation on Riemannian surfaces: the role of volume growth in classification and rigidity results
papers.abstract: We study the Liouville equation $-\Delta_g u = e^u$ on a complete, connected, non-compact, boundaryless Riemannian surface $(M, g)$ with non-negative Ricci curvature. Assuming only some asymptotic lower bound on the solution, we establish classification results for both the solutions and the ambient manifold, discussing also their optimality. Our results reveal a close connection between the volume growth of the manifold and the classification of both the solutions and the underlying manifold.

papers.title: Interface-Confined Superconductivity with Thickness-Independent Superfluid Stiffness in (Pb,Sn)Te/FeTe Bilayers
papers.abstract: Interface-induced superconductivity in FeTe-based heterostructures provides a promising route toward topological superconductivity, yet the roles of the neighboring layers topology, symmetry, and electronic structure remain unresolved. In this work, we employ molecular beam epitaxy to grow Pb1-xSnxTe/FeTe bilayers and use angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy to track the evolution of the Pb1-xSnxTe layer from a trivial insulator to a topological crystalline insulator hosting multiple Dirac surface states. Electrical transport measurements reveal robust superconductivity throughout the entire composition range, with a nearly constant superconducting transition temperature of ~12 K despite substantial changes in the electronic structure and topology of Pb1-xSnxTe. Double-coil mutual-inductance measurements further reveal comparable superfluid stiffness across the topological phase transition and nearly thickness-independent superfluid stiffness despite large variations in the constituent-layer thicknesses, demonstrating that superconductivity is confined near the interface. These results establish that superconductivity in FeTe-based heterostructures is largely insensitive to the topology, crystal symmetry, and detailed electronic structure of the neighboring layer, supporting a primary origin in modifications to the FeTe layer. The coexistence of interface-confined superconductivity and tunable multiple Dirac surface states in Pb1-xSnxTe/FeTe bilayers provides a versatile platform for exploring topological superconductivity and interactions among multiple Majorana zero modes.

papers.title: Continuous Time Quantum Walk Propagation for Irregular Temporal Graph Forecasting
papers.abstract: Continuous time quantum walks built on graph Laplacians produce non monotonic graph propagation features through quantum interference during evolution, which classical diffusion cannot achieve. Such walks deliver a physically motivated propagation scheme for temporal graph signal modeling. We propose Quantum Walk Temporal Architecture (QWTA), which replaces classical graph propagation with a CTQW-type parameterized spectral propagator. QWTA embeds effective observation intervals into the spectral phase modulation of the propagation kernel. QWTA-Base preserves exact CTQW spectral evolution and serves as a physically faithful propagation reference. QWTA-GR further introduces phase soft clipping and gated residual fusion to stabilize propagation. The results show that explicit phase encoding of irregular time intervals, when combined with suitable stabilization, provides a physically motivated and competitive graph propagation design for temporal graph forecasting with missing historical observations.

papers.title: Transmit Coefficients and Receive Combining Vector Design for OTA-FL with Imperfect CSI
papers.abstract: Over-the-air (OTA) computation has recently gained significant attentions as an effective approach to enhance the communication efficiency of wireless federated learning (FL). By enabling simultaneous transmission and aggregation of local model updates, OTA-FL can substantially reduce both latency and bandwidth consumption. However, a key challenge lies in the imperfect aggregation of global models caused by channel state information (CSI) uncertainty, which introduces distortion to the final learning performance. To address this issue, we study the long-term mean squared error (MSE) minimization problem for OTA-FL under imperfect CSI conditions. Through convergence analysis, we establish an upper bound for the time-averaged MSE, thereby revealing the effect of aggregation errors accumulated throughout multiple communication rounds on the overall training performances. Based on this analysis, an optimization framework is developed to minimize the long-term MSE via the joint design of (i) transmit coefficients at the local devices and (ii) receive combining vectors at the parameter server (PS). Since this alternating optimization approach requires non-causal CSI, a Lyapunov-based optimization method is further introduced to handle causal CSI scenarios. By incorporating virtual queues to characterize long-term energy consumption, the proposed method effectively decouples temporal dependencies and allows transmit coefficients to be optimized based on the causal CSI of each aggregation round. Comprehensive evaluations on Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 datasets have demonstrated that the proposed algorithms can significantly reduce the degradation of test accuracy caused by imperfect CSI. Comparisons with other benchmark schemes further verify the superiority of our proposed algorithms.

papers.title: Deep Adaptive Bayesian Screening
papers.abstract: We introduce Deep Adaptive Bayesian Screening (DABS), a method for performing adaptive factorial screening in discrete design spaces under tight experimental budgets. DABS learns a policy network offline to sequentially select informative experiments, amortizing Bayesian Optimal Experimental Design. It handles binary designs, incorporates sparsity and interactions via a spike-and-slab prior with strong heredity. The model is trained using a contrastive lower bound on information about factor activity with nuisance effect sizes and noise variance analytically integrated out. Unlike prior amortized Bayesian design approaches, DABS also integrates posterior inference at deployment, yielding posterior probabilities of factor activity and credible intervals on effect sizes. We evaluate DABS on simulated screening problems calibrated to published experimental benchmarks, and show that it matches or outperforms the strongest non-adaptive Bayesian baseline, with the largest gains when the budget is small relative to the number of candidate factors.

papers.title: Scalable Attention for 5G NR Channel Estimation
papers.abstract: Attention-based neural estimators achieve strong channel-estimation accuracy, but the computational cost of global attention over the time-frequency resource grid grows quadratically with the number of subcarriers, and these estimators are typically tied to a single resource allocation. This paper proposes Channel Estimation Attention (CHEA), a low-complexity channel estimator for 5G New Radio (5G NR) multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO). CHEA replaces global attention with a multi-resolution windowed design: a high-resolution encoder preserves local pilot detail, a low-resolution encoder captures wider frequency-domain context, and a local cross-attention decoder transfers this coarse context back to the high-resolution pilot tokens. A per-Physical Resource Block (PRB) upsampling module then reconstructs the channel over the full slot. Because every attention operation is confined to a fixed-size window and reconstruction is performed per PRB, the cost of CHEA scales linearly with the number of subcarriers, and a single trained model supports different PRB allocations without retraining. On a standard-compliant Physical Uplink Shared Channel (PUSCH), CHEA achieves the lowest Mean Squared Error (MSE) among conventional and state-of-the-art neural estimators, while requiring 2.8x to 22.0x lower operations than existing attention-based estimators.

papers.title: Quantitative Theory for the Amplitude of Fluorescence Quantum Beats from Geminate Triplet-Pair Fusion
papers.abstract: We derive the amplitude of fluorescence quantum beats caused by geminate triplet-exciton fusion from the full set of parameters that characterize singlet fission and triplet exciton dynamics. We apply the theory to tetracene and rubrene single crystals. We find that the amplitude depends on the fission time in tetracene, but does not do so in rubrene, where it is determined by the dimensionality of triplet transport. Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations reproduce the experimental data in both materials, for a fission time of the order of 200 ps and isotropic triplet transport in tetracene, and for a triplet hopping time along the herringbone axis of 200-300 ps and anisotropic transport in rubrene.

papers.title: The Norton Theorem for Quantum Circuits and Systems
papers.abstract: It is well known that classical analog circuits and systems benefit from the powerful Thevenin and Norton theorems. These theorems enable rigorous and exact mathematical simplification and representation of the effect of the rest of a system on the part we want to focus on. We show that there are corresponding versions of a "Quantum Norton Theorem" that enable exact simplification and reduction for quantum circuits and systems, not just for one port, but also for multiport and even open quantum systems. We demonstrate the method on two level systems, chains, system environment partitions, Lindblad examples, and Grover search. The Grover examples show how the reduced network isolates the bright pole governing ideal search and exposes how diagonal disorder transfers spectral weight into dark poles that degrade performance. By partitioning finite dimensional Schrodinger dynamics into retained and eliminated sectors, we show that Gaussian elimination gives an exact reduced equation in which the eliminated subsystem appears as a dynamical self energy and a source term. In the circuit representation, these terms become the Norton admittance and Norton current source seen by the retained quantum port.
