Here, we combine fluorescence recovery after photobleaching (FRAP) with fluorescence correlation spectroscopy (FCS) and calibrated fluorescence imaging to disentangle partitioning, interfacial resistance, and differences in diffusion inside and outside of condensates. Applying this approach to polyelectrolyte condensates across a range of salt concentrations, we find substantial, salt-dependent interfacial resistance, which causes molecules to undergo multiple rounds of internal mixing before escaping. DDX4-YFP condensates in living cells also exhibit substantial interfacial resistance, although they are more permeable than polyelectrolyte condensates with comparable partition coefficients. Our results indicate that interfacial resistance is a tunable property of condensates that can place them in distinct transport regimes, favoring distinct functions such as dynamic reaction crucibles or insulated molecular sinks.

papers.title: Image Rotation Angle Estimation: Five Circular-Aware Methods Across Sixteen Architectures
Constraints on the Physical Association between ICECAT1 Neutrinos and Fast Radio Bursts Using the Second CHIME/FRB Catalogue
papers.abstract: We present a search for neutrino counterparts to fast radio bursts (FRBs) using temporal and spatial cross-matching between the 1423 non-repeating FRBs of the Second CHIME/FRB catalogue and the 73 alerts of the IceCube high-energy alert-track catalogue ICECAT1 from 2018 July 25 to 2020 December 31. Because current FRB-neutrino models do not agree on the emission order, we adopt a two-sided temporal hypothesis and define the significance criterion from the expected number of chance coincidences before the search. We find no statistically significant association: no pair lies within the $3\sigma$ and $5\sigma$ coincidence windows of $3.50 \times 10^2$ s and $7.43 \times 10^{-2}$ s, and the pair closest in time, FRB20190630C-IC190629A, is consistent with a chance coincidence ($p = 0.254$, $0.66\sigma$). Using a population-level stacking analysis, we derive 90% upper limits on the neutrino-to-radio luminosity ratio of FRBs, $\xi \lesssim 1.4 \times 10^{11}$ for a neutrino spectral index $\gamma=1.0$ to $6.8 \times 10^{12}$ for $\gamma=3.0$, assuming neutrino emission within the burst duration. For a neutrino number spectrum $dN/d\epsilon \propto \epsilon^{-2}$, the corresponding limit on the neutrino fluence per burst is about a factor of 4 below those of previous stacking searches. For $\gamma=2$, the limits on the isotropic neutrino energy, $10^{49}$-$10^{52}$ erg, lie more than five orders of magnitude above the predictions of magnetar-driven shock models, so the present data do not constrain these models. Nevertheless, our blind significance criterion and population-stacking limits provide a baseline for future multi-messenger searches.

papers.title: Template-Driven Machine Learning Standardization for Large Model Fleets
Dynamics of O(2) excitations in a non-reciprocal medium
papers.abstract: We investigate emergent dynamics due to non-reciprocity in the O(2) model. The lattice XY model, where non-reciprocity stems from vision cone like couplings, can be described by a continuum description in which non-reciprocity translates into a new term depending on the rotational of the orientation field. We argue that non-reciprocity is akin to activity and we highlight the connection between our hydrodynamic equation and the constant density Toner-Tu framework. The active force advects and reshapes patterns, a generic feature found in many non-reciprocal systems. We show how 1d excitations in the non-reciprocal O(2) model can be described by a generalized Burgers equation, derived from our continuum model. We then extend the results to 2d perturbations. As such, we establish the first principles of excitation trajectory control in a non-reciprocal O(2) medium. Concretely, we explain how tuning the degree of non-reciprocity and the orientation of the background medium impacts the time evolution of excitations. We also showcase how initially different excitations lead to very different dynamical behavior. Non-reciprocity also affects the stability of defect-free excitations with non-zero winding numbers and, unlike in its equilibrium O(2) counterpart, enables the system, above a certain threshold, to relax to its ground state.

papers.title: GateSID: One Gate to Balance Semantic and Collaborative Signals across the Item Lifecycle
NemoANN: I/O-Efficient Filtered Vector Search on SSDs with Graph Tunneling
Quasi-local thermodynamics of Kerr-Newman black holes: Pressure, volume, and shear work
papers.abstract: While the quasi-local thermodynamics of spherically symmetric black holes is well described by pressure and volume, extending this framework to rotating spacetimes poses a significant challenge. Rotation induces an oblate deformation of the horizon, breaking the direct functional dependence between geometric volume and area. In this work, we resolve this difficulty by establishing a quasi-local thermodynamic framework for Kerr-Newman black holes. We demonstrate that accommodating this kinematic deformation requires extending the thermodynamic phase space to include a geometric eccentricity parameter $Y$ and its conjugate, a thermodynamic shear tension $X$. Consequently, the rotational contribution is incorporated into the first law with a shear work term $X dY$. We derive the generalized first laws and Smarr formulas (Euler relations) for both the internal energy and enthalpy representations, showing that these thermodynamic potentials can be obtained through Legendre transformations that isolate the quasi-local energy from the rotational energy. Thus, this framework provides a novel perspective on the thermodynamics of rotating black holes, integrating the geometric deformation of the horizon into a quasi-local description.

papers.title: Combinatorial Properties Related to the Higher Baumgartner's Axiom
papers.abstract: We isolate two combinatorial properties, each expressible by a $\Pi_2$-sentence over the structure $(H(\omega_3),\in,\omega_1,\omega_2,\text{NS}_{\omega_2})$, such that each property is consistent with CH, and their conjunction together with $2^\omega \le \omega_2$ and $2^{\omega_1} = 2^{\omega_2} = \omega_3$ implies the existence of a c.c.c. forcing which forces the higher Baumgartner's axiom.

papers.title: Learning to Watermark the Denoising Trajectory: Fast and Robust Watermarks for Diffusion Models
CAF-Score: Calibrating CLAP with LALMs for Reference-free Audio-Text Alignment Evaluation
Enhancing Multi-Corpus Training in SSL-Based Anti-Spoofing Models: Domain-Invariant Feature Extraction
The Ferrers bound for spanning trees in bipartite graphs
papers.abstract: We prove Ehrenborg's conjecture that every connected bipartite graph $G$ with parts of size $m$ and $n$ has at most $\frac{1}{mn}\prod_{v\in V(G)} \operatorname{deg}(v)$ spanning trees, and that equality holds if and only if $G$ is a Ferrers graph.

papers.title: A Noise Sensitivity Exponent Controls Large Statistical-to-Computational Gaps in Single- and Multi-Index Models
papers.abstract: Understanding when learning is statistically possible yet computationally hard is a central challenge in high-dimensional statistics. In this work, we investigate this question in the context of single- and multi-index models, classes of functions widely studied as benchmarks to probe the ability of machine learning methods to discover features in high-dimensional data. Our main contribution is to show that a Noise Sensitivity Exponent (NSE) - a simple quantity determined by the activation function - governs the existence and magnitude of statistical-to-computational gaps within a broad regime of these models. We first establish that, in single-index models with large additive noise, the onset of a computational bottleneck is fully characterized by the NSE. We then demonstrate that the same exponent controls a statistical-computational gap in the specialization transition of large separable multi-index models, where individual components become learnable. Finally, in hierarchical multi-index models, we show that the NSE governs the optimal computational rate in which different directions are sequentially learned. Taken together, our results identify the NSE as a unifying property linking noise robustness, computational hardness, and feature specialization in high-dimensional learning.

papers.title: Kinematic Foundations of Defect-Mediated Plasticity: A Gauge-Theoretic Framework
papers.abstract: Plastic deformation is widely regarded as an intrinsically dissipative phenomenon whose theoretical description relies heavily on phenomenological constitutive assumptions. We argue instead that defect-mediated plasticity possesses a universal, non-dissipative backbone: the kinematics and mobility constraints of defects are fixed by symmetry and conservation laws prior to dissipation. Starting from the spontaneous breaking of spacetime symmetries in a crystalline phase, we construct an effective field theory in which elasticity reorganizes into a coupled higher-rank tensor-vector gauge structure emerging directly from stress and defect conservation laws rather than being postulated microscopically. Dislocations, disclinations, and singular frame-geometric configurations appear as gauge sources whose coupled continuity equations and mobility constraints follow from generalized Gauss laws. The construction provides a symmetry-based organization of the kinematic sectors relevant to defect-mediated plasticity and a starting point for a subsequent dissipative theory of defect motion and stress relaxation.

papers.title: Geometric structures of $G$-fans associated with rank $3$ cluster-cyclic exchange matrices
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the geometric structures of $G$-fans associated with rank $3$ real cluster-cyclic exchange matrices. In this class, a simple recursion for tropical signs was found, which enables us to study the detailed properties of $c$-, $g$-vectors. We introduce two kinds of upper bounds of the $G$-fans. The first one is the global upper bound, which comes from a hyperbolic surface containing all $g$-vectors after an initial mutation. The second one is the local upper bound, which reflects the internal separateness structure. As applications, we prove that there is no periodicity among $g$-vectors, and we completely determine the sign of $g$-vectors. We also prove the monotonicity of $g$-vectors under the minimum assumption. Moreover, we show that the three global upper bounds can be simplified to a single uniform upper bound.

papers.title: Optical Magnus effect on gravitational lensing
papers.abstract: The optical Magnus effect refers to a transverse shift of a trajectory of light caused by its polarization and arises as a correction to geometrical optics at the linear order in wavelength. Here, we start from Maxwell's equations in a curved spacetime to derive the equations of motion for a wave packet of circularly polarized light, which confirm the known results involving the helicity-dependent anomalous velocity with some generalization and clarification. We then study possible consequences of the optical Magnus effect on gravitational lensing in the Schwarzschild spacetime as well as in an expanding spacetime with a weak gravitational potential. Among others, by formulating a lens equation modified to incorporate the optical Magnus effect, the Einstein ring is found impossible to emerge from a point source for any axially symmetric thin lens. Analytic solutions to the modified lens equation are also obtained for simple lens models, illuminating how image formation is affected by the optical Magnus effect.

papers.title: A superposition approach for the ISS Lyapunov-Krasovskii theorem with pointwise dissipation
papers.abstract: For nonlinear time-delay systems, we show that the existence of a Lyapunov-Krasovskii functional (LKF) with pointwise dissipation (i.e., dissipation in terms of the current solution norm) suffices for input-to-state stability, provided that uniform global stability can also be ensured using the same LKF. To this end, we employ elements of a recently developed stability theory in which the behavior of solutions is not assessed through the classical norm but rather through a specific LKF. As a consequence of our results, we obtain a strengthening and extension of the classical Lyapunov-Krasovskii theorem for undisturbed systems to systems with uniformly bounded disturbances. We discuss the advantages of our approach by means of an example.

papers.title: Pulsar timing arrays: the emerging gravitational-wave landscape
papers.abstract: Pulsar Timing Array (PTA) experiments have found evidence for a nanoHertz gravitational wave (GW) background (GWB). The challenge is now to turn evidence for a GWB into an understanding of the sources and physics that produce it. This review connects the physics of the Hellings--Downs correlation to the interpretation of the GWB spectrum and anisotropy, asking whether supermassive black hole binary populations consistent with electromagnetic observations can explain the signal. Searches for individual binaries take these questions further: multi-messenger observations and pulsar terms can reveal the evolution of these binary systems. Realizing this potential requires reliable noise models and candidate validation. We explain how pulsar noise, unresolved sources, and incomplete sky coverage limit these inferences. The same PTA observations also probe cosmic strings and ultralight dark matter, while fitted timing parameters extend GW searches to picohertz frequencies and enable measurements of Galactic acceleration. Rapid data combination and the larger, more precisely timed arrays expected from the Square Kilometre Array Observatory and Deep Synoptic Array will increase the sensitivity of these searches and measurements, sharpening our view of the emerging GW landscape.

papers.title: The Challenge of Out-Of-Distribution Detection in Motor Imagery BCIs
Conformal Vacua in Boundary-Glued AdS$_3$
papers.abstract: We argue that the purely topological gluing of AdS$_3$ spacetimes, which are otherwise independent due to Dirichlet boundary conditions, can still produce non-trivial spaces after a quotient. In this direction, we extend the study of a recently discovered non-orientable AdS$_3$, which is a $\mathbb Z_2$ quotient of two AdS$_3$ spaces glued along their conformal boundaries. We find that this space is compact and boundaryless and that the quotient sends the gluing surface to a torus comprised of a null lattice with halved periods. However, the bulk wraps around both its sides, which means that as an embedded space this gluing surface forms a one-sided torus. We discover that it supports a permutation-twisted sector of two CFT$_2$s with shared Dirichlet boundary conditions and conjecture that conformal maps can be extended across this gluing surface. Using this extension, we show that the vacuum of pairs of Rindler wedges, which share a boundary in this non-orientable AdS$_3\times$S$^2$ space, are conformal to static patch vacua, which are supported on two dS$_4\times \mathbb R$ glued together at their conformal boundaries.

papers.title: Every 3-connected $\{K_{1,4},K_{1,4}+e\}$-free split graph of order at least 13 is Hamilton-connected
papers.abstract: A graph is split if its vertex set can be partitioned into a clique and an independent set. Let $K_{1,4}+e$ denote the graph obtained from $K_{1,4}$ by adding an edge between two leaves. Ryjáček et al. [J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 134 (2019), 239--263] conjectured that every $4$-connected graph with minimum degree at least 6 that contains neither $K_{1,4}$ nor $K_{1,4}+e$ as an induced subgraph is Hamiltonian. They proved the conclusion for $5$-connected graphs with the same minimum degree bound. We prove that every $3$-connected split graph of order at least 13 that contains neither of these induced subgraphs is Hamilton-connected. Together with Dirac's theorem, this proves the conjecture of Ryjáček et al. for split graphs.

papers.title: TERMINATOR: Learning Optimal Exit Points for Early Stopping in Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
Towards Generalist Models for Molecular Property Prediction: Distilling Verbalized Knowledge from Decision Trees
Gradient-robustness in optimization subject to stationary Navier-Stokes equations
papers.abstract: In this article, we discuss gradient robust discretizations for the simulation of non-linear incompressible Navier-Stokes problem and the optimal control of such flow. We consider several formulations of the flow problem that are equivalent for the continuous non-linear forward problem and compare their gradient robust discretization. We will then discuss the influence of the chosen formulation on the adjoint equations needed for gradient computation in the solution of the optimal control problem.

papers.title: Trustworthy Calibration or Vulnerability? Unveiling the Over-Calibration Paradox and Attack Surface in Rashomon Sets
Performance Analysis of Discrete-Phase Fluid Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface-Enabled Index Modulation
Linear response of the Chern insulator MnBi$_2$Te$_4$: A Wannier function approach
papers.abstract: Recent work demonstrated that in the long wavelength limit the linear response of a Chern insulator to finite-frequency electric fields is the sum of two terms: A general frequency-dependent Kubo contribution that is present irrespective of band topology, and a topological Hall term that vanishes for topologically trivial insulators. Motivated by recent experiments and theoretical predictions, we use these expressions to calculate the optical conductivity and susceptibility of intrinsically magnetic MnBi$_2$Te$_4$ thin films with one, four, five, and eleven septuple layers by combining density functional theory with "single-shot" Wannier functions. To characterize the underlying topology of these systems, we compute the two-dimensional Chern number of these films using recently derived global expressions formulated in terms of Bloch energies and velocity matrix elements; the use of these expressions allows us to circumvent numerical issues at band crossings. Films with eleven septuple layers are of particular interest. We find that they have the same Chern number as five septuple layer films, in contrast to the reported "higher Chern-number phase" of these systems in other studies; we discuss a few possible reasons for the discrepancy. A layer-resolved decomposition of the static reactive susceptibility reveals a non-uniform spatial distribution, with interlayer contributions dominating over intralayer contributions and the bulk layers accounting for nearly 70% of the total response. We also identify spin-orbit coupling-driven band inversions as a possible indicator of these topological phases.

papers.title: When Slots Compete: Slot Merging in Object-Centric Learning
Anomaly detection using surprisals
papers.abstract: Anomaly detection methods are widely used but often rely on ad hoc rules or strong assumptions, and they often focus on tail events, missing "inlier" anomalies that occur in low-density gaps between modes. We propose a unified framework that defines an anomaly as an observation with unusually low probability under a (possibly mis-specified) model. For each observation we compute its surprisal (the negative log generalized density) and define an anomaly score as the probability of a surprisal at least as large as that observed. This reduces anomaly detection for complex univariate or multivariate data to estimating the upper tail of a univariate surprisal distribution. We develop two model-robust approximations to these tail probabilities: an empirical approximation based on the observed surprisal distribution and a GPD approximation that fits a Generalized Pareto Distribution above a high threshold. For the empirical approximation we give conditions under which tail ordering is preserved and derive finite-sample confidence guarantees via the Dvoretzky-Kiefer-Wolfowitz inequality. For the GPD approximation we establish broad tail conditions ensuring classical extreme-value behavior. Simulations and applications to French mortality, Test-cricket and Old Faithful geyser data show the approach remains effective under substantial model mis-specification.

papers.title: Correlation between nuclear isospin asymmetry and $α$-particle preformation probability for superheavy nuclei from a Bayesian inference
papers.abstract: In the study of $\alpha$ decay within the superheavy nuclear region ($Z \geq 90$ and $N \geq 140$), the $\alpha$-particle preformation probability $P_{\alpha}$ serves as a crucial physical quantity linking nuclear structure to decay observables. We introduce a phenomenological model incorporating the decay energy $Q_{\alpha}$, mass number $A$, orbital angular momentum $l$, isospin asymmetry $I$, and unpaired nucleon effect. For the first time, a Bayesian inference method combined with Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling has been employed to impose global constraints on the model parameters, enabling the systematic and high-precision calculation of $P_{\alpha}$. The results reveal a significant suppressing effect of isospin asymmetry on $P_{\alpha}$, a finding independently corroborated by random forest-based feature importance analysis, which identified $I$ as a dominant factor. Furthermore, calculations using the maximum a posteriori (MAP) parameters not only reproduce the shell effect at $N=152$ but also yield $\alpha$ decay half-life predictions in excellent agreement with experimental ones, thereby validating this model universality. This work provides the first global analysis tool for probing the $\alpha$ preformation mechanism in superheavy nuclei, underscores the potential of the Bayesian framework for inverting complex nuclear physics problems, and establishes a reliable theoretical benchmark for guiding future experimental exploration of superheavy nuclei.

papers.title: RL unknotter, hard unknots and unknotting number
papers.abstract: We train a reinforcement learning agent to simplify hard unknot diagrams and pair it with a learned crossing selector to search for short unknotting sequences. Three examples found by the agent lead to an infinite family of prime two-bridge knots of unknotting number three whose connected sums with the figure-eight knot also have unknotting number three, and fifteen new unknotting upper bounds were found on the set of prime knots up to 13 crossings.

papers.title: BPS vortex from nonpolynomial scalar QED in a $\mathbb{C}\mathrm{P}^1$-Maxwell theory
papers.abstract: We investigate a generalized gauged $\mathbb{C}\mathrm{P}^1$-Maxwell theory in which the electromagnetic sector acquires a field-dependent magnetic permeability generated dynamically through fermionic vacuum polarization. We couple a Dirac fermion with an effective mass to a gauged $\mathbb{C}\mathrm{P}^1$ sigma model whose target space carries the Fubini-Study metric. Integrating out the Dirac fermion at one loop induces a logarithmic correction to the Maxwell kinetic term. This dependence is retained in the planar effective theory after dimensional reduction. Within this framework, one builds a generalized $\mathbb{C}\mathrm{P}^1$-Maxwell model by admitting Bogomol'nyi-Prasad-Sommerfield (BPS) configurations. Taking this into account, we solved the self-dual equations that describe vortex-like solutions with quantized magnetic flux.

papers.title: Three heteroclinic orbits induce a countable family of equivalence classes of regular flows
papers.abstract: We solve the problem of topological classification for smooth structurally stable flows on closed four-dimensional manifolds, the non-wandering set of which contains exactly two saddle equilibria, and the wandering set contains isolated trajectories connecting these saddle equilibria (heteroclinic curves). In particular, we show that for a flow of the class under consideration on $\mathbb{CP}^2$, the number of heteroclinic curves is a complete topological invariant, while on the sphere $\mathbb S^4$, there exists a countably many equivalence classes with an arbitrary odd number $\gamma\geq 3$ of heteroclinic curves. These results contrast with a three-dimensional case, where under similar conditions there exists only finite set of equivalence classes for each number of heteroclinic curves.

papers.title: How Private Are DNA Embeddings? Inverting Foundation Model Representations of Genomic Sequences
papers.abstract: Genomic foundation models are increasingly used to share dense representations rather than raw DNA sequences. This is particularly pursued for mean-pooled representations that are later used for downstream prediction tasks. Whether this practice protects the privacy of the underlying sequence is largely unknown. We evaluated model-inversions against zero-shot embeddings from DNABERT-2, Evo 2, and Nucleotide Transformer v2 (NTv2). Substantial reconstruction remains possible: a single multi-length Length-Conditioned Query Decoder reconstructed NTv2 sequences with mean Levenshtein similarity from 0.98 at 10 nucleotides to 0.68 at 100, and Evo 2 sequences from nearly 1.00 at 15 nucleotides to 0.67 at 100. DNABERT-2 showed higher resistance (0.56 to 0.51), although it remained above the random baseline at short lengths. Therefore, we further evaluated, whether a linkage attack similar to Homer's attack is possible based on the mean-pooled representations of human DNA sequences. At SNP-enriched length-25 loci and known coordinates, Evo 2 and NTv2 reached 99\% identification at 32 loci and DNABERT-2 at 256 loci. With alignment-based coordinate recovery, the corresponding 99\% budgets were 64 and 128 loci for Evo 2 and NTv2, while DNABERT-2 did not reach the reported identification thresholds. Random loci required larger budgets. These findings show that mean-pooled embeddings can leak sequence and identity, with risk depending on sequence length, representation, locus informativeness, and coordinate information.

papers.title: Spatial Calibration of Diffuse LiDARs
Thermodynamics of Coupled Transport: Quantum Dots as a Model System
papers.abstract: This review presents a thermodynamic perspective on quantum coupled transport processes in nanoscale systems. Our analysis is formulated within the framework of the entropy production rate, the central quantity governing non-equilibrium processes and expressed through conjugate force-flux pairs. Although thermodynamic laws are universal across classical and quantum domains, the discussion is developed within a microscopic open quantum system framework, focusing on quantum dots (QDs) coupled to electronic reservoirs. We first examine elementary single transport processes and highlight their strong thermodynamic constraints in the near-equilibrium regime. This motivates the study of coupled transport, where multiple force-flux pairs coexist and interact, leading to richer thermodynamic behaviour. Using entropy production as the guiding principle, we analyse coupled energy and particle transport in a minimal two-terminal single-QD setup and show how conventional thermoelectric phenomena, including Seebeck and Peltier effects as well as thermoelectric heat engines and refrigerators, naturally emerge as thermodynamic cross-effects. We then extend the framework to a three-terminal coupled quantum dot (CQD) geometry, which provides a versatile platform for studying coupled transport and reduces, under suitable constraints, to the well-known Sánchez-Büttiker configuration. Beyond standard cross-effects, we discuss the phenomenon of inverse currents in coupled transport (ICC), where a current flows against mutually parallel thermodynamic forces without violating the second law. We show that ICC requires breaking the symmetry between energy and particle transport and identify the conditions for its realization in coupled quantum-dot systems with attractive interdot interactions.

papers.title: Skeleton-to-Image Encoding: Enabling Skeleton Representation Learning via Vision-Pretrained Models
Human-Data Interaction, Exploration, and Visualization Systems in the AI Era: Challenges and Opportunities
RepoLaunch: Automating Build and Management of Code Repositories across Languages and Platforms
Beyond Text: Text-Image Fusion for Scalable Two-Tower Retrieval
Designing and Validating a Self-Aligning Tool Changer for Modular Reconfigurable Manipulation Robots
Gait Generation Balancing Joint Load and Mobility for Legged Modular Robots with Easily Detachable Joints
SGR3 Model: Scene Graph Retrieval-Reasoning Model in 3D
Generalized Bayes for Causal Inference
papers.abstract: Uncertainty quantification is central to many applications of causal machine learning, yet principled Bayesian inference for causal effects remains challenging. Standard Bayesian approaches typically require specifying a probabilistic model for the data-generating process, including high-dimensional nuisance components such as propensity scores and outcome regressions. Standard posteriors are thus vulnerable to strong modeling choices, including complex prior elicitation. In this paper, we propose a generalized Bayesian framework for causal inference. Our framework avoids explicit likelihood modeling; instead, we place priors directly on the causal estimands and update these using an identification-driven loss function, which yields generalized posteriors for causal effects. As a result, our framework turns existing loss-based causal estimators into estimators with full uncertainty quantification. Our framework is flexible and applicable to a broad range of causal estimands (e.g., ATE, CATE). Further, our framework can be applied on top of state-of-the-art causal machine learning pipelines (e.g., Neyman-orthogonal meta-learners). For Neyman-orthogonal losses, we show that the generalized posteriors converge to their oracle counterparts and remain robust to first-stage nuisance estimation error. With calibration, we thus obtain valid frequentist uncertainty even when nuisance estimators converge at slower-than-parametric rates. Empirically, we demonstrate that our proposed framework offers causal effect estimation with calibrated uncertainty across several causal inference settings. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first flexible framework for constructing generalized Bayesian posteriors for causal machine learning.

papers.title: Nuclear interference by electronic de-orthogonalisation
papers.abstract: Interference is a universal consequence of superposition, yet in composite quantum systems it can encode correlations between subsystems. We show that in coupled electron-nuclear dynamics, interference in the nuclear density can arise dynamically even when it is initially absent. Starting from a superposition of orthogonal Born-Oppenheimer electronic states, we demonstrate within the exact factorisation framework that genuine non-adiabatic electron-nuclear correlations induce de-orthogonalisation of the electronic factors, thereby generating interference terms in the nuclear density. Such interference has no counterpart in adiabatic evolution. Unlike conventional nuclear wave-packet interference or interference that merely reflects electronic coherence in a chosen basis, the effect identified here is a manifestation of the compositeness of the full electron-nuclear state. Nuclear density interference thus emerges as a direct dynamical signature of correlated quantum motion in composite systems.

papers.title: How Controllable Are Large Language Models? A Unified Evaluation across Behavioral Granularities
A Comparative Study of UMAP and Other Dimensionality Reduction Methods
The Poincaré polynomial of the type B analogue of $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0,n+1}$
papers.abstract: We establish formulas for the Poincaré polynomial of the type B analogue of the Deligne--Knudsen--Mumford moduli space of rational curves with n marked points, providing type B counterparts to results by Keel, Manin, Getzler, and Yuzvinsky. We establish functional and differential equations satisfied by the bivariate exponential generating function of these polynomials. We show how this generating function relates to the classical one in type A. We deduce the gamma-positivity of these polynomials via a quadratic recursion and discuss a type B analogue of a formula found by Aluffi, Marcolli and Nascimento in type A.

papers.title: On the Stability Connection Between Discrete-Time Algorithms and Their Resolution ODEs: Applications to Min-Max Optimisation
papers.abstract: We establish a connection between the stability of discrete-time algorithms (DTAs) and continuous-time dynamical systems, in particular their $O(s^r)$-resolution ordinary differential equations (ODEs). We show that exponential stability of a common equilibrium transfers to the DTA whenever the one-step error is small relative to the distance to the equilibrium and the one-step Lyapunov decay. This condition is sharp in order, and one-step consistency alone is insufficient. The result is local and allows step-size-dependent ODEs and Lyapunov functions, covering $O(s)$-resolution ODEs whose decay rate vanishes as the step size tends to zero. Asymptotic stability is not inherited in general, but a comparison criterion and a checkable compatibility condition ensure it carries over for equilibria and compact sets. For resolution ODEs, joint regularity of the update map guarantees the required error bound. We apply the framework to two-timescale gradient descent ascent (TT-GDA), generalised extragradient, two-timescale proximal point, and (regularised) damped Newton, showing that for small step sizes and suitable parameters, every saddle point with invertible Hessian is locally exponentially stable for all but TT-GDA. For degenerate saddle points, the framework yields asymptotic stability and convergence rates.

papers.title: Krall-Type Orthogonal Polynomials and Integrable Isomonodromic Deformations
papers.abstract: Krall-type polynomials are orthogonal polynomials for a Stieltjes measure obtained by adding jumps at the boundary of the orthogonality interval of either the generalized Laguerre polynomials or the Jacobi polynomials. We show that both the recurrence relations and the second-order linear differential equations defining these polynomials are explicitly determined in terms of specific solutions of certain integrable systems. When only one jump is present, this leads to integrable cases of the Painlevé III or the Painlevé V equation. In the case of two jumps, first studied by Koornwinder [Canad. Math. Bull. 27 (1984), 205-214], we obtain a new integrable system of partial differential equations of Schlesinger type. When the jumps are equal and the starting polynomials are the Gegenbauer polynomials, this system reduces to an integrable case of the Painlevé V equation.

papers.title: Clawdrain: Exploiting Tool-Calling Chains for Stealthy Token Exhaustion in OpenClaw Agents
Unified Ranking Across Retrieval Channels: A Large-Scale E-Commerce Approach
MediX-R1: Open Ended Medical Reinforcement Learning
Approximating parametric suprema for constructible and power-constructible functions
papers.abstract: We prove that one may approximate parametric suprema of constructible and power-constructible functions using functions within the same class. This resolves a conjecture by Adiceam and Cluckers, which was posited after studying a question posed by Sarnak. We apply our result to prove that a certain subclass of Cexp-class distributions is tempered and to make uniform a bound concerning pushforward measures.

papers.title: Sharp Convergence Rates for Masked Diffusion Models
Revisiting Chebyshev Polynomial and Anisotropic RBF Models for Tabular Regression
Assessing the Impact of Speaker Identity in Speech Spoofing Detection
Functional central limit theorem for superdiffusive SDEs with stable noise
papers.abstract: This paper establishes a functional stable central limit theorem for a class of superdiffusive solutions to stochastic differential equations driven by an $\alpha$-stable process.

papers.title: Long-Term Multi-Session 3D Reconstruction Under Substantial Appearance Change
A Super Version of a Theorem of Fricke-Klein
papers.abstract: We start studying the character variety of the algebraic supergroup OSp(1|2) from the algebraic perspective. We do this by first investigating the specific case of the character variety of the free group on two letters and try to describe the ring of invariants with respect to the conjugation action. The explicit description of the corresponding character variety for SL(2) was done by Fricke and Klein, so this can be seen as a variant of this theorem for its supergeometric counterpart OSp(1|2) and briefly touch upon the character stack for OSp(1|2)

papers.title: Axially symmetric wormholes
papers.abstract: In this work, we derive an exact static, axially symmetric, nonrotating vacuum solution of the Einstein field equations depending on three constant parameters: the throat radius $r_0$, a parameter $q$, which is closely associated with the Komar mass, and a parameter $s$, which determines the axial/polar structure of the geometry. For $s = 0$, the asymptotically flat wormhole sector appears, and the solution reduces to the Gibbons-Volkov ring-wormhole geometry, while the ring conical excess of the extended geometry is removed from the final physical manifold by the cut-and-paste construction. For $s \neq 0$, the solution exhibits a stronger axial singularity instead of a finite axial conical defect.

papers.title: Variational Trajectory Optimization of Anisotropic Diffusion Schedules
Digital Quantum Simulation of the Holstein-Primakoff Transformation on Noisy Qubits
papers.abstract: Quantum simulation of many-body systems offers a powerful approach to exploring collective quantum dynamics beyond classical computational reach. Although spin and fermionic models have been extensively simulated on digital quantum computers, the simulation of bosonic systems on programmable quantum processors is often hindered by the intrinsically large Hilbert space of bosonic modes. In this work, we study the digital quantum simulation of bosonic modes using the Holstein-Primakoff (HP) transformation and implement this protocol on a cloud-based superconducting quantum processor. Representative bosonic dynamics, including the driven harmonic oscillator, bosonic squeezing, and the Jaynes-Cummings (JC) model, are simulated on quantum hardware. Using data obtained from the quantum simulations, we systematically examine the interplay between algorithmic and hardware-induced errors to identify optimal simulation parameters. The dominant algorithmic errors arise from the finite number of qubits used in the HP mapping and the finite number of Trotter steps in the time evolution, while hardware errors mainly originate from entangling-gate infidelity, decoherence, and readout errors. We demonstrate two-excitation JC dynamics and squeezed-state generation involving qubit-qubit interactions under the HP transformation, extending the simulations beyond the simple single-excitation regime. Furthermore, we show that quantum error mitigation substantially improves the fidelity of the quantum simulations on current hardware. Our results demonstrate the feasibility and limitations of HP-based digital simulation of bosonic degrees of freedom on current quantum processors and provide a framework that can be extended to more complex spin-boson and multimode cavity models.

papers.title: Topological initial state independence in Boundary Time Crystals
papers.abstract: Boundary time crystals (BTCs) break time-translation symmetry and exhibit long-lived, robust oscillations insensitive to initial conditions. We show that collective spin BTCs can admit emergent topological winding numbers in operator space. Expanding the density operator in a spherical tensor basis, we map the Lindblad dynamics onto an effective local hopping problem, where collective degrees of freedom label sites of an emergent operator space lattice. Whenever the emergent winding number is non-zero, topological obstructions prevent the localization of operator modes on the lattice and instead enforce their delocalization across operator space. This delocalization enables non-unital sourcing from the identity sector to propagate across operator space and continuously feed the observable sector in an initial state independent manner, thereby generating robust oscillatory responses in the time crystal phase. Our results frame BTC dynamics as a form of topologically constrained operator space transport and suggest a close connection to non-Hermitian skin effects.

papers.title: NestRL: A Nested Training Regime for Mutual Adaptation in Human-AI Teaming
A Fully Discrete Nonnegativity-Preserving FEM for a Stochastic Heat Equation
authors: Ana Djurdjevac (1 and 4) ((1) Freie Universität Berlin

papers.title: Sandwich-adjusted Bayesian copula inference and model checks for joint laboratory extremes in emergency care
papers.abstract: In this paper, we estimate how often creatinine and aspartate aminotransferase are both unusually high in the same emergency department specimen. We fit copulas using a rank-based Bayesian working posterior with a restricted Jeffreys prior. This posterior treats estimated margins as known and repeat visits as independent, which can make its 95% intervals too narrow. We apply a sandwich adjustment and compare adjusted intervals with patient bootstrap intervals. In our simulation study of independent continuous pairs and rounded, repeated pairs under six copula families, adjusted posterior and bootstrap coverage was 94.0-95.7%. For unadjusted posteriors using mid-ranks or random tie-breaking, coverage was 79.7-93.6%. For the application, we analysed first qualifying encounters for 107,387 adults at Stanford Health Care in 2020-2023. Both measurements exceeded their 95th percentiles 1.63 times as often as under independence (95% confidence interval 1.49-1.77). This ratio ranged from 1.43 to 1.84 across modelled age, acuity and recorded sex groups. Among eight families, the Student t copula had the lowest pseudo-Bayesian information criterion but overestimated the overall 95th-percentile joint rate by 33.3%; survival Clayton, with the highest criterion, overestimated it by 4.2%. Interval calibration must be accompanied by checks that fitted copulas reproduce observed joint rates.

papers.title: Band splitting in the altermagnet CrSb
papers.abstract: Altermagnets are a class of metallic magnets characterized by spin-split electron bands. Like an- tiferromagnets they lack spontaneous bulk magnetisation. The initial description of the momentum dependent spin splitting of electron bands in altermagnets was based on the spin groups approach, which is valid when relativistic interactions are neglected. Then the spin-orbit coupling has been taken into account according with time-reversal-odd, even-parity irreducible representations of cen- trosymmetric point groups formally considered by this http URL et al, Phys.Rev.B 109, 024404 (2024). The problem of electron band splitting should be discussed based on crystal symmetry of concrete altermagnet material. Here, the band spin-splitting in hexagonal altermagnet CrSb is established using magnetic groups formalism that allows to find the additional spin splitting missed in frame of exchange approximation. Another type of spin splitting takes place in so called hidden altermagnets. This type materials do not possess symmetry in respect of space and time inversion but are symmetric in respect of the product of these operations known as toroid symmetry. There is demonstrated the real space spin splitting in materials with toroid symmetry.

papers.title: Max-Min Bilinear Completely Positive Programs: A Semidefinite Relaxation with Tightness Guarantees
papers.abstract: We study max-min bilinear completely positive (CP) programs and their associated min-max programs. We establish reformulations of these problems as linear optimization over the product of the CP cone and the copositive (COP) cone, namely, the COP-CP programs. A hierarchy of coupled Moment-SOS type semidefinite relaxations is proposed to solve these COP-CP programs. We show that this approach has asymptotic convergence under mild assumptions. Moreover, we use the coupled flat truncation conditions (FTCs) to certify tightness of semidefinite relaxations, and we give sufficient conditions for finite convergence of the hierarchy, under which the FTCs hold at every optimal solution of all sufficiently high-order relaxations. Numerical experiments are presented to show the effectiveness of our method.

papers.title: Concept Influence: Leveraging Interpretability to Improve Performance and Efficiency in Training Data Attribution
Recursive regularisation in lattice Boltzmann magnetohydrodynamics
papers.abstract: Recursive regularisation (RR) improves the stability of lattice Boltzmann schemes, but its structure and limitations in magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) remain insufficiently understood. This work connects RR to central-Hermite-moment (CHM) collisions on D2Q9 and D3Q27 through a closed-form reconstruction valid for arbitrary second-order relaxation rates. The central moments of the Maxwell stress coincide, up to sign, with the recursion coefficients, providing a systematic basis for MHD collision operators. Common two-dimensional raw- and central-moment schemes thus correspond to regularisation with a unit bulk relaxation rate. In three dimensions, a CHM implementation reproduces RR to round-off, while a monomial central-moment collision differs at fourth order and produces a four- to twelve-fold larger kinetic-energy error in the tested flow. Chapman--Enskog analysis shows that, with a magnetic field, the hydrodynamic recursion reconstructs the third-order non-equilibrium with a relative error of $78$--$96\%$ ($4\%$ without a field). A local correction largely removes it, yet changes the solutions by less than their discretisation error, consistent with its Burnett-order character. Three-dimensional vortex simulations show approximately second-order convergence at $\mathrm{Re}=100$ and agree with pseudo-spectral solutions through the peak current at $\mathrm{Re}=1000$ and, with a unit bulk rate, at $\mathrm{Re}=3000$. There, single-rate RR develops a compressive instability whose onset depends on the grid, lattice Mach number and initial magnetic configuration. For the standard initial field, a unit bulk rate suppresses it at $\mathrm{Ma}=0.034$ for $N\ge128$. This improvement does not extend to BGK collisions or prevent failure at $\mathrm{Re}=10,000$. These results show that robust three-dimensional MHD simulations require regularisation and bulk dissipation to be considered together.

papers.title: Constrained and Composite Sampling via Proximal Sampler
papers.abstract: We study two log-concave sampling problems: constrained sampling and composite sampling. First, we consider sampling from a distribution proportional to $e^{-f}$ on a convex set $K\subset\mathbb R^d$, where $f$ is convex. Using an epigraph lifting, we reduce this problem to uniform sampling up to a one-dimensional exponential tilt over a convex set in $\mathbb R^{d+1}$. We then apply the proximal sampler to the lifted distribution. We develop an unbiased implementation of its restricted Gaussian oracle by using the cutting-plane method and rejection sampling, requiring only a separation oracle for $K$ and evaluation and subgradient oracles for $f$, without relying on projections or barrier functions. Second, we study composite sampling from $e^{-f-h}$, where $f$ and $h$ are closed and convex. This structure arises naturally in Bayesian inference, where $f$ represents data fidelity and $h$ encodes prior information. By applying an epigraph lifting to $h$, we reduce composite sampling to constrained sampling in $\mathbb R^{d+1}$, allowing us to build on the approach developed in the first part. This leads to a double lifting formulation in $\mathbb R^{d+2}$, for which we implement the proximal sampler using different combinations of subgradient and proximal oracles for $f$ and $h$. We establish mixing time bounds in Rényi and $\chi^2$ divergences for both problems. Finally, we revisit the convergence analysis of the proximal sampler from a variational perspective. Starting from variational formulations of its two half-steps as optimization problems over probability measures, we use a dynamic formulation of entropy-regularized optimal transport to recast them as optimal control problems. This allows us to derive their governing PDEs directly through the lens of optimization, without first analyzing particle-level SDEs.

papers.title: Robust Hybrid-Gain Control with Prescribed Transient Performance
Fast Catch-Up, Late Switching: Optimal Batch Size Scheduling via Functional Scaling Laws
papers.abstract: Batch size scheduling (BSS) plays a critical role in large-scale deep learning training, influencing both optimization dynamics and computational efficiency. Yet, its theoretical foundations remain poorly understood. In this work, we show that the functional scaling law (FSL) framework introduced in Li et al. (2025a) provides a principled lens for analyzing BSS. Specifically, we characterize the optimal BSS under a fixed data budget and show that its structure depends sharply on task difficulty. For easy tasks, optimal schedules keep increasing batch size throughout. In contrast, for hard tasks, the optimal schedule maintains small batch sizes for most of training and switches to large batches only in a late stage. To explain the emergence of late switching, we uncover a dynamical mechanism -- the fast catch-up effect -- which also manifests in large language model (LLM) pretraining. After switching from small to large batches, the loss rapidly aligns with the constant large-batch trajectory. Using FSL, we show that this effect stems from rapid forgetting of accumulated gradient noise, with the catch-up speed determined by task difficulty. Crucially, this effect implies that large batches can be safely deferred to late training without sacrificing performance, while substantially reducing data consumption. Finally, extensive LLM pretraining experiments -- covering both Dense and MoE architectures with up to 1.1B parameters and 1T tokens -- validate our theoretical predictions. Across all settings, late-switch schedules consistently outperform constant-batch and early-switch baselines.

papers.title: Quantum Algorithm Framework for Phase-Contrast Transmission Electron Microscopy Image Simulation
papers.abstract: We present a quantum algorithmic framework for simulating phase-contrast transmission electron microscopy (CTEM) image formation using a fault-tolerant, gate-based quantum circuit model. The electron wavefield on an $N\times N$ grid is amplitude-encoded into a $2\log_2 N$-qubit register. Free-space propagation and objective-lens aberrations are implemented via two-dimensional quantum Fourier transforms (QFTs) and diagonal phase operators in reciprocal space, while specimen interaction is modeled under the phase-object approximation (POA) in a single-slice multislice formulation as a position-dependent phase grating. We validate projected potentials, contrast transfer function (CTF) behavior, and image contrast trends against classical multislice simulations for MoS$_2$ over experimentally relevant parameters, and provide resource estimates and key assumptions that determine end-to-end runtime. Extracting a complete $N\times N$ intensity image by direct sampling requires $O(N^2/\epsilon^2)$ repetitions, which rules out a generic polylogarithmic-cost image-generation algorithm. We therefore analyze end-to-end cost, including state preparation, repeated execution, measurement precision, and the best classical calculation of the same output, and identify the conditions under which limited-output tasks could be candidates for quantum advantage; the present benchmarks establish implementation agreement and do not demonstrate such an advantage. This framework provides a physics-grounded mapping from CTEM theory to quantum circuits and establishes a baseline for extending toward full multislice and inelastic scattering models.

papers.title: Securing SIM-Assisted Wireless Networks via Quantum Reinforcement Learning
On the effective Yau--Tian--Donaldson conjecture for projective bundles
papers.abstract: Consider the projectivization $\mathbb{P}(E)$ of a holomorphic vector bundle $E$ over a smooth curve, equipped with a fixed Kähler class $[\omega]$. Our first main result establishes that the existence of an extremal Kähler metric in $[\omega]$ is equivalent to the weighted stability of a moment polytope $\Delta$ with respect to explicit weight functions depending on the topological data of $\mathbb{P}(E)$. We then introduce a class of test configurations, which we call compatible test configurations. These are constructed by gluing horospherical test configurations of the fibers, arising from convex functions on $\Delta$ via Delcroix's construction, to the principal bundle associated with $\mathbb{P}(E)$. Our second main result shows that the weighted stability of $\Delta$ naturally arises when computing the relative uniform K-stability of $[\omega]$ with respect to compatible test configurations.

papers.title: A geometrical invitation to BMS group theory
papers.abstract: In these lecture notes, a group-theoretical introduction to BMS symmetries is provided in a self-contained manner. More precisely, all definitions and structures are purely based on geometrical and group-theoretical notions defined at null infinity and valid in any dimension (four or higher), in a way that circumvents its traditional bulk realisation as asymptotic symmetries. The topics which are reviewed are: the definition of BMS transformations as conformal Carrollian isometries of null infinity, the semidirect structure of the BMS group, the holographic reconstruction of Minkowski spacetime in terms of good cuts, the one-to-one correspondence between good cut subspaces and Poincaré subgroups (aka vacua), as well as a basic introduction to the unitary representations of the BMS group.

papers.title: Self-EvolveRec: Self-Evolving Recommender Systems with LLM-based Directional Feedback
Real-Time Dynamic N-1 Screening: Identifying High-Risk Lines and Transformers After Common Faults
papers.abstract: Power system operators routinely perform N-1 contingency analysis, yet conventional tools provide limited guidance on which lines or transformers deserve heightened attention during fast post-fault transients. In particular, static screening does not reveal whether (1) the same faulted line repeatedly triggers severe downstream overloads, or (2) a specific transformer emerges as vulnerable across many distinct fault scenarios. This paper introduces a real-time dynamic N-1 screening framework that addresses this gap by estimating, for each counterfactual single-phase transmission fault, the probability of transient overcurrent on critical grid elements. The output is an operator-facing dashboard that ranks (a) faulted lines whose outages most frequently lead to dangerous transformer overloads, and (b) transformers that consistently overload across top-risk scenarios, both of which are actionable indicators for real-time situational awareness. The approach models post-fault electromechanical dynamics using a linear stochastic formulation of the swing equations with short-lived, fault-localized uncertainty, and combines analytic transient evaluation with cross-entropy based importance sampling to efficiently estimate rare but high-impact events. All N-1 contingencies are evaluated in parallel with linear computational complexity. The framework is demonstrated on the IEEE 118-bus system, where it reveals latent high-risk lines and transformers that remain invisible under deterministic dynamic or static N-1 analysis. Results show orders-of-magnitude computational speedup relative to brute-force Monte Carlo, enabling practical deployment within real-time operational cycles.

papers.title: Differentiable Modal Logic for Multi-Agent Diagnosis, Orchestration and Communication
Dynamic Pricing in Two-Sided Markets: Learning Barriers and Price Differentiation
CADET: Context-Conditioned Ads CTR Prediction With a Decoder-Only Transformer
Deformation quantization of symplectic vector fields
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study deformation quantization of symplectic vector fields à la Fedosov. We provide an explicit construction to quantize each symplectic vector field as a derivation of the deformed star algebra. This recovers a result of Müller-Bahns and Neumaier with an explicit formula of higher total degree terms. Moreover, we show that this quantization yields a non-abelian $2$-cocycle on the Lie algebra of symplectic vector fields with values in the deformed star algebra. For a Fedosov deformation quantization with vanishing first characteristic class, this non-abelian $2$-cocycle can provide a formal deformation of the crossed-product algebra generated by the action of symplectic vector fields. In this sense, we can quantize any Lie algebra action by symplectic vector fields.

papers.title: Equivariant Kazhdan--Lusztig Polynomials of Thagomizer Matroids with a Hyperoctahedral Group Action
papers.abstract: We compute the equivariant Kazhdan--Lusztig and inverse Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials of the thagomizer matroid $T_n=M(K_{1,1,n})$ under the action of the hyperoctahedral group $\Bn$. For $n\ge2$, this action identifies $\Bn$ with the full automorphism group of $T_n$. For every $n\ge0$, we give multiplicity-free decompositions of all coefficients of both polynomials into irreducible representations and prove that both coefficient sequences are strongly induced log-concave with respect to induction from $\Bn\times\Bn$ to $\B{2n}$. The formulas for Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials follow from the palindromicity of the equivariant $Z$-polynomial and the known equivariant formulas for the graphic matroids of cycle graphs under the action of $\Sn$. The inverse formula follows from Proudfoot's equivariant inversion identity. For $n\ge2$, we also obtain explicit formulas for both polynomials of $M(K_{2,n})$ under the inherited action of $\Bn$, again with multiplicity-free coefficients.

papers.title: CODE-SHARP: Continuous Open-ended Discovery and Evolution of Skills as Hierarchical Reward Programs
Allure of Craquelure: A Variational-Generative Approach to Crack Detection in Paintings
Robust Trust
papers.abstract: An agent chooses an action based on her private information and a recommendation from an informed but potentially misaligned adviser. With a known probability, the adviser truthfully reports his signal; with the remaining probability, he can send any message. We characterize robustly optimal decision rules that maximize the agent's worst-case expected payoff. Every optimal rule is equivalent to a trust-region policy in belief space: the adviser's reported beliefs are taken at face value if they fall within the trust region but are otherwise projected onto the trust region's boundary. We derive alignment thresholds above which advice is strictly valuable, explicitly characterize the solution in binary-state environments, and develop a procedure for computing the trust region numerically.

papers.title: Affirmative Action in India with Hierarchical Reservations
papers.abstract: We study the design of affirmative action mechanisms, focusing on India's system of horizontal reservations within vertical reservations. We consider a one-to-all policy, under which an applicant eligible for multiple horizontal categories simultaneously contributes toward each category's minimum guarantee. When horizontal reservations have a hierarchical structure, we introduce a choice rule that selects the unique merit-optimal set of applicants subject to these guaranties, satisfies the substitutes condition and size monotonicity. In a matching-with-contracts framework, we show that the generalized deferred acceptance mechanism is stable, strategy-proof, and eliminates justified envy under aggregate choice rules using the hierarchical choice rule in each vertical category. We establish a fundamental trade-off between merit and affirmative action between the one-to-all and one-to-one counting policies.

papers.title: Reasoning under uncertainty in humans and language models
An Automata-Based Approach to Games with $ω$-Automatic Preferences
On Busemann subgradient methods for stochastic minimization in Hadamard spaces
papers.abstract: We study the recently introduced Busemann subgradient method due to Goodwin, Lewis, López-Acedo and Nicolae, extending it to minimize the mean of a stochastic function over general Hadamard spaces. We prove a strong convergence theorem under a local compactness assumption and further prove weak convergence of the method over separable Hadamard spaces. The proof is based on a general (weak) convergence theorem for stochastic processes in Hadamard spaces which confine to a stochastic variant of quasi-Fejér monotonicity, together with a nonlinear variant of Pettis' theorem, which are of independent interest. Lastly, we provide best function value estimates as well as a strong convergence result under a strong convexity assumption, and in that latter case in particular derive explicit rates of convergence. We illustrate the practical use of the general mean minimization problem and the associated Busemann subgradient method through statistical models for phylogenetic inference via the Billera-Holmes-Vogtmann tree space.

papers.title: Dynamic Load Model for Data Centers with Pattern-Consistent Calibration
What Does Machine Learning Learn from Numerical Calabi--Yau Geometry? A Controlled Study on the Fermat Quintic
MSN: A Memory-based Sparse Activation Scaling Framework for Large-scale Industrial Recommendation
Flow Matching for Offline Reinforcement Learning with Discrete Actions
Distribution-free certificate of similarity between distributions with blurred total variation distance
papers.abstract: Classical two-sample tests aim to determine whether two distributions are equal or not based on samples from each one. Even in an distribution-free setting, well-known methods such as the permutation test can provide statistical evidence that the two distributions differ. However, failure to reject equality does not necessarily establish that they are similar. In this work, we study the complementary problem of certifying distributional similarity with finite-sample confidence, without imposing assumptions on the underlying distributions. We show, however, that for continuous distributions, any distribution-free upper confidence bound on the total variation (TV) distance must be trivial with high probability, even if the distributions are identical. Thus, certifying similarity in TV with a distribution-free guarantee is practically impossible. We therefore examine the blurred TV distance, a relaxation of TV distance that enables us to quantify similarity after applying a common blurring operation while retaining the interpretation of TV. We construct distribution-free upper and lower confidence bounds on blurred TV, establish their finite-sample validity, and examine its properties in high dimensions.

papers.title: Optimal scaling laws in learning hierarchical multi-index models
papers.abstract: In this work, we provide a sharp theory of scaling laws for two-layer neural networks trained on a class of hierarchical multi-index targets, in a genuinely representation-limited regime. We derive exact information-theoretic scaling laws for subspace recovery and prediction error, revealing how the hierarchical features of the target are sequentially learned through a cascade of phase transitions. We further show that these optimal rates are achieved by a simple, target-agnostic spectral estimator, which can be interpreted as the small learning-rate limit of gradient descent on the first-layer weights. Once an adapted representation is identified, the readout can be learned statistically optimally, using an efficient procedure. As a consequence, we provide a unified and rigorous explanation of scaling laws, plateau phenomena, and spectral structure in shallow neural networks trained on such hierarchical targets.

papers.title: Sparse Video Generation Propels Real-World Beyond-the-View Vision-Language Navigation
PieArena: Ranking and Profiling Language Agents in Realistic Negotiation Scenarios
Multi-layer Cross-attention is Provably Optimal for Multi-modal In-context Learning
papers.abstract: Recent progress has rapidly advanced our understanding of the mechanisms underlying in-context learning in modern attention-based neural networks. However, existing results focus exclusively on unimodal data; in contrast, the theoretical underpinnings of in-context learning for multi-modal data remain poorly understood. We introduce a mathematically tractable framework for studying multi-modal learning and explore when transformer-like architectures can recover Bayes-optimal performance in-context. To model multi-modal problems, we assume the observed data arises from a latent factor model. Our first result comprises a negative take on expressibility: we prove that single-layer self-attention models fail to recover the Bayes-optimal predictor uniformly over the task distribution. To address this limitation, we introduce a novel, linearized cross-attention mechanism, which we study in the regime where both the number of cross-attention layers and the context length are large. We show that this cross-attention mechanism is provably Bayes optimal when optimized using gradient flow. Our results underscore the benefits of depth for in-context learning and establish the provable utility of cross-attention for multi-modal distributions.

papers.title: ImmuVis: Hyperconvolutional Foundation Model for Imaging Mass Cytometry
On Pseudo-Effectivity and Volumes of Adjoint Classes in Kähler Families with Projective Central Fiber
papers.abstract: This paper is devoted to studying the deformation behavior of pseudo-effective canonical divisors and volumes of adjoint classes in Kähler families. Based on recent developments in the Kähler minimal model program, for flat families with fiberwise canonical singularities, we establish the global stability of the pseudo-effectivity of canonical divisors and uniruledness, assuming in addition that one fiber is projective, while the same conclusion for Kähler threefolds is also true without the projectivity assumption of the central fiber. For a smooth Kähler family whose central fiber is projective with a big adjoint class, we show that its volume remains locally constant. Finally, using the (relative) minimal model program for Kähler threefolds, we verify the deformation invariance of volumes of adjoint classes and plurigenera for smooth Kähler families of threefolds, thereby partially confirming Siu's invariance of plurigenera conjecture in dimension three.

papers.title: Agentic AI-Empowered Dynamic Survey Framework
Have Large Language Models Enhanced the Way Civil & Environmental Engineers Write? A Quantitative Analysis of Scholarly Communication over 25 Years
WAXAL: A Large-Scale Multilingual African Language Speech Corpus
papers.abstract: Recent advances in speech technology predominantly favor high-resource languages, leaving speakers of Sub-Saharan African languages underserved. To bridge this divide, we introduce WAXAL, an open, large-scale speech dataset spanning 27 African languages representing over 100 million speakers. WAXAL comprises over 14,100 hours of speech collected in partnership with African academic and community organizations to build local research capacity: an Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) corpus with 2,340 hours of transcribed, image-prompted natural speech across 19 languages (plus ~11,760 untranscribed hours) and a studio-quality Text-to-Speech (TTS) corpus of ~247 hours across 15 language configurations. We empirically benchmark three architecturally distinct ASR models -- Gemma 3n 2B, Whisper-Large-v3, and MMS-1B-all -- across the 19 ASR languages on strictly speaker-disjoint splits. Fine-tuning on WAXAL yields substantial gains, reducing macro-average WER by up to 58% for Whisper-Large-v3, 56% for Gemma 3n 2B, and 17% for MMS-1B-all (and Character Error Rate by up to 70%). WAXAL-fine-tuned models generalize zero-shot to three out-of-distribution benchmarks: FLEURS, Mozilla Common Voice, and Sunbird SALT. Finally, an LLM-as-judge semantic evaluation confirms that fine-tuning preserves speaker intent beyond surface-level transcription metrics. WAXAL is released at this https URL .

papers.title: Why Steering Works: Toward a Unified View of Language Model Parameter Dynamics
Unlocking the Duality between Flow and Field Matching
PCA of probability measures: Sparse and Dense sampling regimes
papers.abstract: A common approach to perform PCA on probability measures is to embed them into a Hilbert space where standard functional PCA techniques apply. While convergence rates for estimating the embedding of a single measure from $m$ samples are well understood, the literature has not addressed the setting involving multiple measures. In this paper, we study PCA in a double asymptotic regime where $n$ probability measures are observed, each through $m$ samples. We derive convergence rates of the form $n^{-1/2} + m^{-\alpha}$ for the empirical covariance operator and the PCA excess risk, where $\alpha>0$ depends on the chosen embedding. This characterizes the relationship between the number $n$ of measures and the number $m$ of samples per measure, revealing a sparse (small $m$) to dense (large $m$) transition in the convergence behavior. Moreover, we prove that the dense-regime rate is minimax optimal for the empirical covariance error. Our numerical experiments validate these theoretical rates and demonstrate that appropriate subsampling preserves PCA accuracy while reducing computational cost.

papers.title: Function-on-function nonlinear autoregressive model (F2NARX) for probabilistic surrogate modeling of stochastic dynamical systems
papers.abstract: Constructing accurate and computationally efficient surrogate models for predicting dynamical system responses is critical in many engineering domains, yet remains challenging due to the strongly nonlinear and high-dimensional mapping from external excitations and system parameters to system responses. This work introduces a novel Function-on-Function Nonlinear AutoRegressive model with eXogenous inputs (F2NARX), which reformulates the recently proposed $\mathcal{F}$-NARX method from a function-on-function regression perspective. The proposed framework substantially improves predictive efficiency while maintaining high accuracy. By combining principal component analysis with Gaussian process regression, F2NARX further enables probabilistic predictions of dynamical responses via the unscented transform in an autoregressive manner. The effectiveness of the method is demonstrated through case studies of varying complexity. Results show that F2NARX outperforms state-of-the-art NARX model by orders of magnitude in efficiency while achieving higher accuracy in general. The probabilistic prediction capability of F2NARX is further demonstrated by combining it with active learning for first-passage probability estimation, showing its potential for reliability-oriented applications.

papers.title: A Statistical Theory of Gated Attention through the Lens of Hierarchical Mixture of Experts
Interpreting and Controlling Model Behavior via Constitutions for Atomic Concept Edits
Probing the Trajectories of Reasoning Traces in Large Language Models
Log canonical thresholds at infinity
papers.abstract: The paper considers a global version of the notion of log canonical threshold for plurisubharmonic functions $u$ of logarithmic growth in $\mathbb{C}^n$, aiming at description of the range of all $p>0$ such that $e^{-u}\in L^p(\mathbb{C}^n)$. Explicit formulas are obtained in the toric case. By considering Bergman functions of corresponding weighted Hilbert spaces, a new polynomial approximation of plurisubharmonic functions of logarithmic growth with control over its singularities and behavior at infinity (a global version of Demailly's approximation theorem) is established. Some application to tame polynomial maps are given.

papers.title: Unified $(q,s)$-concurrence: a two-parameter family of bipartite entanglement measures
papers.abstract: Quantum entanglement is a fundamental resource in quantum information processing, yet its quantitative characterization remains challenging, especially for mixed states. In this work, we introduce a two-parameter family of entanglement measures, referred to as the unified $(q,s)$-concurrence, which generalizes both the standard concurrence and the recently proposed $q$-concurrence. This measure is inspired by the unified entropy and provides a flexible framework for quantifying bipartite entanglement. By combining the positive partial transposition and realignment criteria, we derive an analytical lower bound for this measure for arbitrary bipartite mixed states, revealing a connection to strong separability criteria. Explicit expressions are obtained for the unified $(q,s)$-concurrence in the cases of isotropic and Werner states under the constraint $q>1$ and $qs\geq 1$. Furthermore, we explore the monogamy properties of the unified $(q,s)$-concurrence for $q\geq 2$, $0\leq s\leq 1$ and $1\leq qs\leq 3$, and establish an entanglement polygon inequality for any multipartite qudit system when $q\geq 1$ and $qs\geq 1$. Our results provide a unified and versatile tool for entanglement quantification, with potential applications in quantum communication and multipartite entanglement theory.

papers.title: Tabular Foundation Models Can Do Survival Analysis
Flow Perturbation++: Multi-Step Unbiased Jacobian Estimation for High-Dimensional Boltzmann Sampling
Evidence of the de Almeida-Thouless transition in three-dimensional spin glasses
papers.abstract: The nature of spin-glass states in a magnetic field remains a major open problem in statistical physics. The existence of the de Almeida-Thouless (dAT) transition for three-dimensional (3D) spin glasses in a field is still debated. We introduce a new computational method to define the spin-glass susceptibility, which is robust against the broad tail in the overlap distribution that undermines conventional analyses. Applying this approach to the Edwards-Anderson spin-glass model in 2D and 3D, and contrasting with the 3D Ising (without disorder) and mean-field spin-glass models, we find a stark difference: the locus of susceptibility maxima bends to the right in the field-temperature plane for the Ising and 2D spin-glass cases, indicating a supercritical crossover line, but bends to the left for the mean-field and 3D spin glasses - a signature of the dAT line. Finite-size scaling further suggests that the peak susceptibility diverges with system size in 3D spin glasses under a field, while saturating in 2D. These results provide direct numerical evidence for the dAT transition in 3D, supporting the replica symmetry breaking scenario.

papers.title: A Local Discontinuous Galerkin Method for Dirichlet Boundary Control Problems
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider control constrained $L^2-$Dirichlet boundary control of a convection-diffusion equation on a two dimensional convex polygonal domain. We discretize the control problem based on the local discontinuous Galerkin method with piecewise linear ansatz functions for the flux and potential. We derive a priori error estimates for the full as well as for the variational discrete control approximation. We present a selection of numerical results to demonstrate the performance of our approach and to underpin the theoretical findings.

papers.title: Multivariate Multicycle Codes for Complete Single-Shot Decoding
papers.abstract: We introduce multivariate multicycle (MM) codes, a Koszul-complex formulation of abelian multicycle (AMC) codes, which are multidimensional scalar lifted-product codes over a finite abelian group algebra, that unifies bivariate bicycle, multivariate bicycle, abelian two-block group algebra, generalized bicycle, trivariate tricycle, and toric codes. MM codes are Calderbank-Shor-Steane (CSS) codes defined from length-$(t+1)$ chain complexes, and for $t\geq4$ they possess metachecks for both types of checks, which can be used for single-shot decoding. We offer a framework that facilitates the construction of long-length chain complexes through the use of the Koszul complex. In particular, obtaining explicit boundary maps (parity check and metacheck matrices) is particularly straightforward in our approach. We also determine when an MM code encodes logical qubits, count the independent check relations not generated by its metachecks, and show that middle-degree codes with even $t$ have equal $X$ and $Z$ distances. This simple but very general parameterization of codes permitted us to efficiently perform a numerical search, where we identify several MM code candidates with high rates and high code distances. Examples of new codes with parameters $[[n,k,d]]$ include $[[96,12,8]]$, $[[144,12,12]]$, $[[486,24,12]]$, $[[630,70,9]]$, and $[[648,60,9]]$. For selected codes, we report confinement profiles and study single-shot and few-shot decoding under phenomenological and circuit-level noise. Our codes also include explicit collapsed 5D through 9D instances, and our 5D instances have check weights lower than those of recent small instances of quantum Tanner codes.

papers.title: Hamiltonian Decoded Quantum Interferometry for General Pauli Hamiltonians
papers.abstract: We study Hamiltonian Decoded Quantum Interferometry (HDQI) for general Pauli Hamiltonians $H = \sum_i c_i P_i$ on an $n$-qubit system, where $c_i \in \mathbb{R}$ and the $P_i$ are Pauli operators. Given access to a suitable decoding oracle, we construct efficient quantum algorithms that prepare the state $\rho_{\mathcal P}(H) = \frac{\mathcal P^2(H)}{\text{Tr}[\mathcal P^2(H)]}$ for any univariate polynomial $\mathcal P(x)$, which in turn approximates the Gibbs state of $H$ for appropriate choices of $\mathcal P$. The central technical ingredient is a matrix product state (MPS) representation of the reference state, which enables handling the asymmetric coefficient structure that arises for general real coefficients. Our results substantially extend the scope of HDQI beyond stabilizer-like Hamiltonians, providing a unified method for Gibbs state preparation and Hamiltonian optimization across a broad class of physically and computationally relevant quantum systems.

papers.title: Elementary Quantum Gates from Lie Group Embeddings in $U(2^n)$: Spectral Geometry and Intrinsic Factorization Lengths
papers.abstract:
We study intrinsic factorizations of quantum gates using determinant-one unitaries supported on arbitrary two-dimensional subspaces of $\C^N$, where $N=2^n$. For $U\in U(N)$ write $r=\operatorname{rank}(U-I)$. When $r\ge2$, we characterize all factors that lower the active rank by two through traceless compressions of the Cayley transform on $\Ran(U-I)$. For the ordered active eigenangles $\vartheta_j\in(0,2\pi)$, existence is equivalent to $\vartheta_1+\vartheta_2\le2\pi\le\vartheta_{r-1}+\vartheta_r$.
