For $U\in SU(N)$, combining this construction with eigenangle merging realizes the classical reflection-length formula in two-level form: $\ell^{SU}(U)=\max\{
u(U),r-
u(U)\}$, where $
u(U)$ is the positive eigenangle sum divided by $2\pi$. On the full-rank open set, the age indexes $N-1$ connected components with constant intrinsic length. We place these factorizations within the spectral description of the dictionaries formed by faithful $SU(2)$ and $U(2)$ embeddings. For $n\ge2$, these dictionaries are Haar-null of Hausdorff dimensions $N^2-N+1$ and $N^2-N+2$; the former is compact and the latter dense. Distances to compact sectors reduce to eigenvalue matching. Further results concern ambient minimality of embedded geodesics and a first-order sharp spectral bound on coherence production.

papers.title: Mutually c-Conjugate Potentials in Multimarginal Optimal Transport: Dual Representation and Stability
papers.abstract: We establish dual representation and stability results for multimarginal optimal transport (MOT) with bounded continuous costs. Our approach uses mutually $c$-conjugate potentials: each component is the largest function compatible with the dual constraint when the others are fixed. A single sweep of successive component updates produces such a family from any real-valued feasible family while preserving contact points. The resulting potentials are bounded and upper semicontinuous. On fixed compact metric spaces, normalization at fixed reference points yields a compact class of continuous potentials in the product uniform norm. This class is independent of the marginals and contains a dual maximizer for every marginal tuple. We prove its Lipschitz dependence on the cost in Hausdorff distance. Under uniform cost convergence and weak marginal convergence, transport values converge. The corresponding normalized optimizer sets are upper stable in the product uniform norm, without uniqueness assumptions. We also obtain value bounds in total variation and, for coordinatewise Lipschitz costs, Wasserstein distance. For coordinatewise Lipschitz reference costs, a power-growth condition on the dual objective gives one-sided Hölder estimates for optimizer sets under joint perturbations. On finite spaces, polyhedral structure yields linear growth and one-sided Lipschitz estimates with reference-dependent constants. On Polish spaces, total boundedness of the coordinate cost profiles in the uniform norm yields a compact normalized representation. For a fixed cost satisfying this condition, value continuity and upper stability of normalized conjugate optimizer sets hold under weak marginal convergence.

papers.title: GRASP: Guided Region-Aware Sparse Prompting for Adapting MLLMs to Remote Sensing
What Does a Cosine of 0.8 Mean? Monotone Calibration of Embedding Similarity
Will It Survive? Deciphering the Fate of AI Agent-Authored Code in Open Source
Length Spectrum Rigidity and Flexibility of Spheres of Revolution with One Equator
papers.abstract: We define a notion of marked length spectrum for $S^1$-symmetric Riemannian metrics on the two-sphere having only one equator. We prove that isospectral metrics in this class have conjugate geodesic flows. Under a further ${\mathbb Z}_2$-symmetry assumption, we show that the marked length spectrum determines the metric. Finally, we show that every isospectral class of metrics contains a unique ${\mathbb Z}_2$-symmetric metric and give an explicit description of this isospectral class as an infinite-dimensional convex set, generalizing the known description of $S^1$-symmetric Zoll metrics. This paper contains also two appendices, in which we provide an elementary proof of the fact that a $C^2$ real-valued function on an interval is determined by the set of tangent lines to its graph, and we classify a class of $S^1$-invariant contact forms on three-manifolds.

papers.title: Adaptive dynamics of eco-evolutionary repeated games: Effect of reward and punishment
papers.abstract: Long-term evolutionary processes can strongly influence common-pool resource conservation by generating new traits or behaviours that modify the feedback between population strategies and the resource state. Here we develop an eco-evolutionary framework in which individuals repeatedly interact with the same opponent and follow direct reciprocity through reactive strategies. The strategic dynamics is coupled to a renewable common resource and analyzed using adaptive dynamics. After our exhaustive non-linear dynamical analysis of $2\times2$ strategic games, we focus on comparative and combined usefulness of institutional incentives in the form of rewards and punishments in preventing the Tragedy of the Commons even when defection dominates in the replete resource state. We also report possibility of robust stable oscillations -- emerging via Hopf bifurcation -- in resource state and population strategies.

papers.title: Electronic structure, phase stability, and transport properties of the AlTiVCr lightweight high-entropy alloy: A computational study
papers.abstract: We investigate the thermodynamics and phase stability of the AlTiVCr lightweight high-entropy alloy using a combination of ab initio electronic structure calculations, a concentration wave analysis, and atomistic Monte Carlo simulations. In alignment both with experimental data and with results obtained using other computational approaches, we predict a $\textrm{B2}$ (CsCl) chemical ordering emerging in this alloy at comparatively high temperatures, which is driven by Al and Ti moving to separate sublattices, while V and Cr express weaker site preferences. The impact of this $\textrm{B2}$ chemical ordering on the electronic transport properties of the alloy is investigated within a Kubo--Greenwood linear response framework and it is found that, counter-intuitively, the alloy's residual resistivity increases as the material transitions from the $\textrm{A2}$ (disordered bcc) phase to our predicted $\textrm{B2}$ (partially) ordered structure. Our results give fresh insight into the atomic-scale structure and consequent physical properties of this well-studied, technologically relevant material.

papers.title: Leave-one-out testing for node-level differences in Gaussian graphical models
papers.abstract: We study two-sample equality testing in Gaussian graphical models with the aim of localizing distributional differences at the node level. The proposed procedure targets departures in the joint distribution, which may arise from mean shifts, variance changes, or covariance differences. We extend Bartlett-adjusted likelihood ratio tests to a leave-one-out framework on a fully connected working graph. The resulting increments have standard chi-square null limits, enabling calibrated inference for single nodes and fixed-size subsets. We also discuss how decomposable graphical structure can be exploited to apply the approach locally on larger graphs. Simulation results indicate good calibration and competitive power, and a real data application highlights the practical applicability of the method.

papers.title: VIOLA: Towards Video In-Context Learning with Minimal Annotations
A geometric approach to the uniform boundedness of $\ell$-primary torsion points
papers.abstract: We prove that for a non-isotrivial abelian scheme over a smooth curve, the genus of a generic sequence of multi-sections with small heights tends to infinity. As an application, we give a new proof of the uniform boundedness of $\ell$-primary torsion points on fibers of an abelian scheme over a smooth curve, a result originally proved by Cadoret and Tamagawa. Furthermore, our approach allows us to reprove a conjecture of Cadoret and Tamagawa without additional assumptions. Our approach is based on the theory of Betti foliations and the arithmetic equidistribution theorem.

papers.title: Contingency Planning for Safety-Critical Autonomous Vehicles: A Review and Perspectives
A Quantum Many-Body Approach for Orbital Magnetism in Correlated Multiband Electron Systems
papers.abstract: Orbital magnetism is a purely quantum phenomenon that reflects intrinsic electronic properties of solids, yet its microscopic description in interacting multiband systems remains incomplete. We develop a general quantum many-body framework for orbital magnetic responses based on the Luttinger--Ward functional. Starting from the Dyson equation, we reformulate the thermodynamic potential in a weak magnetic field and construct a controlled expansion in powers of $B$ applicable to correlated electron systems. A key technical advance is a modified ``Fourier'' representation using noncommutative coordinates, which allows the thermodynamic potential to be expressed in an effective momentum space where the magnetic field acts perturbatively. This formulation makes analytic progress possible within the Moyal algebra. As an application, we derive the spontaneous orbital magnetization for approximations whose skeleton diagrams contain no fermion loop enclosing magnetic flux (e.g., Hartree--Fock, self-consistent RPA, and single-site dynamical mean-field theory). Vertex corrections consistent with the self-energy are included automatically, without a separate diagrammatic analysis, and the result is expressed entirely in terms of the zero-field Hamiltonian renormalized by the self-energy. For frequency-dependent but Hermitian self-energies, we generalize the orbital magnetic moment and Berry curvature to momentum-frequency space and identify two gauge-invariant contributions built from these quantities. For frequency-independent self-energies the result reduces to the familiar geometric formula for noninteracting systems. This framework provides a unified foundation for computing orbital magnetic responses in correlated multiband materials.

papers.title: Domino tilings of black-and-white Temperleyan cylinders
papers.abstract: We consider the dimer model in cylindrical domains $\Omega_\delta$ on square grids of mesh size $\delta$ with two Temperleyan boundary components of different colors. Assuming that the $\Omega_\delta$ approximate a cylindrical domain $\Omega$ as $\delta\to 0$, we prove the convergence of height fluctuations to the Gaussian Free Field in $\Omega$ plus an independent discrete Gaussian multiple of the harmonic measure of one of the boundary components. The limit of the dimer coupling functions on $\Omega_\delta$ is holomorphic in $\Omega$ but not conformally covariant. Given this, we determine the limiting structure of height fluctuations from general principles rather than from explicit computations. In particular, our analysis justifies the inevitable appearance of the discrete Gaussian distribution in the doubly connected setup.

papers.title: Logarithmic dispersion at marginal stability in collective attention
papers.abstract: How cross-sectional heterogeneity evolves in nonequilibrium populations of competing, ageing units is a collective question that cannot be resolved from a representative trajectory or the ensemble mean alone. Analysis of more than two million age-aligned English Wikipedia page-view trajectories from six yearly cohorts spanning 2015-2020 shows that the variance of logarithmic attention grows linearly with $\ln t$, while the ensemble mean relaxes on the same logarithmic clock. This dispersion law recurs across all six cohorts and is systematically favoured over the tested power-law alternative; temporal increments also exhibit consistent antipersistent scaling. A complementary trajectory-level analysis reveals broad, non-Gaussian variation in effective relaxation rates, showing that this collective regularity coexists with heterogeneous observed trajectories. A minimal scale-free stochastic model combines mean relaxation with self-affine temporal fluctuations of age-dependent amplitude. Within this model class, logarithmic spreading emerges when fluctuation accumulation balances ageing attenuation, defining the marginal boundary between algebraic broadening and saturation. Together, age-resolved cross-sectional dispersion and temporal-increment scaling provide a transferable ensemble-level criterion for distinguishing amplification, marginal spreading, and saturation in other populations of competing, ageing units.

papers.title: Lost in Aggregation: The Causal Interpretation of the Instrumental Variable Estimand
papers.abstract: Instrumental variable estimation has emerged as a standard approach to mitigating confounding bias in the social sciences and epidemiology, where conducting randomized experiments can be too costly or infeasible. However, justifying the validity of the instrument is frequently challenging. We highlight a problem generally neglected in arguments for instrumental variable validity: the presence of an "aggregate treatment variable", where the treatment (e.g., education, GDP, caloric intake) is composed of finer-grained, unobserved components that each may have a different effect on the outcome. While the aggregation problem itself is general, our focus is on instrumental variable estimation in a linear setting, the regime underlying much of applied instrumental variable practice. We show that the causal effect of an aggregate treatment is generally ambiguous, as it depends on how an intervention on the aggregate is instantiated at the component level. We formalize this relation using the aggregate-constrained component intervention distribution (ACID). We then identify two key conditions under which standard instrumental variable estimators identify the aggregate effect. The contrived nature of these conditions implies major limitations on the interpretation of instrumental variable estimates based on aggregate treatments and highlights the need for a broader justificatory base for the exclusion restriction in such settings.

papers.title: Orthogonal Vector-Valued Rational Functions with Applications in Rational Approximation
Advancing ESG Intelligence: An Expert-level Agent and Comprehensive Benchmark for Sustainable Finance
Topological classification of certain nonorientable 4-manifolds with cyclic fundamental group of order 2 mod 4
papers.abstract: The classification up to homeomorphism of closed topological nonorientable 4-manifolds with fundamental group of order 2 due to Hambleton-Kreck-Teichner can be used to classify a large set of 4-manifolds with $\pi_1 = \Z/2p$ for odd $p > 1$. It is plausible that this set comprises all homeomorphism classes of such 4-manifolds. This is done through a cut-and-paste construction, which is then used to calculate an extension of the Hausmann-Weinberger invariant for every cyclic group of even order and to produce 4-manifolds that are not homotopy equivalent to a connected sum and which need not be smoothable.

papers.title: Simulation of noisy quantum circuits using frame representations
papers.abstract: One of the core research questions in the theory of quantum computing is to find out to what precise extent the classical simulation of a noisy quantum circuits is possible and where potential quantum advantages can set in. In this work, we introduce a unified framework for the classical simulation of quantum circuits based on frame theory, encompassing and generalizing a broad class of existing simulation strategies. Within this framework, the computational cost of a simulation algorithm is determined by the one-norm of an associated quasi-probability distribution, providing a common quantitative measure across different simulation approaches. This enables a comprehensive perspective on common methods for the simulation of noisy circuits based on different quantum resources, such as entanglement or non-stabilizerness. It further provides a clear scheme for generating novel classical simulation algorithms. Indeed, by exploring different choices of frames within this formalism and resorting to tools of convex optimization, we are able not only to obtain new insights and improved bounds for existing methods -- such as stabilizer state simulation or Pauli back-propagation -- but also to discover a new approach with an improved performance based on a generalization of the Pauli frame. We, thereby, show that classical simulation techniques can directly benefit from a perspective -- that of frames -- that goes beyond the traditional classification of quantum resources.

papers.title: An Empirical Investigation of Robustness in Large Language Models under Tabular Distortions
MHRC-Bench: A Multilingual Hardware Repository-Level Code Completion benchmark
CD4LM: Consistency Distillation and aDaptive Decoding for Diffusion Language Models
When the Shadow Meets Its Measure: Assessing the Feasibility of Submillimeter Black Hole Shadow Imaging in Megamaser-disk Active Galactic Nuclei
papers.abstract: Well-modeled water megamaser disks offer a path to black hole shadow (BHS) tests of strong-field gravity beyond Sgr A* and M87*: their very long baseline interferometry (VLBI) angular dynamics precisely constrains $M_\bullet/D$, the maser-disk orientation, and the dynamical center within the maser reference frame, thereby predicting the fiducial Schwarzschild BHS angular size without an externally adopted distance. We assess 21 megamaser galaxies as BHS targets using published maser measurements to calculate BHS angular sizes and baseline requirements. We combine new Submillimeter Array (SMA) continuum observations with archival Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) and Very Large Array (VLA) measurements to estimate arcsecond-scale 230 GHz flux densities and identify the strongest nuclear-region sources for higher-resolution follow-up. We also estimate the maximum dust and extended-jet contributions, examine limited variability measurements, and, for the leading candidate NGC 4258, evaluate the astrometry required to detect a spin-dependent offset between the BHS center and the maser dynamical center. Only NGC 4258 has an adopted BHS angular size resolvable with an Earth--L2 baseline; the other adopted sizes require longer baselines, while an Earth--L4/L5 separation would be sufficient for all. Five sources reach $S_{230}\gtrsim10$ mJy. However, whether the observed 230 GHz emission arises on BHS scales and is sufficiently optically thin to reveal a BHS remains unknown throughout the sample. NGC 4258's submillimeter excess is consistent with a thin disk transitioning to an advection-dominated flow; its spin-offset test remains infeasible with present maser astrometry.

papers.title: Full-Time-Scale Power Management for Hybrid AC/DC/DS Microgrid with Dynamic Concatenation and Global Equivalent Circuit Modeling
Importance sampling of unbounded random stopping times: computing committor functions and exit rates without reweighting
papers.abstract: Rare events in molecular dynamics are often related to noise-induced transitions between different macroscopic states (e.g., in protein folding). A common feature of these rare transitions is that they happen on timescales that are on average exponentially long compared to the characteristic timescale of the system, with waiting time distributions that have (sub)exponential tails and infinite support. As a result, sampling such rare events can lead to trajectories that can be become arbitrarily long, with not too low probability, which makes the reweighting of such trajectories a real challenge. Here, we discuss rare event simulation by importance sampling from a variational perspective, with a focus on {the computation of committor functions and mean first exit times that both play a prominent role in molecular dynamics}. The idea is to design importance sampling schemes that (a) reduce the variance of a rare event estimator while controlling the average length of the trajectories and (b) that do not require the reweighting of possibly very long trajectories. In doing so, we study different stochastic control formulations for committor and mean first exit times, which we compare both from a theoretical and a computational point of view, including numerical studies of some benchmark examples.

papers.title: Higher-Order Domain Generalization in Magnetic Resonance-Based Assessment of Alzheimer's Disease
Completeness of closed Kleinian flat Pseudo-Riemannian Manifolds of Signature (2,2)
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbb{R}^{2,2}$ denote the model space of flat pseudo-Riemannian manifolds of signature $(2,2)$. We prove that the only domain divisible by a discrete subgroup of the isometry group of $\mathbb{R}^{2,2}$ is $\mathbb{R}^{2,2}$ itself. In the Kleinian setting, this provides the first completeness theorem of closed flat pseudo-Riemannian manifolds beyond the Euclidean and Lorentzian cases. Along the proof, we show as a result of independent interest concerning the existence of syndetic hulls in semidirect products $R \ltimes G$, where $G$ is a homothety Lie group. This construction generalizes earlier constructions in affine geometry due to Carrière and Dal'bo.

papers.title: Stochastic Thermodynamics of Associative Memory
papers.abstract: Dense Associative Memory networks (DenseAMs) unify several popular paradigms in Artificial Intelligence (AI), such as Hopfield Networks, transformers, and diffusion models, while casting their computational properties into the language of dynamical systems and energy landscapes. This formulation provides a natural setting for studying thermodynamics and computation in neural systems, because DenseAMs are simultaneously simple enough to admit analytic treatment and rich enough to implement nontrivial computational function. Aspects of these networks have been studied at equilibrium and at zero temperature, but the thermodynamic costs associated with their operation out of equilibrium are largely unexplored. Here, we define the thermodynamic entropy production associated with the operation of such networks, and study polynomial DenseAMs at intermediate memory load. At large system sizes and intermediate and low load, we use dynamical mean field theory to characterize out-of-equilibrium properties, work requirements, and memory transition times when driving the system with corrupted memories. We characterize a failure mode of higher order networks not observed at zero temperature. Further, we develop a method for calculating work and power costs in the mean field limit. Finally, we find tradeoffs between entropy production, memory retrieval accuracy, and operation speed.

papers.title: Fidelity Before Structure: Verbatim Chunks Beat Lossy Artifact Extraction in Long-Conversation LLM Memory
What makes vertical federated learning work with thirteen samples? A controlled benchmark on coral thermal-stress multi-omics
papers.abstract: Vertical federated learning (VFL) lets laboratories that hold different omics layers of the same samples train a joint model without sharing raw data, but it is usually developed for datasets with thousands of samples. We benchmarked VFL on a Montipora capitata thermal-stress dataset with 13 samples and 90,579 features across transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics and microbiome data. The benchmark crosses two VFL backbones (a split-network model implemented in NVIDIA FLARE, and LASER-VFL) with three per-silo feature-selection strategies (gradient saliency, random, univariate t-test) and two allocations of a 1,300-feature budget, and adds a centralised elastic-net reference. All models were trained for the same number of steps and evaluated by repeated stratified 3-fold and leave-one-out cross-validation, with separate estimates of seed and data-split variability and end-to-end label-permutation tests. Plain VFL on all features classified heat stress well above chance (3-fold AUROC 0.869, 95% CI 0.838-0.895; permutation p = 0.020). Gradient-saliency selection with hand-set omics priors (0.904) could not be distinguished from plain VFL, from equal budgets or from random subsets of the same size (corrected p >= 0.56), and its selected features were no more consistent across seeds than random ones. LASER-VFL failed on all features at a learning rate of 1e-3 but matched the other methods at 1e-4. This version corrects versions 1-3 of this preprint, which reported that standard VFL performed at chance and that domain priors stabilised training; we show that those results arose because every model selected its checkpoint on a single-sample validation set, which evaluated the baseline after one optimiser step. With very few samples, evaluation choices outweighed every method choice we tested, and we give recommendations for evaluating federated models in this regime.

papers.title: Approximate Computation via Le Cam Simulability
papers.abstract: We propose a decision-theoretic framework for computational complexity, complementary to classical theory: moving from syntactic exactness (Turing / Shannon) to semantic simulability (Le Cam). While classical theory classifies problems by the cost of exact solution, modern computation often seeks only decision-valid approximations. We introduce a framework where "computation" is viewed as the efficient simulation of a target statistical experiment within a bounded risk distortion (Le Cam deficiency). We formally define computational deficiency ($\delta_{\text{poly}}$) and use it to construct the complexity class LeCam-P (Decision-Robust Polynomial Time), characterizing problems that may be syntactically hard but semantically easy to approximate. We show that classical Karp reductions can be viewed as zero-deficiency simulations, and that approximate reductions correspond to bounded deficiency. Furthermore, we establish the No-Free-Transfer Inequality, showing that strictly invariant representations inevitably destroy decision-relevant information. This framework offers a statistical perspective on approximation theory, bridging the gap between algorithmic complexity and decision theory.

papers.title: Measuring Mixed-State Topological Invariant in Open Photonic Quantum Walk
papers.abstract: Pure-state manifestations of geometric phase are well established and have found applications across essentially all branches of physics, yet their generalization to mixed-state regimes remains largely unexplored experimentally. The Uhlmann geometric phase offers a natural extension of pure-state paradigms and can exhibit a topological character. However, observation of this invariant is impeded by the incompatibility between Uhlmann parallel transport and Hamiltonian dynamics, as well as the difficulty of preparing topologically nontrivial mixed states. To address this challenge, we report an experimentally accessible protocol for directly measuring the mixed-state topological invariant. By engineering controlled nonunitary dynamics in a photonic quantum walk, we prepare topologically nontrivial mixed states from a trivial initial state. Then, by machine learning the full density matrix in momentum space, we directly extract the quantized geometric phase of the nontrivial mixed states. Furthermore, we observe that this transition of the quantized mixed-state topological invariant from a trivial to a nontrivial value is closely associated with the emergence of a topological kink structure. These results highlight a geometric phase framework that naturally extends to open quantum systems both in and out of thermal equilibrium.

papers.title: Micro-Macro Tensor Neural Surrogates for Uncertainty Quantification in Collisional Plasma
Exploring the Potential of Spiking Neural Networks in UWB NLOS Identification
Electric-field-controlled altermagnetic spin-momentum locking and ultrahigh tunneling magnetoresistance in Bilayer Cr$_{2}$SeO
papers.abstract: Altermagnets offer a promising platform for spintronics by combining zero net magnetization with nonrelativistic spin splitting, yet efficient electrical manipulation of their spin-dependent transport remains challenging. Here, using first-principles calculations, we show that an out-of-plane electric field induces spin-momentum locking in bilayer Cr$_{2}$SeO, gives rise to a magneto-optical Kerr effect, and drives a semiconductor-to-metal transition at sufficiently high field magnitudes. Reversing the field direction switches the spin-momentum-locking pattern, which reverses the sign of the Kerr rotation angle as well as that of the longitudinal and transverse spin conductivities. Leveraging this electric-field-controlled spin-momentum locking, we propose a dual-gate altermagnetic tunnel junction in which high- and low-resistance states are realized without reversing the Néel vector. The resistance switching originates from the matching and mismatching of spin-polarized conducting channels in momentum space, yielding a tunneling magnetoresistance ratio on the order of $10^{8}$. Our findings provide a theoretical basis for realizing electric-field-controlled spin-momentum locking in bilayer Cr$_{2}$SeO and developing all-electrically controlled altermagnetic spintronic devices.

papers.title: On construction of differential $\mathbb Z$-graded varieties
papers.abstract: Given a commutative unital algebra $\mathcal O$, a proper ideal $\mathcal I$ in $\mathcal O$, and a positively graded differential variety over $\mathcal O/\mathcal I$, we provide a $\mathbb Z$-graded extension, whose negative part is an arborescent Koszul-Tate resolution of $\mathcal O/ \mathcal I$. This extension is obtained through an algorithm exploiting the explicit homotopy retract data of the arborescent Koszul-Tate resolution, so that the number of homological computations in the construction is significantly reduced. For a positively graded differential variety over $\mathcal O$ that preserves the ideal $\mathcal I$, the extension admits a manifest description in terms of decorated trees and computed data. As a by-product, to every Lie-Rinehart algebra over the coordinate ring of an affine variety $ W \subseteq M = \mathbb{C}^d$, one associates an explicit differential $\mathbb{Z}$-graded variety over $M$ whose negative component is the arborescent Koszul-Tate resolution of the coordinate ring $\mathbb C[x_1, \ldots, x_d]/\mathcal I_W$ of $W$, and whose positive component is the universal dg-variety of the given Lie-Rinehart algebra. Concrete examples are given.

papers.title: Cyber Resilience in Next-Generation Networks: Threat Landscape, Theoretical Foundations, and Design Paradigms
On Oscillatory Integral Operators Satisfying the cinematic curvature condition
papers.abstract: We establish improved $L^r\mapsto L^p$ estimates for oscillatory integral operators satisfying the positive cinematic curvature condition. In ambient dimension $n\geq4$, the output range is $p>2+8/(3n-4)$, with the full Knapp-admissible input range $r'\leq (n-2)p/n$. The proof combines a transverse covering $L^2$ estimate, Wolff's two-ends reduction, and refined decoupling. In dimension $n=3$ we retain the range $p>4$.

papers.title: Better Call Graphs: A New Dataset of Function Call Graphs for Malware Classification
Differential calculus on bigraded spaces and Koszul duality
papers.abstract: Koszul duality for superalgebras involves both the intrinsic super parity and the degree shift introduced by suspension. We study this duality while keeping the two gradings separate, using a $\mathbb Z\times\mathbb Z$-graded refinement of the commutativity convention of Deligne and Morgan. In this setting, the Koszul suspension preserves the parity degree and raises the independent weight by one. We realize the polynomial superalgebr $\mathcal O(k^{m|n})$ and its Koszul dual as function algebras on bigraded spaces and construct an isomorphism between their differential calculi of polyvector fields and mixed differential forms. For admissible quadratic Poisson structures, whose bivectors have bidegree $(0,2)$, this isomorphism descends to the differential calculi on Poisson cohomology and mixed Poisson homology. With respect to the corresponding mixed volume forms, Koszul duality preserves unimodularity and, in the unimodular case, identifies the induced Batalin--Vilkovisky algebra structures on Poisson cohomology.

papers.title: Unraveling time-varying causal effects of multiple exposures: integrating Functional Data Analysis with Multivariable Mendelian Randomization
papers.abstract: Mendelian Randomization is a widely used instrumental variable method for assessing causal effects of lifelong exposures on health outcomes. Many exposures, however, have causal effects that vary across the life course and often influence outcomes jointly with other exposures or indirectly through mediating pathways. Existing approaches to multivariable Mendelian Randomization assume constant effects over time and therefore fail to capture these dynamic relationships. We introduce Multivariable Functional Mendelian Randomization (MV-FMR), a new framework that extends functional Mendelian Randomization to simultaneously model multiple time-varying exposures. The method combines functional principal component analysis with a data-driven cross-validation strategy for basis selection and accounts for overlapping instruments and mediation effects. Through extensive simulations, we assessed MV-FMR's ability to recover time-varying causal effects under a range of data-generating scenarios and compared the performance of joint versus separate exposure effect estimation strategies. Across scenarios involving nonlinear effects, horizontal pleiotropy, mediation, and sparse data, MV-FMR consistently recovered the true causal functions and outperformed univariable approaches. To demonstrate its practical value, we applied MV-FMR to UK Biobank data to investigate the time-varying causal effects of systolic blood pressure and body mass index on coronary artery disease. MV-FMR provides a flexible and interpretable framework for disentangling complex time-dependent causal processes and offers new opportunities for identifying life-course critical periods and actionable drivers relevant to disease prevention.

papers.title: Hierarchical filtrations of vector bundles and birational geometry
papers.abstract: We study chains of locally free subsheaves of equal rank whose successive quotients are nonzero divisorial torsion sheaves. Fixing the determinant of the initial term defines a normalized hierarchical depth. An ample intersection argument proves finiteness on every smooth projective variety. On an algebraically closed smooth projective curve, the depth equals the degree of the determinant difference precisely when that difference is effective; otherwise, no normalized filtration exists. For birational morphisms of smooth projective surfaces, reflexive pushforward contracts exactly those steps whose determinant divisors are entirely exceptional. This yields a comparison of filtration lengths without a commutativity assumption. Explicit examples show that pullback can strictly increase depth and compute a depth of twenty on a two-point blowup. Finally, we distinguish preservation of evaluation codes for genuinely descended bundles from removal of zero coordinates caused by exceptional fixed components. The coding statements use specified compatible fiber bases or the block Hamming metric.

papers.title: The Narrow Corridor of Stable Solutions in an Extended Osipov--Lanchester Model with Constant Total Population
papers.abstract: This paper studies a modification of the classical Osipov-Lanchester model in which the total population of the two sides, $N=R+B$, stays constant. In this model the ratio $y=R/B$ obeys the Riccati equation $\dot y=\alpha y^2-\beta$, which is solvable in elementary functions for all values of the parameters. The main result is a complete classification of the stable regimes. An asymptotically stable invariant set in the quadrant $R,B\ge 0$ exists only in three cases: $\alpha<0,\ \beta<0$ gives a stable interior equilibrium; $\alpha=0,\ \beta<0$ makes the boundary $B=0$ stable; $\alpha<0,\ \beta=0$ makes the boundary $R=0$ stable. If $\alpha>0$ or $\beta>0$, every solution except one unstable equilibrium reaches a boundary of the quadrant in finite time, where the model stops being applicable. If the parameters vary in time, a fixed distance from the boundaries is kept when $\alpha(t)$ and $\beta(t)$ obey buffer dynamics that push them away from zero. Finally, in the case $\alpha<0,\ \beta<0$ the original system grows exponentially, while in the two degenerate cases it grows at most linearly. Growth demanded of a given cost, the sum of the two channels, bounds their imbalance and, with the perturbation bound, confines the parameters to an explicit wedge about $|\alpha|=|\beta|$ truncated near the origin: the narrow corridor of the model.

papers.title: VeruSAGE-Bench: A Benchmark Suite for Rust System Verification
Correcting quantum errors one gradient step at a time
papers.abstract: Probabilistic approximate quantum error correction (PAQEC) lets a recovery fail with some probability, in exchange for higher fidelity when it succeeds. Prior PAQEC code searches keep the codewords orthonormal with penalty terms and tune the code without its best recovery. We propose a gradient method with three new parts. First, the codewords move on the complex Stiefel manifold, so they are orthonormal at every step without penalties. Second, every code is trained against its best recovery, which we solve for at each step rather than learn. Third, a fast Petz recovery that we can differentiate even for symmetric codes gets the search close, and the exact semidefinite program finishes it. We train a single five-qubit code over generalized amplitude damping noise. At weak noise ($\gamma = 0.1$, $p = 0.05$) and equal success probability, it has $23$ times lower infidelity than the permutation-invariant code of prior work, and $9$ times lower than that work's numerically optimized code. At equal fidelity it succeeds $91\%$ of the time, against $76\%$ for the permutation-invariant code.

papers.title: On-Demand Millisecond Storage of Spectrotemporal Multimode Telecom Photons
papers.abstract: The realization of scalable quantum networks for distribution of entanglement over long distances hinges on quantum repeaters. To outperform the exponential transmission loss in optical fibers, quantum repeaters must employ multiplexing schemes in the temporal, spectral, or spatial domain. The performance of such a multiplexed scheme is contingent on efficient quantum memories offering both extended storage times and large multimode capacities. Towards this goal, we experimentally demonstrate a memory platform operating at telecom wavelength using an Er$^{3+}$:Y$_{2}$SiO$_{5}$ crystal. We record on-demand storage and recall of weak coherent pulses for up to $1$ ms, exceeding by an order of magnitude that of previously reported demonstrations based on Er$^{3+}$. The memory exhibits an efficiency of 10.36 % at 300 $\mu$s storage time with a signal-to-noise ratio of $10.9$, mainly limited by spontaneous emission noise. We also store two spectral modes representing a frequency-bin encoding and retrieve the state with an overlap of 81.8 %. Furthermore, we demonstrate multimode capacity by simultaneously storing 20 temporal and 3 spectral modes with on-demand and selective recall capabilities, serving as a promising step toward a scalable quantum repeater architecture.

papers.title: From Evidence to Judgment: Trace-Augmented Reasoning under Conflicting Evidence
CLARiTy: A Vision Transformer for Multi-Label Classification and Weakly-Supervised Localization of Chest X-ray Pathologies
Fiberwise criteria for Fourier--Mukai equivalences
papers.abstract: We prove fiberwise criteria for full faithfulness and equivalences of integral transforms between proper flat families of schemes over a separated Noetherian base. The kernels are bounded pseudocoherent complexes which are relatively perfect over each factor, and need not be perfect. A key ingredient is the calculus of mates, which controls the units and counits of adjoint integral transforms under base change. In particular, we give a complete argument for a fiberwise criterion of Hernández Ruipérez--López Martín--Sancho de Salas, and extend it to arbitrary separated Noetherian bases. As applications, we extend a result of Orlov on field extensions to singular varieties, and show that over a Noetherian local ring these properties can be detected on the special fiber.

papers.title: On the connectedness of a minimizing cluster's boundary
papers.abstract: We verify that an isoperimetric minimizing cluster on a simply connected homogeneous Riemannian manifold with at most one end always has connected boundary. In particular, the boundary of a single-bubble isoperimetric minimizer on such manifolds must be connected, and hence all isoperimetric sets and their complements must be connected. This is demonstrably false without the simple connectedness assumption or the restriction on the number of ends.

papers.title: Duality Relations of Graph Polynomials
papers.abstract: The duality theorem of Lass relates the matching polynomials of a simple graph $G$ with the matching polynomials of its complement $\bar G$. In particular, this relation gives rise to Godsil's result, which offers a nice interpretation of the Lebesgue integral associated with the Hermite orthogonality measure. In this work, we show that similar to matching polynomials, the path-cover polynomials also satisfy duality relations and give combinatorial interpretations of the Lebesgue integral and the inner product in the space of associated Laguerre polynomials. Similar duality relations hold for clique-cover polynomials and chromatic polynomials. As applications, we find an efficient algorithm that computes these graph polynomials for cographs. We also give explicit formulas to compute the number of Hamiltonian paths and cycles in complete multipartite graphs.

papers.title: Noise-Induced Thermalization in Quantum Systems
papers.abstract: In the current Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum era, noise is widely regarded as the primary obstacle to achieving fault-tolerant quantum computation. However, certain stages of the quantum computing pipeline can, in fact, benefit from this noise. In this work, we exploit the Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis to show that noise generically accelerates a fundamental task in quantum computing -- the preparation of Gibbs states. We demonstrate this behavior using classical and quantum simulations with Haar-random and phase-flip noise, respectively, on a spin-1/2 chain with a local Hamiltonian. Our non-integrable model sees ~3.5x faster thermalization in the presence of noise, while our integrable model, which would not otherwise thermalize, reaches a thermal state due to noise. Since certifying a local Gibbs state is relatively easy on a quantum computer, our approach provides a new practical solution to a key problem in quantum computing. More broadly, these results establish a new paradigm in which noise can be harnessed on quantum computers, enabling practical advantages before the years of fault-tolerance.

papers.title: Large-scale patterns of small-scale vorticity interactions foster moist convection during cyclogenesis
papers.abstract: Understanding the self-organization of small-scale moist convection at synoptic scales during tropical cyclogenesis is essential. We examine the role of vorticity interactions in dynamical organization of moist convection during cyclogenesis in the Bay of Bengal. Using time-varying complex networks, we encode local vorticity correlations between nodes (locations), only within a spatial proximity of sub-meso length scales. Links are established using short-time correlation of vorticity fluctuations. Spatial patches of high network connectivity depict regions of locally coherent vorticity dynamics. We find that various patches of high network connectivity arrange into extended structures forming identifiable large-scale patterns. Examining the co-evolution of moist thermodynamics parameters with local vorticity coherence, we discover a unique spatial correlation between the convective processes occurring at far away locations, owing to self-organization. We find that such spatial correlation are evident only for depressions that form cyclones, and not otherwise. We discover the physical mechanism of self-organization using modal analysis of network connectivity and vorticity budgets. In regions identified as most influential by the modal analysis, we find that vertical vorticity is enhanced locally as well as advected horizontally outwards to other locations. Such horizontal advection of vertical vorticity induces nonlocal interactions and couples small-scale convective processes across a large domain. We show that, vertical vorticity transported from regions of high convective potential help sustain strong updrafts and weaken convective inhibition in other regions. Thus, spatial interdependence is introduced between small-scale convective processes at different locations, thus explaining the self-organization of moist convection during cyclogenesis.

papers.title: Comparative Evaluation of Embedding Representations for Financial News Sentiment Analysis
Illumination-Robust Localization around Unknown Space Objects using Multispectral Image Fusion
An unfitted divergence-free higher order finite element method for the Stokes problem
Mind the Gap: Cross-RFC Formal Analysis Exposes DNSSEC's Hidden Vulnerabilities
Universal relaxation speedup in nonequilibrium quantum many-body systems through transient resetting
papers.abstract: Speeding up the relaxation dynamics of many-body quantum systems is important in a variety of contexts, including quantum computation and state preparation. We demonstrate that such acceleration can be universally achieved via transient stochastic resetting. This means that during an initial time interval of finite duration, the dynamics is interrupted by resets that take the system to a designated state at randomly selected times. We illustrate this idea for few-body open systems and also for a challenging many-body case, where a first-order phase transition leads to a divergence of relaxation time. In all scenarios, a significant and sometimes even exponential acceleration in reaching the stationary state is observed, similar to the so-called Mpemba effect. The universal nature of this speedup lies in the fact that the design of the resetting protocol only requires knowledge of a few macroscopic properties of the target state, such as the order parameter of the phase transition, while it does not necessitate any fine-tuned manipulation of the initial state.

papers.title: A Simulation Framework with Guaranteed Error Bounds for Safety and Fuel-Efficiency Analysis of Vehicle Platoons
Balancing Weights for Causal Mediation Analysis
papers.abstract: Causal mediation analysis decomposes the average treatment effect into components that operate through intermediate variables and a component that does not. This paper studies weighting estimation of generalized mediation functionals, whose contrasts include natural direct and indirect effects, for any fixed finite number of causally ordered mediators. Inverse propensity score weights are vulnerable to (a) weight instability, because they are products of estimated probability ratios, and (b) finite-sample covariate and mediator imbalance, which can bias the estimator. We instead propose sequential balancing weights, which address (a) by minimizing weight dispersion and (b) by imposing exact balance. Stage one balances covariates between a treatment group and the full sample. Each later stage adds the next mediator and balances a treatment group against the preceding weighted group. A finite-sample bias decomposition of the augmented weighting estimator determines these variables and targets. When exact balance cannot be attained in a small sample, the procedure relaxes the balancing conditions by tolerances selected without using the outcome. Under the stated assumptions, the estimated weights converge at every stage to their population inverse-probability counterparts, with errors from preceding stages entering additively. We also establish asymptotic normality and semiparametric efficiency of the augmented weighting estimator, together with conditions for consistent variance estimation. In the main simulation design with two ordered mediators, the proposed weights outperform the compared methods in bias, root mean squared error, and coverage. In a small media-framing experiment with two ordered mediators, the proposed weights reduce the imbalance left by propensity-score weighting.

papers.title: On the Green's functions and Martin boundary structure of a planar diffusion in a discontinuous layered medium
papers.abstract: We consider a two-dimensional diffusion process in a two-layered plane, governed by distinct covariance matrices in the upper and lower half-planes and by two drift vectors pointed away from the $x$-axis. We first analyze the case where the generator of the process is in divergence form, that is, when the flux is continuous across the interface. Then we extend the study to a broader class of processes whose behavior at the interface forms an oblique two-dimensional analogue of the skew Brownian motion. We provide a detailed theoretical analysis of this transient process. Our main results are as follows: (i) we derive explicit Laplace transforms of the Green's functions; (ii) we compute exact asymptotics of the Green's functions along all possible trajectories in the plane; (iii) We determine all positive harmonic functions, identifying the full and minimal Martin boundaries, which turn out to be distinct. The nonminimality of the Martin boundary is a noteworthy phenomenon for diffusions with regular coefficients. To obtain an analytical description of the process, we fully develop a three-variable version of the so-called kernel method by deriving and exploiting a functional equation involving unknown Laplace transforms of Green's functions and two known kernels $\gamma_+(x,y)$ and $\gamma_{-}(x,z)$. The introduction of independent auxiliary variables $y$ and $z$, associated with each half-plane, is a key idea.

papers.title: Regular black hole sourced by the Dehnen-type distribution of matter: The sound of the event horizon
papers.abstract: We compute the fundamental and overtone quasinormal modes of a regular, asymptotically flat black hole supported by a Dehnen-type matter halo. Gravitational perturbations in this background split into two distinct axial sectors, and our analysis confirms that the presence of the halo parameter $a$ separates the spectra of the two axial matter-perturbation prescriptions, which coincide in vacuum. The dependence of the quasinormal spectrum on $a$ is moderate for the fundamental modes and even weaker for the overtones, which approach one another in the complex-frequency plane as the halo parameter increases. We have found that no pronounced overtone outburst is observed at least for the first several overtones, indicating that the halo does not induce the type of strong near-horizon effects characteristic of quantum-corrected or exotic compact objects. Overall, our results show that the dark-matter halo introduces controlled and comparatively mild modifications to the ringdown spectrum while preserving its qualitative structure.

papers.title: Measurement of Z$γ$ production in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13.6 TeV and constraints on neutral triple gauge couplings
papers.abstract: A measurement of the Z$\gamma$ production cross section in proton-proton collisions at a center-of-mass energy of 13.6 TeV is presented. Data corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 34.8 fb$^{-1}$, collected by the CMS experiment at the LHC in 2022 are used. Events with an oppositely charged pair of muons or electrons, with an invariant mass corresponding to a Z boson, together with an isolated photon are selected. The measured fiducial cross section for the combined electron and muon channels is 1.896 $\pm$ 0.033 (stat) $\pm$ 0.054 (syst) $\pm$ 0.006 (theo) pb, in agreement with the standard model prediction of 1.922 $\pm$ 0.094 pb. Constraints on neutral triple gauge couplings generated by dimension-8 operators in a recently proposed effective field theory framework are determined for the first time.

papers.title: Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Joint Source and Parameter Estimation in Advection-Diffusion Equations
papers.abstract: Source inversion problems under sparse measurements for parabolic partial differential equations (PDEs) are particularly challenging to solve using physics-informed neural networks (PINNs), due to their severe ill-posedness and the multiple unknowns involved including the source function and the PDE parameters. Although the neural tangent kernel (NTK) of PINNs has been widely used in forward problems involving a single neural network, its extension to inverse problems involving multiple neural networks remains less explored. In this work, we propose a weighted adaptive approach based on the NTK of PINNs including multiple networks representing the solution, the unknown source, and the PDE parameters. The key idea behind our methodology is to simultaneously solve the joint recovery of these unknowns thereby using the underlying PDE as a constraint that couples multiple unknowns functional parameters, leading to more efficient use of the limited information in the measurements. Furthermore, we provide a theoretical analysis of the approximation error of PINNs in a source inverse problem governed by the advection-diffusion equation (ADE) with known velocity and diffusion coefficients. In particular, we derive an error bound for the estimated source function in terms of the PINN's training error, the noise level and the discretization error. This analysis provides theoretical insight into the factors influencing the approximation accuracy. We present numerical experiments on 2D and 3D ADE using different types of measurements data reflecting practical engineering systems. Our results demonstrate the successful performance of PINNs in solving our source inversion problem and its robustness to noise in the measurements.

papers.title: Approximate Surface Tension of Phase Separating Interfaces using Residual Forces
papers.abstract: Extending methods that have been successful in determining the surface tension of equilibrium interfaces to active Brownian particle systems have resulted in negative and/or unusually large values of the interfacial tension, raising questions about the applicability of these frameworks to nonequilibrium interfaces. The absence of a general framework for understanding interfacial tension independently of equilibrium thermodynamics makes this problem particularly challenging. Here, I develop a new framework that provides an order-of-magnitude estimate of the interfacial tension using average force densities that are accessible even when the system is not in thermodynamic equilibrium. Applying this framework to active interfaces yields estimates that differ substantially in both sign and magnitude from previously reported results, highlighting the need to reassess existing approaches to interfacial tension in active matter.

papers.title: jahn-teller-dynamics: Python package to determine vibronic interaction demonstrated on molecules and trigonal defect qubits
papers.abstract: Trigonal solid-state defects are often subjects of spontaneous symmetry breaking driven by the $E\otimes e$ Jahn-Teller effect, reflecting strong electron-phonon coupling. These systems, particularly paramagnetic defect qubits in solids are central for quantum technology applications, where accurate knowledge of their fine-structure parameters - shaped by the complex interplay of spin-orbit and electron-phonon interactions - is essential. We introduce the $\mathtt{jahn {\text -} teller {\text -} dynamics}$ package, a Python code that implements the first-principles approach of [Phys. Rev. X 8, 021063 (2018)] to accurately compute the spin-orbit-phonon entanglement in trigonal defects utilizing the output from density functional theory calculations (DFT) to predict fine-structure parameters of zero-phonon lines (ZPLs), including Zeeman shifts under external magnetic fields. We demonstrate its capabilities on negatively charged Group-IV-vacancy (G4V) defects in diamond: SiV$^-$, GeV$^-$, SnV$^-$, PbV$^-$ and the neutral N$_3$V$^0$ defect in diamond, and the CH$_3$O$^0$ methoxy radical. Additionally, we implement a generic electron-phonon code that is capable entangling an arbitrary amount of (i) vibration modes and (ii) electronic levels by (iii) arbitrarily high order of vibronic interaction terms. Exemplarily, we demonstrate the Jahn-Teller multimode problem on the CH$_3$O$^0$ methoxy radical and the Pseudo Jahn-Teller case on the $C_4H_4^+$ butatrien cation.

papers.title: A Survey of Bugs in AI-Generated Code
Adapting Large Language Models to Low-Resource Tibetan: A Two-Stage Continual and Supervised Fine-Tuning Study
A choice-based axiomatization of Nash equilibrium
papers.abstract: An axiomatization of Nash equilibrium is provided for games of complete information in normal form. The Nash equilibrium correspondence is shown to be the unique solution concept that satisfies four simple and intuitive axioms. Two axioms reflect a mild form of individual rationality: one states that any profile of dominant strategies in a game must be a solution, whereas the other says that any solution to a game should not depend on strictly dominated strategies. The remaining two axioms are adaptations to non-cooperative games of standard choice-theoretic axioms about contraction and expansion consistency.

papers.title: Guideline-Based Medical Reasoning in LLMs
Observation of an anomaly in the statistics of Kibble-Zurek defects
papers.abstract: The Kibble-Zurek mechanism quantifies defect formation during finite-rate passage across a continuous phase transition, providing key insights into universality in quantum many-body systems. We explore counting statistics of defects in finite-rate ramp experiments on long 1D Rydberg atom chains. The experiments reveal an anomaly in the defect number distribution at long ramp times, challenging the hypothesis of defect formation through independent domain mergers. Numerical simulations reproduce the anomaly and support an interpretation in terms of post-critical coarsening during the ramp, while prepare-and-hold experiments reveal no subsequent secular growth of the measured correlations. Our results show the limits of classical or integrable system descriptions of Kibble-Zurek defect formation for interacting quantum systems.

papers.title: On the future cover of a sofic shift
papers.abstract: The paper contains a new proof of the theorem by Krieger which establishes the canonicity of the future cover of a sofic shift. In addition the paper describes a method to produce new canonical covers from a given one, resulting in canonical covers related to, but generally different from the future cover.

papers.title: Kicking for Goal or Touch? An Expected Points Framework for Penalty Decisions in Rugby Union
papers.abstract: Following a penalty in rugby union, teams typically choose between attempting a kick at goal or kicking to touch to pursue a try. We develop an Expected Points (EP) framework that quantifies the value of each option as a function of field location and game context. Using phase-level data and observed penalty kicks, we construct two context-aware surfaces: (i) the expected points of a possession beginning with a lineout and (ii) the expected points of attempting a kick at goal. Comparing these surfaces yields decision maps that identify where kicking for goal or kicking to touch maximizes expected points, and how the boundary shifts with game context and expected meters gained to touch. To our knowledge, this is the first comprehensive EP-based assessment of penalty strategy in rugby union; it also provides a foundation for future refinement with richer event data and extension to win-probability analysis.

papers.title: Strong nonlinear detectability and moving horizon estimation for nonlinear systems with unknown inputs
Breaking the Visual Shortcuts in Multimodal Knowledge-Based Visual Question Answering
Campana separable rational connectedness of toric orbifold
papers.abstract: Campana introduced a notion of Campana rational connectedness for Campana orbifolds and conjectured that certain Fano orbifolds are Campana rationally connected. In this paper, we study a version of this conjecture in positive characteristic and verify a stronger statement for some toric orbifolds. We also provide examples illustrating the relation between the failure of separable Campana rational connectedness and singularities.

papers.title: Mutual arc presentations and braided open books
papers.abstract: We show that every canonically fibered link in $S^3$ is the binding of a braided open book in $S^3$, addressing a question of Montesinos and Morton. We introduce mutual arc presentations as our main technical tool, which we consider to be of independent interest. We prove that any fibered link admitting such a presentation is the binding of a braided open book.

papers.title: Model-free practical PI-Lead control design by ultimate sensitivity principle
Towards superior van der Waals density functionals for molecular crystals
papers.abstract: Ubiquitous van der Waals (vdW) interactions play a subtle yet crucial role in determining the precise atomic arrangements in solids, particularly in molecular crystals where these weak forces are the primary link between constituent building blocks. Within density functional (DF) theory, the most natural approach to address them is the use of vdW-inclusive density functionals. Through a detailed analysis of the underlying formalism, we have developed a computational scheme that combines vdW functionals of type DF1 and DF2 providing a readily tunable framework to improve the theoretical description and prediction of molecular crystals and other sparse materials. The proof of principle is demonstrated by benchmarking our method on the X23 dataset of molecular crystals.

papers.title: CrypTorch: Unified PyTorch-based Auto-tuning Compiler for Private Machine Learning Inference
A Layered Protocol Architecture for the Internet of Agents
Re(Visiting) Time Series Foundation Models in Finance
papers.abstract: Financial time series forecasting is vital for trading, portfolio optimization, and risk management but is challenged by noisy, nonstationary, and heterogeneous data. Time series foundation models (TSFMs), inspired by large language models, aim to learn transferable temporal representations. Whether pre-training on massive, diverse datasets enables similar generalization to finance remains an open question. This study provides a comprehensive empirical evaluation of TSFMs in global financial markets using large-scale daily excess-return data. We assess zero-shot inference, fine-tuning, and pre-training from scratch against strong benchmarks. Off-the-shelf TSFMs generally perform poorly, while finance-native pre-training improves long-window gross portfolio performance. Larger pre-training datasets and synthetic augmentation improve selected specifications, particularly at longer input windows. Configuration changes have mixed effects across forecasting and portfolio metrics, and TSFMs do not consistently outperform strong benchmarks. These findings caution against uncritical AI adoption in finance, where insufficient validation can lead to unreliable forecasts and substantial financial losses.

papers.title: On the Iterates of Endomorphisms of Projective Varieties
papers.abstract: We initiate a study of certain notions related to the algebraic dynamics of endomorphisms of projective varieties. Our main results include: (i) a characterization of projective varieties that occur as iterated images of endomorphisms of normal projective varieties; (ii) exploring stability behavior in the Stein factorizations of the iterates; and (iii) a structure result concerning endomorphisms whose iterates lie in a finite union of connected components of the endomorphism scheme, thereby completing a result of Brion.

papers.title: Diffusion-based Surrogate Model for Time-varying Underwater Acoustic Channels
Adaptive Layer-Wise Transformations for Post-Training Quantization of Large Language Models
Quadratic Mean-Field BSDEs and Exponential Utility Maximization
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study a class of real-valued mean-field backward stochastic differential equations (BSDEs) with generators of quadratic growth in the control variable and the mean-field term. For bounded terminal conditions satisfying suitable structural regularity, we establish existence and uniqueness under two complementary quadratic regimes; the uniformly continuous path-dependent case additionally requires a uniform quadratic bound on the normalized generator. Our approach for these results combines Malliavin calculus with refined BMO and stability estimates, and bridges the gap between the quadratic BSDE results of [Ann. Probab. 45 (2017), pp. 3795--3828] and [Ann. Appl. Probab. 35 (2025), pp. 2128--2174]. Motivated by a mean-field exponential utility maximization problem, we further extend our framework to terminal conditions without imposing continuity or Markovian structure on the terminal condition. Under a suitable smallness condition on the oscillation of the terminal value around its mean, the associated quadratic BSDE admits a unique solution in a suitable small solution class. We then apply the extended theory to solve a mean-field exponential utility maximization problem, thereby extending the constrained exponential utility framework of Hu et al. [Ann. Appl. Probab. 15 (2005), pp. 1691--1712] to a mean-field setting.

papers.title: A convex approach for Markov chain estimation from aggregate data via inverse optimal transport
papers.abstract: We address the problem of identifying the dynamical law governing the evolution of a population of indistinguishable particles, when only aggregate distributions at successive times are observed. Assuming a Markovian evolution on a discrete state space, the task reduces to estimating the underlying transition probability matrix from distributional data. We formulate this inverse problem within the framework of entropic optimal transport, as a joint optimization over the transition matrix and the transport plans connecting successive distributions. This formulation results in a convex optimization problem, and we propose an efficient iterative algorithm based on the entropic proximal method. We illustrate the accuracy and convergence of the method in two numerical setups, considering estimation from independent snapshots and estimation from a time series of aggregate observations, respectively.

papers.title: LoC-IN: Real-Time Localization of Cameras in Neural Rendered Prior LiDAR Maps
Almost-simple algebraic supergroups
papers.abstract: We investigate certain almost-simple algebraic supergroups over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero or odd characteristic. Beyond those whose Lie superalgebras are simple and appear in Kac's classification, we construct new families of almost-simple supergroups whose Lie superalgebras are either non-simple or simple but fall outside Kac's classification.

papers.title: Recursive Entropic Variational Inference for Nonlinear State-Space Models
The Walls Have Ears: Unveiling Cross-Chain Sandwich Attacks in DeFi
SciEGQA: A Dataset for Scientific Evidence-Grounded Question Answering and Reasoning
Dynamics of Dehn twists in the outer automorphism group of a free group
papers.abstract: We study Dehn twists in the outer automorphism group of a free group through the doubled handlebody, a connected sum of copies of the product of a circle and a two-sphere, in which the Dehn twist along a primitive torus is induced by twisting a regular neighborhood of the torus. Our main result states that sufficiently large powers of the Dehn twists along a compatible collection of primitive tori generate a right-angled Artin group. The proof is a ping-pong argument in the universal cover, the complement of a Cantor set in the three-sphere, where intersection numbers become counts of orbits of lifts. Along the way we show that commuting Dehn twists along primitive tori have tori whose lifts never cross, and that a Dehn twist determines the oriented cyclic splitting dual to its torus. Finally, we construct a compact space of primitive curves on which multitwists act parabolically and fully irreducible outer automorphisms act with north--south dynamics.

papers.title: An auto-initializing algorithm to determine electronic ground states from random Slater determinants
papers.abstract: Accurate quantum many-body calculations often depend on reliable reference states or good human-designed ansätze, yet such knowledge can become unreliable in hard problems like strongly correlated systems. Here we show that high-accuracy many-body ground states can be discovered directly from random Slater determinants. We introduce the Trimmed Configuration Interaction (TrimCI) method, which self-refines by iteratively expanding and trimming configurations in the variational space. TrimCI matches state-of-the-art accuracy using orders of magnitude fewer determinants and computer time: $10^6$-fold fewer than a recent quantum computing calculation on an iron-sulfur cluster, $10^5$-fold fewer than a leading classical method on a larger iron-sulfur cluster in nitrogenase, and over 99% of the ground-state energy of a strongly correlated lattice system from $10^{-28}$ of its Hilbert space, exceeding quantum Monte Carlo accuracy by orders of magnitude in some regimes. TrimCI thus provides an auto-initializing, accurate and highly efficient framework for quantum many-body systems, whose compact explicit wavefunctions enable direct and rapid evaluation of observables.

papers.title: Giant enhancement of attosecond tunnel ionization competes with disorder-driven decoherence in amorphized silicon
papers.abstract: High-harmonic generation (HHG) and tunnel ionization in solids are strong-field phenomena sensitive to the attosecond dynamics of laser-driven electron-hole pairs. While HHG has been used extensively as a spectroscopic probe in crystalline systems, its potential as a probe of disorder on the length scale of electron-hole trajectories remains relatively unexplored. Furthermore, with the advent of petahertz electronics, there is a growing need for controlling ionization on the nanoscale. Here, we show how focused-ion beam driven amorphization of silicon leads to a giant enhancement ($>$250 times) of yield for lower-order harmonics and quenching of higher-order harmonics, consistent with a dramatically enhanced tunnel ionization yield and disorder-induced decoherence, respectively. Modelling the real-space quantum dynamics, we show how electron-hole coherence in the amorphous phase is lost over a characteristic length of approximately five lattice sites. HHG spectroscopy also reveals remnant order inherited from the original cubic structure. Our results establish HHG spectroscopy as a probe of medium-range order and pave the way for new opportunities in lightwave nanoelectronics.

papers.title: Efficient Hamiltonian-aware Quantum Natural Gradient Descent for Variational Quantum Eigensolvers
papers.abstract: The Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) is one of the most promising algorithms for current quantum devices. It employs a classical optimizer to iteratively update the parameters of a variational quantum circuit in order to search for the ground state of a given Hamiltonian. The efficacy of VQEs largely depends on the optimizer employed. Recent studies suggest that Quantum Natural Gradient Descent (QNG) can achieve faster convergence speed than vanilla gradient descent (VG), but at the cost of additional quantum resources to estimate the Fubini-Study metric tensor in each optimization step. The Fubini-Study metric tensor used in QNG is related to the entire quantum state space and does not incorporate information about the target Hamiltonian. To take advantage of the structure of the Hamiltonian and address the limitation of additional computational cost in QNG, we propose Hamiltonian-aware Quantum Natural Gradient Descent (H-QNG). In H-QNG, we propose to use the Riemannian pullback metric induced from the lower-dimensional subspace spanned by the Hamiltonian terms onto the parameter space. We show that H-QNG inherits the desirable features of both approaches: the low quantum computational cost of VG and the reparameterization-invariance of QNG. We also validate its performance through numerical experiments on molecular Hamiltonians, showing that H-QNG achieves faster convergence to lower energy while requiring fewer quantum computational resources.

papers.title: An Online Multiobjective Policy Gradient for Long-run Average-reward Markov Decision Process
Modeling stellar convective transport with plumes : II. Transport Properties of Locally and Non-locally driven Convection
papers.abstract: We perform three-dimensional hydrodynamic simulations of two idealized convection setups: a cooling-driven model (Model C) and an entropy-gradient-driven model (Model S). The two setups exhibit clear differences: while Model S develops large, relatively stationary eddies excited at depth, Model C is dominated near the surface by intermittent plume-like downflows that produce broad non-Gaussian velocity distributions and a turbulent energy flux that exceeds that in Model S by nearly an order of magnitude in the upper convection zone. Conventional gradient-diffusion (GD) closures reproduce the transport in Model S but significantly underestimate it in Model C, demonstrating that the plume-dominated transport realized in our cooling-driven setup cannot be reproduced by a local, gradient-based model. To address this, we introduce a Time-Space Double Averaging (TSDA) method that extracts coherent fluctuations, yielding a diagnostic variable $\tilde{\mathbf{u}}$ that peaks where the flux is largest. Building on this insight, we propose a modified GD closure in which the turbulent diffusivity is corrected by a plume-mediated term, achieving quantitative agreement with simulation results. Although the closure requires a calibrated model parameter and a careful choice of the averaging window, it provides a physically transparent framework that links coherent plume dynamics to mean-field transport and offers a pathway toward improved subgrid models for non-equilibrium stellar convection zones.

papers.title: A Systematic Analysis of Out-of-Distribution Detection Under Representation and Training Paradigm Shifts
Log-Averaged Mirror Prox for Fast, Large-Scale Optimal Transport in Linear Space
papers.abstract: We propose Log-Averaged Mirror Prox (LAMP), a linear-space primal-dual method for large-scale optimal transport. LAMP implements primal mirror prox updates by tracking an averaged dual sequence, reducing storage complexity from $\mathcal{O}(nm)$ to $\mathcal{O}(n+m)$ while preserving dense, GPU-friendly reductions. Consequently, LAMP preserves the last-iterate $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(\|C\|_\infty nm\varepsilon^{-1})$ arithmetic complexity of conservatively parameterized primal-dual mirror prox. We further analyze LAMP as a direct optimal transport solver in a more performant parameter regime, providing a last-iterate sub-optimality certificate dependent on infeasibility and an explicit $\mathcal O(\|C\|_\infty\log (m)/t)$ term. Moreover, we give a computable sufficient condition for ergodic convergence. Numerical experiments with an optimized CUDA implementation show that LAMP outperforms first-order baselines in several high-accuracy (entropic) optimal transport problems. LAMP is further shown to scale up to problems with $n=m=2^{18}$ marginal supports, which were previously beyond the reach of primal-dual first-order methods.

papers.title: Automorphisms of the Worm Domain
papers.abstract: The Diederich--Fornæss worm domain, an important example of a smoothly bounded pseudoconvex domain without a Stein neighborhood basis, provides key counterexamples in the theory of several complex variables. In this paper, we examine its automorphism group and observe that its boundary is locally spherical everywhere except at the exceptional locus and the closure of the caps.

papers.title: 2.5D Transformer: An Efficient 3D Seismic Interpolation Method without Full 3D Training
papers.abstract: Transformer has emerged as a powerful deep-learning technique for two-dimensional (2D) seismic data interpolation, owing to its global modeling ability. However, its core operation introduces heavy computational burden due to the quadratic complexity, hindering its further application to higher-dimensional data. To achieve Transformer-based three-dimensional (3D) seismic interpolation, we propose a 2.5-dimensional Transformer network (T-2.5D) that adopts a cross-dimensional transfer learning (TL) strategy, so as to adapt the 2D Transformer encoders to 3D seismic data. The proposed T-2.5D is mainly composed of 2D Transformer encoders and 3D seismic dimension adapters (SDAs). Each 3D SDA is placed before a Transformer encoder to learn spatial correlation information across seismic lines. The proposed cross-dimensional TL strategy comprises two stages: 2D pre-training and 3D fine-tuning. In the first stage, we optimize the 2D Transformer encoders using a large amount of 2D data patches. In the second stage, we freeze the 2D Transformer encoders and fine-tune the 3D SDAs using limited 3D data volumes. Extensive experiments on multiple datasets are conducted to assess the effectiveness and efficiency of T-2.5D. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves comparable performance to that of full 3D Transformer at a significantly low cost.

papers.title: Harmonic Control of Dynamical Freezing in Programmable Rydberg Atom Arrays
papers.abstract: Periodic driving enables the engineering of complex quantum matter, yet in interacting systems it generically leads to energy absorption, which limits the lifetime of the engineered states. To address this challenge, dynamical freezing has been proposed as a mechanism for stabilizing non-equilibrium states over parametrically long timescales. While theory predicts robust freezing under simplifying assumptions, realistic platforms inevitably include additional interaction processes that alter its stability. Here, we report the experimental observation of dynamical freezing in programmable Rydberg atom arrays of up to 100 atoms in one and two dimensions. We find that while single-frequency driving produces pronounced suppression of excitation dynamics, the freezing behavior is restricted to a narrow parameter regime due to interaction-induced heating channels present in realistic simulators. Using a perturbative Floquet analysis of the fully interacting atomic system, we identify the dominant microscopic heating processes responsible for this destabilization. Leveraging this understanding, we design a dual-parameter modulation of detuning and Rabi frequency that coherently suppresses these absorption pathways and substantially broadens the freezing regime, making it also robust across different geometries. Our results reveal how heating processes shape the stability of dynamical freezing in interacting Floquet systems and demonstrates a route to control driven many-body dynamics in realistic experimental platforms.

papers.title: A General Theorem for Non-Simultaneous Hat Guessing Puzzles
