The model's capability to differentiate between FoG episodes and normal movement was used to evaluate its performance, and on the Kaggle Parkinson's Freezing of Gait dataset, the proposed Transformer Encoder-Bi-LSTM fusion model produced 92.6% accuracy, 80.9% F1 score, and 52.06% in terms of mean average precision. The findings highlight how Deep Learning-based approaches may progress the field of FoG identification and help PD patients receive better treatments and management plans.

papers.title: Structure and asymptotic preserving deep neural surrogates for uncertainty quantification in multiscale kinetic equations
Computer-assisted proofs for the fourth algebraic transfer in certain generic degrees
papers.abstract: This paper restructures the author's earlier article in Journal of Homotopy and Related Structures to correct its erroneous invariant-dimension calculations for the fourth Singer algebraic transfer and is written as a replacement for that article. More precisely, we determine the domain and image of the transfer in the degree families $2^{s+t+1}+2^{s+1}-3$ with $t\ne3$ and $2^{s+t}+2^s-2$ with $t\notin\{2,3,4\}$, where $s,t$ are positive integers. Divided-power spikes are basis elements dual to polynomial monomials whose exponents have the form $2^j-1$ for nonnegative integers $j$. Their translates under ${\rm GL}_4(\mathbb F_2)$, the group of invertible $4\times4$ matrices over the field with two elements, generate submodules of the Steenrod kernel, the subspace annihilated by all positive Steenrod squares. We present these submodules as quotients of sums of permutation modules on complete flags, which are chains in $\mathbb F_2^4$ containing one subspace of each dimension $0,1,2,3,4$. Identifying the relation spaces in these presentations gives explicit equivariant comparison isomorphisms. A recursion obtained by separating even and odd exponents in each variable reduces the comparisons to specified identities of finite-dimensional subspaces. These comparisons apply to both complete degree families, including the parameter values omitted from the transfer theorem. Duplication and partial flag embeddings also give theoretical comparisons in specified parameter ranges. As a consequence, Singer's injectivity conjecture holds in rank four in both degree families under the stated parameter restrictions. The cokernel is one-dimensional in homological degree $256$ and zero in every other degree in those ranges.

papers.title: SDP bounds on the stability number via ADMM and intermediate levels of the Lasserre hierarchy
papers.abstract: We consider the Lasserre hierarchy for computing bounds on the stability number of graphs. The semidefinite programs (SDPs) arising from this hierarchy involve large matrix variables and many linear constraints, which makes them difficult to solve using interior-point methods. We propose solving these SDPs using the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM). When the second level of the Lasserre hierarchy for a given graph is intractable for the ADMM, we consider an intermediate-level relaxation of the hierarchy. To warm-start the ADMM, we use an optimal solution from the first level of the Lasserre hierarchy, which is equivalent to the well-known Lovász theta function. Additionally, we use this solution to determine which degree two monomials to add in the Lasserre hierarchy relaxation to obtain an intermediate level between 1 and 2. Computational results demonstrate that our approach yields strong bounds on the stability number, which are computable within reasonable running times. We provide {improved} bounds on the stability number of various graphs from the literature.

papers.title: Large Language Modelsfor Injury Surveillance: Evidence from E-Bike Incidents
On accuracy of density estimation in generative models based on stochastic optimal control
Learned Controllers for Agile Quadrotors in Pursuit-Evasion Games
BitBypass: A New Direction in Jailbreaking Aligned Large Language Models with Bitstream Camouflage
Regular genus of $\mathbb{S}^2 \times \mathbb{S}^1 \times \mathbb{S}^1$, $4$-torus, and small covers over $Δ^2 \times Δ^2$
papers.abstract: A crystallization is an edge-colored graph encoding a contracted triangulation of a closed PL manifold, providing a combinatorial framework for studying PL-manifold invariants. In this framework, we determine the regular genus of several important $4$-manifolds. We first prove that $\mathcal{G}(\mathbb{S}^2\times\mathbb{S}^1\times\mathbb{S}^1)=6$, thereby resolving a conjecture on the regular genus of $\mathbb{S}^2\times\mathbb{S}^1\times\mathbb{S}^1$. We also establish that $\mathcal{G}(\mathbb{S}^1\times\mathbb{S}^1\times\mathbb{S}^1\times\mathbb{S}^1)=16$. These computations lead to further observations on the regular genus of the $n$-torus and motivate the conjecture $\mathcal{G}(\mathbb{T}^n)=1+\frac{(n+1)!(n-3)}{8}$ for $n\geq 5$. We then apply our combinatorial methods to small covers. For the simple polytope $\Delta^2\times\Delta^2$, we classify the corresponding small covers up to Davis-Januszkiewicz equivalence and obtain exactly seven equivalence classes. One of these is $\mathbb{RP}^2\times\mathbb{RP}^2$, while the remaining six are $\mathbb{RP}^2$-bundles over $\mathbb{RP}^2$. We prove that all seven small covers have regular genus $8$. Thus, the paper provides regular genus computations for a collection of $4$-manifolds arising from products and small covers. The approach is purely combinatorial and relies on various combinatorial moves.

papers.title: Single Domain Generalization for Alzheimer's Detection from 3D MRIs with Pseudo-Morphological Augmentations and Contrastive Learning
But what is your honest answer? Aiding LLM-judges with honest alternatives using steering vectors
SPAR: Placement-aware Self-Supervised Representation Learning for Distributed Sensing
Quantum-to-classical transition and the emergence of trajectory level Darwinism with measurements distributed in time: a path integral approach
papers.abstract: We present a path-integral formulation of the emergence of classical dynamics that incorporates continuous measurements. Each Feynman path picks up a random phase due to measurements, and we give conditions under which the dominant contribution comes from the vicinity of the classical paths. This information proliferates across the environment, as in quantum Darwinism, via scattering of probes by the system. The scattering which decoheres a trajectory also heats it. This bounds how redundantly an individual classical trajectory can be recorded before back-action turns it into Brownian motion.

papers.title: Learning-based Autonomous Oversteer Control and Collision Avoidance
Left-Chiral Neutrino Secret Interactions Probed by High-Energy Neutrinos Surviving the Cosmic Neutrino Background
papers.abstract: This work explores the potential of astrophysical neutrinos to probe neutrino secret interactions ($\nu$SI) through their propagation in the Cosmic Neutrino Background (C$\nu$B). Using representative energies and distances for SN 1987A, NGC 1068, TXS 0506+056 and PKS 0735+178, together with distance hypotheses for KM3-230213A, we derive single-event survival benchmarks for the mediator mass and coupling. We focus on scenarios that do not populate right-handed neutrino states in the early Universe and therefore avoid the strongest cosmological constraints: a massive spin-one mediator with a left-chiral coupling to Dirac neutrinos and a scalar mediator coupled to Majorana neutrinos. We also consider scalar exchange with Dirac neutrinos, a common benchmark in propagation studies, and demonstrate that on the standard relic background its resonance is helicity suppressed, with a strength controlled by the relic-neutrino mass. The analysis covers a broad range of mediator masses, including the light-mediator, resonant and heavy-mediator regions, and accounts for the effects of the relic-neutrino masses and of cosmological evolution along the propagation path. We illustrate the main features of each scenario in a common-mass approximation, with analytic expressions for the non-relativistic and ultra-relativistic relic background, and then extend the analysis to realistic non-degenerate neutrino mass spectra. Owing to its energy, the KM3-230213A event shifts the resonant sensitivity to heavier mediators, while distant-source hypotheses increase the propagation sensitivity in this mass range.

papers.title: NeuronGen: Neural Network Parameter Generation via Large Language Models
Benign Overfitting of Two-Layer ReLU Networks in Fixed Dimension through Localized Initialization
Forests for Differences: Beyond Parametric Difference-in-Differences
papers.abstract: This paper introduces the Difference-in-Differences Bayesian Causal Forest (DiD-BCF), a novel non-parametric model addressing key challenges in DiD estimation, such as staggered adoption and heterogeneous treatment effects. DiD-BCF provides a unified framework for estimating Average (ATE), Group-Average (GATE), and Conditional Average Treatment Effects (CATE). By structuring separate regression forests for cohort-specific levels, common untreated trends and treatment effects, the model directly embeds conditional parallel trends and no-anticipation restrictions into Bayesian nonparametrics. We establish non-parametric identification and integrated treatment effect consistency of the exact treatment effect posterior distribution. Extensive simulations demonstrate DiD-BCF's superior performance over established benchmarks, particularly under non-linearity, selection biases, and effect heterogeneity. Applied to U.S. minimum wage policy, the model uncovers significant conditional treatment effect heterogeneity related to county population, insights obscured by traditional methods. DiD-BCF offers a robust and versatile tool for more nuanced causal inference in modern DiD applications.

papers.title: Simple yet Effective Semi-supervised Knowledge Distillation from Vision-Language Models via Dual-Head Optimization
LiteLMGuard: Seamless and Lightweight On-Device Guardrails for Small Language Models against Quantization Vulnerabilities
A Novel Non-Stationary Bias-Correction Framework for Hurricane Risk Assessment under Climate Change
papers.abstract: Conventional hurricane track generation methods typically depend on biased outputs from Global Climate Models (GCMs), which undermines their accuracy in the context of climate change. We present a novel non-stationary bias correction framework, developed for and applied to the North Atlantic basin, that adaptively accounts for evolving biases in GCM outputs. The framework combines dimensionality reduction with data-driven surrogate modeling to learn the nonlinear evolution between historical and projected GCM climate states, allowing the bias correction to evolve with changing climate conditions. The learned relationship is subsequently applied to a reanalysis-based historical baseline to generate bias-corrected environmental fields under future climate scenarios. Using the empirical Weibull plotting approach, we calculate return periods for wind speed and rainfall across selected North American coastal cities. Our results reveal substantial differences in projected hurricane hazards with and without bias correction, highlighting the importance of accounting for evolving GCM biases in climate-risk assessment and resilience planning. This work highlights the necessity of adaptive techniques for accurately assessing future climate impacts, offering a critical advancement in hurricane risk modeling and resilience planning.

papers.title: Easy-plane ferromagnetism in single-crystal ErB$_{2}$ at low temperatures
papers.abstract: We report a study of high-quality single crystals of the hexagonal rare-earth diboride ErB$_{2}$ prepared by means of the self-adjusted flux travelling-solvent floating-zone technique. Comprehensive measurements of the ac susceptibility, magnetization, specific heat, and electrical resistivity consistently establish a paramagnetic state at room temperature which develops strong easy-plane magnetic anisotropy of the hexagonal basal plane below a temperature $T_{\rm x} \approx 50$~K. Below a pronounced second-order phase transition at $T_{c} = 14$~K long-range magnetic order stabilizes. Excellent agreement with both the qualitative phenomenology and the quantitative characteristics of the thermodynamic and transport properties under applied magnetic fields up to 30\,T identifies the magnetic order in ErB$_2$ as a showcase par excellence of pronounced easy-plane ferromagnetism of Er$^{3+}$ local moments, in the presence of crystal electric fields and Van Vleck contributions.

papers.title: Kudla-Rapoport conjecture for unramified maximal parahoric level
papers.abstract: We prove the Kudla--Rapoport conjecture for unramified unitary groups with maximal parahoric level structure. Our approach differs from the local proof of C. Li and W. Zhang. We reduce the conjecture to a global intersection problem using local-global compatibility. Then we apply an inductive procedure based on the modularity of generating series of global special divisors. This strategy follows the framework developed in the proof of the arithmetic fundamental lemma by W. Zhang and Mihatsch--Zhang and arithmetic transfer identities by Z. Zhang and Luo--Mihatsch--Zhang.

papers.title: Estimating Random-Walk Probabilities in Directed Graphs
OpenClassGen: A Large-Scale Corpus of Real-World Python Classes for LLM Research
The Palomar 5 Stellar Stream in DESI Legacy Surveys DR10: Wide-field Morphology and Constraints on the Inner Halo Potential Shape
papers.abstract: The Palomar 5 stellar stream probes the gravitational potential of the inner Milky Way, where the disk, dark halo, and time-dependent perturbations all contribute substantially to the force field. Using the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys Data Release 10 (DR10), we map the wide-field morphology of the stream over $-25^\circ<\phione<20^\circ$ and $-5^\circ<\phitwo<10^\circ$. Our analysis combines a cluster-calibrated PARSEC color--magnitude diagram filter, a continuous main-sequence turnoff plus RR Lyrae distance relation, and a field star response tied to local imaging depth. After applying the response correction, we recover the stream clearly over $-15.5^\circ\le\phione\le7.0^\circ$ and reveal no coherent low-surface-brightness extension beyond this range within our DR10 search footprint. Mock stream fits to the measured centroid and width yield an NFW potential flattening parameter $\qphiz=0.82^{+0.13}_{-0.11}$, assuming a static Hernquist bulge, a Miyamoto--Nagai disk, and a potential-flattened NFW halo with fixed $r_s=20\,{\rm kpc}$ and fixed $V_c(R_0)=232\,\kms$ at the Solar radius. The posterior favors an oblate effective inner halo potential, with a minor dependence on the assumed progenitor mass. The DR10 stream morphology therefore provides a homogeneous observational reference well suited for future joint analyses that incorporate density information, proper motions, line-of-sight velocities, and time-dependent perturbations.

papers.title: Local-Order Auxiliary Losses Can Improve Autoencoder Reconstruction
picoRing mouse: ultra-low-power ring-based wireless tinymouse
Fermat Distance-to-Measure: a robust Fermat-like metric
papers.abstract: Given a probability measure with density, Fermat distances and density-driven metrics are conformal transformations of the Euclidean metric that shrink distances in high density areas and enlarge distances in low density areas. Although they have been widely studied and have shown to be useful in various machine learning tasks, they are limited to measures with density (with respect to Lebesgue measure, or volume form on manifold). In this paper, by replacing the density with the Distance-to-Measure, we introduce a new metric, the Fermat Distance-to-Measure, defined for any probability measure in $\mathbb{R}^d$. We derive strong stability properties for the Fermat Distance-to-Measure with respect to the measure and propose an estimator from random sampling of the same measure, featuring an explicit bound on its convergence rate.

papers.title: Asymmetric graph alignment and the phase transition for asymmetric tree correlation testing
Breaking the Silence: A Dataset and Benchmark for Bangla Text-to-Gloss Translation
Multiparameter extensions of the Christ-Kiselev maximal theorem: strong variational bounds
papers.abstract: For a linear operator $T$ bounded from $L^p(Y)$ to $L^q(X)$, the Christ--Kiselev theorem gives $L^p \to L^q$ bounds for the maximal function $T^{*}$ associated to a filtration on $Y$. This result has been extended to the multiparameter setting, establishing bounds for the maximal function associated to a product of filtrations. In this note, we strengthen these results by proving $\rho$-variational bounds for the multiparameter truncations when $\rho>p$. Furthermore, we give a multilinear extension of the Christ--Kiselev theorem, establishing strong variational bounds for the multiparameter truncations for a general multilinear operator.

papers.title: Gravitational lensing due to charged galactic wormhole
papers.abstract: We propose the back reaction to the charged galactic wormhole spacetime based on Yoshiaki Sofue's exponential dark matter density profile to find exact solutions. The charges act as an additional component to the static wormhole, which is primarily formed by the galactic dark matter density. Unlike traditional mass-based models, this solution incorporates charge effects within a realistic dark matter distribution, revealing unique interactions between dark matter, electromagnetic fields, and spacetime curvature. This study confirms the criteria for wormhole formation, designating it the "Charged Galactic Wormhole," and offers a new framework for investigating galactic structures, with potential observational signatures that deepen our understanding of dark matter and spacetime. Later, the proper radial distance and the embedding surface were also analyzed. Furthermore, the deflection of light around a charged galactic wormhole was investigated, along with a comprehensive review of the resulting image. The deflection of massive objects (charge less) near charged galactic wormholes is studied using the Gauss-Bonnet and Rindler-Ishak methods, with a detailed comparison of the results from both approaches. Additionally, in both the Rindler-Ishak (RI) and Gauss-Bonnet (GB) methods, when v tends to 1 i.e. when particle's velocity comparable to the speed of light , the results from these approaches converge, producing the same outcome as strong gravitational lensing.

papers.title: Near-Optimal Techniques for Distributed Entanglement Generation and Purification
papers.abstract: We develop a purification-aware optimization framework for distributing high-fidelity entangled states over quantum networks. In repeater-based architectures, the framework jointly selects entanglement swapping, fusion or graph-state growth, and purification operations to maximize generation rate under a fidelity threshold. Different purification models can be incorporated through their fidelity-update, success-probability, and latency rules. We introduce purification-augmented generation trees and dynamic programming (DP) algorithms for entangled-pair (EP) distribution. Hypergraph-flow linear programming (LP) formulations support level-based structures and concurrent generation across multiple trees and demands. We extend the framework to GHZ states and arbitrary graph states constructed from remote EP resources, introduce graph-state construction primitives, and derive closed-form fidelity-vector updates for GHZ fusion and purification and graph-state growth and purification. We provide optimal formulations under the adopted models, discretization, and purification bounds, together with efficient DP and LP heuristics. We bound fidelity- and rate-discretization errors and establish convergence for fixed constructions under stated regularity conditions. NetSquid simulations of EP generation using our LP approach show an average 160% increase in generation rate over the compared prior approaches, with gains up to 330% in some scenarios. GHZ and graph-state simulations demonstrate the heuristics' effectiveness in balancing generation rate, output fidelity, and computational overhead.

papers.title: Modeling and Analysis of an Optimal Insulation Problem on Non-Smooth Domains
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study an insulation problem that seeks the optimal distribution of a fixed amount $m>0$ of insulating material coating an insulated boundary $\Gamma_I\subseteq \partial\Omega$ of a thermally conducting body $\Omega\subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$, $d\in \mathbb{N}$. The thickness of the thin insulating layer $\Sigma_{I}^{\varepsilon}$ is given locally via $\varepsilon \mathtt{d}$, where $\mathtt{d}\colon \Gamma_{I}\to [0,+\infty)$ specifies the (to be determined) distribution of the insulating material. We establish $\Gamma(L^2(\mathbb{R}^d))$-convergence of the problem (as $\varepsilon\to 0^+$). Different from the existing literature, which predominantly assumes that the thermally conducting body $\Omega$ has a $C^{1,1}$-boundary, we merely assume that $\Gamma_I$ is piece-wise flat. To overcome this lack of boundary regularity, we define the thin insulating boundary layer $\Sigma_{I}^{\varepsilon}$ using a Lipschitz continuous transversal vector field rather than the outward unit normal vector field. The piece-wise flatness condition on $\Gamma_I$ is only needed to prove the $\liminf$-estimate. In fact, for the $\limsup$-estimate is enough that the thermally conducting body $\Omega$ has a $C^{0,1}$-boundary.

papers.title: Triangle-free graphs with the fewest independent sets
papers.abstract: Given $d>0$ and a positive integer $n$, let $G$ be a triangle-free graph on $n$ vertices with average degree $d$. With an elegant induction, Shearer (1983) tightened a seminal result of Ajtai, Komlós and Szemerédi (1980/1981) by proving that $G$ contains an independent set of size at least $(1+o(1))\frac{\log d}{d}n$ as $d\to\infty$. By a generalisation of Shearer's method, we prove that the number of independent sets in $G$ must be at least $\exp\left((1+o(1))\frac{(\log d)^2}{2d}n\right)$ as $d\to\infty$. This improves upon results of Cooper and Mubayi (2014) and Davies, Jenssen, Perkins, and Roberts (2018). Our method also provides good lower bounds on the independence polynomial of $G$, one of which implies Shearer's result itself. As certified by a classic probabilistic construction, our bound on the number of independent sets is sharp to several leading terms as $d\to\infty$.

papers.title: Coherent manifolds and quantization
papers.abstract: We study the differential geometry of coherent manifolds modelled on convenient vector spaces and apply it to coherent quantization. A smooth coherent product determines geometric structures on the label manifold. We construct a common invariant domain for the quantizations of coherent vector fields and of coherent diffeomorphisms with smooth diffeomorphic adjoints. These quantizations are distinguished operators on the associated quantum space and satisfy commutator, covariance, and formal adjoint relations. Their coherent matrix elements can be calculated by differentiation and substitution in the coherent product. Extending the operators to the common invariant domain leaves their Hilbert space closures unchanged. Motions in subgroups of diffeomorphisms give rise to Lie algebras of generators without requiring a Lie group structure on the subgroup. Suitable coherent motions recover the infinitesimal quantization by differentiation. We express quantum dynamics through coherent matrix elements and obtain a coherent action principle by restricting the quantum action to coherent states. For Klauder spaces, the construction gives creation and annihilation operators, the canonical commutation relations, Segal fields, Weyl operators, and normal ordering on the common invariant domain.

papers.title: ResBench: Benchmarking LLM-Generated FPGA Designs with Resource Awareness
Higgs production from anomalous gluon dynamics
papers.abstract: We present a two-loop analysis of the contributions to Higgs production via gluon-gluon fusion arising from the triple-gluon operator in the Standard Model effective field theory (SMEFT). Our discussion covers all aspects of renormalization group (RG) improved perturbation theory, including matching and running within the SMEFT. This study can therefore be seen as a blueprint of the intricacies and subtleties that arise in RG improved SMEFT calculations for collider processes beyond the leading order.

papers.title: Time-Varying Causal Survival Learning under Staggered Adoption
papers.abstract: Staggered adoptions are settings where study objects convert from control to treatment at different times. Often the outcome is a time to an event, such as survival after an organ transplant or the time until an employee becomes a regular user of a new AI tool. Although many papers have studied staggered adoptions on repeatedly measured outcomes, little work has addressed survival outcomes, which are observed at most once and may be censored. We give causal assumptions under which a time-dependent survival model identifies a heterogeneous treatment effect, which tells who benefits most. Because a direct Cox learner is biased when baseline risk is learned flexibly, we introduce a time-varying, event-risk propensity score. Constructing this propensity score is nontrivial because both treatment and outcome are times to events, so it must track which individuals have not yet experienced the event and the treatment status of each at the time. Unlike existing propensity scores, centering by this propensity score makes the Cox partial-likelihood equation Neyman orthogonal. We establish the double machine learning property and the corresponding convergence rate, and an influence-function-based variance estimator. Simulations show that orthogonalization reduces error and supports near-nominal inference when the baseline risk is complex and the samples are large, whereas direct Cox estimation is more precise when baseline risk is linear. We illustrate the framework using lawyer-level Copilot adoption data and the Stanford Heart Transplant study.

papers.title: $C^0$-Contact Anosov flows
papers.abstract: We prove that smooth reparametrizations of the geodesic flow on a manifold of constant negative curvature are contact Anosov flows. In particular we give a new class of exponentially mixing Anosov flows. Moreover, this introduces the notion of $C^0$-contact and we prove that the classical Gray stability theorem that is known in the smooth case fails in this setting.

papers.title: Cardinalities of Ultraproducts of Finite Sets in ZF + DC
papers.abstract: Relative to an inaccessible cardinal, it is consistent with ZF + DC that there exists an ultrafilter $U$ on $\omega$ such that two infinite ultraproducts of finite sets, $\prod A_n / U$ and $\prod B_n / U$, have the same cardinality if and only if $0 < \lim_U |A_n|/|B_n| < \infty$. In particular, this holds in $W[U]$, where $W$ is the Solovay Model and $U$ is $[\omega]^\omega$-generic.

papers.title: The Sharpness Disparity Principle in Transformers for Accelerating Language Model Pre-Training
papers.abstract: Transformers consist of diverse building blocks, such as embedding layers, normalization layers, self-attention mechanisms, and point-wise feedforward networks. Thus, understanding the differences and interactions among these blocks is important. In this paper, we uncover a clear Sharpness Disparity across these blocks, which emerges early in training and intriguingly persists throughout the training process. Motivated by this finding, we propose Blockwise Learning Rate (LR), a strategy that tailors the LR to each block's sharpness, accelerating large language model (LLM) pre-training. By integrating Blockwise LR into AdamW, we consistently achieve lower terminal loss and nearly $2\times$ speedup compared to vanilla AdamW. We demonstrate this acceleration across GPT-2 and LLaMA, with model sizes ranging from 0.12B to 2B and datasets of OpenWebText, MiniPile, and C4. Finally, we incorporate Blockwise LR into Adam-mini (Zhang et al., 2024), a recently proposed memory-efficient variant of Adam, achieving a combined $2\times$ speedup and $2\times$ memory saving. These results underscore the potential of exploiting the sharpness disparity to improve LLM training.

papers.title: Rectifying Conformity Scores for Better Conditional Coverage
papers.abstract: We present a new method for generating confidence sets within the split conformal prediction framework. Our method performs a trainable transformation of any given conformity score to improve conditional coverage while ensuring exact marginal coverage. The transformation is based on an estimate of the conditional quantile of conformity scores. The resulting method is particularly beneficial for constructing adaptive confidence sets in multi-output problems where standard conformal quantile regression approaches have limited applicability. We develop a theoretical bound that captures the influence of the accuracy of the quantile estimate on the approximate conditional validity, unlike classical bounds for conformal prediction methods that only offer marginal coverage. We experimentally show that our method is highly adaptive to the local data structure and outperforms existing methods in terms of conditional coverage, improving the reliability of statistical inference in various applications.

papers.title: Black Hole Chemistry Knows Extra Dimensions
papers.abstract: We study black hole chemistry in the eight-dimensional Einstein-Yang-Mills-Maxwell theory, where the stabilized size of the compact internal space dynamically determines the four-dimensional thermodynamic pressure. Analyzing AdS black holes, we show that larger extra dimensions lower phase-transition temperatures and broaden the range of thermodynamically excluded black hole sizes. Additionally, we investigate a geometric representation of the thermodynamic volume by defining a volume-constrained minimal surface using a lapse-weighted volume functional. This codimension-two surface minimizes its area under the constraint that its enclosed volume exactly matches the thermodynamic volume. This surface prescription naturally reproduces the event horizon for dyonic and Schwarzschild-AdS black holes. We also apply this to the Kerr--AdS black hole and find an off-horizon surface numerically and analytically for finite and small angular momenta. In addition, we interpret the thermodynamic volume in terms of an effective number of disentanglers in a MERA system.

papers.title: Light Edge Fault Tolerant Graph Spanners
The infinitesimal subgroup of interpretable groups in some dp-minimal valued fields
papers.abstract:
We continue our local analysis of groups interpretable in various dp-minimal valued fields, as introduced in [8]. We associate with every infinite group $G$ interpretable in those fields an infinite type-definable infinitesimal subgroup $
u(G)$, generated by the four infinitesimal subgroups $
u_D(G)$ associated with the distinguished sorts $K$, $	extbf{k}$, $\Gamma$ and $K/\mathcal{O}$. To show that $

papers.title: $T_{cc}$ and Hidden Charm Tetraquarks $1^+$ and $0^+$in QCD sum rules and Heavy-Quark Spin Symmetry
papers.abstract: In this work, $T_{cc}$ double charm tetraquark and $1^{+}$ and $0^{+}$ hidden charm tetraquarks are studied within the QCD sum rules framework. In the heavy-quark limit, the $1^+$ and $0^+$ tetraquarks are degenerate and the difference in their masses is an $1/m_c$ effect. It is shown that, although the uncertainty in the mass predictions of each of these hadrons is ${\cal O}(100\;\mathrm{MeV})$, when the mass differences are studied, the uncertainty is reduced to less than ${\cal O}(10\;\mathrm{MeV})$. Hence, it is concluded that if one of the exotic hadrons is observed and its mass is used as input, the masses of the other hadrons can be determined with a precision of ${\cal O}(10\;\mathrm{MeV})$ using the QCD sum rules method.

papers.title: Training-free Task-oriented Grasp Generation
Anomaly Detection via Autoencoder Composite Features and NCE
The Revenue Cost of Inference in Online Assortment Optimization
papers.abstract: A seller running an assortment experiment must earn revenue while collecting data to compare future offers. For a regular finite-dimensional parametric choice model and a finite assortment family, we characterize the oracle frontier between expected revenue loss and the largest local first-order variance constant across prespecified revenue comparisons. The oracle benchmark remains finite at zero cost exactly when revenue-maximizing assortments provide information in every target-gradient direction. When costly offers can supply the missing information, we derive the exact leading coefficient of the inverse-budget variance law and the limiting optimal spending shares. A pilot-based procedure reserves reference offers to preserve information and tightens the estimated budget constraint to account for uncertainty. We give conditions for the implemented design's variance criterion to converge to the stabilized oracle value at a fixed budget and reference share. Simulations with synthetic instances and Expedia-calibrated markets show that allocating offers across the full assortment family can improve the precision of revenue comparisons under a common opportunity-cost budget. Additional experiments assess pilot spending, budget protection, and sensitivity to choice-model misspecification.

papers.title: 3D-MoE: Towards Spatial Intelligence with Mixture-of-Experts for 3D Reasoning and Action Generation
Rational values of the weak saturation limit
papers.abstract: Given a graph $F$, a graph $G$ is weakly $F$-saturated if all non-edges of $G$ can be added in some order so that each new edge introduces a copy of $F$. The weak saturation number $\operatorname{wsat}(n, F)$ is the minimum number of edges in a weakly $F$-saturated graph on $n$ vertices. Bollobás initiated the study of weak saturation in 1968 to study percolation processes, which originated in biology and have applications in physics and computer science. It was shown by Alon that for each $F$, there is a constant $w_F$ such that $\operatorname{wsat}(n, F) = w_Fn + o(n)$. We characterize all possible rational values of $w_F$, proving in particular that $w_F$ can equal any rational number at least $\frac 32$.

papers.title: TTC Domains
papers.abstract: The Top Trading Cycles (TTC) rule is fundamental to object reallocation: it is the only rule that is individually rational, pair efficient, and strategyproof on the unrestricted domain. Despite its desirable properties, at some profiles, TTC precludes longer trading cycles that could lead to more appealing allocations. We explore restricted preference domains as an avenue for finding alternative rules satisfying the three axioms. Our main contribution is to introduce a richness condition on domains, the top-two condition, and show that it characterizes TTC domains: domains to which the above characterization of TTC extends. The condition requires that, within every subset of objects, any two objects that can each be ranked first can also be ranked as the top two, in both possible orders. For every domain that fails the top-two condition, we construct a rule distinct from TTC that is individually rational, Pareto efficient, and strategyproof, and that executes longer trading cycles that TTC precludes.

papers.title: Hallucination Mitigation using Agentic AI Natural Language-Based Frameworks
Compactly supported $p$-adic pro-étale cohomology of analytic varieties
papers.abstract: We study properties of compactly supported $p$-adic pro-étale cohomology of smooth partially proper rigid analytic varieties. In particular, we prove a comparison theorem, in a stable range, with compactly supported syntomic cohomology, which is built from compactly supported Hyodo-Kato and ${\mathcal B}^+_{\rm dr}$-cohomologies. We derive from that a (limited version of a) fundamental diagram.

papers.title: On a Problem of Kac concerning Anisotropic Lacunary Sums
papers.abstract: Given a sequence of integers $(n_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$ satisfying $\liminf_{k \rightarrow \infty}\frac{n_{k+1}}{n_k} \ge q > 1$, a scheme of real-valued weights $(c_{k,N})_{k \leq N}$, and a function $f: \mathbb{T} = \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{R}$, it is a classical problem to determine whether \[ S_N(x):=\frac{\sum_{k=1}^N c_{k,N} f(n_k x)}{ \sqrt{\sum_{k=1}^N c_{k,N}^2}} \] converges to a normal distribution as $N \rightarrow \infty$. This question can be traced back to early works of Kac and Erdős and has since then been investigated. It is well known that the asymptotic behavior of $S_N$ is determined not only by the analytic properties of $f$, but also by the arithmetic properties of the sequence $(n_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$ and by the subtle interaction between the two. In this article, we identify conditions on $(n_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$, $f$ and $(c_{k,N})_{k \leq N}$ that can be regarded as minimal for a central limit theorem to hold for $S_N$. This addresses a question raised by Mark Kac [Ann. of Math., 1946].

papers.title: A unified framework for net effects in signed social and ecological networks
papers.abstract: With improvements in data resolution and quality, researchers can now represent complex systems as signed, weighted, and directed networks. In this article, we introduce a framework for measuring net and indirect effects without simplifying these information-rich networks. It captures both direct and indirect interactions, the effect of the whole network on a node, and conversely, the effect of a node on the entire network, while accommodating the complexity of signed, weighted, and directed links. Our taxonomy unifies and extends existing approaches and measures from network science, computational social science, and ecological networks. We demonstrate its value in ecological systems, where net and indirect effects are critical yet difficult to quantify. Using generalized Lotka-Volterra dynamics, we find a strong correlation between negative net effects and species extinction. We further apply the framework to a real-world social network, where it identifies informative rankings that illuminate influence propagation and power dynamics.

papers.title: $P$-trivial MMP, Zariski decompositions and minimal models for generalised pairs
papers.abstract: We develop an inductive method for generalised pairs (g-pairs) without the NQC assumption. It is based on $P$-trivial MMPs, whose steps are trivial with respect to a given nef divisor $P$. For klt g-pairs, if $P$ is numerically equivalent to an effective divisor, we perturb the boundary so that any MMP on $K_X+B+M+\alpha P$ is $P$-trivial for $\alpha\gg0$. For lc g-pairs, the components with coefficient one cannot be perturbed, so we use induction on lc centres. If $K_X+B+M-P$ is a $\mathbb{Q}$-divisor, then local Cartier indices control the coefficients under divisorial adjunction, and we prove a special termination. This includes the case $P=0$, where $K_X+B+M$ is a $\mathbb{Q}$-divisor. As applications, we prove that a projective lc g-pair $(X,B+M)$ of dimension $3$ has a minimal model if $K_X+B+M$ birationally has a Nakayama-Zariski decomposition with nef positive part and either $K_X+B+M\equiv D\geq0$ or $M\equiv D\geq0$. We also prove this for klt g-pairs in arbitrary dimension. In dimension $4$, the last condition can be replaced by the log abundance of the nef data. For usual pairs, this is a theorem of Birkar and the author.

papers.title: Categorical Diffusion of Weighted Lattices
papers.abstract: Quantales are well known in logic and computer science, and categories enriched in them unify ordered, metric, relational, and tropical structures. Problems in dynamic programming, synchronization, and discrete event systems require reconciling local data, represented by objects in a quantale-enriched category, across the edges of a network, represented by an undirected graph. Concurrently, replacing inner products with hom-objects and linear adjoints with adjoint functors initiates a categorification of graph and sheaf Laplacians, with a view toward enrichment in larger monoidal categories and bicategories. To this end, we lay the foundations for an enriched harmonic analysis on graphs through cellular sheaves of quantale-enriched categories and a Laplace operator that we call the Lawvere Laplacian. Over an arbitrary unital quantale, the weighted global sections of such a sheaf are the vertex data that agree across every edge up to the tolerances of a weight function. They form the quantale-enriched category of natural transformations from a weight diagram into the sheaf, which is a weighted limit when the quantale is commutative. When the restriction maps have right adjoints, we prove that the weighted global sections are the suffix points of the Lawvere Laplacian, which are the equilibria of its harmonic flow. Under a continuity hypothesis, the harmonic flow converges to the greatest weighted global section below its initial cochain, and for central weight functions the weighted global sections form a complete coreflective subcategory of the cochains. Instances of the theory include the Bellman--Ford iteration over the Lawvere quantale, the reconciliation of local cost estimates, quantale and clock synchronization, and coupled max-plus discrete event systems.

papers.title: On statistical and causal models associated with acyclic directed mixed graphs
papers.abstract: Causal models in statistics are often described using acyclic directed mixed graphs (ADMGs), which contain directed and bidirected edges and no directed cycles. This article surveys various interpretations of ADMGs, discusses their relations in different sub-classes of ADMGs, and argues that one of them---the noise expansion (NE) model---should be used as the default interpretation. Our endorsement of the NE model is based on two observations. First, in a subclass of ADMGs called exogenously bidirected graphs (which retain most of the good properties of directed acyclic graphs and bidirected graphs), the NE model is equivalent to many other interpretations, including the ordinary Markov and nested Markov models. Second, the NE model for an arbitrary ADMG is exactly the union of the observed margins of NE models on its exogenously bidirected expansions. This property is referred to as completeness, as it shows that the model does not commit to any specific latent variable explanation. In proving the nested Markov property, we also develop an ADMG-based theory for causality and its complete characterization via the potential outcome calculus. Finally, we compare the NE model with the closely related but different interpretation of ADMGs as directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) with latent variables that is commonly used in the literature. We argue that the ``latent DAG'' interpretation is mathematically unnecessary, makes obscure ontological assumptions, and discourages practitioners from deliberating over important structural assumptions.

papers.title: Mean--Variance Portfolio Selection by Continuous-Time Reinforcement Learning: Algorithms, Regret Analysis, and Empirical Study
papers.abstract: We study continuous-time mean--variance portfolio selection in markets where stock prices are diffusion processes driven by observable factors that are also diffusion processes, yet the coefficients of these processes are unknown. Based on the recently developed reinforcement learning (RL) theory for diffusion processes, we present a general data-driven RL approach that learns the pre-committed investment strategy directly without attempting to learn or estimate the market coefficients. For multi-stock Black--Scholes markets without factors, we further devise an algorithm and prove its performance guarantee by deriving a sublinear regret bound in terms of the Sharpe ratio. We then carry out an extensive empirical study implementing this algorithm to compare its performance and trading characteristics, evaluated under a host of common metrics, with a large number of widely employed portfolio allocation strategies on S\&P 500 constituents. The results demonstrate that the proposed continuous-time RL strategy is consistently among the best, especially in a volatile bear market, and decisively outperforms the model-based continuous-time counterparts by significant margins.

papers.title: Projected gradient methods for nonconvex and stochastic smooth optimization: new complexities and auto-conditioned stepsizes
papers.abstract: We present a novel class of projected gradient (PG) methods for minimizing a smooth but not necessarily convex function over a convex compact set. We first provide a novel analysis of the constant-stepsize PG method, achieving a unified iteration complexity for finding an approximate stationary point for convex and nonconvex problems. We then develop an "auto-conditioned" projected gradient (AC-PG) variant that achieves the same iteration complexity without requiring the input of the Lipschitz constant of the gradient or any line search procedure. The key idea is to estimate the Lipschitz constant using first-order information gathered from the previous iterations, and to show that the error caused by underestimating the Lipschitz constant can be properly controlled. We then generalize the PG methods to the stochastic setting, by proposing a stochastic projected gradient (SPG) method and a variance-reduced stochastic gradient (VR-SPG) method, achieving new unified complexity bounds in different oracle settings. We also present auto-conditioned stepsize policies for both stochastic PG methods and establish comparable convergence guarantees.

papers.title: The large $|U|$ expansion for a half-filled asymmetric Hubbard model on a triangular ladder in the presence of spin-dependent magnetic flux
papers.abstract: We consider a half-filled system of spin-1/2 fermions on a triangular ladder with spin-dependent hopping in the presence of spin-dependent flux. Using the Schrieffer-Wolff transformation, we derive an effective spin Hamiltonian describing the infrared properties of the system in the limit of strong on-site repulsion. The expansion is performed up to the third order in the hopping amplitude over on-site interaction energy. It is shown that the low-energy spin excitations are described by an anisotropic $XXZ$ Heisenberg model with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction and an unconventional three-spin (correlated exchange) term in the presence of an extended magnetic field. The latter couples not only to $z$-projection of the total spin on a triangular plaquette but also to the product of $z$-components of three spins located on vertices of the triangle. In the case of strong attractive interaction, the corresponding effective model is derived from the repulsive one using the one-spin-component particle-hole transformation. The effective Hamiltonian is given by the same $XXZ$ Heisenberg model, as in the repulsive case, but in terms of pseudospin (charge) operators.

papers.title: ExclaveFL: Verifiable Claims for Federated Learning using Exclaves
Transfer Learning for High-dimensional Quantile Regression with Distribution Shift
papers.abstract: Information from related source studies can often enhance the findings of a target study. However, the distribution shift between target and source studies can severely impact the efficiency of knowledge transfer. In the high-dimensional regression setting, existing transfer approaches mainly focus on the parameter shift. In this paper, we focus on the high-dimensional quantile regression with knowledge transfer under three types of distribution shift: parameter shift, covariate shift, and residual shift. We propose a novel transferable set and a new transfer framework to address the above three discrepancies. Non-asymptotic estimation error bounds and source detection consistency are established to validate the availability and superiority of our method in the presence of distribution shift. Additionally, an orthogonal debiased approach is proposed for statistical inference with knowledge transfer, leading to sharper asymptotic results. Extensive simulation results as well as real data applications further demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed procedure.

papers.title: Log-concavity of polynomials arising from equivariant cohomology
papers.abstract: We study the equivariant cohomology classes of torus-equivariant subvarieties of the space of matrices. For a large class of torus actions, we prove that the polynomials representing these classes (up to suitably changing signs) are covolume polynomials in the sense of Aluffi. We study the cohomology rings of complex varieties in terms of Macaulay inverse systems over $\mathbb{Z}$. As applications, we show that under certain conditions, the Macaulay dual generator is a denormalized Lorentzian polynomial in the sense of Brändén and Huh, and we give a characteristic-free extension (over $\mathbb{Z}$) of the result of Khovanskii and Pukhlikov describing the cohomology ring of toric varieties in terms of volume polynomials.

papers.title: Development of a Low-Cost Prosthetic Hand Using Electromyography and Machine Learning
Safe Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Convergence to Generalized Nash Equilibrium
Neural Graph Simulator for Complex Systems
$δ$-Poisson and transposed $δ$-Poisson algebras
papers.abstract: We study two new classes of Poisson-type algebras, namely, $\delta$-Poisson and transposed $\delta$-Poisson algebras. We show that these algebras are related to many interesting identities; in particular, they are related to shift associative algebras, $F$-manifold algebras, algebras of Jordan brackets, etc. We classify simple $\delta$-Poisson and transposed $\delta$-Poisson algebras and find their depolarizations. We study the Koszulity and self-duality of the $\delta$-Poisson and mixed-Poisson operads. Bases of the free $\delta$-Poisson and mixed-Poisson algebras generated by a countable set $X$ are constructed.

papers.title: Towards Identification of Political Posts in Social Media Text Using Deep Learning Models
On the optimality of the HOD dichotomy
papers.abstract: In the first part of the manuscript, we establish several consistency results concerning Woodin's HOD hypothesis and large cardinals around the level of extendibility. First, we prove that the first extendible cardinal can be the first strongly compact in HOD. Second, answering a question in \cite{CFH}, we prove that the first supercompact cardinal can be the first strongly compact, non supercompact, of HOD. We extend a former result of Woodin by showing that under the HOD hypothesis the first extendible cardinal is $C^{(1)}$-supercompact in HOD. We also show that the first cardinal-correct extendible may not be extendible, thus answering a question by Gitman and Osinski \cite[\S9]{GitOsi}. In the second part of the manuscript, we discuss the extent to which weak covering can fail below the first supercompact cardinal $\delta$ in a context where the HOD hypothesis holds. Answering a question of Cummings et al. \cite{CumFriGol}, we show that under the $\mathrm{HOD}$ hypothesis there are many singulars $\kappa<\delta$ where $\mathrm{cf}^{\mathrm{HOD}}(\kappa)=\mathrm{cf}(\kappa)$ and $\kappa^{+\mathrm{HOD}}=\kappa^{+}.$ In contrast, we also show that the $\mathrm{HOD}$ hypothesis is consistent with $\delta$ carrying a club of $\mathrm{HOD}$-regulars cardinals $\kappa$ such that $\kappa^{+\mathrm{HOD}}<\kappa^{+}$. Finally, we close the manuscript with a discussion about the $\mathrm{HOD}$ hypothesis and $\omega$-strong measurability.

papers.title: Multilingual Hallucination Gaps in Large Language Models
Formalizing Hyperspaces and Operations on Subsets of Polish Spaces over Abstract Exact Real Numbers
Markov-Nash equilibria in mean-field games under model uncertainty
papers.abstract: We propose and analyze a framework for mean-field Markov games under model uncertainty. In this framework, a state-measure flow describing the collective behavior of a population affects the given reward function as well as the unknown transition kernel of the representative agent. The agent's objective is to choose an optimal Markov policy in order to maximize her worst-case expected reward, where worst-case refers to the most adverse scenario among all transition kernels considered to be feasible to describe the unknown true law of the environment. We prove the existence of a mean-field equilibrium under model uncertainty, where the agent chooses the optimal policy that maximizes the worst-case expected reward, and the state-measure flow aligns with the agent's state distribution under the optimal policy and the worst-case transition kernel. Moreover, we prove that for suitable multi-agent Markov games under model uncertainty the optimal policy from the mean-field equilibrium forms an approximate Markov-Nash equilibrium whenever the number of agents is large enough.

papers.title: A Projective Twist on the Hasse Norm Theorem
papers.abstract: A finite extension of global fields $L/K$ satisfies the Hasse norm principle if any nonzero element of $K$ has the property that it is a norm locally if and only if it is a norm globally. In 1931, Hasse proved that any cyclic extension satisfies the Hasse norm principle, providing a novel approach to extending the local-global principle to equations with degree greater than $2$. In this paper, we introduce the projective Hasse norm principle, generalizing the Hasse norm principle to multiple fields and asking whether a line through the origin that contains a simultaneous norm locally in every field must also contain a norm globally in every field. We show that the projective Hasse norm principle is independent of the conjunction of Hasse norm principles in all of the constituent fields in the general case, and that the projective principle holds whenever the fields are all Galois and jointly linearly disjoint, without assuming their individual Hasse norm principles. We also give a criterion in terms of their Galois groups and prove that the implication holds whenever the Galois group of their compositum has fourth-power-free order. A counterexample of Demarche and Wei shows that this bound is sharp. We also prove an analogue of the Hasse norm theorem for the projective Hasse norm principle, namely that the projective Hasse norm principle holds for every finite family of cyclic extensions.

papers.title: quanda: An Interpretability Toolkit for Training Data Attribution Evaluation
Classification of real nodal orders
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study properties of nodal orders defined over arbitrary base fields. In particular we give a classification of complete real nodal orders.

papers.title: Identification and estimation for matrix time series CP-factor models
papers.abstract: We propose a new method for identifying and estimating the CP-factor models for matrix time series. Unlike the generalized eigenanalysis-based method of Chang et al. (2023) for which the convergence rates of the associated estimators may suffer from small eigengaps as the asymptotic theory is based on some matrix perturbation analysis, the proposed new method enjoys faster convergence rates which are free from any eigengaps. It achieves this by turning the problem into a joint diagonalization of several matrices whose elements are determined by a basis of a linear system, and by choosing the basis carefully to avoid near co-linearity (see Proposition 5 and Section 4.3). Furthermore, unlike the generalized eigenanalysis-based method which requires the two factor loading matrices to be full-ranked, the proposed new method can handle rank-deficient factor loading matrices. Illustration with both simulated and real matrix time series data shows the advantages of the proposed new method.

papers.title: Linear-time Rule Mining Under Formal Guarantees
On Sparsity and Sub-Gaussianity in the Johnson-Lindenstrauss Lemma
papers.abstract: The Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma is the theoretical core of the dimensionality reduction methods based on random projections. While a standard probabilistic proof uses matrices with Gaussian entries, the computational cost of random projections can be drastically reduced by the use of simpler variables, especially if they vanish with a high probability. In this paper, we propose an elementary analysis of random projections under classical assumptions that emphasizes the key role of sub-Gaussianity: any 1-sub-Gaussian distribution with variance 1 yields the same sufficient target dimension as the Gaussian distribution. We then extend the analysis to sparse projections, with data-dependent sparsity conditions on the pairwise differences of the points, and we quantify the cost of sparsity on the target dimension. A complementary lower bound shows the limits induced by the sparsity of the data itself.

papers.title: ARMAr-LASSO: Mitigating the Impact of Predictor Serial Correlation on the LASSO
authors: Alessandro Giovannelli (3) ((1) L'EMbeDS and Institute of Economics
papers.abstract: We explore estimation and prediction accuracy for sparse linear models, focusing on scenarios where both predictors and errors carry serial correlations. We establish a clear link between predictor serial correlation and the performance of the LASSO, showing that even orthogonal or weakly correlated stationary AR processes can lead to significant spurious correlations due to their serial correlations. To address this challenge, we propose a novel approach named ARMAr-LASSO (ARMA residuals LASSO), which applies the LASSO to predictors that have been pre-whitened with ARMA filters and lags of dependent variable. We establish oracle inequalities for the feasible estimator and assess its estimation, selection, and forecasting performance empirically. Our findings are supported by extensive simulations and an application to real-world macroeconomic data, which highlight the superior performance of the ARMAr-LASSO for handling sparse linear models in the context of time series.

papers.title: Shift associative algebras
papers.abstract: We present a comprehensive study of algebras satisfying the identity $(xy)z=y(zx),$ named as shift associative algebras. Our research shows that these algebras are related to many interesting identities. In particular, they are related to anti-Poisson-Jordan algebras and algebras of associative type $\sigma$. We study algebras of associative type $\sigma$ to be Koszul and self-dual. A basis of the free shift associative algebra generated by a countable set $X$ was constructed. An analog of Wedderburn-Artin's theorem was established. The algebraic and geometric classifications of complex $4$-dimensional shift associative algebras are given. In particular, we proved that the first non-associative shift associative algebra appears only in dimension $5$.

papers.title: Asymptotics of a Gauss hypergeometric function related to moments of symmetric square L-functions I
papers.abstract: We prove an asymptotic formula for a special case of the Gauss hypergeometric function, which arises in the explicit formula for the second moment of Maass form symmetric-square $L$-functions.

papers.title: Two-Step QAOA: Enhancing Quantum Optimization by Decomposing K-hot Constraints in QUBO Formulations
papers.abstract: The Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) has shown promise in solving combinatorial optimization problems by leveraging quantum computational power. We propose a simple approach, the Two-Step QAOA, which aims to improve the effectiveness of QAOA by decomposing problems with k-hot encoding QUBO (Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization) formulations. By identifying and separating the problem into two stages, we transform soft constraints into hard constraints, simplifying the generation of initial conditions and enabling more efficient optimization. The method is particularly beneficial for tackling complex societal problems that often involve intricate constraint structures.

papers.title: Homotopy $n$-types of cubical sets and graphs
papers.abstract: We give a new construction of the model structure on the category of simplicial sets for homotopy $n$-types, originally due to Elvira-Donazar and Hernandez-Paricio, using a right transfer along the coskeleton functor. We observe that an analogous model structure can be constructed on the category of cubical sets, and use it to equip the category of (simple) graphs with a fibration category structure whose weak equivalences are discrete $n$-equivalences.

papers.title: Approximate Distributed Monitoring under Partial Synchrony: Balancing Speed and Accuracy
Orbital antiferromagnetic currents in a frustrated fermionic ladder
papers.abstract: We consider a spinless $t$-$t'$ ionic Hubbard chain at 1/2 filling and large hopping ratio $t'/t$. In this limit the model adequately maps onto a weakly coupled triangular ladder with a potential interchain bias. The low-energy properties of the system are formed due to the interplay of geometrical frustration, correlations and charge imbalance. We derive the effective field-theoretical model to study universal properties of the model in the scaling limit. We show that at full dynamical frustration the ground state of the ladder represents a repulsive version of the Luther-Emery liquid with dominant orbital antiferromagnetic correlations exhibiting the slowest power-law decay in the ground state. Pairing correlations also display algebraic order but are subdominant. At an incomplete dynamical frustration a finite commensurability gap is dynamically generated, and the fluctuating OAF transforms to a long-range ordered state with a spontaneously broken time reversal symmetry. The mass gap in the spectrum of relative density fluctuations gets suppressed upon increasing the potential bias.

papers.title: RECOVAR: Representation Covariances on Deep Latent Spaces for Seismic Event Detection
Tensor Network Based HOBO Solver
papers.abstract: In the field of quantum computing, combinatorial optimization problems are typically addressed using QUBO (Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization) solvers. However, these solvers are often insufficient for tackling higher-order problems. In this paper, we introduce a novel and efficient solver designed specifically for HOBO (Higher-Order Binary Optimization) problem settings. Our approach leverages advanced techniques to effectively manage the complexity and computational demands associated with high-dimensional optimization tasks. The proposed solver is a promising tool with significant potential for future extensions in terms of formulation. This solver holds promising potential for a wide range of applications in quantum computing.

papers.title: Mixed-Precision Lloyd's Algorithm for k-means Clustering
Quantum inverse scattering for the 20-vertex model up to Dynkin automorphism: 3D Poisson structure, triangular height functions, weak integrability
papers.abstract: We initiate a novel application of the quantum inverse scattering method for the 20-vertex model, building upon seminal work from Faddeev and Takhtajan on the study of Hamiltonian systems. In comparison to a previous work of the author in late 2023 which characterized integrability of a Hamiltonian flow for the 6-vertex model from integrability of inhomogeneous limit shapes, formalized in a work of Keating, Reshetikhin and Sridhar, notions similar to those of integrability can be realized for the 20-vertex model by studying new classes of higher-dimensional L-operators. Such L-operators provided by Boos and colleagues have algebraic, combinatorial, and geometric, qualities, all of which impact leading order approximations of correlations, products of L-operators, the transfer matrix, and the quantum monodromy matrix.

papers.title: Harary's Sum and Integral Sum Graphs -- A Survey in detail
papers.abstract: Harary introduced the concepts of sum and integral sum graphs. A graph $G$ is a {\em sum graph} if the vertices of $G$ can be labeled with distinct positive integers so that $e = uv$ is an edge of $G$ if and only if the sum of the labels on vertices $u$ and $v$ is also a label in $G$. An {\em integral sum graph} is also defined just as sum graph, the difference being that the labels may be any distinct integers. This survey presents results obtained by different authors, in detail, on sum and integral sum graphs.

papers.title: TARGO and TARGO-Net: Benchmarking Target-driven Object Grasping under Occlusions
A locking-free isogeometric thin shell formulation based on higher order accurate diagonalized strain projection via approximate dual splines
Sfumato Supervision: Learning Instance Segmentation with Noisy Labels
Finding pure Nash equilibria in large random games
papers.abstract: Best Response Dynamics (BRD) constitute a family of strategy update rules designed to identify Pure Nash Equilibria (PNEs) in strategic games. In each iteration, a player is selected uniformly at random and adopts a best response strategy, maximising their payoff given the current strategies of the other players. If no improvement is possible for the selected player, another is chosen. The process terminates upon reaching a state where no player wishes to deviate, corresponding to a PNE. However, convergence is not guaranteed as either PNEs may not exist, or the dynamics may become confined within substructures of the game, which we call traps, that admit no PNEs. We investigate this behaviour in the context of random games with $N$ players, each choosing between two actions and receiving independently and identically distributed payoffs. The payoff distribution is permitted to have atoms, allowing for the possibility of ties. The induced dynamics define a class of random walks on the $N$-dimensional hypercube, where the landscape includes two types of absorbing sets: PNEs and traps. Our analysis encompasses BRD, simple random walks, and a broad class of nearest-neighbour processes. We prove that, with high probability, these dynamics reach a PNE before encountering any trap. Our results complete and generalise the ones by Amiet, Collevecchio, Scarsini and Zhong (2021), using a different approach.

papers.title: Could Mobile AI be Exploited?: Understanding the Exploitations of Trust and Ethics Gap in On-Device Small Language Models
An Empirical Calibration of the Tip of the Red Giant Branch Distance Method in the Near Infrared. II. JWST NIRCam Wide Filters
papers.abstract: The tip of the red giant (TRGB) is a standardizable candle and is identifiable as the discontinuity at the bright extreme of the red giant branch (RGB) stars in color-magnitude diagram (CMD) space. The TRGB-based distance method has been calibrated and used to measured distances to galaxies out to $D\leq20$ Mpc with the $I$-band equivalent Hubble Space Telescope ($HST$) $F814W$ filter, and as an important rung in the distance ladder to measure the Hubble constant, $H_0$. In the infrared (IR), the TRGB apparent magnitude ranges from $1-2$ magnitudes brighter than in the optical, and now with the IR James Webb Space Telescope ($JWST$) observatory the feasible distance range of the TRGB method can be extended to $\sim50$ Mpc. However, in the IR the TRGB luminosity depends to varying degrees on stellar metallicity and age. In this study we standardize the TRGB luminosity using stellar colors as a proxy for metallicity/age to derive color-based corrections for the $JWST$ Near-Infrared Camera (NIRCam) short wavelength (SW) filters $F090W$, $F115W$, $F150W$ and the long wavelength (LW) filters $F277W$, $F356W,$ and $F444W$. We provide recommended filter combinations for distance measurements depending on the requisite precision. For science requiring high precision ($\leq1\%$ in distance) and robustness we recommend measuring the TRGB in $F090W$ vs $F090W-F150W$ or $F115W$ vs. $F115W-F277W$ with the caveat that even with $JWST$ long integration times will be necessary at further distances. If lower precision ($>1.5\%$ in distance) can be tolerated, or if shorter integration times are desirable, we recommend measuring the TRGB in either $F115W$ or $F150W$ paired with $F356W$. We do not recommend $F444W$ for precision TRGB measurements due to its lower angular resolution.

papers.title: Minimal submanifolds and stability in Einstein manifolds
papers.abstract: In this paper, we compute the index and nullity for minimal submanifolds of some complex Einstein spaces. We investigate the stability of these minimal submanifolds and suggest a criterion for instability for some cases. We also compute some higher eigenvalues for the Laplacian of the Berger spheres and provide with an algorithm.

papers.title: On Bivariate Jacobi Konhauser Polynomials
papers.abstract: Recently, Özarslan and Elidemir (2023) introduced a methodology for constructing two-variable biorthogonal polynomial families with the help of one-variable biorthogonal and orthogonal polynomial families. The primary objective of the paper is to introduce novel class of two-variable biorthogonal polynomials namley bivariate Jacobi Konhauser polynomials. We investigate several fundamental properties of these polynomials including their biorthogonality property, operational formula, generating function, and integral representation. Furthermore, We inverstigate their images under the Laplace transform, fractional integral and derivative operators. Corresponding to these polynomials, we define the new type bivariate Jacobi Konhauser Mittag Leffler (JKML) function and obtain the similar properties for them.

papers.title: Quantitative asymptotics for polynomial patterns in the primes
papers.abstract: We prove quantitative estimates for averages of the von Mangoldt and Möbius functions along polynomial progressions $n+P_1(m),\ldots, n+P_k(m)$ for a large class of polynomials $P_i$. The error terms obtained save an arbitrary power of logarithm, matching the classical Siegel--Walfisz error term. These results give the first quantitative bounds for the Tao--Ziegler polynomial patterns in the primes result. The proofs are based on a quantitative generalised von Neumann theorem of Peluse, a recent result of Leng on strong bounds for the Gowers uniformity of the primes, and analysis of a ``Siegel model'' for the von Mangoldt function along polynomial progressions.

papers.title: Pricing Expertise with Information Spillovers
papers.abstract: Why do experts charge value-based fees for some services and flat fees for others? For example, an analyst charges the same fee for a stock report whether the client invests a thousand dollars or a million, while an investment bank charges a higher fee for a fairness opinion on a large merger than on a small one. We consider the problem of an expert who sells expertise to a client whose private type determines his project and how much he has at stake. Because project states are correlated, cheaper expertise about a related project can substitute for expertise about his own. We develop a Markov model of information spillovers and provide an explicit characterization of the optimal menu. With perfect spillovers, as with a stock report, a common flat fee for full information is optimal. With sufficiently weak spillovers, as with a fairness opinion, each client receives full information at a value-based fee equal to his willingness to pay. Between these extremes, low types can receive distorted expertise at their full willingness to pay, while middle and high types receive full information. Middle types pay a common base fee plus a project-specific fee that rises with what is at stake, and high types pay a value-based fee equal to their willingness to pay. Because higher types lose more by buying expertise about another project, the project-specific fee can rise faster than willingness to pay, so client surplus can peak among middle types and fall to zero at the top.

papers.title: Secure Distributed Matrix Multiplication with Precomputation
New Tools for Smoothed Analysis: Least Singular Value Bounds for Random Matrices with Dependent Entries
On Elliptical and Inverse Elliptical Wishart distributions
papers.abstract: This paper deals with the Elliptical Wishart and Inverse Elliptical Wishart distributions, which play a major role when handling covariance matrices. Similarly to multivariate elliptical distributions, these form a large family of covariance distributions, encompassing, \textit{e.g.}, the Wishart or $t$-Wishart ones. Our first major contribution is to derive a stochastic representation for Elliptical Wishart and Inverse Elliptical Wishart matrices. This later enables us to obtain various key statistical properties of these distributions such as expectations, variances, and Kronecker moments up to any order. The stochastic representation provides an efficient method for generating random matrices from these distributions. Additionally, Elliptical Wishart distributions have a specific dependence structure - a random scale shared by all columns - which strongly influences their asymptotic behavior. Lastly, the practical relevance of Elliptical Wishart distributions, particularly the $t$-Wishart distribution, is demonstrated through a fitting experiment conducted on real electroencephalographic data. This experiment highlights their effectiveness in accurately modeling real covariance matrices.

papers.title: Stochastic optimal control problems with measurable coefficients and unbounded drift
papers.abstract: We consider controlled SDEs with measurable coefficients, a uniformly elliptic diffusion coefficient and an $L_d$-drift. In this framework we investigate the relationship among value functions, PDEs, and operator semigroups. First, for a cost with an infinite time horizon on a bounded domain, we identify the value function as an $L_{d_0}$-viscosity solution to an HJB equation and we establish quantitative regularity estimates. The constant $d_0 \in (d/2, d)$ only depends on the space dimension $d$, the ellipticity constants of the diffusion coefficient and the $L_d$-bound of the drift. To illustrate applications of these results, we provide a uniqueness theorem under an additional assumption on the diffusion coefficient, showing a stochastic representation, and we discuss stability of value functions. Second, we consider a cost with a finite time horizon, terminal and running terms, assuming an $L_{d + 1}$-drift. We show that the value function indexed over the terminal cost is a nonlinear semigroup on $C_b (\mathbb{R}^d)$ and we establish a regularization by noise effect, which shows that the semigroup regularizes lower semicontinuity to local Hölder continuity. We also establish quantitative regularity estimates for the semigroup that are local in time and global in space. Lastly, under an additional $L_{d + 2, loc}$-assumption on the drift, we relate the semigroup to a parabolic PDE, showing that the associated value function is an $L_{d + 1}$-viscosity solution. Our proofs of the regularity of the value functions, the $C_b$-Feller property of the semigroup and its regularization by noise effects are based on a strong Markov selection principle and analytic estimates for linear diffusions that were recently established by N. V. Krylov in a series of papers. We highlight that our method covers frameworks without uniqueness of the controlled SDEs, as well as the associated PDEs.

papers.title: Nontrivial Massey products on compact Kähler manifolds
papers.abstract: We show that the bigraded quasi-isomorphism type of the bigraded, bidifferential algebra of forms on a compact Kähler manifold generally contains more information than the de Rham cohomology algebra with its real Hodge structure. More precisely, on any closed Riemann surface of genus at least two, there is a nontrivial ABC-Massey product. Furthermore, starting from dimension three, there are simply connected projective manifolds with a nonzero ABC-Massey product of three divisor classes. In particular, compact Kähler manifolds are generally not formal in the sense of pluripotential homotopy theory.

papers.title: Control of the Schrödinger equation in $\mathbb{R}^3$: The critical case
papers.abstract: This article deals with the $H^{1}$--level local null controllability for the energy-critical nonlinear Schrödinger equation in $\mathbb{R}^3$. Firstly, we demonstrate that the problem under consideration is well-posed using Strichartz estimates. Moreover, through the Hilbert uniqueness method, we prove the linear Schrödinger equation to be controllable by means of a control force supported in the exterior of a ball. Finally, we use a perturbation argument and show local controllability for the critical nonlinear Schrödinger equation.

papers.title: A sharper observability for diffusion equations in $\mathbb R^N$
papers.abstract: We establish that for any small constant $\varepsilon>0$, there exists a nontrivial equidistributed set (with an unbounded complement) such that the observability cost in the short time $(0,T)$ of diffusion equations over $\mathbb{R}^{N}$ can be improved to a sharper exponential form of $Ce^{\varepsilon/T}$, where $C>0$ is a constant independent of $T$.

papers.title: Gaussian-Channel Regularity and Distribution Learning with Flow Matching
papers.abstract: We study distribution learning by flow matching with linear interpolation from a Gaussian source under Gaussian-channel regularity, a condition on the target distribution. For an integer $r\geq2$, we establish spatial regularity of order $r$ for the population velocity, together with temporal Lipschitz continuity on the full interval and local time analyticity before the terminal time. We use these properties to construct a finite multiscale ReLU sieve with a spatial Lipschitz bound independent of the truncation radius. For an exact minimizer of the empirical flow matching risk over this sieve, we obtain an upper bound on the expected Wasserstein-$2$ error of order $n^{-r/(d+2r)}$, up to a logarithmic factor, where $n$ is the sample size and $d$ is the dimension. The bound includes Euler discretization up to time one, without early stopping. The conditions hold at $r=2$ for targets with strongly convex $C^2$ potentials and two-sided Hessian bounds. They also hold at every fixed order $r\geq2$ for distributions obtained by convolving a law of bounded support with a nondegenerate isotropic Gaussian. For sufficiently large fixed constants defining the target class, we prove a minimax lower bound of order $\max\{n^{-1/2},n^{-(r+1)/(d+2r)}\}$.

papers.title: Fractional Calculus Operator Emerging from the 2D Biorthogonal Hermite Konhauser Polynomials
papers.abstract: In the present paper, we introduce a method to construct two variable biorthogonal polynomial families with the help of one variable biorthogonal and orthogonal polynomial families. By using this new technique, we define 2D Hermite Konhauser polynomials and we investigate several properties of them such as biorthogonality property, operational formula and integral representation. We further inverstigate their images under the Laplace transformations, fractional integral and derivative operators. Corresponding to these polynomials, we define the new type bivariate Hermite Konhauser Mittag Leffler function and obtain the similar properties for them.
