In order to establish new fractional calculus, we add two new parameters and consider 2D Hermite Konhauser polynomials and bivariate Hermite Konhauser Mittag Leffler function. We introduce an integral operator containing the modified bivariate Hermite Konhauser Mittag Leffler function in the kernel. We show that it satisify the semigroup property and obtain its left inverse operator, which corresponds to its fractional derivative operator.

papers.title: On the enumeration of signatures of XOR-CNF's
On Some Infinitary Logics
papers.abstract: We define a new class of infinitary logics $\mathscr L^1_{\kappa,\alpha}$ generalizing Shelah's logic $\mathbb L^1_\kappa$ defined in \cite{MR2869022}. If $\kappa=\beth_\kappa$ and $\alpha <\kappa$ is infinite then our logic coincides with $\mathbb L^1_\kappa$. We study the relation between these logics for different parameters $\kappa$ and $\alpha$. We give many examples of classes of structures that can or cannot be defined in these logics. Finally, we give a different version of Lindström's Theorem for $\mathbb L^1_\kappa$ in terms of the $\phi$-submodel relation.

papers.title: The transversal game
papers.abstract: Two players take turns claiming empty cells from an $n\times n$ grid. The first player (if any) to occupy a transversal (a set of $ n $ cells having no two cells in the same row or column) is the winner. What is the outcome of the game given optimal play? Our aim in this paper is to show that for $n\ge 4$ the first player has a winning strategy. This answers a question of Erickson. We also consider variants of the game in which the family of winning transversals is restricted, both in the original game and in its Maker--Breaker version.

papers.title: On the Separability Problem of VASS Reachability Languages
Dynamic portfolio selection under generalized disappointment aversion
papers.abstract: This paper addresses the continuous-time portfolio selection problem under generalized disappointment aversion (GDA). The implicit definition of the certainty equivalent within GDA preferences introduces time inconsistency to this problem. Within the class of bounded, right-continuous deterministic strategies, we provide a necessary and sufficient condition for equilibrium in the form of a fully nonlinear integral equation. Investigating the existence and uniqueness of the solution to the integral equation, we establish the existence and uniqueness of the equilibrium in this class. Our findings indicate that under disappointment aversion preferences, non-participation in the stock market is the unique equilibrium in this class. The semi-analytical equilibrium strategies obtained under the constant relative risk aversion utility functions reveal that, under GDA preferences, the investment proportion in the stock market consistently remains smaller than the investment proportion under classical expected utility theory. The numerical analysis shows that the equilibrium strategy's monotonicity concerning the two parameters of GDA preference aligns with the monotonicity of the degree of risk aversion. Finally, in a switching-drift market with a random expected return, we prove the existence of a non-deterministic equilibrium.

papers.title: On the role of dense ideals on $\mathcal{I}$-characterized subgroups and associated $\mathcal{I}$-Arbault sets
papers.abstract: This article is a continuation of the work done in [Das et al., Annals of Pure and Applied Logic 174 (2023), 103289] on $\mathcal{I}$-characterized subgroups and concerns in addition the generalized version of Arbault sets, namely, $\mathcal{I}$-Arbault sets that is generated from this collection. A special class of ideals, namely, non-$snt$ ideals was introduced in 2023 ($snt$ stands for ``strongly non translation invariant") which was found to be effective in understanding ``Eggleston's dichotomy". Here we introduce another new class of ideals $\mathcal{H}$, a subclass of non-$snt$ ideals. We are able to establish a (new) necessary and sufficient condition for a $P$-ideal to be dense in Theorem 2.8 using the condition used to define the class $\mathcal{H}$ from which it follows that $\mathcal{H}$ coincides with dense $P$-ideals. Furthermore the important fact is established that the class of non-$snt$ ideals strictly contains the class of dense $P$-ideals. Subsequent investigation leads us to Theorem 2.14 which establishes the novelty of $\mathcal{I}$-characterized subgroups for ideals coming from the class $\mathcal{H}$ and arbitrary arithmetic sequences showing that these are not even Arbault sets. Before all these, we also present a correct and revised proof of the main result of [Das et al., Annals of Pure and Applied Logic 174 (2023), 103289], namely Theorem 3.8 (which had a gap in the proof). Finally we extend the results of [Das et al., Bul. Sci. Math. 179 (2022), 103157] for generalized version of Arbault sets and primarily show that for each ideal coming from the class $\mathcal{H}$, the class of $\mathcal{I}$-Arbault sets not only properly contains the class of classical Arbault sets but also a large subfamily of sets of absolute convergence while being contained in the class of weak Dirichlet sets.

papers.title: Credible Sets of Overall Ranking of Entities
papers.abstract: Ranking, and inferences based on ranking of a set of entities, are important problems in numerous contexts. This is especially true in small area statistics where there may be only a limited amount of directly observed data from each entity or small area, while precise and accurate estimates of best or worst performing entities are needed for fund allocation, planning and policymaking, stakeholder advocacy, evaluation of welfare programs, and so on. However, ranks estimates constructed exclusively on point estimates of parameters lack uncertainty quantification, and may lead to imbalances and inequities when these are based on small sample sizes. We propose novel Bayesian approaches to address this problem. Our proposals result in partitions of the parameter space with posterior distribution driven partial ordering of the sets in a partition. This in turn translates to a coherent probability mass function over ranks for every entity, and a coherent probability mass function over entities for every rank. Our Bayesian algorithms significantly outperform the state-of-the-art non-Bayesian alternatives, and are amenable to inclusion of covariates in the model as well as borrowing strengths across small areas. We evaluate our proposed Bayesian algorithms in terms of accuracy and stability using a number of applications and a simulation study. Additionally, we develop a novel theoretical framework for inference and ranking problems involving a triangular array of Fay-Herriot models and data, and provide probabilistic guarantees of performances of the proposed Bayesian ranking algorithms.

papers.title: Inverse Gram Matrix Methods for Prioritization in Analytic Hierarchy Process: Explainability of Weighted Least Squares Optimization Method
papers.abstract: This paper proposes Inverse Gram Matrix (IGM) methods to prioritize Pairwise Reciprocal Matrices (PRMs) in the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP). The IGM methods include Pseudo-IGM, Normalized-IGM, and Lagrangian-IGM. Interestingly, the proposed IGM methods achieve the minimum Weighted Least Squares (WLS) error. Since clarity, explainability, usability, and verification of the closed-form solutions of WLS appear to be incomplete in the literature, comprehensive mathematical proofs, detailed computational demonstrations, and intensive simulation verification to extend the prior studies are offered in this study. After a simulation of one million random PRM instances was performed to verify the equivalence of the IGM methods, another simulation of ten thousand random PRM instances was performed to verify that any one of the proposed IGM methods is the exact closed-form solution to the WLS optimization problem. The proposed IGM methods under the WLS framework provide the promising alternatives to Saaty's Eigenvector method in AHP. The open-source R package igm4ahp, along with its user manual, tutorials, and simulation datasets, is publicly available on GitHub and permanently archived on Zenodo.

papers.title: Integrating Fairness and Model Pruning Through Bi-level Optimization
Monodromy of rational singularities on surfaces in mixed characteristic
papers.abstract: We study the monodromy on the $\ell$-adic cohomology of smooth proper surfaces over complete discrete valuation fields of mixed characteristic $(0,p)$, with algebraically closed residue field and $p>5$. When the surfaces admit proper models whose special fiber has at worst a rational double point, we show that the monodromy action of inertia is finite, depends on an étale neighborhood of the singularity and its nontrivial part coincides with a restriction of the reflection representation of a Weyl group naturally associated with the singularity. We extend this description for degenerations into general rational singularities whose deformations lie in the Artin component: the monodromy is described by restricting the reflection representation of the Weyl group associated with the exceptional $(-2)$-curves in the minimal resolution of the special fiber. Moreover we determine minimal finite extensions over which such surfaces have good reduction. The proof relies on a mixed-characteristic extension of Grothendieck--Springer simultaneous resolutions and an identification of monodromy and Springer representations via relatively perverse nearby cycles.

papers.title: Existence, uniqueness, and universality of global dynamics for the fractional hyperbolic $Φ^4_3$-model
papers.abstract: We study the fractional $\Phi^4_3$-measure (with order $\alpha > 1$) and the dynamical problem of its canonical stochastic quantization: the three-dimensional stochastic damped fractional nonlinear wave equation with a cubic nonlinearity, also called the fractional hyperbolic $\Phi^4_3$-model. We first construct the fractional $\Phi^4_3$-measure via the variational approach by Barashkov-Gubinelli (2020). When $\alpha \leq \frac{9}{8}$, this fractional $\Phi^4_3$-measure turns out to be singular with respect to the base Gaussian measure. We then prove almost sure global well-posedness of the fractional hyperbolic $\Phi^4_3$-model and invariance of the fractional $\Phi^4_3$-measure for all $\alpha > 1$ by further developing the globalization framework due to Oh-Okamoto-Tolomeo (2024) on the hyperbolic $\Phi^3_3$-model. Furthermore, when $\alpha > \frac{9}{8}$ , we prove weak universality of the fractional hyperbolic $\Phi^4_3$-model by utilizing the convergence of Gibbs measures.

papers.title: Prescribed projections and efficient coverings by curves in the plane
papers.abstract: Davies efficient covering theorem states that an arbitrary measurable set $W$ in the plane can be covered by full lines so that the measure of the union of the lines has the same measure as $W$. This result has an interesting dual formulation in the form of a prescribed projection theorem. In this paper, we formulate each of these results in a nonlinear setting and consider some applications. In particular, given a measurable set $W$ and a curve $\Gamma=\{(t,f(t)): t\in [a,b]\}$, where $f$ is $C^1$ with strictly monotone derivative, we show that $W$ can be covered by translations of $\Gamma$ in such a way that the union of the translated curves has the same measure as $W$. This is achieved by proving an equivalent prescribed generalized projection result, which relies on a Venetian blind construction.

papers.title: Transposed Poisson structures on solvable and perfect Lie algebras
papers.abstract: We described all transposed Poisson algebra structures on oscillator Lie algebras, i.e., on one-dimensional solvable extensions of the $(2n+1)$-dimensional Heisenberg algebra; on solvable Lie algebras with naturally graded filiform nilpotent radical; on $(n+1)$-dimensional solvable extensions of the $(2n+1)$-dimensional Heisenberg algebra; and on $n$-dimensional solvable extensions of the $n$-dimensional algebra with trivial multiplication. We also answered one question on transposed Poisson algebras, posted in a paper by Beites, Ferreira and Kaygorodov. Namely, we found that the semidirect product of ${\mathfrak sl}_2$ and an irreducible module gives a finite-dimensional Lie algebra with non-trivial $\frac{1}{2}$-derivations, but without non-trivial transposed Poisson structures.

papers.title: On minimal subshifts of linear word complexity with slope less than 3/2
papers.abstract: We prove that every infinite minimal subshift with word complexity $p(q)$ satisfying $\limsup p(q)/q < 3/2$ is measure-theoretically isomorphic to its maximal equicontinuous factor; in particular, it has measurably discrete spectrum. Among other applications, this provides a proof of Sarnak's conjecture for all subshifts with $\limsup p(q)/q < 3/2$ (which can be thought of as a much stronger version of zero entropy). We also show that all such subshifts are balanced, and that orbit equivalence between them is characterized by the additive eigenvalue group. As in [CP23], our main technique is proving that all low-complexity minimal subshifts have a specific type of representation via a sequence $\{\tau_k\}$ of substitutions, usually called an S-adic decomposition. The maximal equicontinuous factor is the (possibly twisted) product of an odometer with a rotation on a compact abelian connected one-dimensional group (either a circle or solenoid), for which we can give an explicit description in terms of the substitutions $\tau_k$. We also prove that all such odometers and groups may appear for minimal subshifts with $\limsup p(q)/q = 1$, demonstrating that lower complexity thresholds do not further restrict the possible structure.

papers.title: A biregular classification of smooth quotients of abelian surfaces
papers.abstract: We classify smooth projective surfaces that are quotients of abelian surfaces by finite groups. We also record the orbifold boundary associated to a quotient map and describe its structure explicitly in the case of augmented irregularity one.

papers.title: Discrete and Continuous Concentration of Measure: Geometric Obstructions, Predictive Gowdy Evolution, and Observable Limits
papers.abstract: We compare concentration in increasing dimension with geometric and metric--measure degeneration of compact Cauchy hypersurfaces. For vacuum $T^3$-Gowdy developments we establish an exact law for redistribution of normalized spatial volume, without imposing polarization. An explicit strict bound on the \emph{initial} spatially averaged wave-map energy guarantees divergence of the transverse circle length $L(\tau)$. Under this expansion hypothesis, we classify \emph{all convergent distance-scaling regimes}: if $a_\tau L(\tau)\to\ell$, the rescaled sections concentrate to a point for $\ell=0$, to the uniformly measured circle of circumference $\ell$ for $0<\ell<\infty$, while for $\ell=\infty$ their associated pyramids converge to the maximal pyramid. The classification applies to Ringström's generic non-polarized class, including nondegenerate true spikes, and requires no uniform geometric control at spike points. The argument compares orbit metrics with their initial values outside an exceptional set of probability at most $L(\tau_0)/L(\tau)$. The normalized Laplacian splits into periodic one-dimensional Schrödinger operators indexed by toroidal Fourier modes; its non-invariant sectors satisfy a uniform spectral gap $\Lambda_\tau\ge cL(\tau)^2$. Thus only torus-invariant modes persist at bounded spectral energy, with quantitative heat-semigroup and resolvent estimates. Separately, an initial-data perturbation criterion yields strictly monotone transfer toward a prescribed region in a relatively open low-velocity non-polarized class. Explicit high-velocity solutions exhibit contrasting point-collapse and unbounded-diameter geometries governed by the torus marking.

papers.title: Almost Sure Averaging for Fast-slow Stochastic Differential Equations via Controlled Rough Path
papers.abstract: This paper establishes the averaging method to a coupled system consisting of two stochastic differential equations which has a slow component driven by fractional Brownian motion (FBM) with less regularity $1/3< H \leq 1/2$ and a fast dynamics under additive FBM with Hurst-index $1/3< \hat H \leq 1/2$. We prove that the solution of the slow component converges almost surely to the solution of the corresponding averaged equation using the approach of time discretization and controlled rough path. To do this, we employ the random dynamical system (RDS) to obtain a stationary solution by an exponentially attracting random fixed point of the RDS generated by the non-Markovian fast component.

papers.title: Faster Algorithms for Structured Linear and Kernel Support Vector Machines
papers.abstract: Many machine learning problems are quadratic programs, including Support Vector Machines (SVMs). A general quadratic program has input size $\Theta(n^2)$, and assuming the Strong Exponential Time Hypothesis (SETH), no $O(n^{2-o(1)})$ time algorithm exists when the objective matrix is positive semidefinite (Backurs, Indyk, and Schmidt, NeurIPS'17). SVMs, however, are given by $n$ data points of dimension $d$, often much smaller than $n$, and have only $O(1)$ equality constraints. In this work, we design the first nearly-linear time algorithm for solving quadratic programs whenever a low-rank factorization of the quadratic objective matrix is given, the number of linear constraints is small, the coefficients of the objective and some optimal solution are bounded by $\mathrm{poly}(n)$, and some feasible point has all entries between $1/\mathrm{poly}(n)$ and $\mathrm{poly}(n)$. For linear SVM on $d$-dimensional data, our randomized algorithm runs in expected time $\widetilde O(nd^{(\omega+1)/2}\log(n/\epsilon))$ when $(d+1)^{\omega-1}\le n$ and the data points have norms at most $\mathrm{poly}(n)$ and margin at least $1/\mathrm{poly}(n)$, where $\omega<2.258$ is the matrix multiplication exponent. Its output satisfies the equality constraint only approximately. For Gaussian kernel SVM, when $d=O(\log n)$, the squared dataset radius is $o(\log n/\log\log n)$ and the dual variables lie in a box $[0,R]^n$ with $R\le\mathrm{poly}(n)$, our randomized algorithm runs in expected time $n^{1+o(1)}$ for any accuracy $\epsilon\ge 1/\mathrm{poly}(n)$. We also prove that, assuming SETH, when the squared dataset radius is $\Omega(\log^2 n)$, $\Omega(n^{2-o(1)})$ time is required on some inputs to reach error $\exp(-\Theta(\log^2 n))$ for the program without the bias term. This improves upon the prior best lower bound in both the dimension $d$ and the squared dataset radius.

papers.title: Stationarity with Occasionally Binding Constraints
papers.abstract: This paper studies a class of multivariate threshold autoregressive models, known as censored and kinked structural vector autoregressions (CKSVAR), which are notably able to accommodate series that are subject to occasionally binding constraints. We develop a set of sufficient conditions for the processes generated by a CKSVAR to be stationary, ergodic, and weakly dependent. Our conditions relate directly to the stability of the deterministic part of the model, and are therefore less conservative than those typically available for general vector threshold autoregressive (VTAR) models. Though our criteria refer to quantities, such as refinements of the joint spectral radius, that cannot feasibly be computed exactly, they can be approximated numerically to a high degree of precision.

papers.title: The Brauer-Manin obstruction on algebraic stacks
papers.abstract: For algebraic stacks over number fields, we define their Brauer-Manin sets, Brauer-Manin pairings, and extend the descent theory of Colliot-Thélène and Sansuc. By extending Sansuc's exact sequence, we show the torsionness of Brauer groups of stacks that are locally quotients of varieties by linear groups. With mild assumptions, for stacks that are locally quotients or Deligne-Mumford, we show that the Brauer-Manin obstruction coincides with some other cohomological obstructions such as obstructions given by torsors under connected groups or abelian gerbes. For Brauer-Manin sets of these stacks, we show the properties such as descent along a torsor, product preservation are still correct. These results extend classical theories of those on varieties.

papers.title: A Comprehensive Survey on Orbital Edge Computing: Systems, Applications, and Algorithms
Selective Inference for Survey-Weighted Generalized Linear Models: Growing Dimension and Average Marginal Effects
papers.abstract: This paper extends the $\ell_1$-penalized likelihood Selective Inference method to survey settings. We establish its asymptotic validity for generalized linear models with an increasing number of covariates and survey weights, allowing inference on pseudo-true parameters of possibly misspecified selected models. Moreover, we generalize the method to facilitate inference on nonlinear functionals, such as the average marginal effect in survey-weighted logit models. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is illustrated using simulated data and the 2020 Canadian Internet Use Survey.

papers.title: Boundary to bound dictionary for generic Kerr orbits
papers.abstract: We establish a new relation between classical observables for scattering and bound orbits of a massive probe particle in a Kerr background. We find an exact representation of the Hamilton-Jacobi action in terms of the conserved charges which admits an analytic continuation, both for the radial and polar contribution, for a general class of geodesics beyond the equatorial case. Remarkably, this allows to extend the boundary to bound dictionary and it provides an efficient method to compute the deflection angles and the time delay for scattering orbits, as well as frequency ratios for bound orbits, in the probe limit but at all orders in the perturbative expansion.

papers.title: Ensemble Modeling for Time Series Forecasting: an Adaptive Robust Optimization Approach
Stop Using Plausibility as the Criterion for Explainable AI
Storage and Learning phase transitions in the Random-Features Hopfield Model
papers.abstract: The Hopfield model is a paradigmatic model of neural networks that has been analyzed for many decades in the statistical physics, neuroscience, and machine learning communities. Inspired by the manifold hypothesis in machine learning, we propose and investigate a generalization of the standard setting that we name Random-Features Hopfield Model. Here $P$ binary patterns of length $N$ are generated by applying to Gaussian vectors sampled in a latent space of dimension $D$ a random projection followed by a non-linearity. Using the replica method from statistical physics, we derive the phase diagram of the model in the limit $P,N,D\to\infty$ with fixed ratios $\alpha=P/N$ and $\alpha_D=D/N$. Besides the usual retrieval phase, where the patterns can be dynamically recovered from some initial corruption, we uncover a new phase where the features characterizing the projection can be recovered instead. We call this phenomena the learning phase transition, as the features are not explicitly given to the model but rather are inferred from the patterns in an unsupervised fashion.

papers.title: Cartesian Gray-Monoidal Double Categories
papers.abstract: In this paper we present cartesian structure for symmetric Gray-monoidal double categories. To do this we first introduce locally cubical Gray categories, which are three-dimensional categorical structures analogous to classical, locally globular, Gray categories. The motivating example comprises double categories themselves, together with their functors, transformations, and modifications. A one-object locally cubical Gray category is a Gray-monoidal double category. Braiding, syllepsis, and symmetry for these is introduced in a manner analogous to that for 2-categories. Adding cartesian structure requires the introduction of doubly-lax functors of double categories to manage the order of copies. The resulting theory is algebraically rather complex, largely due to the bureaucracy of linearizing higher-dimensional boundary constraints. Fortunately, it has a relatively simple and compelling representation in the graphical calculus of surface diagrams, which we present.

papers.title: Lower bounds on the measure of the support of positive and negative parts of trigonometric polynomials
papers.abstract: The measure of the positivity set $\{ x \in [0; 2\pi] \mid f(x) > 0 \}$ of a trigonometric polynomial $f$ is bounded from below by the Motzkin density. We generalize the bound to polynomials in several variables and almost periodic functions. We then use these generalizations to extend known results on Taikov's problem.

papers.title: Contextual Causal Bayesian Optimisation
Measuring price impact and information content of trades in a time-varying setting
papers.abstract: We propose a non-linear observation-driven version of the Hasbrouck vector auto-regression framework for dynamically estimating trades' market impact and information content. We find that market impact displays an intraday pattern superimposed with large fluctuations. Some of them are exogenous, and, as an example, we investigate market impact dynamics around FOMC announcements. Unlike the vector autoregression results, we reveal that the information content of the trades depends on the local liquidity level and the recent history of prices and trades. Finally, we use the model to estimate the time-varying permanent impact parameter, which allows performing a dynamic transaction cost analysis.

papers.title: Satellite knots that cannot be represented by positive braids with full twists
papers.abstract: A positive braid with at least one full twist is known to be a minimal braid, i.e, it achieves the braid index for its closure. In this paper we find knots that are the closure of positive minimal braids that cannot be represented by positive braids with full twists. More precisely, we show that some satellite knots with companions and patterns given as the closure of positive braids cannot be represented as the closure of positive braids with full twists. As a consequence, we find infinitely many satellite knots with companions and patterns being Lorenz knots that are not Lorenz knots. This gives an answer to the question whether a satellite knot having Lorenz pattern and companion is also a Lorenz knot, originally addressed by Birman and Williams in a special case in the 1980s.

papers.title: The geometry of Coherent topoi and Ultrastructures
papers.abstract: We show that coherent topoi are right Kan injective with respect to flat embeddings of topoi. We recover the ultrastructure on their category of points as a consequence of this result. We speculate on possible notions of ultracategory in various arenas of formal model theory.

papers.title: Double negation stable h-propositions in cubical sets
papers.abstract: We give a construction of classifiers for double negation stable h-propositions in a variety of cubical set models of homotopy type theory and cubical type theory. This is used to give some relative consistency results: classifiers for double negation stable propositions exist in cubical sets whenever they exist in the metatheory; the Dedekind real numbers can be added to homotopy type theory without changing the consistency strength; we construct a model of homotopy type theory with extended Church's thesis, which states that all partial functions with double negation stable domain are computable.

papers.title: Transposed Poisson structures on Galilean and solvable Lie algebras
papers.abstract: Transposed Poisson structures on complex Galilean-type Lie algebras and superalgebras are described. It is proven that the principal Galilean Lie algebras and superalgebras do not admit nontrivial transposed Poisson structures. We also prove that each complex finite-dimensional solvable Lie algebra of dimension greater than one admits a nontrivial $\frac{1}{2}$-derivation and a nontrivial ${\rm Hom}$-Lie structure, and that each complex finite-dimensional non-abelian solvable Lie algebra admits a nontrivial transposed Poisson structure.

papers.title: Safe Policy Learning under Regression Discontinuity Designs with Multiple Cutoffs
papers.abstract: We study policy learning under the regression discontinuity (RD) design, where deterministic treatment assignment requires extrapolation to identify improved treatment cutoffs. We develop a robust optimization approach that leverages the multiple cutoffs common in RD settings to minimize worst-case welfare loss relative to the status quo policy. Under the maintained assumptions, the resulting cutoffs guarantee overall welfare at least as high as that under the existing policy. We also establish oracle-gap bounds for the learned policy. Finally, we illustrate the proposed methodology through simulation studies and apply it to data from an educational assistance program in Colombia.

papers.title: Peer Prediction for Learning Agents
On Iwasawa invariants of modular forms with reducible and non-$p$-distinguished residual Galois representations
papers.abstract: Let $f$ be the ordinary $p$-stabilization of the weight-one Eisenstein series, where $\chi$ is odd and $\chi(p)=1$. Under a Gorenstein hypothesis on the cuspidal Hecke algebra, we prove a factorization of the even branches of the cyclotomic $p$-adic $L$-function of $f$ by evaluating a cup product of cyclotomic units via local reciprocity. The odd branches follow from the Eisenstein specialization formula of Fukaya and Kato with a minor modification for the exceptional character considered here. We then obtain results on the $\mu$- and $\lambda$-invariants. On the algebraic side, we compute the Selmer characteristic ideals at $f$ and the Iwasawa invariants of the higher-weight specializations. For every nontrivial twist of $f$, the ordinary characteristic ideal is generated by the corresponding $p$-adic $L$-function. On the untwisted branch it has one additional factor, the cyclotomic augmentation parameter. Imposing the strict local condition at $p$ removes this factor. For higher-weight specializations coming from newforms of level prime to $p$, Kato's divisibility then gives the cyclotomic main conjecture after inverting $p$.

papers.title: Dealing with Logs and Zeros in Regression Models
papers.abstract: Log regression is widely used to express effects in percentage terms, but zeros, heterogeneity and retransformation pose distinct difficulties. We unify the interpretation, identification and estimation of proportional effects through weighted individual percentage changes. We connect these parameters to pseudo-maximum likelihood estimation, characterize finite-sample differences between consistent estimators, and establish relationships with log regression. We develop a new shifted-log transformation that yields unit-invariant proportional-effect parameters and use it to construct iterated ordinary least squares (IOLS), an algorithm that estimates power-mean models through repeated OLS regressions. We prove global numerical convergence, consistency and asymptotic normality, and extend the approach to endogenous regressors. Furthermore, we develop fixed-effect cancellation and bias-correction methods that address incidental-parameter bias in common panel settings under general working variances, extending beyond the familiar Poisson-PML case. Finally, simulations document numerical reliability, competitive speed and finite-sample performance, while an application to economic development illustrates their empirical relevance.

papers.title: On Higher-Order Reachability Games vs May Reachability
Training Multi-Layer Over-Parametrized Neural Network in Subquadratic Time
Emergent kagome-like electronic texture in epitaxial $β$-Sb on Al(111)
papers.abstract: We report the epitaxial growth of $\beta$-Sb on Al(111) and the emergence of a kagome-like electronic texture with increasing Sb coverage. The surface evolves from disordered clusters through honeycomb and dice patterns before kagome-like regions appear. Diffraction, scanning tunneling microscopy, spectroscopy, and density functional calculations identify the ordered phase as $\beta$-Sb formed by AB stacking of two dice layers, with the honeycomb phase serving as a precursor. The kagome-like maxima occupy bridge positions within the same lateral lattice and differ in apparent height from dice regions by only about 25 pm. Together with the absence of an additional chemical component or distinct band manifold in photoemission, these observations support an electronic origin of the kagome-like contrast. Comparison of local tunneling spectra with calculated orbital projections suggests an energy selective change in the relative spectral contributions of Sb p states. Interface separation tests reveal sensitivity to Al-Sb coupling, while vacuum local density of states calculations identify states with enhanced bridge density. These results suggest that local interface changes could alter the balance between atomic and bridge contributions to tunneling within $\beta$-Sb. For a reference $\beta$-Sb model retaining the epitaxial geometry after Al removal, spin-orbit coupling modifies local band dispersions while the structure remains metallic. The model exhibits a finite intrinsic spin Hall response that varies with chemical potential.

papers.title: Distribution-Free Prediction Bands for Multivariate Functional Time Series: an Application to the Italian Gas Market
papers.abstract: Uncertainty quantification in forecasting represents a topic of great importance in energy trading, as understanding the status of the energy market would enable traders to directly evaluate the impact of their own offers/bids. To this end, we propose a scalable procedure that outputs closed-form simultaneous prediction bands for multivariate functional response variables in a time series setting, which is able to guarantee performance bounds in terms of unconditional coverage and asymptotic exactness, both under some conditions. After evaluating its performance on synthetic data, the method is used to build multivariate prediction bands for daily demand and offer curves in the Italian gas market.

papers.title: An XAI Approach to Deep Learning Models in the Detection of DCIS
Percentile in Percentile: Evaluating Scholars Across Career Stages
Hilbert's Tenth problem and NP-completeness of Boolean Syllogistic with unordered cartesian product
papers.abstract: We relate the decidability problem for BS with unordered cartesian product with Hilbert's Tenth problem and prove that BS with unordered cartesian product is NP-complete.

papers.title: $\frac{1}{2}$-derivations of Lie algebras and transposed Poisson algebras
papers.abstract: A relation between $\frac{1}{2}$-derivations of Lie algebras and transposed Poisson algebras has been established. Some non-trivial transposed Poisson algebras with a certain Lie algebra (Witt algebra, the algebra $\mathcal{W}(a,-1)$, the thin Lie algebra and a solvable Lie algebra with abelian nilpotent radical) have been done. In particular, we have developed an example of the transposed Poisson algebra with associative and Lie parts isomorphic to the Laurent polynomials and the Witt algebra. On the other side, it has been proved that there are no non-trivial transposed Poisson algebras with a Lie algebra part isomorphic to a semisimple finite-dimensional algebra, a simple finite-dimensional superalgebra, the Virasoro algebra, $N=1$ and $N=2$ superconformal algebras, or a semisimple finite-dimensional $n$-Lie algebra.

papers.title: Adventures in Multi-Omics I: Combining heterogeneous data sets via relationships matrices
papers.abstract: In this article, we propose a covariance based method for combining partial data sets in the genotype to phenotype spectrum. In particular, an expectation-maximization algorithm that can be used to combine partially overlapping relationship/covariance matrices is introduced. Combining data this way, based on relationship matrices, can be contrasted with a feature imputation based approach. We used several public genomic data sets to explore the accuracy of combining genomic relationship matrices. We have also used the heterogeneous genotype/phenotype data sets in the this https URL to illustrate how this new method can be used in genomic prediction, phenomics, and graphical modeling.

papers.title: Online Neural Network Training via Closed-Loop Model-Free Tracking Control: An Empirical Study
The set of numerical semigroups of a given multiplicity and Frobenius number
papers.abstract: We study the structure of the family of numerical semigroups with fixed multiplicity and Frobenius number. We give an algorithmic method to compute all the semigroups in this family. As an application we compute the set of all numerical semigroups with given multiplicity and genus.

papers.title: The classification of $2$-dimensional rigid algebras
papers.abstract: Using the algebraic classification of all $2$-dimensional algebras, we give the algebraic classification of all $2$-dimensional rigid, conservative and terminal algebras over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0. We have the geometric classification of the variety of $2$-dimensional terminal algebras, and based on the geometric classification of these algebras we formulate some open problems.

papers.title: Using the Tsetlin Machine to Learn Human-Interpretable Rules for High-Accuracy Text Categorization with Medical Applications
papers.abstract: Medical applications challenge today's text categorization techniques by demanding both high accuracy and ease-of-interpretation. Although deep learning has provided a leap ahead in accuracy, this leap comes at the sacrifice of interpretability. To address this accuracy-interpretability challenge, we here introduce, for the first time, a text categorization approach that leverages the recently introduced Tsetlin Machine. In all brevity, we represent the terms of a text as propositional variables. From these, we capture categories using simple propositional formulae, such as: if "rash" and "reaction" and "penicillin" then Allergy. The Tsetlin Machine learns these formulae from a labelled text, utilizing conjunctive clauses to represent the particular facets of each category. Indeed, even the absence of terms (negated features) can be used for categorization purposes. Our empirical comparison with Naïve Bayes, decision trees, linear support vector machines (SVMs), random forest, long short-term memory (LSTM) neural networks, and other techniques, is quite conclusive. The Tsetlin Machine either performs on par with or outperforms all of the evaluated methods on both the 20 Newsgroups and IMDb datasets, as well as on a non-public clinical dataset. On average, the Tsetlin Machine delivers the best recall and precision scores across the datasets. Finally, our GPU implementation of the Tsetlin Machine executes 5 to 15 times faster than the CPU implementation, depending on the dataset. We thus believe that our novel approach can have a significant impact on a wide range of text analysis applications, forming a promising starting point for deeper natural language understanding with the Tsetlin Machine.

papers.title: A Convergent Linear Regression Method for Forward-Backward Stochastic Differential Equations with Jumps
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce a large class of convergent numerical methods, based on (linear) basis function regression technique, to approximate the solution to a forward-backward stochastic differential equation with jumps (FBSDEJ hereafter). Numerical experiment shows good applicability of the proposed method.

papers.title: Strichartz estimates without loss outside two strictly convex obstacles
papers.abstract: We prove global Strichartz estimates without loss outside two strictly convex obstacles, combining arguments from this http URL (1982,1988) with more recent ones inspired by this http URL , this http URL , and A. Hassell (2010) and O. Ivanovici (2010). This is to be contrasted with the loss in the smoothing estimate for the Schrödinger equation with Dirichlet boundary conditions in the presence of a trapped geodesic.

papers.title: Critical binomial ideals of Northcott type
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study a family of binomial ideals defining monomial curves in the n-dimensional affine space determined by $n$ hypersurfaces of the form $x_i^{c_i} - x_1^{u_{i1}} \cdots x_n^{u_{1n}}$ in $\Bbbk[x_1, \ldots, x_n]$ with $u_{ii} = 0$, $i \in \{1, \ldots, n\}$. We prove that the monomial curves in that family are set-theoretic complete intersections. Moreover, if the monomial curve is irreducible, we compute some invariants such as genus, type and Frobenius number of the corresponding numerical semigroup. We also describe a method to produce set-theoretic complete intersection semigroup ideals of arbitrary large height.

papers.title: Tuning long-range interactions in Sr Rydberg atoms: the effect of series perturbations
papers.abstract: We investigate the effect of series perturbation on the second-order dipole-dipole interactions between strontium atoms in the $5sns({^1}S_0)$ and $5snp({^1}P_1)$ Rydberg states as a means of engineering long-range interactions between atoms. The series perturbation in these atoms enables modifying the strength and the sign of the interaction by varying the principal quantum number $n$ of the Rydberg electron. We utilize experimentally available data to estimate the importance of perturber states, and find that the van der Waals interaction between two strontium atoms in the $5snp({^1}P_1)$ states shows strong peaks that deviate from the anticipated hydrogenic $n^{11}$ scaling. We identify this to be the result of the perturbation of $5snd({^1}D_2)$ intermediate states by the $4d^2({^1}D_2)$ and $4dn's({^1}D_2)$ states in the $n<20$ range. This demonstrates that divalent atoms offer a unique advantage for generating substantially stronger or weaker inter-atomic interactions than those that can be achieved using alkali metal atoms. This is due to the highly perturbed spectra of divalent atoms and other multivalent atoms that can persist up to high $n$. Such irregularities can be especially useful in engineering asymmetric Ry blockade requiring the simultaneous presence of both ``weak'' and ``strong'' interactions.

papers.title: A maximum-entropy reduction for coalition formation with anonymous outsiders
Arithmetical Foundations - Recursion. Evaluation. Consistency
papers.abstract: We fix constructive foundations for Arithmetic on a map theoretical, algorithmic level. In contrast to elementhood and quantification based traditional foundations such as Principia Mathematica PM, Zermelo-Fraenkel set theory ZF, or v. Neumann-Goedel-Bernays set theory NGB, our fundamental primitive recursive theory PR has as its basic "undefined" (not further defined) terms just terms for objects and maps. Goodstein's axiomatic uniqueness rules are derived as theorems in PR - with equality definability as a side result -, S is obtained by predicate comprehension, and the equivalence of the theory of partially defined maps and the categorical theory of mu-recursion identifies mu-recursive maps and while-loops with partially defined maps. Keywords: Goedel theorems, primitive recursion, categorical free-variables Arithmetic, mu-recursion, totality

papers.title: Bessel Integrals, Periods and Zeta Numbers
papers.abstract: We present a summary of recent and older results on Bessel integrals and their relation with zeta numbers.

papers.title: On the Milnor classes of local complete intersections
papers.abstract: In this work we study algebraic, geometric and topological properties of the Milnor classes of local complete intersections with arbitrary singularities. We describe first the Milnor class of the intersection of a finite number of hypersurfaces, under certain conditions of transversality, in terms of the Milnor classes of the hypersurfaces. Using this description we obtain a Parusiński-Pragacz type formula, an Aluffi type formula and a description of the Milnor class of the local complete intersection in terms of the global Lê cycles of the hypersurfaces that define it. We consider next the general case of a local complete intersection $Z(s)$ defined by a regular section $s$ of a rank $r$ holomorphic bundle $E$ over a compact manifold $M$, $r \geq 2$. We notice that $s$ determines a hypersurface $Z(\tilde s)$ in the total space of the projectivization $\mathbb{P}(E^{\vee})$ of the dual bundle $E^{\vee}$, and we give a formula expressing the total Milnor class of the local complete intersection $Z(s)$ in terms of the Milnor classes of the hypersurface $Z(\tilde s)$.

papers.title: Formalism of operators for Laguerre-Gauss modes
papers.abstract: In this work apply the algebra of operators of quantum mechanics in the Helmholtz wave equation in cylindrical coordinates in paraxial approximation to describe the raising and lowering operators for the Laguerre-Gauss modes.
